This Scotch Laminator works great but takes up more space than the laminator I bought about 2 months ago.  The heat up time was about 5 minutes but once you run a pouch through it the Ready light turns off so you need to wait another minute so it can heat up again.  It laminates quickly and does a good job. I thought the cord storage area under it was a pretty nifty idea in case you want to store it away when you are not using it. It also has a hidden handle built into the left side. These are two reasons why it seems bulkier than it needs to be though.It comes with two modes, the 3 mil mode for regular paper, and the 5 mil mode for photos.  This seemed odd to me since other laminators base thickness on the mils of the pouch, and I am not sure that changing the setting really does anything except cause the ready light to go off for a minute.  The unit has a tray in the back that you lay the pouch on to feed it from the back of the machine, to where it comes out in the front.  This is opposite of my other one which takes the pouch through the front and out of the back.  The Scotch will take a pouch that is up to 9 inches wide, which given the size of the unit is surprising since you would expect it to take a wider pouch given its width.Here's my take. I also have a Swingline GBC Inspire that has a much smaller footprint, heats up more quickly, feeds into the front and out the back, and does a perfect job without requiring settings (just on or off), and it takes the same size pouches while being considerably less expensive than this one.  This Scotch brand laminator has a high price tag but it is very sturdy and does a really good job.  It seems a bit bulky compared to my other one but it will turn itself off after an hour of non-use and that is pretty cool given I am prone to be forgetful.However, I don't need a laminator very often and this one might be overkill for me, plus it really doesn't do anything my other laminator doesn't do except take up more space.  Although this is clearly a high quality product, I am not sure the extra features like the handle, cord storage, and jam-free technology (never had one jam before) warrants the high price tag unless you are a "Power Laminator" with lots of laminating to do. So, Overall it is great at getting the job done, but at this price and size I would really expect it take pouches 12 inches in width and so I can't give it a perfect 5.

I despise writing in books.  The thoughts, comments and interests of the scribblers and markers are fleeting and distracting.  I have an extensive library and am a reluctant lender because books rarely come back as pristine as they left.  Additionally, writing and highlighting lowers the resale value for books including texts.  These little sticky notes provide a solution.  In either transparentl yellow or pink, they are arrow shaped.  You can write on the note which is a little short of 3" x3".  I have tried them on books, briefs, assorted paperwork and have been satsified. Be aware that the the notes are only lightly glued at the tip of the arrow.  They are nicely transparent and you can read with ease through the color.  The pink and yellow colors are attractive and ball point pens perform well on them.These are ideal for both office and school.  In fact if I ever loan out another book, I will toss in a packet of these notes.

Kensington Wireless Presenter Pro with Green Laser PointerThe Kensington presenter remote installed and worked in a Windows 7 64-bit environment without any problems. I also have a Logitech R800 presenter that I've been using for over 2 years with great success, so I have a baseline to compare the Kensington.First, the Kensington isn't intended to be a top of the line "Cadillac" remote. There's no LCD display for battery life, a timer, or a vibrating motor. It is a no frills unit that gives you a green laser, forward, backwards, and blackout screen functionality with PowerPoint. The Kensington is shorter and fatter than the Logitech R800, which in my opinion fits a lot better because it is so wide. The Kensington's buttons are also very tactile and spread apart, so there's no accidental pressing of a button or hunting for a button. I found myself trying to find the right button on the R800 from time to time.The Kensington's green laser isn't very bright. I couldn't see it as clearly in a dimly lit office compared to the R800 which has a very bright green laser.Overall: 4/5 stars, not as feature-rich as a R800 due to the lack of a timer, LCD display, and other non-mandatory functions, but my only genuine complaint is that the green laser could be much brighter.

Lately I've been so disgusted with highlighters that I had quit using them. As a result, I've been underlining with a ball-point pen. What a mess! The highlighters always bled through thin pages, dried quickly, and smeared. The manufacturers of these new Sharpie Accent Gel Highlighters have solved these problems. I am enjoying using these, since they have restored my confidence in highlighters. Highly recommended.

I *really* like writing on graph/quad ruled paper so I decided to just order a big pad of it. The Ampad is great in that it's got 100 sheets, so I can go through the paper without worrying I might run out (as I tend to do with quad-ruled journals). The only drawbacks are that the blue lines of the quad ruling is fairly thick and bright (not subtle) and the paper is very thin (similar to cheap looseleaf paper). But I love that it's in a pad and sealed together on the top- I can store it easily and keep everything together.I wish they'd make a quad rule/graph pad with GRAY lines... But until I can find one, this will do great.
I am using these in my classroom.  I put file folder games, and other small games in them and put it with my unit studies.  Great way to organize, and the price is right!
Most mechanical pencils use 5mm to 7mm lead.  The finer lead here is very good when drawing accurate technical diagrams.

My first thought with these Fruit Design Post-It Notes was that they would have a faint smell of orange, lime, and strawberry. That, thankfully, is not the case. The design is merely to spice up an otherwise drab office product so that it looks nice sitting by your telephone or on your desk. The orange cube is a nice bright orange, the lime is a somewhat brighter green than in the traditional office version, and the strawberry is pink. Each cube has a small Post-It logo on the front so you know from which corner to peel the next sheet. And each label sticks well to any appropriate surface. I've added these to my basement workshop where they stand out nicely on a particleboard or punchboard surface.

These clips are okay for general use around your house, unless, of course, you need something fancy. I didn't pay too much, so I didn't expect too much. The paint colors  on the clips are on the dull side and some of the clips were painted closed and a few needed some finger muscle to open them, which is why I gave it only 4-stars. For what I need them for, they will do the job as I'm not too fussy about clipping things for my own use. The price was good and for most people that can still use their fingers, these will be a good buy.  +JMJ+

The Plusses:>Clean design for calendar; available with white frame>Size: Neither too big nor too small for use in many spaces in home office, kitchen, elsewhere in home.>Good size for one person's calendar notations>Nice that you can write on it with dry marker, use magnets, and have option (if you hang it) of pinning stuff on bottom bar of cork.Post-its seem to stick fairly well to surfaces.>>cleans easily with only a dry tissue or paper towel; no residual ink on surface. (Don't know if that's because of markers we used or the surface material or a combination of both.)The Negatives:>>Cheaply made, especially the frame>>Can only hang via use of sticky squares that come with it. Not good for some surfaces (messes the surface) and will not hold on other surfaces>>Unless you've got a very thin pointed dry marker, you can't write much on the squares>>Cork section is useless unless you are hanging this unit somewhere rather than leaning it against something.But the reason it only got three stars?The dry marker it came with, and the others we tried with it, produced mushy/blurred text  on the very shiny surface. Also, they came out very light and fading no matter who used the dry markers or how hard they pressed. Suggest trying different markers because the one that came with it is useless. (On the upside, there is no ghosting of ink when you remove what you've added.)

There isn't too much to write about when it comes to labels.  They print well, and the toner sticks to them -- you don't get those horrendous looking labels where the letters look like they have the plague.  And, while I'm sure they're not environmentally perfect, these are more "green" than the traditional labels.  All in all, they're a good choice if you need to print loads of mailing labels.  (Great for the holidays!)

The standard packaging provides an AC adapter, black on white label cartridge, and USB cable.  However, the evaluation unit was also accompanied by five additional packages of labels to show the versatility of this particular system: clear transparent, iron on, ribbon, glow in the dark, and strong adhesive.The unit has a power port, USB port, and security cable point.  The bottom of the housing accommodates for 6 AA alkaline batteries.  Pairing was simple but I do recommend downloading the Application from the AppStore if you're using an Apple product.Placing the cartridge inside is intuitive and simple.  Just open the compartment and place the cartridge inside, and guide the tape end to the slot.The versatility comes from being AC or battery power.  It can function as a desktop device or fit into a briefcase or backpack.So many permutations and possibilities for making labels.  Handwritten labels, numerous script designs, numerous icons and even a QR code.  The iron on ribbon is a great idea, as are clear labels or glow in the dark labels.  Using the Epson Label App, downloaded for free from the App Store without In App Purchase options is good (at least as of this writing).Contacts from your address book can be printed onto mailing labels.  You can print party ribbons with creative designs, and you can even incorporate a photo from your Photo album.Printing speed is respectable, though I have no metric upon which to base this.  It is also relatively quiet in operation.OverallThis is a well designed and versatile system for anyone who wants to be organized, has creativity or just needs to have limitless options.Highly recommend.

I have a couple of other dry erase boards and regularly buy dry erase markers. I was excited to try this sheet of paper sized board. Unfortunately, I'm just not impressed. The neon markers are a nice dice idea, but in practice the markers fall short of the graphic shown to market this product. The aluminum frame is very flimsy and subject to easy denting, and the back is not quite the same material as my other boards, so it could easily be subject to water damage. No eraser is included either. A small cloth would have been a nice touch.I would buy a neon dry erase board in the future as long as the markers are greatly improved. For now, it's a fun product but not something I would recommend at this time.

This printer is such a job and is hooker up wirelessly to our laptops, desktops, ipads.  It can print, copy, and scan plus print photos directly from the memory card out of your camera.  The menu screen is easy to read and although the image of what photo your are printing is small, you still get a good enough idea.  You can use different size paper and use color or black and white.  It has never jammed on us which is amazing considering all the paper jams we've had with our other printer.  We are very pleased with this printer and all it can do.  It can handle all the needs of our busy household and college students.  I don't think it would be able to handle a busy office, but just fine for home office or family use.
Easy way to keep your Shredder working for the long haul without messy oils.  Try the Paper method and you`ll be convinced for sure.

I generally use an Aeron desk chair, admittedly a more expensive unit than this HON, and one I'd expect to be more comfortable given the cost. On the positive side of the balance sheet, the HON has a comfortable seat, and I found the back to be nicely supportive. The tension of the back, however, cannot be adjusted as it is based entirely upon the strength of the plastic frame. Users on the heavier side might find the tension too light and without enough lumbar support. So the back is perfect for the lighter occupant. On the other hand, the overall seat is designed for a, uh, wider individual whose arms will fall at a certain width supported by the armrests. I found my arms falling inside the armrests which are not adjustable in that direction but only vertically.Construction is very good and the unit moves up and down smoothly and easily, rolling nicely across both carpeted and hardwood surfaces. The arms are mounted using two bolts apiece; it wasn't obvious to me which way they went on, and after seeing that they slanted down, I realized I had mounted them in reverse. It was easy enough to swap them.Not surprisingly, I'm staying with my Aeron, but for a person with the right fit, the HON is a perfectly satisfactory desk chair.

I pulled this tray set out of the box, cut off the tag, put them on my husband's desk and viola!  He's a happy camper.  He likes the mesh and the fact the trays feel and look like quality (probably because they are).  They will give him years of satisfaction.

This take is very strong, does not stretch much at all, and the glue seems weaker than on other types of packing tapes that I have used. It is quite thin, cuts easily by scissors and may be torn by hand after making a small initial cut on the side. It can serve as a decent packing tape IF you wrap it around the box, i.e. ends of tape wrapped around a box shoud overlap a few inches. It does adhere somewhat to cardboard, but I would not feel comfortable assuming that this will hold: when I pulled it off, small cardboard fibers did stick to the tape, but I did not have to apply any considerable effort me peel it.

In today's world a product not only has to perform well, but it also must be environmentally friendly.  I'm happy to say that the Fellowes boxes meet the first criteria, but I have my doubts about the second over the longrun.First, let me say these are the easiest boxes I ever put together.  They literally come in one unit and are pre-scored so all you do is a few hand motions and they are ready for action.  They are solidly built, not at all like those cheap boxes you find at the office supply stores.  I'd have no worries about loading heavy books or even glassware into these boxes.  In the durability and ease-of-use category they score a solid A.However, I am concerned about the "tab" closure and what it means to the re-usability of the boxes.  After using the tabs a few times I found they were quickly losing their strength and ability to stay in the handles.  I have this feeling that after a few uses these boxes will no longer be able to stay closed, which means that they are not good for more than a few uses or for storing things that might need to be accessed say every year (like Christmas decoration).  I would like to see them redesign this part of the box to make it more durable so it encourages people to reuse instead of throw away.

I have a lot of pens, pencils, and markers that I use for making greeting cards.  This pencil cup is plenty big enough to hold all that I need for a project (I only take out the items I need at the time).

This shredder cuts paper and credit cards into pieces that are each about 1/8" by 1".  It also has a slot for optical disks (CD/DVD/etc) that cuts the disk into 3 pieces. The label with be easily legible after shredding, but the data will be destroyed.The waste bin has a clear window on the front that allows you to easily check when it's time to empty it. There is also a removable tray inside that catches the CD pieces, keeping them separate from the paper.Following the guidelines to make sure you only feed 10 sheets at a time, this shredder has never jammed on me. You really need to be sure to remove paper clips to prevent damage to the blades. I have not had an issue running staples through it, but the manual recommends removing those as well to prolong the life of the blades.This is a pretty good shredder, and the only reason I took away a star was due to its power. It really means what it says about 10 sheets at a time - any more than that and the blades can get stuck. That means that if you have an envelope with 3 pieces of paper inside that are folded twice, then the envelope and it's contents amount to a thickness of 11 sheets of paper, so the shredder will probably get stuck while shredding it. That means many pieces of mail need to be opened and unfolded prior to shredding, which may or may not matter to you.

I tested these on multiple surfaces and they perform just as ultra fine "S brand" permanent markers but they come in 36 different colors.  On some surfaces, like waxed milk cartons, the text bubbles up and appears to stay wet but it does dry after a few seconds just like the S brand markers and will not smudge once dry.  These are not intended for standard paper and they will bleed through but if you are looking for fine point permanent markers in many colors, these are the ticket.
I ordered this to put on my stainless steel fridge and it has worked out perfect.  It doesn't stand out and blends in with the decor.
well thought out and can be stuck via magnet to a fridge/cabinet or hung with hooks. I like that it's stable enough to be stood upright on its own as well to boot.

Choosing a printer depends on what you are using it for and how much you want to spend.  For me this printer does not do anything special and is a bit pricey. Yes it prints, copies, faxes, scans and has duplex--but so does most other printers at equal or lower price.Now if you are looking for a compact printer, then this takes up very little space.If you will be printing lots of pages, then this is not ideal as the paper tray is very small.Like most of the newer Epsons, you can set it up and connect to your network directly from the printer touch screen.  Just have your network password.  Once the network is set up, then you need to acquire the printer driver on your computer.  Overall, the set-up is easy and takes less than half an hour.Finally, for the print quality, it is as good as any other Epson product (which I feel is excellent.)

This is not of the same quality as the Kensington foot rest.  I now have both it and this one.It is a smaller version and does not have the same range of motion and comfortable gel foot pads.BUT, it is far cheaper.So in balancing the function versus the price it is a very acceptable solution to leg pain when working for prolonged periods at a computer desk.I was needing another foot rest at my L shaped computer desk but did not want to pay the high price of the Kensington model.When balancing the cost and usability of this foot rest I am pleased with my purchase.  It provides most of the same qualities of the more expensive options.  It is worth the price asked and I find it to be restful.

and these sheet protectors fill the bill. I've used sheet protector for years for my recipe binders but I never cared about the quality or their being acid free until now. I used to buy them at discount, in dollar stores, etc. since all I cared about was convenience and protection from splatters.Recently, a friend lost over 500 GB of family photos when his external hard drive failed. (He has sent it to a service that might be able to salvage something for big $$$, let's see how that goes). Anyway, it has brought to my front burner something I've been considering for years: making prints and real, old-fashioned albums out of my many digital scans and captures so I can leave something physical for my grandchildren. I know how much I value my old family photos and have always worried that, somewhere down the pike 'jpg' may not be something that my grandchildren can view (assuming the hard drives don't fail before then and future computers can still read them (remember floppy disks?)What I'm doing is going through every folder on every hard drive and selecting the best images to print. I have four big three ring binders: one for us; one for my son; one for my daughter; and one for "others" (photos I print to give away to people who appear in them). The top size I will print is 8x10 (which fits in the sheet protector), some 5x7's and most are 4x6. Each sleeve (sheet protector) becomes the storage for a bunch of photos for an event, date, or category and I have some sleeves with only one photo but some contain more than 15 of various sizes. These sleeve protectors are heavier-duty than the usual and the holes don't strain or stretch because they are full/heavy.At this point, I am in select, edit, and print mode. I haven't yet hit the 1/4 done mark, and haven't even started to make albums, so the photos will need to stay there for a long while and it's a relief to know that they are well protected and won't lose quality. The whole project may take a couple of years (or more) and, since neither printing nor archival albums are inexpensive, I have to pace myself and budget.  But I'm glad that--at last--I started and that I found these sleeves that give me  peace of mind.

This product almost delivers on its promises:1. The labels are fully adhesive and they are really useful.2. They stay in place and you can remove them cleanly.3. The non-stick tab makes it easy to lift.BUT...1. The 3 individual packets of labels easily detached from the main package. Handling the pad then becomes cumbersome if you want to keep the 3 units together.2. The non-stick tab sometimes rips apart from the main label and then the label becomes not so easy to lift.You can work around issue #1 by dealing with each pad independantly. Issue #2 is not a big deal, just a minor annoyance.Suggestion to Avery: Fix these 2 issues and you have a 5 stars product.

I've always hated lead pencils. I never met a lead pencil I liked untill now. My husband uses the Bic disposables all the time. They're everywhere, here, there, everywhere, every room in the house. They're in continual use for statistics for Fantasy baseball that my husband is consumed with.. Whenever I've used a  Bic  pencil the lead broke off as soon as soon as I put any pressure on it. Just starting to write was enough to break the point off. This doesn't happen with this Papermate.. A very first EVER. Maybe I have a heavy touch but that has been my experience. This #2 color is  very dark compared to other #2 Bics. Maybe it's because I can finally use it. The eraser is absolutely perfect! No smudges and immediate erasure. They are reason alone to buy this product.. The large individual erasers on sale with school supplies should be as good.  Wrapping an extra strip of plastic where you hold the pencil to make the grip more comfortable was ingenious. Such a simple idea for such added comfort. I love the bright colors. Of course the double eraser is a GREAT bonus and so are the bonus erasers . This is a wonderful new improvement on an old product. The only improvement I can think of is selling a package of ten at a reduced price..This took too many years in coming. This superior quality is very welcome and now I will actually use a lead pencil and know I can erase incase I make a mistake which I could never do before as I only used ball points for all my notes. Priced very reasonably and worth every penny. Attractive packaging..  I thank Papermate for this new improvment.  I think it will make all other existing disposable mechanical pencils obsolete! I thank Amazon for having this for me to try and making me into a lead pencil convert.UPDATE:Sept.25,2012 We liked these pencils so much I just received my reorder of 12 more. Paper Mate Quick Flip 0.5MM Mechanical Pencils, 12 Orange Barrel Pencils (1808786) You get 12 pencils for $10.30 which is an extra 4 pencils compared to 2 sets of this starter set. There are no spare erasers but I rather have the 4 extra pencils. They are also available in Blue.

My talents for labeling just took a leap! This device makes labels that make my work look good. A giant step from the amatuer looking labels of old.But! Keep the manual handy... a lot of options need guidence... But it's all there!

I often end up trimming a Post-It so that I have a note just as big as the sticky strip on back, for times when I don't want a flap hanging loose.  Now, I can just use this product!  And it is available in a variety of colors!  I'll be back for one of each color...
Much nicer than even the other quartet markers I reviewed.  I also like that they are slim as I was never a fan of the fatter markers.

Label makers have come a long way, and Epson has been on top of this game for quite a while.  A reasonable cost for something that does so much.  Though it has many features, you are not overwhelmed with the fear of having to learn technical functions.  Very user friendly, and once you get the hang of it, and all it has to offer, you will be having fun making labels for many occasions.  The font styles and sizes are plenty, but now with mini clip-art and decorative features, it makes a more professional or creative looking label.  You can even print text the long way up the tape.Other appealing aspects are the variety of tapes available. The LabelWorks system has various colors, but also have metallic and clear tapes.  The most welcomed addition is the iron on fabric tape.  Perfect for laundry ID, necklines of shirts, inseams and more.The keyboard is large enough and feels like a standard set of keys.  A little getting used to with choosing various art and design, but every key is coded for easy reference.

These dividers are pretty awesome. They're very durable for one and the colors really pop! I love that it is an assortment of patterns and that you don't have to purchase separate packs to get a variety. The quality surprised me because they look so paper thin online but they're really durable!

This is a good product, but they will dry out or not work properly if left in this set, unless you turn it on its side.  I suggest removing them and placing them in a drawer or shelf in an area that does not get too warm or cold.

This sharpener makes a fine point on good pencils, captures the shavings in a little tank (though it will spill on you if you let it overload, best to clean out every couple uses), but struggles with lower quality pencils and colored pencils -- at least my unit anyway.  It is a good office product when pencils are not of primary use. A good home product, but the stand, casing, and performance would not make it a great buy for a heavy use setting, like a school or office where pencil driven note taking or drafting is mandatory.

At first, it didn't turn on. Turns out the provided batteries were dead. After replacing them, it works well enough - the receiver/flash drive pushes out of a slot in the back, plugs into your PC, and you're all set. There are controls to advance and rewind, start and stop, plus the laser pointer. The receiver flashes green when all's well, flashes yellow when battery's low.It's comfy shape and weight plus rubberized finish make it a fun little gadget that's a great idea. However, the price point may be a teensy bit high.
These tabs work great and are very durable. I use them in a budgeting and coupon binder and I haven't had any problems with them ripping or anything. Great dividers!

These are good to affix photos and cards on a surface that does not really matter.I tried them on the metal side of a filing cabinet where I have always stuck up pictures and cards.  These are neater and more useful than your standard cellophane tape, but if you have that tape on hand, it may just be easiest to use it.I originally thought these might be good to hang framed pictures or papers on the wall, instead of using nails, etc, but they will not do that as they cannot support the weight.If you have a lot of little things to put up on a surface that is relatively impervious and hardy, these can do the trick and get that job done. I would neither ask nor expect them to do more.

I use the printer on a wireless network and the printing is agonizingly slow.  The printer also drinks ink at a tremendous rate, and when the gray runs out, it has to be ordered on the Internet because stores do not carry it! I've used Canons for years, but the last three printers I purchased from Canon were unwieldy setting up with Macs, drank ink like a drunk, and now this one uses a cartridge that is impossible to find except online. I'm looking for a different brand. I'm sick of Canon's gouging me on ink.

The QuietSharp isn't what I'd call quiet or sharp.  Since the sound isn't as harsh as some other pencil sharpeners, I won't grumble too much about the "quiet" part of the name, but the "sharp" part is a point (pun intended) of contention.  The guide doesn't line up with the blade precicely, so pencils are sharpened off center more often than not. And a lop-sided pencil has to be resharpened more often (since the point runs into the wood quickly on the short side ). If you used this in a classroom, there would be a nearly constant line of kids waiting to sharpen and re-sharpen their pencils.Two handed operation is required to achieve acceptable results (you have to hold the device in order to maintain the necessary pressure and alignment).  It might work better if the working bits of the sharpener were turned 90 so that the pencil was inserted at the top.  The glow feature is a nice feature for those who think neon kits on cars are cool.It does have a generous well to hold shavings, and it doesn't take up too much room.  The bottom line is that I keep this sharpener around to use when my hands are too tired or achy to twist the old-fashioned manual one (which does a superior job), and I wouldn't recommend it for classroom use.

Yet another so-so message board. I appreciate the slim line as it keeps from protruding off the wall much, and the mounting kit was adequate without being phenomenal (I had to use a different drill bit than recommended to set the anchors). My bigger complaint is that the surface doesn't wipe clean so easily, and the tack cork board is very shallow so things fall off easily if bumped or brushed. Even still, it's functional and a good size so I can't complain too much.

What I like about this label maker:--Many options for typeface and type size--Relatively easy to figure out what the various buttons do--Works fast--Doesn't waste expensive label tape--Easy to make multiple copies of the same labelWhat I don't like about it:--The type quality could be better--I still haven't figured out how to store a frequently used label, although that's one of its most appealing featuresStill, overall a good product.

The set up of this Laser Pointer presenter was very quick and easy, despite of the fact that it was the first time I had ever used one.First, the design is fantastic-the USB wireless part stores inside the presenter (slides in back), so it's not easily lost or broken. It's sleek, fit in my hand nicely and was very easy to use. It is a high-quality, nice glossy construction and felt substantial in my hand.I created a 5 slide mock presentation with PPT and was able to move between slides with ease with the controller. I did notice that the green laser 'fell out' a few times when I pointed at the slides, but that may have had more to do with the color of the background of the slides (green). The controller itself is streamlined with 'back', 'forward', 'power' and 'pointer' buttons, and I clicked through the presentation quickly and effectively.Completely random 'aha' use, but our cats also enjoyed the laser pointer.The set comes with a nice hard shell case, and batteries. Highly recommended-will certainly use for work if needed.
I've bought quite a few binders in my time. The outside plastic looks quite cheap and the edge is very sharp. The D-ring does seem to move smoothly though. Would not buy more.

As a teacher and tutor, one issue I see students facing is with organization. Some of them tend to favor the cheaper notebooks that don't have perforated sheets so that when they tear out pages, it leaves a big mess or leaves shredded bits of paper in the metal spiral that holds the notebook together.Those problems can be easily solved with this high-quality, sturdy notebook from Mead, a brand I've trusted for many years to provide good quality office supplies. The notebook comes with five sections and contains 200 sheets that have been pre-punched (3-hole). The sheets are perforated and tear easily without leaving any mess. The notebook also contains a high quality plastic front and back which will ensure it won't fall apart easily during the school year. There is also a handy exterior loop for holding a pen. The color-coded tabs aid with organization. Overall, this is an excellent notebook and my only reservation here is the rather steep price.

These are your typical lined 3x5 index cards that are good for writing notes for speeches, taking notes in class, using them for flashcards, etc. However, these are thinner than cardstock and than typical index cards. They are also immensely overpriced. one pack contains 100 cards, and amazon currently prices them at $4.20. at my local Staples, I can buy as set of the most expensive Staples-brand cards for $1.99, and they are usually on sale for 50 cents to 99 cents.I was unable to see or feel anything about these cards that would warrant such a huge price differential -- buy the Staples or OfficeDepot brand for your needs.Better yet, if you are in a pinch, take a 8x11 sheet of paper, fold it in half, then fold it in half again. Now, fold it in half one more time. You should now unfold it -- you'll have eight squares. Rip the piece of paper into 8 squares -- there you have your flashcards or your notecards. No need to shell out extra money. You are welcome!

My Cannon Pixma MP780 finally gave out after five or six years of good use. I didn't need all the features on the MX850 but it looked like the next generation MP780 so I decided to purchase it.I believe this printer will give me many years of reliable performance. The reason I say this is that my old Cannon Pixma MP780 is literally in three major pieces now. I disassembled this earlier generation Cannon to see how well it was put together and I was impressed with the internal workmanship of this line of printers possess. I believe the MX850 has this quality of workmanship and it also.I was also pleasantly surprise at how fast the new printer prints.I'm hoping that the new printer will allow me to refill its inks cartridges without getting an error message. I was able to do this on theCannon Pixma MP780 fairly easily and it saved me a lot of money life for the printer. These printer cartridges appear to be the same size but they have a chip which concerns me a bit.The only reason I did not give this printer a five star rating is because my lack of experience with it. I believe five years from now I'll be a link of this printer 10 star rating if that were possible.

What can one write about tape?  On the surface tape has one quality that we care about the most -- does it stick?  You can then elaborate on that by asking a series of other questions such as how hard is it to remove?  Does it leave any marks on the surface?  Is it clear or does it show? I have used several printers, including several all-in-ones, over the years. The three main brands that I've owned include HP, Epson and Canon. They each have their own set of perks and qualities, and overall the functionality and quality of printers have steadily improved over the years. I am still slightly partial to HP printers overall, but this Canon printer definitely has many things going for it. Below are some of my main observations.**** Look and Build ****If you are looking for an all-in-one that will help you reduce the clutter in your office or home, then this one is definitely not for you. It weighs over 30 pounds and occupies a significant amount of desktop real estate. It is however a very solidly built and generally very reliable printer.**** Setup ****The setup was relatively straightforward and pain-free. However, some of the more advanced functions are a bit hard to figure out how to do. The user manual is not of much help here.**** Connectivity ****A Wi-Fi printer connection nowadays seems like a must, and most printers that I've come across in recent years seem to have it as a standard option. This printer easily found my home network. I also appreciate the fact that it has AirPrint as a standard option. My household is heavily reliant on iOS devices and it feels wonderful to be able to print from any one of them.**** Printing ****This is definitely one of the best features of this all-in-one. The print quality is really high for a printer of this caliber, especially when it comes to photo printing. You can comfortably print pictures up to 8.5 x 11 and get some really astonishing results. However, the color printing uses up a lot of ink, and if you don't need the prints immediately, getting them printed online is still a much more affordable option.Printing is also relatively fast, although it takes the printer some good half a minute to wake up for the first print.**** Scanning ****I've only scanned a few documents so far and have generally been impressed with results. However, scanning is very slow and be prepared to wait quite a bit to get your pictures digitized.**** Fax ****So far I have not used the fax feature. You would have thought that by now faxing would have gone the way of VHS tapes, but certain professions (I am looking at you medical professionals) still insist on having most of their official documents faxed to them. So it's a good feature to have for a once-in-a-while faxing need.**** Overall Impressions ****If you are in the market for a powerful all-in-one yet are still budget conscious, then you will not go wrong with buying this device. However, it is really bulky and some of the functions are not as fast and nimble as I would have liked.

Long have I pined for a heavy duty stapler!  Now all my stapler-related dreams can come true!  I don't need it for an office environment, but I play video games as a hobby, and I often print out long FAQs for them (I know I could use a laptop or an ipad or whatever, but I just prefer the look and feel of printed paper).  For many years, I'd struggled to staple together large packets of 20-30 pages with a normal sized stapler.  I'd always be frustrated by bent staples and lack of penetration through all the pages, and I'd have to try several times before I'd get a decent staple through.  I'd always wanted to buy a heavy duty stapler, but for one reason or another, I never got around to it.  This was mostly because I was afraid a decent heavy duty stapler would cost a fortune.  So, after a particularly frustrating packet of paper, I finally broke down and decided to research staplers with the intent of purchasing one.After looking at a couple different options and seeing the nice affordable Swingline Optima 70 with it's good reviews, I decided on getting it.  First off, I love the fact that it only uses one type of staple.  I wasn't relishing the idea of having three different specialized staple sizes and I don't need to staple anything bigger than 70 sheets, so the Swingline Optima 70 was a great choice.  For anyone wondering, yes, it does take special staples (Swingline Optima High Capacity Staples, part#35550), but at least it works with one one type of staple for anywhere from 2 to 70 sheets.  Plus, the staples are pretty inexpensive.  I also like the size.  I know some people have complained that the stapler is huge, but compared to the monstrous staplers I've seen at my college, I'd say that it's actually pretty compact for what it can do.  In case anyone wants definite measurements, here they are: it's about 9.5 inches long and 6 inches high at its highest point.  I suppose I could comment on  the appearance and build of the stapler too.  It's nicely designed with a comfortable handle, and the plastic it's constructed of seems to be pretty sturdy.  I do like the grey and black color scheme, but I kind of wish it didn't have that big orange bottom as it sort of reminds me of a Fisher Price toy, but who really cares about appearance so long as it works.As for the actual performance of the stapler, it's excellent.  First off, if you want to open the stapler to load the staples, you need to press the button on the back and then pull the tray out.  After doing this, I tested it on a packet of 25 papers.  It performed admirably, punching through all of them cleanly and folding the staple nicely at the ends (the staple folds the ends in such a way that they are not parallel like a normal stapler, but it still holds beautifully).  Also, the claim on the box that this is a "reduced effort" stapler are 100% true.  I was shocked by how much easier it is to push down than my old standard stapler.  I don't have arthritis or wrist problems or anything, but it's a nice feature nonetheless.  I next tested it on a full packet of 70 pages, and it held, but the staple was very close to the ends.  Still, it was a firm, solid hold.  Lastly, I tested it on the simple 2 pages it's purported to work on, and it was decent, but a bit loose.  I'll definitely continue to use my normal standard stapler for very small packets of paper and only whip this one out for large packets.  This may annoy someone who was wanting to use this as their 100% everything stapler, but for me, it's fine.So, my conclusions are that for the price and the performance, this is an excellent heavy duty stapler.  The only thing that might hold you back is if you intended to use it for very small size documents as well, in which case it serviceable, but not as great.  Still, this is probably the best heavy duty no-fuss stapler you can get in this price range, so I'd highly recommend it to anyone with large stapler needs.

ProsSingle-piece cartridgeSmall desktop footprintTwo press WPS connectionConsNo duplex printNo XL cartridge optionNo paper tray coverAre you thinking what I'm thinking?  Why in the world is Samsung making printers.  OK, I thought never judge a book by its cover so I decided to give this a try.  We run a business so have printer ranging from HP, Epson and Dell printers, inkjet to laser printing.The Samsung Xpress M2070W is neat and angular, with all its curves in the vertical direction. The flat lid to the scanner - there's no Automatic Document Feeder (ADF)...wait say WHAT no ADF, not a deal breaker but this should be pretty standard with an all in one printer. Built into the lid is the NFC sensor, so you can tap your mobile device onto the most accessible part of the printer.In front of the scanner is the control panel, with a two-line, mono LCD display, a navigation ring and large buttons to start and stop jobs and to switch the machine into stand-by mode immediately.There are four buttons to the left of the display, too, which provide quick access to the Scan to function and to the printer's Eco mode, which saves toner, can print multiple pages per sheet and manually duplex. Nice layout, I like it.Samsung Xpress M2070W - Connection and InstallationKnow what cool?  3 letters NFC.  What's the big NFC thing about, then? Near Field Communication (NFC) is a connection protocol for wireless devices, based on Radio Frequency IDentification (RFID) technology.In a printing application it gets around the need to search for a printer from your mobile device and pair with it before printing. As long as your mobile device supports NFC - many recent Android phones and tablet do, but Apple devices don't - you can just touch the device to the Samsung Xpress M2070W's scanner lid, in the front left-hand corner.The necessary details are then transferred automatically between device and printer, so printing can begin immediately. All this, without affecting the security of any network the printer might be connected to. Tried it with a Samsung Galaxy and it worked perfectly. The connection can be remade using the WPS button on the printer or by tapping the phone on the scanner lid again.  For you Apple devices as we do, unsurprisingly, the M2070W doesn't support Apple's AirPrint either. However, there is a Samsung Mobile app for iOS devices and we had no trouble setting this up with our iPhone and iPad, so there's no real reason why owners of Apple devices couldn't use the M2070W in their offices.  If your smartphone isn't made by Apple or Samsung then the M2070W also supports Google's CloudPrint as well, so it covers most of the bases for mobile printing. AWESEOME!Print SpeedsSamsung claims a healthy speed of 20ppm for the Xpress M2070W and we saw 17.1ppm on our 20-page document under test, which is respectably close. The 5-page text test gave 11.1ppm, but this is a still a good speed for a relatively inexpensive printer. The 5-page text and graphics print achieved the same speed of 11.1ppm.A single-page copy took only 9s and 15 x 10cm photos on A4 took 18s from a PC and only a second longer from the Galaxy Young. All these are very good speeds.Print Quality and CostsThe print quality is average throughout. Text is crisp and light black, as are areas of black fill. Greyscales are generally smooth, though some tone levels are difficult to distinguish, even though representing different colors. Photos are surprisingly well reproduced, though there is some fine banding visible in areas of sea and sky in our test prints.Should I buy a Samsung Xpress M2070W?The simple answer is, yes. If you want a three-in-one (no fax on this machine), which prints simply from a computer or a mobile device.VerdictThe Samsung Xpress M2070W is the first machine of a new range from the company, which looks to have matched connection innovation with pretty good print quality and good print speed. There are a few things missing, like duplex print and a multi-function feed slot, but it still offers a lot of SOHO functionality in a neat case and at a neat price.

My wife and I used a previous Brother printer so heavily for years that we had practically beaten it to death.  We were amazed at its durability for the price and it owed us nothing when it finally died.  Therefore, when it came time for a replacement, we chose this Brother model.  We liked its compact size, printing speed and paper-saving optional duplexing and a design that does not require throwing away the drum with every empty toner cartridge.  Brother brand replacement drums are rated for about 12,000 copies and cost about $70.  Third-party "re-manufactured" drums cost about 1/3 as much.  Brother support has been very good.  This printer has a couple of quirks that keeps me from giving it five stars, however.Quirk #1:  Whether I'm using Brother brand toner cartridges or third-party cartridges, the printer starts giving "toner-out" warnings long before toner in the cartridge is actually gone.  Unless I've gone into the printer's configuration page and set the printer not to stop when it "thinks" that the toner is exhausted, the printer will refuse to make more copies.  Aside from running up the cost of printing, it's wasteful to discard a cartridge that still has plenty of toner in it simply because the printer counted the copies made from the cartridge and "decided" that it should be replaced.  There is a widely circulated "hack" that resets the printer's cartridge count thereby allowing users to run copies until the cartridge is actually empty.  I believe that most people if they're not purists would be satisfied to simply use a cartridge until the pages become faint.Quirk #2:  The manual feeder on the front of the printer works well for labels and heavy paper that would not ordinarily be fed from the paper tray as long as the labels or heavy paper are a standard 8 1/2 X 11 or 8 1/2 X 14 paper size.  Opening the back of the printer for such manual-feed jobs provides a straight paper path.  Odd-size paper and #10 envelopes will print nicely via the manual feed, but once such paper has gone through the printer, the printer will display an error message.  To reset the error the printer must be turned off and then back on.I have found the print quality to be respectable and the print cost-per-page to be reasonable.  Paper feed for this printer has been reliable for me.  There is a separate removable paper tray in the bottom that the printer uses for duplexing.  After the printer prints one side of the paper, it flips the paper into the bottom tray and then prints the other side from that tray.  Paper jams are rare; occurring on average less than once per thousand pages and are easy to clear once you find all of the places in the printer where jammed paper can hide.In summary, if you can deal with the two minor quirks, this printer is reliable and delivers a lot of value for the price.  It's much faster and less expensive to operate than inkjet printers in the same price range.  We like this printer well enough to now own two of them.

For more versatility, initiate the scan from the Epson Scan software on your computer where you can tweak color, resolution, contrast, etc prior to scanning.  Either function works wirelessly.I haven't owned the printer long enough to comment on its durability.  In general, let me mention that the first printer I ever bought cost $400 and lasted me about 7 years.  Today's printers do ten times as many things but they are not built to last, especially at this price point.  I expect to get a couple of years use out of this before something on it fails, by which time I'd probably want to upgrade anyway.A word of advice about ink, I've had experience with 3 other models of Epson printers and they do not handle refilled, non-OEM ink cartridges very well.  You'll get a barrage of error messages when you attempt to install your cheap ink cartridge and even if you get past those, your print quality will be terrible.  Re-manufactured ink is so tempting because of the price difference, but I am convinced that it has killed at least 5 printers in our office over the years.  Buy the name brand ink, print something at least once a week to keep it from drying out and your printer will last a lot longer.

While this was a good price for the pack,the first one I used kept slipping off track. After several "repairs", I decided it was just a defective item. I agree with most of what I have read.  This is a fast printer.  I had no trouble setting it up.  I didn't use the disk. Printing an 8 x 10 for a frame is great.  The scanner is fast and easy to use.  A negative is the lack of a feeder.  This limits its use for a fax machine.  I would definitely consider paying more for that.  There isn't a plug for a telephone line, also limiting its use as a fax. We love these and our on our 2nd set of two of these. They last a few years and are good quality. The traction is great, easy use, small but not too small to navigate, and easy on the wrist.

I've been through quite a few shredders. They typically don't last very long--a jam too many and the motor burns out. The Fellowes Powershred is the first home-use shredder I've used with Jam Block Technology. I actually tried, unsuccessfully, to block the thing. It resisted or easily reversed the blocked paper out of its jaws.So far I've shredded four basketfuls of paper. The Fellowes powered through nearly everything I threw at it--multi-page handfuls, thick paper, even some plastic.The cross-cutting works well. Sifting through a basket, the documents were well destroyed. I felt confident putting even the most sensitive shreddings into my recycling bin.The shredder is large. It won't be unobtrusive in your home office. But its size means that you empty the basket less frequently, it has a more powerful motor, and is relatively quiet compared to smaller, cheaper models.Emptying the basket is far less frustrating than other shredders I've used. With the Fellowes, you just slide the basket out when a red light indicates it's full. You can take the basket directly to your recycling bin and then slide it back in. (No need to remove the shredder at the top.)

Great smooth writing (no blotches), bold ink, comfortable and aesthetically pleasing pen. As a picky pen person I WOULD recommend it to friends and families (and aliens too ... if I was every abducted and the aliens needed to borrow my pen).

Often I am in another part of the house when using my tablet computer or lap top when I want to print something. I have bought any number of this style of floor mat over the years (never from amazon) and the problem is that they either arrive dirty or packaged so that they curl up when on the floor. They can be washed and some of them have been the same finish on the top and bottom so it hasn't mattered, but it's annoying. Granted, they are a difficult item to ship right given the packaging expense to do it right compared to the low cost of the item.This was a complete exception for me: It arrived in a box about 4 feet tall, and maybe 10 or 12" inches per side. The mat was curled up inside it (though not tightly) and it was curled the right way so that when you put it on the floor it has a slight convex curve that flattens out the moment you put a chair on it. And it was clean.One thing to note is that there is a top and bottom to this (or at least a difference in finishes on the two sides). One side is textured and the other smooth. I assume that the textured side goes on the floor to reduce slippage and the smooth side is to make the chair easier to move. I don't really notice the difference between this and earlier mats I've had that were textured on both sides.Like all of these PVC mats, if you see them at an angle with the light reflecting off them, they are milky/cloudy looking, but if kept clean (and until aged by time and use) looking at them from directly above they look almost transparent.

I love the color assortment of these pens, and the barrel is quite comfortable in my hand - the right size and shape. But the ink flow itself is sort of disconcerting. You know that little tug on the page you get when your ink is running low? That's what I'm talking about. It's probably not enough to bother most people, but if you are sensitive to stuff like that (like I am!) you may want to test one before investing in a pack.

While refilled cartridges seem like a bargain, my side by side comparison showed that the print quality was much poorer. The labels are great.  You can print them with a laser or inkjet printer but only a laser will not bleed if they get wet. I got this printer for my wife (she's something of a technophobe) to get her to use  her digital camera more.  The results were fantastic and still coming. The pen is reasonably priced and comfortable to use. The pen's clear barrel minimizes the possibility of running out of ink at an inopportune time.A personal handwritten note is a nice gift. The software included with this Starter Kit (as others have noted, it is PC only, not Mac) installs quickly & is easy to use.  It allows you to print as many or as few stamps as you need at one time, with a graphical "mapping" feature that allows you to precisely place the stamps you want to print on a sheet of labels, making it simple to print on a partially used sheet.When printing stamps, you have to enter the serial number from the sheet of labels on which you are going to print.  I do not know what problems might ensue if there is a mismatch of serial numbers - it doesn't appear to print the number directly on the stamps - perhaps it is encoded in the digital scan area also printed on each stamp.  Printing itself is easy, but one needs to be careful when printing, as your [...] account balance is debited immediately upon printing.  If a sheet is misprinted, a refund request form has to be printed from the software & mailed in to receive the refund as a credit to your [...] account.  Purchasing additional postage is a snap - you select an amount (in multiples of $10), the credit card you used to establish your account is charged, and your [...] account balance is immediately credited.As others have noted, the free postage offer is a bit misleading as stated on the packaging of the starter kit, but is spelled out clearly enough on Amazon's description.There is a lesser expensive $9.99 per month "personal" account option (as opposed to the $17.99 per month "business" account option which is the least expensive option you are presented with when installing the software & establishing your [...] account) - you have to call their toll-free number to switch to it.  But, yet and still, unless convenience alone is worth $10 a month, I feel you need to mail a considerable number of items a month to justify the expense.  Certainly many businesses would be able to justify the expense, but I can't for personal, home use.  If I was an active eBay seller for example, or the owner of a small business, I would definitely continue the service, as I enjoyed using the software and printing my stamps while I had the free trial.  As it is, however, I will cancel my service as I do not use it enough.  If they offered a $5 per month option, I would continue using it...

The Epson Artisan 837 Color Inkjet Wireless All-In-One is easily the best printer I have ever owned. I give it a five stars in every category by which I can measure it. In three minutes I printed off a 25-page document and in 30 seconds a photo worthy of any lab I've ever used for photo development. I will never have to send photos elsewhere to be developed but can do them at home assured of the result.I was pleased at the outset with the ease of set up. The directions were clear and easy to follow and everything went exactly as described. The printer did not come with a USB cable but if you're like me, you have a few of those lying around. There is literally no comparison between the two printers - though I have never been a big Epson fan, the Artisan 837 is superior in every sense. Of course, the printer comes with a set of cartridges to get you started.It's also an attractive printer - shiny blackish (they call it midnight blue) - with a nice fold out touch-screen control panel. It's as beautiful as it is efficient. I can't recommend it enough. You won't need another printer because this one can do it all - print, copy, scan, fax, and of course, photo.

This is probably the best multi-function office machine I've ever owned. It combines pretty much all the usual office gadgets in one unit and makes them better.Setup:It comes with 3 guides: a quick installation and overall guide, a wireless network install quick guide and a CD containing the user's guide and printer software. With so many functions, there is a lot to learn but the good thing is you only need to do this once for your current system.Multi-unit:This unit combines a fax, scanner, printer and copier. This actually makes a lot of sense since each of those functions utilizes the same hardware. For example, the fax, scanner and copier all uses the scanner unit. The fax outputs to the phone line, the scanner outputs to software/editing program, and the copier outputs to paper, etc. Once your paper is scanned, it's just a matter of software how you output it.What makes this unit better than my old combo printer/scanner/fax is that it connects wirelessly to all my computers via my router so I only need one multi-unit instead of several. This is a sure money saver because I won't have to buy ink for all my other devices. And it's even backwards compatible to the old 802.11b devices. And for the first time for me it prints direct from any smartphone or tablet via wifi. I can't remember how many times I'd wish I could print a coupon or something from my phone without having to save it to the computer first.Functions:There are a few nice bells and whistles on this unit. There is an Eco button in grayscale (for drafts), separate toner system, print manager, double sided printing, etc.Quality:Printers have come a long way since the old daisywheels or injets. The quality of the printouts are excellent, the max resolution of this printer is 4800 x 600 dpi.Value:I spent a long time comparing the specs of comparable units from other brands, but it's hard to make a straight comparison comparing exact specs since they are all slightly different. Even the same brand makes several units that differ in only a few regards. What I have found is that this unit has the best print resolution in this price range (at this current moment) but prices do fluctuate and some printers are deeply discounted when a new series is about to come out.Toner prices appear roughly comparable with comparable units. I don't find that toner prices are a big issue with me. At several thousand pages I only change toners at the most once a year and the price differentials become negligible over that amount of time. Toner prices only become an issue with heavy usage. How many pages do you plan on printing and would you get a lower quality printer to save money on toner? Currently there may not be a third party toner for this printer since this printer is new but third parties do make replacement and remanufactured toners for others Samsungs so it's just a matter of time.Overall:An excellent multi-function unit with high quality printouts. It replaces several units in my home. The only thing I cannot tell is how it will stand the test of time; that's an update for another day.

The X-ACTO SharpX Electric Pencil Sharpener is a powerful sharpener intended to handle a lot of work--more an office or school machine than a home machine. It sharpens pencils very quickly and in my experience so far evenly. It has a big drawer for shavings with an LED light that signals when the drawer is full, which is a nice feature. The best feature is that it stops sharpening when it senses the pencil is sharpened: the motor keeps going, but the teeth aren't engaged, so what tells you that the pencil is ready is a slight change in the sound. (Actually, if you're adding LED lights, one that lights up when the pencil is sharpened would be nice.)For the most part, this sharpener is a winner:-- It's powerful.-- It stops sharpening when the pencil is sharp.-- It has a large drawer for shavings that's fairly easily removed.-- The dial for pencil size is easy to adjust.There are negatives, however, which may influence your buying decision:-- When you pull out the drawer you'll inevitably find more shavings under it, perhaps knocked loose from the mechanism as you're pulling out the drawer.-- The  unit has suction cups on the bottom that hold it in place when it's sitting on a kitchen counter (for example), but these won't hold it in place when it's on a wooden surface. You'll then have to hold the unit steady in one hand while you sharpen, which is a bit less convenient.-- The sharpener is *big* and takes up a lot of real estate.-- De gustibus, of course, but in my opinion the sharpener is seriously ugly. I realize, however, that worrying about the attractiveness or not of one's pencil sharpener is probably the epitome of First World problems.In all the most meaningful respects, then, this sharpener does a good job, and it comes recommended.-- Debra Hamel

I had high hopes that I could use this for my various fancy drawing pancils. Alas, it does what so many other mechanical sharpeners have done before - break the lead off just inside the wood. Not all of my pencils are having the problem, but its happening about half the time, with no correlation to temperature or age (the older USA-made pencils are breaking just as often as the newer and more brittle Mexican-made ones).For regular pencils this works fine, with two caveats.  First, there is no automatic stop when the point is sharp, so if you keep pushing, the sharpener will just eat the whole pencil. Second, the non-skid feet are tiny, and only non-skid on a very rough surface. On my granite counter tops the sharpener rotated around the pencil unless I held it down with the other hand (the weight of the batteries does help here somewhat).  Both of these things speak to a powerful sharpener, which this is.(Oh, and if you care about green design, I would note that this has a single blade, like a manual sharpener, with the screw holding it in place clearly visible through the clear plastic, but with no obvious way to replace it.  So once that dulls I guess you throw out the whole thing and start over.).

This Epson XP-310 printer is a great for printing documents and photos. The printer was very easy to set up. It comes with instructions, explaining how to set up the device. The sheet is mostly pictures and you can just follow the pictures since it tells you where certain things are to set up the printer. Make sure you do follow the pictures...I accidentally missed one of the steps in the pictures and had to back up a little bit, but it was no biggie. You set up the printer, install the ink cartilages, prime the ink, and then you can set up the software on a computer. To set up the software on a computer, you can do it wirelessly or with a USB cable. The printer instructions recommend using a USB cable and it is not included with the printer so make sure you have one with you if you do it that way.After installation, I tested the printers many options. I stuck an SD card into the slot from my digital camera and printed pictures from the SD card. You can choose the picture you want to print, the number of copies you want, and you can choose the print quality, type of paper used, and the size. I tested it with both standard quality and best quality. To me, the quality was pretty much the same. I was using photo paper, so it may have been the quality of the photo paper, so maybe other types will affect it. I also connected an iPad to the printer and printed a picture from it quite easily. You go to your photos on your iPad, choose the one you want to print, and then push print. The iPad will ask you to connect to a printer and you just choose the Epson and it starts printing. You can also connect it to your phone and other tablets according to Epson.The printer also has the ability to print notebook paper (both wide and college rule), graph paper, a calendar, and music paper. I thought this to be really neat. The printer can also scan photos and documents onto your computer. You can also copy photos and change the size to your liking by percentage from the printer without doing it on a computer. The settings section for the printer has a place that tells you ink levels, Wi-Fi settings, paper settings, etc.Overall, this is a really good printer and it does a lot for its small size and price. I'll be using it until it dies on me and highly recommend it to those looking for a photo printer.

This 5.5 x 8.5 Avery Binder is small, compact, and has some nice features.Before opening I like the fact that it has the preview pocket (View-Binder) on the front for inserting a label, photo, or other useful information and titling.  This is something I always search for when purchasing a binder.On the inside front cover there is an 8-1/2" x 5-1/4" expandable plastic pocket attached (for now) with a button and loop type closure.  I have a flexible plastic 8" ruler that I received with myThomas Kinkade Painter of Light with Scripture 2013 Hardcover Engagement Calendar.  I never used it with my engagement calendar, but it fits perfectly in this plastic pouch in the Avery Binder.  I have a small tape measure which also fits in the pocket, along with a small calculator.  Best use for the pocket/puch though is to use to retain small size papers, receipts, and business cards to have then handy, but not falling out or sliding around.The down side of the pocket is that the items inside, as well as the poorly designed BUTTON closure, prevent the user from easily writing on the back side of the paper in the notebook.  The conents and button cause the writing surface to be too uneven for writing.  Although I suspect if one only placed papers, receipts, and cards inside the writing surface would be adequate.The type of O Rings used for closure on the binder are attached to the inside back cover of the binder instead of inside the spine of the binder (E-Z turn Rings).  This allows the binder to open flat, but I myself have never liked these rings that attach in this manner.  Being left handed I already fight with the rings on a binder; this location makes the rings even more troublesome when I am trying to right on the paper in the binder.  Other outcomes of binder rings attached in this manner mean the closed binder is 7-1'4" x 9 and the front cover doesn't match the back cover when closed make the binder covers not meet and feel unstable.  This also always causes my pages to be out of place when I close the binder.  The binder rings do close well and the snap open ends work well without too much strength needed to close and open them.Inside the back pocket there is a 3-1/4" deep flat plactic pocket attached.  It is very tight and only the slimmest of items can be inserted.I received this item from the Vine Program which promised filler paper and dividers would be sent with the binder.  There was only the binder.  No paper and no dividers.  In other reviews I note people seem to have a problem finding supplies for the binder.  I have yet to purchase any, but I see that Amazon has a large supply of paper and other items for this binder.Avery Filler Paper, 5.5 x 8.5 Inches, 100 Sheets (14230);Avery Plastic Durable Write-On Dividers, 5.5 x 8.5 Inches, 5 Tabs, 1 Set (16180);5 1/2" x 8 1/2" Pre-printed (Jan-Dec) Monthly Tab Dividers for Small 3-Ring Binder;C-Line Clear Top-Loading Heavyweight Poly 8 1/2 x 5 1/2 Inch Sheet Protectors 50 Count (62058).  I have not actually tried any of these available items; but given their size I see no reason why they would not work fine in this binder.I am trying to find sheets for a 5-1/2 x 8-1/2 binder pre-printed for use as an address book.  I think this size binder would be perfect for an desk top address book because the pages would be replaceable, thus eliminating all the scratching-out and scrunching-in of information that always ends up on the pages of my desk top address book.Overall, if you have the need for a small binder this size - this binder would be fine for your use.  Supplies are available.  The quality seems to be durable.  The cons are not huge.  The price is a bit steep in my opinion for a binder of this size.  But I always think the prices on the items I review for Vine are a bit steep.  Avery has many other 8-1/2 x 5-1/5 binders available on Amazon for lower prices.Avery Durable Binder for 5.5 x 8.5 Inch Pages, 2-Inch Round Ring, Black, 1 Binder (27554);Avery Durable View Binder with 1.5-Inch Slant Ring, Holds 8.5 x 11-Inch Paper, White, 1 Binder (17022);Avery Durable View Binder with 3-Inch Slant Ring, Holds 8.5 x 11-Inch Paper, White, 1 Binder (17042). There are also other brand 8-1/2 x 5-1/2 binders also available on Amazon for lower prices.

This shredder comes well-packaged.  It's so well wrapped that opening the plastic is a small chore. The good thing about that is that the pieces aren't that dusty.  The micro-shredder always produced paper dust which settled in the bottom of the bin. It shreds what it was designed to shred,  and its compact size make it ideal for a small office.

This is the first HON chair I've owned. I know their products have a high reputation and prices to match so I was really looking forward to trying this out. I suspect this is part of their budget line because no way does this seem like an "executive task chair."First thing I noticed when I took the seat and back out of the plastic bag is that they had that new car smell. I like that!Assembly: Most of the other reviewers said assembly was really easy and quick. I would say for the most part I could figure out how to put this together without instructions but it wasn't all that easy because the size of the chair makes it an awkward process.  First of all, like another reviewer, I had trouble putting in the casters. Normally these things go in with some slight pressure and click into place. Not so with this one. It took quite a bit of pressure to make these go into the base and there is no satisfying "click" to let you know they are fully inserted. I didn't want to press too hard for fear of breaking something but I figured that is the only way to do it so I pressed hard and it worked.The instructions tell you to make sure all screws are fully tightened before use. That makes sense but what it should tell you is don't tighten everything until you've connected all the parts together and adjusted the fit. I put the swivel assembly on the seat and tightened it. That was fine. Then I connected the chair back and tightened the bolts. After that, I attempted to put on the arms and found that they did not fit properly. I had to loosen the bolts of the chair back and play around with that in order to be able to make the arms fit. Once the arms were connected, then I checked to make sure everything was straight, and tightened all the bolts.The seat/back assembly is somewhat heavy and that, along with its size, makes it a little difficult to lift up and fit into the base assembly.  It was also awkward trying to properly position the back/seat when connecting things, including the arms because nothing really lays flat. However, in the end everything fit together fine.My wife sat in it first. Her initial remark was that the seat was hard. There's no cushioning. I sat in it and it is quite different from the chair I've been using. The seat feels much harder. I've been sitting in it for a while now and have gotten used to it but if you are expecting something plush, this isn't the ticket.Looks-wise, I doubt if anyone is going to think this is an executive chair unless they are looking at it from a distance. The leather is passable but the chrome looks too shiny for my taste. It swivels fine and the raising and lowering mechanism works fine, too. The seat seems too long for my frame, though (I am 5' 6")so I have trouble sitting back fully to make use of the chair support. The "high back" goes to the middle of my head. I am not tall by any means, so a taller person would not really consider this being high backed.This chair is decent. I quickly got used to the lesser padding and can sit in it for long periods of time and it doesn't get uncomfortable. I still prefer my old chair, though, because of a better fit. I don't feel it is worth the retail price but for Amazon's current price it is okay.

The C309G is not a small printer. The duplex add-on and the front tray take up an enormous amount of room on a desk and you definitely want to take measurements in your small office to make sure it will fit. I've smacked my elbow into it numerous times. Let's start with the basics.The unit does not come with a USB cable, so make sure you have one in the event you do not want to use the Ethernet or WiFi connections. Rest assured, the USB cable isn't needed to connect the printer to the network at all. Everything is set up via software or the touch screen. The LCD touch screen is a very cool feature! The on-screen keyboard isn't QWERTY so it took some time to input the passcode for my WiFi network, but the overall user interface is very sleek and easy to use!When I popped the lid to install the cartridges, I noticed there were no LED's to indicate proper installation of each cartridge like my Canon Pixma MP620. The C309G also makes a steady hissing sound when it is turned on, and you get to hear it for at least 5 minutes during the first initialization of the printer (which is an awful long time to wait when you're anxious to use it).I used the on-board photo printing feature to try out some of the photo paper that was included (100 sheets). The cropping feature is very lackluster and managed to cutoff some of my photographs. It wasn't as flexible in allowing me to crop the photo the way I wanted, and it was hard to tell if the photo quality was going to be good or not, so make sure you use a good camera and take a clear pic. The color reproduction is quite spectacular and the glossy prints look Kodak-quality. I made a few photos for family and they thought I got them developed. The duplex unit worked very nicely but it takes a few moments for the ink to dry before it proceeds printing on the reverse side.The software isn't that great as it takes 15MB or more of memory (not hard drive space) and installs a bunch of IE/FireFox add-ons for no reason. The scanning system works seamlessly as you are able to save directly onto a USB flash drive. Unfortunately the scanner only scans at 300 dpi (fixed setting) and saves as a JPG without any option to store all the images in one session onto one PDF file like my Canon Pixma MP620. This isn't a big deal if you're just scanning photographs from a scrapbook, but I usually scan lots of documents at 150 dpi and it makes it convenient to store 35 pages into 1 PDF rather than store it as 35 JPG's in 300 dpi format.There are some fun maze and puzzles available for print straight from the printer itself. It can print out mazes or Sudoku puzzles (ranging from simple to expert), or other activities right from the touch screen.Pros: Fast printing, individual color tanks, duplex attachment, great photo printing capabilities, onboard WiFi setup, excellent touch screen user interface, and excellent print quality even in the Fast Draft setting.Cons: Takes up a lot of physical space, installation and initialization can take awhile, and the unit makes a hissing noise from the speaker.Overall: Feature-rich printer but I felt my less expensive Canon Pixma MP620 does everything but takes up less room, and has a better scanner interface with the same quality of printing. The really great feature of the HP C309G is the duplex attachment and easier to access paper tray.UPDATE 12-23-2009:A bit of a warning about the ink cartridges:The 564 cartridges don't last very long, specifically the big tank for black ink. After maybe 100-200 print outs, it tells me to buy a new tank. I recommend looking at the 564XL cartridges for higher capacity. They cost more but the standard sized 564 cartridges don't last long at all.
