As a college student, I'm embarrassed to admit how much I was looking forward to receiving this pack of highlighters. I'm already a fan of Sharpie's retractable highlighters, and the added colors were something I was hoping to put to good use.First of all, a few of the colors are less helpful than I'd hoped. The red, dark blue and purple colors are simply too dark for most of my applications, making the text difficult to read. Several of the other colors are a TAD on the dark side but still quite usable. I find the yellow to be the only truly "bright" in the set.Next comes Sharpie's claim that these highlighters will not smear the text. I feel I must add an asterisk here, however. In my experience with these highlighters, they will not smear pre-printed text (i.e.- a textbook) but handwritten notes (in a notebook or in the margins of the textbook) will smear noticeably. This isn't an issue if you are writing large notes, but in the case of smaller writing, or more precise markings such as equations it becomes a problem. Perhaps they made the colors so dark so you wouldn't notice the blur so much, lol. There is also a lot of ink transfer onto the highlighter tips. After the very first use, every highlighter had a blackened tip.Bottom line: I DO like these, and might consider buying them again when these dry out. The retractable mechanism works well, and the markers have been going strong for a couple months now with no fading of color to indicate the end is near. I like the case they come in to keep them from getting lost at the bottom of my bag, although you could always toss that if you prefer the space saving "toss everything in a pocket" method. ;) While they are a little dark, it's only a real problem with 3 of the colors, and even then I sometimes underline with those colors instead of lining over the words and that works splendidly.They are definitely an improvement over the old-school fat, capped highlighters I grew up with!

I wasn't sure what to expect when I ordered this laminator. The reason I say that is that the unit is large (thus the XL designation, which is a good thing if you want to laminate, say, a 9x12 photo or document); and it's heavy for a home "accessory": over 12 pounds.Also, you have to remember that the laminator is a "thermal" device. Thermal means it uses heat. Therefore, it has to generate heat. Just keep all these characteristics in mind when you're trying to decide whether this device is good for your small home office or studio.I read here about people having problems with jamming. I guess I'm lucky, because I didn't have any jams in about a half dozen uses. (I'll use it more, but I have to order some laminating pouches--easily available here on Amazon.) So far I've laminated a few commercially processed photos. I was hesitant to put vintage photos through the laminator--in fact, I haven't yet laminated any one-of-a-kind or irreplaceable items. I want to get used to it first and be sure it's safe for the media I'm running through it.It did a good job laminating the photos of various sizes. I liked the feature that cuts the pouch to yield rounded corners.It did take a few minutes to warm up and cool down. But so does your iron (if anyone uses those things anymore!) This one won't burn your fingers, though, like an iron would--unless you do something really stupid, like try to laminate your finger.I have to use it more to give it a more thorough review, and that means I'll have to invest money in buying laminating pouches. As I'm thinking through this and writing up my thoughts, I've realized I really don't want to laminate irreplaceable items. I think that's just asking for trouble. Even if they laminate well, one day I might want to take them out of the laminate, and I'm afraid the results wouldn't be optimal.

This printer literally sits on the same shelf as an Epson 3810 and Canon ip6600D.  I also have a Epson RX500 somewhere else.  So, I'm making direct comparisons here.The picture output, color, sharpness, contrast, etc. is outstanding. I spread out my photos individually as they come out to let them air out before handling.3.  The ink likes to stick to the plastic covers of the picture slots in photo albums. The backside of the HP premium photo paper is very rough, which makes me concerned about stacking these pictures together tightly.5.  Yeah, the supplies are pricey.Even with the small negatives, the photo output is really incredible for a low-mid priced photo printer. (Updated to reflect experience and the updated version "C" firmware.)This Brother color MFC is a reasonable choice if you are looking for a wired or wireless networked high speed laser-like color printer, copier, scanner and fax all-in-one, but do not need duplex (two-sided) printing/faxing/scanning.  Personally, I duplex almost everything to save paper, and so would prefer the modelBrother MFC-9840CDW Color Laser Multifunction Center with Wireless Interface and Duplexwhich is a small price increase over this one.  (You can manually duplex with the MFC-9320CW by printing odd numbered pages,  taking the output stack and placing it in the paper tray, and the printing the even number pages.  But, just one paper jam would ruin that process.)I have a variety of complaints about the machine and the software which prevent me from giving it more than three stars.Note that laser-class printers are no substitute for photo printers.  Do not expect photo quality color (or even a very wide color gamut) or the ability to print on photo paper.  That is not what this class of device is for.  If photo quality is your expectation, look to inkjet photo printers.  (The scanner on this device is photo-quality, though.)My rating is based on the reasonable expectations of what a color laser is supposed to do:  spot color, color graphics, mixed text and graphics documents, reasonable color copies.... and all water resistant, due to the fused toner.Both wired and wireless networking worked well, although the instructions for the wireless setup are written by and for a geek, so if you're not a techie, you'll probably need a tech friend to help if your wireless network is secure, with hidden SID and password.  It is really annoying that the device prints two sheets of paper when you change the network settings, one with the wired and one with the wireless settings.  That should be a user option.The printer comes with four toner cartridges, each good for about 1,000 pages according to the instructions.  But, there is some kind of bug in the firmware or the software.  After printing only a handful of pages, both the device and the software monitor reported that the Cyan cartridge was almost empty.  The color bar charts showed it empty.  But, the web-based control panel for the printer showed all cartridges full.  The only way to get rid of the Cyan empty messages in all places was to turn the MFC off and then back on again.  Installing the software onto another computer on the network caused the message to come back - this time saying that both Cyan and Yellow were empty.  Updating the firmware from the delivered version "A" to the current downloadable version "C" seems to have fixed this problem.Print quality is quite good, but requires adjustments for printing photos.  I printed the PDF for a software user manual that included various color screenshots.  It looks terrific and printed at close to the 17 PPM advertised rate.  Nice.Even if it is not a photo printer, photos are part of what will be printed on a color laser - as part of newsletters, real estate flyers, business cards, etc.  So I looked at what I needed to do to get the best results from color-calibrated source images.Anything containing photos really has to be printed in the 600 X 2400 resolution to get all of the details.  (600 x 600 is fine for most other documents.)  The white foam of the waterfall in a test image just blurred together at 600 x 600 resolution.  600 x 600 on this LED printer is not the same crispness as 600 x 600 on a laser.I found that photographic images require printing with the Vivid color option, and with brightness increased.  Even though a color wheel looked good, a calibration image containing various faces for skin tones, color patches and resulted in skin tones that looked sepia, in spite of some other colors in the image looking close to correct.  I had to bump the red level to +12 and brightness to +4 in the print settings dialog to start to get the skin to look like skin.  Even then, it was somewhat orange-sepia.  Neither the Caucasian, Asian or African American babies' skin looked right, but the image was more usable.  It seemed wrong that a bump of +12 (out of 20) on red made so little difference.  Further, on making a color photocopy, where there is only +1 and +2 for red, the +1 improved the red in some places, but made green grass look yellow.  There is no reason that adding red should cause that.  So, I think that there are some firmware and/or software issues yet to be resolved here by Brother.Manual fed items must be fed one at a time, unlike other Brother MFC machines that have a multifunction tray that accepts several sheets at once as an alternate feed tray.  But a plus is that when you use the manual feed slot, you can open the back of the machine so that thick card stock can feed straight through the machine (after setting the paper type setting to "thicker").  It is not a truly straight path - the paper comes out the back pointing upwards and has a slight curl to it.After attempting to print both brochures and business cards with the manual feed, I have to give the manual feed mechanism only 1 star.  It is impossible to get a piece of paper to feed through perfectly straight.  So, it is hard to get business cards, labels, etc to align properly.  The manual feed slot has guide bars that are only an inch and half long in a lip that is a little over 2 inches long.  So, not only must you stand there, holding the piece of paper as you insert it (there is no tray), it is impossible in a little over an inch to make sure that the piece of paper is feeding straight.  Infuriating.  I should note that trying to print brochures on thin stock via the paper tray resulted in skewed images also - so the printer is incapable of feeding paper absolutely straight there either.The manual feed is also infuriatingly temperamental.  If you don't push the piece of paper far enough, or too far, the printer senses a paper jam.  No paper has even entered the printer yet.  The directions ask you to open the printer and remove all four drum-toner elements - which requires someplace convenient to put them.  In this case, that is not necessary - just shut the printer again and wait for several minutes while it rechecks itself, try to fee your paper again, and repeat.Toner fixing was a major problem with the business card printing.  More often than not, the last 1/3 of the page was not fixed and just smeared.  I found a buried setting for 'improve fixing', and also held the paper as it came out the rear slot of the machine, and things improved.  But, I still experienced smeared or lumpy toner on the page itself at times - some of it no doubt left on the drums from the previous page that was not properly fixed.The software is common to most Brother MFC products.  I am more than annoyed that after so many years, Brother has done nothing to improve their software for Macs.  Yes, things work on a Mac, but you do not have the identical functionality as on Windows.The printer driver interface for Windows has various options of handling (manual) duplexing.  On the Mac, your options are to print either odd or even pages and in normal or reverse order.  Finally, Windows users have ControlCenter3 which lets me choose between my two installed Brother MFC devices.  On the Mac, it is ControlCenter2 which will not give multiple devices in its drop-down list.  I have to browse each time I want to switch to a different Brother MFC.Another complaint about the software installation is that it does not automatically check the Brother web site to see if there are updates.  You have to manually do that after installing.  Even then, the Brother web site is not very transparent, giving September 2009 dates to "updates" that, when downloaded, were created in January 2009 and thus are not even required.  The names and functions of the update files are pretty obscure.  I know what they all do as I've had Brother machines for some years.  But, non-techie friends  would not have a clue as to what to download or why.  As an example:  you would never know that if the ControlCenter stopped running and needed to be re-installed, that it was part of the Twain driver.Scanning on the Mac stores the scanned files in the hidden /tmp/<user> directory at the root of the boot drive.  You have to use Finder's menus to go to that folder and purge it.  On the other hand, if you set up custom scans, you can both specify the folder into which the resulting file is placed, as well as have a Finder window open to that folder after a scan completes.  I recommend this approach for Windows and Mac.The OCR capabilities delivered via the Twain driver or ControlCenter are really primitive on Windows, and just plain bad on OS X.  On Windows, the OCR is done by PaperPort OCR; on Mac it is done by Newsoft OCR.  When presented with a page having three columns of text and a few font changes, and selecting rich text scanning, on Windows, the text was scanned almost error-free, but without any font changes.  On OS X (Snow Leopard), the text was scanned as columns with breaks but with lots of errors and all over the page; basically useless.  Even on Windows, better OCR software can scan the full page, including layout and images.  Not so here.The MFC has a USB port in the front into which you can plug a thumb drive or digital camera.  With no connection to a computer, you can page through the files on the drive or camera and choose the ones you want to print directly from the memory device.  I printed a PDF from a thumb drive just fine, and then scanned an image directly onto the thumb drive.  Kind of a cool feature if you have someone who wants to 'borrow' your printer or scanner - they don't need to get onto any of your computers.When the machine is awake, there is a really annoying high-pitched buzz/whine.  It is pure bliss when it goes to sleep and the noise stops.  I'm running it wired to my router, but I may run wireless just so I can move this elsewhere and not have to listen to it.The lack of response to color adjustments, poor toner fixing and bleeding, inability to feed paper perfectly straight through the manual feed or the paper tray are my main concerns now that I've figured out most of the quirks of this machine.  If those issues go away in time, I'll update this review again.

I'm an author and freelance writer. My office is filled with paperwork that constantly needs organization - especially my three-ring binder.  I purchased some tab dividers, but each page takes up precious space. Plus, the tabs I bought were not very sturdy and wanted to rip right out of the notebook.My solution is Avery NoteTabs. These little babies are terrific little sticky notes that help you organize massive binders or folders.The sticky portion of the tab is 3 x 3.5 inches - about the size of the average Post It. This seemed a little bit big. After using them, I could see this size would be necessary for certain types of documents; however, I think the sticky side could be cut down a bit so it doesn't take up quite as much room.As advertised, the sticky portion does not remove text. I tried it in magazines and it pulled off without taking the text, but nearly ripped the page. If you use them to mark interesting news stories, be sure to pull them off gently and hold the page taut while you do it. Also, these will leave a ripple in thin sheets of paper, like magazine pages, on certain book pages and some types of thinner copy paper.You can write on the cardboard tab portion. These are reusable, but if you decide to do that after you wrote on them, you will need to use a label or White Out to start fresh.A few uses:~ Use these instead of binder dividers. If you need a lot of sections, this will save a lot of precious space.~ Take a massive project folder and divide the content, using these tabs to separate the documents into sections. They all stay in the same folder, with better organization.~ Mark pages in well-used books. I suggest cutting down the sticky portion so it stays along the edge of the pages. Also, only use these on reference books or sections you use often, as pulling them off will curl thin book pages.

You don't appreciate a good, basic stapler until you've had to deal with a cheaply-built, poorly-designed one. I used this product on my Epson Artisan printer. The label sheets jammed often and also curled up so I had little tough time.I loaded sheet 1 after 1 when I print because I used this product for my customers and I cannot screw it.The price is great and the product should be good too but I don't think I will purchase this again.

pen design can make writing awkward - I actually do not have as much trouble as others I have shared pen with but I find that is dis-prefer it when there is a choice of other pens (and there is always a choice of other pens) and it went pretty quickly out of rotation and into the drawer.I was hoping I would like it more because it uses a good refill but the refill may complete the pen but it never makes the pen.

Neverending nightmare. From the beginning it has been the most trying piece of equipment we've had. It's disconnected itself from the wireless network. Elegant gold tone clips lend a touch of class. Good to have in your cart [or Saved for Later list] for when you need an inexpensive item to bring up your total to the minimum required for free shipping.

This binder is flimsy and has a very cheap feel and look to it. I am not impressed at all and do not have hopes of lasting long when it is taken in and out of my child's backpack.

These 3M whiteboard erasers look a lot like the household sponge shaped Mr Clean erasers. They come in a bag that includes two of them. If you plan on using them one at a time, you can keep the second one in the bag that they came in.In terms of erasing whiteboards, it is very effective. It erased older markings that my traditional dry-erase erasers could not. Erasing is smooth and easy. The eraser is odorless and doesn't seem to pick up marker smells (but I haven't tried it with the Expo Scents). Over time, it does pick up the color of the whiteboards on the white side, so it doesn't look pretty, but it continues to erase without issue.One negative is that because it is essentially just a sponge, it is fairly fragile. One of my boards has rough edges, and little bits (breadcrumb size) from the edges of the eraser have fallen off. Nothing dramatic, but if you are planning to use it in a tough environment, keep that in mind.Adding a little bit of water to one side managed to wipe clean my oldest and stubbornest board.I only use dry-erase markers, so I didn't try it with permanent markers.Which brings us to price. This is priced like a premium product compared to the traditional dry-erase erasers, especially if you buy those during the back to school sales. However, the 3M is more effective, at least compared to the ones I use. Whether that is enough to justify the extra price, it depends on your situation.

The hardest part of setting up and using this printer was getting the old one out of the way so I had the room to start!Seriously.My two young teenaged boys pulled this out for me since I had procrastinated, and I observed as they spent about ten minutes getting everything put together (things like plugging in the cord and inserting the printer cartridges) and running the printing test.I spent maybe 5 minutes following the incredibly easy instructions to get the printer onto my network, and then we were able to print.  Flawlessly.  We have not had a single problem printing anything in the past two months.Double-sided printing (or copying) is so incredibly simple and far faster than I expected.  Making copies is intuitive.  Scanning is easy.The only thing we haven't tried is using it to fax... because that is just something we don't do.We can print from our Mac laptops, our PC desktop, the iPad, and my iPod Touch. This is a decent tape dispenser. I had no problems loading a standard large role of tape with a 3 inch core. The "tape brake" handle is a nice feature for stopping the tape travel when you're at the point where you want to cut the tape. There are occasions when a stylus is helpful while using an iPad and I picked this up for those times. It is well made and balanced and feels good in the hand. Thinking it worked the same as another stylus I have I pulled it to open up the pen part - and it came apart (you TWIST it for the pen) - anyway, put it back together and took a little more time to look at it closely. Very strong packing tape is not needed for every package, but is a necessity with particularly valuable or fragile shipments. I frequently send boxes, sometimes with one-of-a-kind items that can't be replaced.While in shipment, boxes sometimes weighing fifty or more pounds are tossed onto other, much more fragile packages. Given the right circumstances, the regular packing tape may disengage when a heavy weight hits a less substantial package potentially causing the box to burst open with loss or damage to the contents.I envisioned a glue gun might be needed to use this tape, but no. Apparently, it is just a descriptor for the product's strength. This tape is thicker than any I have used in the past, and while it isn't for every situation, it is worth the expense when the shipment warrants extra care.

We keep one upstairs in the office and one downstairs for my craft use (I use a Silhouette Cameo and do many print and cuts), and have another hooked to my daughter's desktop. They are super fast to set up to your home network and I've never had an issue with signal and I love that I get warnings when my ink is running low. One of my favorite features of this particular model is that dual sided copy feature. The colors are crisp and text is fast. We don't use the fax features so I can't comment on those but everything else has worked flawlessly! I'll be buying Canon printers for life!

Review:The scanner was tested on two laptops, one with Windows 7 installing drivers from the CD and one with Windows 8.1 downloading the drivers. Note that the CD contains some other software aside from the drivers and main scanning interface, such as "Bizcard," which is not immediately evident from the Epson website. These applications are all separate installations, so removal is somewhat time consuming.The stumbling blocks in using this scanner came in the setup. For some reason the driver download was extremely slow, despite my connection being fine otherwise. Once it completed, the Windows 8 machine had no problems wirelessly connecting and scanning documents. However, on the Windows 7 machine, despite following all the same steps, was unable to connect with the scanner after numerous attempts. The documentation that comes in the box is quite poor and incomplete (most of this is online, but was also unhelpful in fixing the problem, whatever it was). We also attempted to use it through the USB connection, and this also failed.Once we got the scanner working, it everything seems fine, about what you would expect from a scanner. The software is relatively self explanatory, with a few "modern" features I haven't seen with my old scanners. The software supports a few different cloud services for scanning directly to upload, including Google Drive, and this feature worked well. Being able to scan double sided and multi-page documents relatively quickly is probably the most useful feature, as compared to a typical flatbed home scanner. The image quality is decent, though not as sharp or fast as a large commercial scanner.Build quality is about what one would expect, not particularly robust, but it feels solid. A caveat for this review is that the scanner was not tested over a long period of time, so it is impossible to say anything about the longevity of the device.

Bought this for my daughters playroom so she can sharpen pencils on her own. This is a functional product but very cheap construction. Serves the purpose well but goes to the old saying that they don't make them like they used to!!

This is nice if you have a place for it. Its easy to hang on the wall and is a great way to keep tack of your workout schedule. There is a place to clip the dry erase marker that is included. I don't really feel its a necessary product as any old piece of paper will do the trick.

One of the best thing about the printer is that if you have a wireless network you don't need a usb cable to install, and once you have it setup in your network (which you can do straight on the mini display / interface on the printer itself) you can print from a tablet (iPad) or other mobile devices without having to install anything.The printer was a little louder than expected, but does provide a quiet mode. Loading the paper sticks out in front, towards you (horizontally as opposed to vertically like a lot of compact printers) .The disk to install the software in the computer comes packaged with a lot of what I like to term junk, but some other people might like it. It comes with like 1 GB worth of different small programs to edit images, and who knows what else. During install you have to manually uncheck all the extra software, because it will just load it all by default.I did a few print tests, and while photo printing (on photo paper) was great, text printing on regular white paper shows just tiny little bit of bleeding, and you can clearly tell a paper printed by laser printer (super sharp) to this one.In summary:Pros:- Super easy, no software to install to print from an iPad- No disk needed or cables needed to install in a wireless network- Photo printing is very good*- Relatively fastNeutral- Cartridge install seems a little forced (it snaps harder than most other printers I have bought.- Paper sticks out in front (so the printed paper comes out on top of the white paper (granted there is a divider, but still worth noting)- Lengthy software included (like 8 different products) and most are checked to be installed by default. Keeping this neutral as some people might want the software, but I felt it was mostly useless.Cons- Ink bleeds a little in regular white paper- Not nearly as sharp as laser (to be expected I know, but maybe I was hoping inkjet quality had increased to be more up to par)* As a side note, it is cheaper to print your pictures through any of the big shops than it is to do it on your own printer. The cost of ink and photo paper is much higher for home users.

Short version of this review:This bankers box is a snap to assemble, literally taking 1 second to pop into the box shape.  (just press on the two edges).But the lid is not a snap to assemble, and the perf is hard to press and usually tears the material.  Its not convenient to use scissors on it (due to the construction) and using a box knife could create an office hazard if you are expecting an employee to handle the assembly for you.Overall the box is much stronger than "discount" bankers boxes and can easily be stacked 5 high.4 stars due to the difficult lid perforation.  Otherwise a pleasure to use.Long version of this review:There are two elements to the bankers box.  One is the cover and one is the box itself.  The box is incredibly easy to set up.  And is stronger than your discount bankers box - its a premium box.  It also has the advantage that it is easy to break down after its been set up, in the event that you decide that you don't have the storage requirement for a while.The cover is nowhere near as advanced and user friendly as the main box.  The cover is just another version of your fold and tuck technology.  A minor irritant was the perforations on each corner that did not break out easily and resulted in tearing the surface of the material 80% of the time.  That said it is no more difficult than any other cover, and the cover is stronger than a discount bankers box cover.  All the instructions are on the box itself, but don't show how the handle fold catches the left and right tabs.  And when the cover is put on the box the handle fold exactly matches the cutout in the main box.  This also provides more bearing surface for whoever is picking the bankers box up.  At least, more than discount bankers boxes provide.This "presto" box has a double wall of cardboard everywhere on the box, making it stronger, except for the top and side walls of the lid.4 stars, very good product, very strong.  But the lid needs some more design work to bring it up to the standard that the rest of the box provides.  Why not just eliminate the perf for tearing and have the factory make a cut instead.
What more can you say?  They work fine in my new Bic pencil and come in easy to access packaging.
Easy to install. Produces clear, crisp black and white copies without any smudges or streaks. Lasts through a fairly high number of copies.

These are handy to add near your calendar to stick in all those little papers from the dentist,  birthday invites and so on. After years of using Expo dry erase in black, blue, red, and green I am in ecstasy. Expo lasted a long time and did a great job. But now I find my board diagrams are much more complicated. So instead of using dots or dashes with the same color and intersecting, I can change to a different color.While the Expo markers were thinner, over time my penmanship was better with large markers like these. And I like the flat side that keeps them from rolling off the desk.

I have been a long time HP printer customer but was disappointed by the last two HP printers I have had. I have been fairly impressed by several Samsung products I purchased recently, so I was very eager to get the chance to try out this new Samsung Color Laserjet printer. First off, I am tired of ALL inkjet printers, because the cartridges are two expensive, and even when you do not use the printers, the cartridges go bad and have to be replaced. I have been wanting to move to a home laserjet for some time to allow me to print documents with some color without the expense of the inkjet cartridges.After giving this printer a workout, I must say that I can rate it as "acceptable", but nothing more. My first difficulty in getting it set up was that the paper tray is poorly designed. It serves as the bottom part of the printer. I found it very difficult to get the paper tray back in, since it does not have well designed "guides". I had to fumble with it for five minutes to get the tray back in. Hopefully with time I will learn the "recipe" to get the paper tray to slide back in properly. Second issue with the paper tray is that it has very limited capacity. It holds only a very thin stack of paper.The next issue I had was that it took me three hours to get the printer installed. In the end, I found that the Samsung supplied USB cable was faulty, and the cable was causing the installation problems. When I replaced with one of my own cables, the installation was done in under 5 minutes. My question for Samsung . . . why include a junk cable? Either provide a quality cable, or dont include one. This bum cable cost me an afternoon.With the printer up and running I did some test prints. I found the overall color on photographs to be subpar by color laserjet standards. The similarly priced HP laserjets provide better color on photographs.The printer does an acceptable job for text, and text with charts and graphs, but somewhat less than acceptable on photographs (yes, I understand laserjets are not made for photos, but I have had other laserjets with better photo capability).So, overall this printer is OK for a cheap color laserjet, but keep your expectations in check if you order it.UPDATE: 4/5/2013I have had this printer now for several months. I have used it very lightly . . . maybe once or twice a week. I was shocked to see that already it is telling me to buy a toner cartridges. It is looking like this printer is going to be WAY more expensive than even an inkjet. The toner cartridge cost is terrible, and toner cartridges are hard to find.I am downgrading my rating from 3 stars (acceptable) to 1 star (not acceptable)The other issue I have found with this printer is that it is FREQUENTLY losing track of what IP port it is on. This requires different things from rebooting the router, printer, and computer to "refinding" the printer from the router.I will use the printer until the cartridge runs out, and then will junk it. I don't have to time to continue to fight with this printer.

The Ampad SimpleSort is perfect for my needs. Included are 80 letter size wide ruled paper. They are held in place with two pins in a sturdy "clipboard-like" easy to open clamp at the top. What makes this really nice are the three supplied dividers that can be placed anywhere in the pad. A bit of a let-down for me is the chipboard backing. It's a heavier cardstock than is found on the back of a notepad but is quickly worn at the bottom corners and the layers will separate. Almost like a "disposable" backing for a nice writing pad that is intended for extended usage. Since this is "ordinary" chipboard, it detracts from the quality image that the sturdy plastic clip has. Otherwise, I'm extremely pleased to have a nice writing pad that offers the ability to reassemble the sheets. Very handy. Plus, the sheets are held in place by the two pins. No sliding out like in a regular clipboard and no big clip to hold the sheets.

I got this for my husband so he could use his laptop in bed more comfortably and it works great. It's sturdy and the legs don't collapse constantly like some models do. The legs are also more sturdy than some of other models.  You can adjust the legs to different angles and adjust the table top also. A nice item and well made. In fact, I liked it so much that I ordered another one for my daughter!

The white plastic covering felt thinner than older binders that I already have. Instead of having a smooth, tight surface, the plastic bubbles slightly in places. The outer clear plastic cover (so you can put labels inside) is ok, but overall the notebook looks and feels cheaply made. It serves its purpose but insofar as being heavy duty, I'm not so sure. Even the way it is finished is not as nicely done as binders I've picked up in the past. I wouldn't recommend this brand; I've picked up better quality ones at Kmart and Target.

Summary - a much more economical and efficient alternative to dedicated labelers.When you're labeling spice jars, you want it to be permanent and waterproof.  For many other things, not so much.I have a Brother P-Touch labeler which is great for permanent and waterproof labels (though the refills are ridiculously expensive.  Fantastic for spice jars, but often you want to be able to remove the labels.  I just tried these and was very impressed.  I relabeled my handwritten file folders next (not that many since I was using the Brother labels)The template worked perfectly on my laser printer.  The labels being all the same size look a lot nicer on the pantry shelves than the Brother labels, which end up being different lengths.  Much cheaper and faster too.  The laser printing and paper is far less permanent, but for organizing boxes and labeling shelves, the film cartridge labelers are overkill.Note, DO NOT GO TO THE MICROSOFT WEBSITE FOR THE TEMPLATE!Their site works only for Office 2000 and later - it wouldn't allow me to D/L the template until I accepted a trial of Word 2007.  I'm using Word 97 which is just fine thank you.  I looked around a bit more and found the template at the 3M site, no muss no fuss.  God, I hate Microsoft.If you've found this review helpful or have any questions please let me know!

Tired of having five different sized Post it Note pads all over your desk?Wish they could would just stay together?Now you have it!  Avery has their post it notes in five differnt sizes and colors and bound them together.The idea is great but the sizes are not.  I usually use the small 1" x 2", the medium 3" x 3" and the larger 3" x 5".  This pack starts with the 3" x 3" and then steps by 1/2" to 3" X 5".  So this only partially solves the problem.Now the other thing you might ask is how do the lower levels work.  Each size is seperated by a base page, so you can easily remove from the middle.  Also each is scored as to rip out.  So either way, easy removal from the pack.This is a good idea but Avery needs to talk to thier users and find out the optimum sizes for this concept.

I bought this as a gift to my daughter and was surprised to see I did not get what the picture claims I got.  It's NOT in the package shown; instead, it's in a white HP package, almost as if somebody bought them in bulk and separated the package.  It works fine, but since the picture showed me something I didn't get, I devalued it in stars.

This shredder copies the iconic Swingline Red Stapler look and is a bit prettier than the standard utilitarian shredders. It also says it will do 60 sheets in a stack (that's a lot!) but if you have staples, or odd-sized pages (bills, for example) it has to take them one at a time. Manual setting also does those paper clips, staples, credit cards and CD's. However to do 60 sheets of paper, as advertised, it needs them stacked neatly and you can't put different sized papers or crumpled, thin, invoices and such in the pile.This unit makes a nice gift especially for someone who has accumulated a lot of records and needs to purge them--and isn't comfortable with going to a public shredding event, where they show up with a truck for you to dump in your bag of discarded personal papers. It is difficult to go through years of private papers and if you are cleaning up after someone passes away, it's a big, time consuming job.There is another advantage to this particular shredder; the older style shredders that are a mechanical unit perched on top of a standard waste basket are top heavy. They can fall over and they are a bit difficult for someone older to lift off for emptying. However, this one sits on the floor and is not so easy to lift or move if you are older. But it can sit compactly under a desk and that's a good place for it. As with any shredder, if you don't empty the bin frequently, the pressure of the filled paper backing up onto the teeth will cause a nasty jam.Nowadays, you can't throw this stuff out in the trash because of identity thieves. So a good shredder is a MUST. If you have an older shredder (doesn't do cross-cut, doesn't handle volume) this is a good replacement.

These NoteTabs are very useful.  I like the following:* they have more "sticky" on them than a typical PostIt -* work as tabs* they have lots of room to write on them* see through* can be repositionedThat being said, there are some downsides:*  very thick*  overkill for many applications (I absent-mindedly started one as a grocery list and then regretted the waste)If you need something see through to put in a book and highlight text, take notes, etc. but don't want to destroy the book, these work.  If you are looking for simple list makers, I think these are a bit too robust :)

Ultimately the white one is great and the purple one isn't, so that's the reason for the 3 star review.  Why in the world would you ship a blue/purple maker along with a purple board?  The marker might as well be invisible ink.If you already have set of markers, you'll see the difference immediately.  Even on the white board, the purple marker shipped is very, very light.

We use dry erase boards in our house to help organize a lot of things so we're very familiar with them. These dry erase markers are definitely not the worst markers I've ever used nor are they the best. The one thing I don't get is why the cap is so strangely shaped as it is definitely not necessary - but it does look cool! The colors are true to the cap and they are definitely markers I will be using continually.

As a planner, I found this to be almost as efficient to use as my day planner.  On each page, you can list what has been accomplished (i.e., 9:45AM talked to...11AM received a rejection from, etc.,)  In the Quick Notes (the yellow section of the page) - I list what has to be accomplished during that particular day; whether that be laundry or finishing off a short story.My only complaint with this is that it is only 80 pages long - to be truly useful it should be 90 (so that it would include three full months of data).  Otherwise, it's a very nice planner to jot down what you have accomplished and what still needs to be done.

Okay. I'm a fan of Post-it items. I use the original (old-school?) yellow, square Post-it notes regularly. I have the page/tab/flag dividers. I've even used the huge flip-chart Post-it notes.These, however, serve zero purpose for me.Maybe if I were in college? No. Because I'd just highlight and write directly in my textbook. And most of my notes would be on the computer (paper stickies don't work so well there).Maybe if I were a CEO? No. Again, I'd use a computer. Or have an administrative assistant to organize for me.Wait! I cook often. What about for my recipe books? Again, no. I scan the recipes I like and put them in a tabbed and labeled binder. And write directly on the pages.The idea behind these is a good one, I suppose; it just was not implemented well. While I still have zero idea when and how I would use these Post-it note tabs, the fact that I can only use them vertically is kind of annoying. What if I want to tab the top or bottom of something? The lines to write on would be going up and down. Not at all helpful.

I'm always looking for ways to stay organized and I'm pleased with the weekly dry erase calendar. I like that it's smaller than most write and erase boards and is consolidated into one week. The board is pretty durable and has 3 big magnets on the back. It also comes with a pen with a little eraser on the top.If you have a big family, it's great to stay organized as it has a mine section and theirs section (4 more spaces), allowing you to write in sports and school events for each family member.

These pens do what they need to - they make colorful marks on whiteboards. The colors are pretty solid except the green, which is actually an aquamarine-ish color.The interesting thing about them, and i don't know if it's a function of the vaunted Liquid Ink, is an almost watercolor-like effect. In a single stroke, the intensity of the color will vary slightly. It fades in and out, not enough to cause any trouble, or even to be noticeable from ten feet away, but it does give it an odd visual texture.Again, they work absolutely fine, but if you need your green to be a true green you won't get that here.

Five pads of sticky-notes page markers, 50 sheets on each pad.  The paper is smooth, takes pencil well and erases cleanly.  The little pads are loose inside the blister-pack, so once you open it you have to figure out your own way to keep track of them.  A pop-up dispenser of some kind would be useful here.  The adhesive stays where you put it, and is easily re-positionable at first.  However, after being stuck to a page inside a book for a week, its grip becomes more tenacious; tags that have been in place for a while may "skin" the paper under tham when you peel them off, especially if they are stuck to old pulpy paper.  They may also tear or crease thin pages like you'd find inside a Bible or a Norton Anthology of literature, so be careful pulling them off if they've been on for a while.  The paper these tags are made of is slightly translucent, so there's a bit of show-through of text underneath them.  The light pink and yellow are the most translucent - the green is least so.And that's all I was able to observe about these.  Pretty standard as far as sticky notes go.  The only disadvantage I can see is the lack of a handy dispenser.  Pads this small can be difficult to keep track of & protect from damage.

I had many, many books to pack away and this tape was the perfect packing tape. It is very strong , with the right width, and held the big boxes full books together with just one strip on top and one on the bottom. While I normally use the clear plastic tape, ordinarily for heavy materials, I would have to tape the bottom with multiple strips - not so with this tape. Also whenever I cut off a piece, the edges stayed neat and trim - no filament strings hanging.

These are not great. Cardboard covered with a thin sheet of alloy. The magnets are very feeble.The board attaches using either 4 double sided sticky pads, or 4 'magnets' you attach to the sticky pads.These magnets are also very weak and do not hold securely at all, even to raw steel. I imagine they would be considerably worse when trying to stick to an enamel fridge door.Pen holder barely grips the pen.Overall a very cheap board with limited use.Disappointed.I can't believe this is getting 5 star reviews.You guess it, made in China.

There is nothing snazzy about this drum, but you either buy one or the copier stops...eventually. The warning message came really early. We figured we better have one on hand immediately. came fast love this prints great this was well packed . I had no problems installing this was easy. a must for the holidays

I like it all right, but I'm not crazy about not being able to change the tabs.  They're printed directly on the dividers.  However, it's sturdy, well made, and holds what I need it to.  The only other thing I would change, besides the tabs, is having some sort of cover on it.It bugs me like something will slip out of it or something.  Also, it's not really "leather-like" in any way.  It's a very typical brown expanding file.

These report covers are made to hold up to 30 pages and they open with "landscape orientation".  In other words, if you hold them with the long side going up and down, the cover lifts up, rather than opening like a book.  If your papers are in "landscape" style, then you can open the cover like a book with extra-wide pages.  I was not especially fond of the swing clip, but it holds well enough for the amount of paper involved.  So, if you need a landscape style cover, or don't mind a cover raising up instead of to the side, it makes a professional-looking cover, but only for a report that is a total of 30 pages or less.  The clear cover makes it easy to see what the report is about, but looks professional, too.

While I heartily appreciate the concept behind this product, the execution is lousy.  The suction cup doesn't actually stick to surfaces, the amount of tape included is miniscule, and it more often than not takes both hands to even dispense a single piece of tape without wasting several more pieces.  As a result of the latter, fingerprints get all over the next piece of tape when using both hands, else the tape doesn't separate at all.I would definitely NOT buy this.

We used this to cut Christmas wrapping paper.  Wow... how easy was that.  This made the typical scissor approach so much easier.  It was easy to line up and just push it along.  What a nice cut and so fast.  It sure beats using a scissors.  And no awkward jagged cuts.This is our tool of chose for cutting wrapping paper or any paper that needs to be cut with a clean cut and fast.  No jagged edges allowed.

The basyx HVL210 was quick and easy to assemble.  The chair is well-built and sturdy.  The seat is comfortable and firm.  The back has a horizontal ridge of lumbar support that's perfectly placed.  I would recommend this product.

Plugged this into the USB port on my MacBook Pro, went to Finder, clicked on LM PNP then selected the DYMO Label Light.app.The app looks like a tiny word processing screen and all you have to do is place your curser into the label box and start typing what you would like to have printed on the label. Options available to format the label include bold, underline, italic, font size and type. (I wish the font options would show the style of the font rather than just the name - time consuming to try out each font.)I like that there are options to print the text onto the labels both vertically and horizontally.Another interesting function is the ability to do a screen grab and to insert it onto the label - although I'm unsure of how this could used most efficiently. Just tried inserting a small image and when I printed the label it wasn't clear at all.The unit comes with a rechargeable lithium battery and charges when plugged into a powered USB port.D1 Label cartridges are available in 1/4-inch; 3/8-inch; and 1/2-inch sizes and come in a variety of colors. They are however, not inexpensive.To save on label waste, I like that the unit does not auto cut the label. (You have to press the cut button on the unit.) I owned a different unit, theBrother PC-Connectable Label Maker with Auto Cutter (PT-2430PC)which always wasted a small bit of label each time it would auto cut.The unit itself has a small footprint and won't take up much desk space when not in use.I do wish this unit worked with Bluetooth or WiFi...

Well made and durable with nice color and waterproofing.  I use the file for student grade sheets.  It serves my needs perfectly.  Price is fine for the quality and usability of the product.  The file stays on my desk, so I don't worry about the contents spilling out of the sides, but that might be an issue for others.

Scotch tape is the best, in my experience.  But my problem with this particular tape is that it is narrower than the Blue Scotch tape I currently use, and I do prefer that extra width.  It's thick and sturdy, though, and is worth a try to see if it suits you.

This is a great ballpoint pen.The grip is soft and easy to hold, unlike a typical plastic based ballpoint pen.The writing instrument itself is very smooth and almost silky the way it glides across the page.If you are in a meeting and have to take a lot of notes, it's also a lot easier on the hand.The only drawback is sometimes it does leave smudges on the page with maybe just a little too much ink coming out.  But for me, that is just a quibble.Excellent product.

We have had this printer for two years now and it has performed like a champ.  It is currently connected to several computers in our home via wireless.  The hook-up was fairly simple to accomplish and has worked very well.The quality of the print is very good as well, better than the other printers I have used in the past. Ink is cheaper and lasts much longer than with the smaller and less expensive printers I have owned previously.All in all this has been a great printer and we have enjoyed using it.

The stapler does not include staples, so you will need to provide standard staples for it.  It worked perfectly out of the box.  No jamming. The colorful reels are well made and the twine seems strong. The twine in each badge reel pulls out and retracts easily. Scotch Magic Tape is the only kind of tape I buy. I have used cheaper tapes. They pale in comparison. Magic tape is virtually invisible when applied. It is sturdy yet able to be sliced with a fingernail when you need to adjust the length of the tape on the fly. Cheap tapes just twist and crumple. No frustration with Magic tape. Did I mention that it is the only kind of tape I buy?!

The telephone reps barely speak English (even worse than other India-based tech support) and the chat reps serve multiple customers at the same time, leading to long delays between their responses. Moreover, I have been cut off during chat sessions five times, which leads me to believe it is intentional as this always seems to happen when I attempt to corner them on difficult questions. Presumably, this means the software was written for Vista.
This is actually a good price for ink where I live. I will buy this ink again on here when I need to. Shipping was quick too, which is always nice!

I ship a lot of items, mostly books, and I recycle as many envelopes and bubble mailers as I can. It is so time consuming to peel off old labels and/or mark through the writing on the envelopes. While this isn't a problem that ranks anywhere on the scale of actual world problems, it's nice to have a simple solution that makes one of my tasks a bit easier.The TrueBlock technology actually works. Some of the mailers I use are pretty worn and have already had 2 or 3 labels stuck to them. One of these Avery TrueBlock labels covers all the writing underneath and looks very clean and neat. They work great! As always, Avery offers so many free templates online that using any of their labels is so easy and convenient. There are other brands available that promise the same thing, and Avery labels aren't always the least expensive, but I find over and over that I save money in the long run by buying the Avery products because they work each and every time.I love a product that is simple but works as promised and gets the job done. These Avery TrueBlock labels are exactly that. Highly recommended!

We are in the processing of packing our house for a big move (10 years in our house, so LOTS of stuff).  We've been purchasing the Home Depot boxes for a little over a dollar each.  These boxes are the same size as the Home Depot medium boxes.While these are boxes and pack things just fine, they are a bit on the expensive side.  The only benefit from ordering them from Amazon is getting them in a HUGE box with some extra brown paper you can use for packing.We will be sticking with the boxes we can get locally because they work just as well at more than half the price.

Ok, I know this wasn't its intended purpose, so if you don't sew, feel free to skip this review.For over 20 years, I've used water soluuable marking pens and lamented how they became permanent with the use of an iron.  I mean, how stupid is that?!?  After sewing a seam, the first thing you do is press it!But these pens are FAAAARRR superior to any made for sewing pens on the market.  The ink disappears immediately when the marks come in contact with an iron.  Seriously, Pilot could mark these pens up double or even triple, slap a new label on the package and market them to seamstresses/quilters and make a fortune . . .they're that great.It's important to note, however . . .the garment/quilt, needs to be washed when finished because the pen marks will return if left in.Other reviews have discussed their office qualities, so no need to wax on about that . . .but as an experienced quilter, My sewing studio will never be without these awesome pens.  So if you sew . . .or know someone who does, you NEED these pens!

This special tape is perfect for holiday wrapping chores. It adheres well, is less likely than many to tangle, and has a nice finish that disappears on the paper once it's been applied. The difficulties using those flimsy tape dispensers and lousy cutters, not to mention the tendency to curl up and tangle, make wrapping a chore. Well, this tape doesn't make wrapping a pleasure, but it does make it easy and quick, with a lovely professional appearance.
It feels a bit watery and I wish the blue color was richer and darker. I like the shape of the bottle.

- Bright, sturdy printer paper- I use it on an HP photosmart printer with good results (for photo prints  I use photo paper, but for everything else, this is solid)- Costs a little more money because its higher quality paper, but to me it's worth a couple dollars extra over the super cheap stuff you might find in a large store- I tried one package to see if it was worth it, and just ordered a second package.- Amazon delivered quickly.

Kudos to Smead for creatively simple innovation!

I have lots of scrapbooking friends who also use this Epson printer so when it is time to re-order the Ink and Paper pack we always get together to buy at least 2 at one time so we qualify for free shipping. The price here on Amazon is cheaper than any of the office supply stores or Walmart and the item never seems to go on sale for less.

This new stapler from PaperPro is a nice, light weight unit, handy for keeping in your brief case, if you frequently have a need for a stapler.  It is low priced, comes with staples, is easy to refill, and seems to fulfill its purpose.  If you frequently need a stapler when you're on the go to a meeting, etc. this can inexpensively serve its purpose.

This printer is one of the best I have had.  Had no problem printing from a smart phone. The printer had great printer quality for an ink jet.  I tested the scanner, and it came out with nice quality.  The printer software was easy to use.  I had no problem with the wireless capability. This is always my big issue with printers.  I need them to be wireless.  I always put my printer across the way.  It set up effortlessly, which is very hard to find.  At under 100.00, this printer is a done deal.  The only thing I wish for is a laser printer.  I go through ink too fast on these ink jet printers.

First of all, I recommend that you read the other (1 & 2 star) ratings for this product, so you get an idea of the issues with jamming, etc.Look, this stapler is built as cheaply as possible, with even the follower itself and the hook that attaches the follower to the spring being made of thin plastic. There is NO way that this tiny plastic curved extension (less than 1/8th inch in width) is going to survive any kind of regular use!  Then there's the issue of false dimensions! Yes, the Amazon page for this product says that it is "7 inches" long, and yes that is incorrect. The actual length of the stapler (its footprint) is slightly less than 5 inches.My tiny Swingline Tot 50 (a much smaller and better built stapler) can do everything this Swingline model can do, for less money and for a lot longer, plus it takes up much less space!This "solid color, fashion" stapler is something only a marketing person could think of, and even then you'd expect the product to be of higher quality and more ergonomic than this stapler is.  Since when is anyone you know, trying to make a fashion statement with their office stapler?  There is nothing "fashionable" about this cheap, plastic, boxy-looking colored stapler.

When it comes to imaging, I love the two commercial grade scanners that we own and have used on my book projects.  But for general daily use, an all in one helps to simplify your home office and reduce the tangle of cords. So when we had the chance to try this Epson C11cc87201 printer scanner we jumped at the chance. And there are Three HUGE reasons why I love this printer scanner unit:1. Simple to install. We installed this unit on our wireless home network of two PC's (both 64 bit machines) and a MAC Book Pro.  All three computers easily installed the software, and after the first installation, the printer found the wireless network without any issues.  The subsequent desktop PC and Mac Book were also easy to install and found the printer without any fuss. The Mac interface with the DVD was the smoothest surprise of all.  It found the installation disc, popped up a message that said it needed to go online for the Mac drivers, found them and I installed them.  SIMPLE!  Al three machines printed out test papers without a hitch.2. Epson scan control is by far one of the best interfaces out there, and as an author of image heavy books, I scanned approximately 16,000 images using the Epson interface.  I recommend using the full on professional mode.  The scan quality is superb, and the adjustments that you can make in front of the scan are easy to tweak. The interface is simple to learn and remember.3. Epson's image printing is really second to none.  Compared to an HP Office Jet 6100, which had been our network printer, images render better on the Epson than the HP.NOW, all that said, one word of warning. Epson manufactured inks are slightly different than the HP standard when using photo paper, and it is important that match the Epson printer to Epson photo paper to get the best results.  HP uses an ink that lays on the top of the photo paper that is coated with a ceramic film.  Epson uses an ink that penetrates the top layer of its photo paper - the result is better color and longevity.  So to get the most out of this printer, use the correct paper.So I can't say enough about this machine.  Ours works flawlessly - we love it!
Not too much to say--this is a direct Canon replacement for Canon ink.  The ink gives good Black and the printer is overall good.
A corded land line with a lighted dial, good sound quality, and the ability to have 'saved' numbers for easy redialing.
Don't be fooled by the packaging, you will get all blue erasers (unless I'm the only one.) Works great for engineering where you erase a lot!
Wow, this is fun, bright colors and very useful.  It could be a little higher but is fine for kids (after all, that is who it's made for).

My use for graph paper is to add notes about areas of the body that I am recording from, making symbols over a grid as the study continues.  This means that I need each piece of paper to last a long time and put up with a lot of abuse.  This paper, which is both thick and reinforced, is ideal for the job.  The lines are also nice and sharp, without getting in the way of viewing writing from a standard black pen.  I can't think of a reason not to recommend it, apart from the value not being good for you.  Since I use a single sheet so much before moving on to the next, the price is not as bad for me as it would be for a math student going through multiple sheets a week.

Don't pay the expensive price of VoIP, such as Vonage. I did have a little problem setting up my E911, the customer service was very good. This is also easier to operate than Magic Jack, and is much more user-friendly.

I have been using these in various applications, and I honestly cannot find any noticeable difference between these and the "original" 3M Post-It notes.  The stick on various surfaces is about the same as is the lack of any residue when leaving after several days or when exposed to moderate heat.  They write on fine as well.I also cannot find that these are better in any way either, so I would choose whichever is cheaper. This Black and Decker laminator competently meets my needs.  I use it mostly for signs identifying produce at my farmers market stand--I can also write the price on the plastic with a grease pencil and then easily wipe it off when I have to change it.Operation couldn't be much simpler.  It does cold or hot lamination, and takes maybe a minute to heat up.  Pu the document in the plastic pouch, feed it in, it comes out the other side laminated. If you're hot laminating, it comes out hot but quickly cools. I've had no bubbling and haven't had to redo anything yet.  There's a trimmer to round the corners, which is only marginally useful, but I use pre-rounded pouches anyway.  It comes with only a few pouches, but they're easily available on Amazon or at most office supply stores at reasonable cost. Construction seems sturdy.

The boards are GREAT. Magnets strong and sturdy covering the whole back. The fronts pretty and nice. The marker - I held out high hopes it would work better than most dry erase. I sharpened all the pencils in the office, one after another, and the sharpener did not relent. It blew through all the pencils. NoteTabs are a new product from Avery that take the Post-It note to the next level. Years ago, we suddenly realized that we all needed small yellow pieces of paper that could stick anywhere, then be removed without leaving a trace. Now imagine if those yellow pages were 1) green, 2) transparent, and 3) had a paper tab at the top edge which looks like the tab of a manila folder. Call it a NoteTab. What would you then do with the NoteTab? Presumably, you would stick one into your monthly organizer so that you could quickly identify the current week/month. Or you might stick a few into your textbook so that you're all set for that open book test coming up. Naturally the NoteTabs can be removed without leaving a trace, and even reused several times before they ultimately decompensate and turn into dust (or whatever this product ultimately becomes). This particular NoteTab is 3" x 3.5" and comes in a variety of colors. I happened to get the Cool Green variety in a pack of 20. The NoteTabs work as described and, as with the Post-It note, don't seem to replace an existing product but rather combine several existing products into one in a novel manner. One wonders where NoteTabs have been before.

One might go so far as to wonder whether the representations made on this product page constitute outright fraud.  The product I received was NOT as it is shown on this page.  I did not receive Epson brand cartridges in the box, unopened, as shown.What I received were six cartridges, wrapped three to a package.  So each cartridge was not individually wrapped, as is the case with cartridges ordered from Epson directly.  Once the package is opened to be able to use one cartridge, the other two must sit opened, with only the tape on the ink port to protect against drying out.  The six included a black cartridge, which the enclosed note said was a "freebie" because, while the company assured me these are original Epson cartridges, to "reduce packaging", they were being sent wrapped as they were.I had misgivings, but the cartridges DID have the Epson logo on them, looked like the others I've been accustomed to, so I put them in my cartridge drawer to use as needed.The first cartridges I've used seemed to go much faster than normal, without a corresponding increase in my customary printing load.  Then, today, I went to replace two additional cartridges...certain colors don't seem to get used as much, so replacement rates vary (one of the reasons I love having an inkjet that allows for colors to be replaced individually, rather than as an integrated unit is that you always end up wasting ink on the multi-color single cartridge types).  I used two of the cartridges that had been sitting, unwrapped, in the drawer, because I had already used one of the cartridges in the three-pack.  What a nightmare...the ink didn't flow, wasted paper, seven head cleanings...I FINALLY got ink flowing, but I'm now left with black ink flecks all along the paper.  I don't have this problem with inks I order directly from Epson or that I receive in the original equipment packaging.I really have to wonder what the deal is with these cartridges...are they refilled, remanufactured ink cartridges and simply not identified as such? Regardless of the answer, I WON'T be ordering these again.NOT RECOMMENDED

When asked to review this scale, I almost declined because while we do mail a good number of packages for our business, most of them go US Priority Mail, so weight doesn't matter. The more I thought about though, the more I realized this scale would come in handy as more than a postage scale.The separate display and ability to choose between using battery and outlet power make this thing very versatile. I plan to use it for cooking as well as for weighing the occasional package. The 8" x 8" platform is plenty large for holding a bowl or other cooking container, or if you want to weigh something like a piece of meat, a simple piece of wax paper will suffice. Because the display / controller is a separate unit, attached by what looks like a coiled telephone cord, it's easy to fit all but the largest and most cumbersome packages on the platform. The adjustable angle, blue backlit LCD display has large, easy to read numbers, and the display reads in pounds (decimal format), pounds & ounces, kilograms and grams.I have not yet calibrated my scale, but don't plan on it because it is already accurate enough that adjustment isn't necessary. I checked it with a simple Pyrex measuring cylinder and an empty gallon water jug. Water weighs roughly 8.33 pounds at 70 degrees, and this scale (after tare of the jug) weighed my gallon of water at 8 pounds, five ounces.All things considered, this scale appears to be a great value. It's much more economical than competing models, has a great capacity and is very versatile and easy to use. I love it and have started keeping it on my kitchen island for handy use whenever I want to weigh something.

Parker pens have been a staple in my pen-collecting life from the beginning. This, the JOTTER model, is an absolute must for any serious Great Old School writers. It's up there with theFisher Space Original Astronaut Space PenorFisher Cap-O-Matic S200 Chrome Cap w/ Black Barrel Ballpoint Pen - S251BKand the immortalCross Classic Century, Lustrous Chrome, Ballpoint Pen (3502)(which in my aristocratic youth was a gift to show a boy had become a man).The Jotter is interesting because of its heft and excellent 1950s construction. I own several, one in chrome and the rest with the half plastic barrel. The Jotter, at exactly 5" in length and a bit chubbier than most pens, is an excellent, non-fatiguing ballpoint pen. It is the opposite, for example, of the now-unavailable old Papermate Stick, which is just over 6" in length (and thinner than a No. 2 pencil).This is quite the tirade from the man who says buy the refills only and skip the pen. Professionals and students need a good pen, too, and this is it.Something I have noted from other customers is they are addicted to the retraction (clicking) mechanism of a pen. Parkers have a tendency to 'slip' or malfunction a bit, due to the fact that a Parker refill is configured funny, almost like a "key" that fits into the cap's "lock".Aside from that little freak-out, a Parker will really be the only pen you'll ever need. I have to say, my sister bought me one as a gift, and the refill in it lasted for over a decade. It was the only pen I wrote with - it was really a bit scary. That was an all-chrome satin textured model Jotter. It never quit on me or wore out in any way: it was stolen at almost 11 years of age. (The PEN, not me, dummy!)The only warning I will offer in all seriousness is you may find it difficult to find genuine ordinary ballpoint refills for it; Parker seems to be leaning hard to get people to buy their Parker Gel refills, which are excellent but they last about 2 weeks!Since this is about a pen, I must get on my soapbox. Schools are poised to cut out teaching cursive altogether, instead training children to type on computers. Penmanship is already down the toilet - why teach it? The PC is the new "notebook".Anyone familiar with the Good Old School - I am a proud alumnus - knows that we obsess about the quality of our paper, notebooks, pens and pencils. Think it is insignificant? Think again: every law enforcement officer is issued a notebook which is numbered and catalogued. Military branches have something similar to this practice. This is a vital element of the practice of the authoritative professions.Reporters, both media and court, are even pickier about the writing implements they use. They all file their notebooks, for future reference among other reasons. Scientists are no different and file their hand-written field data plus other research along with the transcripts. Authors and even poets are extremely picky about it too, if they are the Old Schoolers. Yep: it IS that important.So it ought to be as important to the ordinary person, the civilian who is not an author, reporter or scientist, because what you have to note is no less important! Always give this some thought before buying any stationary - especially your pen.As one very excellent reviewer here wrote, a great pen boosts your morale at work, makes you feel enthusiastic about writing, and even encourages your colleagues/clients when you need them to sign something. Just don't fall prey to the Biggest Scholastic Evil in the World: having your favorite pen stolen.

This product is going to come in very handy for me.  I love to cook and I have lots of cookbooks.
