I took one of the Note Tab sheets, tore the tab portion off at the perforation, wrote the recipe name on it, then separated the other three perforated sections and placed them on the page with the recipe.  Eureka!  It works beautifully.  The package said that the sheets are repositionable so I tried taking off a portion and it worked just fine.  I used a Sharpie fine point pen to write with and the ink stayed on the Note Tab even when I purposefully rubbed my finger across it.  This package contained 6 blue and 6 green Note Tabs, 3" x 7.5".Now that I see how useful these Note Tabs can be, I plan to try other colors and sizes in this cookbook project of mine.  The tabs feel very sturdy and durable, the note section allows me to read any portion of the recipe under the note and I like that I can separate the note into 4 different pieces.  I'll probably come up with a code where a particular color represents a specific type of recipe.  What a great find these Note Tabs were.

I loved the idea of this SmoothMove Moving Kit; how neat is it to order a package and have all your supplies come at once? I was about to move two people out of a small apartment and this seemed the perfect thing. The reality fell somewhat short of my vision. Read on for the perplexing details.First, what's good. The boxes. The boxes are terrific. They are sturdy, reusable, easy to assemble and have marked lines for you to list the contents. I loved the variety of sizes, perfect for household items. A+ on the boxes. Also very nice is the black marker that comes with the kit--it held up well to frequent use and didn't dry out.Now, the not-so-good. The roll of tape that came with this kit was discolored, had no dispenser, and STANK. Really bad. I would describe the smell as "Made in a foreign country with not-legal-in-the-U.S. chemicals". Holding it a foot and a half away from me I could still barely stand to use it.And lastly, the inexplicable. This was so odd I had a hard time believing my eyes, but the kit I received did not come with four rolls of bubble wrap. It came with four flat squares, about 4" by 4". Obviously this was a mistake of some kind, but if you were ordering this kit for immediate use you might not have time to resolve such an oversight. The store down the street from us charges a whopping $13.99 per medium-sized roll of bubble wrap, so the wrap in this kit was a big draw for me. Alas, I didn't get any to use.In summation, great boxes, great marker, usable but poor quality and old-looking tape, and for us, no bubble wrap. The company should supply better-quality tape (with a dispenser), and double check to make sure all components are in the kit before shipping. With those two adjustments, this item would be worthy of five stars. As it is:GRADE: B-(I wonder if the makers of this kit are aware that "Smooth Move" is name of a famous laxative?)

Some thing you learn through trial and error that it is better to invest a little extra for the right product. I've bought cheap pencil sharpeners in the past. They eat up pencils, stop working, and make a ton of noise.I am thrilled that this Westcott pencil sharpener is quiet and very easy to use. The base is weighted enough that it doesn't slip around or shimmy. It holds the pencil in firmly and stops automatically when it is done and the point is sharp. It has sharpened kids pencils with the plastic coating as well as other standard pencils with no problems. It runs smoothly and doesn't seem to get hitched up on the edges of any pencil.I really love how solid and quiet it is. Worth the investment.

I really like Elmer's Washable Glue Sticks and is the one I use all the time for all my pictures and Art Projects, for all paper and DVD covers and numerous other Presentations for Home and Work. Elmer's Glue Sticks are the ones I always reach for, it is very Strong and it does keep Materials Glued together for a long time without coming apart. I like the fact that the Color Purple disappears as it dries out. Also it is Acid Free and Washable. One Glue Stick Lasts for a Long Time and the Price here can not be beat specially for 4 Sticks! ...Thank You D.D.

As white-board products go, these are okay, but not great. So here is what I think so far of the marker kit:- The markers write well, but they smear when they erase. I used both the eraser included an another eraser that I have and the marker smeared (left light streaks). This was worse with the eraser included, but still has a light streaking with another eraser.  And you definitely can't erase when the marker is still slightly wet: lots of smudges and smears. I'd definitely prefer Expo markers.- The "anti-roll" cap worked as long as it was laid down without force. You can't push or bump it; it has to be laid straight down and gently. It sort of worked on an incline.- The eraser worked really well (as well as other erasers) when using Expo markers (probably the most well-known brand of dry erase markers).- The spray didn't clean as well as the another white board cleaner that I have. It took more cleaner and an extra wipe over the surface to get it free of the streaks from the markers.My wife is a teacher and has used white board markers for over 10 years. She quickly said that the streaking of these markers when they erase would really bother her. It would take a lot of extra effort to keep the white board white. So this might be a nice bargain pack, and it is good to get the cleaner and eraser with the markers, but if you're planning any serious use of these, I'd recommend getting better ones. On the other hand, if you're just looking for a little starter pack to use at home, maybe this will fit the bill.

I worked in a print shop for 7 years as part of an internal service for a larger organization and we had to bind documents weekly over the years. Sometimes saddle-stitched, sometimes with comb binding and others. For just sheer ease of use in reading large documents, the comb binding method was the most popular used. We went through a few inferior machines, until we got a Fellowes binder and that puppy held up to a lot of use and sometimes abuse by temporary employees that could not follow directions! This new Galaxy Binder is a step beyond what I had to use in the print shop. This thing punched through 100 pages with such ease for me - I've used comb binders before where we had to break the job up into 25 page chunks or it would jam... or we'd grab a strong man (or two) from another department to push on the lever for us. This is not necessary with the Galaxy Comb Binding machine. The machine will punch up to 500 pages at once, but I have not yet had that large of a document to bind.This is a great office supply gadget to have for teachers, or secretaries that have to bind a lot of documents that come through the office. Unlike a number of inferior models, this one does not wear you out by forcing you to body-slam the lever to get the job done. It's a nice, solid piece of office equipment that does not slip-n-slide all over the counter space. It's nicely weighted, but not so heavy that you can't easily move it to another counter space if needed.

I needed to stock up on double sided tape for my son's birthday party favors.  We were making water bottle labels and candy bar wrappers.  I knew I needed a lot of tape!This is a great value and the tape holds wonderfully!  I've also used this tape for scrapbooking, taping things to the wall (it has never pulled off paint for me!), and other uses.

I got this for my wife who loves to sit on an overstuffed chair or on her bed and catch up on Facebook and email. She loves it. The legs snap firmly into detentes. They can be configured in multiple ways, including a little desk (but very low). Only rarely has a gift I bought my wife been used to often and made what she likes to do so much better.

I use this scanner at work and liked it so much that I bought one for home use. It isn't for photos really, or anything that requires a flatbed, but for documents it is Great. It provides a variety of "scan to" options and user control settings. It is more flexible about file naming formatting than is the Canon flatbed scanner I use.  It is pretty fast, keeps count of how many pages have scanned, will scan duplex and skip the backs of blank pages at the same time, and I've scanned many hundreds of pages at a time without having to give it a rest beyond reloading 40-50 new pages for scanning. Cool little scanner!

I usually use Avery, but these work as well, if not better. No printer jams and they adhere to the folders I've used.  So far the labels have stayed where they are supposed to when they should, and when I've needed to move them there hasn't been a problem.You are able to see through them, but that is the case with all labels that I've ever used, so I don't see how that is different.
Purchased these for little sisters in school, they have worked really good all school year. Would definitely recommend to anyone who has to hi-lite a lot. Will buy again for next school year

I have not used a hand held label maker since the days of turn the wheel label makers. I was excited to try out the DYMO LabelManager. It requires 6 AAA batteries which are not included. There is an optional AC adapter.  Once the batteries are put it, the label maker has a bit of heft to it. The first label I printed got stuck. The second label was fine, and I cut off the bad part from the first try.  It has a nice querty keypad and the numbers. It has some features like bold, underline, etc.  There is a key to hit to get to the symbols (and punctuation) quickly and another key for various non-English letters. There is a window on the back so you can easily see what size and color of tape you have in. I have nothing to compare this to, but found it fairly easy to set up and figure out. Once I had found 6 batteries, I was ready to go quickly.

If there were an Olympics for catalog shopping I would have a gold medal.  I use these flags to mark the items I want in each catalog.  I save the catalog until the item arrives.  Makes it so much easier to find information if it is needed,
Way to go Avery. All your products I've purchased and used thus far are top quality, don't get stuck in my printer and adheres to the paper.

I am an engineer, and any engineer working for Epson should be embarrassed to admit they work for this company. Today I am throwing out a perfectly good, like brand new Epson Artisan 800 printer simply because the "Printer ink pads are at the end of their service life. Please contact Epson support.". I am not kidding. My printer has printed less than 1000 pages, and when the ink pads that take the excess ink get full, Epson has it set up so that the printer shuts down and is no longer useable. I am not making this up- it comes straight from Epson. Virtually every time you use the printer after a day of non-use, it goes through a full cycle of head cleaning that literally shoots a tablespoon of ink into the pads. Yes, I am serious, I tested it with my own eyes and have seen other's videos of this. You can turn off the automatic head cleaning, but then you have to deal with frequent bad pages, so it is a catch 22 situation. Anyway, after talking to Epson, I was offered a "deal" on the Artisan 835 to replace this one....Yes, I am serious, Epson designed this unit to be thrown away when it is in perfect condition simply because the ink pads are full. You ask, you mean they didn't simply make it so you could remove the ink pad, clean it, and reset the printer and keep on printing?  Yes, that is what I am saying. Their engineers should have their diplomas stripped. You can buy software to reset the printer (but not from Epson), and then go through the process of removing and cleaning your ink pads. What a joke! Epson should have built the availability to do this easily themselves. If they think their planned obsolescence of the printer will make them more money, think again. I will never buy another Epson inkjet printer.

Our old stapler gave out, so I was excited to try this one through Amazon Vine. When it arrived, I opened the package and found a piece of paper to try it out. To my dismay, there were no staples at all in the stapler! I have purchased many staplers over the years, and I have never found one that didn't include at least a few staples so that you could use the product immediately.I really have no interest in customizing my office products, but to complete the review, I went to the website to choose a skin. At first when I typed in the code, it took me to the homepage where there was  no obvious place to enter a code. I tried to search for a stapler, but nothing came up. I tried again and found that you have to type in the "www" at the beginning of the URL.I was pleasantly surprised to find that there were quite a few designs to choose from. Since we are a military family, I chose a skin that honored the soldiers who have died for our country. Very cool!So basically, 1 star for the stapler (since there are no staples included) but 5 stars for the skin selections.

I just installed my Ooma Telo to replace my existing Vonage service. The installation was easy and quick. It took longer for the device to download the latest firmware than it did to install the hardware.  The sound quality is as good as that with Vonage (and with Comcast before that).  So why switch?  Because I'm saving over $31/mo. with Ooma.  My bill (for taxes) will be $3.75/mo.  The payback period will be about 3.5 months or just under 5 months if I decide to port over my phone no. (which I intend to do).  It's unfortunate that Ooma charges $40 for porting but I factored that into the cost of the system so it's not a deal-killer for me.Activation includes a 60 day free trial of their Premier service.  Mark down the date you activated your service because if you don't cancel Premier before the trial period ends you'll be billed $9.99/mo.  That's still a great value vs. Vonage or Comcast but I don't think I'll take it.  One feature that's only offered with Premier is email notification of voicemails. I'll miss that but it's not critical and I'm more than willing to trade that off for a substantial monthly savings.  Another nice feature if you choose Premier service is the ability to have your calls ring on your landline and cell phone simultaneously or, if you prefer, to have calls forward to your cell phone if your internet service goes down.I haven't had to deal with Customer Service so I can't comment on how good or bad they are.  I have seen that the porting is submitted on-line though your My Ooma account so that should be easy enough.  I'll update this review if I see any significant changes in service or experience anything out of the ordinary with either the equipment or Customer Service.  Yes, I wish they didn't charge for porting and, yes, I wish they offered email alerts for free but overall so far I'm pleased:  easy to install, good sound quality, easy to retrieve voicemail messages from the Telo box or on-line and all at a significant cost savings.

I definitely liked using these pens. The ink is sharp and pens move easily on the paper. The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is because I am slightly more partial to Gel pens, especially those with rubber comfort grips. But these are defnitely worth using.

The Wilson Jones tabs are handy because they come packaged together as an 8-tab set.  I always find myself needing more than the 5 I so often get.The left column with the three hole punches is reinforced (but only on the front) of each divider. The yellow paper that comprises the divider itself is a step up from looseleaf paper but certainly not a heavy cardstock and my package arrived with a lot of dents already in these dividers - just from regular package handling. Not a big deal to me but my kids like their school supplies to start out pristine (as do some adults). The colors on the tabs themselves seem to be a bit washed out at the top - orange, yellow, and pink, then a clear and then your more standard blue, green, yellow, and red.Overall, they are perfectly fine for their function but no one detail stands out that makes you want to recommend them above another set except for the fact that you are getting 8 tabs rather than 5 tabs.

I send a lot of checks through the mail so these have been a godsend (no pun intended). They serve the dual purpose of hiding the contents and indicating whether or not they have been previously opened. For anyone who sends checks, money orders, or sensitive documents through the mail, these envelopes are indispensable. 5/5 stars.

Everyone is trying to be "green" these days and Avery is no exception.  So what is "green" about these?  They are made with 100% recycle material which is processed chlorine free.  They also claim to use Soy and vegetable based inks.  The packaging was also printed using soy based inks and made from recycled materials.So how do they work?  The seem to work as well as other Avery label products --- in other words they work very well.  If you are looking for a more environmentally friendly alternative to other labels I can recommend these.

I love this sticky back velcro.  It's even better than double-sided tape since I can pull off the item easily.  So far, I have used it to mount a message board and also a small waste basket.  The adhesive and velcro is very strong.
I have Sharpies in every color and highly recommend them for labeling. Nothing else works as well, and I particularly love these fine point markers.

All the note-writing sticky sheets you need.  They're not so thin that you have to carefully peel one off the stack.  The glue on the back works well.  With 400 sheets, you're not going to run out quickly.  The colors are sharp and pleasing to the eye.  I use them to write notes to the people I send autographed books to.  I keep some by the telephone to scribble notes while on the house phone.  I even use them to mark my page in a book I'm reading.  I write reminder notes to my husband and stick them on the bathroom mirror or the door of the fridge. You can find so many uses for these sticky notes.

The printer was intuitively easy to set up wirelessly.  I print a lot of color charts with it and the quality is great. It's fast whether printing, copying, scanning or faxing. Although it's a good size printer, it fits on the desk without taking it over. I miss the automatic duplex printing and I'm a bit surprised that this printer does not have it. This printer draws a lot of electricity and causes the lights to flicker and the UPS to cycle so I have to leave it powered off when it's not being used.

I appreciate that the price can change from hour-to-hour and day-to-day but I find Amazon has a cheaper price than my local depot place - even taking coupons into account.I use generic toner but have not found that a generic ink I really like. As we use the ink in a color printer we use to print patient pictures I'm not too worried about cost over quality. OF course these tanks are expensive but I'm happy to pay for the quality

Until I tried using the tabs (those little things that stick up from the enclosed folders that inform you of the folders' contents) I was extremely pleased with this sturdy, handsome file folder. Read on...PRO:1. Excellent quality for the money (with one exception, see below).2. Nicely textured grip for easy holding.3. Holds a lot! It actually has 14 pockets (not 12) if you count the first and last plastic folders next to the front and back covers.4. Well-functioning, easy-to-use folder closer.  A black elastic band attaches to a circular tab on the front. I suppose it could have been made more secure, but this is sufficient.CON:1. The tabs alternate between clear and blue, and someone chose the wrong color blue.  They're simply a few shades too dark, and it makes it difficult to see your label (especially if you didn't notice this before and used blue ink).BOTTOM LINE. For the money, a very good product, especially for household use.The dark blue color on half of the tabs can make it difficult to read the label.

Quadrille pads can be very pricey. I don't need a high quality vellum for most of the projects and sketches I do, so this pack is great. You have the option of using 1/4 or 1/8 squares (front and back). The plastic reinforcement strip is also a very nice touch if you want to store things in a binder and use them often. One star off because some of the pagers are lighter than others. Every other page seemed to be printed slightly lighter though this should not present a problem to someone with normal or near normal eyesight. For what I do that kind of uniformity is not important.
I only got 1/4 of the life of this cartridge.  I, like others am going back to the low yield.  Clearly there is a problem with these cartridges.  They should be pulled.
not the item i was looking for...but it works. i don't know if i would order again, i don't know

This works essentially like double sided tape and bonds two pieces of paper together (it's not for packaging). The advantage to using this instead of tape is that you don't have to pull it off a tape roll, cut and position.  You hold your project (photo or paper) down on your table with one hand, and with the other you use the dispenser to glide down the area you want to "glue down" such as the edge of a photo.  I make note cards from photos and have used double-sided tape for years.  This is SO much easier and faster. You can swirl it wherever you want and put down less (like half the width) where you apply the pressure.The only mistake I made initially was trying to use it upside down -- duh!  The white flip cap doubles as a guide against the surface which helps position it at a 45 degree angle and keeps it there.  If you remember that the lettering on the unit should be in readable upright position, the cap will be down and in place.  I hate glue sticks, but occasionally used them behind a photo to save costs... inevitably just a dab would get on the photo and smear.  This gadget eliminates that, which is great. I'm rating it 4-star because it is a bit pricey and I don't know yet how far a roll will go. If it was in the $3 range I would give it a 5-star rating.  I make tons of cards and don't know yet whether it will be cost-effective for my use.  Stay tuned!

In my opinion, now that I have tried 3 different Bankers Box brand items, I'm spoiled.  For years, I have used their Cardboard Boxes both -white (strongest) and the brown (standard) to store binders/files and heavy books.  Recently, I reviewed the picture boxes and was overall quite pleased.  I love this Wardrobe Box, unlike the other boxes they manufacture, Banker Box failed to provide instructions but no worries, it wasn't a challenge to figure out.My selection of this item was to store expensive formal wear.  I have some very elegant beaded shirts and formal dresses that I want to keep away of my everyday items (since space is limited and I'm concerned that they will sustain damage by catching or snagging on something next to it.  This box worked just perfect for me.  It is very sturdy, too.  I wish it were a bit taller but on the same token at this size, it is more manageable.If I move, I will update this review to indicate its functionality while used to transport.  They are very durable and easy to handle.Though some may feel this is an expensive purchase(I have to say I feel this way to a degree, after all it is cardboard and a rod), it has performed well thus far.  My experiences with their other boxes have been extremely positive, so in this instance I believe I got what I paid for.  They out last other similar products, so it balances out.

I frequently use Avery paper because of the consistently high quality, and these business card sheets did not disappoint. The print quality is excellent and smudge free, ran easily through my printer and are easily separated without the "cheap" looking perforated edges that are prevalent on some other brands of cards.These sheets are smooth and bright white and hassle free! I would recommend these to anyone who print their own cards at home, specially full color cards!

This is my first Quartet Planning Board, and I'm glad I picked this particular planning board for my uses!Year after year, I purchase paper planners to keep me better organized, and year after year, they go pretty much unused. With this planning board, while yes, I WILL have to take the time to properly fill the dates in for each of the months displayed, I can just wipe it clean each quarter, and move on to the next chunk of my year. Since it's undesignated, and relatively sturdy (although not as sturdy as I'd ideally like), I expect to get many years of use out of this board before wear and tear makes it replacement time for it.The size is large enough to allow you to put shorthand notes pretty much wherever you'd need them, the mounting hardware is enclosed, and there's even a dry erase marker to get you started. Just be gentle in mounting it, and ensure you wipe it thoroughly clean, and there's no reason why you won't get far more than your money's worth out of this board! Those Franklin Covey planners I've bought for years now are double the cost of this board, and that's just for one year!Spend smarter, not harder! ;)

As with any ink cartridge, we are black mailed into paying way too much for what amounts to a small amount of ink. If not for the impact on landfills it sometimes is cheaper to buy a new printer then new ink.

The Brother "PC501 Print Cartridge" is the refill for theBrother FAX-575 Personal Fax, Phone and Copier. The cartridge that came with the 575 ran out way too fast, so I suggest getting an extra one of these right away.The cartridge worked as expected and was easy to install in the FAX machine.This is a required component for the 575 FAX machine, so it is "Recommended" as it does what it needed.

Love these!  I've been using hanging file folders for years to organize files in my office.  The advantage of this is that they are pocket folders, i.e. the sides are enclosed and no assembly is required.  The folders that I currently use require me to fold the edges and inserting a small cardboard insert at the bottom to make the folder expand up to about an inch and the insertion of a tab to label.I love that these pocket folders have not assembly, can expand up to 3.5 inches and the enclosed edges keep the papers from sliding out of the sides.  Also tabs are already in place.The only drawback to these relative to others is that you have to take the papers out to sort through them, whereas the ones without sides can be opened, sorted through an simply refolded and re-inserted in to the file drawers.  This is a minor issue, however, relative to the great benefits and capacity of these folders.

The Five Star 2" Zipper Binder is a mixed-bag.Pros: The binder is attractive with the darker stripped print on the outer pocket. The ring mechanism that holds the papers inside is strong and the binder itself is roomy. The inner screened pocket is large and can hold a number of writing tools/school tools. There is a handle along the spine to make carrying the binder (once zippered) easier.Cons: To get a pen or pencil you have to unzipper the binder and the inner pocket. It would have been more practical to be able to grap a writing tool (perhaps with a pencil/pen pocket organizer inside) without having to unzipper twice. Also, the outer zippered pocket for storing papers has five wide pockets for dropping papers in but it doesn't really keep them secured outside of the zipper.Overall, the product seems aimed at middle-school and high-school but doesn't have some of the conveniences students would appreciate and the large paper capacity (it claims 880 sheets) is much more likely to be found being hauled around by an adult taking their paperwork home than a student.For my high-schoolers we'd look around for something with a bit more practical storage design. For me, the binder is nice for use for bill-paying and storage at home, but not something I'd lug back and forth as it was clearly intended for school, not work (particularly in the brighter blue color).

This works well and is designed well. You get ample room for weekday planning and a space to pin/stick messages. Included pen works well and it is easy to clean. It is also extremely light weight. Just make sure you have room. It is quite wide and it was hard for us to find a good place. It barely fits on a standard door for instance. I would have made it just slightly narrower even with the lost of a little room.

These folders are perfect for small to medium size file jobs.  The fasteners are very sturdy and easy to use -- they aren't the super flimsy fasteners that are easy to crush.  They have a nice weight and strength to them.The folders themselves are nicely colored and a little bit thicker than economy folders.  They have reinforced tabs, which is very nice and adds to their strength.  I would not call them heavy duty folders though, and I am not sure I would use them for any file that would see heavy usage.

I've been buying 2-3 rolls of Scotch Heavy Duty Packaging Tape a year in the 1.88" x 800" (22 yards) size. Although I had never used the comparable Duck Brand tape, I was happy to try it. I received the tape too late for Christmas wrapping, but I've used it since then to wrap two packages, as well as a couple of miscellaneous uses, and I like it. For one thing, there's a piece of paper on the end of the tape that keeps the end free. With the Scotch brand tape, I hate trying to get the end of the tape free. The Duck brand dispenser is not too different from the Scotch dispenser, but the addition of a half-inch-diameter plastic roller makes a big difference in enabling the dispenser to be used with one hand.The tape itself appears to be very similar to the Scotch packaging tape. It seems to have comparable strength and stretchiness. Scotch claims that its tape is 20 times as strong as acrylic tapes like the Duck Brand, but I didn't notice much difference in my own informal stretch and tear tests.Overall, I'm very pleased with the Duck brand packaging tape. If I was shopping for packaging tape today, I would likely choose between the two brands on the basis of price alone, since I found the two brands to be very similar in performance.

When I think of colored pens, I tend to think of something children might want for fun. These certainly qualify, but are far from being a children's product alone. The colors are blended, and the description of each color shows that it it blended with black. That means that the colors are subdued yet bold, but not flashy. The green, blue, purple and brown are deep. The red is more of a maroon. They are very attractive, but don't make your writing look like a school project. And the ink doesn't appear black as a result; the colors are what their names suggest, but with a moderate saturation instead of gaudy brightness.The pens themselves are very comfortable to use. They write smoothly without skipping, and the colors do not smudge. They also work equally well with either hand. A problem for many left handed users is that pushing instead of pulling makes it more likely for pens to skip or not deliver ink. Moving your hand immediately over what you just wrote can contribute to smudging. And some pens can poke through the paper when used in the left hand. Most people reading this are probably right handed, and I found that these pens work equally well regardless of which hand I write with. Even with the right hand they are smoother.Uni-ball pens in general tend to write well. What sets these apart from other Uni-ball pens is the ink. I'm glad that the colors are ones I would actually want to use.

These tabs are great for organizing bookmarks in all kinds of books - from technical manuals to cookbooks.  They provide a clean, easy to use tab that is removable like a post-it note, and which has a translucent writable surface on the page itself to jot down a few short notes.  (I recommend pencil.  Pen works, but being plastic, the ink will remain wet and can come off on the opposite page.)I like these for temporary markers - for example, marking optional hikes in a day-hike book, using the numbers for priority-choices.  But, they could easily be more permanent tabs - marking favorite recipes, for example.As temporary markers, they seem to work with most paper - although the package does caution that they will not work with all papers and ink.  For example, I would not consider using these on the thin pages of a bible.  I tried them on a magazine and that worked fine, but after a couple of days, when peeling off, part of the paper peeled off onto the tab sticky surface.The big flaw with these is that the numbers are on only one side of the tab.  This would keep me from purchasing these, as I would like the tab to be adhered to the page of interest - which might very well be the left page in a book - whether due to a chapter beginning there, or a recipe, hike or whatever being on that page.  If you place the tab on the left page of an open book, you can't see the number when the book is closed (unless face down).  Worse, the back side of the tabs are a glossy plastic that you cannot write on, even to work around this design flaw.If the numbers were on both sides, I'd give the product 4 1/2 stars, particularly because the tabs are re-usable. If it were made out of paper and not plastic, I'd give it 5 stars.

This sleek, printer-esque laminator is a workhorse in disquise - it takes up little room and looks modern on a desk, but performs the tasks of a much larger, more cumbersome machine.I manage a bar, and was excited to laminate some of our menus, sidework sheets, helpful hints cards and table tents. I was so pleased, there was never any 'bubbling' as I have experienced with other, older laminators.  The machine is smart - it canse sense the size of paper I'm trying to laminate; it can also auto-reverse the process if the paper were to jam up (though so far, this hasn't happened.) Setup of the unit was extremely easy, and the instruction manual was very clear and easy to follow. My only complaint is that it only came with a starter pack of ten laminating envelopes, and i've already used them all, so now I need to wait for more to arrive in the mail!I definitely recommend this laminator, the final results are crisp and clean, and definitely seem durable. My waitstaff is very excited for the laminating possibilities to come!
I had been looking for something like this for a while and this works great.  Good price and very functional.

Love this. It's so simple to use that I didn't have to read the directions-- tore it out of the box and just happened to have something right next to me that needed gluing, so I tried it. That thing was a fabric animal head that was supposed to be part of a book until my daughter pulled it off. I am a bug about storing documents where I can easily retrieve them.  In the past, I kept important papers in various locations.  When I had to find one, it took a long time to locate it.  The Smead Step Index Organizer has solved my problem.  The file accordions so that it can grow as more papers are placed inside.The first section has two inserts that are suitable for business cards or a small calendar.  A small card is included on which you can list the contents of the file, though I found the limited space impractical for a thorough index of everything contained.There are twelve sections, so the contents can be arranged by month, if necessary.  There's actually another section for miscellaneous papers -- a total of thirteen in all.  There are tabs on all twelve sections for labeling, though the paper tabs themselves are for some reason not included.  The construction of the organizer is sturdy plastic, so it will stand up to lots of use and even the occasional downpour, if you get caught without an umbrella.If you use an attache case or a briefcase, the organizer will fit easily inside. An elastic band slips around a button to close the organizer.  This is for convenience and doesn't offer security against unauthorized removal of materials.The price is reasonable considering how it will put order in your life, whether you use it around the house for recipes, keeping track of bills, or saving reminders; at work; or when traveling.Overall, the organizer does the job of keeping papers handy and at easy reach.  At meetings or at important presentations, easy access to material gives the presenter an air of professionalism.  Struggling with unruly papers at critical times -- or any time for that matter -- makes one look unprofessional, unprepared, and disorganized.

If you won a 900 Pro Mark II you have to buy this set, even if all you have to do is replace 2 or 3 cartridges frequently. great for price paid.nothing special but it works.great for my daughter to get used to the pens.they are long lasting too

After getting tired of the garbage pens stocked in my office supply cabinet a long time ago, I have been trying out different pens in search of a really good pens at an affordable price.I first tried a few Zebra F301 ink pens; I liked these quite a bit, but as I tend to misplace my pens these ended up being a bit expensive, plus I had trouble finding the medium point (1.0mm) I preferred.  I then found theZebra Z-Grip Retractable Ballpoint Pen, 1.0 mm, Black Ink 12-Countwhich wrote pretty well and was cheap.  I have been using these for at least the last four years.Recently I got hooked on the idea of gel pens and tried a few, including theBIC Triumph 730RT Gel Pen (0.7mm), Black, 12ct, thePilot G2 Fine Point, Black Gel Ink Pens, Box of 12, and these uni-ball pens.  It's a close call between the Pilot G-2 and uni-ball 207, but in the end I prefer the 207.  It writes very smoothly, has good writing quality and is a bit crisper than the Pilot, and doesn't smear much for me.  In addition, the pens look a bit more professional than the Pilot G-2, and at least at current prices the 207 is less expensive than the G-2.I've tried three uni-ball 207s out of my box of 12, and so far they have been very consistent.  I'll be sure to update this review if warranted, but at this point I think the uni-ball 207 is a fine pen for about a dollar.Update March 2013: after using these pens along with Pilot G2's and Zebra Sarasa gel pens for the past few months, I'm even more pleased with the uni-ball.  The Pilot and Zebra pens are OK, but just feel mushy when writing compared to the uni-ball.  I highly recommend the uni-ball Signo Gel 207 as an inexpensive pen for every day use.

Somebody has recently started walking a dog around our block and not cleaning up after it. Every morning I exit my house to find a new, steaming landmine of dog feces. What to do? The Lorex LW2731 lets me film out the front of my house and, in theory, catch the culprit in action.My first effort was with the device's automatic motion detection system. No luck; too much routine activity triggered it. For the last several days I've had it in scheduled recording mode, whereby it will record about four hours of material at the time you specify until it fills up. The evil hound has plotted his pooping around my schedule, and thus far avoided detection.I think the intended use of this device is either (1) internal, where motion detection can be used without false triggers, or (2) as a live video feed, not recorded, for use as part of an intercom. I've pretty much given up on project poopcatcher, but I may rewire the device for one of these other purposes, and will report here if it proves more useful.

I used this tape to hang metal crosses and pictures. I wasn't too sure about how it would hold this stuff up. This was easy for me to setup with my mac computer and wifi.  I use it in my home and it is more than adequate to meet my needs with the paper tray.The scan function works well and was easy to use. After recently purchasing a new HP printer, I had to get this ink cartridge.  Compared to the old Lexmark printer I had, this ink cartridge is a bargain. I bought a bottle of Aleene's original Tacky glue about 4 years ago.  I used it for several sewing projects right away - I was using it to hold done some very fine appliqué. The glue stayed usable for 4 years in the original container stored upright at a room temperature.3. The glue is easy to work with, washes off with just soap and water if you clean hands right away4. WORKS GREAT!  I used these in my cookbooks and LOVE them. I imagine they'd be good in text books too, no writing in them means more money at buy back at the end of the semister.

As the product photos show, the display/controller and the weighing platform are connected to each other via a coiled cord that resembles one on a telephone handset.  This arrangement allows weighing packages that are much larger than the platform without covering up the display.  Although the scale works just fine on the two included AAA cells, a universal 120/240V 50/60Hz power adapter is also provided to conserve battery life.  It plugs into the display/controller.  If it's more convenient, the display/controller can be mounted on a nearby wall.From a cold-start, power-on, the scale will take its first reading in about five seconds.  After that, each new weight takes less than one second to stabilize and display.  For a scale that will weigh packages up to 110 pounds, it's surprisingly accurate at the low end, measuring in 1/10 ounce increments.  The US Postal Service has a weight limit of 70 pounds, so this scale should be sufficient for any envelope or parcel that goes through the mail.  Since most people don't press the 150 pound upper weight limits of UPS and FEDEX,  I believe that this scale should be adequate for most mailers and shippers.Although this scale will display weights in all English and metric units, it does not calculate postage or shipping charges.  Just press a button, put your load on the eight-inch-square platform and conveniently and accurately display the weight of any envelope or package in an easy-to-see back-lit digital display.  My Smart Weigh ACE110 Digital Shipping Postal Scale does everything for me that I could expect from a postal scale at a reasonable selling price.The manufacturer sent me this sample in exchange for an honest review, which you have just read.

I have actually all 3 version of the ScanSnap line from the S1100, S1300 and the S1500. If you have large document scanning jobs like 50 pages at a time, then you should order the S1500 as that sheet feeder can handle that volume. However, if you only have 10 sheets, then S1300 is your best bet. I like the S1300 because it is fast and does full duplex and the footprint is very small. With the portable case that you have to buy separately, the scanner becomes very portable and can be thrown into a bag. Some might argue that the S1100 is better for the mobile professional but I find that the single sheet scanning to be cumbersome. The S1100 is half the size but there is so much more capabilities with the S1300 that you could use it as an office scanner also. The S1300 truly can go both ways as a portable device or one that stays on your desk!

This purple binder has a hard exterior with a label on the front and a very small label on the spine that you can write on but again I stress small. The pages are strong and shouldn’t ever rip out. It’s for memory and record keeping as your child progresses from preschool thru 12th grade. Each page has a section to place a photograph and list details like school name, teacher, nickname, age, height and weight. It has a slot in the top for filing away important keepsakes like photos, letters, cards or anything else that is important to you. On the back it has a section for current events, friends, milestones and your child’s signature. I lot of the information might seem a little silly completing but it will be interesting looking back on it 15 years down the road or more. The binder has a smooth band that wraps around it to hold it shut. I like this binder a lot but I wish the exterior was a little different. It has a flat finish that looks nice but picks up finger prints and other marks very easy. I just think a more durable exterior would have been better for something that will be kept for many years. That being said it’s still nice and will serve its purpose.

I'll start with a short review since I just got the printer and have only run 5 prints through it.  I will update in a week or so with more information.Setup and installation was easy.  I have it on my network for my Windows machines and it is connected directly to my Mac Pro.  The install documentation said to get the latest driver for Leopard off of their site, which I did and installed with no problem.  The latest Windows driver was on the installation CD.The reason I called this review "State of the Art" is Epson developed Radiance, the new color-matching technology built into the R1900.  This is the first printer with it, even the current Epson Pro printers don't have it.  [...] has an article about it.The few pictures I have printed are beautiful and they printed very fast.I printed 3 on Epson's Ultra Premium luster 8.5 x 11 paper using Photoshop CS2.  I tried different settings for each print of the same standard color matching target.  All three printed very nice and as expected, a little different.  Using "Photoshop Determines Colors", "Printer Determines Colors" and "No Color Management", with appropriate settings on the printer driver.  So it will be up to you to decide which settings you want to use.Next, as a test I printed a photo, of my daughter, on plain HP Bright White paper.  WOW, is all I can say.  Plain paper and it looked great.For my last test I picked a random paper size, 12" x 12", that I cut from a 13" x 19" sheet of matte paper.  I changed the paper size in the driver and printed.  No problem, it printed just fine and also was beautiful.I plan on getting a roll of paper too.  I've wanted to print some banners, something I couldn't do with my current Canon I9900.So far it is everything I expected it to be. However, I do plan on keeping the I9900 because sometimes I know I will want a dye (not pigment) print (and I still have Canon ink and paper left).I will post more soon.Update 3-10-08:I have been playing with the settings on the driver to see which I like best.  It is a good/bad thing that there are so many settings to play with.  I figure I will eventually figure out which I like best.  There are subtle differences in color, skin tones and gray scales on the gray scales.  If you are interested in the test targets, you can download the printer test images I used from [...]I will start printing some of my real pictures to compare with the I9900 versions.  So I will post another update in a week or two.I tried a roll in the printer.  It was surprising easy to set up and use.  You put the holders on the roll, mount it on the back of the printer, then feed the paper into the printer in the slot on the back.  The printer recognizes you are doing it, then grabs the paper to feed in to the proper starring point.If you print multiple images, the printer spaces them 1" apart.  Unfortunately, Epson still has it's artificial limit length of 44".  There are expensive RIPs (raster image processors) that will allow you to printer longer images, but unless you are going to do this a lot, it can't be worth it.  The cheapest I found is $500.I've decided that I probably will not use the "roll" on the printer.  I want to printer banners every so often, but to use the roll for one print wastes about 10" of paper.  That is the initial feed of about 4" and when you cut it on the back to free it, another 6".  If you are printing many prints on a roll, then it will be worth it and easier.  I suggest (and what I did in my second test), was just cut a 44" of paper (from the roll) and feed it though the (normal) auto paper feeder and that worked fine for the banner without any waste.As for ink usage, I've hardly made a dent with the 10 8x10s, 1 12x12, 3 8.5 x 44 prints I've made.  The banners were not printed at high resolution to save ink for my testing.  I love Amazon, but it's ink prices for this printer are currently way out of line.  Even the Epson store has them for way less.  I hope that changes soon.Update 3-26-08 (my last update).After printing 25 more 8x10 high resolution (and in slow mode for better quality), I finally ran out of ink in one cartridge (and it was the gloss optimizer).  After more reading, I think I used the wrong setting for the gloss and was wasting it on white area outside of the image.  I'm still learning.Some of the other inks are pretty low, so I have stocked up.I still have not printed on a DVD/CD yet, but I'm sure that will be fine.There is not much more for me to say except I am very happy with this purchase and expect to use this printer for the next 3-4 years, when I'm sure something else out there will get my attention.Update 3-22-11Epson just announced the R3000.  By the specs, it looks to be the replacement for the R1900.  The list price of the R3000 is $850 but the R3000 comes with and uses the Epson UltraChrome K3 ink set, which are the larger inks that cost $40-$50, but are 8x larger than the R1900 inks, which meant to me when I got the R3880 (that use the same ink), that the savings in ink will pay for the printer over the R1900.Howard

As a writer who writes first drafts by hand, I am very particular about pens. Normally, I use up 3-4 per week, so I wouldn't use $3 pens for all my writing. But fortunately, these Uni-ball pens can be refilled - and one cartridge is long-lasting. It is fairly thick in diameter, and full from top to bottom, appearing to hold considerably more ink than most pen cartridges do.The pens write very smoothly.  As a left-hander, I find that many pens leave splotches and smears on the paper and stain my fingers as my hand drags over words I have written. Not so, however, with these pens, which dry quickly and do not smear.Skeptical that they are really waterproof, I just dunked an entire page of writing I had done in a sink full of water and let it soak. Amazing! Look Ma, no bleeding or smearing. The pen really is totally waterproof.  This is indeed a great pen for signing checks or legal documents.The pens are quite attractive - neither cheap-looking or expensive looking, with the color of the ink incorporated into the design of the pen so it is easily apparent.They are thicker than the average daily-use pen, but not overly thick. I am 5'5" with short hands and fingers, and they are a perfect fit for me. The textured grip area is firm but comfortable.The attachable clip casing does not fall off, and the clip firmly attaches to a clipboard or notebook.I have been alternating the colors as I write the first draft of this review, so that I can more effectively comment on each of them. The five colors are rich, and because of their blend with black are quite dark, not bright and tacky.The red is a brownish red -an excellent choice for teachers and editors who don't want to use a flashy red for corrections. The purple is a dark almost black purple - a fine alternative to black ink, suitable for business. The bronze is a deep chocolate brown. The blue is a rich deep teal - a lovely color. When I write with blue, my handwriting actually becomes more flowing and legible.Of the five colors, the green is the only one I wouldn't use for business writing - it is brighter than the other colors and conveys the message of "look at me, see how colorful I am." However, if you're a bit superstitious, you might want to carry the green pen in your purse to use for check writing - green is the color of money and associated with prosperity. It's also a good choice for writing messages in cards, and for the grocery and to-do lists which you don't want to forget to carry with you.If colors do not matter to you, you may not want to invest in these pens, but then again, how often do you use pens that really are perfect for your writing needs? They are for me. These may be for you.

This is my third printer from Epson, and I am now pretty well convinced that they manufacture just about the best printers on the market today.  This Epson Workforce 845 is another quiet winner that prints beautifully at a very fast rate.  Plus, the scanner works just as well, delivering high-resolution scans that I can easily manipulate and then e-mail.As with most new printers, you can now print wirelessly from your iPhone or other smart device, and while I have not personally tried out this feature, the setup was very straightforward and quicker than I expected. I was surprised how cleanly these cards separate.  You get ten business cards per sheet.  As soon as you are done printing, you just fold each crease inward (with the front side facing you), and *snap*, the cards separate very cleanly, leaving a very clean edge.  There is no rough perforation left at all.Designing your cards is pretty easy if you are comfortable with MS Word or OpenOffice.  I was able to create double sided, full bleed business cards in OpenOffice with a reasonable amount of effort.Pros:- Nice, thick, bright card stock.- Very clean edges.- Very easy to separate cards (they literally snap apart with little effort).- Affordable way to do short runs of color business cards.- You can download Word templates online easily (login required).- Double side layouts are easy, just create another document with the template, flip over your page, and print.- Good ink adhesion with my Canon ink jet.  No smearing, quick drying.Cons:- This pack only comes with eight sheets.  This leaves little room for practice runs for your layout.  I recommend printing just one card per try until you get it right.  This means you'll print into the upper left card the first time, then have to edit your document to use the next square (so you can reuse the same sheet).- Not the best solution for large quantities--but this is pretty obvious.

The Epson Workforce Pro WP-4530 Color Inkjet Wireless All-In-One (print, copy, fax, scan) is an excellent product that satisfies all of my needs (at least to-date).Everything about the product -- from its packaging through its many product features -- represents high quality. It came in well-protected packaging, yet was still very easy to unpack. Set-up to my network was fast and easy thanks to the excellent Quick Start directions provided, as well as to the CD Rom that included all of the necessary software.  Further, the WP-4530 has all of the features I require. Not only does it print, copy, fax and scan, it enables you to perform each of these functions two-sided automatically. And, its paper tray holds over 300 sheets before needing to add more paper. As to speed, Epson claims that this product is the world's fastest auto two-sided printer. I can't, obviously, substantiate that claim; but I can say it more than satisfies my need for speed.All in all, I'd highly recommend the Epson Workforce Pro WP-4530 when you have a need for a reasonably priced, high quality Color Inkjet Wireless All-In-One.

These hanging magnetic storage pockets are a great aid in helping to organize our mail.  The magnets are very strong and, even when I accidentally shoved something into one of the pockets, the organizer didn’t budge an inch.  There is a space to label each pocket—whether in-coming, out-going, bills to be paid, or whatever.  Rather than stack mail in piles on your desk or a countertop, you can simply sort it and drop it in the appropriate pocket when it arrives.  This will free up space on the horizontal surfaces; all you need do is choose where you’ll hang it.  The simple design on a neutral grey background makes this both complementary to most interior décor and an attractive means of organizing.  Just the right size with great style.  A perfect choice that meets our needs perfectly.  I’d love for them to design a complimentary organizer that’s large enough to hold magazines and file folders.  They make one that would work but the pattern is different and not as aesthetically pleasing to me.

My HP printer produces acceptable black & white and color documents with these ink cartridges. The quality of the prints is not great but presentable. I rarely print photos so I leave that part of evaluation to other reviewers. All I said is true, when the cartridges work. When a cartridge malfunctions and you try to make a warranty claim with HP, you have a problem, because the HP ink cartridge warranty isn't worth the paper it is printed on. This happened to me recently. Previously, I bought my replacement ink cartridge at a retail store. Several months into use, I got an error message that "there is a problem with the Tri-Color cartridge." The ink level was half-full a few days ago. I followed the help menu and cleaned the print head and copper contacts numerous times, to no avail. I read the HP ink cartridge warranty, checked the expiration day on the cartridge and found that it expires on 1/1/2012, almost a full year from today. I decided to make a warranty claim with HP.  After spending a good half an hour talking to a man in India, I was told that because my printer was out of warranty, HP would not warrant the ink cartridge, even thought I bought the replacement cartridges separately from the printer in a retail store.  I wound up throwing out the malfunctioning cartridge and bought a new one.  I wasn't happy. See my comment below for a full account of what happened.

I love the OfficeJet Pro!  It was easy to set up; even the wireless set up only took a few minutes.  I really like being able to print from anywhere in the house without being tethered to the printer!  The print quality is excellent; it even does a very nice job on photos.  The copy function is flawless.  The scanner seems a bit overly complicated to use, but I scan infrequently so the frustration may very well be the result of user error.The only issue I have with this printer is that, in addition to the 940 ink cartridges, it requires two 940 print heads(black/yellow and magenta/cyan). The print heads look very much like ink cartridges for some of the smaller HP printers.  There is an expiration date about a year out printed on the print head, but my experience has been they never make it a full year.  I live in a major city and have access to loads of office supply stores, but I cannot find the 940 print heads locally at Staples, Office Depot, Office Max, et. al.  I can order them from Amazon, but it's very difficult to wait for shipment when you're in the middle of a print job and the print head goes bad.Calling for customer service is a hassle.  The call center appears to be in India, and the reps struggle with any English they are not reading from their screen.Overall, I like the printer - but the customer service and the short lifespan of the print heads are a definite minus.

I received this product through the Amazon Vines Program.  I currently have an HP Officejet 7410 All in one and was looking for something that was a bit smaller.  The Kodak ESP 7250 really surprised me with the size and ease of setup!  From the time I started opening up the box until I had the unit up and running with my wireless network and software installed on my laptop took a total of 33 minutes. Here are the plus features of the unit:1.  Easy to install.  The instructions are very straight forward and short.  I actually completed most of the setup just by looking at the unit and following the pictures.  I only referred to the written instructions PRIOR to powering it up to ensure that I had done verything correctly.2.  Wireless networking was simple and works great!  No more need to have your printer located somewhere where cables can be run to connect the printer to the network or to the computer!  Loading the software onto the laptop and desktop was quick and it immediately located and installed the drivers for the printer on the wireless network.3. Size is much smaller than the HP 7410 printer, though the HP includes a Fax (something that this all in one does not) and the HP also has a sheet feeder (something that the Kodak unit also does not have).  Still, it is about half the size which helps to locate the unit in smaller locations.4.  There is a seperate photo paper slot that handles either 4X6 or 5X8 photo paper.  This is seperate from the regular paper tray and you can have both loaded at the same time.  A selection on the printer software tells the printer which paper to draw upon.5.  Scanning surface works very well and I feel is a bit better in quality than the HP.6. The included software for working with your pictures is simple and does a nice job in the printing of pictures.  I was very pleased with each of the pictures that printed and they were dry and ready to use as soon as they came off the printer.  No smudging or running ink!!Surprises with the Printer:The only surprise was that as soon as I loaded the software onto my laptop, it found that there was an update to the firmware for the printer.  Since this is a brand new model, that did surprise me.  However, the laptop was able to download and install the firmware update for the printer over the wireless network quickly and everything worked fine the first time through.Negatives:1.  As with any ink printer, this is not the quietest unit in the world.  The unit does vibrate and make noise as it aligns itself and as it prints.  So, insure that you put it onto a stable surface!!2.  Although it says that it is an all in one printer, it does not support Fax!!  Yes, that is a dying feature, but it is still one in use.3.  No feeder tray does make it a bit less usefull if you are trying to copy several pages at once.  However, the included two sided capablity does at least ensure that you are able to use both sides of the paper automatically if you so desire.All in all, I am very pleased with this printer and it will be replacing my HP All in One.

Epson WorkFouce 630 Injet Printer and ScannerI find this to be an average printer with the software being below average.QualityOut of the box there is a lot of plastic wrap and tape that has to be removed. It is mostly plastic including the gears and runners. I don't print an awful lot so it should last a while. The control panel, interface, and connections are easy to get to and use. However, the output tray is right above the paper cassette making it a bit cumbersome to load paper.SetupSetup and install was pretty straight forward for me. I tried both the wired and wireless network connections and both went flawlessly. Using the control panel on the printer wireless setup and security was pretty easy. It can also be setup through your PC. I normally setup my devices with static IPs to which I had no problems doing with this printer.Printer cartridges were easy to install. However, the software utility says they are empty (see below)SoftwareI have yet to see great software from hardware manufactures and this is no exception. While the install went ok and really didn't take that long the first thing I noticed was that my computer acts differently. I have a few problems with the display (why I have no idea), it is a lot slower and the settings on some of my regularly used software are gone. How could that be?Another annoyance is that the program startup icons are installed in several application groups making it difficult to find what you need. The manual icon is installed on the desktop but with no image.When printing, the Epson Status Monitor shows that I am out of ink on the first print. Of course the Buy Epson Ink button is highlighted. It is constantly saying it is attempting to connect yet it still works.Updates look like the Windows 95 interface and take a long time with multiple install runs. Makes one a bit nervous as to what is being installed.If you run uninstall it does not remove everything like the manual and its no image icon on the desktop.ScanningI like this feature. Not only does it scan like a regular scanner but it has an auto feed feature which works really well even for scanning documents to files on your computer. However, the paper can be slightly off for a slightly crooked scan.It comes with a third party software called ABBYY FineReader for character scanning. While it appears to do a good job converting the characters it adds page/section breaks. I wouldn't expect any formatting so now I have to spend time removing all the extra stuff. A huge annoyance is an always started and running piece of software just for the license. It won't run without it.One disappointment is no slide scanning.PrintingPrinting is fairly quick but of average quality. Printing a photo is ok, they are slightly grainy, especially light colors. If it is hanging on your wall it will look good each time you walk by but for high quality printing this is not that great.Printing under 8.5 x 11One problem with smaller paper or envelopes is that the paper cassette centers the paper. But when used by software like Microsoft Word the driver doesn't automatically take that into consideration. Even though it appeared correct in preview, the printing was off and will need to be adjusted manually.Sample PaperIt came with two sheets (yes, that's right only two) of Epson photo paper, one glossy and one matt. I have no idea which is which because the glossy is no where near other glossy paper I have used for photos. So the glossiest of the two was not photo quality at all.Memory CardsIt has slots for the popular memory cards. However, again with the software, it automatically connected my computer to the card reader so when the printer is off, or there is no card, it shows the disconnected drive. That can contribute to slowing down your computer and creating problems. These BiC's, which made their first American appearance in 1959, were designed exceptionally if not bizarrely well. And I don't mean in a quaint, historical way. These pens respect principles of space, form, structure, density, and gravity. Because of their hexagonal shape, they require minimal plastic while also retaining a surprising strength (try snapping one), and the hexagonal grip points give the pens impressive writing stability. A tiny hole drilled in the barrel's body keeps the air pressure the same both inside and outside the pen. Gravity feeds the thick ink down a tube to a free-spinning ball bearing that was manufactured within a fraction of a micron of accuracy. The result is that when the pen is pressed against paper, the ink slides out cleanly and, well,... perfectly. It's not only one of the most inexpensive pens, it's also probably the most efficient pen, with a single pen able to write over 100,000 words (or about 2 novels). A true masterpiece of design. I'm not the only one who thinks so. They have their own exhibit in the Museum of Modern Art.This particular pen is a slight variation on the original, with a slightly wider foundation and using slightly more ink (hence the "Bold"). It's still great, you just probably wouldn't be able to write 2 novels with it.
You cannot go wrong with the price, speed or output of this small footprint laser printer that works either via USB or Wireless.

This is a side-by-side comparison between the Canon MX452 and the Canon MX522 PIXMA printersCanon Office Products MX452 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner, Copier and FaxBasically, here you go:(I tried to create this as a chart, but Amazon's text box won't keep my formatting, so bear with me...)PRICE:PIXMA MX452Retail: $99.99Amazon: $84.99 (4/28/2013)PIXMA MX522Retail: $149.99Amazon: $129.99 (4/28/2013)_____________________SPECIFICATIONS:MX452Weight: 19 poundsDimensions: 15.2"x 18.1"x 7.9"Color:  Matte BlackMX522Weight: 22 poundsDimensions: 15.2"x 18.1"x 7.9"(Note: the Canon website lists a larger size for this printer, and Amazon lists them as being identical. This cable was not necessary for either set up, but I did have trouble with their "quick WiFi set up"--on both printers.Both printers have quick-set-up for connecting to your WiFi home network.  You press your router's network button and the printer is supposed to find it and hook up to it.  The trouble is, neither did.  It wasn't that they didn't "see" the router/network.  They did, and both showed it.  But they couldn't make that connection on their own.  We went to the Canon website (as instructed by the little flyer(s) inside the package(s) with the manuals.) We followed those directions (which were basically the same as the instructions that popped up on the screens of the printers), and had no luck.  I finally went into an alternative network setup option and found the router and inputted the security code and both printers hooked into the network without a problem.  Seems something about the quick-start didn't work with my Verizon router.  Neither printer required any physical connection to the router nor any computer for Network set up.There are lots of options for both printers--the trouble is, with the 452, it's hard to maneuver the menus because it is hard to see the screen.  The 522 was easy and seemed simpler (even though it has a few more options).The optional software has printing programs for photos, etc.  Typical for all Canon and other big-name companies.The face recognition software was pretty neat--and kind of creepy.Both can do borderless photo printing, are optimized for Canon photo papers, and claim that with the combination of Canon inks combined with Canon papers, your photos will last up to 100 years in an archival-quality photo album.  (Up to?  Not much of a promise...if they said, "at least", we'd be talking...)Auto scan modes, auto document fix, Movie Print, 30 Sheet Auto Document Feeder, and more are on both printers, and work equally well (but I do think the 522 is a tiny bit faster).The 452 does NOT have full duplex printing. My current printer has this, and once you have had it, you don't want to go back.The Fax programs are the same, and work equally well.  Of course, the menu/caller ID is far easier to see with the 522.  Transmission speeds on both are (black) 3 seconds per page and (color) i minute per page.  Both have a 50 page memory, and both have modems that transmit at 33.6 Kbps.As a Copier, both Reduce/Enlarge from 25% to 400%.  Both have menus that allow you to lighten/darken the copies.  Copy speeds are (color) 4.7 ipm.The Scanner is identical on both printers.  Both have a Scanning Element that is a Contact Image Sensor (CIS), with resolutions of 1200x2400 dpi (optical), 19,200x19,200 (interpolated) with ADF (Auto Document Feeder):600x600 dpi (optical).  Both have a max color depth of 48-bit internal/24-bit external, and the same max document size of 8.5x11.7" on the flatbed scanner and 8.5x14" on the ADF (Auto Document Feeder)Standard Interface is identical, except that the 522 includes PictBridge. This is not listed for the 522.Both printers can use the XL and XXL ink cartridges.On the Canon Website, they have some apps that are pretty neat--the printing apps are the iEPP (Print pictures, Scan items), and Mobile Printing (Print Documents, Web Pages, and Images).  Both work with iPhone and can be downloaded directly from the App Store for free.Because the 452 has the 2-Line LCD display with NO BACKLIGHT (How did you miss this one, Canon?) it is quite difficult to read.  I have pretty bad vision, and had a tough time getting through the menus.The 522 has a very bright and clear LED display.  It's not a touch screen (that would be the one improvement I'd like to see).  It is very easy to read and use, and for those like me with bad vision, it's a blessing.Both printers have fax, capability, copying capability, Scanning capability, and Caller ID/Call block rules for the fax.Both printers have built-in templates for graph paper, ruled notebook paper, children's printing paper, schedules, calendars, to-do lists, and more.  Getting to the menu options for these is much easier on the 522, but isn't too bad for the 452.The Quiet feature is wonderful.  I don't know how they do it, but both printers ran quieter and the "beep" and "alarm" volumes are very adjustable.They are each quite capable printers, both are quiet, quick, and do an excellent printing job.  BUT there are many differences.If you are looking for a utilitarian-looking printer, the PIXMA MX452 is a good choice, but the screen is not very easy to read, and you have to do a LOT of scrolling to get through the menus.  If you're more like me, and like easy-to-read menus and the sleeker shiny surface and/or you are a Google-Cloud Printer or double-sided printer, you will be better served with the Canon PIXMA MX522.I took a bunch of pictures of them side-by-side, during the set-up.  I will post them on the Customer Images section of this page.I hope this review helped you out--sometimes we don't realize we "want" a feature until we have seen it elsewhere.  (For me, the Google-Cloud Print was my "surprise" feature--but now that I have seen and used it, I know I'll use it again.)For my use, which is typical home-use and school-use, I'd opt for the MX522.  It's 50 dollars more expensive, but I know I'd save that in paper (with the duplex) in no time.  It looks better--more sleek, and the LED screen is bright and looks nice, too.
