This fast and efficient grinder-style sharpener performs as advertised.  It has an easily removable shaving reservoir with an auto-shut-off switch, which might make this a good fit for a classroom as well as a home office.The feature that stands out with this product the most is how it is able to detect when sharpening has completed.  Upon inserting a dull or new pencil, the sharpener will begin grinding the pencil to sharpness.  When sharpening is done, you can feel that it stops grinding.  It seems to work every time.  However, if you insert the sharpened pencil again, you will end up grinding it down further.  This is one of the biggest issues with sharpeners like this -- the way they will grind a pencil down to nothing in seconds.  I think this product solves that problem well.Removing the shaving reservoir is very easy.  There's a sort of bubble catch in the front that allows you to easily grip it for removal.  It then slides right back on and clicks into place.The product is about the same size as any of these sharpeners -- about 2 man-sized fists.

I'm quite pleased with the results I get with this scanner. Please note, I'm only using it to scan oversize images from books that I cannot scan with my regular printer (it only does 8 1/2" X 11" standard size). I am not using it for negatives or any other print work. I do feel it's a great value for the money since scanners can be ridiculously expensive. Is it super high quality for $99? No. It's a printer that you would expect to get for the cost. Compared with going to Kinkos (now FedEx), I am saving myself $10 per scan so I'm happy about how much money this Epson is saving me (I have 50+ scans to do!). Since the plastic is not built for high durability (the lid, particularly) treat it with care and it should keep going. Manhandle this scanner and you'll be out $99 real quick. I had no trouble with the software, it loaded up & was easy to use without incident. This Epson gets the job done for me at a very reasonable price.
Good quality paper clips, the coating is nice and I really like the variety of colors.  I think the price per tub is a fair price.

The first thing you'll notice about the Epson WorkForce 845 Wireless Color Printer is the excellent packaging.  Most companies package well enough to keep the equipment from being damaged in transit, but Epson has found a way to keep the printer in one piece AND make it easy to get out of the box.  While the printer is by no means small, it's lightweight.  It's easy to pick up and carry if you need to reposition it.Dual paper trays is a nice touch.  You could dedicate one tray to plain letter size paper, and the second tray could be used for legal size or photographic paper. Unfortunately the trays feel flimsy, so you'll want to be careful while you're refilling them or adjusting the paper guides.The ink cartridges have thoughtful packaging, too.  They are vacuum sealed in clear plastic with a notch for easy tear opening. Lift the scanning bed, and you'll find it's very easy to load the four (black, yellow, cyan and magenta) cartridges into the ink well.  Once the ink cartridges are clicked into place, the printer will "prime" them for up to five minutes (mine took about 90 seconds.  Priming does use some ink, but does not automatically print a test page unless asked.  This is much faster and wastes far less ink than the obligatory alignment, print test page, copy test page that you go through when you change the ink on a similar HP printer.Setting up the printer (language, date, time) and the software on the computer, was fast and painless.  You will need to set up the software on every PC that will be using the WiFi print, scanning, and/or network fax features.  If you have a visitor that just needs to print something from a laptop and is not on your network, then a USB cable will enable them to send documents to the printer.  Even if you're setting up the printer for WiFi use, you are instructed to connect the USB cable between the printer and computer during the software set up.  The USB cable is not included in the packaging.  In fact, the USB cable has not been included with the last four printers I've bought; it's something you probably already have on hand though.Scanning is easier with the Epson than with the HPs I've owned.  It's very simple.  Open the scanning option on the desktop; put the document on the glass; preview the document; click scan.  My HP Print Center always assigns a proprietary file extension that has to be converted later, and saves to an inconvenient folder. Epson lets you choose to save your scans at .jpgs or .pdfs or other common file types and lets you choose to park them in My Pictures or My Documents.Faxing seems to be going the way of the dinosaur, but I have a need for it and will use this feature often.  With the installed software, you can open the Fax Utility and easily set up a list of Speed Dial numbers, or Groups.  It's much easier to set this up from the computer than the touch screen.  I found the touch screen somewhat difficult to use, even though I have small fingers it was easy to fat finger the numbers, especially since the touch screen is not particularly responsive.  Often I had to touch a selection or a number several times before hearing the beep signifying the key had been entered.  Despite my lack of love for the touch screen dial pad, I was able to successfully send faxes from the Epson Workforce 845.  Once you enter the number and hit the enter button, the machine scans the document into memory, then it dials, connects, and sends the fax.  Leave the machine ON in Auto Receive mode to receive faxes at any time.Printing seems average.  The print quality was good, but not exceptional.  While the printer is definitely not slow, I didn't find it remarkably fast either.  In their literature, Epson makes a statement that printing photos will not be as fast as printing documents, but that is not unique to Epson or this model.  Photo printing always takes longer than document printing; that's just a fact of life.  The Epson Workforce 845 is not a quiet printer; there is a lot of clicking, rattling noise while it's queuing up a sheet of paper in the feed.  It's not unusually noisy for this type of printer; however, if this is your first printer / scanner / fax unit, you may be surprised by how much noisier they are than the compact printer only units.To sum up, this is a very nice mid-price printer, scanner, fax combination unit.  It has the size and many of the features previously found only on printers in the $350 and up price range.  The basic functions are not overly complex or difficult to learn/use.Recommended.

We bought a dedicated photo printer for our preschool.  Epson XP-600.  It was smallish and held photo paper in its trays. Wow, I didn't know there are differences in index cards.  I was surprised these are so thin and not as heavy weight as the ones I usually use.I write on both sides on the cards.  With these cards, when I write on the first side, I can see and feel the imprint of my writing on the second side. The kit contains materials to produce four bound documents of ten pages each.  I think you could bind up to 20 pages (40 with front/back printing). I was surprised when I started using this pencil, because each time I touched the lead to paper and started to write the pencil seemed to give a little...it turns out that the tip is spring-loaded.  If you are like me you don't expect the lead on a pencil or even the tip of a pen to move at all when you write.  I think that the design of this pencil is such that there is a spring-loaded piece that holds the lead, and whenever you push the lead onto paper the spring gives a little, turns the lead a bit, minimizes the likelihood that the lead will break, and turns the lead a little maintaining a somewhat sharper lead than you'd have otherwise.  While this is interesting engineering, it does take some getting used to, as I mentioned above.Well, the lead is already fairly narrow, 0.5 mm, so I don't really see the need for a sharpened tip, but, well, a 0.5 mm line is good for most casual pencil work.Once the lead is on the paper and you have applied a little pressure it writes like any other mechanical pencil, but every time you pick up the tip the unit clicks and you feel the spring when you put tip to paper again.  Maybe I' a little picky, but I find this clicking and the movement of the lead holder to be distracting, and as a result I don't like the pencil any better than other mechanical or wooden pencils that I own.So, all in all it's a nifty idea, and the engineering shows creativity, but that combo didn't sell me...not that a pencil will make or break my life or anything, but, as I mentioned above, I don't really care for the action.It's OK.  It looks nice, feels good in your hand, and works fine, but I just don't care for the clicking and moving point. Sorry.  3 stars.

Also, it is not rigid, meaning it can be bent a little to get into your small carryon luggage.You get 2 of these organizers for $14.  This is the reason for 4 stars versus 5 stars. I have not used a wrist rest for several years because my last one was foam based and with a cloth cover and not only did it get icky grimy (though I could wash the cover), I now realize that it wasn't actually supportive enough. This is an impressive sturdy piece and I'm really happy to have it.Pros:1. Heavy. Surprisingly heavy. It's not going to easily travel around on the desk, and it's very supportive.2. But appropriately squishy. Not very squishy, mind you, but it's not a brick, is what I mean. It does give if you need it to. (But you don't... you're not putting that much weight on it. It's not hard, is really the point. It's comfortable to rest on.)3. Oh wow. I didn't notice at first that there's a plastic film on the bottom that can be removed, making this hold on to the desk surface even better than just its weight. (No adhesive or anything, just a rubbery surface, instead of slick. It does not slide on my wooden desk. I have to pick it up and reposition it.)4. It will be easy to clean.Cons:1. Well, not much. But I have a metal Mac keyboard and this rest is about two inches longer than the keyboard. I first centered the wrist rest with the keyboard, and it was getting in the way of my mouse reach. But now it's off center and it's bigger than I need, but it's not in the way of the mouse.2. The bottom part will pick up gunk. Don't peel off the plastic if you don't want. And I'm sure it's still cleanable; worst case is that it might become less tacky over time.Love it.

My dad kept telling me to get this glue, he loves this stuff.  He showed me some blue jeans he had used to glue patches on telling me he had glued the patches on 2 years ago. These labels are of good quality and just what they should be. Bankers Box had a moving and storage box design  than allowed the sides of the box to fold over and become the top. That all-in-one design was a good idea except it left an opening in the middle of the box top. Now Bankers Box has gone back to the preferable separate tops but figured out that they can still make the top and bottom of the box one piece if they design the box with the top attached to one of the side seams. All the assembler has to do is cut through the perforation where the top is attached and then assemble the boxes normally.  This is great for retailers who now need less room  to store boxes than before and great for businesses who like to keep back up boxes on hand.These are good boxes. They have about the same  volume as a box that holds ten reams of paper, or maybe a little more, but they have a couple inch smaller footprint and are a little taller. The lips of the tops are too narrow.  Even a half inch  wider lip would add greater stability to the box and moving the hand holds down a half inch would not in any way make the box less easy to carry  or hurt the integrity of the box.  Cutting the top off the box is a good idea but it leaves a ragged edge so that even a new box looks used. The cardboard in these boxes is thinner than the cardboard in used for copy paper cases.  These boxes will bend out of square even when new.  I have them stacked 4 high now. I'm not sure they will not start to collapse soon. I think there might be a manufacturing process problem too. One of my boxes was not glued together because a piece of cardboard stamped out of a flap had fallen into the glue preventing the seams from meeting. Extraneous cardboard should be blown or shaken from the box well before the gluing stage of manufacture.I like these boxes so much after I got my 1st 10 I ordered 30 more.
the 3M Large Mouse Pad with Gel Wrist Rest is a perfect addition to my desk.  the pad help prevent carpel tunnel, and the surface is perfect for optical mouse.
The ink has always worked well. I tried generic, but Canon ink is far superior. The best way to purchase is a 5 pack.

The labels are a very good thickness, have durability, and work like the common name product "Av..y". I bought 2 packs these are great have not used a lot but, have not broke and they come already presharpened and the price was good!

This nice Wilson Jones binder is listed as being an "ultra duty" binder. I can see nothing special that makes it an ultra duty binder! What I did see that was a real plus is the easy to open rings! We had a Panasonic unit before this and were never very happy with it. It was always staticy and the controls and buttons were hard to see.  This GE unit is very clear and the buttons are easy to see and use.  Everything lights up - our old phones did not.This is very easy to set up and use.  The only feature I do not like is the size of the "off/cancel" button - I'd like that a little larger, but other than that we have no complaints about the phones.Programming the various functions was very easy - I didn't even have to look in the manual except when it came to the speaker phone button. That makes sense, so we'll get used to it quickly.My wife gets very annoyed by 411 charges, so that Google-411 should turn out to be very handy (though we haven't used it enough to say whether it's accurate or complete - I would think it would be).Even though our house isn't all that large, we do like the monitoring and intercom features.  We could just shout, but if someone is sick in bed it will be nice to use those features. Having just reviewed another binder from the same designer/manufacturer, my reaction to both binders was still the same. Quality product. Clear and crisp. Worked great in my laminating machine. Great price and perfect size for business cards or ID cards.

Labels are gorgeous, the templates need much improvement.  The labels are perfect, the problem lies with the fact that there are no blank downloadable templates available to use for them.  Avery has online templates but they are not blank so you have to use the designs available or make your own. Five Star makes good notebooks, and this is no exception. The cover is durable vinyl, the paper is the right quality and width (college ruled) and the two interior pockets are useful. I always appreciate any new design for convenience and the three holes that can (optionally) extend from the (heavy cardboard) back of the notebook could be helpful.The idea is that you can reverse the notebook so the spiral faces toward the opening of your larger binder/notebook. We had an older Board Brothers calendar organizer and loved it.  At some point along the way someone opted to clean it with window cleaner, ruining it.  Since it was on its last legs I opted to try out this new one.Here's what I like:Cork liner is thicker than my previous board so I can actually pin things to it without worrying about them falling off.Color tagged corners helps differentiate tasks/people/dates so it's easy to divvy up the board.The rest, less than satisfying:Board was thick so it protrudes from the wall more than a typical wall board profile.The supplied pen was thick and hard to write clearly with.The surface was thick vinyl and rip/puncture prone.Mounting system was flimsy.Ultimately I think there are better white board organizing centers out there and wouldn't recommend this one.

Our family has had a number of All-In-One printers over the years.  We do a lot of general printing from our computers, a little scanning/saving, and a few copies here and there.  We use both black and white and color (although I try to print more with black and white to save on the more expensive color cartridges). Although the box makes no claims of having special tamper features, the description does. Five Star notebooks have been my go to brand for over 20 years.  About four years ago when I was in need of a better way to organize my materials for a CCD class I teach and I stumbled on this NoteBinder and it has been my preferred teaching binder ever since.  Overall, I think this note binder is well done, but there are a few things that I dislike about it, so I'm going to address them first.While I think it's pretty neat that I can flip the cover to the back of the note binder like you would on a note book, that very feature is where my issues of dislike begin.  Because this isn't an ordinary binder, there isn't really a spine on this notebinder that you can easily grasp.  I don't like that I have to grab it between the rings.  I wish they had used some sort of rubber flexi material for the flexible spine and placed it on the outside of the three rings.  Despite my original misgivings about the fabric spine, it has held up over time.  The rings of this binder are plastic and are called "Tech Lock Rings".  They are pretty easy to open and close and  they can stand up to the kind of abuse dished out by a middle school student.  The divider and folder pages of this note binder are pretty sturdy, but after a few years of use, the pocket seams may start to separate.  I just depends on how much you put in thos pockets.  Some of my folders have split while others are still in perfect condition.This note binder has many positive attributes.  Because of the "Tech Lock Rings" you're not going to have that age old problem of papers slipping out of the rings thanks to those run of the mill openings in the metal rings.  Papers won't be slipping out of this note binder unless they're ripped out.  The cover of this note binder certainly stands up to use and abuse.  The front cover is the same plastic material that I've come to love on the regular Five Star notebooks.  The folder pages (pending the seams hold up to use and abuse) offer useful functions such as index card storage, pocket folder (with a nifty little corner flap to keep pages from falling out in the event that the notebinder is inverted), and file folders which can easily accommodate 10 pages, but I have managed to fit as many as 20 pages in these folders at times.I like this binder for the purpose which I am going to use it (housing lesson plans and carrying worksheets for the class).  I don't think I'd like this notebinder if I were looking to use this for note taking for a class since it's not exactly left-handed friendly.

I was excited to try this binding kit out, because as a landscaper I thought it would be very cool to send bound portfolios/ information about my business to potential clients who I am about to meet with. I figured that would help people realize how much they definitely want to work with me, before I even showed up. :)Unfortunately, after creating four booklets of nine pages each (wanted to save a bit of paper in case my printer smudged ink or something) and twisting the wire to bind them, I was "over" it. But if you want to bind multiple documents a week, save some effort and get yourself one of those binding machines.

This is a sturdy staple remover made of chrome plated steel and a small part that actually gets under the staple and lifts it out that appears to be heat-treated steel, which is even stronger.  It removed staples up to 3/4" without strain.  It is almost overkill to use it to remove smaller staples that are just holding several sheets of paper together.  I also tested it on 5/8" furniture staples that were solidly embedded in hardwood.  It removed those staples with ease as well.  It is strong enough however to occationaly break staples that are embedded in hardwood.  Several times I needed to pull one embedded end of the staple with pliers, but I did not regard this as a problem; rather, it is a testament to how strong this devise is.  I also doubt that this would ever happen with staples embedded in paper.The only potential problem occurs when you are first using it.  Sometimes extra force is necessary to push down on the chrome plated handle which can be a little slippery if you do not apply the downward force without gripping the handle with your fingers curled underneath it to provide stability.  If you just use your palm to push down on the handle, your hand can slide off and the remover may slide forwards away from you.  This happened to me twice before I realized how to use it properly.  It did not cause any injury, but I imagine it could be a source of minor injury in rare occasions to new users.The product does what it is supposed to do in an almost effortless manner and with the quality of its construction, it should last more than a lifetime.  I am a retired executive and if I had been aware of this product before retiring, I would have bought one for my Administrative Assistant to make her life a bit easier.

It seems the high page yield Epson is flaunting with this printer is mostly a gimmick.  Unless you aren't buying it for the laserjet comparable yields, or can get by with very faded printing (even from greyscale) in the printer's economy mode, stick with laserjet.I've been using an HP laserjet for years.  And while it's held up well, and been pretty reliable, $80 per cartridge (full SRP is actually at or over $100 depending on who you ask) was just rediculous.  I'd tried recycled cartridges, but what you're saving in cost, they more than make up for by not putting nearly as much ink in the cartridge.  I only got about 150 good pages from the last replacement cartridge I bought.  So, when I saw an inkjet advertising the same print yield as my laserjet, but with original manufacturer cartridges that cost about the same as the recycled cartridges I've bought, I was intrigued.I commenced reading reviews, both user and "professional", though the term "professional" should be used very lightly these days, as it seems most "professional" reviews have devolved into little more than product publicity for the manufacturer, evaluations based on specs rather than actual experience with and testing of the product.  Aside from your typical bad units seeming a bit overly represented in user reviews - which is common online, if not understandable that a disproportionate number of people with problems would feel compelled to go through the trouble of writing a review, compared to those finding the unit to perform to their expectations - I found the reviews at the time to be convincingly positive.  Enough so that I figured I'd give it a try, afterall, the entire printer cost only a little more than one of the four cartridges I needed for my HP.I have no extensive expertise with printers:  my experience is mostly limited to the dozen or so models I've personally owned over the years. I've only printed about 50 pages with this Epson thus far as well, which is hardly a test of the build's reliability or even the ink capacity of the starter cartridges it comes with.  BTW, if you don't already know, the starter cartridges included with this printer are estimated at only 1000 pages for black and white, not the 2400 (black and white) or 1200 (color) pages the standard XL cartridges are supposed to be capable of.  I'm still on the starter cartridges.I should also qualify this by saying that I'm going on the assumption that the 2400 yield number being so aggressively advertised only applies to printing in greyscale, in fast, economy mode, not normal mode, which is probably closer to the quality most might expect.  I couldn't find any clarification in the literature either, what little there is.  Remember when printers used to come with 1/2 inch thick books telling you everything you actually needed to know?Text in fast economy, greyscale mode is very faded.  Rather than black, it's a medium gray that looks about like a laserjet on an empty cartridge, or more precisely, like when I keep printing with the laserjet, well past the point it says to change the cartridge, because my replacement was bad or out of stock and recycled cartridges aren't very good about warning you ahead of time when they're about empty.The Epson's normal mode is what I'd reasonably expect of economy inkjet printing, based on other inkjets I've owned.  So, it seems Epson didn't reinvent the wheel, nor are the XL ink cartridges the reason for them being able to tweak the numbers for inkjet to be in line with your lower end laserjets in terms of print capacity.  It seems they're just using a lot less ink, which really shows in the quality of the print job.  I tried printing a couple coupons off the internet in economy mode; they were so faded, all but the barcode was illegible.  Generally, text is dark enough to read, if the font isn't too small or thin.  And I don't think it's too light for shipping labels, but I haven't confirmed with the USPS that their scanners can pick up the barcode or not.  Based on the intensity of black, I'd assume if printing in something more realistic, like normal mode, you'd need to half your page expectations.  This is probably not the best printer for photographs, though the high quality setting does look reasonably good from what I've seen of it's handling some simple graphics.The printer is extremely fast, at least spitting out the pages themselves is; preping the print seems to take just as long as most others.  I also expect the print jobs use less energy than any laserjet, and assuming you don't turn off the printer when not in use, I suspect it uses less energy in standby too, as it doesn't run automated checks every so often like my HP.I'm not too thrilled about having to get a special device to be able to reprogram the ink cartridges just to be able to use all the ink you're paying for.  But, if I didn't consider printers solely on the grounds of unwanted or unnecessary design constraints, there wouldn't be any to choose from.BTW, these cartridges also expire and Epson recommends replacement after 6 months, whether they're depleted or not, for best print quality anyway.
This is the perfect item to line my Fellows shredder with. It is light weight and seems quite durable. Highly recommend.

To be honest, I feel a little silly reviewing file folders as they are exactly what they claim to be. The colors in real life are just as vibrant as they appear in the picture on my computer monitor and the additional space for the label is wonderful. The only downside I can see is if you were mixing these file folders in with other file folders that have tabs that don't stick up quite as high, as the height of these tabs might obscure any lower-cut tabs behind them but this can easily be solved by either switching to these file folders completely (which I know might not be the ideal solution) or don't put a middle tab folder directly behind another middle tab folder (now that personally drives me nuts but again, I understand how it may be challenging to avoid that depending on the organization of your file system and the frequency with which files are either added or discarded) or, the easiest solution and something I've been doing for some time now, is creasing your traditional file folders at the crease lower than the middle one which will cause the back side of your standard manila folder to be well higher than the front which puts the tabs just about even with the tabs on these new SuperTab folders. I liked the idea of having the option of USB, battery, or AC power for a pencil sharpener, but in the real world this was a good idea that doesn't quite reach its potential.Forget about sharpening pencils with the unit powered via USB, it simply doesn't have the power you'd expect in a pencil sharpener.  The power is there when using batteries or AC (via a USB wall adapter, not included), but even then, it doesn't get a pencil to that super sharp stage you want in a sharpened pencil.This might be a good idea for students who just need an occasional pencil sharpened, and "kinda" sharp is good enough, but if you use a pencil for any precision writing, I don't think you're going to like the way this sharpens.

Thank goodness, this thing actually cuts!  Previously, I had bought a cheap paper cutter and it just didn't do the job and basically 'ate' my paper because it tore it up so badly. This works so much better, and the blade seems to be quite sharp. I will say that it seems to work better with more than one sheet of paper at one time. If you are cutting a long single sheet of paper, then I would recommend that you hold it down in the middle/opposite end of the way the blade swings or it could possible raise up some (the paper itself). Sort of hard to explain, but it may happen. What I did was take a piece of cardboard and set it on top of the paper so it stays stable. If all else fails, just flip the paper upside down and cut the part you were having issues with from the top. One thing I don't really understand is the bar that goes across- next to the blade. If this was adjustable, it would be great; but I haven't seen or found a way to lower it so it is pretty pointless. All in all, an affordable cutter that works well.

I was hesitant to try the Samsung SCX-3405FW Printer because the the stock photo makes it look big and bulky. I was wrong! The printer is definitely more compact than what you see in the picture and I will try to get an actual pic up here for you so that you can see for yourself! This is a beginner's review. A few weeks ago I had an inspiration to start sketching. This is my first sketchbook. For a beginner, this is great. I did a lot of small drawing exercises following an ebook, and having the big 11x14 inch pages was great. On a single double sided sheet I managed to get a lot of little drawings. The front cover is not thick, but the back cover is thick, and since I don't have any other accessories, I sketch with the paper on top of the back cover. The first page has a pocket on both sides for storing drawings. The pocket is six inches tall and covers the whole width of the page. One of the most useful things about this postal scale is the display, which is separate from the platform. It can sit on the table or be mounted on a wall (use your own screws, hardware not provided). Why is this useful? If you are a technical person, you may have heard the story how 3M invented Post-It Notes. It was a failed effort by one of their chemists to develop a new adhesive - the stuff he came up with peeled right off. But some marketing genius at 3M realized that people might just like paper notes that peeled right off without damage. The rest is history.Now that the 3M patents have expired, peel-off adhesive notes are a generic product. This is the Avery version, which are available in dozens of styles - adhesive edge only, adhesive whole page, colors, recycled, etc. This item is a set of pastel pads, stiff enough to write on as a self-standing notepad. But never in 3M Yellow - that's trademarked.Avery makes nice ones in pleasant colors - recommended.

This is a reliable, all-in-one printer from an established manufacturer. I've used Epson printers before and have appreciated their ease of use, work-horse reliability, and convenience. Not being one who enjoys poring over instruction manuals for half a day before I can use an item, I was pleased with how easy it was to set up the WF-3620.I think there are functions I won't really need, such as its ability to copy on both sides of the same sheet of paper automatically, but it's satisfying to know I can copy, print, and scan all on the same machine. These plastic tabs would be very useful for students, editors, cooks, or anyone else who needs to make temporary notes in books or other hardcopy, but does not want to write on the paper itself.  Plus, a divider tab at the end allows them to be used to index pages as well.  The two main areas I focused on when reviewing these NoteTabs was "write-ability" & "stick-ability".First, "write-ability".  I wrote on these with a fine-point Sharpie, a rolling ball gel ink pen, a ballpoint pen, an erasable gel ink pen, and a mechanical pencil.  All of these writing instruments wrote well on the plastic surface.  The liquid gel inks require a few seconds to dry or they can be smudged, but otherwise the writing was clear and legible.  The pencil & erasable gel pen (the latter is erased with a rubber "nub" on the end of the pen via the heat of friction) both erased completely & the erased spot could be easily written over.  In short, these NoteTabs had all I could expect or want regarding "write-ability".Next, "stick-ability".  The adhesive on the back of these NoteTabs sticks well to the paper - almost too well at first.  By that I mean, the first couple of uses, I had to take care removing the NoteTab to not rip the page in my test book (a textbook).  This was not a drawback - I just had to take a little care it peeling the NoteTab off of the paper.  After a few rounds of sticking & removing, the adhesive still stuck well to the paper, but was a little easier to remove.I removed & re-stuck one of the NoteTabs over two dozen times on a book page, and the adhesive held up, gripping the paper adequately each time.  So, between this "re-stick-ability" if you will, and the ability to erase pencil & erasable gel ink, this is truly a reusable product.I have two final comments about this product in general.  One, the plastic appears slightly frosted when held up to the light, yet, once stuck onto a printed page, the text beneath is very legible.  Also, the plastic is fairly stiff - on the one hand, this contributes to the durability of the NoteTabs (for instance, the index tabs will not get torn or dog-eared when handling the book they are in).  On the other, however, I would imagine that the thickness of the NoteTabs would start to become a bulky issue if one were to try to have a lot of them inserted in one book.Now, regarding this size of the product in particular.  It is the same size as a "medium" PostIt Note (i.e., 3" x 3"), with the addition of the 1/2" index tab.  So, it would be ideal for the same applications as one would use this size PostIt Note, but where the increased durability & "re-usability" that these NoteTabs provide is desired.  In my mind, this would include margin notes in a book.  However, if notes, editing marks, etc. need to be placed over specific text, a longer version of this product would be better, like the3" x 7.5" Perforated NoteTabs.To summarize, I think this is a very useful product, but only for certain people, like students & editors, for example.  It is well designed, well made, highly functional, attractive, and durable.

The handle is very comfortable and the blade is very sharp. There is a nice safety feature that requires you to depress a button to get the blade to drop down. It works very well for many uses-opening boxes, cutting string, etc (it's similar to but much safer than using one blade from a pair of scissors or a razor blade).The problem is the blade does not come far enough down to work on a lot of plastics (specifically clamshell cases which is what I was really hoping to use it on).

The Perfection V370 Color Photo Scanner provides an excellent scanner at an affordable price.  The software is easy to use and fairly self-explanatory and the scanner comes with software for various tasks (e.g., photo software, OCR, etc.).  While the basic software is necessary, the others may not be if you either have superior software for that purpose or do not need that particular function.  Some of the software will also slip in a screen changing the default file open choices to this software.  I would recommend clearing these until you have tried the software and decide you actually want it to be the default on one or more file formats.I installed it on both a Windows 7 and Windows 8 laptop.  The Windows 7 installation went without issue.  The scanner does not list Windows 8 compatibility but there was no major problems here as well.  The one odd thing is that in the latter case some of the screens (where it asked you to make a choice or that the software was installed) appeared on the screen minimized.  For a moment, I thought the process had frozen until I noticed the extra icon on the taskbar.  Once clicked, up came a screen asking me to make some choice or other.The scanner also comes with a plastic contraption that might look like something destined for the trash.  It is actually a holder for slides and photo negatives so if you have either, keep it!The instructions specifically tell the user to first install the software and then plug in the scanner.  This is common with scanners and I followed the directions.  I just mention this as a warning because I have had issues when I missed this with other models.The quality of the images were excellent especially given the inexpensive pricepoint and home use audience.  While one could spend hundreds and get a more powerful scanner, it is difficult to find one of this quality at this price.

Those boxes of documents, love letters, photographs from both my wife's family and mine have weighed on my mind for almost 20 years.  In fact, 15 years ago I ordered a Visioneer portable scanner with the intention of getting a load off my mind (and out of the attic). The device proved buggy, partially effective and extremely time-consuming, leading to my aborting the project and selling the scanner.  But in the past several months, the regular television commercials for Neato portable scanners renewed my interest.After reading some of the reviews for Neato portables, I questioned whether the technology had advanced far since my first Visioneer.  But before abandoning the project a second time I investigated other possibilities, with the following findings:  You can spend several dollars on one of many scan "apps," designed to work with the camera of an iPhone or iPod (good for a couple of documents, maybe).  In the 50-100 dollar price range you might pick up a Magic Wand (make sure your hands are steady and your patience long)VuPoint Solutions Magic Wand Portable Scanner (PDS-ST410-VP).  In the 150 dollar price range there's a decent Brother personal scanner (looks good for occasional use and when on the go)Brother DSMobile Scanner (DS-600)and a wireless device called the Doxie (be sure to read consumer reviews as well as the maker's claims)Doxie, the amazing scanner for documents.Getting to devices for the more "serious" user, there are several reputable scanners in the two hundred dollar range, above all the Fujitsu Scansnap S1100Fujitsu SCANSNAP S1100 CLR 600DPI USB Mobile Scanner (PA03610-B005)and the HP Scanjet 1000HP Scanjet Professional 1000 Mobile Scanner (L2722A#BGJ).  These deserve consideration from users who plan to move about and travel, taking the scanner with them on business trips, etc.  But besides size and weight, be sure to to note the presence or absence of features like duplex printing, drivers, automatic feed.Once you're at the $200 mark, it's difficult not to notice what's available for an extra fifty to eighty dollars. The two scanners in this range that stand out--combining the convenience of a portable, USB-powered scanner with the features of a professional office machine--are the Fujitsu S1300 (Fujitsu is clearly the champ with Amazon purchasers)Fujitsu ScanSnap S1300 Instant PDF Sheet-Fed Mobile Scanner (PA03603-B005)and the Canon P150Canon imageFORMULA P-150 Portable Document Scanner(Scan-tini).But wait!  There's also the pictured machine, the Canon P215, the newest offering and one which, though slow to be discovered by consumers, is gradually rising in Amazon's sales rankings (it's moved ahead of the Canon P150 in just the past week).  Admittedly, the feature differences between the two Canons are almost as small as the price difference.  Size and performance of the two machines are practically identical.  The P215 is .2" wider and 2 oz. heavier.  The P215 comes with "Advanced Text Enhancement," "Character Emphasis," and several user-adjustable color settings not advertised with the P150; it has a "dedicated" card reader (which accepts thick, laminated cards as well as paper biz cards); its high-speed interface includes USB 3.0 along with USB 2.0; finally, Mac users can be assured that it's "Lion-ready."  In short, the P215 seems slightly more "future-proofed" than the P150.On to the showdown: Canon or Fujitsu? The Fujitsu S1300 accepts 10 sheets in auto-feed mode; the Canon P150 and P215 both accept up to 20 sheets ; the Canons have built-in Twain drivers for guaranteed out-of-the box plug-and-scan convenience; the Fujitsu does not. The Fujitsu includes an AC adapter; the Canons list it as an option. In sum, if I had any hesitation between the two brands, it was because of the Fujitsu's bundled OCR software program: the well-regarded ABBYY FineReader.  But once I considered the two brands from a broader perspective, noting my satisfaction with my printer (Canon MP640) and camera (Canon SD780), the final decision became inevitable.  ("PC Magazine," for one, seems to agree, rating it "best of breed.")

This 3M gel wrist rest impressed me with it's quality when I removed it from the box packaging. It feels very firm and looks quite classy and well made. The Reveal-n-Seal envelopes are fine envelopes.  They're sturdy, they're nice and smooth... what else could you ask for in a business envelope?Here's what you COULD ask for -- an envelope that's easy to seal.  This isn't.  You have to pull up a flap and then pull down the top part of the envelope.  Even after many attempts, I can't seem to quite get the hang of doing it without getting my fingers trapped to the sticky part.  Maybe it's a skill that I just don't have, but I'd almost rather go back to the "old" way of licking & sealing my envelopes.  Well, okay, I wouldn't go that far.  Still, I've seen much simpler designs out there than what these envelopes have to offer.You could also ask for an envelope that hides its inner contents.  This does -- sort of.  Okay, so the packaging/product never actually claims that it will protect your secret documents, but as a consumer, I wish it would!  You can see through the envelope if you hold it up to the light; so... they're not very secure.However, if you're just mailing ordinary things, these envelopes pass the test of usability.  They're certainly not bad or cheaply made.  They just could be better.

The AmazonBasics Mouse Pad is, as the name suggests, a basic mouse pad sold via Amazon. This mouse pad is enough to get the job done, but if you're looks for a mouse pad with a great surface, ergonomic design or comfortable padding, this is NOT it. For a few bucks you get a 9-inch by 8-inch mouse pad that has a bottom made of thin foam rubber and an even thinner surface made of polyester similar to a cheap T-shirt.In my opinion there are two problems with this mouse pad:1) It's too small.2) It's made of cheap materials.I've honestly received free mouse pads that are better made than this one, and the 9x8 dimensions don't give you much room to maneuver a mouse if you're got a high-resolution display and a low-res mouse. The X-ACTO Guillotine is a powerful ally in the battle against improperly trimmed photos, invitations, and coupons. No longer do my photos look like they have been hacked into shape by an ornery 6 year old with ancient safety scissors. (To be honest a 23 year old with a knife from the kitchen) The Guillotine provides easy and precise cuts that makes jagged edges and paper hang nails history.Out of the Box:The set up time for the paper trimmer was about 10 minutes. I had some problems getting the screw into the handle. This was not a huge problem, but it did take a little attention from Mr. Hammer.Highlights:What I like most about this paper trimmer is just how light it is, yet the constitution is that of durability. The old paper trimmer that I used back in school was very heavy, as it was made of wood. This is what I had in mind when I ordered this product, but it surprised me with how portable and light it is. I do not have any problems storing the Guillotine wherever I wish.Key Issues:Because I live in a small apartment functionality is very important for me. Things that I own must be able to do two things. A hammer is not only used to pound screws into the X-ACTO Paper Trimmer, but it also must participate in Spider Squashing and Meat Tenderizing. The Plunger participates in all Toilet Emergencies as well as takes small dents out of my car.Because of this, I also tried to use my X-ACTO Guillotine in the kitchen. This is an unconventional approach, admittedly, but my reasoning was if cutting vegetables with my X-ACTO Guillotine is wrong I don't want to be right.Let me shoot straight with you, The X-ACTO Guillotine is a terrific tool to cut papers, coupons, and pictures but it makes a lousy vegetable slicer. For this reason, I have to detract a star for its lack of functionality.You also do not want to purchase this if you are interested in cutting up linoleum, very thick card stock, or heavy cardboard.Conclusion:Overall this is a great product and I think it will easily take care of all of your paper cutting needs.

To start with the good... The scanner has a small footprint, easily scans small items, is fast, and provides a good color scan. The scanner is single sided so two sided documents require twice as much scanning. There is no document feeding option so it can be laborious for multi-page documents.If Visioneer is listening... For this price point, I hope they can modernize the software and user interface in later releases and add a flip-out document feed for at least 5 pages (preferably more). In a perfect world duplex scanning would be nice too, but I know I'm pushing it now... As it stands today, it's hard to recommend this scanner when you can easily get an all in one printer and scanner with a document feeder for less than half this price, for example:Canon Pixma MP530 Office All-In-One Inkjet Photo Printer. Now I know this solves a different need given its small footprint and direct no-nonsense access to scanning (especially for business cards and receipts), but with all the compromises that it's bringing along, it's hard not to look for alternative solutions.

The Epson R1800 is an excellent pigment ink printer. Fantastic quality, fast, and quiet. I'm a graphic designer and photographer, and have used it exclusively for design proofs and photography, most usually printing the larger 13x19 sizes. I've been through two of them in the last three years.Here's the "but" in my review: if you're a heavy user like me, you'll fill up the waste ink tank very quickly. What's that? The waste ink is what happens when you clean your printer and/or it dumps the excess as it's printing. While I don't clean mine too often, I do use it a lot, so standard cleanings are the norm. To replace the waste ink tank runs about $150-$200, so it becomes a question of replacement, hacking your machine to install an external tank (only recommended if you're mechanically inclined and btw, it will void your warranty) or buying a new printer.The average life of my printers have been about 16-18 months, and in my opinion, that's not long enough for a printer that costs as much as the R1800 and R1900s cost.The ink cartridge prices are expensive, as well, so I converted mine to a bulk in feed system using Media Street's Niagara bulk continuous ink system (CIS). One caveat there: these inks tend to clog if not used on a daily basis, so again, you'll be replacing the ink waste tank sooner if you don't print regularly. However, you will save thousands in ink costs, and I'm not kidding. My yearly ink cost went down over $1,000 by abandoning the cartridges and using the bulk feed CIS.Overall, the R1800 is an excellent printer. The colors are true, printer is fast, and you can't beat it's fairly decent price.

Bottom line: this provides a great value for the price. Lots of adjustability, decent construction quality, and nice looks.Full review: This is a great laptop workstation for when I want to use my laptop while on the sofa but don't want to use my actual lap top to hold it. It also is great for holding a tablet so I can view a video while eating without getting the tablet in harms way of some errant food.Assembly was straightforward. Basically I just needed to attach the casters, the center pole and the table top. The only fasteners were 4 screws and 2 bolts, so it went together in just a few minutes. A combo allen wrench/phillips screwdriver is included, but I found it much more comfortable to use a regular screwdriver. The instructions were clear and easy to follow.In addition to being a table, it includes a USB hub which is a very welcome addition. It also has a cooling fan built into the table top (USB powered from a laptop) and a LED light on a stalk (3 AA batteries needed, which are not included).The table top, when fully extended on the center pole, is 30.5 inches tall; fully retracted it's 22 inches tall. More than enough adjustment room. The table itself is 15 inches by about 22 inches (measurements taken at the widest points). I had no problems using it with a full-size laptop and had enough room left over for using an external mouse.The table top tilts and can be locked into any angle. It can also be placed in a vertical position to save space when it's being stored. When the top is in a vertical position the entire unit can be easily picked up and moved by using the built-in handle, which I found to be a very nice design feature. I also liked that there is a small cubby under the table top that is useful for storing cables and other small items.The wheels are small, but I didn't have any problems moving the table back and forth in use on both a medium pile carpet and a hard floor. Only two of the casters have locks, so when assembling it, make sure the wheels with the locks are on different sides to ensure good locking performance.The build quality is quite nice - far better than I expected given the price. The legs and supports are all metal; the adjustment ring for the table height locks tightly, and the adjustment for the table tilt is easy to use.The appearance is also quite nice. It  looks more like furniture than my old one (which was all beige and looked like it belonged in a hospital). The cherry-colored wood-grained top looks nice against the black legs.All in all, very pleased with this and would definitely recommend it if you're looking for a laptop table.[The manufacturer provided the product for review]

This tape has a UPVC film backing.  What does that mean? I'll tell you: "U"PVC is an "un"-plasticized PVC, which makes the material less flexible and more durable.  UPVC is recyclable, which PVC is not, nor are there any health or safety concerns as there are with PVC.  (It does not contain BPA or Phthalate as PVC does.)I've used it several times already, and have come to appreciate both its sticky rubber resin backing and its color.  It is very thin and pliable without any stretch.  We've used it in the shower stall where it held up plastic sheeting to protect fresh caulking; so it is water resistant and water tight.  We used it to hold plastic sheeting around our tomato cages, trying to protect the young plants from 40mph wind gusts; so it is strong and the adhesive holds really well.And, this is an unusual application for the red-colored tape:  We noticed this while using it in the garden to hold plastic sheeting for wind protection:  It drew the orioles that were migrating through our area last week!  They are attracted by orange and red colors.  They usually fly down because they are attracted to our bottle brush tree, and we do put out oranges and grape jelly for them, but this year they specifically came down to check out the tape in the garden--so we set out another feeder by the tape.  Interesting, I think.This tape kind of does the same kind of jobs that duct tape does, but it is way thinner, doesn't stretch, doesn't leave white goo behind, and is easier to remove (from solid or non-porous materials).  It does not have that typical woven texture that you can feel on the top of duct tape, either. There are many colors from which to choose, which makes it good for color coding and for differentiation.  The UPVC makes it long-lasting.  Like PVC it is NOT biodegradable.The technical data sheet, (downloadable from the Product Description section on this product page), says it is also chemical resistant and good for "temporary" holding applications.Its 66 meter length is the same as 72.17 linear yards.  It is 2" wide.  Not only does this tape come in other colors, it also comes in other widths.

But, for the result itself, I would say the metal had some strange effects.When I wrote on the lid, you would have thought it were wet or sweating. The marker ran and seemed to flow away, much like a cheaper marker would, leaving it easy to wipe off and illegible. This would be troublesome if you used them for all sorts of items, mixing and going whenever you picked them up. My mom does that and I honestly do not know what would happen with use of these on those cans on either the can side or the marker side. All I know is that i tried it and that was odd.So, if you use these for daily stuff like labeling CDs or boxes or household items, they're nice. i color with mine sometimes and liked the way the look flowed into the pores of wood. It looked nice. If you go beyond that then check it first, making certain you do not can or need them to write on metal. I have yet to try it on a bunch of metallic surfaces to compare them on say a construction project versus the canning item, but it does make me worry a bit.Thanks.

I should start out by saying that this item looks great!  The material and construction look very nice.  However, the case itself is more what I would describe as plastic, than rubber... and it is pretty thin.  I could be wrong, and I hate to make a judgment prematurely, but this material looks to me like the sort of stuff that will get brittle and start to crack after a while.  So, if you're looking for something more short term that is priced right and looks great, this would be a great choice.  But for longer term use... the jury is still out.

See my review of the Brother dual width label printer.  I use the label printing system to keep snippets of information that I can print when I need them to stick on a piece of paper on the wall next to may desk.

These are pretty nice overall. Avery sends an instructional insert for help with formatting with various products from Microsoft, Corel, Adobe and Borderbound.  I'm using Ms Word 2007, so the instructions provided do NOT apply.  But I received HELP from Word and was able to easily create a text box for the labels.  The size you choose is up to you, as you are creating the box itself.  The text box holds a large version of the first letter of my last name.  If you go with a text box, you can use shading and color, rotation and other Word-preset options such as shadow and 3D.  You need some time to play around with it a little, use your imagination and see the endless possibilities.I do not like the relationship of text box to text.  It's simple to just use your spacebar to move text around the box, but it can also be more limiting that having separate fields. To duplicate text box from one label to the next, it is *not* as easy as Copy and Paste.  Perhaps in earlier versions of Word you will have no problem, as the instructions suggest.  But in 2007, when you copy the box it superimposes itself onto the original graphic and you must then drag it to other labels, each time.  Clipart, on the other hand, copies and pastes with ease (as will their other preset options - they copy as an entire label, not as separate text box/text parts).  Microsoft's clipart gallery is apparently very large, but you can also use your own art - you just have to add it to Microsoft's gallery.  Their ready-to-use gallery is basic, but I found a cornucopia for Thanksgiving.  You can also insert an image, which takes you right to My Docs.  I'm having problems with inserting clipart and images from My Docs, as far as adding return address alongside, as the text cursor ends up on the bottom right corner of the image, so the text does not fit on the label.  I've been trying to make this work using text alignment and direction, to no avail.  Frustrating!!Use your printer's highest quality settings, as suggested by Avery.  But make sure you allow the ink to dry for a good 3 minutes before touching, peeling off and applying, or the ink will come off as you apply.  NB : Cannot comment on how well color inks work on this gold foil, as I use grayscale printing exclusively.

This isn't the fastest shredder I've used and definitely not the quietest, but for a compact basic personal shredder I was surprised at how well it worked. It powered right through a stack of junk mail that I've seen similar size personal shredders get jammed by. I've been using it a couple weeks now and not once has it gotten jammed.

I had high hopes for these reusable stickers: alternative to magnets on the refrigerator, hang artwork on walls or windows.  My package contained 18 pink reusable shapes (circle, heart, star) and my kids quickly found some items that we wanted to hang.  The package says they'll hold up to 3/4 lb, but after a week only 1 of our photographs is still sticking to the refrigerator.  Two photographs (matted on heavy duty construction paper) fell off the fridge every hour. I put them on a window but they also failed to stick (even with 4 stickers). I must admit that I (and my kids) quickly lost interest in these, but after reading some other reviews I may try some other surfaces.These have been mostly a novelty in my household. Very cute. But I'm a little underwhelmed and surprised that they did not work better.

This rest claims to be anti-bacterial; there's no way I can prove or disprove that fact. However the claim that it's anti-skid really doesn't hold up, it slips around much more than other rests I have used. The rest, I had before this, was a gel, it started leaking and luckily  I spotted it before it got into my keyboard. The seams on this are on the bottom which means, even if it leaks, it would probably not get into a keyboard.This rest has a black leatherette cover which is not as comfortable, (soft) and definitely not as good looking as the gel wrist rests. Hey, this is cool stuff. I'm not having any trouble with the adhesive like some other reviewers. It goes on easy and works like a charm. You will need to clean the surface you stick it to.

After several years my old Canon Scanner finally quit working. So because my old Canon had been such a faithful companion, I decided to stay with Canon and bought the LiDE210 Color Image Scanner.It connects by USB, but install the software first. The software is much improved over the older software that my old Canon scanner came with. For two years I have fallen for incredible deals on other brands of glue. I buy at least 50 bottles of glue each year for my classroom. I have tried glue from two big box stores and two major office supply chains. I have also bought other craft brands. None of them compare to Elmer's Glue. To be honest, it is not actually the glue that I am reviewing - it is the BOTTLE. No other brand makes a bottle that compares to the bottle produced by Elmer's. I can pull out my box o' glue on Monday after hastily putting away the 15 or so bottles on a Friday and find a few open bottles. With Elmer's, you close the bottle, pick off the little dried bit of glue, and it's good to go. All other bottles would be ruined. The Up & Up (Target) and Staples brand bottles I tried this year clogged within an hour of opening. They stopped working WHILE being used. Many times, the entire top popped off, sending glue gushing forth to form a big puddle of goo all over some unfortunate child's project.I've had enough! I just bought 30 bottles for the rest of the year, and threw out all the other bottles of glue in my classroom.I usually send my unused glue home with the children each summer, but this year I will keep these bottles and order the gallon glue refill next fall.No more knock-off bottles!!

OK, I'll admit it: I'm an office products junky.  I'm always looking for that perfect black fine-point pen, or just the right file folders.  I've probably sampled just about every permutation of repositionable labels available in my search for the perfect stick-on tab for research materials (for my interminable thesis) and music.These new Post-it Durable Tabs are very good.  The colors allow me to color code references I need to be able to locate quickly (red for historical dates/etc., green for social customs, blue for religious connections, etc.).  I also use them as quick index markers for music in a couple of choral groups.  In one group, we usually sing 20-30 pieces for a concert, and I need to be able to locate the next piece we're working on during rehearsal.The extra space under the white tab allows me to make a few notes, too -- which I can then erase if I reuse the tabs.This aren't quite as substantial as the Avery labels of similar size -- the plastic is thinner in these Post-its -- but it's certainly sufficient to make these durable enough for most uses.
There is not much to say about HP cartridges.  I use a lot of ink cartridges, and I have only received one defective one from HP over the years.  They are not cheap, but all-in-all they are reliable.

I bought six .7mm automatic pencils. Every one of them had issues except this one. The twist eraser works perfectly and you don't end up pushing it back in as you erase as you do with others. So I would give it 4.5stars really.The runner up is another Pentel that has that feature but does not come with the twist eraser, so you use up the eraser pretty fast.

The fact that it holds a pen makes it even better. I'll probably pick up a few more for other areas of the house and office.Great product!
I love the feel of these. I have not been able to find them very easily and they work well.

The Smead MO File Box is extremely convenient for keeping client papers organized and right at hand.  Previously, I was carrying tons of paper around on client visits.  Now, I only take what I need in this easy to handle file box.  I recommend it to anyone dealing with paper overload.

Included in the package are 2 black, 1 blue, 1 red and 1 green marker along with a multi-layer eraser and a bottle of cleaning solution for dry erase boards.The products claim to be low odor, so the first thing I did was a sniff test. The markers didn't have much odor, and the eraser fluid, which usually smells strongly of ammonia, smelled more like an everyday household cleaner. This is a good start.The eraser comes in layers.....when one gets dirty, you peel off a layer to expose a new, clean layer. In addition, the eraser has a nicely designed handle, which makes it easy to hold while erasing the board. Finally, the package claims that the eraser is refillable, although I don't see the point. By the time the eraser is used up, the pens will most likely be dead and it would be just as easy to buy an entire new kit.The pens worked well, although they have a more narrow point than some of the other markers on the market. To me, this is an advantage, as I prefer a thinner point. It wrote well and the ink was very visible.Overall, a very good marker set, particularly if you prefer a finer pointed marker.

It didn't take long for me to put the "Fellowes L80-95 Laminator" to work soon after it was delivered as I had a variety of items to laminate. Summary: I am very happy overall with this printer. In the past other printers I have owned would set up very easily on the PC but were totally unfindable on a Mac or vice versa. Windows found it and installed it almost effortlessly.Colors +Amazingly sharp colors when using photo paper (some supplied)Print Speed +It is fast on black. I thought I'd give these some time before posting a review, to see how well they held up. They don't. I loved the idea of being able to move the labels on the plastic drawers I use for organizing everything I like to tuck away in cabinets, from office supplies to toiletries. But, less than a month after putting these in place, the labels were falling off every time I turned around. I found one that had made its way, somehow, from my home office out to reappear in my car. And, another one turned up on my cat's foot!A couple labels that I tested on manila folders did work better, and seem still to be in place for now. It's a great idea, but it needs to go back to the drawing board!

I was in serious need of a new cutter, when this little trimmer arrived I wondered if it would do the job as well as my old klunky cutter.  It does.This is a very light weight cutter/trimmer. I used the Avery Textured Scallop Round labels as name-tags for an event that I hosted.  In the past, other hosts have used a variety of rectangular labels manufactured by various companies. The scallop labels stood out, and many commented on their appreciation for a deviation from the standard rectangle labels (even men).  Additionally, unlike some other labels which had issues with synthetic material, the Avery scallops stuck well to a wide variety of clothing material.Printing and designing is easy, but you have to register an email. I'd rather that Avery put accessible templates on their website without having to provide an email.  Once registered, you will be directed to a page where you can enter the label number & obtain the template.  You can use pre-designed labels & insert text or you can design your own. There is almost a page worth of pre-designed labels. You can also choose to curve your text across the top or insert your text (text box)in various areas of the label.  There are quite a few font choices & font sizes. There is also a transparency choice so you can "watercolor" a background picture if you want to do so. I used a pre-designed label & created my own text with a curve at the top.  I left room to hand write a name in the middle as my guests showed.One issue that we had was finding the edge of the scallop to peel the label.  It was especially hard for those who didn't use a pre-printed label.  You literally have to search for the edge, and pull off the label to find the center.  I don't think there is a fix to this issue other than to use completely printed labels, but it is something to be aware of if you plan to write text by hand.Overall, the scallop labels are a nice and different style label & it is good to see Avery branch out with more creative shapes. While I don't like the fact that I had to register an email address in order to obtain the templates, I think the design templates & variety of choice are excellent for this product.  I'm sure Avery will add more pre-designed templates as time goes on.

My old scale only measures up to five pounds, and these days sometimes I need a scale with higher capacity - for example, when making sauerkraut at home, the bowl plus enough cabbage to fill a crock is much more than five pounds. I was out of sticky notes and thought I would give these a try. They work fine, but in my opinion, aren't really any better than Post-Its or other regular sticky notes. Part of the reason I say that is I tend to use these notes on places where having the note lay flat is not an issue - like the edge of my computer monitor or the edge of a book page. In addition, I can't say I've ever had a problem with Post-Its curling up. If you're someone who uses sticky notes in places where laying flat is a distinct advantage, then these might represent an improvement. For me, not so much. And one thing I really don't like about the second adhesive strip is that it makes the stack of sticky notes stick together to the point that it's hard to find the bottom edge so you can peel it off to use it.All in all, they're nice enough sticky notes. They do what they're supposed to do. They don't have any real advantage over Post-Its in my opinion.

The House of Doolittle Academic Weekly Planner is a good size, has a nice, sturdy cover, and does everything one might reasonably wish for a weekly planner to do. I particularly appreciate the "Important Dates" section, which includes holidays, Daylight Savings Time Begins, First Day of Summer, etc. It even has "Sweetest Day" which I've never heard of, but which sounds like a nice holiday to have. On the final two pages there is also space for names, addresses, etc.My only critique is this: Each weekday has spaces for 7:00 in the morning to 9:00 night, in 15 minute increments. Saturday goes from 7:00 to 5:30. Sunday has a couple of little spaces with no times on it. For me, the 15 minute increments are a bit much. If they had one hour increments, or even 30 minute increments, there would be more room and I wouldn't have to write in such tiny letters. Also, then there would be some space for events occurring after 9:00pm on weekdays or after 5:30pm on Saturday. Presumably, things happen at those times, too. It would be nice to have some little, tiny space set aside for the off hours.Aside from that one facet of the layout, I think this is pretty darn excellent.

This is a disappointing printer.First let me say, I am a huge laser printer fan.  So many of us have been conned into buying inkjet printers. They are slow and very expensive...  The ink clogs, runs out, and costs more than liquid gold.  The only benefit is color printing which I find very rarely useful.  Meanwhile, laser printers are available that are fast, robust, and very inexpensive.  I have been using a Brother printer that cost under 100 dollars for years.  The 2000 sheet toner cartridges (non oem which are great) cost under 20 dollars.  It doesn't compare to this in that it doesn't have a scanner or fax... but it does have networking!!  There are many lasers with all the features of this and more that are less expensive.In summary:1.  It has a very large footprint.  I am not sure what justifies this.  There are many less expensive laser printers available that are as robust and as or more functional that take up considerably less space.  For an office, this may be fine but for home, I need something more compact.2. The description says 'Built in Network & Duplex"  This is wrong and misleading.  First, there is no built in network.  It will do air print from a tablet/phone or from google cloud but only through a connected router.  There is no networking module. I spent a long time trying to get the networking hooked up before I realized this.  This is really inexcusable.  Much less expensive laser printers, including by samsung have a wireless module.  As far as duplex, there is duplex printing but not scanning. [A note about lasers and wireless.  Most wireless ink jets allow you to send directly from computer to printer wirelessly.  Most lasers only allow you to send from router to the printer.  This isn't a problem if you have a router...but for my daughter in her dorm room without a router, it was an issue.  There is usually a workaround but it isn't pretty.  All that is moot for this printer because there is no networking, even from the router except for AirPrint and google cloud print.3.  The toner cartridges are very expensive.  Still much less than inkjet.  Only OEM cartridges are available and they are about 2x as much as the brother oem cartridge... and much more expensive than the non OEM ones.  It is possible that non OEM cartridges will come out as this printer ages.4. As big as this is, it won't take an entire ream of paper.. only 50 sheets.  Can understand that!5. Print quality is excellent, but no better than less expensive laser printers.  You can push an eco button to save electricity and toner.  Scanner is excellent... as are the other features.  However, I just can't see spending so much for a printer that offers less than so many inexpensive printers which are available.

Cut from extra-thick colored stock and given an extra-large labeling area, these folders are exactly what they seem to be. Factors to consider while shopping:1. The extra-thick stock makes these folders considerably more rigid than traditional colored folders. This could make them a good choice for carrying around in a briefcase or portfolio, especially when you're carrying documents that you want to keep in pristine condition.2. The extra-large label area may not be much of a blessing. If you store these folders in hanging folders, the lower part of the label area will be hidden. If you use an electronic label maker, you don't need the extra space ... unless you feel like using two labels, one above the other.3. If you don't have experience with colored folders, and if you typically write directly on your folders -- as opposed to using some sort of stick-on labels -- you should be aware that writing does not show up well on a colored background.4. If you open a standard folder and you open and lay one of these folders on top, you will see that these folders are about a half inch shorter from end to end. The bigger tab allows Smead to use less stock. You can look at this as an environmentally friendly move, or as a cost-cutting move. They're folded so that the height of the tab when sitting in a drawer is no different from that of a standard folder, so I doubt this has any practical significance.5. They're pricey. If you have a problem with folders wearing out quickly, or if you prize the greater rigidity of these folders or the bigger label area, the extra cost may be worth it. Otherwise, you're probably better off with standard color or plain-manila folders.

My wife and I recently did a DIY project of creating our own chalkboard for the kitchen (thanks to Pinterest). We bought chalkboard paint and painted it on a glass window. It took a couple coats but after the 3rd one, it was ready to go.She asked if I would buy her some chalk on Amazon after the chalk she bought (some cheap brand) did not write on her board cleanly/evenly. Having been out of school for a long time (I haven't seen chalk since college), I didn't know there was such thing as "quality chalk" or "low dust chalk". I thought chalk was chalk!After reading several reviews on various products, I finally settled for Prang Hygieia. According to other reviewers who seem to know more than me, Prang is one of the "best" chalk brands. Wanting to learn more, I found this from a 3rd party website (Amazon does not let you link externally).**HYGIEIA CHALK Hygieia is made of 95% pure calcium carbonate. This high percentage of pure levigated or refined chalk means it is virtually free of grit, greasy binders, or other ingredients harmful to board surfaces. This high quality produces a clean, white mark, easily legible anywhere in the classroom. It erases easily (the heavier particles settle in the chalk tray and significantly cut down on dust). Hygieia outlasts ordinary chalk, and actually preserves chalkboard surfaces by keeping the "tooth" of the board in perfect writing condition.**I'm not a geologist, so I have no clue what calcium carbonate does vs whatever traditional chalk is made of but this chalk truly is magical. It writes smoothly/evenly/clearly (even on chalkboard paint surfaces). There doesn't seem to be much dust at all and it erases nicely.My only complaint is that some of the chalk arrived in broken pieces but I'm not docking stars for that. Out of all 12 sticks, only 2 of mine were broken. Bottom line, chalk is fragile. Whether you buy it from Amazon or you buy it at your local store like Walmart. All of it comes from the same place and it is stored in warehouses. The slightest drop/bump/hit will break your chalk. If you get a pack with all of them in one piece, then consider yourself lucky. But there is no reason to dock stars just because your chalk is broken. That's like docking stars from a Butterfinger or Heath candy bar that isn't in one piece.

My rating for this printer: 4.5 stars.This attractive looking XP 800 has the same small footprint as the XP 600, but is a more capable all-in-one color inkjet printer than the XP 600.  Not only does it offer higher print (e.g., 11 vs. 9 pages per minute 1-sided color) and copy (e.g., 11 vs. 10 pages per minute 1-sided black) speeds, and maximum scan resolution (e.g, 2400 vs 4800 dpi), but it also provides a capability to send and receive faxes, and a 30-page automatic document feeder that makes 2-sided printing * and * copying jobs more performant in the XP 800 than the XP 600.Since I have experience setting up both the XP 600 and 800, I can mention that setting up the XP 800 required a little bit more time and effort from me than setting up the XP 600.  While I was able to add the XP 600 to my wireless network in my first attempt, I was not able to do so with the XP 800.  Apparently, using the printer's touch screen control panel to perform the wireless network setup process yielded invalid IP addresses for both the default gateway and the printer itself, so I ended up having to use the Epson software I installed on my Windows computer to override those IP addresses with ones that were valid for my setup. Something to note also:  The virtual keyboard provided in the XP 800's control panel for entering the security password for my wireless network had, in my opinion, a slightly more difficult to use user interface than the XP 600's virtual keyboard.As mentioned above, the XP 800 can print, copy, and scan at higher speeds than the XP 600, and the produced documents have qualities comparable or slightly higher than those produced by the XP 600.  The XP 800's automatic document feeder [ADF] works very well (e.g., unlike the ADF in an older EPSON Inkjet Printer I've had where I had to constantly "nudge" my documents in order for the ADF to take them in, I haven't encountered this kind of problem with the XP 800's ADF yet), and helps make printing and copying -- especially 2-sided -- jobs performant enough for moderate office use.The faxing capability worked just fine with myOoma Telo VoIPsetup, but your mileage may vary depending on your setup.Overall, I think the XP 800 is fast and versatile enough for moderate office use.
