I've noted a number of people have had problems with the cart. springs breaking the tabs that hold them in place. I've had two of these printers and never had a problem with this. What I have run into is the software tends to be VERY conservation on telling how much ink you have. I've noted that HP only suggests that you have an extra cart. on hand when it first pops up the message. My usual response to this message is to continue to use the cart. until I start getting lines in the solid parts of the print out, color or B/W. Using this approach I usual get about three to four warnings before the ink actually runs out so changing the ink cart when you first see the warning will leave you with unused ink and you then will waste it.Also I noted that when you load your paper in the feed tray, if you load a small amount, then another small amount to fill up the feed tray, you may experience the printer pulling two or more sheets of paper when it feeds across the point where you layed the second stack down. Don't know why this happens, but I noted that by loading a single larger stack seems to solve this situation. I just brought another one of these printers and it's working OK at this point. On that cart. spring, I did note that it is possible put a cart in from the up down and catch the spring wrong. I found the best way is to slide the cart in from the front which has the effect of making the spring go the right against the side of the cart holder instead of being forced down which causes the spring to put pressure on the plastic tabs and can cause them to break thus forcing the spring out of place. To this point, I haven't experience this problem. My first HP-6940 lasted over three years of continious duty in an always on situation and if the network was up and running it never failed to print.  It only failed when a cart. carriage guide broke off and I couldn't replace it. Overall, I like this printer but like any printer I've ever used it has quirks and once you find out what they are you can either work with them or decide it's got to many and buy another printer.

The code words here are "professional" and "compact."  This tray is not meant for a pressed-wood, cheaply-made desk as installation requires an electric screw driver. I used the older panasonic similar phone set that had a phone book sent between handsets, and no Do NOT DISTURB feature. This newer KX-TG9334T set is far better with some unusual features I did not expect.First, under features it list "Transferable phonebook = No". And the DO NOT DISTURB looked to simply be a feature to turn off the ringing phone-set by phone-set. Not controlled from the base unit.However, actually the features they add are far superior.The DO NOT DISTURB (or NIGHT MODE) has the ability to enter a time span for NIGHT MODE to engage. So you can enter 11pm to 6am (for example) and turn on NIGHT MODE on one, two or all handsets.What happens is on the set time the ringer will not ring for that time span every day as long as NIGHT MODE is kept turned on.This is a great feature, MUCH better than a DO NOT DISTURB button on the base unit (some other brand phones), that silence all phones. The problem there is you MUST remember to dis-engage the do not disturb button to allow the phones to ring. A task often forgotten.With the Panasonic NIGHT MODE, the "timer" takes care of that for you.FANTASTIC!!!!Another great feature is the phonebook. No, you can not send a list between handsets, because you DONT NEED TO!The Panasonic KX-TG9334T keeps one phonebook list on the base units memory, that all attached handsets can access and add to or edit.That means, you can add a called to the book from  ANY handset, then ALL phones can see the same list. No more updating the list on one handset, then having to transfer that list to all other handsets on the system.The "shared" phonebook system is sooooo much nicer. Again... FANTASTIC!!!And the BLOCK CALLER feature is nice too. Do you have someone/place that tried to bug you selling stuff? Add their number to the BLOCKED LIST and when they try to call, the phone rings only once, then they get a busy signal. TAKE THAT UNWANTED CALLER!!!There are a few quirks I have to mention with the KX-TG9334T system.1. The lighted display is very bright. Too bright. And they should have added a brightness control.2. The message alert light should be more visible. It wraps from the back of the top to the top of the handset. If the handset is at eye level, like on a nightstand facing you, you can not see the flashing message waiting light hardly at all. You almost need to turn the handset backwards so you will see if a message comes in.My old panasonics had the same message light, but it wrapped around over the top to front of the handset, easily viewable.3. The lighted screen needs a timer control. As is, the screen only lights for .5 seconds. So it blanks off while you're still trying to read to make a menu adjustment. Kind of annoying. Like a cell phone, the screen display needs a timer control to allow it to remain lighted to your needs, say up to 5 seconds.But the fantastic features cancels out the quirks, with these KX-TG9334T phones.I was paying $7 a month thru Qwest for their DO NOT DISTURB feature that allowed a timer on-off setting.Now, for $zero$ I have the same feature built into these phones.Pretty nice saving $84 a year on my Qwest bill... FANTASTIC!!!

I like this safe quite a bit, but after careful consideration I think I will still have to keep my safe deposit box at the bank.  I had hoped to give up that yearly rental expense.  This safe is quite a hefty piece to carry - weighing in at twenty pounds for the medium sized unit I have.  In the carry position I fully understand why the handle is placed as it is, yet when trying to move it around on the floor of my closet I wished the handle could be on the top side as the lock mechanism faced me.There are some basic things to know when you decide to purchase a storage item such as this medium size safe.  The keys can be accidently locked inside the safe so take care to have the keys outside the unit before pressing down on the latch.  If you should accidently lock the keys inside the safe, there is an 800 number and website to visit to get replacement keys.  That actually is a little disquieting for me so you need to send in the registration card and realize this unit is not burglar proof.  I find the actual usable space inside the safe to be adequate for letter size paper and folded legal size documents.  There are two straps which can be installed to hold down items to keep them from shifting around as the safe is moved so everything remained in place when I decided on a different storage location.  Air tight containers will be required to put watches in before putting them in the safe and the same holds true if you want to store valuable stamps.  These containers are not provided.  Do not store pearls in the safe because they would not be protected in case of fire.  The seal around the middle rim of the safe which allows it to give maximum fire protection is made of a high moisture content material and could negatively impact delicate moving parts on pieces of jewelry.  Photographs would also require an air tight container before being placed in the safe.  Do not store firearms, weapons of any sort, or medications in the safe.So, this safe unit for my home will come in handy for items not specifically prohibited, but I still need to keep my safe deposit box.  Also, if I can carry it around, so could an enterprising burglar who found it where I've placed it.  Keep the safe closed and locked to get the benefits of the fire and water protection and keep your two keys separated and not inside the safe.

Since it has all the basic features you'd expect in a product like this and they all work (answering machine, phone book, flash/hold, caller ID, etc.), I'll skip those details and focus on the ones that stand out. Scroll down for the couple of dings that brought the review down and the final sum-up.The Good Stuff:First, the most interesting one: the Link-to-Cell feature. It's a really nice feature, especially if you're one of the many people who still haven't given up their main home phone line and gone all-mobile, all-the-time. You use a Bluetooth link (as easy as setting up a Bluetooth headset) to connect the mobile to your base station (yes, that's where the link is so that's where your mobile phone will remain, though this isn't necessarily a bad thing). From then on, calls coming in on your cell will also ring the various handsets. You can also configure the system to direct calls from each mobile to a specific headset so you don't ring the entire house when you get a call. You can also call out via your cell (maybe that long-distance plan is better or if it's your work line essentially...). In general, it works and works well. The sound quality usually seems fine though I've had cases where I'd hear an echo that I wouldn't hear on the cell phone itself. Just seems to depend on the connection (with the cell and the handset). Nothing to write home about though.The only real downside to the Link-to-Cell feature is that it's limited to two (2) mobile phone connections. Unfortunately, I don't have enough cell phones to try to see if I could "force" the system to allow me to trade-off between two cells but then I can't imagine why it would let me do that. Obviously, if it's just you or you and a significant other/roommate/sibling, you should be fine. But, if you're looking to use this in a household with more than two mobiles, you'll be out of luck. In my mind, I would've liked to see the ability to maybe link to a handset station (not the base station) to expand the number of phones you can "attach" to the system. Then you could have the base station ring for the two main cells and have additional handset stations be exclusive to someone else or something.Another feature that's not exactly new (new to me!) but is still interesting is the talking caller ID. When a call is coming in, the handsets can read out the number so you don't have to look at the phone to figure out if you want to take the call or not. Also useful if you're like my parents and can't read the handset screen without your glasses handy.Speaking of parents, the phones and base station both have nice a large buttons. They're handy for me as well given my large hands. Just nice to see since it expands the system's user base more.Lastly, there's a nifty little feature that will block unavailable calls coming in. Just drops them. Great if you're tired of getting calls from telemarketers during dinner (or ever really, am I right?).The Not-So-Good Stuff:I didn't want to call these bad necessarily since they might not matter much to you (they just did to me). Take them with a grain of salt:First, the answering machine. The system supports a whopping 18 minutes and 64 messages. Sorry? So, if I go on vacation and aunt petunia decides to rattle on for 15 minutes, every other message is getting dumped? C'mon...in an age where you can buy 1GB of RAM (which could store hundreds of minutes of MP3s) for $15 or less RETAIL, you can't put a couple more chips in this answering machine and store 30 minutes or more? And 64 messages? Granted, I doubt I'd have THAT many messages after a week or two but you get one persistent telemarketer and you've burned through 20-30 messages with 2 second hang-ups.Second, for whatever reason, they opted to not have anything more significant on the base station as far as display beyond a 2-digit LED. If the base station did nothing but act as an answering machine, I'd say that's probably fair. But, since you can actually make calls from the base station (not the handset, the base station itself), it just seems weird. I can't see the number I dialed (note abovementioned big hands) or see the caller ID without hunting down a handset? There's an older model (see below) that seems to have all the same features and actually has a display you can use on the base station (though it's $12 more as of the writing of this review).The Summary:All in all, the system does what it's supposed to do and so far (about two weeks into it) it's doing well. I love being able to leave my cell plugged in and charging by the base station and being able to still receive calls in another room. The flaws are minor (unless you get a lot of talkative people leaving you messages) but to me they are feel like Panasonic being either silly or cheap. This isn't a $30 system so I don't get why they're skimping on such minor details. If you're with me on the "cons", then check out the Panasonic KX-TG7642M. Outside of a color difference and that it's older, it has the display (apparently the 18 minute limitation still existed back then too...no progress Panasonic?). Again, this might be the smallest and weakest gripe known to mankind to you. If so, this system is worth a look.

I really don't have much to say about the Vtech phone with door monitoring system from the phone perspective.  I pounced on it because of the door monitoring feature since we get an inordinate amount of unsolicited visitors from school fund drives, charities, church groups, home specialists, lawn treatment professionals, window replacements, roof estimates, political campaigners, and the list goes on and on and on.  Like caller ID, I'd love to be able to filter whether I answer the door.  Especially when you're in the middle of preparing a meal and your hands are covered in ingredients.So as a phone, it's your typical standard feature and functionality cordless phone with answering system. I don't believe it has a speaker phone capability or at least not one that is obvious since there's no button clearly labeled speaker.  I have two lines and it supports both easily.  There aren't any fancy bells ans whistles but let's be honest, no one picked this item for the phone.  so on to the door monitoring.  I wasn't thrilled with the idea of having to drill a hole in my door so thank goodness I tested it all out before I put holes in my door.  The bottom line is that the image quality is very sketchy.  Sometimes the picture is clear and other times it looks like melted camera film.  I noticed others say that it worked better at night and this is true, but in an America's Most Wanted sort of way.  At least there's no huge flash that goes off when it takes a pic that would scare people off, but with all my unwanted visitors, that may be a good thing.I find it odd that it relies on an AC charger like a regular phone since I don't see myself grabbing my doorbell and recharging it occasionally.  That's something that I won't remember to do and keeping it plugged in all the time isn't going to happen without snaking the cord through the exterior wall.  Otherwise there will just be a cord hanging on it and likely an extension cord unless you have an outlet right next to your door.Overall, I was really hoping this would be a home run and vtech gets five stars for the idea, but the execution levels it out.  I'm sure the next generation will be even better, but for now, I would hold out.

A few of my many pet peeves are pencil shavings and eraser crumbs.  I do not like them.  While this product won't do a thing about my eraser crumb problem, let me tell you about my pencil shaving problem.  When you use this fabulous looking sharpener, which sharpens pencils to perfection at an acceptable decibel level, make sure you do not sharpen too many pencils without emptying the shaving tray.  When I put this sharpener into its new home in our home art room, my daughter sharpened every pencil she could find with it.  Great!  So then I pulled out the tray to empty it, and there were shavings everywhere.  It would be instant hatred except for the fact that the sharpener works so well.  Now I need a handheld mini vacuum cleaner.  Yes, you can see that the tray is full, but you can't see HOW full it is above the part that is above the tray.  That is why I gave it three stars out of five.  I have a few upright electric pencil sharpeners, and the pencil shaving reservoir holds a lot more, and it's a lot easier to unplug from the cord and walk it over to the trash can and dispose of the shavings without getting them all over the floor.The cord is long enough, even though I was afraid it wouldn't be.  It's probably 6' long, it took me so long to shove the cord behind a shelf stand that I won't go back and unplug it, sorry!  It has a standard polarized plug.The manufacturer says this is for heavy moderate use, which means nothing to me, really.  Since I have used it, I will tell you that I wouldn't use it in a classroom full of kids, I wouldn't use it in an office with a lot of folks using it, I would use it for my home, and my two kids that use it.

When I was looking at label makers in staples, I was a little overwhelmed by all of the choices.  Did I need 70 fonts?  What about all of the special characters or ways to format a label?  This maker was on sale for ten dollars, a fraction of the cost of the other label makers, so I picked it up.And the bottom line is, I haven't taken it off of the basic settings and I have labeled everything in my house.  It has absolutely supported my efforts to get organized and get systems in place, from budgeting to home management to business management (I have a home based photography studio) and so on.  You really don't need a fancy label maker.This one can be a little annoying, for example, you often have to press extra keys.  The "CAPS" button is a caps lock, so you can't just capitalize the first letter of a word without hitting the button again.  To erase a label line, you hit the shift and backspace button together, and then you have to hit the return button again to start typing.  If I ever need another label maker, I might look for one that lets me make labels faster without all of the extra key strokes.Also as others noted, the low battery warning shows up even when your batteries are perfectly fine.Finally, the little slit on the back to help you peel the label off of the backing takes some getting used to, but I am now very proficient at getting the label off.All in all, a wonderful productivity and organizational tool.

This is not the same Glue Stick I bought for my daughter in the 80's. (Which is a good thing). This glue dispenses easily and serves its purpose well. My first use was to glue Doilies onto red paper. I made a huge mess, w/ the holes... Lol. Fortunately this glue was easy to clean up. I recommend using this on SOLID paper.

I got this at the Big Box retailer that I despise.  Apparently, they only carry this in black.  URGH!!!  I LOVE that it comes in pink.  (Totally would have bought it on Amazon had I known about it.  Every day I find more and more things to buy on Amazon with my Prime Membership, not that I'm plugging Amazon, but I love Amazon.)  I also love that this shows two lines for previous entries.  That was the major selling point for me for when I do my accounting online homework - my laptop computer doesn't have the numeric keys, so it's frustrating to have to use the numbers above the QWERTY keyboard, and it's also time consuming. I love this calculator - very useful.

I run a small clothing company on the side and these bags are my favorite packaging to ship with. They do not offer protection like padded envelopes but the plastic is very tough and hard to stretch/rip so I am confident when shipping something small and light like a shirt or pair of pants.

This is my first laminator. When I got the chance to get it, i was excited to laminate signs and other sheets I had out to people a lot to make them reusable.I've only used the 3 MIL pouches. Other reviews have said it doesn't work for 5 or higher. I haven't tried it.It does take a while to warm up and then it beeps and light tuns green. The 10 included pouches are meant for heated lamination. Like others I had a little trouble figuring out which method to use with the pouches and what the advantages are of hot vs cold laminations.Anyway, the results looked good for me. Other than the beeping when it's ready to be used, it was quiet. It's also pretty slow so it's not meant for a pro setting.For the price, it's really good. The replacement pouches aren't expensive. This to me was the most important thing. If the sheets were expensive I would have not recommend it.

I was in need of a small printer stand when I came across this unit. It seemed adequate so I bought it and have been very pleased with it. The stand was extremely easy to assemble and strong enough to hold a heavy printer. A++

I use this tape all the time.  It is strong, sturdy, and easy to dispense.  It gets used for packaging, but also to make labels sturdier and reinforce pages or fix tears.  Great product!  I've used other brands that are similar, but don't have the same strength as the Scotch.

I've had this printer since April and this is the first time (september) I've had to change the color ink cartridges.  I use my printer daily and this lasted longer than my previous printers.  I do not print photos, so I can't tell you the quality or longevity of the cartridges used in that area, but for general printing it's been great.  This is the second time I've had to change the black ink 220 but I print a lot of papers that are just black so I'm just glad that there are multiple cartridges to change!  The small black 221 still hasn't run out yet and I just saved it in my drawer for later use.  Make sure that you check your printer to see which black is empty when you are ordering.  I ordered and didn't realize it was my 220 that was out and not the 221 that comes in this pack.  Now I have to place another order and wait another day.

It fits just right on the fridge door.However, the included double side sticker is not strong enough.Don't use the attached dry erase pen.  The pen dried up very fast.The only problem I see is the cheap plastic frame.I got this specifically for the kitchen and it works as planned.

This product is just what you would expect, a adhesive address label that sticks to paper envelopes and cardboard boxes.  The labels are a decent size, so it is easy to fit longer addresses on the labels.

I have used all 4 steps of Mead's Eadly Learning Idea builders now for my 6 year old DD. A couple I have favored and seen a use for but overall I strongly feel these books just are not all what they are hyped up to be. My DD has OT issues and I have found that the HWT program (Handwriting Without Tears)is far superior to Mead's pages and a simple brainstorming session provides more than enough inspiration for adults and children to figure out a subject to base a sentence on. For starters, pull out a deck of alphabet flash cards with the pictures on them and use those 26 for aubjects. Or look around a room and help the child model a sentence based on what he or she observes. That IMO requires a bit more creativity and it is free.My DD went from barely being able to write her name to being able to spell and write sentences in less than one year with the HWT program combined with her cyber school's phonics cirriculum. I would not suggest anything except for the HWT program to those seeking to improve their children's handwriting skills. :)

A long time user of Avery labels, I was especially drawn to these because of the promise of smudge-free labels with sheets that pass easily.  I have a finicky, but expensive, printer that on occasion wrinkles sheets that pass through the manual, non-drawer feeder.  This happens most frequently with labels.  So I was happy to see that after using more than 2 dozen of these sheets that they do indeed pass smoothly as described, furthermore no smudging!!!  This is vitally important as with these big labels pressing them onto envelopes sometimes requires quite a bit of handling.  I'm very happy with these labels and will definitely be switching from the regular 2X4 labels to these with TrueBlock that work seamlessly and smudge-free.Highly recommended!

It tickles me that I have various ring tone options on a home cordless phone. From a basic and boring to Ride of the Valkyries (which is what I now have). Besides a choice of ringtone, the Panasonic works great for us. We are using an OOMA box and the internet for our service. The sound quality has been great on the Panasonic with no echoing. both the main phone and the secondary keep a nice long charge.The redial, caller ID work perfectly. I'm very pleased with the panasonic. Setup was very easy, the phone plug into the OOMA and the regular plug into an outlet. I didn't want a recorder since the OOMA works as the recorder. Excellent experience with this phone system.

I recently hooked-up a new hp printer & used this combo pack as required. Thus far, I have printed several pages as I continue to do so & have not run dry yet. I never had a problem ordering hp Ink from Amazon for both of my printers, which require different numbers for the Ink Cartridges. The black & the multi-colored ink is bright. I always worry about the black Ink fading quickly, but have not had that problem when ordering on Amazon.However, through the years, I've purchased the same hp Ink in different stores & not only did it cost much more, but the Ink ran dry quickly. I am grateful that I have not experienced such disappointment, after ordering on Amazon. My only regret is not doing this soon enough, but lesson learned. Highly recommended!

I must say that I looked this product on the regular Amazon.com, not the Vine Program and it looks like it is the same as the product with the number 64082.But anyway, the term FasTab fits the product. For your permanent files in an office you might want to use regular hanging file folders and use word processing for the labels. But if you are in a hurry to get organized or for home use these are great.I used a Sharpee marker and my polymer eraser and they do erase. The tabs are extra sturdy, and you could, of course, stick permanent labels on them. What a time saver over plastic labels and inserts. They are really convenient.You could also type super sticky file folder labels and slap them on these easy-to-use tabs.

This is a handy tool for holding up heavy books if you do a lot of transcribing. I find it most suitable for an office setting. However, it takes up quite a bit of space on your desk, and barely leaves space for anything else. If you're not using it you will probably want to fold it and put it away, but then bringing out the heavy stand each time can be time consuming. So unless you do a lot of copying of books etc., it will not be used as much. I really don't find it very useful in the kitchen like some others, as I hardly ever cook from cook-books. And when I do once in a while I'll just leave a cook book open on the counter in a clear plastic bag, rather than use this stand as it takes up a lot of space and is not meant to be moved around a lot.I found it to be a nice way to hold 2 side-by-side information sheets at a booth or on a counter top in a store. Although, it is very nicely built, the price still seems a bit high. I got mine to test through the Vine program but I don't think I'd have bought one unless I really needed it.

This is a nice, lightly viscous glue that does a pretty good job of staying put (vs the old school watery version), though it will run a bit on vertical surfaces if you don't bond it immediately. I didn't do the constuction-helmet-and-I-beam test they used in those 70s commercials, but it did a good job on various surfaces around my house (I especially like it for locking in loose screws).But the bottle here is the difference, and it really does make it easier to use. If you're like me and you always end up with super glue all over your fingers somehow, you'll appreciate the applicator, which gives you dropper control instead of the little metal tubes, which even with the gel type mix still always end up as much on me as what I'm trying to glue.But the biggest benefit to me was that with the bottle stored upright, the glue stays liquid and clog free. This was a definite plus for me, since I don't think I've ever been able to use any super glue twice--inevitably when I go back to it even a few weeks later, it's always clogged or dried up--and I don't want to pick at it or stab it with a needle, since I'll inevitable get it all over me and end up half-glued to the bottle. I used this bottle for several little jobs around the house, and when I went back for it a month or two later, it was still flowing freely. I've always stored my tubes upright and it's never seemed to prevent clogs/drying, so this was a nice surprise. The bottle seals tightly and the semi-rigid design means the excess glue can flow back into the bottle, keeping the applicator clear.

In this package you get four colors of removable labels: blue, pink, yellow, and green. They work well, and don't leave sticky gunk behind when you remove them. This is perfect, because neurotic people love to label things, but hate sticky residue.They work well for the usual office and storage uses, but I also found them useful for labeling containers in the refrigerator. There are a lot of produce items that I store regularly in containers, and I can peel the sticker off and reuse it next time I store that item.I also like them for labeling cables and power plugs on electronic devices.With the Post-it Super Sticky Removable Color Coding Labels, you can go forth and label (with bonus color-coding) to your hearts content, or keep a neurotic person out of your hair for days at a time with just one package. That is a great value.

Overall I recommend this product. I print about 15 pages a week and this toner has lasted me months and months... Don't forget to turn the toner upside down a few times when it is running low to get some more life out of it!

A good supply of notebooks comes in handy since it seems like someone always needs one - and who likes running out on a school night for emergency supplies? And, they're different COLORS, so no arguing about whose is whose!

If you're looking for a larger format photo printer, this prints beautifully. Prior to this I had a Epson Stylus Photo R300. Now, comparing the two of those, in terms of print quality, I printed the same photo on both printers with the same settings in the software and I couldn't tell the difference between the two. So if you're just looking to print up to standard paper size (8.5 x 11) or smaller prints, maybe you don't need to shell out the extra money for this one. You can go for one of the less expensive Epson printers instead.However, this printer has much higher ink quality. I have noticed that prints from my old Epson have faded somewhat over time. The inks in this printer will last much much longer (allegedly) and it prints much larger prints (so it has a larger footprint than other photo printers).I'm using Mac OS X (Leopard) and the software is straightforward and works well. I also love having the ability to print directly onto printable CD-Rs (though my R300 also did that). Another plus is that this printer prints much much faster than my R300 - easily twice as fast, which is really nice. One drawback is that my R300 had a little display and buttons to navigate through different menu options directly on this printer. This printer lacks that functionality and I find that I miss it.All in all, this is a great printer if you need to print larger long-lasting prints.
I've been using this for a long time now. I appreciate the ability to place large envelopes on the scale and the readouts are accurate. It has also done well on heavier packages.

My son works for an office supply store and happened to be with me when I spotted this item. He heartily recommended it. As soon as it came, he brought me plastic sleeves and I use this to store my clear stamps. It's sturdy, attractive and holds a lot of stamps. Just what I needed to get better organized in my craft room.

This is the sturdiest Mead binder I have gotten  this year. The front and back cover have an extra thick plastic that makes it more like a book. The material this is covered with is more cloth like and less plastic feeling than the zipper binders we got at the same time. The the snap looks nice and is working well. (Its aluminum or a silver covered metal) My only reservation is the open bottom and top. Because it has no zipper things could slide out and get lost BUT...I bet there are people out there that dislike the zippers. If that describes you then you will probably like the Trapper Keeper.

These taps are great!!!!!!  You cannot beat the price.  If you go any Office supplies store they sell tabs for $5.00 to $7.00.  To me that's to expensive.  That is why I use Amazon, not to overpay!!!!!!

Much easier to apply than the normal super glue. Nozzle does not get clogged up so no more trying to poke holes in the dried crust with a safety pin. The glue is a little runny so be careful there. Seems to hold just as well as the thicker kind.

Easy to use, doesn't jam, and it doesn't take up much space on the counter.  The best part of this laminator is time: it heats up quickly in 5 minutes and it laminates a full sheet in about a minute (my mom was a teacher and I'd help her laminate sheets, and I've used some excruciatingly slow laminators!  This isn't one of them, thankfully).  Using this Scotch laminator, I was able to laminate a set of instruction sheets with no bubbles.  Very happy with its performance.

These work fairly well but have a distracting strip on top where the adhesive sits. I think if I used them a while, I probably would not notice it, but I do now. I feel as though the stickiness could be slightly better as I had them fall off a door at least once when leaving notes for myself.

I use file folders for my home paperwork (bills, Amazon.com invoices;) and after buying new ones every year, I have now started to recycle them. These labels are perfect for re-labeling those files.They are also large enough to be used for title labels for other folders, like printing out a e-book. There are templates available from 3M's website that I downloaded and had no problem using or printing from them.

I set this scanner up on a windows 7 computer with no problems.  I'm no expert in photography, but the scans I've made of old photos have turned out as good as can be.  It automatically corrects faded color to my satisfaction.  It also saves some time by recognizing multiple photos on the bed and saving them as independent files.  I have not used the auto stitch feature for bigger scans yet.
Very satisfied with these clear inkjet labels.  They seem much easier to remove from the backing than the off-brand I previously bought.
This is the perfect correction pen for those small errors and typos. It dries quickly and lets you correct everything much faster, and is super comfortable — even for a lefty, like me!

These are exactly as advertised.  They're manila folders with large tabs that really stand out.The special feature is that the tabs have a plastic coating that makes them erasable and reusable.  You can only write on them with a Sharpie or other permanent marker.  After you write on them, you can completely erase the tab with a "white eraser" and reuse them.First, I tried a felt tip pen, just to see what would happen.  It smeared right off, but when I used a Sharpie as instructed, it looked great and didn't smear.  I had aFaber Castell Eraserin my art kit, and that erased the Sharpie like it was never there.  I also tried a pencil eraser to see what would happen, but it didn't completely erase, and if I wasn't careful, I could imagine it ripping the plastic.So basically, this is just what it says it is.  If you have permanent markers and a good eraser, you can use these for great looking reusable folders.  Recommended.

This replaced a 6 yr old pad with a gel-infused wrist support.Basically, the reasons that this pad is better than that one are that:-The material it's made from soft plastic that doesn't hold grime like the old pad did that was covered with a felt-like material.-The support covers a wide area and holds the wrist without being too firm.-Seems like the mouse lazer works better on the slightly textured pad than a cloth-like material.

Not only is this chair one of the most comfortable office chairs I've had, it is a nice looking one, too! (I was supposed to have received the blue but was shipped the brown) I have major back problems and this chair makes it feel really good when having to sit for any length of time. I use it at my sewing machine and for computer work. One problem I noticed is on the right arm, the "pad" always comes loose from the base of the arm. Not a huge problem because it snaps back on but, a problem just the same. It arrived almost put together! All I had to do is attach the arms underneath the chair and set the chair on the base. The seat is adjustable and the arms are also.

The real gem is Avery software. Of course, the labels are easy to pill off the sheet, to stick to any reasonably smooth and hard surface thanks to a permanent adhesive, and to remove without leaving residue. The Avery software allows very productive laser and ink jet printing from edge to edge including full color background. One option is to design & print online using thousands of professionally prepared templates without a need for downloading. The other is to produce labels in-house that requires downloading a wizard or blank templates or pre-designed ones for Microsoft Word, Adobe software, or Apple Pages. Both, the wizard and the online option allow mail merge and filling the whole sheet at once resulting in high productivity and low cost of professionally looking labels also with bar codes.

I've been really pleased with the performance of this scanner.  We've been using Fujitsu Scansnaps of various flavors (S500, S1500 and S1300) around the office for several years now and I feel that they set a pretty high standard for quality and ease of use.  The Brother ADS2000 has proved itself the equal of the Scansnap, if not a hair better.  It's a little bit louder than the Scansnap (it does have a quiet mode, but I'd rather have the speed) but it experiences fewer feed issues - in fact, I've put a good amount of paper through it and have not had a -single- misfeed.  I've run card stock, copy paper, receipts and more through it without any issues.  My experience in this regard is materially better than any of the six or so Scansnaps I've used.  I don't like the software (Mac) as well as the Scansnap Manager - but it may be a matter of familiarity.  There are more options for scanning (e.g., save to .tiff format) as opposed to the Scansnap (.pdf only), but I prefer the simplicity of Scansnap Manager because I really only want docs in and pdfs out.  So, better on paper handling but not as good in software - but still an all-star and at a significantly lower price.
I use these for writing on dark surfaces and they are very durable and last a long time.  Good product

I use a Brother laser printer for personal/school use, so I'm not an expert by any stretch of the imagination.What made me choose Brother for my laser printer from the getgo was their great laser cartridge design which allows you to super easily refill your own toner (literally pop open a black cap on the side and pour the stuff in).  Save some money and the environment at the same time!For my casual usage, this cartridge is well-priced and great quality.

I had a larger model in the past and was looking for something similar but smaller.This model had a smaller footprint but was still quite large. That's ok, considering it takes the place of printer, scanner, copier and fax machine. I've had Brother All-In-One models that are 2x the size and function less.Set up was easy and quick. Love the ADF (Automatic Document Feeder) for large scanning and copy jobs. The Airport is a bonus but works only sporadicly. Seems to come in and out and sleeps when they printer does. Not very helpful to print from another place in the house.I did print a few photos and was happy with the results. Not perfect but not horrible either.The ink is pretty pricey and I worry how often I will have to purchase it. But all in all this is a good, solid printer that we'll keep for a while.

These are exactly as advertised. Storage Boxes. For that they work well. We keep several years of our tax forms in case we ever get audited. The forms were cluttering up our roll-out oak file cabinet so we wanted to put all but the previous years tax forms in the attic. These are perfect for that application. I hope I never have to see those forms again.

These double-sided stickies are great for posting up featherweight items on a fridge, wall, etc. Their advantage is that they don't obscure like a magnet or clip would. But they can't really hold on to anything with a bit of mass. Even if you use several of them, the objects tend to fall off after several minutes. So be careful.

If seeing someone wax rhapsodic about book tape freaks you out, stop reading now. I fell in love with book tape as a high school student. I was a book junkie who was somewhat financially hard-pressed, so most of the books I bought were old paperbacks from the used book store. When I worked in my high school library, one of my jobs was using book tape to repair books, and I thought this stuff was amazing! For the novice, book tape is basically  like very high quality, clear strapping tape that can be used to repair books. Unlike normal strapping tape, it is acid-free so it will not cause the book to deteriorate further. In short, it's a godsend to people who don't want their old books to fall apart. After I got out of school, I never knew where to buy real book tape, so I sometimes used strapping tape for the same purpose. However, it doesn't work as well and can cause more damage to the book as it can turn the paper yellow, make it brittle, etc. Librarians always told me it would have to be ordered from a library supply place, but now I can get it from Amazon! Hooray! I love this stuff! Now my first Harry Potter paperback can be repaired and enjoyed by my kids without worrying about the cover falling off in their backpack.

This binder is an OK product. The plastic pocket is a nice touch, although I don't think it will hold up to a lot of use especially if you put the kind of items into it that are shown. I was hoping to use this for recipes for a cookbook I am working on, but the unusual size makes that impossible since I am using a standard sized paper. Reading the marketing information I am not quite sure what the purpose of this binder would be. It might be good for teens or children to carry and organize their lose items.

I think this product has great potential. It tears easily along the cutter in a nice straight line. Seems to stick well. The only problem I had was writing on it. Tried a couple of different pens, but couldn't get a good smooth flow of ink. Otherwise good!

We can continue to relay on the Post-It name brand. These labels appear to be like any other and come with easy-to-follow directions for typing and printing. However, the main sales point of this product is that the labels are "removable". Because of this very sales pitch and creation, the labels have a strong adhesive, but not a permanent adhesive. They firmly adhere to the file folder, then when you are ready, they will peel off so that the folder can be nearly re-used.After several uses of a few file folders with these labels, I can say that I highly recommend this product.

This is a very nice table.  In my case it will stay up all the time.  Have a computer on one side and all of my grandson's current Lego creations on top.  There is enough room for two boys to sit side by side.  Of course if you did not have it against a wall like I do you could easily handle larger groups.

I love this little labeling system and have used a few different ones in the past 2 years since I adopted theGetting Things Donesystem.  The system is really neat and though I am not always faithful, when I adhere to it, I am able to get things done, indeed.  A labeler is critical for this system and important for organization in general and this little guy does the job.Pluses:-Small-Quick-Very nice printout-Easy to use-Ready-made formats for VHS/MiniDV/CDs/File tabs/Dividers-Easy-to-obtain refillsMinuses:-No AC power option!  Even if it were an additional $20 I would do this because it is a...-BATTERY VAMPIRE!  It goes through fresh batts at an incredible rate, even using nice fresh Duracells.[Note: I want to say that I wish this at least took AAs instead of the tiny AAAs because the small size increase means almost a tripling of the power and would be well worth it for this device.  Also, some other reviewers have noted that you could use rechargeable batteries, but I find that with the always-highly-rated Eneloops, I get the "Low Batt" warning almost immediately.]-Semi-expensive ribbon refills-A moderate amount of ribbon wasteOverall, this is an outstanding product and is essentially perfect in function, I hold back one star given some of the practical issues on using it regularly, namely the lack of AC adapter option in the setting of pretty voracious battery use.For folks who use it only intermittently, I give this 5 stars.For folks using it daily, I would caution you to consider a model with the AC adapter.

Keep in mind that the package includes "6" envelopes, but 3 are decorated, and 3 are plain.  You put your item in the decorated package, and then you put that envelope in the plain one (for mailing).  Or, I guess you could just hand the decorated envelope to someone if they are local and use the plain one for some other mailing.Yeah, I agree with other reviewers that the graphics aren't that great, but they are ok.  These decorative folders will expand some, and they are good for items like books, CDs, DVDs, calendars, scarfs/mittens (other small items like this).  The nice thing, you don't have to find a box to put some of your items in, then to wrap it on top of that.I don't typically give a lot of gifts like that, but, its nice to have a couple on hand.

The package arrived with a slight tear in the soft molded plastic that holds everything together. The two 5x8-inch magnets were in excellent condition and had pleasant colors. The boards and the magnets are thick enough to allow excellent adherence to our refrigerator.The problem was that there was no magnet on the pen. What's the good of a dry-erase board without a dry-erase marker right at hand? I had read descriptions here and knew that the pen was supposed to have a magnet--but this one didn't. After puzzling over this, I decided to look inside the packaging and found a small, thin magnet that had fallen off the marker. There is a small slot on the top end of the pen that looked like something had been glued into it but had fallen off. Sure enough, the little magnetic strip fit into that slot. I glued it back in place, and now I'm able to keep the pen on the side of the refrigerator. I wouldn't put it on the door, because the magnetic part is very flimsy and I would expect that repeated opening and closing of the door would cause the pen to fall off from time to time. That would be a hassle.As for how useful it is, well, it's been up on the refrigerator for 4 or 5 days and we haven't used it yet other than to write a test message (and then erase it--writing and erasing worked well).

First of all I do not understand how anyone can give this binder one star.  It's white; that automatically rates at least four stars!  And with those 2-inch rings, I have plenty of room to move around, just not so much that I get into trouble and shame my husband.  Really, this is just the perfect binder for a proper lady.
I have nothing but good things to say about this printer! It is not a "photo" printer, but it prints nice photos. The black is nice and rich and the colors pop! Great quality...must have!

Don't get me wrong, this product has many positives.  The folder itself is heavy duty.  The tab is sturdy and thick.  It is just that if you call something Easy Slide Tab, then the tab should slide easily.  It does slide, just not easily.

It's great tape and holds packages closed.  In my experience it's best to ship using a good tape however this product is overpriced.  I buy it to get over the free super saving threshold once in awhile.

I was looking for something in between a cheap plastic lap desk and one of the heavier, more padded ones and thought this might be a good solution. It just doesn't do the job.The top is a nice size, allowing about few inches on either side of my 16" laptop. It's firm but not hard - if I put a little muscle into it, I could bend it like cardboard which was fine when I first got it. A month of daily use later, it's started to warp, which I mostly blame on the inadequate cushioning underneath it.The velvety fabric is filled with those lightweight styrofoam beads and there aren't enough to distribute evenly unless it's sitting on a flat surface. Any gap between your legs, any time you shift the desk to one side, the beads shift around the high point of your lap, essentially putting the top of the desk right on your leg. It negates the point of the desk and if you have a laptop that runs hot sometimes like I do, a very warm lap.I'd go with something more expensive or at least something designed better.

I have a major thing for Kanye, and not only cause he's from CHI-TOWN.At first I was like yeah, I'm copping this CD just because I loved to hear GOLD DIGGER, but then as I let the entire CD play it was like WHOA...I'm not like the other reviewers where I'm running down the beats, this track, and that producer. It had been a few months since my father's shredder bit the dust, and with sensitive documents piling up it was time to get a new shredder.  For the price you pay, the W-11C is a fantastic shredder that eats and eats and eats without so much as a hesitation; making short work of the large pile up of paperwork my father had been unable to shred/dispose of properly.  Below I have broken the shredder review down into three crucial parts, Performance / Design / Durability** PERFORMANCE **The Fellowes Powershred W-11C is a monster.  To start things off the shredder is rated at 190 inches per minute ( ~16 feet per minute ) which is fairly fast considering other shredders in this price range.  The fast shredding rate made quick work of virtually anything it was fed and showed no hesitation on up to 6 sheets of paper.  The shredder began to slow when 7+ sheets were fed into it at once so I recommend no more than 6 sheets to avoid unnecessary motor stress.When it came to inserting documents to shred, the 9" opening was perfect and the machine cared little for how the document was fed through it.  Even when the paper began to crunch up against the side (which constantly jammed our old shredder) the W-11C just ate through it without jamming or slowing down.  The material that comes out is "Security Level 3" Cross-Cut confetti.  It looks like tiny rectangular sheets and leaves documents in such a confetti-mess that it would be a nightmare to have to piece it back together again.Overall the performance is 5 stars!  The W-11C is just a beast that hungers for paper and devours almost anything fed to it!** DESIGN**The system has a very simple but effective design which is broken into two parts.  WASTEBASKET and SHREDDERSHREDDER - The guts of this monster.  It accounts for most of the product weight (about 15 lbs of the 17lb shipping weight).  While heavy, the product is built well having a sturdy design that lets it slip right into the wastebasket nice and snug.  It includes a folding handle for when you need to lift the top of the device to make it easier to grip and lift.  The opening for shredding paper is 9", which is very generous and makes feeding paper quite easy.  The power switch is fairly solid but what concerns me is the "lock" switch.  It is nice to have a lock out feature but the switch feels very flimsy compared to the rest of the machine.  I can see the switch snapping if you forget to push down the lock button and pull.  While a minor issue it could end up causing a problem if it does snap.WASTEBASKET - Nice and spacious.  Offers plenty of storage for the confetti, and contains a slot in which you can feed envelopes and non shred-able material in without having to lift the heavy shredder top.  The only real flaw here is that the basket is very light.  The basket itself might weight one pound, while the shredder weights almost 15 pounds. This makes the overall design very "top heavy".  If you want to move the "assembled" device or accidentally nudge it with your foot there is a risk of the entire thing tumbling over / becoming unstable as-is with most top heavy objects.  Not a major concern but does make moving the basket and shredder a bit difficult to do as one piece.** DURABILITY **The W-11C is meant to take a beating.  While it isn't designed for constant long term usage, it does hold up exceptionally well over time.  There is very little wear-n-tear on the machine after constant use.  The only flag that goes up is that the shredder does get fairly warm after constant use if you are using it on and off for around 10 minutes straight.  The motor does get warm fairly quickly so I wouldn't use it longer than 5 minutes of constant use; or 10 minutes of casual shredding for risk of overheating the motor. (the W-11C has a 5 minute auto turn off anyhow; probably to avoid overheating the motor)** OVERALL I would give this shredder 5 stars.  It is a beast of a shredder that will not let you down.  What few problems/flaws it might have are minor and with some care and a little caution you won't ever have a problem with the device.  If you are in the market for a decent shredder that cross-cuts the W-11C is the one you want.  Good Security level confetti shredding, excellent performance and a quality design.** NOTE: For Maintenance, the W-11C calls for Non-Aerosol Vegetable Oil. However, if you only use your shredder casually the use of Vegetable oil can be a problem since it could go rancid and begin to gunk up the gears.** NOTE: For lubrication I prefer using UNV-38036 sheets.  They are basically 8.5" x 5.25" sheets of paper that you shred.  Inside is a lubricant that gets all over the gears. Just shred, run the shredder for 15 seconds in reverse and you are done. No squirt bottles, no messy clean up etc.

We got this to replace our old HP Officejet 5610 which we use for scanning and storing documents and old pictures as well as color print jobs (assignments, homework, t-shirt design etc). This printer is compact, yet larger than your average inkjet printer. apporximately 1.5ft W x 2ft D x 2ft H; The second paper tray is added by simply placing it under the printer - You can get the printer w/o that paper tray (WF-4630 model) and shave several inches off the height and also save a good chunk of $$$ .The printer came very nicely packed and there were lots of tapes to remove. Make sure you remove some tape and plastic inserts inside the printer as well before using. There were very clear quick setup instructions. The ink cartridges are very easy to install. The initial set-up does take about 20 minutes including software installation. After that the printer can be connected to the network very easily (wired or wireless) or connected to a computer using USB cable. You can either use the large and convenient touch screen LCD or the software tool to configure and connect the printer to your network. For wifi direct, the LCD menu provides the option to check the printer's SSID and password using which you can connect a mobile device to the printer. Do note that, you need to use the Epson app to print using this method. For Airprint and network printing, the printer and the mobile device must be on the same wifi network.The printer uses a large inkjet for printing and therefore prints multiple lines at the same time. So it's much quicker than your average inkjet printer. The print quality is also really good. I should note however that in draft mode, colored/gray scale text is not that good compared to black and white. So if you want to save ink and use draft mode, make sure you print in pure black and white. There are a number of memory slots in the printer for preset print preferences which is very convenient if you have different types of print jobs you use (pictures, draft document, normal color etc). One convenient feature here is a auto-duplexing - meaning it can automatically print in two-sided mode. Do make sure you select short-edge or long-edge binding for proper double sided printing.This printer can also be used as a scanner (including through mobile devices) where you can scan documents in to pdf files or scan images in to tiff/jpeg files. This is very convenient for us to store important documents as pdf files. The scanner accepts source documents either from the flatbed glass or from the document feeder. This is very convenient if you want to automatically scan a bunch of documents together or something like a bulk mortgage document. We used a flatbed for pictures and books. It's very convenient.The printer also acts as a copier; I normally scan and store documents as pdf and print them when needed. However, the fast print capability of this printer makes it a convenient copier. It also has fax capability if you need.The two paper trays at the bottom hold more than 250 sheets each. There is a small try at the back to use for envelopes and other special paper (as well as fax). There is a top tray to use for scanning. Overall, a very decent multi-functional printer with amazingly fast printing speeds for an inkjet printer. Very good print quality. A tad bulky and color text is not that great in draft mode.

You will have to do most of the figuring out of this machine on your own, the instructions are pretty bad. But, once you realize the spiral spines have to sit BEHIND the comb, in a certain direction, and that you do NOT pull the "opener" arm all the way as shown, but only as far as you can see the comb bend, and that the punched paper DOES NOT slip in the comb, but in front of it, it's a really great machine. The draw setting are not really explained either, but they are intuitive as long as you have an awareness of basic paper stock, knowing the difference between letter, A4 and A5. You have to be certain you set the switches to the right sized paper, and really check the line-up plate - it may seem fine to your eye until you actually rest paper against it to make the punch, when it slips tight against the groove driver for the plate. Make sure you check that alignment before you pull the punch arm down.  For me, though, that follows a pretty normal rule - measure twice, cut once.What I love about this device is that is requires no electricity, can be reboxed when you don't need it, and once you have it figured out, it is easy to teach.  The small "started" pack of spines and covers was great to play with. Practice on a short project you want to bind before you do anything where you spent more cash on supplies for the machine.  The weight of the device keeps it from sliding around, which is needed for big projects. You do need to wrestle with bigger efforts, this is mechanical not electrical - but like all efforts, you learn a system, get the hang of it, and soon are making great products!Worth the money - but - jeez, an instructional on-line video would have been better than the nearly meaningless picture card instructions provided.

These Avery sticky notes are the shape of a stubby arrow (approx. 2 3/4-in. square), in the bright colors of pink and yellow highlighter pens, and made of non-rippable, micro-thin plastic material like Post-it Flags.They're good for marking a spot (I use them as bookmarks, positioning them at the exact line where I leave off), but are even better for making a note; they're basically an alternative to highlighter pens. I originally assumed that a sticky note is a sticky note. What would differentiate them? So, I thought about what I want from a sticky note. I want to be able to write on it and have it continue to stick but remove cleanly when done.Obviously, you can write on Avery Sticky Notes just as well as you can write on Post-It Notes. So, on to the stickiness. Many times, I've found Post-It Notes on the floor, because they stopped sticking after awhile.So, I did two tests with Avery and Post-It 3 x 3 sheets. In the first test I stuck one of each note on the wall and applied one firm thumb swipe across each. A couple hours later, the Post-It note was on the floor. 10 hours after that, the Avery note was still firmly in place. One point for Avery.I've also found that Post-It notes quickly lose their stickiness if you remove and reapply them multiple times such as in whiteboard exercies. So, I stuck one of each note onto the dining room table (horizontally) 10 times each. I tried to use the same motion and pressure with each one. The following morning, both were still stuck to the table but the Post-It note had started to peel and curl. The Avery note was firmly attached and flat. Avery leads 2-0.I found that both notes peeled cleanly without leaving and stickiness behind, so no points there.After these tests, I definetly prefer the Avery notes. I don't know if I would pay a lot more for them, but looking at similar quantities on Amazon for 3 x 3 multi-color sticky notes, they seem to be almost exactly the same price per sheet.Avery wins.

Epson's Expression range of all-in-ones stretches from a simple entry-level machine up to the Expression Photo XP-850, which has all the extras you are likely to ask for. Although it has the Photo tag, mainly indicating that it's a six-ink printer, it also includes an Automatic Document Feeder (ADF) for its scanner and full fax functions.The printer has a surprisingly small footprint (which we LOVE) to its largely glossy black case and when you lift it you can tell that a lot is being packed inside, because of its solid and heavy make-up.  The control panel hinges out from the front surface of the printer with dedicated touch buttons down either side. Below this is a flip-down cover for the two, separate paper trays. The top one of these takes 20 sheets of photo paper, while the bottom one takes only 100 sheets of plain paper, which seems small when you have more than 1 person printing to this printer.There's no option for an extra tray, either, though a flip-down cover at the rear provides access to a single sheet feed for envelopes and special media. Lastly, right at the bottom is a CD/DVD carrier, which pulls out and slots in above the trays for direct disc printing.The output tray and the touchscreen control panel above work in a similar way to HPs Envy lifestyle all-in-ones, but only do half the job. If you start printing without opening the machine up, it very intelligently folds out the control panel to a convenient angle and powers out the output tray.However, like machines further down the Expression range, getting this tray back in again involves pressing on its front edge against quite a graunchy-feeling mechanism. This printer is a very good choice for the small workgroup that needs a printer with large capacity input bins, or who needs the multiple bins for different size paper. It prints rapidly, has good scan capabilities, and utilizes a newer type of ink cartridge that is very simple to install. As near as I can tell, the printer is actually the exact same model as the 4530 except that this model sits on top of a second input tray. If you don't need the extra capacity or flexibility, the 4530 is considerably cheaper. For home use, the smaller model would probably be better due to its smaller size.Pro:Simple setup. The normal method is to install the driver and then hook up the printer via USB (temporarily) to complete the setup. I chose to connect the printer to the network via the front panel and then just install the software. I did this because I didn't have a USB A to B cable handy, but it is nice to know one can set it up without the USB connection if needed; the printer might not be near the computer during setup.Wireless or wired operation. The printer supports the standard wireless security, and it is easy to set up.The print output is very nice. Basic business printing looks good on inkjet paper. There are lots of options for printing everything from basic black to photos. The photos would normally be printed via the small capacity rear input tray. The manual indicates that this tray is also used for printing envelopes.The multiple input trays are very useful for the small business - either one can put different size papers in the two trays, or simply use them for letter size so that one does not have to refill as often.Scanning can be direct from a USB drive, initiated from a computer, or input into a specific computer on the network via the front panel of the printer. These options make it very flexible and useful. There is a nice document feeder on top that works well to feed the scanner.Duplex printing is defaulted and works well (in Windows 7 - see below). This can be changed via the printer or windows settings.The new ink cartridge design is simply outstanding. One pulls the cartridge out of the plastic case and inserts it - no removing tabs or anything like that. The cartridges click in and out with the push of a finger. Excellent!The fax works well and has settings to work with an answering machine - a necessity for the home business.The printer comes with "XL" capacity cartridges, rather than some kind of "starter" cartridges. This means it is ready to work when you set it up. Be sure to have a spare set of cartridges on hand (see below as to why). Also, there are individual color cartridges, which is much more cost efficient - one only needs to replace the cartridges that have run out. Many other printers include all the colors in a single cartridge.Con:For Windows XP, the printer will not print duplex - unless you want to remove the paper and then place it back into the input tray, which is the manual way of doing it. This seems to be a characteristic of the newer Epson printers; my workforce 840 is the same. The XP settings indicate that duplex is enabled, but it just doesn't work. It will print duplex on Windows 7 just fine.The manual states that the printer will not work if any cartridge is out of ink. I presume this means that if one runs out of color, then the black printing won't work. I have not run through the high capacity cartridges yet, but if this is true it is not the optimum design - the printer should continue to output black text even if a color cartridge is empty. After all, most business output is black, and this printer is a bit large for household use.Summary:If your small business or workgroup needs a capable printer, this one fits the bill. Great printing and print handling, simple scanning, fax capability - it has what the job needs. Recommended.

As a previous owner of an Epson R1800, I expected nothing short of extraordinary with the R2880.  The R1800 met every need I had and produced quality prints with absolutely no hassles.  Does the R2880 live up to the same standard?The R2880 is not a direct upgrade from R1800 (which was replaced with the R1900), so I will not compare the two in every aspect.  However, as an amateur photographer I have gotten used to the prints that the R1800 produced.  The R2880 is a very large printer and you should plan to have some workspace set aside for it.  The footprint is about the same as the R1800.  When fully expanded with the paper trays you will need almost an entire table for this printer.I have tested the printer with various print sizes (4x6, 5x7, 8x10, up to 13x19).  Thus far, every print has been clean and crisp.  The colors are well saturated and the tones are dead on.  I enjoyed the gloss option that was on the R1800, but it's not a deal breaker.  The colors were vibrant, but also impressive was the black and white prints.  The detail and tones were amazing.  I prefer the Epson Premium Luster Paper for most of my prints and the R2880 does an excellent job on that paper.  I was truly impressed.The speed of prints was on par with similar models.  I have not timed them, but it does have decent printing speed.  By simple comparison, it might be a tick slower than my previous R1800.  But again, I did not time them.The features that are included with the R2880 work out fairly well.  I tend not to use the roll mechanism, but it is included.  The CD printing tray works perfectly.  I do wish they would include an ethernet connection on these models though.  For this price range, I think it should be a default feature. USB works fine, but in this day and time an ethernet connection for any printer over $600 (or even $300 for that matter) should be assumed in my opinion.My complaints are fairly minor, but only time will tell if they get worse.  First, is the price of the ink.  The R2880 uses a smaller cartridge than my previous printers, yet, the price per cartridge remains the same.  I realize the ink itself is different (and to their credit, seems to do a great job), but at my current rate this printer will likely cost me almost twice as much to operate.  I'd recommend shopping around, as I've seen almost a 35% difference in cartridge price at different stores.  No matter what you do, be sure to keep extra ink cartridges around.  The size of these cartridges relegates their printing capacity in a major way.  After my initial test prints, my ink levels were showing about 50%.My second complaint is somewhat related to ink.  There are times during the start of a print job (my printer is already on, but I haven't used it in days) that it will take almost a minute to begin printing.  It appears that it is going through a cleaning or preparation procedure (usually done only when you turn the printer on or off).  I'm not sure if any ink is being used, but my major complaint is the time.  I should not have to wait for a simple word processing document to print out.My third and final complaint is the fact that I have to swap out the photo and matte black ink cartridges.  I'm not entirely sure why Epson chose to do this, but I was really disappointed.  This is an expensive printer and outperforms its competition in so many ways, but they couldn't include a slot for both cartridges?  Seems strange.At the end of the day, I do highly recommend the R2880.  The prints are fantastic!  While the printer does have some pitfalls, it does do one thing very well: create outstanding photo prints.  I would hesitate recommending that a person upgrade from an Epson R1800, R1900, R2400 or similar model.  It would be difficult to justify the costs.  However, if you are in a market for a new large format photo printer, this should be one of your choices.

The Epson R1900 is a large format professional photo printer optimized to produce glossy prints. It can print up to 13 x 19 inch prints through traditional sheet feed, or up to 13 x 44 inch panoramas via the included roller feed mechanism (all borderless). You can also create custom-printed CD/DVD media (make sure the media you use are those that allow printing) using an adapter that is also included. The printer takes 8 small individual ink cartridges (5 color, two blacks, and a gloss optimizer), which sell for about $15 (you get 4 gloss optimizer cartridges for about $16, which suggests to me that the printer drinks this stuff like Kool-Aid!). I have yet to get an idea of the amount of printing provided by this ink system. Apparently Epson has optimized the R1900 to be stingier on ink while maintaining excellent output. The printer uses the latest Epson Hi Gloss 2 Ultrachrome pigment ink, which according to industry standard setter Wilhelm Research has fade resistance of up to 200 years, depending on the paper usedThe controls on the printer are quite simple, consisting of an on off switch and three buttons that control other aspects of printer life. There is no LCD on the printer. For a printer of this size, it is fairly compact. The paper feed and output trays telescope and fold up into the printer resulting in a smaller (though not small, you will need a large and sturdy amount of desk space to accommodate the R1900) footprint when not in use. This design also might aid in keep dust out of the printer over the long haul.  The printer is attractively and simply designed. The printer body is primarily plastic, but feels of high quality. The fit and finish seem quite good. The printer inspires confidence in terms of build quality. The printer comes with a full complement of inks (I am assuming that these are filled to capacity, but this is not clear to me). There are -surprisingly - no paper samples. The instruction manual is slim and not terribly useful. Installation is a breeze. Remove all the packing tape, install the ink cartridges, install software, and you up and ready to print in about 10 minutes. The printer driver is easy to use, and fairly intuitive.I have tested the printer out on a variety of papers and sizes:1) Canon Photo Paper Plus Glossy (4 x 6);2) Inkpress Lustre (5x7);3) HP Premium Glossy (8 x 10).The output produced is simply stunning. Colors are vibrant, images are sharp, print speed is adequate (these large format printers are not the fastest printers in the market, look elsewhere if speed is your primary concern), the print textures have a Pro-Lab feel to them, no roller marks, and the R1900 is surprisingly quiet. I was especially curious about the Inkpress Lustre (a matte photo paper) and they were fantastic (phew!), so this is not just a glossy print machine, in my experience. I enjoy the look and feel of luster/satin papers so was pleased that the R1900 produced such excellent prints on this paper type. The paper feed mechanism works very well in my limited-to-date testing, yet discernibly better than the similar class HP B8850. The paper tray is not large-capacity (30 sheets of photo-paper), which may be a drawback to some users over some of the competition. To me it is a non-issue.If you are a photo enthusiast or pro, who enjoys printing on a variety of papers and sizes, this would be an excellent printer for you. However, if you are printing mainly 4x 6 inch prints or mixed text, look somewhere else. I look forward to working with this printer in the future and further exploring its capabilities.Very highly recommended!

A typical ordinary 3-ring vinyl covered binder sells for about $1.00 - $2.00. Leave off the vinyl and they sell you only the cardboard but now the price is almost $8.00?  On what planet? This product just smacks of charging you more but giving you less.It's not that it's a bad idea. There are uses for it where a cheap vinyl binder would look, well, cheap. It is especially well suited for craft projects in which the user can decorate and personalize it. One of the best ideas is one that I read in these reviews is for the kids to get creative and cover it with whatever their minds can come up with. So not only isn't it a bad idea, it's actually a great idea.So why can't it earn more than 3-stars (which remember is NOT a bad review, 3-stars means I like it). It can't earn "I love it" or "It's awesome" because it is grossly overpriced. Being basically a sheet of cardboard it acquires greasy fingerprints as soon as you touch it. The edges fray and if your intent is to keep it looking like it did when you bought it, that will be impossible. $8.00 is a lot to spend for a binder that you can't even touch.By the way, this binder is made in China. I'm guessing at a total cost of 5 cents per unit. While there may be something to be said about using "environmental" materials, any benefit is far offset by the carbon footprint left by transporting the product via rail, ship, airplane and truck to your doorstep. Don't be so easily fooled by the manufacturer telling people who buy this $8.00 binder are "protecting the environment".And as far as being recyclable, that is a beautiful objective, but life's reality is that people buy binders to KEEP things in, often for many, many years. A binder is one of the least likely products someone would buy and throw away a few week, months or even years later. IMHO this binder is actually WORSE for the environment because if you get it wet it will be destroyed and you'll have to throw it away (recycle it), something you would not have to do with an ordinary binder.

I like Sharpie Highlighters.  As a schoolteacher, I use them for a lot of things, so I have a bunch of them.  I compared these new Sharpie Gel Highlighters to theSharpie Accent Pocket-Style Highlighters, 12 Colored HighlightersandSharpie Accent Retractable Assorted 8 Pack).  I really liked them all.COLOR:  These come in Yellow, Orange and pink only -  the others come in wider variety, but I hope that will change.  The color on the Gel highlighters is MUCH better.  The Gel orange is almost florescent compared to the darker orange of the Accent orange.  The others are also much brighter in Gel than standard.WINNER: GEL HIGHLIGHTERBLEED-THROUGH:  The Gel highlighters do not bleed through.  PERIOD.  The Accent highlighters bleed through - particularly thin papers like Bibles and newsprint.WINNER:  GEL HIGHLIGHTERSMEAR:  The Gel highlighters DO smear.  They smear a great deal on glossy pages like photographs and calendars and such.  The Accent highlighters also smeared, but the excess ink would dry out quickly.  The smear of these comes from tiny particles of gel.  They do not dry out, but rather remain intact and smear under pressure.  The highlighted areas feel a bit 'waxy,' as if they had been written on with crayon.  I did a simple test by highlighting an area with Gel and regular.  I placed another piece of paper on it and rubbed the paper.  The Gel transferred to the blank page, but the Accent did not.  Still, If you are careful, both are good.  The Accent Highlighters tend to smear ink and pencil on the paper; the Gel markers do not.WINNER:  TIEDURABILITY:  I've accidentally left Accent highlighters uncapped overnight and they died.  I deliberately left the orange Gel Highlighter uncapped for over 24 hrs.  It was still fine. My middle school daughter has projects due all the time. I was spending a fortune on ink at the local office supply store. After laminating a bunch of items, I do not understand why this laminator is so special that it should have a relatively high price. My son had a presentation at school and I handed him this nifty gadget to see if he could set it up and use it with ease.  1-2-3 and he was ready to roll. Oh, did I mention that he is 13? ...it's the people who still need improvement.  We recently moved into a new home and shortly thereafter I got a leg injury.  While recovering from surgery it seemed like every random person with an agenda wanted to test our door bell during the day and it was driving me nuts, so I ordered this sign.  Used the included double-sided table and affixed it to our front door.  The size of the sign is perfect -- not obnoxiously large, but not so small that it would be hard to ignore.
