The Avery 8395 labels -- generically called name badges -- are outstanding in both features and price.  Following are four pluses and two minuses.+ + + STICKYAt the Kansas City, Missouri, affiliate of Habitat for Humanity, where I've been volunteering on construction job sites since 1997, we all wear name tags.  These tags are merely strips of duct tape written on with a marker, and I can tell you from all those years of experience that they fall off pretty readily when applied to clothing that then endures several hours of twisting and turning and stretching and contracting and pulling and -- don't forget -- sweating.This product withstands all those problems, so you can imagine how much better it will withstand the rigors of, say, your typical business seminar where the guests wear business suits, unless your business seminars frequently include guests wearing overalls and do-rags and muscle shirts and construction boots and tool belts.These Avery 8395 name badges stay stuck.  Let me tell you how I know.  Yesterday afternoon I attached one to a t-shirt and then here's what I did:== Mowed the lawn and did some other yard work, enough to work up a sweat== Wrestled with our 70-pound dog for a while== Rode my motorcycle for half an hour, at one stretch reaching 70 miles per hour (in a 35 mph zone)== Just to see what would happen, I literally scrunched the badge and the fabric underneath it; at first I scrunched pretty lightly, but then I scrunched pretty darned much, a total of maybe half a dozen scrunches altogether== Removed the badge and replaced it== Doffed the shirt and re-donned it== Finally, I slept in the shirt.Then I took the photograph I've added to the Amazon listingAvery Adhesive Name Badges, 2.33 x 3.375 inches, White, Pack of 160 (08395)for these Avery 8395 labels.  As you might not be able to tell, so I will tell you, except for a couple of light crinkles the badge is pristine, because the material it's made of, which I assume is some sort of plastic, is more flexible and thus less likely to crease than paper.  It wants to conform to the shape of the clothing it's attached to no matter how that shape changes.But what's more impressive is that it's still stuck securely to my t-shirt.  After all the grief I put it through, it should have given up and fallen off at SOME point, but it never did.Later: I started another test.  I thoroughly soaked a portion of a different t-shirt with water, and then I applied another of these badges, which I think must be an extreme test.  As of now, an hour later, the badge is firmly planted on my chest, and the fabirc is still faintly wet.And now it's the next day and I've slept wearing the second badge, and I've also scrunched it roughly a few times, and I've also removed it and replaced it twice (no, no wind test or dog-wrestling this time), and it is still stuck quite nicely, thank you.To reiterate, this name badge stays stuck really well.+ + + STURDYAnd not only does it stick well, it's also really sturdy.You literally can't tear these badges apart with your fingers without considerable effort.  If a normal paper badge can be torn with X amount of shear force, these badges won't tear till you've applied maybe 20 times that X amount.  I estimate that 50% of your average grandmothers literally could not tear one of these badges in half.  The plastic film strongly resists efforts to rip instantly in twain and instead merely deforms, which I assure you, even if I can't describe it well, is less catastrophic.+ + + WRITING SURFACEThe front face, the one you write on, feels slicker than paper and seems to be perfect for writing on with a marker; it has just the right texture or the right finish or something.+ + + TWO-WAY REMOVALThis product offers yet another handy feature -- two-way removal -- which is clever.  Expensive, I'm sure, but no less clever.In one scenario you, the badge-monkey, use some sort of broad-stroke marker to write in the guest's name on a badge and then remove it from the backing and hand it, sticky-side down, to that guest, at which point the next move pretty much has to be that that guest applies it to his or her clothing right then and there.  And you can do that with this product as well, if you remove the badge from the FRONT of the sheet as is normal.But if you remove it from the back of the sheet you get a different result.  The result is a separate badge with its backing still attached.  This means you also have the option of merely handing out those self-contained badges, presumably along with a marker, to guests as they arrive.  They can then do the writing and then the removal of the backing (and then the application to their clothing) themselves, and they can do it at their leisure, after putting down their Blackberries and their briefcases.Another option, of course, is for you, the badge-monkey, simply to remove a whole bunch of these badges from the backs of the sheets and lay them out on a table or a counter and direct your guests to them.- - - PRICEAs I think I prove below, no matter how you measure it per inch these name badges are expensive, so you should decide whether they are worth it.  (Prices vary over time, so keep that in mind if you are reading this long after I wrote it, which is April 10, 2011.)At 10 cents per yard, 2-inch duct tape costs $0.009375, or just under a penny, for a name tag that's 3-3/8 inches wide.  At, say, $25 per 400, these Avery 8395 badges, which are cut to that same 3-3/8 inches in width, cost $0.0625 each, which is 6-2/3 times more expensive.  If you account for the fact the badges are 2-1/3 inches high instead of only 2 inches, they're still 600% more expensive than the same acreage of duct tape.Perhaps a more useful point of comparison, unless you're supplying rough, tough Habitat for Humanity volunteers with name tags, is that one model (Avery Border Name Badge Labels, Red, Pack of 100, 2.34 x 3.375 Inches (5140)) of Avery's plain badges of the same dimensions is available on Amazon for, let's say, 3-1/2 cents each, which still makes the fancier Avery 8395 model nearly 80% costlier.(If I got any of that math wrong, please leave a comment.)- - - FORBIDDEN SURFACESAside from these name badges' high price, a drawback is the fact the manufacturer warns, "Do not apply to vinyl, plastic, leather, suede, velvet, curduroy, silk or other delicate fabrics."  I want to know what happens if you do, but I've run enough tests already on these Avery 8395 badges, don't you think?

At not much more than 1/3 the price of theSwingline 747 Classic Stapler, you get a practical stapler that works well. It's rated at 15 sheets, compared to the 20 sheets of the 747, but it doesn't seem to struggle with more sheets than it's rated for.Compared to the 747, it looks smaller. But it's about the same length from end to end. The distance from the part where the staples come out to the part where the stapler pivots is also the same length for both staplers. But this stapler is lighter and has more plastic. The metal part is less visible, giving it the illusion of being smaller than it is. As with other similar staplers, it can be folded open to staple things to flat surfaces such as bulletin boards or wall. This opens short of 180 degrees, placing the tip on the surface at an angle. But the angle seems to work quite well for attaching things to walls. There is no release lever for opening it, so you'll have to be careful not to eject a staple when opening or closing it.One of the purported features of this stapler is environmental friendliness. But the fine print tells you that it's 50% recycled content. And the finer print tells you that the number refers to the top part only. So if you are concerned about keeping plastic out of the landfills, this doesn't seem as if it will help in the long run compared to the 747, which is mostly metal. This stapler also comes with a one year limited warranty, compared to the lifetime limited warranty of the 747. That's not to say that this will fall apart after a year. I can't say how long it will last, and it will most likely last far longer. But I would expect an environmentally friendly product to be designed to last as long as possible.The stapler also features an anti-microbial design. Desktop items are good at picking up germs from regular use, and if this stapler's resistance saves you one trip to the pharmacy over its lifetime, that feature will let the stapler pay for itself. The technology for antimicrobial surfaces is mature enough that I would expect it to be effective. Thus of all the hyped features, this one may be the one that could make a real difference.Overall, I didn't find that this stapler lived up to its major selling point, but it works well and is a good stapler for the price. Had they not made the claim about environmental friendliness, I would have found that this deserves at least four stars, perhaps even more considering that it's a bargain.

This is a comparison review of the Epson LW-300 and LW-400 labelers that I received from Amazon Vine to review, and the Brother P-touch 1880 that I bought from Costco. All three are in the same approximate price range, although the Brother was significantly cheaper than SRP at Costco. I'll hit upon the key differences that I noted but will not discuss the PC linking available to the P-touch 1880 since it doesn't work with a Mac.The Epson 400 screen is a two-line display comprised of illuminated blue letters on a white background, making it MUCH easier to read than the 300 or the Brother. In addition, the size and shape make the 400 more conducive to handheld portable labeling use. The 300 is smaller and somewhat lighter, and would work well for the same purpose, but the shape is not as efficient for secure, handheld use. The 400 also includes a lanyard attachment point making it even better for secure portability and ease of use. The Brother is designed for desktop use, but is light enough to be portable and it runs on 6 batteries like the Epson units (Epson 400 and Brother use AA; Epson 300 uses AAA).All three units are cartridge systems. The Epson labeling tape cartridge is removed or inserted by easily removing the back. The batteries are in the same area so they are replaced the same way. The Brother's batteries are in back also, but the cartridge is inserted by lifting an access flap on top. Brother's method is easier, and doesn't require setting down the back piece while inserting the cartridge, nor would you need to lay the display face down in the process, thus eliminating the chance of scratching the bezel in the process. However, with care, the Epson method should present no issues to the user, but would take a few seconds longer to accomplish.I printed a sample from each machine and tried to include pictures of those samples but it is not yet allowed by Amazon. The resolution of the Brother is somewhat superior to both of the two Epson units, the outputs of which appear identical to me. It is important to note, however, that the Epson units provide quite acceptable results for most applications. But if clarity is of primary importance to you, then the Brother appears to be the more capable unit for large, standard-sized text. The small text is crisp and clear on the all machines. The easy to remove split-back tape is universal between all the machines. Brother claims to make hardier tapes, but I did not have the facilities to test longevity on either brand. Tactilely, the Brother tapes feels stiffer and stronger to me, but not by much. Some Epson tapes can be ironed on, but I do not know if Brother has entered this realm.Another area where the Brother excels is in print speed. The two Epson units printed the 52 letters in my test about 33% slower than the Brother. (Brother 29.2 seconds; both Epson units took 40.1 sec).But where the Epson units excel compared to Brother is in the lack of product waste through lead in and lead out. The short, 10mm lead-in and lead-out are appropriate to prevent jamming in the printer and better tape adhesion, plus they require no manual trimming unless used in a tight spot. (At the time of this review, the Epson tapes were not available for sale so I could not provide a comparison price, but the tapes issued with the labelers are longer than Brother's at 9 meters long, and appear on the Epson site at the same length). The Brother tapes are NOT cheap. The 12mm tapes are 26 feet long and currently cost ~$12-14, or roughly 50/ft, and it wastes about an inch at each end unless the settings are adjusted to trim that back on one end to save about 3/4". But the other end is not adjustable so it must be manually trimmed for balance if the other end is reduced to save product, wasting time as well as material. If your labels are short (say 2", for file folders) then  of the tape is wasted!!! That computes out to $6 of every $12 spent going into the trash!All of these labelers include multiple fonts, various sizes, some special characters, multiple symbols, and various formatting options. Of note is that the Brother is limited to two fonts whereas the Epson has 14 fonts, including old english and script, albeit pretty lame looking in my opinion. In addition, the 300 can print on two lines (like the Brother) but the 400 can put out some pretty sharp 3 and 4 line labels, although the text is pretty tiny (as expected). The method of showing multiple lines on the 300's single-line display is a series of letters with a symbol showing the beginning of the second line. The 400's two-line display is much better. It shows each line separately, and the lines can be scrolled for review, thus making it easier to balance the line lengths.One thing that irritated me about the Brother is apparently common to the Epson 300 and 400: the largest print size is the same on the 1/2" tape as it is on the 3/4" tape. I was hoping that the print head would take advantage of the extra print area, but it does not. The additional tape width is apparently to make the label stand out, or to help in adhering to the surface to which it is attached; it is not to make the font bigger.These new labelers take a little getting used to. In order to provide all the functionality, fonts, special characters, symbols, etc, several keystrokes are sometimes required. This is common with all three units. Once the user gets familiar with the function, however, it doesn't take long to compose and print one or multiple labels. The Epson printers come with basic use guides adhered to the back for quick reference.There are a couple of other nice features incorporated in the 400 that I found useful and convenient. It will format your labels so that they become either index tabs, cable flag labels, cable wrapped labels, or even barcode labels. At home or in business, it's nice to have the formatting for these types of labels already built into the machine.The functionality of the 300 and 400 are the nearly the same; same print speed, same fonts, symbols, and styling, same borders, same print clarity, etc. The differences lie in the 400's much improved display, better portability, and the additional built-in labeling formats (see above). Except for the slightly reduced clarity, the Epson units are both more functional and less wasteful than the Brother I own, and if the tapes are comparably priced, they'd be cheaper to operate.At the time of this review the Epsons were priced at $39 for the 300 and $49 for the 400, which is also the SRP. The display and other features on the Epson 400 makes it a wise choice for the additional $10. I'm rating these machines based on bang for the buck.[SAFETY NOTE: according to the safety instructions, the Epson units are not designed to be used as a step. If you or one of your employees want to use a plastic labeler to gain a couple inches in height, you can expect the thing to break.]

Stanley Bostitch makes power tools, so I was interested to see how that translated into something more refined for the office. I can't say that I'll use the other size choices very often, but it's nice to know that I have that available.This sharpener claims to sharpen a pencil in 2.6 seconds - how does this compare to a cheap electric sharpener?  When I sharpen with the cheap one, it takes 5 seconds for the initial sharpening, plus more to pull it out & look at the progress, then another 2-3 second sharpening interval, then another check and possibly one more final "top-off".  This Bostitch sharpener really does sharpen in about 2-3 seconds, with a perfect point every time so far for me (and my kids!)Yesterday I sat down with the box of my children's colored pencils, to see how the Bostitch would handle the volume - there are about 50 pencils in there, and usually my cheap sharpener would auto-shut-off halfway through due to an overheated motor.  This Bostitch unit, however, easily did the whole box (much faster, of course), and almost seemed to say, "That's all you've got?!"  It was nice to have the job done quickly and efficiently.If the pencil is about 3.5" or shorter, it is too short to be sharpened by this unit.  Of course, with writing pencils that is reasonable.  However, with kids' coloring pencils (especially their favorite colors that they like to use until the pencils are ridiculously tiny), this is a disappointment.The tray that catches the shavings is huge!  I do find it difficult to reinstall it after emptying.  Rather than being a true drawer, it has two little metal spring-like clamps on the bottom of the sharpener that catch little divets in the bottom of the tray - not easy to work with.  I played around with it a bunch, and found it helps to press on one of the metal clamps to allow the tray to catch easily, but to do this you must pick the sharpener up.  This is not easy or convenient, I really do not like this feature.Overall, this is a great tool.  It's a bit pricey, but you definitely get an item of greater speed and accuracy.

The installation process for this printer was clunky and did not work for me.  The root issue was a simple thing (I am an experienced computer user and it still got me)... the drivers on this new printer did not work with Windows 7 and I had to pull fresh from Epson's site (this is 2011 not 2010... Win 7 should not pose an issue).Installation problem:Installing the product onto a windows 7 ultimate 64bit system was a problem.  Following the install instructions (load software, plug in printer, continue installation,etc.) to the letter resulted in installation failure (error message saying can't find files).  To make this worse, for whatever reason, the install process is extremely slow (on a very fast computer), I tried re-installing several times slightly different ways, so I can testify how slow the process is.Solution to issue:Not having success with installation, I googled the issue and eventually found a forum buried saying that win 7 64bit users should toss the install cd and download drivers from the epson.com page.  (this is the face-palm point... normally I always download drivers from the web, but since this was a printer newly introduced, this is 2011 so I expect Epson to be able to handle Win 7 64bit... I did not suspect that the disc provided would already be out of date).  Upon downloading drivers, installation went through without a hitch (though still slow).  Further reading seemed to point to a software issue with pointing to the right file locations in Win 7.Printer:The printer quality was nice at the middle quality level and quick. The criticism I have with the scanner is that the software provide did not estimate the image size based upon resolution (150, 200, 300 dpi) so that I could tell if I was about to save a 100kb file or a 40mb file.User interface in general:In general I was disappointed with the user interface.  It tried to make everything simple to the novice user by limiting the options and selections.  Normally this is fine as long as advanced options are available... they weren't always available, nor were the limited selections of the novice users intuitive.  Instead, the options felt limiting and had me scratching my head a number of times trying to figure out how to do what I knew was an option, if only I could find it.Overall.... -1 star for install process and for user interface software limitations

This is a good performing, basic scanner. It’s not feature packed – I have the base model (TT-BS010) which is pretty basic with regard to features. It is hard-wired only, but offers good performance for the price.The build quality is pretty good. While it’s not rugged enough to stand up to a high-volume environment, it appears more than durable enough for light office use, or perhaps very light retail use. The casing feels pretty solid, and the trigger fires with an easy press. The USB cord is excellent – very thick and stout. That’s good, since the cable is usually the first thing to go since it can get a lot of stress during use.The included stand assembles easily and holds the scanner securely. The scanner can be used as either a hand-held unit (tethered to the PC) or it can scan while in the holder using the auto sensing feature. That feature worked very well – it never failed to sense that something was held in front of the scanner, and the laser stayed on for more than enough time to read even poorly printed UPC stickers. By my rough count, the laser stays on for about 6 seconds.Scan accuracy was excellent with pristine codes and more than acceptable with poorly printed codes. It also did OK with curved codes, but those nearly always required a couple of tries to register. Still, given the price, I’d give it a “good” rating with regard to scan accuracy.The downside of this scanner, and the reason for the loss of a star, is the poor documentation. I was able to get it up and running, but I have set up other scanners, so I knew the general drill. While the documentation does include scan codes to program the scanner for a variety of setup situations, the instructions are so technical and hard to follow that I imagine someone who was doing this for the first time would have a very difficult time, if he/she was able to do it at all. In comparison to the documentation I’ve received with other scanners, this is nothing short of dreadful.If you’re comfortable setting up a scanner and want a budget-priced direct-connect model that performs well, this is well worth considering. I would not, however, recommend it to someone who has never set up a scanner before given the limited value of the documentation.[Sample provided for review]

I've had this printer for a 3 weeks now, using it daily. Here's what I have noticed.Incidentally, for a few years now, I had bought only Canon printers and have had good luck with them.Note: I do not use the fax function, so I didn't set it up, but I do use wireless.Setup: Was easy and went smoothly. I had to have my son in law make a couple choices with the Wireless set up. But we were able to get it going without using the supplied CD.Features: Regarding the scan function, I like to use the grayscale mode at times, and I found I did have to install the CD drivers, which prompted me to download an update (to update the Windows 7 driver that worked fine otherwise), to get the grayscale mode to show up. I should say that I usually use Photoshop Elements 5 to do my scanning with, so maybe that was why I had to install the CD. But I suspect the printer needed the updated driver for the grayscale option to show up.Print quality:  Is very high. I was able to print some beautiful photos borderless at 8.5x11" for visiting relatives.Two Issues:  (1) As other reviewers have pointed out, it is noisy, especially on startup and at times when feeding paper, clunky sounding. And it is noticeably slower than my other printer: Canon Pixma MG5220. The noisiness to me is not a problem except when I want to print late at night when family members are sleeping. So far, none have woken up due to the printer sounds.  The slowness is a bit aggravating, since I am used to my older model faster printer.  The other evening it took about 10 minutes to prepare a preview for a color photo at high quality printing on photo paper. It was long enough that I cancelled the printing and tried again in case something had gone wrong. Nothing had gone wrong; it was just unexpectedly slow.(2) The paper feeder is not flawless. When I was printing another 8.5x11" color photo, this one at standard quality, I placed a Canon sheet of Photo Paper Plus Glossy II in the printer with regular printer paper. The design of the paper cassettes/trays and feeding path is such that you must place the side you want to print on facing down, that is in contact with any other paper in the cassette/tray. So the glossy side of the photo paper came into contact with the regular printer paper. Consequently when the printer fed the paper in for printing, it took two sheets, instead of only the photo paper sheet, and printed mainly on the regular printer paper, not the photo paper. Thus wasting a considerable amount of ink. It worked fine when I removed the regular printer paper and placed only one sheet of the glossy paper into the cassette/tray. I have not had this problem with my other Canon printer.So, basically, a good printer that produces high quality prints. Recommended for those who can live with the issues I mentioned above.

This dispenser has a nice look and feel to it, easy to fill and use with only one hand. Does what it is made to do, which is always nice, don't you think?  +JMJ+  p.s.: it really looks better than what it shows in the picture.

Who needs the awful cheapness of a Swingline stapler when you can have a first class one that succesfully manages a reasonably big amount of paper, and with the ease of pushing a button with one finger.Having dealt with the frustration that the competition provides, this brand name should hopefully disthrone it and make a name for themselves, for good engineering, ease, best quality and reasonable price.Go for it.

I love using colorful pens, especially ones that retract like these do so there's no cap to lose, but these have a practical purpose too. I teach my students to put all the color options to use when taking notes and making outlines from textbooks or recopying lecture notes. Topics, questions, main points, or whatever will be useful can be color coded making each type of information stand out so it's easier to find. Most of these colors stand out well--just a few of the lighter ones would be bettered saved for doodling.

I have a large wide format Epson printer that I really like but is too large to be close to where I work most of the time. So this smaller, compact sized multi-format printer seemed the perfect thing to put near my workstation, to handle quick scans particularly of photos that require a flatbed and cheap print jobs.Overall, I'm pretty happy with it. It can fit four 4x6 prints for scanning, and the quality has been pretty good. Setup with the Wifi was every bit as easy as the other Epson and no problems sending jobs from my iPad. I have a separate document scanner that I use for the majority of multi-document scans, and since this doesn't have a ADF, it's not a good choice if scanning is a big feature you are looking for. The printing is okay, but it also wouldn't be my first choice if good photo prints was something you need. I also find that both this Epson and my other one routinely seem to have problems with my Mac, but not sure if Epson or Apple is to blame for that but it's very frustrating when I need to scan a photo and the Mac refuses to see the devices that are there.So this printer meets my needs for the most part, if it didn't have random connection issues I'd be happier but it does the job for me.

I feel it is well made, feels very solid, even though it is plastic. It's light weight and easy to handle and use. I had no problem scanning barcodes and entering them into Excel.But there are no instructions at all. There is a quick guide, but I found the simple instructions a little frustrating. It says for setup: Scan the "Enter Setup" barcode, then "function setup" and read "exit with save". Well, I didn't have a "function setup" barcode to scan. It also didn't tell me I needed to open my own software, such as excel or word, to import the scanned barcodes into. Once I figured that out, it was easy to scan the "offline mode activation" barcode provided, take the scanner into any room and scan as many barcodes as I needed. It holds about 2500 before it needs to be uploaded and cleared to use again. It charges via the USB cable provided. The quick guide also comes with all the barcodes you need to setup the scanner for wireless scanning and uploading, so you really need to be sure to make a digital copy of this guide in case the paper one gets torn or lost.To get full benefit of this scanner, you really need your own data base software that you can import the scanned barcodes into, to keep track of what personal items you have. Otherwise you just have a list of barcodes that really doesn't mean a lot when you find you need to look up something or something goes missing. I was thinking that, once imported into a software, it would give you a description of the item, not just the code. It does not do that. I was made aware of several personal databases you can get on the internet for special lists, like books or DVDs. That would make this scanner invaluable.
As advertised, happy. I like this shape for the tip of the container. Not much else to say about something like glue.

If you need to handle folding money or other papers with a propensity to stick together, these rubber finger tips will solve the potential problem.  They go on easily, stay on fine, and come off when you want them to.  No objectionable odor.

This product does what it is supposed to do.  It is a pad of labels for with From/To on it.  Each label has its own backer, so you can peel off the label without exposing the adhesive, which is handy if you want to hand a label to someone else to fill out.It could be used for presents also, if you stuck some decorative stickers in the corner, which was a nice use my children found for it this weekend.It would be nice if the cardboard backer had a magnet on it, so it could be stuck to the fridge, or warehouse shelving, or whatever.  However, this is not a defect only an observation.  You could easily glue an old refrigerator magnet to the back.Adhesive is good and stuck to both boxes and tape.In case its not obvious: it would be difficult or impossible to use these label with your computer's printer.  These are for hand written labels only.

For up to 30 pages, this is a pretty good report cover. There is a swing clip which isn't complicated but if you're not into mechanics, you may have to fumble with it for a little bit. The plastic seemed a little stiff to me but I don't know if that is characteristic to the cover, I got one of a bad batch, or if that's a result of a hot shipping environment. Overall, it does offer a nice professional look that is significantly better than the old-fashioned kind with the slide-on plastic binders.

I've been trying to get a good scanner for many years...  Finally this one is pretty close.Pros-The machine itself appears quite well built, more so than i expected.The quality of the scans is excellent; i mean really extremely good.The speed is far faster than my earlier scanners.  The LEDs allow the scan to begin very quickly, without the pause that my earlier scanners had.  The speed of the actual scan is faster than my others.  Speed has always been one of the problems with earlier scanners; it was too tedious to slowly scan numerous documents.  This one is fast enough that i can use it, rather than send-out my photos to a scanning service.Cons-The connection is USB2.0, i would have liked to see USB3.0.Conclusion-Without a doubt, the best scanner in its price range

My mother will be having some work done on her house and she needs lots and lots of boxes to move stuff around. I decided to try out these BANKERS BOX STACKABLE STORAGE BOXES to see how they worked. The boxes are easy to fold and put together and they are fairly sturdy. The black, plastic handles are nice and the see-through window gives the owner the benefit of knowing what's in the box without having to write on it. However, the see-through window also weakens the strength of the box; you could carry/store slightly heavier items if the window wasn't there. The uniform size allows the boxes to stack quite nicely upon each other. I think we will be using these boxes even after the remodeling has been completed.

This is just a printer, not an all in one with scanner and fax included. However, it is a pretty fast printer for printing office docs, so if you're looking for mainly a printer and not an all-in-one it is much faster and allows printing of larger photos and documents.Pros:- Fast printing, prints several pages per minute, much faster than my all in one printer from Epson.- Wireless mode, was easily set up through the included CD which came with printer. I did not need any cables, and did not even need to enter any passwords. It gives you the option for wireless, cableless sync during the set up.- Great text printing, due to a XL sized black pigmented ink plus 4 dye based inks.- All ink tanks are separate allowing you to change the one that's running out, although that is pretty standard now in printers.- Air Print enabled, once set up through one laptop it automatically worked with all laptops, iPads and iPhones - it just showed up when printing options were selected.- PictBridge enabled to work with Canon cameras.Cons- Not an all in one printer - no scanning or faxing or copying- No LCD - last 5 printers I've had (Epson, HP, Lexmark) all had LCD screens - some allowed almost everything to be done through LCD so it's strange to have to go through my laptop for everything for this printer. It's also not easy to diagnose all the problems easily - the alarm button starts flashing on the printer and then one must go to the laptop and open up the software to figure out what the issue could be- Duplex printing is available in this printer but is manual which can be a pain. You have to manually turn over the pages to print on the other side.Still TBD (will update review)- Ink usage - still to be determined as it is a new printer. It does not seem to soak up ink like my latest Epson XP-950, which was an all in one printer. However, time will tell, as it is a fairly new printer.Overall recommended for office use or for large photo printing when all you need is a speedy printer. Canon inks are usually reasonably priced, so hopefully it will be cheaper in the longer run than some other printers.

This book is about learning to write and form letters/numbers and then early math.  I have a 6 year old who writes numbers oddly and this has been very helpful in showing how to form the letters correctly so they are more legible and easier to write.The examples on how to form the numbers are excellent!  Examples:  3 is learned by showing a bumpy slide.  4 is shown as how you climb through a play set.  9 is shown by using a bee's path as an example.  These make writing fun but also gives that important visualization that children need.  There's definitely nothing boring or stodgy about these examples at all.Later counting exercises are creative and actually use examples inside the house.  Kids get a 'scavenger' hunt type of challenge that is fun and interesting - and very personalized for them.  An example would be to count the number of sinks, fill in a calendar, or draw a picnic set up and then count how many plates or cups were drawn.  It's all very creative and the examples are bright, fun, and cheerful.  It's more like a funbook than a workbook.My only complaint is that this is more ideal for homeschooling in America than for those ex pats raising kids in foreign countries.  Examples such as a telephone with a keypad to fill in is outdated in the cell phone world and cultural specific visuals such as a baseball diamond or American football will leave non-American raised children baffled.In all, I am very happy with this book and my 6 year old had a great time doing the workbook.  It's such a pleasure to see schooling presented creatively, colorfully, and with fun and challenges rather than writing on plain white paper.  I feel Mead did an excellent job with this and highly recommend it for the kindergarden set.

Several family members have been using these markers on our white board.  My grandson practices spelling and drawing with them, and my son-in-law uses them for his college math problems.  The markers are good quality and last quite a while.  The spray solution is not the best way to keep a board clean.  And I prefer an old t-shirt to the spray and to the eraser.  But I would buy the markers again, no problem.
Been using it for 1 month and I love it. Soft, flexible, and greatly reduces the pain in my wrist resulting from too many hours spent in front of my laptop. Strongly recommend.

This printer is the primary copier, primary color printer, and primary fax machine in our engineering office with six professionals. It is also our primary scanner. We have a total of six printers in service - four HPs and two Brothers. This Brother replaced an HP 7700, which died after four years of good service.This Brother gives good print quality at a reasonable speed and is loaded with features including duplex printing. Installation was easier than similar HPs. Construction quality appears as good as HP. (An earlier Brother 11 X 17 color printer, which is still in service, had flimsy trays and other paper-path components.) There have been no significant jams after three weeks of heavy use.Note the size and weight; this is a central office printer, not a work station printer. It takes two to carry it in its shipping container. It is meant to be an office workhorse and is much bigger than the cheesy ink-jet printers. Don't forget to turn the sleep timer to a longer setting if you want to make copies without a wait.The price seems very fair. After buying about fifty printers over our thirty-year history, I am very pleased with this purchase. It looks like Brother has come of age for the corporate world.

This thing is great! Very easy to make a small precise erasure. Much better than trying to use the corner of the regular eraser. And the Magnetic holder is a great way to keep it handy. It comes with several erasure pads on it and when one finally gets too dirty to use it can be peeled off and you have a new one underneath again, The flat part is large enough to use as a regular eraser or for a larghe area of bigger drawing. This helps offset the higher price because you get more use out of it.

This board came with two broken corner caps so there is no way I would be able to hang it by using screws through the caps. It also came with scotch tape residue on it which won't come off. I don't generally want to screw anything into a wall or door so this is not a feature I would use anyway. However, I do like products which come with a wire or picture hanging accessories so we can hang the product by a hook or what I refer to as a *wreath hanger.* There is no way to install one of these on the board. If you're using this board leaning up against a wall or in a window (like a restaurant), it would work fine.The actual board itself works well and the pen markings erase easily. It comes with a pen and a couple magnets but the pen holder slips off easily and is not big enough to properly hold an eraser. It should be bigger, and I assumed at first that it attached by magnetic pull, but it doesn't. There are no directions telling us how this pen holder attaches.I suggest much better packaging for this product and a few more intuitively placed accents. It's unusual that something this basic couldn't be done correctly the first time. This is not *rocket science,* as they say. (smiling)

This is the solution to easy gift wrapping...  a quick pull for a perfect strip of tape.  Unlike a traditional tape dispenser with a roll and a cutter, each strip is precut and uniform.  This provides both quicker tape pulls, and the tape is no longer cut with a serrated edge that remains raised.Note the unit is not heavy enough to counter weight the force of pulling a tape from the dispenser, the bottom of the dispenser has a suction base, which works well on smooth surfaces, but would not work on rough or uneven surfaces, requiring two hands for operation.Also.. kinda of fun to use, even more so for a curious 3-yr old that throughly enjoyed the magic of the tape dispenser.Recommended for gift wrapping,  but wouldnt replace a traditional desk dispensor for longer strips or cheaper refills.
These dividers help keep my school work neat and organized.  I felt I got a good value for the amount that comes with this package (set of six).

I use my shredder mostly at home for receipts, you know, like I get from Amazon in mailed packages. A lot of those receipts have a sticky return section, that clogs up my shredder, so I thought I would try these. I'm sure that these were designed to enhance the actual mechanism of the blades, but I fed 2 through the machine, and it did "unstick', some  of the stuck paper. And the sound of my shredder now is much smoother. I know I shouldn't use my shredder for those sticky sheets, and as usual will just replace the shredder as it gets clogged, but this seems as though it may lengthen the time between replacements, which is why I tried these.

The shredder works great. Even better when you feed a sheet of paper through with a little oil on it, every so often. Speed is fast and I can shredder up to 14sheets of paper (2 more than specs :)). However, it's a bit bulky for my limited office space.For a more compact version which takes in less sheets of 8, try belowhttp://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0050BPWBQ/ref=as_li_tl?ie=UTF8&camp;=1789&creative;=390957&creativeASIN;=B0050BPWBQ&linkCode;=as2&tag;=nealo10a-20

I really don't have presentation needs or whatnot for these pouches.  To be perfectly honest, my Fellows Cosmic 125 kind of just stands compactly out of the way most of the time, to the point where I'm thinking, "Why do I have a laminator again?" --- and then I need it, again.  A few days ago I laminated a bread machine baking chart for a quick cheat sheet so I don't have to reference the manual again and again, also a "proof of insurance" for my wallet, since the paper printout from the website had gotten tattered.Yes, 3 mil is very thin, but it is also surprisingly sturdy over time.  If the material I am laminating is flat, and if I am careful to use a carrier sheet when using one pouch for multiple small items, I see zero bubbling or other marring. (Just be sure to have enough margin around EACH item to cut up without separating the lamination layers.  Idiotically, I kept making the same mistake early on of cutting *through* the laminated papers rather than trimming before laminating.  Don't do that.You can get cheaper per-sheet, but I've seen cheaper per-sheet in my kids' classrooms in the past.  Okay but often a little less bubble-free or a little more prone to separation.Oh, and a PSA: Remember to clean your rollers!  - no brand of laminating sheets can compensate for dirty rollers in a laminator, and how hard is it to run through a cleaning sheet?

I have used a number of Task Chairs over the years and have not experienced a problem with any in terms of basic durability.They all sit on a five point base and they all have casters. One I bought ten years ago (made by Global Upholstery Co.- the “GUC chair”) is still at my desk and in good condition. But different task chairs offer different levels of comfort and high end ones cost more. The basyx HVL251 by HON is a good desk chair.It took about fifteen (15) minutes to put it all together after removing the pieces from the box. It should take even less time if I should do it all over. The seat is sufficiently broad for a large person and the back rest is similarly broad. The seat is adjustable up and down. The contemporary design of the back rest gives the chair extra appeal.While the seat is quite well cushioned for a moderately priced desk chair the back is hard plastic. Unlike the GUC chair this back does not pivot at all; it is firm. True, one can sit on the chair sideways and even backwards as stated by the manufacturer but what is the point in that when the chair swivels 360 degrees?What makes the basyx chair in my opinion better than the GUC chair is that its back rest is attached to the seat with three strong screws that will all have to come loose for the back to fall off. This back does not slide in and out and that makes it the safer design. Just remember that a chair with no arms is meant for use a few hours at a time.

Maybe it's just me but I always get a lot more out of the Canon branded product than I do the OEM products and I gave up on getting refills at the local store a long time ago.Yes, this is more expensive than the OEM product, but they last longer.
These envelopes aren't thin or cheap and the seal-it strip works without fail. They're made by Mead in Dayton, Ohio and say "Made in USA" on the box.

Started out so simple - assembled quickly without any issues. I like the color too, nice and dark, perfect to store my old bank, mortgage and other files.  I have a whole filing cabinet of closed account folders which were using up space, so I moved them to these boxes and out of the way.  Love these to organize!

I really love the bright vibrant colors that these sheets come in and the sure sticking factor I get with these Post-it labels is fantastic.I used to send away for my return address stickers,then I discovered these wonderful thingies!By going to the website listed on the pack,I get the Free templates to use in making labels that look better and importantly Stick better than my old choices.These labels look wonderful and I Love them!
Very happy with this.  Worth the expense and effort.  Regular mouse pad does not even come close to the performance of this pad.  It is rigid, and works great for gaming.  Recommended

This whiteboard comes with three magnets to attach it to the fridge or whatever other metal thing you want to attach it to. If you prefer to stick it directly to the wall, you can use the foam double stick tape to do that as well. However, because this board is so light, it will quite happily live on your fridge door with no problems at all. The magnets are quite sufficient to the task of keeping the whiteboard onto the fridge. The included marker has an attached eraser, which cleans the board off perfectly. Even when using the broader Quartet markers, I can still get a clean board with the attached eraser.

I just love Prismacolor.  They provide a rich laydown of color and vibrancy that you just do not get from any other artist's pencil.  I just missed having any options in the gray range, so I purchased the next set up and between the two sets, I am thrilled.  I use the pencils up quickly, so having two sets is not a waste at all.  Very highly recommended if you do not want to have a range of gray in your collection.  It has everything else.

These perform exactly the same as the 3M Post-It notes we all know and love.  The "gimmick" here is that one stack provides multiple sizes.  It's easy to grab one of any size -- it doesn't break up the stack to pull one from the middle.  The colors are very bright.The only downside I see with this product is the packaging.  With the standard boring sticky notes, the packaging can be as simple as a cellophane wrapper around a cube of notes.  The stair-step shape of this stack requires more packaging.  It is in a plastic cover bonded to a cardboard backing.  So even though this multi-size pack is handy, I will probably purchase a more traditional stack the next time I buy sticky notes.

This stapler works as advertized: it requires less force than my old Swingline and it can do 20 sheets in a breeze.There is a quirk however that is unlike the "standard" staplers that get the staple to go through as you press down. On this one sometimes the staple seems to kick in just as you pressed it all the way down and you're releasing the pressure. I suppose it has to do with the spring loaded mechanism. Also when trying to staple things in rapid succession you sometimes have to wait for the mechanism to reset.It is otherwise a pleasing design, easy (although different) to load and appears well made.

This product works as advertised. Stick it to your laptop and you've always got a post-it handy. One reviewer asked, why not just open a document on your laptop to type your notes. Good question. I have a sticky-note program (NoteZilla) on my computer to keep random notes. But the other day I talking to someone and they wanted my email address. I grabbed a post-it, scribbled my number, and handed it to them. It was very nice to not have to scramble around looking for something to write on.These came in a pack of three. I put one on my laptop. I stuck another one to the side of an external DVD drive next to the monitor on my desk. And I have a zippered notebook that I take to meetings, and I put the third post-it holder on the inside cover of the notebook.So these don't have to be used with laptops, or even with computers at all. Be creative. Stick one to the refigerator. Put one near the front door for when you need to leave a note on the door for UPS to leave the package on the porch.This is a brilliant concept, and I forsee having these all over the house in those places where I'm always thinking, "I need something to write this down!"

The Post-It Color Coding Labels is another quality product of Post-It Notes. Too often when I have used other store brands the quality is not the same. I used Microsoft Word and Print Shop 23 to print on the labels. Both programs were well. I used an ink jet printer to print my labels. The quality of the paper is very good and the adhesive worked exactly as the package said it would---easy to remove. The color coding is what makes these labels. I use one color for office supplies and another color for photo negatives as I have each stored in plastic boxes that one cannot see through.When printing only four labels I found I could go back and print additional labels and the paper would properly feed through my printer. In addition these are removal should you decide to pull the label off the container. Other store brands that I have used cannot be easily removed from the container once the label is pasted on.This is not always the case.This is a quality product that is well worth the price.

Used these labels to make labels for paper merchandise bags for a local craft fair.  They made my bags look really professional when I logged onto the Avery website and got a template allowing me to bring the design all the way to the edge.  Recommend that you print on a piece of white paper to check alignmenht prior to printing them on the actual label pages - some printers work differently - the settings on my home printer were much different then the printer at my friends house.

I am very impressed by the performance and versatility of this sleek little workhorse of a printer.  I picked it up for its color printing capacity and thought I might occasionally use the copier and scanner (our office has both of these readily available, but I thought every once in a while it would be convenient to have them handy at my desk).  While I have no use for a fax and haven't used that, I've discovered that many of the other capabilities of this machine will be very useful.One excellent feature I know I'll use a lot (and didn't expect) is that if you scan in documents the built in software can convert them directly to text files.  I know that will be useful, since I often need to transcribe long passages from texts I'm reading onto the computer (usually to share with students).  This way, I can just scan them in and convert the text and email it, rather than typing it in or cutting and pasting to give on a handout.This makes color and black and white copies or scans, and they look quite good.  One thing I really like is that  instead of having to change the settings every time (between color or b/w) there are two "go" buttons, one for color scans/copies/etc. and one for b/w.I love the wireless feature, love that I can print directly from my laptop and send scans directly to my desktop.  What I'm most impressed by, however, is the quality of Canon's service.  It did take me a while to figure out how to set the printer up on my network - I followed the manual, and installed the software (on a mac) and then when it didn't work I reinstalled it, checked everything on the troubleshooting guide, and still didn't get it.  So I called Canon's customer service, quickly reached a tech guy, and was amazed by how helpful he was.  He walked me through the process step by step and I finally figured out what I'd done wrong (it was my misunderstanding and not something wrong with the manual) and it was set.  I've had similar experiences with Canon in the past - that time with a camcorder accessory - where I had a problem and their customer service patiently helped me to resolve it.  I have always been impressed by the quality of Canon products, but I am consistently amazed by the helpfulness of their support and their support team.Highly recommended for anyone looking to replace a scanner, fax, copier and printer with a do-it-all device that is well built, looks good, and is supported well by a reliable company.

The Brother MFC-6890cdw All-in-One with printing, copying, scanning and faxing capabilities has been in daily use in my home office for some time now, and it has proven to be invaluable. The wireless networking has saved my family time and effort. Another feature I really appreciate is the ability to use paper sizes up to 11 x 17. Altogether a sturdy, easy-to-understand and convenient machine.

This binder has two sleeves in the front and back for loose papers, instead of the more common single sleeve. The D ring opens and closes easily with the tab, which is plastic so you don't get cuts in your fingers like the old binders sometimes gave. There are clear plastic sleeves on the outside, so you can slide in pages on the front, back and side. I think it could have been enhanced by adding a clip for more loose papers, but otherwise, this is very suitable for things like seminars, where you might acquire hand-outs and be taking notes. The only thing you need to consider is an inexpensive 3-hole punch, since few papers now come pre-punched. Overall, I find this useful - and it makes me oddly nostalgic for high school!

This mouse pad works great with my optical mouse. It isn't thick and bulky nor is it a slippery vinyl pad. It's the perfect size to sit next to my keyboard along with my bead-filled wrist cushion. It is a COMFORTABLE mouse pad covered with a soft  polyester fabric attached to a non-skid sponge rubber base. The texture provides good control for my mouse. For me, it's the perfect mouse pad, it's a nice color, and the price is right, too!

I like these clear labels.  They print up easily and look great on all envelopes.  I am currently using them for business, but they would work well for personal items as well.  Especially invitations as they would make it elegant being that they are clear.  Easy to use, print is clear and dark.

I was reading the reviews on this and expected something decent for the price.  I've written with fountain pens in the past and love them, however this Lamy Safari series was a letdown.  I found the body to be ok, but it is plastic....so nothing fancy.  You can't expect fancy for this price point though.Now let's get to my cons section of this review...and there's only one thing I can point out!  I started signing my name to see how it felt and a few times, the ink stopped flowing.  I thought I'd leave it nib side down a while and came back and hour later, but same issue.  The inconsistent ink flow in the pen I got made it unusable and so I had to return it stating it was defective.  When I get the new replacement in, I will see how that one work, I'm hoping it was just a defective pen I got...

These Wilson Jones Ultra Duty Round Ring View Binders with Extra Durable Hinges are very good quality and are certainly a step up from the budget binders we usually pick up. I have seven of these binders in varying thickness and all of them are excellent choices for holding important presentations and documentation.This is marketed as having Extra Durable Hinges and they are indeed quite sturdy compared to the lower end binders we buy in bulk. These are more expensive, so would reserve these for customer use instead of causal office use.Recommended!CFH

If you don't do much color printing, you'll do okay with this.  But the ink system in this machine is really really lousy.  It works fine otherwise.  I love the two-sided printing feature, and the wireless system works fine from anywhere in the house.  But it really is lousy when it comes to ink cartridges.  Don't try the refill ones, it'll just screw you up.  It'll even stop recognizing good ones, and make you take it out and replace it, over and over, to get it to recognize it.  I'm tired of HP - thinking of Epson or Canon now.

The Panasonic cordless phone set works great.  The phones have many nice features; I particularly like being able to store lots of names & phone numbers in all the phones.The transaction was excellent in all respects. The product arrived in perfect shape and as promised.

Decent pen, feels balanced in the hand and has a comfortable grip. I removed the small plastic ring that was at the tip of the pen and it writes perfectly now. Very fine point but thick enough to be easily seen (if that makes sense). Overall a great budget pen.

Although listed as laser printers, I found the labels worked just as well on my ink jet printer as my laser printer.I fed sheets through the printers multiple times (manufacturer advises against this) and there was no jamming or warping of the sheets.I had no issue setting up my labels in MS Word using the Avery 5160 template.I was skeptical of the "super sticky removable" adhesive.  If they were removable, would I be able to use them as address labels?  If the adhesive was that secure, would I really be able to remove them without tearing them?  Believe it or not, the answer is yes to both.  Once affixed, the labels stay firmly in place.  I tried bending the envelopes they were on at the corner to see if they would start to peel off but they didn't.  You need to lift a corner with your fingernail and then they peel off.  I was very impressed.

I use this with our Brother Laser Printer and it always works well. Easy to install and it lasts a long time. I don't keep count of the copies, but it lasts us longer than a year. I use the printer for mostly homeschooling, and my husband uses it extensively to print articles from his favorite religious websites. The copies are good.

works as intended, had it for a while now and it hasnt given me any problems *knock on wood*... havent tested out the duplex yet though... really just needed it to print papers

The Livescribe Smartpen is a pen that records your handwriting in sync with an audio track. It is a life changing invention. At meetings, for example, you can write a note while recording the speaker. Upload both the written notes and audio to your computer. You can then locate the audio by tapping on the written note. If your handwriting is very legible, you can even convert it to text. Livescribe Smartpen is an amazing device and something you should investigate.Livescribe Smartpen uses special paper encoded with millions of microdots. You can print your own if you have the right printer or buy tablets of the special paper. Until now, these tablets were available in standard (approximately) 8.5 x 11 and 6 x 9 sizes which are not the most convenient for total portability.With the introduction of these approximately 3.5 x 5 pads and the attractive leather binder, Livescribe has brought the special paper down to a truly portable format, perfect for tucking into a shirt or other pocket, purse or what have you. It's the right size and the binder gives just enough support to make writing comfortable.The Smartpen is controlled largely by touching control panels that are printed on each page and on a special page included with the binder.Now, the Livescribe Smartpen, for all its good qualities, does have at least one drawback: it is on the bulky side. The case that comes with it does not have a clip and putting both the Smartpen and the Flip Notepad into a shirt pocket is impossible. A somewhat expensive accessory case with a belt clip becomes a necessity.With the Flip Notepad, the Livescribe Smartpen becomes a complete written and audio note taking system with very high portability. It is really a marvelous device that you'll quickly come to treasure and wonder how you got along without it. The Flip Notepad comes with the binder and four notepads.Jerry
