After the moving, I have to throw the boxes away since the boxes cannot be reused.  Even with the heavy taping, I have always had the problem of things falling out because of the weak bottom.  These Fellowes moving boxes are great.  It is very easy to assemble and very sturdy.  And after the moving, it can be easily folded back so that I can keep it.  This box is the best package box I have ever used.  However, I give it 4 stars because of the higher price.  Other than that, this is just a great box that I can recommend to any one.

This would be my 3rd electric pencil sharpener. My first died on me. Battery burn out I guess. I still have the second. This one works better than either of the previous two. It's faster and quieter. It sharpens a new pencil in seconds.It still does that thing that electric pencil sharpeners do when they stop occasionally. The only improvement I can recommend would be a larger cup for the shavings. It's easy to remove and less messy than the other two I used, but it also holds less.This is a very good sharpener. I would recommend it.

Mead Organizher Magnetic Shopping ListOverall, it is a pretty good product. Sticks to the fridge without issue. Handy and nicely organized.A few minor things (none of which would prevent me from buying it)-Way too many pre-printed items on the sheet. I can figure it out for myself- Dumb name organizher (what is this 1954?)- It would be great if you a place for a pen was available.

This printer makes amazing prints even on just plain white paper.  I haven't had a chance to use all of its cool features, so I'll update my review when I do.On my Mac, I had to figure out on my own how to set it up, however.  There is no display panel on the printer itself, so all configuration has to be done remotely.  I connected the printer via USB and had to download the "Canon IJ Network Tool", which allowed me to connect to the printer and configure it with my WiFi.  Unfortunately, it doesn't support the 5GHz 802.11n band, so I had to use my "backup" 802.11g network instead.  Not a big deal, but it's disappointing for a new printer not to support all current 802.11 networking standards.I do not recommend this printer as a general purpose home or office printer.  It really is designed for printing high-quality output on a regular basis.  I keep this printer turned on, but if you don't use it for a while, it will still take about a minute to "warm up" (I really don't know what it's doing) before it will start printing anything.

This is one of the best items I have gotten from the Vine program unfortunately a series of financial challenges has left me without an air compressor right now.  I had an air compressor that was giving me a hard time.  When I took it out to test out this item, it gave me a hard time and eventually I put it to rest (R.I.P. P.O.S. Air compressor!).  Regardless I do like this staple gun so far.  I need to submit this review for Vine purposes otherwise I would have waited until I could get a little more time in using this item.  What I like about this staple gun is the small handy features and how easy it operates.  The staple tray easily slides out by pulling a handy level and is easy to fill.  It accommodates a variety of staple sizes.  It has a nice compact and lightweight design.  Overall I think this is a nice quality project.  I may have even given it five stars had I had a little more time to use the product.  I may make an addendum to this review after I get a new air compressor.
Good thick paper on these envelopes. Makes it so that my letters stay nice and snug inside, without others being able to see in. And the price is a fraction of what Staples or Office Max charges.

I love these ink cartridges. They are so much more affordable than the Canon ones and they work just as well. I was leery about buying them at first because they are not name brand, but I have not had any problems with them.

I'd rate it a 5 but the picture seems to give a more vibrant green than it really is. I'd say in this it sort of looks lime but in reality it is more of a dull-ish avocado color. This may not matter to some (most?) people but I personally was hoping it was more vibrant/lime like the picture. Other than the color it's a great board.

Pockets like this is really a good idea! They're really great for journals and for holding all of those pesky receipts that, without a better place to put them, we shove into whatever little nook or cranny is available at the time - and then forget where we put them when tax time rolls around. I would like it if they were also available as packages of one size... I could really use a lot of the smaller ones for my various written and art journals. Leave it Post-It to come up with another great idea!

*Addendum to review below- The glow-in-the-dark label has been on my stainless steel travel mug for months. It has weathered dishwasher washings galore and still functions like new. Absolutely amazing!*This little label maker is amazing for several reasons. The options available for printing run the gamut from cables to large items that need to be identified quickly from across the room. Tapes are made of vinyl, not paper. Cartridges types are available in a wide variety of colors, widths, and their length is substantial.Need varying widths of tape? This tool has it down! Several are available to meet your labeling needs and all have excellent adhesive, durable material, and a wide variety of font sizes to meet printing needs. Our biggest surprise was the glow-in-the-dark tape (equivalent to a small night light in strength). Need three lines of print? No problem!When compared to similar P-Touch label printers, the Epson LabelWorks LW-400 is a substantial improvement and cost effective. Tapes cost about the same but the Epson's quality is substantially higher when combined with this portable printing tool that allows for extremely specific labeling. If the display setting has the back-lighting turned off, battery life substantially improves too. After 3 months, our printer has the original set of batteries still installed.For our home use, it is essential for labeling A/V cables, car wiring harnesses, travel mugs (dishwasher washed), and much used tool drawers. Seriously, it is amazing and doesn't take a thick instruction book to operate. At work, file folders, cubbies, and frequently used totes return to the classroom because these labels hold up to heavy wear.This purchase is, and remains, a wise one.

I've been using this printer for a little over a month and I wanted to test it before giving it a review.I have to say that this tiny thing is a power horse!  I am throughly impressed with it!Prior to this, I was using a large printer meant for offices for my small business but I found it lacking in quality and the amount of ink it went through was positively insane.  It seemed I was constantly getting new ink and they were not remotely cheap.This printer has already surpassed my old printers ink use mark and it's still quite happy.  The quality of the prints is fantastic for both paper and photos.  The only small gripe that I have is that it does not hold a lot of paper at once meaning frequent filling but I'm willing to deal with this small sacrifice to have a small printer that does such a great job.I also have found that the wireless networking has worked flawlessly.

When I'm not at my desk with a large desktop computer, I have a second small desk on which I keep a small laptop. This little mouse pad/wrist rest is the best thing I have ever tried for the space I have. The mouse pad is the typical sponge material, and the wrist pad is so very comfortable I can use it for hours. The combination is exceptionally thought out, and eliminates the separate and often in the floor* wrist rest.I cannot speak highly enough about this product. Perhaps if you are doing art or playing games, it may not have enough room, but for my use, mostly word processing, it is completely adequate and highly comfortable. Definite buy-again product for me.* p.s. it ends up in the floor because my hand lays upon it until sweat sticks it to my arm, and when I raise it, it falls. Sorry for the graphic explanation, but it is a bother.

This is a nice product from Fellowes. The flat cardboard is easy to fold up in to a storage box. The storage box is of nice size and looks nice (with its fake wood finish print). It holds file folders properly and we have stacked up to ~4 of these w/o any problem. I wouldn't recommend that since am not sure how long the one in the bottom would hold up when stacked.The boxes have a nice big area for labels on the sides. Excellent product over all.

The Swingline 747 is an all metal stapler in a black matte finish. The stapler is heavy-duty without being overly heavy to hold. There is a release lever that allows you to make the stapler vertical for stapling things to a wall or board and the stapler then closes quietly. The staples load well with a sturdy spring pulling up as you lift and the copper colored plate at the end of the spring makes it a bit easier to keep track of staples as you do the loading, if your eyesight isn't what it used to be.The box calls for using S.F. 4 staples for optimum performance. We loaded standard staples first and they worked fine for our needs. It easily stapled through multiple sheets and didn't jam after repeated uses.  This is a good stapler for a desk that sees a lot of stapling work or as a teacher's stapler for her or his desk.

Scotch tape is critical to life, a true utility only one step below duct tape.  Though I don't care for this particular type (the "frosted" one-I like the truly transparent smooth one!), this is excellent for when you need to write on it with a ball-point pen.  The dispenser is cool, and kind of reminds me of a dinosaur.  In all, an excellent product from 3M.
These are perfect for school crafts.  The kids love them and I love the fact that glue doesn't get everywhere.  I also love that they are reasonably priced.

These tabs are super easy to use. They slide right over the top edge of your folder and are fairly large, so the label is easily readable. I like them better than the ones that came with my folders originally. With those I had to tuck the edges of the tabs into slits on the folder. It wasn't rocket science, mind you, but these are still faster.

The hook up was easy.  The printer works great.  The paper tray took me forever to find (it is almost invisible under the feeder tray).  I felt really dumb looking for it.  I am unclear on the paper unjamming (it seems to just open up at the bottom and there is the paper hanging out - no trap door in the back like i'm used to).  But, it rarely jams.  The wifi works really well (I've had bad luck with HP wireless, so this was a charm).  I bought a second one for my son to take to college.  Price is right.  I highly recommend this.

Although it arrived too late to be of use in what I suspect is it's primary function (Gift-wrapping), The Scotch PopUp Tape Handband Dispenser is an interesting gadget....I collect comic-books, so the pre-cut strips of tape are the perfect size for taping the plastic storage bags shut. As for gift-wrapping, I'd suspect that, at 75 pieces of tape per refill, you'd go through the whole pack after a handful of presents. (At least, you would if you wrapped presents like a guy....LOTS OF TAPE!!) Aside from the convenience of having the dispenser on the back of your hand for easy access, I'd have to think it'd just be more practical, as well as cheaper, to just use a roll of Scotch Tape.It's interesting, for what it is, but I doubt I'd buy more refills for it, once I ran dry.

Five Star 6 Pocket Expanding File is around 13 inch by 9 3/8ths (my approximate measurement), plastic construction and made in China per the text above the bar code on the sticker on the front.This has six compartments and it includes one piece of white paper that has six perforated (tear out) small paper labels to slide in at the top of each compartment. Or you can use your own paper (cut it to the right size so if fits in) if you want to color-code things or replace them due to wear and tear.As you can see in the picture, there is a giant Fivestar sticker on the front, but you can easily remove it and it leaves no sticky residue behind.The pocket locks and unlocks with a rubber band with a metal tip that wraps/unwraps around a button. It is easy to lock/unlock with one hand.What is not easy with one hand is adding and removing documents. If you are planning to add/remove documents from this on a regular (eg daily) basis, you may find it too frustrating and annoying. On the other hand if you plan to use it for longer term reference (tax documents, car maintenance records, health records, etc), then it's not as big of an issue and given its modest footprint, it is a good candidate for this task.The easiest way to add/remove documents I found is to unlock the rubber band, grab the flappy part with my index finger, fold it, then use my thumb to push the part further up (the one with accordion lines on the inside) towards the back. This way it doesn't block the opening of the folder. Better yet, push that part under the table, while having the file folder on your lap. You can then easily add, remove or flip through the documents, undisturbed by the flappy part.I like the flexibility of the lock/unlock, but the ergonomics of adding/removing documents ruin what could have been a great product.

I've been using a Fellowes ten sheet shredder purchased at a warehouse store for a few years. It cost around $90, is very loud, stalls out when attempting to handle credit cards (something its manual claims is one of its functions) and balks when I try to shred more than five pieces of paper at a time. The difference between the Fellows ten sheet and the much quieter Amazon Basics twelve sheet shredder is significant.After a few days of extensive use, the Basics unit has not jammed once, although it slows down when more than ten sheets are inserted at one time - but it still does the job. To avoid any slow down during shredding, about seven sheets maximum should be inserted at one time.The credit card and CD shredders each have their own separate slot from the paper area and both handle the items as if they were butter. The function operates smoothly and efficiently. In comparison, my Fellowes shredder is larger, louder, handles less paper at one time and struggles to shred credit cards and CDS. The Amazon unit is infinitely better and seems quite solid.The instructions recommend using shredder oil once a month, although a plain vegetable oil may also be used. It may be tempting to skip this step, but this is something I've been doing for years with my shredders and I believe has prolonged the life of the equipment.And, I learned something new - the user manual stated that window envelopes, newspaper and padded envelopes should not be shredded. I expect many years of use from this shredder and will update my review if I encounter any problems.

This packaging is great if you're using one or two drops.  Any more than that, it's problematic.  I needed to glue some felt pads to some violet pots to keep them from scratching the furniture.  Simple enough, right?  It wasn't.I needed to apply the glue on portions of the rims on the bottom of the pots, then apply the felt pads.  In other words, I had to describe arcs of glue on the pots.  The bottle is simple enough to open, but it dispenses too slowly, and it's made of fairly rigid plastic.  You can't really squeeze it and keep it aimed where you want it.  You have to let it drip or take your chances with brute force.  I did choose brute force and successfully completed my project, but I was less than impressed with the packaging.  I finished with a "phew!"Super Glue is a very handy product, and I highly recommend it, but this packaging does not suit all needs.  There are other fast-adhesives available with more useful packaging.

3M's new line of antimicrobial office comfort supplies are helpful to have around, but don't be misled - the "antimicrobial" feature is not meant to retard the common cold and other germs, as I'd initially thought was the case when I saw "antimicrobial" listed as a feature of this line of products. The coating on 3M's antimicrobial products actually retards the growth and effects of microbes that would cause the products themselves to deteriorate (faster? Slower? At the same rate? Not sure).This particular 3M Antimicrobial mouse pad with gel rest is also supposed to preserve your mouse's battery power. Since I've got a wireless (battery-powered) Logitech mouse that I use on this pad, I was hoping to notice a difference in battery life, but honestly, I think that my mouse is efficient enough that I just have yet to be able to detect a difference while using this particular mouse pad. I won't, however, complain if the feature really and truly DOES work!I read other reviewers' comments about the base of this mouse pad curling, and followed the many suggestions to leave the plastic film adhered to the bottom of the mouse pad to avoid curling corners, but honestly, the corners of my mouse pad came out of the packaging slightly curled, so I'm not quite sure what the proper fix for that issue is.Overall, this IS a good mouse pad. The wrist rest is comfortable, but it's not as thick and deep as the one is that I'd salvaged from an old combination mouse pad/sheet easel that had a gel wrist rest built in. I'm glad I've got this mouse pad and wrist rest combination piece, but I keep debating busting out my old, comfy, thick wrist rest, especially since little things like curling corners bug me, visually.Good product, just not great. If you catch it on sale, it's worth picking up.
much better price than the cannon name brand stuff.  May not be perfect, but I cannot tell a differnece.  You decide!  This will get you where you need to be and look good at the same time.
Great price for a quality ink. I love my pixma for printing color as well as black and white photos.

This works better than my old one, it only did 2 sheets of 20 lb. text paper paper at a time. If you tried 3 it jammed. This has done 4 sheets of 24 lb. text paper at the same time and went right through, no hesitation. I just wish the trash containers that came with shredders was at least 3 times the size it is because, believe it or not, shredded paper takes up more room unless you constantly take the shredder top off and smash it all down every time you use it. Still, nice to have all your personal, private papers shredded before they go to the burn barrel. When it's a little windy some papers can get away but at least this way they are shredded and your private information stays private. We can burn here in our small community of 85 people when ever we want and I do use a large deep burn barrel but sometimes just a light wind can blow in like a circle and pick pieces up before they are burned completely. I do like the black color as well, looks new and sleek for my office.

I bought this after my old Canon Pixma IP1500 finally died. I have to say for such an inexpensive printer, that was a really good one & lasted a long time. I almost went with a Canon again, but all the reviews I read kept talking about how expensive they were to keep them in ink, so I did some research online & found out that an older model of this Brother Printer was rated at the top for 5 yrs. in a row. I would have never bought a Brother printer otherwise. So, I decided to go for the newer model & am really glad I did! It was really easy to set up wirelessly & I've had no problems with it at all. I print shipping labels everyday for my small business & use an online printer for my photos or prints, so this is mostly a business printer. I haven't set it up for the FAX yet because I really don't need that. So far, I don't have any complaints. I haven't run out of ink yet and it seems to print flawlessly. I would definitely recommend it. It's a good buy! And the price was very reasonable for the quality.

I bought a Uniden Cordless Phone/Answering Machine over ten years ago and never had one single problem with it.  It was a great phone.  So when the battery finally died on the old phone, I naturally decided to go with another Uniden.  Boy, was that a HUGE mistake.First, this phone is half the weight of the older model.  It's made of cheap plastic.  I hooked it up, charged the handset and it worked okay for about 6 weeks except for a few problems with an echo on the sound.  I fiddled with the volume and it got somewhat better, so I kept the phone.  I wish I'd sent it back right then.  Now when it rings I push the 'talk' button to answer it and sometimes it picks up and sometimes it doesn't.  The button seems to be faulty.  When it does pick up and I'm talking, if my cheek even lightly touches the pause button, the caller goes kaput and I can't hear them.  When I try to rectify the problem, the phone hangs up.  It is very frustrating.  At other times, I'll be talking and it just goes dead for no reason.  Also, the redial button on the bottom of the phone does not work at all.  It just stopped working.If you're looking for a good, inexpensive phone....DO NOT BUY THIS ONE!!!  It is not the high quality Uniden Phone of the past.  This one will be going into my garbage and I'll be buying a different brand from a local box store.  I'm ashamed of Amazon for selling such a low quality, piece of crap product.

I’m sorry to report that I’m not real impressed with this expensive designer pen. I guess I’m just too cheep to spend good money on a pen. It looks good and works fine, but so does a $1 gel pen made of plastic. For the moment, I’ll assume the reader is looking for a designer pen.If you work in a profession where you need a nice pen to look professional, then this might fit the bill for you. I like how it feels in the hand and the cartridge is easily replaced. The retractable clip idea is kinda cool, but it holds the ink cartridge upside down which can lead to writing failures (although I had none). However, I admit it looks a lot cooler to have the touch-screen tip hidden and to do so means putting the clip on the writing end, and that makes a retractable clip make more sense. By the way, the touch-screen tip works just fine.If you need a nice, professional, dual-use pen and don’t mind spending the extra money, you probably aren’t reading this review anyway since $40 is chump change to those making the big bucks. But if you are, I recommend you try out this pen. It’s cool and looks good.If you’re not rich, just buy cheap pens (you’ll lose ’em anyway!) and spend the rest on a nice Kershaw Leek pocketknife. Your friends will be more impressed with that slick knife than they would with a cute aluminum pen anyway, right?

This has been the best thing ever for someone taking medication and needing a handy place  to keep a pen, small tablet of paper and also, for us, a pill cutter, which was constantly getting lost on a shelf.The magnets are great!  Once this was put on the fridge, it has not moved at all.I've even put a pill bottle in one pocket to remind me to call for a refill that day.For us, it is serving one purpose; has saved us time; is so convenient and appears to be very durable.

I am of the mind set where I do not mind paying the extra $$$ for manufactures toner. I have found in the past aftermarket toner and ink, although more money up front, in my opinion, extend the life of the device they are installed.That said…I have 12 year old Brother HL-5040 that I’d like to replace and have used Verbatim toners the past year in that machine and that also seem to work flawlessly.

These performed exactly as described: no curling on the edges and no haze on the sheets.  The price is great for 100 sheets, and I'm so glad that the price of laminators has decreased to make home use reasonable.Some sheets of other products feel too thin, but these, with both sides, make a nice solid laminated final product.

This is really beefy tape, and way more than you need for taping up most packages.  It's transparent (although not as transparent as conventional packing tape) and has fiberglass threads embedded in a crosshatch fashion.  You won't be able to tear this with your hands, but I found that inexpensive kitchen shears did a perfectly fine job of cutting it.  The tape also doesn't appear to stretch at all.  The sticky factor is very good.  All in all, if you want to make sure that your package won't come undone, even if it's going to the moon, this is your tape.  I probably would save it for repair applications around the house.  Tape it with this and it will stay taped.

This is a great shredder.  I've had it for about 6 months and it's been awesome.  I've probably shredded about 130 gallons of documents with it.  I've sometimes put in too many documents and jammed it, but it's easy to unjam.However, the plastic bin that holds up the motor is cheap and it is showing signs of warping due to the heavy weight of the top.  I am not sure how long the shredder is going to hold up without some kind of reinforcement on the right side.One of my concerns with buying this shredder was the need for special bags, but I've found it works fine without buying the overpriced bags.  I have a large garbage can in my office and I can dump the shredder bin into it without making much of a mess.The motor is very quiet, the cross-cut pieces are small enough that I feel comfortable shredding very valuable information and discarding it in the trash.  For the price, I feel it's a good buy--but it loses a star for being too cheap with the plastic bin.

I was a little taken aback when I opened the box and saw the size of this storage binder. It's BIG.  It takes up a lot of room in a backpack, and if you usually carry a bunch of books and other materials, you might have a hard time fitting this in.Size aside, this is a pretty nice product. It has a cloth covering, zippers, and lots of pockets and loops to store all of your items, including pens or pencils.I asked my teens (15 and 19) if they would use something like this, and they both laughed and said no.  So this might be something geared more towards a younger student. Something to consider before you purchase.

Scotch High Performance Masking Tape 232 Tan, 36 mm x 55 m, worked so well for many of the typical ways artists use masking tape. From using to hold down paper to drawing boards, masking off edges, masking of straight edges in paintings, to sticking art or reference material to the wall, this tape did it all and did it all peeling off easily with no sticky residue left behind. It stayed in place and didn't get funky when using a hair dryer to dry watercolor and acrylic paintings or a heat gun for various FX spot jobs. You can buy cheaper masking tape but cheaper doesn't perform to the standards this one does. If it make a difference in the final outcome of my artwork it's definitely worth the cost. Not to mention, when you think about how much all the other art supplies cost this tape is a bargain!

The Wilson-Jones ColorLife Expanding File is just the right size to keep my important papers safe and handy.  I am using it to keep documents pertaining to my new car.  It looks nice on my shelf, and later I can use it for other things I want to keep handy.  The file is flexible and sturdy enough for the purpose I have assigned it.  I would definitely purchase more.
This is a great mouse pad. The size makes it very easy to use as you can more or less put it in any position relative to your computer and the surface makes it easy to move the mouse.

Like most people, I have waayyyyy to many electronic devices and find it challenging to store and charge it in an organized way.  I bought this for that purpose.  The mesh material allows for great ventilation while charging or storing.  Looks clean and organized.  The product is very well constructed and solid. You don't feel like it is cheap and flimsy.  Will last a long time and looks great on our desk.
I always buy 3m product. But after reading few reviews, I wanted to try this product. It is good product but if you are use to 3m product, stick with 3m.

I had read a so-so review for this printer online so my expectations were low when it arrived. But when I printed the color demo sheet after setting the printer up, my doubts vanished. It prints color very well and the text is sharp and clear.I also use an Epson all-in-one ink-jet printer in my home office, and the Brother laser printer is definitely a better printer. However, it isn't always tremendously better; unless you were holding print samples from both printers in each hand to compare them, you might not notice the difference when printing text-heavy or grayscale pages.I'm a graphic designer and illustrator, so having that extra bit of quality is important to me. If you're just printing black-and-white text all the time, however, a less-expensive multifunction ink jet with a scanner included might be the way to go.The cartridges for this Brother printer are pricey, but that comes with laser printers from all manufacturers. All in all, I'm happy with this printer.

This is a great price on a case of paper and with free Prime shipping it's even better. The paper quality is better than I expected, smoother than regular "cheap" paper. It did take a couple days to ship, but that was indicated when I purchased it, and shipping was free with Prime. The price definitely beats what we can get locally at an office supplies store.

So lets be clear here, epson has perfected the art of making a cheap good looking printer that will fall apart at the first sign of trouble. This is my third epson printer in 3 years.My first two printers, an Epson WP-4530, and this printers predecessor, the XP-600, both died exactly the same way. After about a year of very minor duty (perhaps no more than 500 pages each), each printer jammed, stripped its gears and died. In both cases I had expensive ink tanks that i wasn't able to use. I called epson to see about fixing my expensive, supposedly business class WP-4530, their suggestion? Have it fixed by a third party at $135/hr, or they offered me a discount code to buy a new printer. The WP-4530 is theoretically rated for a duty cycle of 20,000 pages each.Hope springs eternal though right? I scaled back my print ambitions and got an XP-600 and once again, after a year and no more than 500 pages it jammed, stripped its gears, and was dead. Coincidence? Me thinks not. I know the days of the tank HP 4m printer that runs off 200,000 pages before needing major maintenance are gone but still, GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER EPSON. These printers are AWFUL.Listen here, you're not saving any money buying a cheap printer BECAUSE YOU'RE GOING TO BE REPLACING IT EVERY YEAR. I can't tell you how many Epson ink cartridges I've thrown out because the printer they were for broke.Do yourself a favor, spend a more and buy a better (probably non-Epson) printer. If you do decide to buy this printer, be aware it will work well for a year and then you're cooked.
These Sharpie Fine Point markers are great for writing on DVD's or CD's.  Overall they are great for labeling those small areas as these have an ultra fine point.

This scale is a great buy if you intend to use it for weighing packages weighing over 10 lbs. Anything less and it will be off by a few onces. Not a big deal if precise measure is not critical to your needs. However, If you ship small parcels and packages regularly then you may consider a more accurateUSPS PS-100 10 lb. Desk Top Postal Scale.

If you can get this machine for about 50 dollars, it's worth it for light faxing.  The memory holds about 12 pages worth of documents so if you're a legal eagle who routinely sends 40 page faxes, buy something more heavy duty.  But if you send and receive an occasional fax here or there, this is a nice machine with a very simple and compact design.Print quality and speed are adequate and the machine does a decent job as a light duty copier as well.  The one downside on printing is that the cartridges are expensive, about 30 dollars each and they print about 250 pages.  There are no clone cartridges available that I can find.  But you can find HP original cartridges on Ebay for about 15 dollars if you want to go that route.

This review is based on my usage in scanning photographs for a large client restoration project; not documents. However, I suspect in scanning documents this scanner will perform flawlessly as it did with a massive amount of photographs. Epson has long been the leader in photograph scanning. Back in 2001, I remember paying over $500 for an Epson photo scanner and that was a deal back then. Today, Epson scanners deliver even better quality at affordable prices; quality sufficient for professional photographers.Basic Scanner Specs:-Optical Resolution: 4800 dpi with EPSON MatrixCCD-Hardware Resolution: 4800 x 9600 dpi with Micro Step Drive-Maximum Resolution: 12,800 dpi with software interpolation-Color Bit Depth: 48-bit internal / external-Grayscale Bit Depth: 16-bit internal / external-Maximum Scan Area: 8.5" x 11.7"-Built in transparency lid for negatives (difference compared to V37-Film holder for 35mm and slidesThe Epson V370 is the same scanner as the Epson Perfection V37, just without the negative or transparency capability, providing for a different lid. If you are scanning negatives, the V370 is a far better option and will provide not just greater convenience, but better image scans off those negatives.My comparison basis for this review was my friend's much higher spec (and more expensive) Epson V600 and the comparably priced Canon CanoScan LIDE 110. In reality, it is an unfair comparison to the Epson V600 based on the targeted resolution (same bit depth) difference in that if you need that size (for very large printing for example), you will need to select the V600 to maintain optimum quality throughout the workflow process (think major Photoshop editing). Nevertheless, excluding resolution difference, the V370 performs just as well for my purpose, delivering indistinguishable results for end use and client delivery(digital workflow and professional printing using Mpix and Millers Lab). Meanwhile, the CanoScan, which is less expensive than the Epson V370, delivered visibly (to me) lower quality photographic image reproduction than the V370 (and V37) for my purposes, using the same exact image. Bear in mind the scanned images were being brought in to Photoshop CS6 for image editing. Overall, I found the Epson to be far more accurate in contrast and color replication (I use hardware color calibrated IPS monitors). I also found the Canon interface far more clunky than the Epson and had actually uninstalled it.As with any photographic scanning, especially in restoration efforts, the quality, preservation, and finish of the photograph is critical to final end results. Typically, without using Digital ICE (correction) software, matte photographs may present a problem, often yielding what appears to be dust spots due to the texture of the matte. Unlike the Epson V600, neither the V370 or V37 come with Digital ICE and thus does not automatically correct for the issue. However, in my usage, I found the V370 (like the V37) did a very good job in dealing with the matte; still, in many instances, minor Photoshop retouch was necessary. Glossy finished images reproduced fine, with no issues.Installation of the scanner hardware and software was in a Windows 7 64 bit environment on a Dell Inspiron Computer. As an advanced user, I typically do not install OEM software that accompanies hardware devices. However, I found the Epson interface (Epson Scan) adequate. I did not install any of the provided document capture or Arcsoft software though and I typically recommend you do the same as it is often bloated, invasive, and generally inefficient.Summation:The Epson V370 (and V37) offer high quality scans. If you require an end product that is very large in print or digital size, then it might be worthwhile to upgrade to a scanner along the lines of the Epson V600 for the higher resolution. But absent a specific need, the V370 and V37 will perform incredibly well even for professional level photographic quality work.

There comes a time when one must face reality and deal with the fact that the TI-84 Plus is today's standards and once you hit pre-Calculus, using any other brand, and some may be just as good, is an inconvenience and will cause the student to spend unnecessary time 'translating' TI-84 Plus activities to... Casio or whatever. Just bought two of these for my kids, once upgrading from an aging TI-82, the other from a not so bad but 'different' Casio.There are several reasons you'll want the TI-84 Plus if you are taking or approaching calculus in high school or college:◦  everybody speaks TI-84 Plus - in our case it's true for the kids HS teachers and the Saxon Calculus courseware◦  it is a significant improvement over the previous TI series models being more... graphical- for example there are now little boxes where you can enter then lower and upper limits by navigating there◦  it's generally compatible with the previous TI- models - whatever you learned to do on a TI-82 or a TI-83 you generally do it in the same way on the TI-84 Plus.◦  it's now available at significant discounts as either 'used' or refurbished - saved a lot ordering as good as new refurbished unitsWe are happy with the TI-84 Plus. I am because we don't need to spend a lot of time translating the TI-84-illustrated examples we find in our Calculus courseware and focus on the math instead. The kids are happy because the interface is a lot more intuitive than the TI-82.

I don't have a lot of small things to secure, but fortunately I have a 7 year old son, so was able to really put these to the test.We secured small objects on a variety of surfaces, items made of many different materials.Sometimes it's a real bear getting the fuzzy sided circle off of the backing it ships on. This printer is absolutely amazing for the price.  It is kind of disgusting, I think, that you are almost financially better off throwing this printer away when you run out of ink and buying a whole new printer.  The ink's cost (since there are 5 cartridges) will cost almost as much as this printer does on sale.  What kind of sense does that make??? Ugh.Anyway, I think the printer itself is a wonderful deal for the consumer, and perfect for someone who just wants to print low volume items, but, the ink is a wonderful deal FOR THE PRODUCER OF THE INK.My last printer, a multifunction HP, purchased four years ago cost almost 10 times as much as this printer -and yes, it is a lot higher quality, quicker, and wireless, but if my printer broke today I would probably buy something a lot cheaper with the same functions as this printer.PROS:COST OF THE PRINTER-this is the cheapest-non-piece-of-junk-multifunction-printer that I've ever seen.  The cost might get a little cheaper, but there is so much technology in this I can't imagine it could drop more than another twenty bucks or so.FEATURES OF THE PRINTER -This will fax, print, scan, and make color copies.  Note: Regarding scanning, it took me a while to figure out how to do it (because I usually don't read the instructions unless I have to) but you can only SCAN by clicking on the printer software icon ON YOUR COMPUTER, not the printer.  (The software comes with the printer and must be installed).  With this printer you MUST have a computer to scan: you cannot just scan an image directly to a memory card without a computer.  I used to do this all the time for my higher end printer so it was a little confusing.  On the other hand, you can make copies (B&W; and COLOR) without a computer, just insert your document, push the button on the printer, and off you go.SETUP IS EASY -this is the case with many printers, but I wanted to point it out.  You get simple "getting started instructions" and I had no issues with software install or printing.  Pretty painless.But, as you might expect, because of the cost, this printer isn't perfect.CONS:VERY, VERY, VERY SLOW -if you are only printing for leisure, and have a couple of minutes to wait, then no worries.  The text printing (on highest quality) is slow -just like the dot matrix printer I had in the early nineties.  And, if you print a picture on high quality, expect to wait up to what seems like 5 minutes for the page to come out.  That is a LONG time! Forget printing pictures in a hurry.  Note: if you are going to be printing school or work papers on this thing I urge you to consider a more expensive, quicker model, because you are going to be waiting around a lot to print these off, and it is not a good printer if you have time constraints.  (On my aforementioned dot matrix printer that I once had, it took me thirty minutes to print a thirty page paper.  Nobody has that kind of time when you are rushing off to a class...)COST OF THE INK -there are five cartridges, and when you need to refill them you are going to pay 80% of the original printer cost.  The printer is like your Mach 3 Turbo razor, and the ink cartridges are the refillable blades.  You are going to be paying many times the printer cost over time in ink costs.  Is this a fault, specifically, of this printer? No.  It is the manufacturer who wants consistent revenue over time.  You get a super cheap printer and pay the company back over time with the unnecessarily expensive inks.  My take on this is if you are buying this printer, the low cost is important to you -so you might consider buying generic or refilled ink cartridges to cut the ink cost in half.NOT WIRELESS -ok, I am not putting down the printer here, it is so cheap that I wouldn't expect to have wireless, but if you do want multiple people in the house printing to this printer from laptops or other computers in other rooms, DON'T buy this printer.  If, however, you just need a printer for one computer in one room, or just want it because it can scan or make copies, then this is the one for you.If you only need to use this printer for leisure (and not work or school) then the cost of the printer and the functions of this printer can't be beat.  But if speed and wireless capability are important to you, I urge you to consider a more advanced/expensive model from either Epson or HP.

This paper trimmer isn't quite what I expected. The cutting edges are a kind of cartridge rather than razors or long cutting blades (also known as guillotines). The good news: if the cutters wear out, you can replace them instead of trying to sharpen a long blade. The bad news: the cartridges seem flimsy, and the instructions for replacing them are on the packaging rather than printed on the front or back of the gadget or on a small insert that could be filed. Since the packaging is the first thing to be thrown out, that doesn't make sense, especially since the cartridges are supposed to be long-lasting. By the time I get around to replacing one, I will have forgotten how to do it. There's a 15-year warranty, also on the packaging. Why isn't this a separate piece of paper to be kept with all my other warranties and manuals? The flip-out ruler is okay, but I would have preferred a graph board of at least 8 1/2 x 11" to coincide with letter-sized paper. The graph board is much narrower, about 3 or 4". This means that larger paper bends off the base and it's pretty difficult to keep a straight edge while trimming. Therefore, I think it's best suited for casual use: clipping coupons, neatening the edges of clipped articles from magazines. I'm not sure I trust it with photos. It seems to work best with flimsy paper, and it definitely works best with one sheet at a time. In the case of magazine articles, which sometimes run for several pages, I found the papers tended to fan out so the pages were trimmed straight, but not with the same margins on each page. For someone with a home business, or a serious hobbyist, I'd recommend investing in an industrial-strength paper cutter with a full 8 1/2 x 11" base and a guillotine handle. This trimmer is not up to heavy duty. If you want to clip coupons with it, it will work fine, but I consider it pricey for such casual use (plus the cost of replacement cartridges).

I'm a pretty forgetful person, so if I don't write things down, things tend to go undone and messages left unsent.  The problem was, I didn't always have something to write on.  I'd use receipts or scraps of paper, but sometimes my notes would wind up in the trash before they'd actually remind me.No more!  This product is called a "laptop notes dispenser," but really, it can be stuck to most any flat, smooth surface.  Each dispenser is made of thin plastic and comes with adhesive that can be removed and reapplied for when you refill the Post-its.  I stuck it on my laptop and removed it after a few days, just to test it out and it doesn't seem to have left any residue.The pros of this item are its slim profile, the ability to remove the dispenser and refill it, and its convenience.  C'mon, it's Post-its!The only complaint I have is the color and designs.  It's not bad, but as a guy, the hot pink and neon green are a little gaudy for my tastes.  My wife, on the other hand, loves them.  So, I have the black/gray design on my laptop.  It really is just a personal choice, but I think I'd prefer more solid colors or earth tones.All in all, a great product and something I'd recommend to anyone as forgetful as I am.  Now, all I have to do is to remember to buy the refills!

The contents of the package include four lengths of bubble wrap - two that are eight feet long and two that measure ten feet. A large black Sharpie marker is included for labeling along with a regular 55 yard roll of 1.88 inch wide, clear box sealing tape. The bundle includes eight small and six medium sized boxes. The quality is excellent - they are sturdy with a reasonable level of rigidness. These are not flimsy containers.Good for anyone packing up a relatively modest amount of items for storage or a move to a new residence, this kit would also be ideal to send to a child away at college, as a convenient way to pack-up their dorm room at the end of the school year for a trip home.Obviously, the end-user has a need to order a pre-packaged assortment of boxes and supplies rather than gather them locally. People have different circumstances to consider where a kit like this would make sense. Besides the above college student example I can think of situations where it would be very helpful to have these items delivered right to the door. A person with limited mobility, local unavailability or wanting to have supplies delivered to a separate location so they are there waiting to perhaps help someone else pack up are among the possibilities. And, the cost of shipping this almost 23 pound kit is another factor, besides convenience, to be considered when calculating the cost.

The Pilot FiXion pens are like regular ball-point pens except for the fact that they erase!  It is like a small miracle in ball-point form.Before trying them myself, I was skeptical as to how well the pens would actually erase.  Being in my 40s, I remember when PaperMate came out with erasable ball-point pens.  They definitely erased, but the ink was not very permanent and would even rub off when your hand passed over the page.Welcome to erasable pens 2.0.  These new friction-erasable pens are amazing.  The look is exactly like a regular ball-point pen, but the eraser is now a rubber knob at the top of the pen that doesn't flake off as it removes the ink.  The ink is truly removed by the friction of rubbing the knob over the ink.  If you rub with your finger, the ink will stay.  The amount of pressure you need to erase the ink is a bit more than a pencil eraser, so I wouldn't recommend using the pen on thin paper, such as tissue paper.  However, on regular writing paper, it erases fine.  And when I say fine, I mean that you can't see the ink...no ghosting.  The only thing I don't know yet is if the ink ever becomes permanent.  In other words, if I came back in six months and tried to erase the pen, I don't know if it would work.  However, over the course of writing a letter or completing an assignment, it erases just fine.I highly recommend these pens...just don't use them on any permanent documents!

This pencil looks pretty eye catching. When a classmate saw it, they usually thought it was a pen. Because this pencil seriously does look like a pen. Also, this pencil's tip (the end you write with) creaks with a noticebaly loud noice (of course, its pretty quiet), if I were to use this pencil in a loud room, I probably wouldn't be able to tell by just the sound. You can feel the tip move a couple nanometers. There's not much of a grip on this pencil. Its pretty much all plastic except for a extremely thin rubber strip near the tip. On top of that, the so called "eraser" is all but useless. Its tiny to the point where whenever somewhat vigorous amount of force is applied to erase a pencil mark, the eraser actually falls out of the pencil. There's a cap on top of the pencil, which covers the eraser during normal operation. But I'm always afraid of accidentally losing the cap. Which would be very bad since its difficult to advance the lead without the cap. Overall this pencil is worth its price, just don't buy the "diamond infused lead" refills. That's likely just a gimmick since I have had the lead break before when very little lead was extended out of the tip.

I do not foresee any more HP printers in future--this one, or an eventual Epson successor, is the one for me!

I received the Canon PIXMA PRO-100 Color Professional Inkjet Photo Printer as part of the Amazon Vine review program.  I've owned several inkjet printers from Canon, HP, and most recently theEpson WorkForce 545 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, Copier, Scanner, Fax, iOS/Tablet/Smartphone/AirPrint Compatible (C11CB88201), but never before had the pleasure of using a 'pro' quality photo printer.First impression, "This thing is HUGE!"  The box weighed 54 pounds and the printer filled most of that space. Used to smaller footprints, I had to figure out a space for it.  Luckily it's wireless and I could put it anywhere in my house.  Eventually I decided on a location and started unboxing it.In the box is all the stuff you need to get started.  Cords, ink cartridges, photo paper (a few sheets), software on CD for both PC and Mac users, a sheet of instructions and a CD tray.After you take off all the tape and remove padding per the instructions, you power it up and let it sit for about 2 minutes while things align.  Then you put in the ink cartridges (of which there are (8); unwrapping, unscrewing the ink cap, and setting them into the print head, which you will have already installed prior to plugging in the printer.IF your cartridges are not seated properly in the printer, you'll see an orange light on the front of the printer.  I saw the orange light, reseated the cartridges and still had the orange light.  I ended up checking out Canon's online support and found that it could also be an improperly locked bail on the printer head, which locks down the ink cartridges.  It was, and once secured, the orange light went away.Loading paper per the instructions sheet should be easy, but it was confusing to me.  There are actually two paper intake slots.  One at the very back of the printer, and one a bit forward of that.  The forward one is the slot you want, but it took me way too long to figure that one out!After you have things set with ink, paper and only the white (power) light and the blue (Wifi - if using that option) light, then it's time to add the software and drivers via your PC or Mac.Mine installed in approximately 15 minutes on a Windows 7 64-bit PC with plenty of 'oomph' to do the job.  Printer was recognized and a toolbar (L shaped) at the bottom of my desktop screen appeared.  A launchpad for printing, tweaking and manuals for this device.I printed two test pages and both were quickly produced onCanon Photo Paper Glossy, 8.5 x 11 Inches, 100 Sheets (0775B024), offering vibrant results from my own digital images.  No tacky residue or smearing of the ink, certainly beautiful results as expected from this professional inkjet.I also printed from photos taken on my iPad via AirPrint - a fantastic feature - which came out great too!The reason I give it 4 out of 5 stars has more to do with my frustration over the set-up and the size/weight of the printer.  I'm not a novice at setting up printers, but the directions on this one while 'simple', would benefit from photos versus diagrams and a bit more information - not requiring the user to go to the Canon site for clarification.The weight and size of this beast may be a necessary evil to get awesome results, but those with limited space will need to 'make a hole and make it wide' for this one.Overall, for printing professional quality prints, brochures, and similar, it's a great choice.  Feature-rich with fine detailed print reproduction from digital images, the Canon PIXMA Pro 100 is as promised.I recommend it!

After good experiences with the Pixma MX850 and MX860, I endured months of pain with anEpson XP-800 all-in-onethat was literally the worst printer I've ever owned -- going back to a Seikosha dot matrix printer, circa 1988. I knew it was time to come back to Canon.Out of the box, I was really surprised by how massive the MX922 is. It's a desk monster, and the entire front bezel needlessly flips down as a paper tray. I can't fathom why Canon made this design choice, but it's a real waste of space. (If you're not clear on what I mean here, instead of the tray being about 8.5" wide, it's literally the entire width of the printer -- but the printer can't use paper wider than 8.5")Canon has also opted for the "black chiclets that light up in contextual menus" type of interface like newer Epson printers. Personally, I preferred the directional pad used in the MX8XX series, and I kind of expected in this day and age, the display would be touch-sensitive. It's not difficult to use, but the design isn't nearly as thoughtful as what one would usually expect from Canon.Setting up the Macs and Windows 8 systems in my house was no problem with the included disc. The computers saw the printer, the printer saw the computers, everyone was happy. Setting up Google Print was a little stranger than I've seen on other printers, but wasn't hard.I liked that the ink cartridges seemed large, and LOVE that the bottom paper tray can hold tons of paper -- easily three or four times what the MX860 could hold. The upper paper tray is useful for photo paper, and while it "can" hold envelopes, the results there were not very good. Other printing, however, is quite good -- once the MX922 gets going.One of my favorite Canon features is almost instantaneous printing, even on models that I've connected with WAPs. Sadly, the MX922 takes a REALLY long time to wake up and print. It almost reminds me of the old Epson Stylus 740, in how it will whurr and click and slide and snap, and screw around for a full minute before actually printing. And printing even simple mixed documents, you can practically watch the ink meters drop. How is it chewing through so much ink?To a newcomer, I'm sure the MX922 is an exceedingly good printer. At just over a hundred bucks (or less, if you got in on the Gold Box deal), it's a very nice value. It's just not as good as previous models, and that's a shame.

I've been interested in a small projector for both personal and business reasons. I am a Systems Engineer at a Systems Integration company and we often perform demos of our software for customers during the sales process. Having a small portable projector is ideal for those times when I accompany a salesperson to a customer's office to perform these demos.At home, I wanted a projector to more comfortably view movies and shows streamed to my PC via HBO Go, Amazon Prime Streaming, etc. While I can view it on my laptop, having these videos play on a larger screen is much nicer.The 3M MP300 Mobile Projector is definitely compact - I could even fit it in my purse if I wanted to. Most people would be able to fit this in their briefcase, unless that briefcase is already bulging at the seams.It is also refreshingly easy to connect and set up. The projector comes with a standard HDMI cable, which I connected to the HDMI port on my laptop, then turned the projector on. Voila! The projector immediately mirrored my laptop's display and adjusted the resolution to one ideal for the projector. Disconnecting the projector from the PC automatically returns the computer's resolution to your normal setting.I was also able to change the display to use an extended desktop view rather than mirroring my desktop so that I could show something different on the projector than I displayed on the laptop's monitor. This is a great configuration for demonstrations so that you can show slides or a product on the screen while checking or taking notes on the laptop.3M makes a tabletop screen they recommend for this projector, but I opted for a screen with a tripod instead,FAVI 16:9/72-Inch Portable Tripod Projector Screen (TRI-HD-72). I wanted a screen I could place anywhere - even the patio - without need for a table. The MP300 works very well with this screen and takes advantage of the wide screen aspect. The further back you move the projector, the larger the picture on the screen is.The projector also plays sound through its internal speaker. However, the sound may not be loud enough for some meeting rooms. To accommodate this, 3M has built this projector with an audio out port so you can attach some better external speakers if you wish.The projector has a rechargeable battery, so you can use it without external power for a few hours - long enough to watch a movie or give most demos. Should you have a need for longer use, you can use the power adapter that is included in the package to keep it powered on. The same adapter is used to charge the battery.I am very pleased with the 3M MP300 projector. Interested buyers should be aware that this projector only works with HDMI ports, so you should check your device to make sure you can connect to it.

It is pretty easy to "de-click" and "re-click" something with the strips.The connection is pretty heavy, so if you "de-click" an item that is fragile, you have to be careful--these holding strips are a lot tougher than velcro.I don't want to remove the stuff I put down permanently, but I tried a strip on paint and it came off easily. The glued backing came off the strip, though, so I couldn't actually reuse the strip. If you left a strip in place, it could be reused indefinitely.Update: Two months later: The picture on the mirror is still there--even though it is in the bathroom, where is it pretty moist. Unfortunately, the USB port came off--it was too heavy and leaned to one side, so the glue couldn't hold on to it. The fastener part is still as secure as when I first put it on.

Honestly, I ordered these from Vine by mistake. I saw "laminating sheets" and just blindly clicked because I was excited to be able to order something to use in my newScotch Thermal Laminator. Unfortunately, I completely missed the "SELF SEAL" graphic on the front. I really think "self seal" should be in the listing title.Anyway.After testing these on small insignificant things like magazine pages (for cut out recipes) and Lego Minifigure checklists (which are folded and tend to get ripped a lot) before trying something I didn't want to ruin...I came to the conclusion that I'd just rather use my thermal laminator. Trying to get a good-looking application is kind of like attempting to put on an iPhone screen protector...you need to do it with no wind, no fuzzies floating around, and perfectly stable finger work and then it still isn't quite right. Of course, you don't need medical precision to laminate a recipe, but for the anal retentive person (like me) it just didn't look and feel how I wanted it to. Plus it feels somewhat flimsy.If you do a lot of laminating, I'd seriously consider a thermal one. Otherwise, if you really want something laminated, I'd just go to your local office supply store and pay the $1.29 a page.

I guess the first thing I should say is that the tip of these markers is not a brush at all, it's just a regular felt tip shaped like a brush.  The purpose of this shape, the way I see it, is that you can use the very tip of the marker to make a very fine line and the side of the marker to make a wider line and anywhere in between.  The widest line I was able to draw was about 1/4".  The colors are very vibrant, but you do not get any type of shading - the color stays pretty much the same no matter how hard or light you draw.The only thing I think might be a problem for some users is that the color will bleed through the page you are marking unless you are using card stock or something similar.  When I used card stock, the color bled through to the back of the page, but not onto the sheet below.  But, when I used regular copy paper, the color bled right through to the page below.  If you plan on using these for any type of artwork on lightweight paper, you'll need to be sure to keep a heavier sheet under what you are working on.

Post-Its and this Avery brand of them, Sticky Notes, have become understandably ubiquitous at schools, places of business and in homes. A great, inexpensive and always useful little thing to have around, the Sticky Notes/Post-Its, to date, have been 'flawed' only in that they sometimes came off the thing they were attached to too quickly. This new variety does not completely solve that problem but improves their 'stickability' considerably by adding a second, parallel adhesive strip. If you have a home office that is used for business, or if you have a family that likes to print, scan, and fax - the Epson WorkForce WF-7520 is an excellent choice. This all-in-one device is really a semi-commercial grade machine. This would also make a very good solution for the small professional office.The first impression of the WF-7520 is that it is a sizable device. You will need some significant desk or table space for this printer. The product dimensions are 22"W x 16.5"D which is roughly the size of the top of a deep two drawer filing cabinet (which is a nice place to keep it). The unit can be up to 18" high with the document feeder open.SETUPInitial setup of the WF-7520 is very easy. Follow the quick start guide, and you'll have the printer ready to go in about 30 minutes (including software installation). At the end of the installation, there is an automatic check for firmware updates, which was required for mine. This adds another 10 minutes or so.  If you have a Wi-Fi Network and wish to connect the WF-7520 to it, the setup is quick and easy. Even if you have a non-broadcast network, it is easy to enter the SSID and Passphrase using a "select the letter" method from the control panel. You also have the choice of using an Ethernet port to connect the device to your network via cable.PRINTINGThere are two paper storage trays, each of which are highly adjustable and will accommodate a variety of paper types and sizes. This allows you to have not only multiple sizes of paper, but multiple grades (even ready to use photo paper). The printer is FAST. It is respectable for any office printer, and blazing fast by home printer standards. The quality is top notch, as are most EPSON printers. There is a pull-out tray to catch and hold the ejected printouts, which includes a flip-up stop.COPYINGCopying is also very fast, and the reproduction is extraordinary. You have the choice of placing your original on the copy glass, or using the automatic document feeder (ADF). The ADF is fast, and so far for me, has had no problems or jams of any kind. Copying can be done in color or black and white.SCANNINGSimilar to copying, you can load a page or image and scan it to be saved digitally. The ADF can also be used for easy scanning or for multiple pages.  In addition to the very good EPSON Scan software, the package includes ABBYY Fine Reader 9.0, which gives you some great options and functionality for scanning. You can scan directly into Microsoft Word and Excel, as well as direct to PDF. Scan quality is excellent, up to 9600 dpi.FAXI don't use a fax too often, but it is good to have one when you need one. The EPSON software for the fax is pretty straight forward and easy to setup and use. It allows you to maintain a log of sent and received faxes, import contacts and create an address book, and send a fax to a group of numbers, etc.OVERALL & MISCMy overall impression with the WF-7520 is very good. For full family use at home, for home office use, or for light to medium duty in a professional office, this all-in-one printer/scanner/copier/fax from EPSON should serve very well. It is also a very good looking printer. Virtually solid black, with a sleek but stylish control panel (angle adjustable), it does not draw attention to itself like some units with lots of silver all over them.- The paper trays and print/copy output tray are a little bit on the flimsy side. This indicates a design more geared to home office than heavy duty use. You'll want to treat it nice, or I am sure it is possible to break some of these thin plastic parts.- Epson inks are among the best in the business, and this unit takes four cartridges: Magenta, Cyan, Yellow, and an oversized black. The price for ink will range from $90-100 for a full change-out. I have not yet used all the ink supplied with the printer, so I can't comment on longevity. I may update this review with that information at a later date.- SD and CF cards can be directly read into the printer for photo printing. An expected feature these days. USB input is also available.- Have an iPhone or iPad? You can print from it to your Epson printer using the "app for that". I printed a photo from my iPhone to the printer while standing in my garage - and it works great. (there may be an Android version, but I do not know for sure)- I haven't had  a problem using multiple paper trays - you can select your preference from the printer properties when printing.- At this price point (~$350), the EPSON WF-7520 is a good deal and a good system in my opinion.

I added a couple of pictures to this product page, including one that shows two printouts side-by-side.  One is a test pattern using Brother toner (from a cartridge that wasn't at the "toner low" stage yet) and the other was from an AmazonBasics remanufactured cartridge.  I was surprised to see the print from the remanufactured cartridge had darker blacks than the OEM cartridge.  The prints are from an MFC-8640D.The quality of the test print from this cartridge is excellent and matches the OEM cartridge in detail.  I know it's the drum that puts the ink on the page but I didn't know what to expect from the toner in this cartridge.  It's been my experience that refilled inkjet cartridges aren't equal to the quality of the OEM product - this is my first experience with non-OEM toner.  Up until now I've always purchased Brother toner and drums.The cartridge itself is a Brother cartridge (you can see the two cartridges side-by-side as well in a picture I uploaded) so it fits perfectly with the drum and in the printer.  The cartridge was in excellent shape, just a little light scuffing on the bottom.  I probably wouldn't have noticed it if I wasn't examining the cartridge so closely.A postage-paid mailing label is available for download from Amazon for recycling, though I normally take my old toner and ink jet cartridges to a local office supply store (which gives me a few dollars credit for them).I would not hesitate to recommend this remanufactured cartridge.  You can see it in the pictures I've posted - nice dark blacks and a high quality print overall.  If anything changes I'll be sure to update my review.

I was actually looking for a monitor arm for my second monitor (not my Cintiq) when I came across reviews recommending this product for use with the 21-inch Cintiq.  I decided to order it thinking that if I didn't like it with my Cintiq, I would use it with my second monitor which was my original intention.Well, it's on my Cintiq and I'm keeping it there. If you're marketing an expensive scanner like this, your customer almost surely wants it to deliver everything it's advertised to do (wireless scanning) and to do it with tools that make the usage very intuitive and handy (good software package).  This product falls way short in both of these key areas, based on my experience.I finally gave up on getting the wireless feature to work and just used the USB connector.  Since I have a fairly new iMac and an Apple Airport Express router, along with iPads, iPhones, etc., I'm accustomed to things working pretty intuitively and setting up pretty smoothly.  Epson fails to provide adequate instructions to make wireless connection work easily and the setup steps are not helpful, either.  As I wrote above, I gave up on wireless and went USB.  Then, on using it, the software for setting up scans comes with two choices and neither is any good in terms of being intuitive or simple or helpful.  You can get it work and get your scan set up and named and placed, etc., eventually, but don't expect it to be straightforward.  To me, this kind of stuff is inexcusable in 2014.On the plus side, the scanner feeds pages smoothly and scans quickly.  So, if you're happy with USB and are willing to go through the frustration of figuring out the screens on the software and you have a lot of volume to scan, this product may be fine for you.  And, I hate to rip on a product I got for free through Vine, but, to be honest, this setup process and usage software just irritated me.

And I have a 6'3" John Wayne-type husband with an unconventional sense of humor who gets REALLY offended by these incursions on his time.IF HE BEATS ME TO THE DOOR, he will actually (with a completely straight face and sincere demeanor) tell the Jehovah's Witnesses that he's an atheist, the Mormons that he's a Baptist minister, and the Pentecostals that he's studying to become a Rabbi. After reading the reviews posted on this product (A bunch of fine reviews too, I must say), there seems to be a very wide range of opinion concerning this electric pencil sharpener.  After reading both the good and bad reviews it would almost seem like we are all talking about two completely different products.  I am not sure why this is happening and can only speculate.  I suspect that it is a combination of things ranging from customer's different expectations all the way to some major quality control issues at the factory (Where ever that is) where the sharpeners are made.Be that as it may, I can only tell you my personal experiences with this particular product.  I had and have an earlier model of this sharpener here on my desk.  It has given me about eight years of very dependable services.  Of late though you can tell it is suffering from old age and is about to give up the ghost.  When these machines became available on Vine I jumped at the chance.The price here is quite reasonable for what you are getting.  These are not industrial type sharpeners.  They are for light office use and I do not recommend them for use in places such as schools.  There are reasons for this.  First, they are noisy; unbelievable noisy as a matter of fact.  Having a bunch of kids destroying perfectly good pencils for seven or eight hours could quite well drive you to distraction...to say the least.  Secondly, these sharpeners are designed to do the work for you.  By that I mean you are suppose to gently but firmly place the pencil in the sharpener and let it work for you.  Kids do not like to do this.  They will invariably cram the pencil in as hard as their little hands will allow and see how much pencil they can eat up before you tell them to stop.  That is just the way kids are...always have been, always will be.  If you put too much force on the pencil you will find that the point comes out quite lop-sided with wood going all the way to the tip.Now that being said, when I first opened this sharpener I immediately sharpened 24 pencils that I had in my desk.  This sharpener is extremely fast and delivers a very, very sharp point.  The down side here is that the exposed wood on the tip is a bit rougher than I like.  I suppose the single blade versus the double grinders found on hand sharpeners makes the difference.  This is a minor problem though and is more a personal thing than anything else.I like the fact that this sharpener is electric rather than battery.  Sharpeners eat up batteries at about the same rate they eat up pencils.I liked the rather long cord; it was much longer than my old model had which had created some problems in the past.  I also like the sleek look of this thing.  I also like the fact that it is heavy enough that you do not have to bolt it down somewhere.  I liked the fact that this machine did not break ever other point as it sharpened.Now I do a lot of drawing and sharpen most of my drawing pencils by had using a knife.  This is particularly true of my colored pencils.  I am old, it was the way I was trained and I have no intention of changing.  It should be noted though that if you use this machine or any other electric pencil sharpener, that you may have a problem with some of the wax based leads in some of the colored pencils...they can cause clogging.  That is the nature of most sharpeners.The reason I am giving this one four stars rather than five is due to the noise level and the fact that every so often you find that you get a lop-sided tip...this was probably my fault, but I feel the machine should have been engineered to cover up my stupidity and ineptness.Nice sharpener for the money.  Hope it lasts as long as the last one.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks

We all know how the story goes, you break something, you think to yourself "No big deal, I have superglue!" Then you go to dig out the superglue from your junk drawer and find out, yet once again, that your glue has dried out.I always wondered why a civilization that could put a man on the moon couldn't cure the common cold or create a tube of superglue that wouldn't dry out.Not that I spend nights awake thinking about that of course. For a long time I thought it was either something about the chemicals used to make superglue, that they were so sensitive to being exposed to air that just opening the package would make it dry out. The more cynical side of me wondered if the glue drying out was a marketing ploy to make us have to buy glue everytime we needed some. Of course that would imply that superglue producers design their packages in order to cause the glue to dry out, and that is sort of getting into tin foil hat territory!.Anyway, Scotch, a maker of other fine sticky products (they make my favorite packing tape!) has created a package that helps keep the glue from drying out between uses.And while they might get snubbed at parties and conventions by the other superglue makers, at least they have made a product that makes life a little easier for us, the consumers!
