One of the newest members of the Epson printer family, the WorkForce 4530 brings a new level of power and production to the small business or high production home office user.I have owned a good many printers since I purchased a small HP inkjet to use with my first desktop over 20 years ago. The move to multifunction machines was a natural as I discovered that I had need for copying, faxing and scanning in my home office. Of the four I have owned and heavily used, this new WorkForce Pro 4530 from Epson is, by far, the most powerful, productive and user friendly multifunction machines I have used.The fact that the WP-4530 is wireless is nothing particularly remarkable these days, but it is a nice touch with a machine that can put out about 2,400 black printed pages and over 1,200 full color ones without changing the cartridges. It's duty cycle is rated at 20,000 pages. Based on my current usage, I expect to be replacing ink cartridges only once every 9 - 12 months! Its production capacities are clearly impressive but are only one of the features worth mentioning.But I must start at the beginning of my experience with this multifunction inkjet printer, fax, copy and scanning machine. From the moment I took it out of the box and removed the (many) pieces of blue tape that help it securely for transit until I tried and tested each of the functions, I have been nothing but impressed with the technology and genuine utility of this machine. If you need more than a standard inkjet printer, the cost of this Epson WP-4530 will be retrieved quickly through its overall economy and immediate productivity.The Epson WP-4530 is larger than my old multifunction machines (the footprint is approximately 18" X 18" X 10"). The larger size is primarily attributable to the paper storage capacity and larger cartridges. The paper tray holds 330 sheets of paper!SetupThe complete setup took me about 45 minutes. The Quick Setup Guide is explicit and there were no glitches for any of the functions. There is a `Priming' phase for the ink cartridges that takes about 15 minutes during which it is best to walk away from the machine rather than sitting watching waiting for the `water to boil.'Connected to a computer with the software loaded, the directions are clear. It would be difficult to make a mistake but, just in case, the process is a forgiving one with a simple `Back' option at each step to allow for necessary changes or corrections. I was especially pleased to discover that while the Guide recommends setting up the connection initially as a hard-wired one (using a USB cable), I set mine directly as a wireless connection without a problem. My Linksys wireless `N' adapter found the machine immediately and added it to my network.The specifications for the WP-4530 are impressive and can be found on the Amazon product site or at the Epson doht cahm so will not be repetitively detailed here.Here are a few comments about each of the specific functions as I have experienced them:PrinterIn addition to the high-volume capacity of the printer, there are other characteristics which recommend it. The print quality is quite precise and clear and the ink used in the cartridges is a special, proprietary formulation (DURAbright Ultra Ink) that dries on contact and is highly resistant to smudging - a common bane of those of us who use colors and sometimes put a lot of ink on a piece of paper. Automatic two-sided copying is an option and can save a great deal of paper.The printer is not silent but is less noisy than many smaller and slower machines on the market. It is quick and prints at a rate of about 16 ppm (black) and 11 ppm (color.) In addition to the major, large paper tray that loads in front, there is a back feed capacity that is useful for photos, envelopes, etc.The WP-4530 takes four high-yield Type 676XL cartridges (Black, Cyan, Magenta and Yellow) that can be replaced individually as needed. They are large and not inexpensive BUT last a very long time. The economy of printing has been rated at about half the cost of laser printing the same pages and compares quite favorably to other `economy' inkjet printers currently on the market. The black cartridge retails for about $38. and the colors for about $25. each. Discounted multi-packs are not available at this time.CopierThe copier, like the scanner or fax, can feed multiple pages from either a simple flat-bed tray or a motorized document feeder. The copies are as crisp and quickly produced as are simple printing jobs.Date can also be read from or copied to a thumb drive via a built-in USB port that is placed, conveniently, on the front of the machine rather than on the back where these things are often hidden and difficult to access.FaxThe fax can be used either through the keypad on the 4530 itself, or via a computer interface. The computer interface also includes a quick cover page easy-send option that works simply and perfectly.The fax operates at a standard 33.3 Kbps speed over any plugged-in telephone line. There are plug ports for two separate phone lines and the fax works equally smoothly for both inbound and outbound transmissions.The built-in speed-dial feature makes faxing to regularly used numbers especially easy.ScannerThe scan feature is especially smooth, easy to navigate and comes with versatile and useful software. The scans can be saved as PDF or Word documents and are easy to edit and save. When it comes to maintaining business documents, less paper is better and a scanner has become, increasingly, a necessary piece of office equipment. This one does the job quite nicely.The WP-4530 can also be configured for mobile access so you can actually utilize it from a mobile device!All-in-allTaking initial cost, ink replacement and overall productivity into account, the Epson WorkForce Pro WP-4530 is a nice addition to a home office, small business or to the moderate-heavy personal user. It is clean, quick and economical. Epson's new line of WorkForce Pro machines is well worth considering.Uniquely, the Epson 4530 has its own internet address that allows you to email documents and pictures directly to it from anywhere you happen to be on line!TheWP- 4530 is Energy Star rated and draws considerably less power when not in use than my old, smaller and slower multifunction machine did.The only caveat I can think of is that of cautioning people considering this machine to evaluate their own needs carefully. For people who do only occasional printing at home, the WP-4530 is probably overkill. Its size and capacities are best appreciated by users who really can take advantage of the many features this multifunction machine offers. There are perfectly adequate multifunction machines available for less than one-half the cost of this one. The Epson WP-4530 is available at its list price of $299.For the user who needs fast and frequent copying along with clear and reliable faxing, copying and scanning capacities, this may be just the machine for you. It sure is for me!I recommend it highly.

The Samsung SL-M2885FW/XAA Wireless Monochrome Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax was very easy to set up and ready to print in minutes.With no PC or software to install, I was able to quickly and easily add my password protected wireless network directly from the control panel and immediately send a print job from my iphone which automatically found the printer and the pdf I printed came in duplex without any trouble.The printer also supports NFC configuration with the Samsung Mobile Print App as well as Google cloud print.The printer does come with software that you can install on a PC or Mac with print drivers, configuration manager, and documentation, but I was able to use the printer from iphone or mac with no software. I did have to install software to scan from printer to desktop. They also ship a USB cable which is not needed for wireless printing.The paper storage tray is a little weird, after unpacking and removing all shipping tape and installing the toner which was a bit messy, you have to extend the tray after pressing a small green lever on the carriage. There are two, one in the middle that seems like the obvious choice, press the other one on the right... Then you extend the tray for the appropriate paper size (LTR for standard 8.5x11) when you install the carrier back in the printer, this extension sticks out the back of the printer.Copy with document feeder or single sheet for items like books was one button easy and the printer has a built in ID scan feature which allows you to scan something small on both sides before the output job is run putting both front and back of your ID on the front of the output page. All documents printed fast although the duplex process does seem to slow 2 sided down a bit over comparable single sided jobs. Basically the printer prints out the page, pauses a second while it changes the path and then pulls the paper back in from the output tray to print the opposite side. If single sided there is no pause and pages pop out very quickly.Design wise this printer is a bit weird in my opinion, it looks like two devices stacked, but it is all one piece. Output is in the gap between the black and white sections.Why do we still have telephone based fax? ARGH! I still have to send them but I certainly don't want to receive them. Would be great if there was a standard protocol so I could just assign this printer to use some cloud service to send faxes. For now we are still stuck so if you need to fax, you can with the Samsung SL-M2885FW/XAA Wireless Monochrome Printer with Scanner, Copier and Fax.

I print a lot of finish quality documents and duplex printing is crucial for me.  I've used the same old LaserJet 2200D for the past six years (bought it used, refurbished).  It was a great workhorse, but it finally died.I've been using this 1606dn for a little while now and I wish my old one had died sooner.  I can't believe how much faster this printer is.  I just printed an 85 page document full of rich formatted text and lots of complicated images and diagrams.  The print quality is laser crisp, but the speed is what amazes me.  This document would have taken about 15 minutes on my old printer.  It took just over six minutes on this one.  That's faster than most of the printers in my corporate office.The setup was simple.  I was in a hurry when I first unpacked it, so I just connected it directly via USB.  The installation was typically slow for an HP product: the installer is slow and bloated.  But once that was over, it ran fine.To connect it via the network connection, I had to re-run the bloated installer.  It recognized the printer right away though, so I can't complain.  The installer had to open a port on the firewall on my Vista PC.  I've never had to do that before.  It runs find now--no performance lag over the network.For some reason I expected the network connection to be wireless (my fault).  I disconnected my old printer and used that wired Ethernet connection.  Disconnecting the cable from my old Jetdirect box reminded me that I paid more for that network box than I just paid for this printer.BUILD QUALITY: I love this printer, but I really don't trust the plastic construction.  The plastic is pretty flimsy and I won't be surprised when something breaks.  I wish that weren't so, because my older printers fail in the engine, not in the plastic body.  I guess that's how things are going nowadays though.  I think it's fine for a home office, but I wouldn't put one of these in a busy office with lots of bodies, because someone will break it for sure.

I am an amateur and passionate photographer.  When I needed a print of any of my photos, I went to the local drug store and quickly made them.  After a few years of encouragement from friends and family to start hanging my work on the walls, I've decided to finally get a photo printer. What a pleasant surprise.  My review is based on someone who has never owned a printer designed exclusively for photo printing.This printer is heavy and large.  It measures 15.2 x 27.2 x 8.5 inches and weighs 43.9 pounds.  I had to rearrange my cluttered desk top to have everything fit on the table in a workable manner.  The size of this thing is clearly meant for the professional photographer who takes photo printing seriously.Following directions is paramount. All ink cartridges have a specific position.  The printer requires some calibrations with the computer.  This took of most of my time as the actual set-up was easy.  The directions are straight-forward.  I also had to print a few trial photos before I got what I wanted.The machine works quietly but it does work slowly.  This does not bother me as this is a photo printer, not a document printer.  The time it takes for an 8"x10" print is still significantly faster than taking a work order to a photo lab.I don't print a lot of my own work; I keep my photos mostly online.  Replacement cartridges currently sell for around USD 15 each; that comes to USD150 to replace all the cartridges and this printer requires several cartridges for blacks.  Photo paper isn't cheap, either, but for an enthusiastic amateur or a budget-minded professional, I would suggest this printer.

Folders are an important part of organization and Smead Classification Folders make organization easier with their multiple dividers and sections.  With two dividers, each folder has a total of three sections for storage and six sections to attach paper. Fasteners exist at the top of each section, on each side, and they work by punching the pointed metal tip through sheets of paper and then folding the metal fasteners back. They can come in very handy for those who desire a means to separate notes into sections.Another quality I like with these Smead folders is the reinforced spine. Some folders gradually break apart in this area, but these folders have reinforcement to extend their useful life. The reinforcement isn't anything extreme. It isn't made of metal or anything like that, but it is still more than what you will find with most folders and it is just enough to keep the folders from breaking down. I also like the fact that the reinforced spine has an accordion- style base. This is nice because it means the folders will expand a little bit to accommodate more paper. Additional expansion would be nice, but these folders still earn points for offering this feature.Labeling is an important part of organization and these folders do offer a tab for attaching a label or writing in something as a label, both on the main folder and on each insert.  These tabs could be improved, however, if they were a little taller. They offer a good deal of width, but they are very limited in height so there is little space on which to write a comment or attach a label. I have found that an added extender tab is necessary in order to have enough space to create a label.I like to stay organized and these Smead folders are good at their intended purpose. Whether you are a student, teacher, businessperson, or just someone who has things to organize and needs multiple separation sections, these Smead folders can make your life much more orderly.

If you forget to turn it off it will do that automatically after 5 to 6 minutes.I want to add that this unit is not flimsy at all and feels very solid and not like some cheap piece of junk.  Sit it on your desktop and it will stay where you put it, until you decide to move it elsewhere.A calculator of this type used to cost upwards of 100 dollars back in the day and wasn't built half as well and sucked batteries dry quickly.  The Amazon basics version is a step up in all regards and has a nice affordable price without sacrificing quality.My 81 year old Dad needed a new calculator to use in his home office and this fit the bill perfectly.  He reports he has had no trouble at all using the nice large keys or seeing the numbers in the display.  I am also a senior and the two of us have both decided to give this calculator the "Two Thumbs Up Senior Approval" rating!  It's a good solid value PLUS it's Codger tested, Geezer approved!

I've been using printers of many kinds for more years than I care to remember. Suffice to say, I once owned a Daisy Wheel printer :). In recent years I have mostly purchased Epsons for my ink jet needs (higher end photo printing and printing on CDs) because I'm comfortable with their software interface, I like the individual replaceable ink tanks and the products have generally worked well for me. The water resistance of Epson's current DuraBright inks is also a big plus to me.When the Amazon Vine program offered my a WorkForce 30 to review I jumped on it. The main selling point of this printer is the idea that it can be just as fast as a small laser printer. I was quite skeptical of this claim, so I set about testing it in my own environment. I'm using a 2-3 year old Dual Processor XP based system, which is pretty middle of the road for modern systems. Pretty good hardware, but certainly not the latest and greatest.My everyday workhorse printer is an aging HP LaserJet 3150 combination printer, fax & monochrome scanner. For my test I pulled up two typical documents in Microsoft Word 2003. Document one was a three page primarily text instructional document with a number of photographic illustrations mixed in. On this test document my 3150 laser printer took 46 seconds start to finish to print one copy while the WorkForce 30 took almost twice as long at about 80 seconds.For the second test I opened a four page all text document in Arial 12 point font. The laser printer took 54 seconds to crank this one out while is a similar time per page as for the mixed text/graphics document. However, on this text only document the WorkForce 30 trounced the laser printer by clocking only 30 seconds to output the same four pages. Text quality from the WorkForce 30 was very good, but close examination still gives the quality edge to the old laser printer. Unless you are comparing the two side by side you would probably never know the difference.Water resistance of both the laser and the WorkForce 30 output was excellent. I put sheets from both under running water in our bathroom sink. The paper got soggy and fell apart before the ink could degrade. Horrible water resistance has been the bane of most ink jet output for a very, very long time; I'm glad to see that Epson has licked the water problem.If very fast text printer at a low price is important to you, then this printer might be the ticket. Water resistant output is a huge benefit as well. Besides the fast text output, it does everything one would expect an ink jet printer in this class to do. Changing just one ink cartridge at a time saves money. I'll never have another printer which uses "color" print cartridges with tiny amounts of each color all bound up into one unit. My last HP ink jet went to an early grave because it was absurdly expensive to run.I would think that college students dashing out the door at the last minute to hand in a paper will appreciate the speed and low running costs of this unit, and the ability the ability to deal with liquids!Hint: If you have this printer, buy the "high capacity" # 68 refills, not the low capacity # 69 refills.By the way, this makes an absolutely killer check printer for use with QuickBooks. Spits the things out so fast it is almost scary. Watch the money fly out the door ...

Built like a tank.  I have a cheap Scotch laminator that I use for the kids' crafts and school projects.  Including my wife's craft works for her day care at home. I know, it's tape.  Scotch tape to be precise.  But that is what sets this tape apart from the competition.  Over the years, I've had consistently better results with all forms of Scotch adhesive products.  The difference is so noticeable that I buy Scotch tape products exclusively, regardless of price.  And speaking of price, this is a very good price for a three pack of Scotch tape!Scotch tape:* sticks better* cuts better* tends to bend more naturally* doesn't seem to yellow/discolor as muchThis "gift tape" has a matte finish that hides finger prints and largely disappears on your gifts. I primarily use a laser printer for all my at-home printing. I see no need to have color unless I'm doing photos, and when it comes to printing documents, a laser printer's toner is going to last a lot longer than an inkjet's black cartridge. Laser is also faster. For the past six years, I haven't even used a color printer on my PC setup.The biggest reason for this is because of ink, particularly the speed with which it's used up, and the cost of it. I have especially nasty things to say about Lexmark (cheap printers, outrageously expensive ink) and HP (mid-cost printers, expensive ink that doesn't last long). I've owned printers from all the other major companies over the past 25 years, and this is my first Kodak.What can I say? I'm impressed.First of all, the WiFi connection is awesome. I can put the printer anywhere in the house, and it works without needing to string USB (or, if you're old school, parallel cables) all over the place. Set-up with my network was easy and fast. I'm totally happy with the speed of printing via WiFi, and I'm pleased with the ease-of-use.The print quality is good. Granted, I haven't had a color printer myself in six years, but my wife uses a three-year-old HP All-in-One, and I have to say that the Kodak stomps in in terms of color quality on plain paper. The Kodak is also quite a bit faster, and seems to use a LOT less ink on a single print-out.The print quality goes to top-notch level when you use the Kodak Ultra glossy paper (they include three sample sheets). Photo prints made on this printer are gorgeous, and the ink is dry when the printer spits out the paper. This printer is a really good reason to stop going to the department store to have photos printed out.I like the little status screen on the printer. It makes it a breeze to access menus, print from the SD card slot, and set up the printer. Frankly, I don't know how I got by with older inkjets that required a series of arcane button-presses to get what I wanted out of them.The scanning/copying are both excellent and fast. Color copying is true to the original (and of course, better if you use glossy paper), and black/greyscale are both quite impressive, rivaling my laser printer in terms of quality.Looking around the Internet, I found the ink and glossy paper for VERY reasonable prices. I think Kodak has the right idea here! Instead of selling the printer for dirt-cheap and gouging customers on the ink and paper, Kodak is selling the printer for a reasonable (but higher) price, and then selling us the supplies at a much more sane price point. Affordable upkeep on this printer seems to be the focus when it comes to their pricing scheme, and I agree with it wholeheartedly. Yes, you can pick up a Lexmark or HP for less money initially, but you *will* pay for it in the long run!The only thing missing on this printer is fax capabilities, but it's not like I send many faxes anyway. I can live without it, but if you're in business and need a fax machine as part of your all-in-one, you'd be better to move to Kodak's other models.As far as looks and style, the printer is slick-looking. It's relatively compact, and only needs one cord (AC power) coming out the back of it. The screen flips down, and everything seems kind of classy. I like that when you open the printer to change ink, there's a little prop (not unlike what you'd find under a car's hood) that keeps the printer open while you're doing your thing. I also like that the print head is separate and removable/replaceable. If the print quality ever goes downhill, you have an option to troubleshoot it.I have ONE complaint, and it's a small one: I'm kind of sick of every piece of computer electronics having a bright blue LED on it. In the Kodak printer's case, the large blue LED is the WiFi connection indicator, and it sometimes stays on-- glowing quite brightly-- even after you've finished printing. As I keep my printer in my bedroom, it's one more light distracting me at night. I find myself needing to cover the LEDs with electrical tape with this and other devices. I think a smaller, more subtle light would have been just fine.Bottom line: This printer is awesome. I'm a convert, and while I still like the laser for quick document printing, I now see a lot of use for color and I think I'll get a lot more out of my digital camera now that I can print quality photos at home quickly, easily, and inexpensively.If you're looking for a good inkjet printer/scanner/copier, go for the Kodak.UPDATE 02/11:  So I learned the hard way that even if you have a brand new, unused black cartridge in this printer, it WILL NOT PRINT Black/White documents if the color cartridge is empty or missing. It doesn't matter that you're not printing in color; It flat-out refuses to work at all if BOTH cartridges aren't present and have at least a little ink in them.I think this is a cruddy way to do business. If I am only printing in black, I shouldn't need to run out and get a color cartridge to make the printer function at all. I'm sitting here with a stack of documents to print out, and no way to do it with just a new black ink cartridge. Without replacing color, too, I'm unable to get anything done at all.Kodak: You can release a firmware update that eliminates this boorish behavior by the printer. There's no reason to force us to have color ink just to print a text document. FIX THIS.As a result of this bad business decision on Kodak's part, I have knocked one star off this review. It could have been the perfect printer if not for this shortcoming.Bottom line: If you want to print on the Kodak ESP 5250, you NEED both ink cartridges whether or not you're using color.

I love sticky notes, but wasn't sure about the practicality of see-through ones. I have been pleasantly surprised by how much I like these! The Ampad Versa notebook is a definite crossover between notebook, binder, and organizer all in one!  Needless to say...it was love at first sight.  This is a small notebook, only 5  x 8  inches, but it really does pack a big punch.  The paper itself is made up of a very sturdy stock, perforated for convenience, which I love, and is wide ruled.  Another note to love is that it does have an area for the date up at the top right corner of each page. The inside, as soon as you open up the nice plastic cover (perfect for those of us who use our notebooks as coasters), is littered with any office supply aficionados best dreams.  Sticky notes.  There are various sizes, and bright neon colors of sticky mark it notes, some square, while others have a nice neat point to it to really highlight a key area of any document.  These mark it notes are all on a very sturdy see through plastic piece, and behind those...more sticky notes!!  There are two pads of them that are, again, on a hard piece of see through plastic that happens to be wonderfully lined.  No more sideway notes! Past that, there is a document holder the size of the notebook that has this nifty corner fold over to keep any info stuffed into it perfectly.  The very back of the notebook houses three different colored plastic "tabs," which can be moved to any point in the notebook.  Very good for separating notes!  And lastly the back cover is another page holder!  This one I found so unique, and it actually took me a second to realize it opens!  There is no ugly metal spiral binder clasp, but instead this notebook has round plastic "wheels" that everything is attached to.  But what is utterly divine is that everything, and I mean everything, including paper, the covers, the sticky notes, can simply be taken off the wheels, and repositioned elsewhere in the notebook.  So say you accidentally wrote a note that needed to be somewhere else, or you want to move one of the sticky pads to the back of the notebook.  Just take it out by pulling the end over the wheel, and put it where you want by pushing the paper back into the grooves of the wheel.  Easy and so freaking convenient!  The Ampad Versa notebook is a must have for all note takers, who want the ease of having a binder, notebook, and organizer all in one place!

These are sturdier and the plastic is much thicker than most presentation protectors and it is very professional looking. I am currently using them as portfolios for my web design and photography work. I just added plastic album pages to it.  The window in the front really makes it stand out!

Love it! This is a great laminator. Kit comes with laminator, instructions, registration card, and 10 3ml laminating pouches. Laminator is fairly intuitive. Plug it in and it stays in cold mode with lighted indicator. Cold lamination is available for cold pouches. If you want to use the heated pouches select the thickness (3ml, 4ml, 5ml) and your selection will brink until ready. Then slide your pouch in and wait. Smooth laminations when complete. If you have any issues while the lamination is in progress just use the release lever in the back.My only complaint is with the instruction manual. On one page is your standard diagram with lettered controls, but you have to turn the page to find out what the matching controls and letters mean; it should be on the same page or below the diagram. As it is I had to flip the page back and forth to figure it out. And the quick start guide diagram doesn't make sense when you look at it - except if you already know how these laminators work.Definitely recommend this laminator, works great and I'm happy with it!

So useful and easy to use.  These stickies are right next to your computer.  They don't leave a sticky spot when you pull them off and come with re-fills of both the pads and outer container that sticks to your computer.  A great idea.
These are great colors to add life to all your projects. My 10 year old daughter loves Sharpies and these are no exception.

I am a college student and found that I tend to do much better in my classes if I at least make an attempt to read the book.I bought these because of the price, but was very happy with them. I bought another set, and they too, ended up in the trash.These have yet to die on me.I have a variety of colors because I tend to color code my textbooks.  For me, it makes studying much easier.
This is a good quality carton sealing tape. It's a little pricey for everyday use, but if you want to create tamper-proof seals, it's the one you need.

These will work in any 'pouch' laminator.  I used them in my 3M laminator and they worked every bit as well as the original 3M pouches.  I would suggest you buy whichever is cheapest.I use mine to laminate knitting patterns that I carry around.  It keeps them from getting torn, creased, or dirty. This is a great product for doing custom labels. We used it when we were organizing our basement. We marked each box with the contents using this tape. These are wonderful.  They go thru clean and the edges tear well.  As long as you use them according to the directions, these look almost like you had them done professionally.  They can be used on laser, but are specifically designed for ink jet, which accepts ink differently.

As someone who has tried many different types of these organizers, I can say this is my new favorite. First and foremost, it is sturdily constructed and thus, highly durable. Aside from its great looks (The patterned navy poly material is good looking and not cheap looking as many are. You can take it to a meeting and not have it look messy or ugly.), it's practical: The material is waterproof and resists smudging, fingerprints and spills. No, you can't lug it by itself in the rain, because it has slight openings at the top, sides. But for me, who is constantly placing this on table tops when eating and working or at meetings, it's terrific.As for organizing materials, I really like the stepped and alternating blue/clear dividers. (Small complaint: As others have noted this shipped without the Monthly Tabs and a second white index piece.)Can it hold 600 sheets of paper? I dunno. At say 50 sheets per divider, it's questionable and if it did, don't know how it would affect overall durability. But myself and most folks I know don't carry around that much paper in these files.One last small quibble: I prefer the long, wrap as tight or loose as you want thread-style closure on organizers, rather than the looped one on this. The organizer doesn't stay as "tight" as I'd like when I am carrying fewer papers. The button part of the closure seems sturdy and isn't likely to fall off as many others have (even when the organizer itself is strong).Overall, high marks for looks and function.
I use these in my Dymo LabelWriter 400 Turbo and they do the trick nicely. Easy to load and they print out crisp and clear text.

I hold my pens in an odd way which causes my hands to cramp and callouses to form. l also have some arthritis so writing for any period of time can really hurt. My hands are small so you might think the barrel of this pen would be too large. lt isn't and the squishy but not too squishy covering feels great in my hand. (Even my grandma who had very bad arthritis loved these pens and she wrote everything by hand.)l have been using these pens for decades and I have only had a couple finally break after years of use. They seem rather expensive but they last a long time. Just don't let them wander off,Aside from the thick padded barrel, the most important feature of this pen is the gel ink. The gel ink refills are NOT interchangeable with the standard ballpoint refills. And the gel is so very smooth when writing! The tip of the pen makes it usable on papers that require "ball point". The gel does not write well on things like photos. The ink smears. If you want to write on something other than paper, test it first. You may need to keep a ballpoint pen around. If you do, choose a Dr. Grip ball point.

These things are great.These notetabs help us in marking and notating sections in books and our notes without that dreaded personal grafitti affect.  When I was in school and had my textbooks, I hated the idea of scribbling in them to make things stand out, wish I had these then.  These MAY help keep our personal books pristine.The MAY part above comes from the relatively unknown nature of how easy it is to reuse these items.  Let's say for example, you have a large text book that is quite heavy...and you have some of these within the book.  The weight of the book closed in on itself may bond these tabs to the pages for good, who knows right? (especially after years or decades)  We can only see.  It's not a bad thing entirely, but just something to note (no pun intended).As they are, they have great usability in that you can highlight, notate and/or correct your readings and documents.  Plus they have the added benefit of being page markers for that instant "zip to" reading.

If you're in the market for a new stapler, why not get one that can staple through a stack of quarters? Ok, it may not be quite that powerful, but this is definitely the holy grail of staplers. It takes standard staples for stacks of a dozen or so sheets of paper, or you can use longer "high capacity" staples to staple through up to 65 sheets of paper.  A word of warning, don't use the high capacity staples unless you need to, because they can get pretty messy if you're only stapling a few sheets.This stapler is very easy to use, and the claimed "2-finger operation" is no lie, except that a typical adult could probably easily operate it with even just 1 finger.My only complaint is that it's a bit loud, very similar to a typical staple gun. My office mates 4 doors down can tell when I'm stapling away at stacks of paper.Highly recommended - it is a very solid and good quality stapler!

This all-in-one looks kind of weird. It looks like someone just stacked a scanner on top of an existing printer, and oops, the colors didn't match. "Oh well, it still works, so let's sell it anyway."This is actually a quite nice machine. The print quality is good and it's fast. Scans are okay quality for most tasks, but I have a nicer decidated scanner for photos.Setup through wireless was a breeze. My only issue is that while my Google Nexus 4 phone sees the printer, all the print jobs from the phone come out blank. I had to install the Samsung app for mobile printing to work properly - even then, it's cumbersome and not ideal. And I can't get the NFC printing to work at all.

I'm a Canon Gal. I've always had Canon printers -- since the days way back in my Spent Youth, when Canon made printers for Apple. (We're talking dot-matrix old.)  The Pixma line has always been most excellent. The MX882 is a definite step up. I love this printer! I love anything that *auto duplexes* without me having to take the page out and re-feed it through facing the right direction. (I don't know about you, but I *never* get the direction right on the first try.) It's a true all-in-one that does everything it promises. Plus, it can, to quote my friend's teenage daughter,  "have sex with my phone and make pictures come out!" Grin.For those not technically inclined, some of its functionality may seem daunting.  Don't be intimidated! It's fairly plug and play.  The screen on the printer will guide you through networking set-up, etc. If you can't figure something out, Canon has excellent customer support.Here's what I love about the Pixma MX882:It auto-duplexes  (I'm a writer. I need this. Oh, you don't know how *much* I NEED this!)I can print from any room in my houseI can print photographs straight from my cell phoneIt's networked - I can connect from various Wi-Fi devices as well as my laptop and desktop computersIt faxes like a mad thingIt scans beautifullyThe print quality is excellentIt's *fast*Here's what I don't like:This printer MUST have good, quality laser paper. Thin paper or draft paper upsets it and it jams, burps and refuses to pull the paper down from the back feeder. Being a Canon Fan, I expect this and use high quality paper.It seems to be either it's Wi-Fi or Ethernet. I don't know why. Just is. (If I figure out otherwise, I'll place a comment below my review.) I use Wi-Fi and USB.Even though it has quirks, I give this printer 5 stars because the functionality and quality are excellent. It's great for the price -- and like all Canon printers, it's a workhorse. I'm definitely sold on this all-in-one!!!

We had a little trouble getting it set up, but we used the phone number for technical help and the young man working with my daughter, was able to get it going.  We are not using any of the wi fi access as we are too far away from our router and that was part of our trouble in setting it up, but we worked it out fine.  It works smoothly and is very quiet.  I did not hook it up to the fax as there was no need but I have used the other facets of it.

I've been using this printer for several off-site group meetings, and it had been great so far. It is small and light, thus easy to carry, it prints in reasonable speed (do not expect laser level performance, though), and the ink cost is acceptable.The setup was a pleasant experience. The on device WiFi setup was a breeze, but Windows part required a disc to pair (there is a download on Epson site was well, but Windows Update cannot discover it automatically on the network). It can be setup for Google Cloud Print though, which means you can print from Chrome on your laptop (or mobile device) without need for any drivers. After my last two printers, I changed my mind about WiFi being a useless feature, but actually being a very important one. (It can also scan remotely, or access the media card as a Windows network share over WiFi).And the device is small, but packs a lot of good features, while omitting some. While it has basic printing, scanning, and media card photo functions, it does not contain much extras. For example, there is no input tray, but only manual feed. There is no fax capability. There is no automatic document feeder for the scanner. And while the LCD screen is nice, it is actually not touch screen (the "touch controls" is misleading, basically there are usual touch buttons beside the screen).I was able to print around 200 brochures with the supplied ink. The good thing is, you can change ink cartridges one by one (mine was heavy on the blue, so I only needed to change Cyan and Magenta first). And if you run out of color, the printer asks you to continue in B&W.; Even though they sell individual cartridges, I'd recommend buying themas the color multi pack. Thus given my usage, and today's ink prices, the cost for one color page is around $0.18, and one B&W; page is around $0.06.Overall I liked the printer, and will continue to use it for off site needs. (It can also be useful for people who need a small printer at home due to space restrictions, but that's not the case for me). However if you need a dedicated printer, print a lot, and you can buy a larger one, make your initial investment at a higher class one, and you can save on ink costs in the long run.

Until receiving this machine, we use both laser and inject printers costing over $500.  They are fast and reliable and have their strengths and weaknesses.This printer, at $110 currently, is a little bit slow, but otherwise is just as good as the machines costing 5 times as much.  The print quality for photographs is superb.  It actually blows away the quality of our laser printer, for photos, and is easily as good as our high end inkjet photo printer.This printer is slow and the cartridges don't last very long, but otherwise it is very good.If you want a low cost printer that can't produce a small volume of really good photographs, and perform other basic printing adequately, then is is a good machine.  If your main focus is fast printing or higher quantities, you might want to look elsewhere.

I am not the most tech savvy individual, however I was able to set this printer up in no time just following the instructions and installing the included disc.  Paper tray is sturdy, print quality and speed is good.  Very please with this lightweight printer that takes up so little space!

I would never, ever purchase this again, or recommend it to a friend. It's light as a feather, and flimsy as can be. It even arrived chipped. Ever seen those dime store magazine racks made of plastic?  You know, the ones that crack after you place 3 or more magazines inside?Well, this ain't one of those (pardon the bad English). First impression after unwrapping is that the design is attractive and the build quality is good.Setup (including wireless) was a breeze and the connection is reliable. I'm an educator and a parent and needed an inexpensive but reliable laminating machine for small-scale projects such as laminating worksheet masters, my daughter's piano sheet  music, etc. This laminator fit the bill perfectly. I have now had this Canon MX882 wireless all-in-one printer for about 2 weeks (October 2011) and am a very happy camper.It replaced a Canon MX860 that had been used on a daily basis and always functioned flawlessly until it stopped working after 28 months of use (Error Code 5C20 - apparently a defective logic board, not worth repairing).This is not the fastest printer available, but it performs noticeably better than its predecessor - the MX860. Speed is not important for the circumstances in which I personally will be using this device (home office setting).If you are a speed demon and truly need or simply want something faster, then get a different printer. Don't complain about this all-in-one being too slow! There are other faster printers out there for you, go and buy one!Print quality always has been and continues to be top notch. Canon printer ink is good stuff as far as I am concerned. However, I do regret not being able to use any of my still remaining new MX860 print cartridges since the MX882 does require different size Canon print cartridges.Scanning works wonderfully well and the Canon software included with the Pixma MX882 itself (for PC use) provides readily available and simple solutions for most of my printing/graphics needs that arise on a daily basis.These last 2 Canon printers that I have owned (MX860 and the present MX882) originally replaced a very tall, large/bulky and extremely noisy HP multifunction device which had great difficulties connecting to my wireless network. I must have run the installation software for the HP more than 10 times to finally get something to happen. HP Technical Support also did not provide much help in solving this software installation problem.I finally got rid of this HP multifunction device after a little more than one year of ownership. Before then, I also had owned nothing but a long unbroken line of HP printers going back more than 10 years.What a difference when moving to the Canon Pixma printer line: great much smaller footprint and extremely intelligent design of the  MX882 all-in-one overall with absolutely no problems of any sort connecting to my wireless network. It connected right away the very first time, just like its predecessor the MX860.As far as I am concerned, I will never purchase another HP printer! Canon will be getting all of my future printer business unless something unexpectedly and significantly better comes along.

It has become a drain on my hardware budget.All in all, I would highly recommend the Epson WorkForce WF-3520 Wireless All-in-One for a small office environment.

I had never used a laminating before trying this one and it did a perfect job on the first try. I like devices that are easy to operate and that don't have a lot of room for error. This is one of those devices. You simply plug it in, pull out the feeder tray, select either a 3 or 5 mil thick pouch setting and push that button. While you're waiting for the "Ready" light to come on, slip the document or documents you want laminated into one of the two included laminating pouches. When the ready light comes on, you simply start the feed into the machine and then the laminator pulls it though and deposits your laminated document below. I decided to laminate the instructions for lighting and turning off the pilot for our fireplace insert. We only have to do it twice a year and this will protect the instruction sheet and make it easier to find.I ordered some extra pouchesScotch(TM) Thermal Laminating Pouches,  9 Inches x 11.4 Inches, 20 Pouches (TP3854-20)and a couple of theseScotch Thermal Laminating Pouches, 5.31 Inches x 7.28 Inches, 20 Pouches (TP5903-20)for further projects. It will be nice for laminating photographs and some small signs for around the house, like one for the dishwasher (clean or dirty) or instructions for some of our electronic devices.The machine is 15.8 x 4.0 x 3.9 inches. It will do items up to 9 inches wide. There is a 5 to 7 minute warm up time and it will shut off automatically after a period of time if it isn't being used. The machine weighs only 3.2 pounds so it's easy to carry around. There is a well underneath to wind up the cord and store it. If you do a search on laminating pouches you'll see a lot of choices of sizes and quantity. You can also trim your project after its laminated.

This is a high end ink jet printer built for use by a group of a computers.[Good]Networking: What makes this product really stand out is that all you have to do is connect this to your router, and after installing some software on every computer, all of your computers will have access to this printer instead of being forced to use that one computer in the house hooked up to the printer. It was pretty easy to setup on both Mac and PC. This printer makes a lot of sense in a home office, a dorm or a college house, and for families with more than one computer.Two sided printing: This is a nice feature that saves paper. Personally I haven't seen this in too many low end printers.Speed: Printing speed is comparable to laser jet printers.Quality: Printing color photos on this printer is great. The quality and detail are both very good.Paper Capacity: It stores double the paper that most non-commercial printers can store. This is great when people in your home or small office print frequently.Quiet: It is noticeably more quiet than other ink jet printers.Separate Color Refills: Many color inkjet printers have a single all-in-one color cartridge, so when one color runs out you end up having to buy an all new color cartridge. Fortunately with this printer, each main color has its own separate cartridge. Just replace the color that runs out. It's great for avoiding both waste and pay for more than what you need.[Bad]Large: This is a very large printer. Most people will not fully understand why it is so large, since it doesn't have any other major functionality like FAX or scanning. I don't really think most people care about double paper capacity.Price: This product is about the same price as black and white laser printers. If you're primarily printing black and white documents, I feel that laser printers are still a better long term deal due to the cost of ink jet ink and the frequency of changing the ink.[Misc](I placed some items here since I haven't used this product long enough yet to fully confirm them.)Ink jet: This is an ink jet printer so it will most likely suffer from the same issues that all ink jet printers suffer from, namely ink capacity and long term costs, as well as malfunctioning printer heads if you don't use it often enough.Ink Capacity: I'm not sure if this outlasts other ink jet printers by a great margin, though I'm pretty sure any laser jet will beat it on both ink capacity as well as on overall long term ink costs.

I don't know why I haven't seen this before. [I think we've all worked in offices where when you go to the supply cabinet all you can find are 7 of the 8 tabs, and three of those are the same color. arrgh)QUIBBLE--online template use takes some fiddlingI love this idea. I love that the dividers are grouped together, and I think having the one sheet at the back is an easier alternative to seeing my messy writing on the type of tabs you can write on, or the types of tabs you either have to type out or print out and insert or stick.

I'm always searching for a pen when I need to write a quick note down and I'm not at my desk, I actually don't use this for a white board I just have a bunch of rando pens and markers in it on my fridge - but I love it - it's smallish, so it's not obnoxiously hanging off my fridge and getting in the way. I'm pretty impressed with this device. I was a bit surprised with I opened the box to see how small it was - I thought it would be a lot bigger. Also, the build quality at first was a bit off-putting since it is mostly plastic.But in actual operation it works very well. I very much appreciate that it does not need a PC to operate (although you can tether it to your PC in USB mode for power). Very easy to use - just load it with a slide or a negative and it scans to its internal memory. You can then save the image to an SD card (which is NOT included). It's powered by either a USB port or an included AC adapter.The scan is previewed on its 2.36 inch display. The display is quite clear, and easy to use. You have the ability to do some basic image manipulation, such as flip, rotate, alter brightness, and select either a 5MP or 10MP resolution scan (default is 10MP)It has a 5.1MP CMOS scanner, and produced a 3900x2600 jpg file from a 35mm color slide. I ran a number of slides through it and found the color representation to be accurate. The image quality is quite good as well.The manual is better than I expected - very easy to follow.The only quibble is that negatives are limited to 3 per strip. If there are more, you have to cut the strip. Not a problem for me, but something to be aware of should you have a lot of negatives.This won't compete in terms of quality with a high-end scanner with a slide carriage, but the ease of use and much lower price makes it well worth considering as a quick, inexpensive way to convert old negatives to digital.[Manufacturer provided the product for review]

Even though I have an inkjet printer, I took a chance on this "laser printer" paper because I wanted something better than regular paper but less expensive than photo paper for the calendars I am making for friends and family using photos that I have taken.  This is my first venture into home publishing.  My printer is a Canon Pixma ix6520 and the calendars are being made from a template that was included on the printer's software.  Half the 8.5x11 sheet is picture, half is calendar.  All in all I am pleased with the finished product.  The weight and glossy appearance of the paper is a major reason for my satisfaction.For purposes of this review I am going to speak separately about printing text and photos with an inkjet printer.Text.  Prints very well and looks much better than on  regular paper.  The black letters are darker and where colored ink is use the letters are darker and brighter.  Sheets come out of the printer dry, no problem with smearing, etc.  No hesitation about using this paper in an inkjet printer for brochures and things that are mostly text.  I am very pleased with the appearance of the calendar portion of my project.Photos:  The paper is not photo paper and you can see the difference.  They are usable, and most likely I'm more critical as the photographer than those who receive the calendars will be, but I wish they were brighter and more colorful.  Nevertheless, they are usable and look better than on plain paper.  Whether they look better if printed with a laser printer, I am unable to say.  But I did see comments in the previous reviews indicating that also with a laser printer they were less than what you get on photo paper.  For best results under the circumstances use, when you can, photos that are bright and where the subject stands out from the background and has good colors.  Some of the photos I had planned to use had to be replaced because they looked kind of muddy and the subject didn't stand out.  Be sure to print some test sheets before starting the printing, especially if photos are included.  After trying the various paper setting choices offered by the printer I found that the glossy plus or glossy photo paper setting worked the best.  Photos are more ink intensive than text, but this paper seems to handle it well on my inkjet printer.Regarding the paper, I can confirm that you can print on either side or both sides of the paper.  I wasn't paying attention and discovered to my horror than the pages for a few months were 2011.  Worried that I would not have enough paper I tried printing on the other side of the useless sheets and they printed just like they were fresh sheets.To sum up, the text print quality on an inkjet printer is very good, much better than on  regular printer paper.  For photos, not photo paper quality but much better than on regular paper, at least on my printer.  Also, the ink you use can make a difference, just as it does on photo paper.My printer handles the weight of the paper with ease and I have had no problems with paper jams.I'm pleased with the paper and will buy more.  The quantity that you get for the price makes this paper an excellent value.  It is not a replacement for photo paper (though a lot more affordable),  but for brochures, calendars, etc. with all text or a combination of text and photos it is a good choice.

Unlike the Kindergarten workbooks you can purchase for a few dollars in every big chain store, this workbook really stretches the child's imagination and, in a fun manner, allows them to stretch into areas they're not yet familiar. For example, one of the exercises we did today was to start with a given word/picture (mop) and change one letter to create the next word/picture (map). My grandson is familiar with letters and sounds, but not yet reading, so I thought this might be too hard for him. Happily, I was wrong. By combining the pictures with the word, he was very easily able to tell what the next word was and figure out what letter to replace to get to it. Overall it's a good blend that allows the child to have fun doing what they already know, and then allows them to stretch and reach to try something new.I also appreciate the notes at the bottom of each page that gives a suggestion for a non-workbook activity you can do with your child to reinforce what has been learned in the workbook. These suggestions are both interesting and fun, and require no special articles other than those you already have around your house or in the outdoors.I told my grandson I was going to review this book for Amazon, and asked him what I should write about it. He can do "stuff" that he's never done before, and has fun doing it, and learning all the while.I highly recommend this book!

Recently, I upgraded from the XP-400 to the XP-800.  As you might imagine, the XP-800 is a superior printer that can be used for the home office.  I will highlight some of the main differences between the two printers.One of first differences you notice between the two printers is the physical size.  The increase in size is due in part to the new added features.  For instance, the XP-800 has a larger 3.5" LCD touch screen control panel.  It also has faxing capabilities, a 30-page Auto Document Feeder ("ADF"), a 100-sheet paper tray, and an output tray that automatically slides out when printing.  It is worth mentioning that the XP-800 features automatic 2-sided printing, and since the ADF is duplexing, you are able to copy, scan and fax 2-sided documents.  If you use the ADF, you should also be able to copy, scan and fax legal size documents.  While the ADF is certainly useful, keep in mind that it is a bit slow.After printing both text documents and some color photographs, it was quite apparent that both print speed and quality had improved.  I have print-outs of the same photograph from the two different printers, and the colors from the XP-800 print-out more closely match the colors on the computer screen.  Speaking of color, I should also mention that the XP-800 uses 5 different ink cartridges, whereas the XP-400 only uses 4.With regard to set up, you should bear in mind that a USB cable is not included.  However, that will not be an issue if you set it up as a wireless printer like I did.  The set up guide is easy to follow, and while it took a little longer to set up than the XP-400, I would estimate that I was up and running in about 30-40 minutes.  The set up time included taking the printer out of the box, removing packing materials, installing the ADF and ink cartridges, installing the printer driver / software, and connecting it to my wireless network.Once set up, you can still print and scan wirelessly, and you still have an option for mobile/cloud printing.  The XP-800 offers many new improvements, but the main ones have been highlighted above.  In sum, the XP-800 is in a different class from the XP-400.  Whereas the XP-400 is fine for light and general home usage, the XP-800 is suitable for use in a home office.

Overall, this is a great product for a home office where volume is low and not an issue.

Review updated 9Aug121) Elmers "Ultimate High Performance" is also a Polyurethane (PU) glue and (as far as I can tell) it's as good as Gorilla and Sticky Ass, but tends to be less expensive. I also used PL brand glue PU and can't tell any notable difference between the three. Have not used Sumo but I understand it sets up faster and as a result apparently has a much more limited shelf life (this is generally not a good thing - see item #3)2) Gorilla Glue (In my opinion) has thought out their bottle and cap design better than the competition.  Sticky Ass Glue has a similar design.  While this seems like a minor thing, it really makes a BIG difference in not being messy or wasting glue (See #4)3) PU glues work differently - they foam up and expand in the presence of moisture and then harden.  This means you will need to think about where the glue comes out and how to keep it from making a mess.  Masking tape is your friend.4) PU glues have a limited shelf life and you probably don't need as much as you think. Due to the expansion (see #3) you use a LOT less than other types of glue. 4 oz should be MORE than enough for most people, 8 oz is a BIG bottle. I personally buy the 2 oz bottle unless I have a major project.  PU Glues suck moisture out of the air so unless you plan on using it up within a year or two, a LOT is going to go to waste. Don't ask me how I know this.5) PU Glue is FANTASTIC for lots of things but woodworking glues are still better for woodworking (see #7). They are stronger and you can't clean PU glues up with water the way you can even with the waterproof Titebond products. Also if you use biscuits you will have to moisten them separately to get them to swell.6) KEEP OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN AND ANIMALS! Although the glue itself is not toxic and is food safe once cured, it can kill your pets - like antifreeze it apparently tastes good to animals and will swell and harden inside the digestive tract creating a blockage. There is NO antidote and surgery is typically the only solution. There have been MANY cases - just search Google "Dog Gorilla Glue." Wear gloves (rubber or vinyl) and use lots of wax paper and paper towels.7) Wood glues (Like Titebond II) are still better for wood to wood bonding.  Fine Woodworking did a test (Issue #192) and found Polyurethane glues to be about half as strong in this application.  Search "HowStrongisYourGlue_FWW" for the article.  One exception is if you're gluing oily exotics where I personally still prefer Epoxy - you can dial in your set time, clean up is about the same given the PU glue outflow.If you have questions or comments, or if you have found this review helpful, please let me know!

Okay seriously "I hate strapping tape." As a rule I find it annoying. I have shipped thousands of packages. I started my own wholesale candle business (twice over a decade) and I had to wrap and ship a LOT of homemade herbal candles all over the country. I have used every kind of shipping tape there is. This may be the best. I have always found strapping tape to be a PitA and a complete waste of time. The strings make it card to snap off of the dispenser and often make the ends bunch up.Disclaimer: I used scissors. I cut each strip I used. I didn't use a standard tape gun dispenser. Had I used a tape gun I probably would hate this tape.The stickiness is on the good side of moderate. It is relatively strong, but whenever you add string to tape (e.g. "strapping tape") the string limits the amount of adhesion. All that said, the overall is that this is a decent adhesive tape but not one that will win any awards for adhesion. As far as using to ship boxes this stuff is great. The strips of string are around 1-2 mm apart. You can't teat this open, you have to cut it or tear the tape off completely. If you wrap a box or envelope with this it will become 99% snoop-proof. I have taped up boxes, envelopes, and styrofoam--even applied this to walls, and so far I have no complaints.I have to recommend this tape ABOVE any other plastic shipping tape. You will use less of it and it will secure your box and/or envelopes stronger. I think that is the best value: You use less and it is easily ten times as strong. It will never replace your standard low-cost multi-use tapes, like masking or Scotch tape, but for the big jobs I am sold on this.You won't be disappointed.

Like most folks, I often feel that for every inch-high stack of papers I successfully file or shred, two inches more are lurking, ready to jump into my in-box at work or mailbox at home.Lately, I've been trying to streamline in both places and have been experimenting with several ways of categorizing these flows of documents. I'd anticipated being able to use permanent markers on them but the paper is just a little too porous for a good result.So far, what's worked best for me is to print as many labels as possible the first time through, because once you remove a label, its neighbors don't cling to the carrier sheet as well. These neighboring unused labels do stay put well enough for me to use when making handwritten labels.As for the repositioning? That feature has worked quite well on a variety of surfaces. Epson Workforce 840 garnered CNET's Editors Choice Award in a multi-function shootout amongst several others including the WP-4540. However considering the 4540 is half again the price of the 840 that would be a strong contributor to earning the number one spot. However both machines are built from the same format from the same manufacturer so it surely isn't because the 4540 is by any means a lesser machine. So do you need the extra features the 4540 incorporates, or are they not so important to you? So let's do a comparative analysis, and bring up the differences.The 4540 is quite a bit larger at 18.1 in x 25.9 in at x 18.2 in at 36.4 lbs compared to 17.6 in x 22.3 in x 12 in at 22 lbs for the 840. I am not a printer engineering expert but I feel reasonably sure that the feature of being able to do both automatic duplexing in copying, scanning, and scanning as compared to copying only in the 840 requires the additional hardware and heft to accomplish it. Automatic duplexing with scanning for example allows the automatic scanning of a sheet of paper on both sides. Devices without this capability can only scan a single side of a sheet of paper at a time.The 4540 has Epson On-demand Inkjet - 4-ink technology and the 840 has Epson Micro Piezo - 4-ink. Max Printing Speed on the 4540 is up to 16 ipm (mono) / up to 11 ipm (color) and on the 840 it is up to 15 ipm (mono) / up to 9.3 ipm (color). Surprisingly the Max Printing Resolution on the 4540 is actually a little lower on the 4540 at up to 4800 x 1200 dpi (mono) and up to 4800 x 1200 dpi (color) with the 840 at up to 5760 x 1440 dpi (mono) / up to 5760 x 1440 dpi (color). Both of them can handle Envelopes, Plain paper, and Photo paper, but in addition the 4540 can also handle iron on transfers.The standard media capacity is 580 sheets for the 4540 and 500 for the 840. The office machine features for the 4540 are scan to e-mail, and save to USB flash drive, and on the 840 they are scan to e-mail, print from USB flash drive and save to memory card.Since the 4540 took the Better Buys for Business Editors 2011 award that places both of them as mutual holders of the best of the best in multi-function printers. You can't go wrong with either one of them. Highly recommended.

This is now our second Epson printer, along with the 630, and it's as pleasantly easy to set up and use as the first one was.The wireless set up took just a handful of minutes--I literally took more time  to remove all the little tapes from the printer than to set up the wireless connection--and soon I was printing from both my desktop, laptop, and Touch (via AirPrint) with ease.  And I've never had an issue with it dropping from the network or not being recognized. It'll also let you set up via wired/internet if you want.It prints text quite quickly, has two good-sized paper trays, an auto-feeder (nice!) and the double-sided is convenient and easy to set up and, what I like, keep as a default. Just don't expect it to perch in a tiny spot on the corner of your desk. It still fits nicely and unobtrusively in a built-in bin below our bookshelves behind a sliding door that we just slide open when we need to use it. Highly recommended

I am a strong believer in owning a label maker. Life is so much easier and efficient if items are labeled. I adored my Dymo, so I was interested to see how they compared side by side.First, the Epson came with six different ribbon sets. This may not be the "typical package" - it may have been a Vine special - but I did enjoy all the options and I'm sure these ribbon sets can be bought separately no matter how someone gets their initial label maker. They are simply my storage item tracking system. So depending on how you are using the labeler, you may care or not care about that.I found it a bit heavy. Part of the appeal of the Dymo is that it is light and easy to carry around as I move around on my cleaning and organizing tasks. Not that this Epson unit is *extremely* heavy of course, it's not a giant gold brick. Still, it's noticeable to me.I've been using this for a while to do my testing and giving a lot of thought of which one, going forward, I will use. For whatever reason, I still feel as if I'll go back to using the Dymo even though this is the fresh, clean, new labeler in the house. It really comes down to something about the buttons and the weight. For me the Dymo is just more totable and quick-use ready. I don't use all the symbols and fonts. I don't need lots of special features. I just need to label and go.Still, this is clearly a solid, functional unit, with lots of cool bells and whistles. So for someone who wants to have "fun" with their labeling, I can see this being a good choice.

I admit to fussing with the placement of sticky notes on an original, in an attempt not to cover the very point I am trying to make.  So I was pleased to find the Avery See-Through Sticky Note, thinking it was going to solve my placement issues.  I do love the see-through aspect of these sticky notes - I can stick one right over the paragraph or chart and it is clear enough that I can underline the words I want to emphasize without putting a mark on the original.  I can write a note, or draw an arrow and still see the original's information.  The reader will have to lift the note to easily read the material under it, but the transparency does make it easier to spot exactly what I am pointing out.  I had no problem reading my own note over the top of the original's print.Writing on the sticky notes with ballpoint pen or permanent sharpie works perfectly, with clear, easy-to-read writing that can't be smudged by a dry or damp finger.  My hard-lead pencil marks too lightly and is almost impossible to read.  A highlighter just balls up on the note, but then I never highlight my sticky notes.  However, the gel pen (the type we use to write our checks because it never washes off) takes a VERY long time to dry, and during the drying time it is easily smudged beyond readability with a dry finger.  Even more annoying, it smudges completely off the sticky notes with a damp finger long after the ink has dried.  Since I mostly use a gel pen, these notes won't work for me, but I think they'd be great for anyone who prefers ballpoint pens.  I hope Avery can refine this product to hold gel ink, because I really appreciate the see-through feature.  So, 5 stars for ballpoint users, but 1 star for those of us who prefer hard lead pencils or gel pens.

The Epson XP-600 "Small-in-One" really is that, a remarkably compact home printer/scanner/copier.Setting up the printer is remarkably simple and took about 20 minutes from unpacking to installing on my home wireless network where I could print to it from any of my computers.With the built in card slots (USB and SD card) you can print directly from these devices if you so desire without having to first download the images to your computer. As with most printers nowadays you can also crop, rotate etc. your images directly on the printer using the touch controls which surround the small 2.5 inch LCD display. You can also print directly from your phone and/or tablet (tested with an iPad) if you so desire.The XP-600 uses 5 seperate ink cartridges so that if you need to, you can just buy the specific cartridge you require rather than a whole pack.Print speed is about average for a small home printer (takes roughly 1 minute to print a full page photograph) and the same goes for print quality (you can adjust the print dpi if you wish to but the default setting is fine for most uses. Higher dpi will really just waste more ink without being noticably sharper). Slower than a printer designed for small office use (like its big brother the XP-800) but definately fine for home use.Scanning/copying is easily done through the touch controls, again allowing you to crop etc. before you print and again speed wise its about on par with other home printers.  Scanned images can be put directly on a thumb drive or transmitted to your computer for storing.Although the XP-600 has lots of features, you will find most if not all of these on virtually any all-in-one you buy nowadays. There is nothing that really makes this printer/scanner stand out from the crowd but at the same time it is a very good little printer for home use and one that should last you a while.  For the price, its hard to go wrong with it.

The printing and scanning quality of the printer is excellent. Setup is a bit tedious; the documentation is a bit TOO simplistic and requires one to rely almost entirely on instructions on the small screen. Features are mostly easy to use, but documentation on some features like security and various HP software applications (whether in print or on the printer's help screens) is nonexistent. Also, the setup process requires the machine to be plugged into an active phone line to set up the fax feature, even if the user doesn't intend to ever use this particular feature.Of course, setup is a one-time process, and, despite the lack of clear instructions, relatively easy, if time-consuming. Most of the software included on the driver CD is unnecessary to the operation of the printer.This is not a small printer, and requires more space than expected, but the trade-off in quality seems worth it so far.One aspect I do not like at all: The printer sends "anonymous" usage information to HP, ostensibly to improve their products. Supposedly, this does not include any identifiable or personal information, but it does include details such as what time a print job was initiated and what program was used to print, which I'd consider "personal." Also, it's used to target offers to the user, which would seem to be impossible without personal information. (You can disable this feature during setup.) I wouldn't recommend against the printer for this reason, but would recommend users take the time to deactivate this feature.

"Epson XP-410 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer with Scanner and Copier" is a solid product in many respects. The printer has several good features (cloud printing, easy Wi-Fi setup, etc.), has a small footprint and is priced very cheap. Furthermore, the print and scan quality is respectable for both text and photos, especially given its (upfront) price point. Of note, this printer only connects through Wi-Fi (there is no Ethernet connection) and there is no Fax component; however, that is not unusual for printers at this price point. Also of note, the document feeder on the printer is very limited (there is no duplex and the paper tray can only hold about one hundred sheets).My biggest problem with the "Epson XP-410" is ink. When compared to other printers, the inks are perhaps the most expensive that I've seen in 2013 (even among other Epson printers, which always tend to be a bit costly in the ink department). While the cartridges appear to be priced competitively, that cost is deceptive, as they last half as long (if not less) than other printers that I have used (and am currently using; this includes an "Epson XP-800", which also has a pricey ink system in place). If you intend on printing a lot, are cost-conscious, or simply don't enjoy the hassle of constantly replacing ink cartridges, you will regret purchasing this printer pretty quickly (Don't believe me? Take a look at the reviews for this printer's ink cartridges).In all, if you are looking for an upfront cheap printer with good print/scan quality, have no need for a fax or Ethernet connection and print only occasionally, I can give "Epson XP-410 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer with Scanner and Copier" a mild recommendation; however, all others should definitely check out other alternatives for their printing needs before taking the plunge with this one.

Some people will love this paper and some will not; it depends on your needs.Weight: this is 24-pound paper, as compared to the normal 20-pound paper. You will notice right away that the reams are much heavier. 24-pound is nice for resumes and other important documents. But if you're going to use it for large runs of ordinary printing that you have to haul around in a briefcase or knapsack, you will notice a definite increase in the amount of weight you have to carry. So if the benefit of a 24-pound paper is marginal for you, then stick with a 20-pound paper. Also, the weight/thickness may make it jam more in older printers. My Canon did not have a problem with it.Brightness: This is 92 brightness. Around here, we are brightness freaks and use 96 brightness. It may not sound like a lot, but when you put the papers next to each other, the 92 is actually quite dull. Again, it's your preference and needs. If you need or just prefer brightness, then 92 is rather ordinary.Oddity: I was surprised that in a certain light, the paper has alternating vertical stripes -- very subtle, but very noticeable. It's sort of like the kinds of laid lines you would see in cotton paper, but not quite. It gives the effect of a faint tone-on-tone. I did not like the effect, but again, it may not matter to you.Nicety: I found I like the smaller-size cases of 1500 sheets. I unpacked it, plugged it in, followed the instructions on the handset (to enter Skype username and password), and was up and running. It is that easy to set up.
