When our workhorse Panasonic phone/fax finally gave up the ghost after almost 13 years, we took our time finding the right phone as a replacement. While we didn't need a fax function anymore (because we have health insurance and won't be taking any $99 vacations to Bermuda), we did need something that would cover two rooms, not interfere with our wireless setup, and have an answering machine for screening calls. This DECT unit from Vtech seemed to fit the bill. The price was right and it seemed to have the functionality we needed, so I ordered it. Right out of the box, everything was right about this product. The handsets are sleek and very, very light, almost disconcertingly lightweight. Same goes for the base unit. I was a little nervous, but everything assembled very easily. I plugged the unit in, ran the phone cord, and voila, it began charging. After a few minutes of charging, I picked it up: dial tone. So far, so good. I was pleasantly surprised that the second handset does not require a phone cord plug-in, because the study where we wanted to put it has a large computer desk/bookcase, combo in front of the jack. (The phone wire we ran years ago went dead and all the furniture would have to be moved to get to it.) I plugged in the second unit and it began charging right away. A couple of minutes later, I called the house from my cell phone, both units rang, then the answering machine picked up. It recorded flawlessly, and I like the clear, anonymous-sounding recorded voice, so no need to record a message on the machine. Playback is one touch, message deleting is also one touch. I literally spent less than five minutes setting everything up, and everything works, and it works great while being easy to use and understand. The wife really loves the small footprint of both units, which are about a fourth or a fifth of the size of the previous replacements we tried. The range is good, the sound is great. The phone looks sleek and modern and is  very intuitive to operate. Anytime I can buy a tech product and have it running the way it is supposed to in less than five minutes with zero frustration and no FAQ reading and no support inquiries, that is a good day. Honestly, I could not be happier with this phone, and if you ever call me, I'll be able to tell you all about it.

You can affix them to a bare wood surface, making sure to burnish the labelssecurely, then apply clear finish on top. I've found that they work very well for (of allthings) custom guitar work. It's relatively easy to create your own headstock logo design,and a few coats of clear finish will make them look almost as good as a decal. I have hadno problems with the ink reacting negatively with lacquer or poly finishes. The main pointis that you do not want to burnish the labels directly, as the ink will rub off. Acetateor some similar material should be placed on top before burnishing. I used a graphic artstype burnisher tool, but you could improvise to see what works best for you. Of course,this is only one idea, but the versatility of these Avery labels makes them a good buy.
This relatively small device is sufficient to hold all of the desktop items that I will typically use during the day. Well made, good price. I highly recommend.

I remember when Magic Tape was only used by banks to mend torn money -- All we used when I was a kid was the glossy stuff, which, although it perforemd the job well, was glaringly obvious and didn't make booboos like torn book pages any less sad to look at. Then came Magic tape -- the best and only Scotch tape I will ever use now. It blends with most of its surroundings when used, and if artfully applied can make some torn pages look new once again.This 3 pack came sensibly wrapped in a recyclable cardboard holder -- and each little plastic tape dispenser IS refillable - AND small enough to carry in briefcase, backpack, purse, and even pocket.There were no metal cutters to accidentally snag on clothing or fingers, and, when held at the proper angle, the serrated plastic cutters perform admirably.

I have to admit, I love having this pen stand on my desk. It just looks cool! And anyone who comes into the apartment notices it.The pens themselves are an impressive collection. As far as I can tell, no color is repeated -- these are actually 44 pens in differing shades. Some of them are close, but none of them repeat. They don't feel like the sturdiest pens on the market, but they're not cheaply made, either. And the gel ink seems to be well-formulated.Now, my question is: is there any practical reason to own this many pens? Unless one is a pen artist, then no. It's honestly a novelty item. But a fun novelty item nonetheless!

This works a lot better than the silly plastic, fuzzy erasers that are standard in most office environments and come with the dry erase pen sets.  Those old erasers only work in ideal situations.This 3M eraser works with very little effort on normal lines and took off a lot of stubborn lines with slightly more effort.I tried wetting the eraser as suggested and it does work getting off really stubborn lines but is messy and leaves the whiteboard damp.  I needed to use a paper towel to dry it after that.  Maybe I got it too wet.  It does clean better wet than a wet paper towel.Anyway, I plan to keep these around all the time for my white board.

It is good cheap paper that comes directly to my door with free shipping. Can it get better than that? I looked on staples.com before I bought this and they don't normally beat this price, even though obviously if they did a big sale they could. No issues with the shipping and delivery, and no problems with the product use in my home printerThere not much else I can say about paper, its paper. Ask Dwight or Jim if you have further questions.

This chair has some great and not so great aspects about it.  So let's get into the pros and cons.  First the pros:PROS:The chair is great for posture.  It forces you to sit up straight.  And once you get used to it, it will even make your back feel better.  The chair is much easier to use than sitting on a exercise ball as well.CONS:The cover can't be removed to wash.  The ball might be a little undersized for some bigger people.  Also I had trouble with the air slowly seeping out.  I didn't find any holes in it.  Or any discernible leeks.  But it just looses air over time.  The price is also a little steep.OVERALL:I can't really recommend the chair.  It's not terrible.  But the price seems steep for the little bit of returns you get from it.  D-

This Ivation Portable Handheld Scanner is just about the most practical gadget that I have come across in a long time. We run a small business that provides training and also manage a small library for a crafter guild, so we deal with a lot of printed material. Before being sent this scanner to review, we would use a flatbed scanner when we needed to bring information into the PC but this portable scanner has made it much easier for us.We tested this scanner in the standalone mode (requires 3-AAA batteries, included, and a micro-USB card, which is not included) and also connected to a Windows Vista Laptop via the included USB cable. It worked well in both modes once you figure out the correct speed to move the scanner across the text or image (or combination) to be scanned. To get the best results, the surface should be as flat as possible and you should move the scanner at a consistent, fairly slow speed.It scans in both B&W; and in color, doing a decent job on pictures, but since most of the documents I scan are text the OCR (Optical Character Recognition) functionality was most important for us. The OCR was very good, easily handling all of test documents we tried with about 98% or so accuracy. I was very pleased with result!This is a very good hand scanner that is easy to install and use!Highly Recommended!CFHNote: Unit provided for review by manufacturer

I use this everyday at work! The perfect tool to remove staples without having to worry about that darn claw stapler remover.  I put this near my pens so it's easy to reach and grab.  I've been known at the cool person at work with all the fancy products!  Would definitely recommend to a friend!

Why didn't somebody think of this before?  The pad design is outstanding, rather than having to fish little sheets of labels out of a box every time you need one.  The color coding is nice, as well, if you are into using color on your file labels.  If you are not, you won't find the small amount of color overly distracting.  They are definitely permanent labels.  Once affixed, you need not worry that they will come off.

This board is superb if this is what you need to motivate you!  It's a great idea, and I would love for this to be the impetus that gets me off the couch.  At this point, I don't really have a good place to hang it~ It is really big...  Be sure to note the dimensions.  Okay, I can complain about the size, but truthfully, is that why I don't use the board?  No.  What I don't like about the board is that it doesn't yank me out of bed in the morning and make me exercise.  The board is exactly what it claims to be and how described in the picture and description.  I hope it is just the answer that you are looking for!

We have several cheap white boards kicking around our house that don't come clean no matter how hard we try. Because they are low quality, the first marks are bound to leave ghosting when erased. And, I haven't found a cleaning solution that truly works on those white boards like they do on the better quality white boards.Those cheap white boards were the first guinea pigs for these erasers. I did have to scrub, but the white boards scrubbed clean for the first time since they were new! Most if not all of the ghosting was gone. As of yet, I have not had to wet the eraser to get rid of ink - I've just had to put a little muscle into the scrubbing. Even so, it was a quick scrub - two or three good, hard swipes did the trick.In all honesty, I don't have a problem using sprays to clean my white boards. But, there are times when I need my good big white board, discover that the kids have left pictures drawn all over it, have to spray it to get the old marks off, and then have trouble getting it dry to write on. These erasers are the perfect solution to that problem as well as for cleaning up the lower quality white boards.Having used these erasers on a couple of boards so far, I can see that there is definitely going to be a limit to many times they can be used. For that reason, these will not be my first choice for cleaning my boards. I'll stick with my normal usage of the regular eraser and various cleaning sprays and save these erasers for when I really need a deep clean or a quick dry clean of set marker.

Tired of scribbling all over your boxes and not knowing what's actually in there anymore?  Ta-da!  These labels are easy to use, easy to remove, and look slick.  I recently moved and these were a savior.  Note that the super sticky notes come in two varieties.  One type (what you are purchasing here) is the better kind which has a perforated edge which is not sticky, so that the notes can be separated but then have full stick when attached to object.  The other kind is not perforated and the note always has a non-sticky flap sticking out.Also note that there's a variety of sizes here, and the small ones are too small and worthless.

I've had the Pixma MX860 for a year now and it has been money well spent.  I needed a quick replacement when my Epson Stylus R2400 began having printing issues.  I've never been a fan of any HP product - I stopped using their cheaply made, unreliable products several years ago.  The Pixma has filled the gap and the results have been nothing less than excellent.  8x10 prints are stunning, tonal quality is superb and the ink cartridges have outlasted their competitors.  I do miss the larger sized paper abilities of the R2400 but what the Pixma does, it does very well.  I cannot comment on the fax capabilities as I don't use that feature, likewise for the copy feature.

These file folders are colorful and well designed.  They have folding metal fasteners on both sides and they have organizing tabs on them (top, center, bottom).  They come in three colors.  All in all, these are really nice, except for one thing: the card stock is light weight. The tab-edge is reinforced (2-ply), so you can use it reliably.I plan on using these for organizing data and some reports.  If you plan on using these, you WILL need a two-hole punch, or some means of consistently punching holes in the tops of the papers.

I ordered the Epson Artisan 700 mainly because it prints on CDs and DVDs. It does this very well, better than the HP 5280 which I have used for about two years (and which is practically defunct).The Epson Artisan 700 also has done all other printing tasks very well, with excellent quality in printing photos and text.I am pleased with this purchase, although I was disappointed that the printer uses so much expensive ink.

The TrimAir cuts square and very nearly cleanly. As others have noted, the base is made of a composite wood and the safety guard gets in the way (which, really, is the whole point of a guard). My only disappointment was with quality. The blade in my copy has a small nick that causes a very small perturbation in the paper cut. You can feel the nick as an interruption in an otherwise smooth cutting motion when bringing the guillotine down. Most people would not notice the evidence it leaves in the paper; you have to examine it very closely. Inspecting the larger unit, I see one of the screws holding the blade is not seated all the way in its recess (and the assembler nearly stripped the head). So, overall the design is sound but the production quality on my unit does not merit five-stars. It is clear, however, that most people are not experiencing such problems and that chances are you'll not have to return your copy.

This three ring binder is available in a variety of different colors including pink, red, black, blue, green and white. I tried the pink color and really like this shade of pink. The exterior is strong but it nicer to the touch than the average plastic binder. The spine is angled so that it's almost rounded and is more comfortable to hold than a straight binder. It has the capacity to hold 300 sheets of paper and the binder clips are rounded and close securely so that paper doesn't come out.It has a big window on the front that allows you to customize the look and add pictures or decorations. That was a really cool feature that I have never seen before. If you get bored with it then you can switch it up whenever you want. It also has a strong plastic smoke colored page with dual pockets.This binder is a little bit more but it's really good and will last the whole year long.

The receipt option is great as I have always hated wasting a whole label when printing shipping labels online.Great quality and true to earth when they say no smudging!Crisp and Clear text on all labels printed on these, Highly recommended!

Obviously if you need hanging files, these aren't going to fit your needs. But if you, like I, get a lot of bills, receipts, etc that need to be quickly and easily filed then accessed as a group, these are great.When expanded, they stand up in my filing cabinet easily and allow me to just drop purchase orders and receipts right into them with no hassle. Later, I'll go through the documents to enter them into my accounting program, and these make it easy to grab the most recent group without worrying about anything falling out the sides.Yes, this is a function of the design of standard expanding folders, but the tall grippy section both makes it easier to drop in docs and grab the folders quickly and easily.The only downside is cost. For about the same price as four grip-style ones, you can buy 10 traditional ones. So for me, I'll use them for those groups of regularly accessed files: printed receipts, current orders, purchase orders, recent bills. Anything I don't need to grab and review I'll just use traditional hanging or expanding folders.Look - they're folders - they're not going to change the world. But for types of paperwork one needs to file quickly and grab easily (and often), they're perfect and worth the extra dosh.

This fourpack of spiral notebooks is colorful and useful.  Just what I need for taking notes and making grocery lists.The price is well worth the quantity and quality of the product offered.  I would definityly order it again.
I found these storage boxes easy to assemble and useful. You might want to use some tape to hols a handle flap down if it isn't full of files and other stuff. A sturdy enough box. Recommended!

This is a wonderful product, as are all of Avery's items.  I wanted to try these because I have a small online business.  Often, I like to include a small gift or address my customers' attention toward included advertisements in my shipments.  These labels were exactly what I needed.  I have also used them on the outside of the shipping container to personalize and add a touch of professionalism.I use an inkjet printer and the labels printed perfectly.  Avery's website offers templates that are easy to use and that offer a variety of choices.  Simple.  Easiest thing I've ever done on the Internet.You really can't go wrong with these stickers.  They stick without curling up on every surface in which I have applied them.

I'm a woodworker who is constantly losing pencils. I came fifty or more in a box and they seem to disappear into thin air. These I keep for special detail work in a special place, and when I'm done, I make sure they return to that special place. Work as you'd expect.

These are great for creating different kinds of blending effects with colored pencils, and I am very glad I found them. They are very slightly gritty (as opposed to a completely smooth burnisher like Caran de'Ache's blender pencils), so they blend colors well and I can go over the blend with another color or white to mute it. Wonderful tool!

How many times have you used 3M-brand Post-it notes as item labels?  Dozens of times for me, and it usually works pretty well.  Imagine if 3M put that magical Post-it adhesive over the entire back of a (nearly) 2" x 3" sheet?  It would be label-ease heaven.The wizards at 3M must've had a collective forehead slap when they thought to market these, thinking, "What took us so long to think this up?"  Remarkably simple but very effective, these labels stick just like Post-its (same adhesive), only there's more of it for longer tackiness.  Just write, peel, and stick.  (It seems to work on just about everything except cloth.)  When you're done with the label, it removes cleanly without leaving any discernable residue.All in all, another useful application of Post-its from 3M.

These boxes exceeded my expectations.  I couldn't understand why anyone would buy boxes until I received these.  They are heavy duty cardboard and easy to assemble.  I like the built-in handles that make them easy to handle once you have filled them.  No tape is certainly a plus at my house where it seems we are always looking for the tape and wondering who used it last.These boxes are good for more than moving; they are great for storing seasonal items.  I put my over-sized winter comforter, the bedskirt, the fleece blanket, and sheet set, in this box to store until next winter since they took up way too much space in the closet.  I love it!

These little tabs work very well for hanging very light items on smooth surfaces. If there is any texture to the surface you're adhering to, they have significantly less tack. This worked very well for hanging photos, postcards and notes, but they failed when used to hand a poster that had been rolled up. The curl of the paper would cause the edges to release and the poster would fall to the floor.  Also, be careful with porous paper items, as the stickies tend to adhere a little too permanently to the paper after a week or so and can damage it a bit when removed.  The re-usability of these squares was really impressive though... just wash off any dirt, hair, or lint under running water and they're good as new and ready to go again! Generally works just as advertised. Recommended!
We have a Dymo label printer. The label quality is perfect. We constantly run labels for Fed-Ex & USPS. The labels stick & ink doesn't smudge.

I use the avery design pro software for all my label printing, so this was definitely a cake walk! They printed out easily on the laser printer(brother brand) and adhered nicely to my jars. I love that they're water resistant and the arch is attractive! Will definitely be buying more of these in the future.

These are very good chalk sticks with beatiful colors. I have already colored pictures with them. They are low-dust and easy to use. They blend easily and are beautiful. I have used pastels for over 50 years and these are top-notch.They do not break of crumble. Anyone would enjoy these!
Purchasing the ink in this set saves money and gets a pack of photo paper too.  I always purchase my ink in the package.

This Monochrome (prints in Black ink only) printer was surprisingly easy to set up. Even the Wifi set up (which lets you print and scan from your computer or laptop wirelessly) was easy and painless.  The included quick setup instruction manual was easy to understand and well written too. However changing more advanced settings such as scanning resolution wasn't as easy to do on the printer itself. I ended up using the Epson program on the computer to change the scanning resolution. Settings on the program were easy to figure out. My test print and scan came out nice with default settings. Although I would recommend changing the resolution for scanning higher. The default was 300  dpi (dots per inch), but you can change it to as high as 1200 dpi. If you are scanning a photo, you would want this number as high as possible. For regular text documents, 300 dpi should be fine and this keeps the file size down too... around 1mb. Keep in mind that while this printer only prints in black and white, the built in scanner scans in full color.For the cost and features of this printer (such as the convenience of wireless printing through your home wifi), I would definitely recommend this printer to anyone who prints a lot in black and white. It's too bad it doesn't print in color though. I'm not sure if this ink is as efficient as advertised... supposedly it's more cost-efficient than b&w; laser printers. The replacement ink doesn't look too expensive so if it is as efficient as it states, this could be another big reason to get this one over similar models from other manufacturers.* Please note that this printer doesn't come with a USB cable or paper.  If you're setting this up to use with your wifi network, a usb cable isn't needed at all though. This printer uses a standard USB printer cable, so you could use the old one off of an old printer if you have one laying around.

I was able to set this printer up and connect it to my wi-fi network without ever physically connecting it to a computer - which is exactly how it should be. (although you can of course use the included USB cord for a traditional connection). Remember, this printer does NOT print in color, so while it is affordable for home use, I assume the target market is small businesses who only need to print in monochrome, and also be able to scan and copy.The print quality is excellent, producing crisp text outlines that appear much more precise than my inkjet printer. There is, however, no automatic double-sided printing, so be aware if you need that feature. The current price point is good for an entry level laser printer, but (and now the caveat) the cost of replacement cartridges are a bit high when compared to their below-average capacity (around 1000 pages) so your long-term operating costs may be more expensive depending on your printing volume.
I have no complaints about these markers. They work perfectly on our kids dry-erase board. They don't smell strong like some dry erase markers do. They seem like they will last a long time.

I was very impressed with this sharpener. It's fast, for one thing -- compared to the sharpener that it replaced, the thing sharpens blazingly quick. And it's got a larger tray than I'm used to, which is nice ... along with a little LED to tell when it's full, which is REALLY nice as my old sharpener would get gummed up if the shavings got to full and I didn't notice.It is a bit larger than my old sharpener, and also a top-loader, which meant reorganizing my office space a bit to accommodate it. But it looks good on the desk, and I like that the suction-cup feet hold it in place (kids have such a tendency to pull cords!).

I was very excited to get this product because I have a wall at work where I tape up photos of the kids.  I regularly put up new pictures so the idea of removable and reusable sticky tabs was perfect.  My first complaint was that they were too big.  They may come in smaller sizes, I'm not sure.  I didn't rate them down due to size though since they are easy to cut down, which I did.  I didn't have any of the problems some of the other reviewers had with them coming off the wall.  Instead, my problem was removing the tabs when I wanted to change the photos.  They were REALLY stuck and tore up the back of the photos.  I also had used one on a printout on standard printer paper and when I went to take it down a day later, it ripped the paper completely.  My daughter has a very heavy weight poster (poster board thickness) hanging on her bedroom door right now and it hasn't budged since put up so I'm pleased with that.  I'm sure it would have hit the floor numerous times if it had been put up with tape.  I'm a little nervous about what kind of damage there will be to my door when it needs to come down though.So, based on my experience, I'm giving them four stars.  They seem to attach well and, when I can get them off, they are definitely sticky enough to use again.  The removal part needs to be revamped though.

The 3M Gel Wrist Rest (WR340LE) is an outstanding wrist rest.  The leatherette, anti-microbial cover is very comfortable.  The gel is firmer than others I've used but no less comfortable.  The firm gel seems more durable than the others too.  Other gel wrist rests I've used became malformed after a short period of use.  Also, because of the firmness, it keep my wrists from sagging and maintains a more ergonomic, neutral position.I highly recommend this series of gel wrist rests by 3M.

I've love pens and pencils and have enjoyed Uni-ball products for many years and this new roller ball pen with the black-based color inks is terrific.  The colors that came in the package are blue, brown, green, purple, and red and because of the inclusion of black in the colors they have a different slightly muted look as opposed to other pens with colored inks that tend to shout their color at you.Also the pen writes smoothly which means that if you write extensively with it, your hand won't tire quickly.Highly recommend this product.

You should be aware that this printer has a serious "ink low" behavior. When any ink cartridge is getting low (which still means a lot of ink left by the way), it changes the Fax reception model. Instead of printing your faxes as they arrive, it dumps them into memory. So, even though yellow (say) is low, it will not print your B&W; fax!It takes more than 5 steps to print the fax and delete it (menu, scroll to memory item, ok, scroll to print, OK document, scroll to print all pages, ok, menu to go up, scroll to delete, ok to delete, ok to delete, menu to get out).Worse, after a couple of these, the memory is mixed up. So, when you want to send a Fax, it will say "memory full" even though the memory is empty. You then have to power cycle the printer (hold down on/off for 1 second, wait 10 seconds, power on, wait for it to get ready (another 10-20 seconds).This means you either have to waste ink by throwing out cartridges before they are empty, or you have to deal with this mess. Canon says there is no workaround or fix for this.There are 3 other problems with copying you should know before you buy (I wish I did):1. You cannot use the Auto Document Feeder (sheet feeder) when copying or scanning with any setting in auto (exposure, size, etc). It does not make any of that clear, so if you find it refuses the auto doc feeder, reset everything to manual :-(2. Black duplex printing uses color cartridges for one of the sides, so uses the more expensive ink. That is, it does not use the blank ink for both sides.3. Copying speeds are much slower than the blurb implies. If you make 10 copies of one page, it is as fast as they say. If you copy multiple pages, each one takes much much longer, does the scan, and then does the print. Also, if any setting is in auto mode, it does a two pass scan (one to check the page), and that takes a really long time.

I love this Scotch Tear by Hand Tape!!  A bit of background here, when it comes to taping box's there's one thing that *always* happens to me--inevitably I cut the tape the proper length just to have it curl up on itself and become useless...  Well, Scotch Tear by Hand Tape has stopped that problem!  I don't have to worry about the tape curling up on me, or the scissors failing me at the last possible second, I can just tear it by hand and place it on the box.  It makes setting up boxes directly in the post office much easier and faster, too!  So far, I've had no problems with this tape and haven't heard any negative feedback from the recipients of the packages, either.  If you ship a lot, then this is something to look into getting!

I have to wear a swipe key at work to make sure I can get back into my office suite after using the bathroom. I received a lanyard at work but find it impractical at best. The retractable badge reel is a lot more comfortable to place on pants, skirts, etc.I like the different colors, and suppose that one can match the different outfits with them, but I prefer to attach the badge to a reel and use it until it breaks. These reels aren't always the most durable, but so far, it's been a month and the first reel hasn't broken.

I am using Epson, pretty much, exclusively these days.  Their products are dependable, reasonably priced, and I haven't found anything better.  If I have one qualm it is the fact that if one ink cartridge goes, it must be replaced before you can continue printing.  I shouldn't have to replace the yellow ink cartridge if I am only printing something in black.  But, that seems to be the way of it anymore, not only with this printer but with others.  Other than that, this printer does a great job of making beautiful poster sized pictures.  Prints come out quickly and as clear as the original.  It holds a LOT of paper.  And I love that, because it's always irritating to have to reload paper right in the middle of a job.  It was simple to setup wirelessly and I have enjoyed using it.  I haven't used fax yet, but I'm using this at home, not the office.  So, I have really no need for it.

1  inch binder with 1 year guarantee:  This binder has a little more integrity in its construction than some of its counterparts.  It does not have nearly the number of bubbles and dents in it that the 1 inch binder does.  However, the slots inside are positively useless.  While they may hold a couple of pages to start out with, they are not strong enough to have any lasting effect.This binder does not have the easier to open hinge that some of the Wilson Jones binders do and this one is very difficult to open.I'm not sure what they mean by a 1 year guarantee.  I don't think it is very likely that someone would go to the trouble to return one to the manufacturer.  I personally, would just throw it out when it became compromised.

The Sharpie Fabric Markers were great for repainting the faded artwork on a T-shirt that I loved.  I felt like a Master painter retracing the borders on the design and filling in the brilliant colors on the leaves and flowers.  The markers were easy to hold and the colors applied boldly and sharply.  I was also pleased to note that they were odorless.

This product comes complete with storage bag, calibration materials and cleaning supplies. Installation, while a bit lengthy, was easy due to the well designed instructions and the on line videos. It does require you to turn off your Virus protection to install, no reason given, so that may give people pause. [it does not need it off to function, so the window is small for infection]The first receipt I scanned was a co-pay on my HSA account credit card - the ones you need to file/fax in to prove that you used the funds correctly? Scan time is fast - you will wait an extra minute for the software to fully 'recognize' the data. The software prides itself on word recognition to fill data cells - but on my first attempt it failed to recognize both the name of the business AND the total charge of $25, listing instead nothing for the name and a charge of $5. It is easy enough to change and update this issue before saving the information to the database, but a bit of a letdown. One pull-down data field has you specify what type of expenditure this was - and these choices mostly center around the business traveler as none made mention of Health providers. I had to use 'other'.This tool can create instant PDF files of anything scanned [nice plus] and the tutorial even suggests storing your child's art work this way. A neat idea, as long as the original art fits the scan opening. Will scan in B&W; or color - nice surprise. Software allows data to be linked up with other packages such as Quickbooks & TurboTax - nice!All in all, a great way to preserve those items most easily lost - bits of ephemera that are important and fade with time/heat. [i.e. - most receipts generated now] For those with thousands of business cards, this tool would be a great way to organize, save and then discard the paper version.

I must begin by saying I personally do not find this to be a bad stapler, when all the basics are considered.  But unfortunately this is the case of a little stapler wanting to be all fancy, which means the stapler must then be used all the time to meet its fancy nature, which means the stapler will probably get used more than is good for it.  To be fair, I'm only a huge fan of electric staplers when I'm stapling one thing after another in a concentrated period of time--because I have yet to meet an electric stapler that impresses me without throwing a tantrum on me.All the intricate adjustment settings do make this good for a busy office setting, though I think the smaller office or home won't need so many gizmos.  It's a sturdy stapler that won't get jostled about unduly, and the stapling occurs quickly.  The 45 sheet capability is a nice perk and this indeed handles that many pages as promised.But... after so long and so many uses... one may find herself swearing and smacking the stapler as it eats staples or the paper so one finds herself tearing the paper out little by little.  Annoying, though less apt to happen if this stapler is reserved for special projects.Again, I just prefer a manual stapler for my heavy-duty projects and this electric one does not seem up to heavy-duty long shifts.  But for moderate use or special occasions, it would do the trick.

This stapler arrives with a white cover.  You don't get any staples and need to order the cover.  I ordered a peacock design that came pretty quickly and looks really nice.  I like this size since I use it on my craft desk.  I wouldn't try to staple a whole lot of paper at a time but it works just fine and looks good.

The labels are semi-transparent white on the sheet, but clear once adhered to the surface.  The dilemma I always have with these types of labels is that I just want to print one or a small handful, but the sheet has 30 and I don't want to waste the rest.  One reviewer had a good suggestion to tape a piece of paper over the labels that you don't want to use up.  I find that sometimes if I don't do this carefully it will jam the printer.  So another trick that I discovered is:1. Make a layout in the software for a small number of labels.2. Print onto a blank sheet of paper.3. First, the simplest advice I can give to anyone buying a graphing calculator for their child for school: Check what the teacher recommends, and ASK if it's OK to use something other than what is recommended.  If the teacher recommends a particular calculator, there could be a very compelling reason for that recommendation.  Having said that, here's the review:If you're reading this review, you're no doubt aware of the seemingly universal "standard" that Texas Instruments has set with their graphing calculators.  Should you switch to Casio?  Well, it depends.  It's tempting, because they are less than half the cost of a TI calculator.  And Casio is a respected name.  One of my very first graphing calculators, back in the late 80s, was a Casio.First, here's one reason NOT to buy the Casio:I've taught high school math classes where I needed my students to have a graphing calculator.  We did some advanced things with those calculators (specifically, we were doing some programming to demonstrate some precalculus and calculus concepts).  During that time, it was important to me that all my students have the same kind of calculator, so that we could work together going through the same steps to reach the same results.  In that particular instance, if one student were to show up with a Casio when the rest of my students were using a TI, the Casio student would have been in trouble.  In that scenario, the Casio student would likely have fallen behind, as some of the features are different enough to make it near impossible to follow along.  The features of the Casio FX-9750GII and the TI-83 (or 84) are similar...but the differences would have been a real difficulty in that classroom setting.  SO...if your child is going to partake in classroom activities, and if the teacher recommends a TI so that your child can follow along, then DON'T get the Casio.Another, similar reason to go with TI instead of Casio:There is a vast library of programs (think of them as apps for a calculator) that can be shared from teacher to student, or from student to student.  There is no way that a TI program will work on a Casio calculator.  It IS possible to write programs/apps for the Casio, but they are not compatible with TI calculators.But there are plenty of GOOD reasons to buy the Casio FX-9750GII:* If you just need ANY graphing calculator (something that can do calculations, graphing, statistics, and can be used on SAT/ACT/AP exams), then this is a very good calculator.  It has all the functionality I would expect.* If it's not important or necessary for you to have the same calculator as other users (for example, if a math teacher says, "Get any kind of graphing calculator you want.").* If you want to save money.If you do a side-by-side feature comparison of the TI-84 Plus and the Casio, you will find that both calculators have "mostly the same" features.  Both do math/stats/graphing.  Both are programmable.  Both can be used on the common exams taken by high school students.  The specs on the TI are better than those of the Casio: The TI has better screen resolution and more memory.  But if you are doing "typical" high school math, those differences may be irrelevant.I will give a little more credit to TI: I find that it's easier to navigate TI menus to find the features I need.  I think the TI options are better organized (though I might be biased because I've been using TI calculators for so long).  My only reason for giving the Casio 4 stars instead of 5 is because I had a hard time finding certain features.  This included difficulties in using the Casio manual...it's a big manual, but the organization made it hard for me to find practical information.  I suppose, though, that as I spend more time with the Casio, I'll get used to where things are.The Casio fx-9750GII really is a very decent graphing calculator...and at less than half the price of a TI graphing calculator, it's worth considering.  Just understand that it may not be the right choice for some classroom situations.

This is quite possibly the best printer that I've ever owned.  That's saying a lot, considering how many printers I've gone through.  Let's go through the various pieces and I'll show you why I like it so much...Print Quality - It's rather trite, but the number one job of a printer is to print.  The print quality of the Artisan 810 is outstanding.  Using decent quality paper, the output is sharp and clear.  Small point type is very readable and fine lines are clearly defined.  Normal single-sided printing is very fast.  Two-sided printing is considerably slower, as the printer waits for the ink to dry before printing the second side.Photo Printing - The Artisan 810 adds two more color cartridges to the standard cyan, magenta, yellow and black mix.  By including a light cyan and light magenta cartridge, it's possible to produce prints with subtle shades and smoother color gradation.  More expensive, dedicated photo printers (e.g. Epson R1900 or R2880, Canon PRO9000MkII) add in still more ink colors and can produce larger prints, but this printer produces excellent prints for all but the most discerning user.  There is one application where I wouldn't recommend this printer - very high quality black and white photo printing.  If you plan on producing high resolution B/W prints, you should look at the Epson R2880 or the Canon Pro9500MkII.  Those units have light black and other cartridges designed specifically for that application.  Outside that, though, prints from the Artisan 810 are truly stunning.Paper Tray - If you're tired of pulling the paper tray and adjusting the guides every time you want to print a photograph, the Artisan 810 has a solution - the paper tray simultaneously holds both photo and regular paper in two different sections.  At my house, I'm keeping 4x6 photo paper loaded in the top section, while the bottom holds standard printer paper...the printer automatically selects the correct paper depending on what's being printed.  The downside of this arrangement is that the tray has a fairly small capacity, only holding 120 pages of normal 20lb paper.  Note that this printer doesn't have a rear paper feed slot.  This prevents its use in applications requiring a straight through paper path.CD/DVD Printing - I don't use too many CDs and DVDs anymore, but when I did, I used a Black Sharpie marker to label my disks. (Except when I was feeling ambitious and had time to burn.  Then I used LightScribe disks)  No more.  The Artisan 810 has an integrated tray to feed printable CD's into the printer.  Just about anything that you can think of - Illustrations, photos and/or text - can be directly printed onto the disk's surface.  Even if what you're printing is just a list of file names, it's better than writing them out by hand.  One of the included software programs formats text and pictures to fit on the CD's surface.  It's nothing fancy, but it works.Scanning - Direct to PC or USB - Buttons on the touch screen display allow you to select the destination of a scanned document.  The scanned image can be sent to any computer that has the Epson drivers installed.  The file can be saved in .jpg or PDF format.  OCR software (Presto PageManager) is included in the software package to convert scanned documents into editable text.  Like most all-in-one units, the scanner only scans one side of the page.Document Feeder - Swinging the feeder input tray closed also lifts the feeder's output tray to make a smooth top...cosmetically it's nice, but more importantly, it also reduces the chances of paperclips and other office debris falling inside.  I've copied a 30 page document without a problem...the maximum thickness of the paper stack is spec'ed at 3mm, or roughly 1/8"Faxing - It works.  There's nothing new or exciting...punch in the number, hit the button and off it goes.  You can store up to 60 numbers in a speed dial directory if you frequently send faxes to the same place.  You can also assign numbers to various groups, so you can easily send the same fax to multiple locations.Copier = Scanner + Printer - As I mentioned above, I've copied a 30 page document without a problem. The copier is only a single-sided copier.  For duplex coping, you need to flip over the paper stacks and run them through a second time.  With CD printing as one of the features, the Artisan also incorporated a CD/DVD copy mode.  You put the original CD in the middle of the glass and hit the dedicated "Copy CD/DVD" button.  The firmware is smart enough to correct minor centering issues.Touch screen controls - Between the keypad, function select buttons, various setup and navigation buttons and everything else, most multi-function machines have a ton of buttons on their front panel.  By using a touch panel that just displays the necessary buttons, the Artisan 810 considerably simplifies the user interface.  The displayed buttons are bright, readable and large enough to easily use.  The viewing angle for the panel is not very large; however the assembly can be tilted upwards to make it easy to read when you're standing over the printer.  One concern that I have has to do with the tilt mechanism...it can easily move up, but you have to push a release to get it to rotate back down.  The latch seems very flimsy and I'm pretty sure that it will break when someone inevitably pushes down on the screen without pushing the release.Ink consumption - With 6 different ink cartridges, ink can get expensive.  As always, your ink usage will depend on what you're printing.  Standard business correspondence uses virtually no ink when compared against glossy photos.  Single page business letters seem to run in the 10-12 cents per page range; 8x10" color photos might as well have a direct line into your local ATM.  There are both standard and high-capacity versions of the cartridges available - I always recommend getting the high capacity version.  Cartridges are available individually and in multi-pack boxes.  I also recommend that you keep a spare set around at all times.  The printer stops printing when any one of the cartridges runs dry and that inevitably happens Thursday at 11:30pm when the kid's trying to print out her homework.Connectivity - Both wireless and wired networking is supported, although you can only use one at a time.  It was very easy to configure the networking and I had the printer up and running inside of ten minutes.  It would have been even faster if I'd read the instructions.  Even a non-technical user should be able to quickly get it installed and working.  If you're going to be using the printer wirelessly, plan on initially use a wired connection to get it configured...you can do it through the front panel, but it's a lot of button pushes.  Once the printer is up and running, you can disconnect and move it to wherever it's going to live.Memory Card + USB port - Nothing too special here.  Like any other printer with a display, you stick in the memory card, select the picture you want to print and go.  Unusually, the USB port was designed to supply enough power to allow it to be used as a charger for iPods, cell phones and similar devices.  You obviously need to supply the correct cable.Extras - Coloring Page, graph paper and lined paper printing - Not exactly a reason to purchase a printer, but nice extras - The Artisan 810 can print lined notebook paper and graph paper.  Since most office supply stores use notebook paper as a loss-leader to get customers in the door, I wouldn't plan on using this to fill up your binder.  On the other hand, it's certainly convenient if you need a couple of pieces quickly.  The ability to turn a picture into a coloring page is another extra.  Kids get bored on a car ride?  Print out some pages and have them color them in.  Just don't leave crayons on your back seats and park in the sun.  Trust me.So...My Conclusion?This is a really good, general-purpose, all-in-one printer for a family or home office.  Its fast, has excellent print quality and a well designed feature set.  It was obviously designed by an experienced engineering team.  This is my ninth all-in-one printer, the fourth one that I've reviewed for Amazon, and the first one that warrants five stars.  Highly recommended.

I bought this scanner so my sister and I could both have a record of family photos and documents where we only had 1 copy.  I received it the week I was suppose to drive down to the 'home place' to work.  We were working at the home place that week-end and had finally gotten around to the "scanning" part of our day--about 10 p.m.  I unpacked and began following the instructions on the big, handy Epson fold-out.  (Very clear instructions, BTW.)  I got to the step for loading the drivers onto my MacBook.  But, wait!  The CD wouldn't load into my computer!  I tried several times, even wiping it gently to see if there was a speck of debris or glue on it.  But, "no".  My laptop whirred, trying hard to recognize the data, then spit the CD out every time.This was very frustrating because we had to leave by noon the very next day to make the long drive home and we couldn't get out scanning done--or even started!  We had no internet service at the house and the local coffee shop 'hot spot' was closed for the night. So, I had to wait until the next morning to drive to the coffee shop and download the proper drivers from their online site.  It didn't give us much time to get any scanning done since we had to leave that morning.  The good news is--at least we'll have the scanner for our next trip.  It was certainly a disappointment, though--and an unwelcome surprise.  Nobody ever expects that to happen to them.I'm sure that Epson, like most everyone else, hires out work done overseas.  That may be the problem--no, or little, quality control.I don't know if anyone else has had that problem with the CD being faulty, but, I thought buyers might like to know that it's possible.ADVICE:  If you're unpacking your new scanner away from home (or internet service), be sure to hook up your new scanner before the local wifi spots close down for the day!PROS:  Excellent scanner!  Would definitely buy again.  And, the price I landed from Amazon the week I bought it was a little less than $80.  Not too shabby!  It's not "lightning" fast, but, I think we human beings of today hate to wait for ANY number of seconds on ANYthing.  We're just too impatient.  I'm going to try to schedule my scanning time for a time when I can do something else while I wait.  Watch TV, do some 'surfing', or just talk to the whoever is in the room with me!  Yeah,...that's the ticket!  Multitask.BONUS:  I've not used the feature yet, but, one reason I bought this unit was because of the negative & slide feature!  WOW!  I hope it proves handy.  Never thought I could find that feature in such a low priced unit.CONS:  CD w/drivers couldn't be recognized by my MacBook.  Was inconvenient because I had no internet access to download them at the time I really needed the scanner.

I love pens and almost all types of writing implements and I have since I was a kid. And since I sit in a home office all day, I need things around me to procrastinate with--having lots of colored pens nearby helps.The thing that I like most about this particular pen set is just the sheer number of colors. I didn't realize until I got the pens that they also vary by tip size, which is nice. I've only been playing with this set for a few hours, but here are my initial observations:Pros:*  Having 100 colors is great--this is a great color range. And there really is a broad range of colors here from black to very pale yellow. There are no less than nine different greens, for example, and about the same number of pinks. I think that there are some color duplicates, but I gather that means that those vary by tip size. I'm a writer and always color-code my notes, so these will help big time. I do think some colors got short changed, see below.*  The carousel is very handy, a nice way to store all of these pens without taking up too much geography on your desk. The carousel spins very smoothly and it shows off all of the colors very well. The carousel is very useful.*  The pens write very nicely--they are comfortable (there is a small grip pad) and write very smoothly.*  The tips are metal and seem well made.The maker claims the pens have very good lasting power and they they resist drying out even if the caps are left off. I can't attest to that yet, but I'm sure to find out.Cons (bear in mind, I like this set, the criticisms and mild and purely personal):*  The pens are not numbered or named. This is my biggest criticism and I think it is a flaw. Not having the colors numbered (especially when there are so many of similar colors) means that if you're trying to match a color to one you used previously (in a scrapbook, for example), you just have to guess. Not having the pens numbered also means that it's impossible to order specific refills.*  Speaking of refills, I was surprised (shocked actually) that there was no refill order form shipped with the set. Aren't I a captive audience for refills at this point? If you were selling a kit like this to people who probably burn through pens, wouldn't you take the opportunity to put an order form in the box? Or a discount coupon that you can use to buy a friend a set?*  The carousel while very convenient and fairly steady has a bit of a wobble to it--no big deal. I do wish the recess for each pen was a bit deeper, but they hold the pens fine--they do not fall out. I've spun it hard and quickly a few times to test it--the pens stay right where they belong. Again, not a complaint, just a few observations.*  There seems to be a lack of reds. There seem to be at least a dozen purples, but only a few true reds and there is no really strong, distinct orange. I really thing they need to increase the reds.*  These pens, like all gel pens, smear on a coated surface. That's not a fault of these pens, but keep it in mind. They do not smear on non-coated papers (like legal pads).In conclusion, I like the set very much. I think the carousel is a very convenient way to store and access the pens and I think the color range is pretty good (not great). If the pens last a long time I'll be very pleased.
I like these pens. They work well and reliably and are affortable, not to mention refillable.I gave these to my granddaughter who loves pink.They also support a good cause.Recommended.

This sharpener is powerful and smooth, creating a very sharp, well-centered point.  It also leaves a smoother wood finish than my other pencil sharpeners.  It can sharpen a brand new pencil in less than 5 seconds!  In the few cases that the pencil tip is off-center (with too much wood on one side), I just stuck the pencil back in, twisted it a little, and it came out fine.It plugs in (as opposed to batteries) and mine had a 4'8" cord with a 2-prong plug.  It takes standard diameter pencils only, and isn't recommended for "crayons, chalk, or soft waxy pencils as they will clog your sharpener's cutters."  However, you can get at the blades through the waste receptacle opening if you need to clean them.The waste receptacle is plastic with a bar sticking out the back that triggers a switch inside the sharpener so it will only turn on with the receptacle in place.  The receptacle is a complete bowl (unlike my other electric sharpener) so the shavings won't spill when you pull it out.  These shavings are by far the finest of my several sharpeners - a fine dust that can electrostatically cling to the plastic receptacle (and innards of the sharpener)!The warranty is 2 years on the "cutter parts", 90 days one everything else (such as the plastic waste receptacle).This will replace my battery-operatedStaples Battery Operated Pencil Sharpenerwhich took 4 AA batteries and had barely enough power to sharpen and stalled frequently.I also have a manualX-Acto Model KS Table- or Wall-Mount Pencil Sharpener (1031), which can handle various pencil diameters, and which I recommend if you don't want a powered model.

This printer is a few steps up form my Workforce 600 which I love and has now moved into another room. The differences are not only cosmetic but internal too. One of the first things that changed is the front interface and buttons. Each task (Fax, Copy, Scan) has its own section and set of buttons accordingly. While in theory its easy, seeing all the buttons covering the front is a bit confusing. The 600 had all the menu's for setting up everything in the main screen sorta like cell phones where you find what you need and scroll around. Now on the 635 there's a button for just about everything on the front. Again, it gets a bit crazy with all these buttons. Its faster to find and select everything though with having dedicated buttons for all the sections.Another big change is that the printer no longer has the paper holder/feeder in the back. This printer now has it on the front bottom, a tray slides out. Well, its good but bad at the same time. I ran into problems putting the tray back in, as it kept getting stuck and going in crooked. Another problem was that the guides in the tray to hold the paper were hard to move and very in accurate to adjust to the right paper size setting. Its very cheap plastic and I thought I was going to break it. Another problem is the finisher paper pullout tray. Its thin plastic and will break if you are hard on it. I had issues with it also.The printer itself has a smaller footprint than the 600 and being the paper supply is on the bottom it fit my desk so much better. The top has the paper feeder for copies and fax which I love and now has a textured patter in the plastic, guess the last one had fingerprint issues so they made it nicer. I have mine setup thru my network so there's only 2 wires, the AC plug and the fax line. It was super easy to setup on the mac, both for the network and the install disc with the drivers. Win7 on the other hand was a little more tricky. Not only did it take over 15 minutes to load the software but when it was going thru the wizard to locate the printer, it failed and said to start over. I decided to go to the Epson web site and download the most current driver set for my Win7 64 bit and then got it working in about another 15 minutes. 30 minutes on windows to get it running is just ridiculous but that's windows for you. Mac literally took 5 minutes.final thoughts, I think the new features are a huge improvement and although all the buttons on the front are confusing at first, they do make selecting much faster once you get used to the layout. The paper feed and output trays are cheaply made and I feel those need to be improved. All in One printers are great and this one really does work great and is so worth the money. Ink replacement is fairly cheap so its not a bad deal.Pros:sizefeaturesspeedseparate ink tankswirelessCons:windows install is a painpaper trays both feed and output are cheap plastictoo many buttons on the front to figure out

For the price of this (over 200 dollars as of reviewing) I'm afraid I have to rate it only 3 stars, even though at a lower price, I'd find it a great item...as it is, it's acceptable but with a few issues.  Lost one star for image quality, and other for some issues with the document feeding.However, it definitely has highlights, including the easy set up, the portability, and the relatively simple but effective software on the device itself.Set-Up: Only tested with Windows computers, but this was great!  You can literally be scanning in under 60 seconds.  It only requires one USB input - no extra power cords or anything.  There is a DVD of optional software, but you don't actually need it.  You can plug the device into any (Windows, possibly other) computer and use the software that is resident right on the device to begin scanning.  (Open the device in windows, click on the "CaptureOnTouch Lite" .exe that you'll see in the folder.)  By default it is set to fully auto and you need only set flip up the lid, pull out the tray arms, put in paper, and hit the button to begin scanning.Other software settings:  You can control some settings if you take it off the fully automatic setting in the software.  This includes contrast, brightness, dpi, color vs. black and white, some settings associated with document feeding, background, and text detection, and image orientation.  It's pretty basic, but okay.  My biggest issue is that you must do this before scanning - once the image is captured, you will need image editing software to further adjust pictures.  Not that editing software is difficult to come by, but you may have to scan multiple times if you want to make changes this way.Document feeding/double sided scanning: It was not immediately obvious to me from the documentation that the scanner did double sided scanning, but it does!  If automatically skips "blank" pages so that if there is nothing detected on the backside of a page it will ignore it, but if there is something on both sides of the document, the scanner will capture both sides (as two separate images).  The instructions claim that the capture side needs to be face down, but because of this feature, that's not true.  (However, if scanning both sides, the "face down" side will appear as the first image.  Where I had issues with the scanning though was when scanning multiple page documents.  The scanner claims to be able to gracefully handle 10 page documents.  So I tried it a few times with an 8 page double sided letter I had from a relative.  And...every time I scanned it I had two reoccuring issues:  1) It will (10-20% with standard paper, none of the time with thicker photopaper and 100% of the time with thin paper like reciepts) of the time feed multiple pages at once, meaning that the two sides of the pages grabbed together that face each other will not be scanned and 2) some pages feed crooked.  Pages on top sometimes "catch" on the lower pages as they drag through, causing those pages to be crooked when they are grabbed by the scanner.  The tray arms are supposed to keep it feeding straight, but they don't fully fix this.  Generally the crooked page will start off kilter then straighten out as it feeds, leading to an odd scan that is crooked and wavy where the page was moving.  The software claims to have a feature (automatically checked) to automatically straighten skew, but if it was doing anything, it wasn't very effective.  Anything that fed crooked looked crooked. DO NOT try to do multiple receipts or anything on very thin paper through this...the thin paper and smaller size absolutely guarantees feed issues every time I did it.  I did not have any issues with crooked feeding when scanning single items, whether they be documents, receipts or photos.After you have the image(s) and saving: This part I love, though I wish there was some additional flexibility for retaining the pictures after the initial save.  Each page (or side of the page if scanning double sided artifacts) shows up as a separate numbered image.  You can scan additional documents or images to add to this, allowing you to capture a large number of images or a document with far more than 10 pages.  You can also rearrange the order of the pages by simple click and drag.  There is not much available for editing...just rotating and zoom.  But you can then save your captures in several formats... as a pdf, a power point file (.pptx) or as an image file (.jpg, .bmp, or .tif)  I personally like .png, but not having this as an option is not a big deal.  If saving a multi-image file in .pdf it saves it as a multi-page document, in .pptx, it's multiple slides, and if saving in an image format it will save as multiple images.  One small nitpick is that you can only choose one option.  As soon as you save it, your options are to open the file you saved it to or to "return to top" where you have to go capture another image.  Could not find a way to retain the images I scanned in the temporary storage of the software and save them in another format.Image quality: this is my biggest disappointment.  You can save up to 600 dpi which is acceptable, and it is true that there are some options for contrast, brightness and gamma as well as background smoothing, edge emphasis and color.  And if you're scanning photos, you will want to play with these.  For documents and text the defaults are fine - you'll get great looking text and acceptable capture if you just want digital copies of things, but if you're trying to digitize photos, the automatic settings are a disaster.  It's saturated in blue and red, the brightness is too low, and the contrast is too high.  What this means is that shadows are deepened, a lot of things are dark, and certain tones are blotchy.  For example - I scanned in pictures of my boyfriend and myself and we looked like we had dark shadows under our eyes and like our skin had patchy red marks while at the same time having blue veins in our hands, none of which was emphasized in the actual photographs.  The real photos have much warmer yellow tones and are brighter, looking much more attractive.  I also got a few artifacts (random pixels that were an odd color - like dust on the photo although I couldn't tell that it did correlate to actual dust and it seemed to be random on multiple trials (sometiems not appearing at all).  On only one photo did I get streaking.  Compared to (1) the xerox at work that is fantastic, (2) the HP Photosmart CP C6180 at home that is a bit streaky but high dpi and otherwise great quality, and (3) the Pandigital SCN02 that I've used to scan whole albums which, though prone to artifacts and streaking and limited to 6" width does a good fast job over a USB port also, this one is the worst of the 4 in terms of what the actual photographs look like.  Even after adjusting the settings off of auto, I could not get the warm yellow tones to come back into the photos and it was only through a lot of trial and error that I got the contrast and brightness approximately okay.Size/durability/weight: the size is good - no bigger than it needs to be to scan normal 8 1/2 wide documents (can even do slightly wider, but not much), and fairly light weight.  Love the single cord.  The little tray that flips open and arms that pop out seem kind of easy to break (especially as the need to put it somewhere where you have room to feed documents through leads to bad behavior on my part, like putting it on the floor where it could get stepped on)  I suspect you could use it even if these broke, just not as well.  The arms are adjustable in width so that smaller items can be fed through securely as well.  Not very heavy.  I actually expect it to weigh more based on looking at it, but the lack of an internal battery means it's not all that dense...the feeder mechanics and housing take up most of the room, with optics in there too.  Not bad, fairly convenient.  Slightly bulky for some laptop cases (wouldn't fit a sleeve most likely) but easy enough for a backpack or larger case.  Compared to the Pandigital SCN02, this has a lot fewer accessories (which is nice) and is large enough to take on whole page documents or larger pictures (that were too wide for the other scanner)End result: this is a very compact, handy and fast way to scan documents, and the integrated software means you can do it from any PC with a USB port (again, I only tried it on Windows PCs - Windows 7 and XP both are fine).  The double sided detect is super handy, and the ability to rearrange and combine multiple scans or pages into a .pdf or .pptx is nice.  But for photos or things requiring good looking images...look elsewhere.  Also, if using multiple feed, always check your scans before saving to make sure no pages were missed or looked funky.  You can delete bad ones or rescan before saving for any pages that were missed...which is nice, but not as convenient as being able to trust without always verifying which would be the ideal.

I've reviewed a number of task chairs in the past from HON and Amazon Basics. In the past, I worked as a furniture installer assembling hundreds of chairs from all the major brands. HON makes great chairs, and this one is no exception. That said, it does have a few significant annoyance that I'll cover in detail later in this review.PROs:+ Build Quality is good overall. Solid pneumatics, good casters that roll freely, and a solid frame that doesn't creak+ Tilt Tension works well. Most chairs in this price range don't have a tilt tension control+ Arm height has plenty of play to fit under low desks or raise your elbows at a higher desk+ Material quality is good. The mesh breaths and will serve you well in warmer weather. I love that you can point a fan at your back while working and actually feel it.+ Seat comfort is great for 2-3 hour intervals. If you're going to sit longer than that, get a more expensive chair. Also, don't sit that long--it's not goof for you ;)+ 5 year warrantyCons:-The back of the chair doesn't tilt much. Not nearly as much as I would prefer. The seat itself tilts forward or back, allowing for different seat angles, but the chair back is very limited in how much it tilts-The sliding arms don't move that smoothly. They also make noise when you reposition your arms. I don't like their design.Other options worth considering:1)Office Star Space Professional Air Grid Back Managers ChairCheaper but from a less prestigious brand, the Office Star Managers Chair lacks tilt control and has less than optimal armrests. It is, however, more comfortable to sit on.2)HON VL700 Series Mid-back ChairAnother HON chair, the VL700 is more comfortable than the HL532 at about the same price. The seat of the VL700 is slightly less comfortable, but the arm rests are superior. For my money, I would buy the VL700 (in fact I am sitting in it right now as I type this review).3)High Back Super Mesh Office Chair with Black Italian Leather Seat]A taller task chair with a headrest, this chair offers a bit more support at the expense of build quality. It's great if you want a high back task chair. The HON and Office Star chairs are built better.Overall:This is a fine chair, but HON's VL700 is better. I'd go with the VL700 if you plan to use the armrests. That's a huge part of a chair's overall comfort, almost as important as the seat itself.

The process is pretty cool to watch and the printer must be fairly well designed to be able to keep the paper in the exact location it needs to be for each pass through.The issue I have is that you have to buy the photo paper and 'ink' at the same time and it can get expensive. I picked up my last office chair at a Staples Black Friday sale, 2011. And sure as if you had called it, 11 months later a caster broke right out of the composite plastic base. Not only did Barge's cement not get that sucker back in there, but another caster followed. Fortunately for me, Amazon Vine came through with the Lota, my first mesh office chair with ergonomic features. It's got some quirks, but out of the box it's good to go.--Shipped in the USA>The chair arrived in a hefty cardboard container, with each major component individually boxed or wrapped inside. Nothing was loose and all parts and paperwork appeared to be accounted. Foam inserts were kept to a minimum and I was able to take down the packing materials and recycle.--Made in China>Mis-aligned holes, wobbly parts, and self-loosening bolts are the facts of life for the last two chairs I've owned. This model went together quickly, quietly, and tightly. Too tight and not all quiet when it came to those casters--like other reviewers I found the barrels in the base were pretty tight. I used a rubber mallet to pound them in place without damaging the parts. The punematic chair post dropped right in.When I got my mits on the shiny base I was delighted to find it was made out of aluminum, and not brittle plastic. It isn't a solid cast of metal, but certainly the heftiest base I've ever had. However, scratches and scuffs cover the metal after three months. There is no protective plastic or tape, and while my shoes don't slip off them when I tuck my feet back,  consider getting something aftermarket to stick on top of the spokes. The wheels are working--no cracks or wobbling, and they don't catch things like cables drooping on the floor as readily as other chairs I've had.Arm rests and the base of the back are also made from aluminum, and like the wheel base are hefty. Unlike every other office chair I have ever owned, this model does not look like it will fail due to metal fatigue of the tilting base. The back attaches to the chair through a big steel slot and secured with four bolts. Because the back reclines without taking the seat with it, the chair is designed so that the arm rests are only attached to the underside. Three bolts apeice and the arm bases are study enough, with only a little play after hand tightening. Or else the armrests can be removed and set aside as desired.The main seat back is a plastic frame with no cross bars or lumbar padding. The mesh is stretched over one side and takes my back well enough. If there is going to be a significant material failure that makes the chair next to unusable, I'd expect it here. Plastic is otherwise probably a good idea for comfort and weight. A metal frame would probably upset the balance among other ergonomic problems.--Operation>After about three months of use, no bolts have come loose, fabric frayed out, or metal broken off.Far as fit and comfort goes, the upper part of the armrests are a dense plastic foam with almost no give. It should be easy to clean spills off this surface. As other reviewers have noted, the arm rests can be adjusted for height, tilted across 90 degrees from diagonal inwards to diagonal out, and slide backwards and forwards. Only the height can be locked in, so the rests will shift around just in friction with your arms.The seat contains a stiff foam insert that springs back into place. It overlaps the plastic and metal underside so there is no rim cutting into the back of your knees. On the other hand, the fabric and foam just doesn't feel as comfortable to my thighs.Seat controls are easy to reach--for someone with two hands. Height adjustment on the right side, and locking the back tilt from the left side. If somebody was missing one or both arms and didn't have a sufficiently dexterous prosthetic, this could be a problem. On the other hand, this chair doesn't sink down on the post as readily, so one should not have to adjust as often.Both seat and back use fabric; the back mesh has a more open and pliable weave. I haven't had any major spills, but imagine that stuff would be difficult to get out of either part of the chair.The mid-back comes up to my shoulder blades. I'm shorter than your average man, so somebody over 6 foot might find this leaves their upper body feeling unsupported. Fits me just about perfect. However, it could use stronger support for my lower back.--Money Money Money>All points considered, this chair is a fine alternative to the $600+ ergonomic models on Amazon. Because of quirks like the limited control over the armrests, the lack of more specific and adjustable lower back support, a back piece that is possibly a bit too short for some users, and a firm but not quite as comfortable cushion, I feel the list price is too high for what one would pay. Even with the thick aluminum parts in place of plastic, there is still enough plastic and enough play that the engineering too doesn't quite justify the asking cost. Get the chair on a hefty markdown; otherwise, take a look at other models in the $600 to $900 range.Compared to $60 and $90 chairs down at the local Staples or Office Max, though, the Lota lifts head and shoulders above them all.
