Thanks to Amazon Vine for offering this to me... I am such a pushover for office, art, paper supplies, and containers of all kinds! $15.31 per 2-pack is high for this type of item, but you may be able to find these locally for less.

I wasn't sure if I would be happy with this little printer or not.  Surprisingly the longer I've been using it the more I like it.  While I do not feel it is a 5 star printer, it is up there when you consider what you get for the price.First it has a small footprint but don't let that fool you, it has a good amount of features.  My previous printer was a big fancy Canon with all the bells & whistles.  One day it decided to stop working.  I think I had it for a little over a year.  An error message came up & that was it.  I was pretty upset because I work from home & need the printer for obvious reasons.  I immediately ordered a Epson printer with all the bells & whistles. About a week later I got this printer as well.  So far I have not needed the more expensive Epson as this little bugger does everything I need it too!  I feel a lot better now that I have a back up printer.My peeves first:-When using the scanner the image does not transfer all the details of the original.  This is a huge problem for me when it comes to the fine lines on ledger paper.-Second is the paper feeder.  I print out a lot of product labels.  If the paper doesn't sit exactly right in the tray, the labels are ruined.  I used the bottom loader in my Canon & never ever had a problem with labels.-Third the wireless doesn't always work.  I cannot figure out why.What I like:-The colors are fabulous!  Truly vibrant compared to my Canon.-The touch screen is on the front of the printer.  At first I didn't like it. I quickly got used to it & realized, "Wow this is great!"  The screen can also tilt up for you to view if needed.-The ink that comes with the printer does not last as long as the ink you buy separately.  At first I thought the ink was way overpriced but after installing new purchased ink, it is lasting much longer & I have no complaints.  My ink use so far:8-22 started using printer.9-14 need black ink (ink sent with printer lasted 3 weeks).9-26 replaced yellow ink.10-22 have not replaced any ink since 9-26.-The printer is easy to set up & easy to use (except for already mentioned wireless issues).-Doesn't take up a lot of space.If you do not have to print out labels or something similar, I highly recommend this little printer.  So far it has turned out to be a fine little machine for the price.

These Post-it Super Sticky Folder Labels with Removable Adhesive work fine.  They say they'll "stick securely, remove cleanly" so you can reuse file folders.  You can handwrite on them or use your inkjet or laser printer.  I tried all three methods of making labels with these with no problems.While I do think the idea of "Stick Securely, Remove Cleanly" is brilliant, and that these labels do so just as advertised, I'm giving them only three stars because the paper seems a little flimsy and rough.  I like a more substantial label with a slicker finish.

This notebook is about as tough as it gets. It can take being carried around and dropped and tossed around. The part of a notebook that seems the toughest for manufacturers to reinforce is the spiral wire, which often gets bent and then it's hard to turn pages. This notebook even has a stronger (though not indestructible) wire spine.If you just need an inexpensive normal notebook with no separators, etc., you can get one much cheaper than this one. But this notebook is not expensive given what you get.

My son needed a mouse pad for his desk.  This item fit the bill perfectly. The mouse pad looks "retro" in black/white.  It's completely flat on the desk and does what a what a mouse pad should - give the mouse it's own little smooth work area.Very good product indeed.

This is so easy to set up and run.  Literally less than 5 minutes for me and I was scanning things.  I can scan photos or regular paper, makes no difference.  I don't travel with it, just leave it hooked up and resting on my desk. It takes up so little room, compared to a regular scanner.

I wouldn't recommend this for a businessperson who wants to make an impression but for just about anything else, this is a handy and cute little organizer. The material is more sturdy than paperboard, and the clasp works well. The pricepoint for the product is just right. It comes in handy.

I've been meaning to get a whiteboard and when this one was offered, I snapped it right up. It's perfectly satisfactory in that it does exactly what it claims to do. The magnetic surface is a real plus. Unfortunately, one does not get to choose color and of course the person who hates orange more than any color in the world (beside turquoise) got one with an orange frame. No big deal--it's still allows me to do what I wanted with a whiteboard. It looks like the price is right; it's not fabulously luxe, but it's not a dollar store item either.

These came just in time for me to post some property.  I only followed the instructions as far as doing the actual printing because I wanted to put them outdoors.  Mine were printed on both sides and hung from tree branches just above easy reach.  They were laminated on both sides and pierced with grommets before being hung on monofilament fishing line.  Handy, easy to use and effective..... think how well they would work when used as they are intended.

Jan 29 2014, I just love this mouse pad!!!  It looks so very nice, even better than it looks here.  I hope I can find it in other colors. I purchase this blue one for my son who has a blue pc for Christmas, so all computer stuff must be blue per his favorite color.I would like to have a bronze and a purple one. So, I plan to look into the other available colors as I did not at the time I ordered this one....
Good color combinations, trusted brand.  It was nice to find a variety of colors in the thin design at a decent price.

This machine is a lifesaver for me. I am an entrepreneur who teaches seminars and workshops and this machine comes in very handy. It makes my presentations look much more professional. I love this machine because when I'm traveling I can take it with me along with my other business necessities as it does not require a power source or batteries. It is a little heavy, but that is to be expected. It takes several lb sizes of paper and can bind an average booklet up to 150 pages depending on the type of paper or stock you are using. I really recommend this to the entrepreneur or small business owner who doesn't want to spend an arm and a leg on printing and binding services. One suggestion is make sure the blade/punchers are clear of debris, it did stick on me once but that was because I did not clear the paper entry.

I needed a variety of permanent markers and the good news, these work. There are tons of colors -- probably more than I will ever need -- but the ink is sharp and clear. My only complaint is that because the points are very fine, they are also very sharp, and can punch holes in less than sturdy materials. This includes aluminum foil, which is one of the things I write on. But if you are careful, you shouldn't have problems.

Oh how I wish I could've enjoyed it longer.  After about three months of use, it stopped working completely.  I don't know if it had anything to do with the laser being used too much to entertain my cat...but I wouldn't think so.  Bluetooth had trouble here and there because of the wireless keyboard and mouse (mostly just glitched once in awhile).  It was very easy to use when I brought it into work for presentations, worked flawlessly on the laptop.  Don't know if I really want to dish out 60 bucks for another but if my hopeful promotion depends on it I probably will invest in this exact one... I think maybe I will use it less for play and more for work.

This cork board is very sturdy and well made.  It's large, 2' X 3' and has a solid wooden edge.  I am going to cover the cork with some decorative fabric to pretty it up a bit.  Then I'll use it for an ever-changing scrapbook for our wall.  I'd recommend this product.  It's nothing fancy, but of good quality and very reasonably priced.
Sound quality is excellent and setup is easy. It can block about 250 call numbers, which is the reason I bought it. It also can store about 3000 numbers in a caller directory.
Key question to bear in mind:  do you want paper or plastic? An alternative is to use ordinary Post-It notes.

Unfortunately it has no software or drivers that will allow it to be used with Tiger OS. The less expensiveCanon CanoScan 4507B002 LiDE110 Color Image Scanneron the other hand does. I considered upgrading my OS to Panther ( the last upgrade available for G5 Macs) but at almost $200  I decided against it. The Epson also needs direct power whereas the canon functions entirely off a USB connection.
This pocket filer is very sturdy and comes in an adorable pink.  Very happy with it and would buy again.

I was disappointed with theScotch Expressions Magic Tape/ 3/4 x 300 Inches/ Tribal/ Blue/ Green/ 3-Rolls/Pack (C214-3PK-4)largely because I think it's overpriced for what is included in the package.  Two rolls of the tape are solid colors and the third is a pretty nice print.  They are essentially like other Scotch brand tapes and are designed to be used in crafty projects like scrapbooking or card making.  I would not use these for wrapping packages because I prefer clear tape for that purpose.  I cut out shapes of the solid color tape and tried to do a little weaving project which was unsuccessful, but I really wanted to find a special use.  The rolls are easy to use rather quickly, so I recommend that if you're starting a project which requires a lot of tape, purchase it at once to avoid running out.

I don't know if I just received a bad one in the batch or if there is a design problem with these 3-ring binders, but this is one that gave me several problems. First, there are bits of tiny pieces of cardboard, presumably from manufacturing, in the cover. Second, and far more egregious, the clear plastic cover has already developed about a one inch rip in the corner that pulls away from the front. This makes an already loose cover even looser. There's really nothing that can be done to fix it, short of duct tape, as experience has shown me that using scotch tape on something like this is only a very short term (and ugly) solution.The problems with the binder aren't just aesthetic. I'm also finding that the binder rings are very difficult to get open. So, despite having these really cool, slanted D-rings, the binder is a chore to use. I can imagine that if I were still a middle school or high school student, the frustration of the rings might actually prevent me from organizing my materials simply because it would be a burden.As I said, I might have just received a bad one, but I'd opt for the Wilson Jones O-Ring Binder, or a different brand altogether, before purchasing this one.

This is the second Wilson Jones binder I own. The single-touch trigger is rather handy and is easy to operate. I would say that the quality/strength of the binder itself is about average. It doesn't feel especially strong or "Heavy Duty" but I do think that it's more than adequate for every day usage. The colors are bright and attractive and the interior pockets are handy, but won't hold a whole lot at one time.

Pros:Easy to use, no more messy glueWorks perfectly with USPS through PayPal (or USPS website)Perforated for easy removal of receiptCons:ExpensiveBottom Line:I would recommend these for people who print a medium volume of shipping labels and don't want to hassle with glue and scissors.  If you print a lot of labels I would try to find a cheaper source.  I will probably buy some more of these just because they are so easy to use.

Fellowes is known for quality products and the PlushTouch MousePad/Wrist Rest is no exception. This product consists of a mouse pad topped with an attached wrist rest that is easy on the wrist. This helps avoid joint pain. It is treated with Microban protection. This is built in during the manufacturing process to help protect against bacteria, stains and odors.I also appreciate the sleek design - the mouse pad has a slight curve to it fitting the way we move our hand nicely. It is very sticky and stays in place making it perfect for gamers.Overall, a super nice luxury mouse pad/wrist pad at an affordable price!

AVERY Permanent FILE FOLDER Label Pad; 1 Pad; 160 Write-On 1/3 Cut Labels.  That is exactly what you get in this pad of labels. The labels are secured together in a glued pad that stays intact until you tear a sheet of four labels off, or peel off an individual label. They will never scatter about in a desk drawer. They each have a bold strip on the top (or bottom) of each label, there are four distinct color strips: blue, red, green, and, yellow.  They are constructed with solid paper that is smooth enough to look neat, but porous enough to handle any medium. I've tested them with lead pencil, ink pen, sharpie marker, and felt tip marker, and nothing bleeds, smears, or smudges.  All markings show up bright against the stark white background. When stuck to the tab of a typical file folder they are held firmly and it doesn't appear that the edges with eventually curl.I spend a lot of time in my home office, where I manage a business; therefore, I use a great deal of these types of office products. It has been my experience that Avery puts out quality goods that deliver. Yes, you can find similar items that cost less, but there is a standard of quality that you can consistently depend on with Avery products. And this particular item seems to follow that expectation.

So what is there to a moving box? How can you review it? Well basically it is all about how simple they are to construct, how sturdy they are when built and how much space they have in them.These boxes come flat packed so first you have to fold them in the right places to make a box. This process is simple; you just follow the 5 steps which are shown on the bottom of the boxes. Once built, I thought they felt very sturdy. The makers are certainly confident and they say they are suitable for heavier items such as books. I varied what I put in them from books to ornaments and clothes but I thought they did a great job and were also neat looking when I stored them on top of each other. Recommended.....

I bought these with the expectation that I would be able to see the entire Caller ID Name and Number displayed but that is not always the case if the name is longer than the display characters available. That seems to be the case more often than not. I would not buy it again. All the other functions work well however with good range and good sound quality.

Please do be sure to read all the specifications relating to compatibility before buying. If you think you're going to Windows 8 anytime soon, you might move to the next model - and computer deaths are never expected so that might be a worthwhile headsup. Also it claims to be compact but isn't, relative to others on the market although it is compared to the old office behemoths. And do consider cost of print cartridges and whether aftermarket ones can be used (no, as far as I can determine).That said, this combination printer/scanner/copier has been working fine for my limited needs for over a year now. I found it easy to install and that it covers all my basic home chores more than satisfactorily.

The Wilson Jones Pocket Filer is a nice little organizational product.  It is made out of a bendable poly plastic.  More durable than the cardboard kind.  Has 7 pockets with tabs on the top for labeling.  The buckle closure is especially nice, as is the handle for easy carrying.  And who can resist the cute pink color?  I'm glad I got this, I'm getting a lot of use out of it.

When we needed a new All-In-One printer/scanner/fax for our home office, we read hundreds of reviews.  This is a major purchase for us, and something we plan to use for years.  So we didn't want to get a lemon or an ink hog, or something that doesn't make crisp copies.  It seems that for each model of printer, there are some who love it and some who hate it.Eventually we settled on this HP Officejet Pro 8600 because of our prior good experiences with HP products. We set it up and got it to talk to the modem and computers, and we've been very happy with it.  It makes clear, fast copies, scans well, and faxes as expected.  We like the touch screen more than we thought we would.  This is a BIG printer, much larger than the Brother all-in-one we were replacing, but it fits on the printer table.I'll update this review if we have anything good or bad to report.  But for now we're very happy with our purchase.

If you use tape a lot and need quick access to it, this product is for you. It is easy to use and sticks to your desktop and does not shift around when you use it. That a great idea in my book. The tape comes out smoothly and the dispenser removes from the desktop leaving no sticky residue to clean off. It's very handy.

I just got it today, so I can't report on long-term reliability, but this little gizmo really surprised me. First, it's kind of cool looking - obviously much like an apple. But what really surprised me was when I stuck in a stubby pencil and it seemed to stop sharpening after only a second or so. I thought it wasn't working and then I pulled out the pencil and it was done! Perfectly sharp. I tried it with a half a dozen others - man this thing is fast... and makes a very sharp point.Recommended so far!

These are genuine HP 564 XL black cartridges.  They work like all new cartridges work.  I enjoy the print quality I get out of my printer but I figure that's more a printer thing than a cartridge thing.

Usually the bigger cartridges are cheaper per page, but right now on Amazon the smaller one is.At current Amazon prices:LC71BK - 300 pages - $0.026 / pageLC75BK - 600 pages - $0.032 / page (bigger and more epensive per page than LC71BK)Printers that support both the LC71BK & LC75BK:MFC-J280W, MFC-J425W, MFC-J430w, MFC-J435W, MFC-J625DW, MFC-J825DW, MFC-J835DW

The utility of these Avery Notetabs is growing on me.  I first tried the round edge tabs, which were smaller in size and good for a smaller book.The 3" x 1.5" tabs are a heftier size and allow for much more use of the write-on and highlight feature.  There can be a little smudging depending on the writing instrument used.  I find it easier to write on the colored portion than the clear area, but it's nice to be able to write on a page without actually writing on the page.The larger size also give the tabs a larger sticking surface, which actually made me tear a page accidentally upon swiping it in a sudden motion.  I wasn't intending to remove the tab, my hand just hit it.  I do have to be more careful when removing this tab as compared to the smaller tabs.The Notetabs are better for semi-permanent usage.  If you plan to remove them frequently, they will lose their adhesive strength quickly.Whether the paper fibers or ink is picked up by the adhesive depends greatly on the type of paper used.  Cheap paperback paper will not fare well.  It works better on coated paper.I really can turn pages using just the tabs.  I can see this product becoming quite popular as people find more uses for them.  It can be especially handy for students.

I echo many of the positive reviews already submitted (in fact, I purchased it based on the positive reviews).  The phones are comfortable to hold, look good, and are really easy to use and understand.  I really like the answering machine (although many others would have preferred that it tell you how many new messages are waiting for you).  To listen to your messages, just press the menu button and the first option is "Message Play".  This can be done from any of the phones or from the base unit.  There is no number to remember or dialing required (like the answering service provided by the phone company).  The Phone Book automatically updates any new entry to all of the phones.  The sound is clear and the phone has great range. I have a large home and find that the phones are fine anywhere in the house and most of the yard.  There hasn't been any interference yet from any household appliances or electric equipment. One other nice thing is that the batteries appear to be simple AAA Ni-MH rechargeables.  So you could replace them without much trouble if they ever start having trouble holding a charge.

This Canon printer is better than any H.P. printer that have owned and I have been using H.P. since 1984. The quite mode and the auto on/off features are the best. The out-put is excellent, I will not use an outside printing service again!!!

The printer arrived by UPS in a sturdy box, was wrapped in plastic and packed in foam with all movable parts taped down securely. I was impressed with how well it was shipped. The printer is quite large and heavy (about 50lbs) and will take up a bit of room. It requires extra free space in front (10") and behind (17"), so plan accordingly.Using the quick-start guide, setup was fairly straight-forward and took about an hour to complete. Assembling the printer consisted of installing the print head and dropping in the 8 ink cartridges. Cartridges have a color coordinated dot and a symbol to match up on the slot in the print head. When they are locked in correctly a light goes on.Next I installed the software and the print driver. This took about 20 minutes to complete. The software install took a little bit longer than I expected, but wasn't difficult, just follow the on-screen instructions. [An aside: I'm not impressed with the Canon software... all you really need is the print driver to be up and running if you already have photo editing software to use. I have several Canon cameras and another Canon printer and don't like any of their software, but that's my opinion, yours may vary.]I wanted to use the wireless connection with a Dell laptop running XP SP3 and found it to be a little tricky to set up. It took me several attempts to get it to work and finally realized I needed to use the usb cable temporarily so the printer could speak with my laptop and then access my router. Once a connection was established I disconnected the usb cable and it now works flawlessly.After the printer is successfully connected to the computer, the print heads need to be aligned before you can print. Once again, following the onscreen instructions was easy and it took only a few minutes. Now I was ready to print. I use Photoshop Elements 10 to edit and print my photos and the printer worked flawlessly with the software. I used Canon Glossy Photo paper for my test prints and the results were superb. The colors are vibrant and a close match to what I see on the screen. Images were crisp and clear and the printing is fast.I am an amateur nature photographer and take photos for my own enjoyment and occasionally to enter contests. The photo printer I had been using is an old bubble jet. It is past it's prime and no longer produces good quality photo prints so I cannot use it for comparison. Instead I have been using the local Walgreens to do my photo printing and they do a decent job although I prefer having the added control my own printer would provide. The Canon Pro 100 prints are comparable or better than the Walgreens prints.There are a few negatives: Besides being a very large and heavy printer, one must consider the high cost of ink. Currently a set of 8 cartridges runs about $125 plus there is the cost of the paper. Online services are much less expensive for mass printing of holiday and party photos.For amateur and pro photographers who want total control or the ability to print on demand, this is a quality photo printer for at-home printing.

I own several fountain pens and have used them for years, but to be honest, I'm more likely to pick upthis Pilot disposable fountain penthan a Waterman or a Lamy.  Those disposables have been fantastic, and when I saw that Pilot now has a refillable fountain pen, I jumped at it.At usual, Pilot did not let me down.  This pen writes smoothly, with a sharp clear line that never skips.  It comes with a black cartridge, and I've stayed away from black fountain pen ink because I've had problems with it clogging in the past, but that hasn't been a problem with this pen at all.This pen lives in my bag and goes everywhere with me, and even though it gets treatment that's not exactly gentle, it has never leaked.Some friends noticed me using a fountain pen so of course everyone had to try it.  If you've never owned a fountain pen before, you should know that this is generally not a good idea.  The nib of the pen (the part that touches the paper) is a precision part and usually fairly delicate and easy to damage, and once it's damaged the pen is useless.  This pen made the rounds, took abuse from a few people, and was undamaged.  I don't know what metal they're using to make the nib, but I wish they'd make my car out of the same stuff.The pen comes in a surprisingly nice gift box.  I'd have no problem giving one of these as a gift.What it doesn't come with is directions.  But you've got kacunnin's review for that.  ( http://www.amazon.com/review/R2ME4P4IFCRBNO/ )  Follow those instructions to install the ink cartridge and you're good to go.  For me, I just have to remember that the cartridge goes in backwards, or so it seems to me after years of handling Waterman refills.I wish the barrel of the pen were a little more slender, but that's just my personal preference, and it has more to do with the way the pen looks than with the way it fits in my hand.  This pen is perfectly comfortable to hold.  It also has a lizard accent, which is very subtle and pretty much has to be held up to the light to be noticeable.  I also wish the barrel left room for a spare cartridge, but the refills are too large for that.  Not a big deal, if you can remember to take a look at the ink level now and then.I never met a Pilot fountain pen I didn't like.  This pen keeps up the tradition.

Using a fine nib, this ink almost appears black on white paper, but a pronounced green cast on cream paper.  The flow is very nice and dries rapidly.  As far as lower priced inks go, Noodlers is definitely my favorite as it's almost buttery in nicer fountain pens.

My husband and I ran a small business shipping out several packages a day for years, and this dispenser would have been a much welcomed addition when we were at that level. It allows for precise pausing when stretching tape, so we could have used it to adhere both labels and seal the shipping boxes.This also helps eliminate a good bit of time in the shipping process because there are fewer manual tasks. The build quality is nice though it is odd to not have a handle. This doesn't impede function but does take a mental adjustment.

This is the next step in  project folders.  It is similar to the two-pocket folders you may have used for reports in grade school.  Although I wish the paper stock was even sturdier, the new and improved folder features the lock-it at the top of the file.  The beauty of the lockit is you can pop up to 50 sheets of paper in the pockets, fold the lockit half- circle over the top of the papers and all those sheets are secure.  Elegant!  You can also place a business card and CD in the die-cut slots on the pockets.What I dislike is once all your hard work is tucked in the two pockets, it is imposible to page through and read it from within the folder, since there are no center prongs to hold the papers.The price point of ap $1.40 each is a tad high, but within reason.

This Academie Sketch pad is very nice.  The pages are nice and big, 14 x 11 inches.  The texture of the paper is nice, of good quality.  70 sheets is a nice, fat amount.  Great for kids and students, too.  I've even run the pages through my computer to print out art prints.  Came out great.  No smudges at all.  Would make a nice gift, too.
It's a calculator. It does everything a calculator is supposed to do. Hmmmm... it says I need 8 more words to be able to post this. So there ya go!!

I needed a calculator that could replace my simple desk calculator for quick figures at my desk. This one has done very well and seems like it will last some time. I bought Canon as that was my old brand and I like it although since I have large hands I wish it was a tad bit bigger. It was hard to determine which one to get shopping online but I am happy with it. There really is nothing I would like to change on it and will use it for years. Not much else to say as it is a basic calculator.

AFter 3 years our other mat is cracked through and discolored. This one doesnt have one crack. Also, if you use this it has to be on a firm/tight office type carpet for high traffic. If you have any plush carpet it will curl or crack....ours gets used all day and almost every day. I would equate its use to 4 years of office use.....

I used these for a product party.  The guests were able to provide their information in a raffle the consultant was having, and the guest got to keep the consultant's information via the tear off portion which worked well as a business card.The paper is card stock, so it is heavier than normal paper but still easily goes through the printer.  I did what another reviewer suggested, and downloaded the template #15164 from their website, then turned on the gridline function so I could see everything as it was set up.  I had no problems adding a picture and my own text, along with lines for people to fill in their information.Love this and can't wait to find other great uses for these tickets/stubs!

This Mead Academie Sketch Book has several things I really love: 1. The size. 9 x 6 is a perfect size to carry with you; not too big so that it screams "I'm an Artiste," but big enough to get your drawing done with necessary detail. Fits comfortably in a large purse. 2. That it is wirebound so you can flip open the top and get a flat surface. 3: that you have the option to tear out the entire sheet of paper, or just the "neat sheet" perforated part of the paper which is 1/8th of an inch away from the spiral holes. 4. As you open the cover, there is a thick manila insert with a useful pocket on each side (I really like useful pockets).The quality of the paper: 1. It is acid free and lignin free. I had to look up "lignin." It's a chemical they put in paper to make it stronger, but alas, it also breaks down in time...so if you want your work to last, acid free and lignin free is the way to go. 2. I tried several different mediums and they all worked well. I don't have any charcoal or pastel, so could not test those. Pencil, pen and several markers were all excellent.My favorite mode of sketching is with a Waterman pen with a bold gel insert. And I bear down heavily with it. Finding paper that doesn't fall apart on me is a lovely thing, and the reverse side of the drawings I made on this Mead Academie Sketch Book only show slight indentations, so this is strong, heavy paper, even without the lignin! This is a wonderful sketch book, at a very affordable price, and it is also SFI Certified (Sustainable Forestry Initiative) so you know the paper stock has been sustainably harvested.
I love this gel rest!  it's also pretty with my flower pens I kept desktop. only drawback is the kids love to poke it and play with it.

The sizing is a little awkward and I had difficulty running them thru my ink jet at home. I was able to use them with my office printer, but had to make sure I changed all settings to allow for heavy paper and then I fed it one sheet at a time (so it seemed to take forever). I like avery products, because they have templates for free use. I would definitely purchase these again, but use them when I had a specific product in mind (simply because the size is odd and won't fit everything!).

Despite never using a label maker before, I found this one to be easy to use and understand.  When you first turn it on, you can just start typing and hit the print button, and you'll get an auto-sized label with the default full-size sans-serif font in a matter of seconds.  The printing is a bit slower than I would have expected, but nothing to really complain about.The screen is nicely backlit, there are a selection of fonts and modes (vertical text, mirror text for cable flags, etc.) that seem useful, and the installation of label cartridges is simple and tool-free.One area where this label maker failed to impress, however, was print quality.  The labels look pretty strongly aliased (blocky), but what's even more surprising, is how the aliasing looks "wavy" or irregular - like an aliased font viewed through a hot-day-on-an-asphalt-road mirage.  You don't even have to look that closely to see it.  I tried a number of fonts, and they all showed up with a similar graininess.The labels are still perfectly legible, and the convenience is there, but when your product is described as a "Label Printer," it's hard to give high marks to one that prints mediocre labels.One final note, the product description indicates that this label printer has "smaller margins compared to other brands for up to 62% less waste."  I don't know what other brands do, but these margins are around 3/4" -- so there's still a pretty good amount of waste, especially when you want to print cable wrap labels.

I have started to archive family photos from several generations, literally thousands of pictures.I have a high end Canon flatbed scanner, but it was taking me an exorbitant amount of time to scan each photo. Looked at the few bulk photo scanners available, and also picture scanning services, but their high cost was a put-off.I then noticed that sheet feed scanners had the right idea, but the reviews left me with cold feet. So I decided to do a side by side face off between two of the most popular in the $200-300 range: the Epson DS-510 and the Brother ADS-2000.The Brother is bigger than the Epson but not hugely so (see my side by side photo). Both scanners were well boxed. The Epson includes a power cord with a power brick (like a laptop) that supplies 24volts. The Brother has a standard power cord that plugs into its rear panel. Both scanners had the USB cable included.Software load on Windows 8.1: On the Epson, the full software installation went flawlessly. The Brother software required a little more hand-holding, but was still fairly simple for someone with some computer experience. I loaded the full software suites even though I didn't need some of the software (like OCR) for photos.I started testing with the Brother, and noticed that the feed tray seemed to hold the photos weirdly. Instead of the guides having smooth sides, there were protrusions that prevented the photos from lying flat. The feeding was fine, but I was always checking to make sure that they were aligned correctly.  I was pleased that the Brother had a "Photo" setting. The Brother has 600dpi optical resolution, and can interpolate to 1200dpi. The scans in both dpi's I thought were disappointing. The color and saturation were good, but the Brother had a grainy appearance that I couldn't alleviate, even at .75% magnification. I really liked the fact that the Brother has a USB port to allow saving files directly to a USB stick, but was disappointed when the software would only let me save PDFs to the USB stick, not JPGs.The good news is that the Brother was great for what it was designed to do, bulk documents. It was slightly faster than the Epson, didn't jam, and both scanners made great scans of documents.The Epson impressed me at every level. The photos sit in the feed chute perfectly. With a little adjustment of the controls (Contrast -40 and Brightness +30) I was able to get good quality photo scans. And even though only optically 600dpi, the interpolation at 1200dpi produced terrific results. The Epson allows saving to TIFF or JPG photo formats, but the 1200dpi JPG's looked fine (and at a huge reduction in file size).  Scanned 3.5 x 5 photos created huge TIFF files of  77MB, and JPG files of only 8MB. I took the digitized JPG files to CVS and printed them at 4 x 6 and the photos  look great with only a very very slight reduction in quality from the original photo. If you weren't looking for it, you wouldn't notice.Would I recommend the Epson to professionals or super picky photo amateurs? Probably not because the software image editing controls are limited to brightness and contrast, and 1200dpi isn't enough for big enlargements.But for us amateurs who need to get a ton of photos digitized with decent quality, the Epson DS-510 works great for me at a reasonable price.

We've had many shredders in the house and this is comparable to any of those.  For people who appreciate protecting your personal information, having a cross-cut shredder is a must.  As I can personally attest, it is possible to tape together a receipt or other important document that you accidentally shredded in a standard linear shredder.  However this is impossible in a crosscut shredder as the pieces are way too small to do anything with.  It also makes disposal of the shredded paper easier as the smaller shredded pieces pack closer together than the longer strips.As with any cross-cut shredders, it is louder than the normal linear shredder.  Also you will need to periodically oil the cross-cut knives so that fed paper doesn't bind, the shredder doesn't overheat, and just to ensure proper working order.  This is standard with any cross-cut shredder as even the larger office shredders require periodic lubrication.  I can also attest that the shredder cuts right through staples as well as credit cards.As far as price goes, the $29.99 Amazon Basics shredder is somewhere in the middle of all the 6-sheet cross-cut shredders that are offered on Amazon.  There are some shredders that sell for as little as $20 while there are others that sell for more than $40.  To me, all of them seem to have the same functionality although I assume that the lower priced ones shred slower and have cheaper construction.All told, the Amazon Basics 6-sheet Cross-Cut Shredder definitely does what you need it to do.  It has no problem chewing through six sheets at a time and can do it quickly.  Although it is somewhat loud, this comes with having a cross-cut shredder - they are all loud.  Finally the basic construction of the shredder head and the waste basket are more than adequate.  Its a nice unit and I would certainly buy it again.

After having at least 10 HP printers over the years, I finally decided to get a Laser Printer.  I initally shied away from Brother, because formerly they were a low cost and low quality brand. It prints quickly, and after alot of pages (a lot, no idea how many), I have not had a single jam.  Also, the toner has lasted so long.  I bought an extra toner cartridge when I bought the printer, but I havent had to use it yet.  I did get a low toner warning, but I followed directions online (search for it) to reset the count, and I am still using the same toner cartridge more than 1000 pages later!  That would have been like $300 in HP Cartridges!!  That alone means the printer has paid for itself.  It is quick, high quality, and everything I could want in a scanner/printer.My one complaint- and its not really a complaint, is that I have found myself using the scanner way more than I thought.  It is very easy, and so many people want documents scanned and emailed these days.  I wish I had gotten one with a feeder.  They do sell ones with a feeder and next time I will get one.  I recommend it if you can find the version of this printer with a scanner feeder.The software is great.  By great, I mean that I don't know that its there.  HP always installs like 10 programs, that fill up your taskbar and send warnings, notices and ads non-stop.  I don't know why I put up with it.  Brother has software that works great, but quietly sits in the background and just does what its supposed to.  In other words, when I hit print, it prints.  When I hit scan, it scans.  If you want a billion useless features and bundled apps, go with HP.  But I really appreciate that I don't even know anything is installed, unless I go looking for it.  Actually, I love it.  I hope you read this HP.A few other little issues.  The wifi is a little tough to set up, but no harder than any of the other printers I've had.  It is though only 802.11b and g, not N.  The problem with this is that your whole wifi can only go as fast as the slowest item on the network.  Everything else in my house is N, except the printer.  This means that I have to use G internet.  N is the same speed as G, so thats not an issue, but the range is better on N.  If none of this made sense to you, then it very likely doesn't matter to you.  There is no fax.  I dont have a phone line anymore, just cell, anyway.  It would be nice to have a fax at the house, but as I dont have phone service anyway, its moot.  If you do, this would probably be a good feature to have.Everytime I print with this printer, I exclaim to my fiancee that "I love my laser printer"  Seriously. It doesn't have a lot of bells and whistles, but it scans/ copies and prints black and white like a printer 10x the cost.I have been seriously impressed by the value of this Brother printer and cannot recommend it highly enough.  I don't say that often.  I don't write reviews very often either.

The Epson V30 does a nice job of combining an easy-to-use scanner for those who don't want to have to tweak - just scan please! - with a scanner that has the bells and whistles for those who want to do more.I used the scanner to scan photos and documents (as a jpeg and also as a PDF). I did not use the email feature (as it basically uses Outlook and I don't use that email package on my home computer).Photo ScanningI tried the Epson with a variety of photos. Photos consisted of several photos of Bryce Canyon in winter (contrast of snow and colors), your basic Grand Canyon photos, a couple of typical people photos (a couple of people standing in a dark room and also photos where the light was more evenly distributed). I also had some photos that had spots in them (black marks in the sky) to test the dust removal option and an old yellowing photo (40+ years old) of a couple to test the color restoration features.Epson's default mode is Full Auto mode. If you don't have any issues with the photos, don't want to preview them, don't need to change the size and you just want to scan them, use this option. As in all other modes, there's no warm-up needed - photos scan quickly and the Epson does a nice job. By default, all photos are saved in your My Pictures directory. (Select Customize and then select the File Save Settings option to change that - you can also change the default name). You can also use this mode if your photos do have issues (dust marks or need the color restored). Select the Full Auto mode, select Customize, select the options - Dust Removal and/or Color Restoration and even for those photos with issues, you can have the Epson give its best shot.  I used this option with my "problem" photos to see how the Epson would do. I found that the Epson did a decent job - all of my dust "spots" were gone. My yellowing photo was nice and clear - no yellowing, and a crisp clear photo. As far as the color restoration, I'd give it a B+. It did a nice job of removing the yellow tinge that was in the photo, though personally, I would have liked to see more color put in the photo (which I could do myself in the other modes).If you want to do more than just scan in the photo - you want to do some tweaking yourself - use one of the other modes that are provided. Office Mode is for scanning documents and previewing the documents (more on that below). Home Mode allows you to customize the settings and preview the photo. It's a nice in-between option between the Full Auto mode where the scanner does it all and the Professional Mode where you need to figure it out - it gives you the ability to tweak, but doesn't give you so many options that you don't know what to do. Professional Mode on the other hand, gives you total control - you tell it about the original, the destination, and the adjustments you want to make. As someone with little experience in tweaking photos, I found the Home Mode the mode I would use most often. I think the Professional Mode is something I would use only occasionally or after playing with this tool a lot.Scanning documentsI also tried the Epson V30 to scan documents - scanned as jpeg images and also as a PDF. The document was a tax form with my signature on it. I used the Full Auto mode and the Office mode and found in both cases, it was easy and quick to use. Office mode gives you more options - I could tell the scanner the resolution, orientation, and make any adjustments to the image. I could also use Full Auto mode to create the PDF. Very easy.ArcSoft MediaImpression came with the Epson scanner. It's another tool that (among other things) allows you to tweak your photos after you've scanned them. It works with "all media files" though I only used it for my scanned photos. It's a photo tool which you can also use to email and archive items. It's a pretty basic tool that's easy to use. A nice addition to the scanner.Documentation that comes along with the product consists of a Quick Start page (English, Spanish, and French versions) and an online User Guide. All were well written and helped me to use the product.All in all, I recommend the Epson scanner if you want to quickly and easily scan your photos and documents. I like how you can have the scanner do it all, or when you're ready, have the ability to tweak it yourself. Nicely done!

I've been using Scotch Gift Wrap Tape for years and there is nothing better. Cheaper tape can be fine for general purpose taping (although I still prefer 3M products), but for gift-wrapping, quality is a must. This tape dispenses evenly and easily, cuts cleanly, applies easily, and is truly nearly invisible once applied. The tape holds well as long as stress is lateral to the tape. When the stress is perpendicular to the tape, it sometimes lifts. This is rarely the case when gift-wrapping. I think it is slightly less tacky than general-purpose tape. Sometimes you can lift it off if you make a mistake, but gift-wrap paper tends to be unforgiving. Because it is nearly invisible when applied, it is often best to cut the seam and leave the tape on the paper if you make a mistake. It is not noticeable. There is not must else to say about tape.

The ink cartridges could last a bit longer, but being able to fax, print, scan, copy and use the cloud with this printer is the bomb.  For the money, it's hard to beat this little gem. I liked this staple gun right out of the box.  With the exception of the staples it was ready to go to work. The edges are not anymore durable and have since collapsed.Recommend if you need a binder but it is necessary to understand that the edges will collapse on you and you will become agitated each and every moment you need to slowly feed all the paper to the right of the D-ring so that they will lay flat.  Impressed with the easy one handed operation... but that is all.

I use these laminating labels all the time to laminate everything from small cards such as a copy of my auto insurance, AAA card, phone list I keep in my wallet to full sheets of instructions and the like that I want to keep around with damaging.

I have been looking at this printer for some time, and finally had the opportunity to evaluate one, thanks to a client who provided me a new i9900 to print several architectural photos for a Home Show display. The photos were stunning and attracted a lot of attention. I had no problem with color shifts, having calibrated my monitor and used the Canon print drivers. I used a Mac G5 and Photoshop Elements. I printed approximately 55 - 8.5 x 11 (cropped to 7 x 10.5) and 32 - 13 x 19 photos. This calculates to approx 83 sq feet of photos. I used Canon inks and Canon Photo Paper Plus Glossy. Here are the stats for the ink usage for this project:Photo Magenta 4 cartridgesPhoto Cyan  3Yellow  2Cyan  1Magenta  1Black  1Red  2/3Green  1/4So ~ 13 cartridges of ink were needed to print 83 sq ft of photos. Assuming a cost of $12/cartridge, this means $156 to print 83 sq ft, or 12000 sq in. This is about 1.3 cents (.013) per square inch. So ink costs for an 8 X 10 would be $1.04, for a 13 x 19, $3.21.Now, the part that intrigued me, how would this printer perform printing black and white? For my source I used a 2 1/4 monochrome negative that I scanned. I imported the scan into Photoshop in grayscale mode. A direct print to 8.5 x 11 Kodak Ultima High Gloss looked quite good as far as color (compared to my darkroom print). However, I don't recommend this paper with this printer since the ink will smear if water contacts it. I tried printing the same negative on Canon Photo Paper Plus and was disappointed to find that the print was tinged with green. So I began checking the print settings and here is how to correct it so the green tinge disappears. Under Color Options, make sure Color Corrections is set to ColorSync (for Macs), or None. Under Quality and Media, make sure the Grayscale box is off (unchecked). Of course make sure the media type matches the paper you're printing on. This seems to make all the difference.Now the amazing discovery....I was checking to see how water-impermeable the Canon paper/ink combination was, so I used one of the green-tinged prints for my test. I found that by wiping the print with a damp soft cloth, the green tinge disappeared and a beautiful, neutral black and white print appeared!!!I'm not sure what is happening here, since if I wipe a color print on Canon paper, no smearing or color change is observed. I would be interested to know if those who have found magenta tints on their prints can wipe them and observe this.I have had excellent results using Konica Premium Silky paper with this printer (no smearing).The only problem I observed, was that when printing multiple 13 x 19 photos, I saw a small smudge of black ink in the upper left hand corner on some prints. This disappeared when I took a break and resumed printing.This is a class-act printer. Very quiet, and fast (compared to Epson). I will be buying one shortly, although I see that Canon may introduce some new printers this Fall with large format capabilities and new ink systems. I may just a while longer ....

These are NOT just for retail...although they are certainly great for store shelves. Anyone who likes to organize, lives with a room-mate, or has a loved one with dementia could really use these.Sadly, many people in my age group have parents with issues, and these are perfect for kitchen and bath shelves as reminder tabs. MUCH better than the post-it's most people use for that purpose. I have one in the refrigerator and it holds in there beautifully, without leaving residue when repositioned. That makes it a must for reminding a roomie that items on that shelf are not to be touched, or a reminder that kids better not touch the cake meant for later.These have a peel off section with just enough room to make it very easy to quickly remove even with short nails, no fuss in that department. Nicely made and a reasonable price for a multitasking product.

The problem I see is that they are not really secure. The "tape" does not extend to the edges and, even more problematic, they are, once sealed, easily opened and resealed with no indication they've been tampered with.  The "spit on the glue then seal" type are far more secure (to me).

So I just happen to be a stay at home mom who meal plans and likes to use lists just like this. Despite being called "OrganizeHER", men can still use it. Let's not be silly. My husband uses this when he makes a trip to the store too, he's never been insulted by the name...of a notepad...ain't nobody got time for that.This is a very thick shopping list with items to check off on the right, meal planning weekly calendar on the left. You get what you see in the photo. The pad is heavy when it's new and unused, but the multiple magnets attached are plenty strong to keep it stuck to your refrigerator.It's just fine, my only small complaint is that the grocery items listed are not nearly as thorough and complete as my other pad, "ALL OUT OF" by Knock Knock. These are standard run of the mill index cards. A bit on the flimsy side as far as the paper stock. They are nice to write on but due to the thin stock I don't think these would be the best for things like recipes where you want to handle them repeatedly over years. Better for short term projects.
This is a dual sided scotch tape, small size and serves its purpose for art and decor work. It is simple and does its job very well.

I use several brown expansion file folder each day for various on the go projects.  This nifty box set up in less than a blink of an eye.  I slipped 2 of my expansion folders in this box and viola, it holds both easy with room to spare.  Now I can easy grab these and go.  Its sturdy and looks much neater sitting on my desk.The price is the only drawback for me.  At the time of this review, these retail for $9.99 each.  Its simply too much for a single box.  I'd like additional boxes in various colors, however the price has stopped me from ordering additional boxes.  I'll keep them on my watch list, just in case the price drops.

This is the perfect size for the front of our fridge.  The magnets work great and hold the board up well.  It's easy to write on (with the included dry-erase marker) and wipes/erases quickly.It comes with 2 small, round magnets so we can post papers on it, too.  Works great.
Not a lot to say about tabbed folders. These will last forever, and I like the bigger tabs for easy reference.

This Scotch mounting tape is sticky enough to hold heavier items, but it also removes easily without taking the finish with it. For heavier items, I put more on the back of the wall hanging, or object, and on lighter items I use less. Also, it really sticks to ceramic, even if it has a glossy glaze! Some mounting tape is not gonna stick to slick surfaces no matter how much you use, but with this product, only one two-inch strip firmly held tiles I mounted above our cooktop. Midstream, I decided I wanted the tiles in a different arrangement, and it was easy to lift them off the wall, without tearing the paint, and move them. (I think when dry, and "set" they might not be so easy to move, because the tape is so sticky, so we'll see.) Excellent, effective, and easy to use product! Recommended.

A girl who has a pink floral skin and a pink leather case for her Kindle NEEDS a pink charger cable as well.  The Belkin Mixit Charge/Sync Cable fits and charges my Kindle like a dream; I only wish the pink wasn't quite so bright.  It is a much more fluorescent looking pink than the photo on-line would lead one to believe.  As an added bonus, the micro-USB port also fits my phone.  My husband has a habit of absconding with my phone chargers, but I seriously doubt he's going to take a bright pink charger cable either by accident or on purpose.  It would be nice if it came with a wall charger as well, but for whatever reason (I've never claimed to be high-tech) this no longer seems the trend.

The Bible cautions against serving two masters, a lesson of truth the product designers of HP have tried to avoid with some but not complete success.First the good news, the printing function is outstanding. Copies in black and white or color  are crisp and clear. HP claims that this printer's cost per copy for color copies is less than those of a color laser printer. Absent a cost/benefit study few working lawyers are prepared to do, I cannot confirm this, but it seems possible.On the copy side, two-sided color copying is a great feature. Again the results are superb, but the scanning/printing time is slow.The scan quality is very good, but scanning times are totally unacceptable. When you have a fifty page document feeder, the expectation is that the scan will be fairly quick. It is not. It is somewhat less than a page per minute but that means nearly 45 minutes to scan a document into a pdf. Scanning for OCR is faster, and the resulting test is quite accurate, but whether that is a function of the scanner or sophistication of the user's OCR software cannot stated with any certainty by this reviewer.The Printer has fax functions, but they have not been reviewed since it has not been connected to a telephone line.It has been tested as a wireless device, however, using the built-in 802.11g communicator. Wireless printing has many practical advantages, not the least of which is the elimination of ugly wiring. One other obvious advantage is that multiple computers can use the device as a network printer.While it is not a perfect device, it represents great value for the money. It performs near the top of the class on most functions. That makes it a clear best buy in my book.

Very dark black, goes on smoothly, nice grip, etc. I have noticed that depending on the angle you hold it either too much or not enough ink comes out. So you do need to adjust how you write a bit. Not that big of a deal though.

I bought this to be used for working on a notebook computer while on the couch. I had tried other things like the Table Mate II but wanted this because of the style and looks. It took about 10 minutes to get it adjusted correctly, not very hard, but it is trial and error. Once done, it fits my needs very well. My only complaint is that is is very light weight and wobbles a bit, but not enought to make it a bad purchase. It looks great and is well made however and you can adjust it to many heights and angles.

These tape dispensers are perhaps intended for the "serious" wrapper - someone who feels naked without scissors in their hand and, uh, tape on their wrist.  Firstly, I must say that the tape in these little dispensers is just fine.  It's good quality Scotch tape and will surely not disappoint, although it's not as invisible as their fancy wrapping tape.  The length that the dispensers release is reasonable-- a little too much if you're already good at wrapping presents but enough to make up for your lacks if you aren't.The desk-top pop up dispenser is an interesting little thing.  It's not too ugly (although for utility I still prefer old-fashioned weighted tape dispensers with teeth!) and the friction mount works *fairly* well.  When I wrapped on the floor, it worked not at all on the slightly uneven hardwood.  I imagine it is perfectly useless on carpet.  Which is probably where the wrist mounted dispenser comes in!  I disliked these gadgets, because although one of them snapped apart easily the other one seems to have some kind of molding flaw and so I had great difficulty getting the tongue to snap in and out of the groove.  I also don't like having a large bulky plastic doo-dad attached to my wrist, it bumps against things and annoys me.  On the other hand, it does save the tape from getting lost and stuck to the floor like it does tend to do with traditional dispensers.Over all I'd rate these items at four stars.  They're fun, but I wouldn't invest too much in them, since they're disposable and the wrapping experience isn't really leaps and bounds over the one you'd have with a plain old roll of tape.

However, my testing shows that for most photos, I actually prefer the output of this Matte Photo Paper.  I found that the color of most objects and people looks more natural with the matte paper.  Best of all, this paper is less than 25% the cost of the Photo Paper Pro on a per sheet basis.  If you're using one of the Canon photo printers, you definitely need to try this paper out.  I think you'll find the output excellent and the value outstanding.

I couldn't be happier with this printer! It does an incredible job printing all forms of documents and photos. I mainly print high resolution photos off of this machine and it does an amazing job. The ink refills are cheap and don't listen to others because the ink lasts a LONG time! People who say this printer goes through ink fast much have a little gnome drinking it while they sleep. I have printed eight 8 x 10 photos in the best quality color and my ink has only gone down about 3-4% all around. And that is with the ink that came with the machine. Which by the way is a full set of cartridges, not half filled demo's like other brands.Overall I highly recommend this product. The features are amazing and fun. As well it has wireless with ePrint technology, so no matter where you are in the world, you just email a document or picture to the printers email address and it will print your project so it is waiting for you at home.I have ZERO cons for this printer. In the 80s and early 90s, there were 4 color pens made by Bic, Pentech and other brands.  Bic had the regular blue, black, red and green inks, while Pentech had the fun colors-pink, purple, green, and turquoise in one, and teal, burgundy, orange, and green-blue in another.  They were called Fireworks pens and I remember how much fun they were to collect.  I remember picking out a few packages in stores with my mom.  I used them to write letters, draw, and even do schoolwork with (when it was allowed-not all teachers liked colorful ink).  I usually used the green ink for school because it was my least favorite color and saved the better ones for my letters.  My cousin had them too, and we wrote many letters using our pens.  I loved the vibrant colors and clicking the various switches to alternate inks.  As you can see I have a lot of memories attached to these pens.  I still have the pens, whether they write or not, as a keepsake from childhood.  I loved them and was sad when they were discontinued.  Bic continued to make the regular colors, but I missed the fun.Now they have the Fashion Colors pen.  This has pink, purple, teal blue and green ink, similar to the Shimmers pens.  Like the Shimmers, the green ink is very light, purple is good; but they've made a couple of nice changes.  Pink is a darker shade than in previous Bic pens.  It's bolder and I like it a lot.  The blue is more teal rather than the usual turquoise.  The 2-pack I opened had a difference in writing though--one writes really great and the other skips a little.  It's not a dud, just not as good.The better one writes really smooth and doesn't leave ink blobs on the paper.  Overall, the pink and blue write better than the Shimmers.  I like having 4 colors in one retractable pen, easy to change with the click of a switch.  The regular colors are refillable, but I don't think these are.  It would be nice if they were.  The barrel of the pen is comfortable to hold, and comes in half white and half green-a nice shade of lime green.  Also good is that they are made in France, not China or Mexico.As soon as I started using one of these, a flood of memories came back.  Now with the internet and everyone e-mailing, the art of writing a letter is pretty much gone save for a few individuals who keep it up.  Using this pen made me wish I still had a pen pal like I did as a child.  The memories alone were worth the purchase.  But it is a good, sturdy pen for everyday use.  I carry one in my purse for taking notes.If you remember using the 4-in-one pens in the 80s, this is a nice blast from the past.  Also convenient if you like to use colored inks and want to carry just one pen around.  5 stars all the way, just wish they came in a 5 pack.

I've never owned a laminator so I don't have another one to compare with this one but I can tell you this one works great! I had a collection of newspaper articles that I wanted to preserve and the laminator handled the job smooth as silk. The pages look so neat collected in a notebook. I ordered the "pouches" from Amazon and they cost about 13 cents each. Warms up quickly and does a perfect job. The laminator look very attractive stored on a shelf with it's cord wrapped underneath and the feeder tray stored. I knocked off one star because when I compared this laminator with others close to this price it seems all of the more expensive laminators are capable of taking 12 to 18 inch wide items not just nine inch max.

Wilson Jones makes all kinds of stationary products.  This transparent divider set is very handy.  The tabs are extra wide so you have lots of room to write on.  I really like the larger sized tabs because it makes it easier to go right to the section I'm looking for.
It's a staple remover. It removes staples. Nicely made materials, holds up well. I have two of them. What more can I say?

This laminator is perfect for anyone who needs to laminate things for home or personal use. I don't know if this would hold up to heavy duty, everyday use, but for occasional use in the home, it's fabulous. I keep looking for more things to laminate! It's so easy and fun to use!!

I am a homeschool teacher and Educational Therapist so I use a three-hole punch quite often. My old one is heavy, takes up a lot of space, gets clogged easily so little paper circles spill all over the floor, and it jams if more than 4 pages are put in at once. I would have to press hard to make sure all 3 holes punched. I disliked the amount of space and effort that old dinosaur required when it could only punch a few pages at a time.My new little Paper Pro 3-hole punch is a delight. It is lightweight. It crisply and cleanly punches through up to 12 pages (depending on paper type) with very little pressure. The footprint is smaller than my old one, taking up only as much space as necessary, and the smooth, rounded shape is comfortable in the hand. It's easy enough for my kids to use without a struggle. The base is plastic and a bit thin; I hope it will hold up and since it;s not a moving part it should be fine. I am very pleased with this product.

I have had many printers since the Apple II era, and one thing that has always annoyed me is the claim of the manufacturers of how many copies per minute it will produce. Reading that this printer would produce 6.2 per minute was a "ho hum" statement to me because I no longer believed those types of claims ---- Until I tried it. It felt really cool seeing it spit out those copies. I actually expected to see only part of the document completed, it was going so fast. My Epson CX4800 served me well for 4 years. I think it probably produced 1 copy per minute, once it got started printing. I'd press the print button and sit and wait for a minute or so for it to get ready to print. It was at least a 2 minute process to get a copy out of it. When it would no longer print any colors any more, who knows why, I said "Time for a new one."I expected a bit of time getting the NX430 connected to my WiFi, but it was simple. It located and locked on to my home network in less than 30 seconds. I spent less than 1/2 hour, once it was unpacked, getting it up and ready to go. The hardest part of it was finding and removing all the tape that is put on these things to keep them from rattleing around while shipping, and that really wasn't all that hard to do by the way.The first thing I do before buying something is to look for any reviews of the item that are available online. Then I read the reviews and throw out all the stupid stuff that people complain about. "It clashes with my fingernail polish". "They said it was SO small, and it's only 3 inches smaller than my previous one". "I was hoping it would have a speaker system for my IPOD", and other nonsence crap.  No difference with printers, and I liked most of the reviews I read about the NX430. My second requirement, specifically when buying a new printer, is to find out how much I'm going to be spending on ink. It's pretty obvious that the cost of the ink is the reason they can sell some of the printers at the prices they do. Ticks me off. Having said that, I found the price of the cartridges for this device OK. Then I found the refillable versions and was very pleased. It's kind of like the difference between when I went from print photography to Digital. With digital I could then take thousands of photos because it didn't cost me. With print photography I would spend time looking at the scene to see if it was worth taking a photo of or not. With this printer and refilable cartridges I won't spend much time deciding if I need a printed copy or not. The only question will be do I want a printed copy or not.I can't speak to how long this printer will last. I haven't had it long enough to know. I've read some reviews that expressed concern about the durability of the plastic case. I'm using it as a printer, not a football. It sits on my desk and prints. My cats are the only ones walking on it. I don't ask it to do anything that will require me to hit it or drop it on the floor. The plastic case is fine.I probably won't use it much for printing photos but it does a wonderful job of doing that even on regular letter paper. I'll probably still go to my local Walmart and print my digital photos there. Everything else that it does, works great.
Very good!  Works great, easily cuts off tape, nice and light.  I do a lot of online shopping, and a lot of returns.  This came in handy, and I'd buy again once it runs out.

I use 3 and 4 inch binders for storing class materials- I take a ton of online art classes, and we tend to get a tremendous amount of materials for the course. I usually get the regular Avery black binders, but decided to give the Wilson Jones brand a try.First, and foremost, the binder seems HUGE. I don't know why it seems larger than the Avery ones, but it holds a TON of paper. I was able to get a whole year of course materials into one binder without an issue.The D-Ring binding is great- easy to open and close, doesn't snag, and the pages turn easily.I love that the covers are so easy to customize, as well- I just stuck some printed paper in there and all the sudden a very plain binder looks like a designer notebook. Much nicer than leaving them blank, and easy to individualize to match whatever organizing system you have going on with your books.I would debate the description of "Heavy Duty"- when opened and closed, the binder covers flap around a little bit. I think with regular use and strain over a long period, the cover would tear at the seams. It's kind of thin and flimsy at the folds, unlike the Avery binders, which are reinforced and stand up to repeated opening and closing and being shifted in my bag on on the book shelf.All in all, it's a good binder and it serves its purpose well. Recommended.

The Avery Pocket Tabs 5-pack, made for CDs, are excellent. You have storage and tab all in one! I love Sharpie markers. I use them for everything from labeling to doodling. So I expected to love these brush tip markers, too. (Hooray for line variation!) However, having used these markers, I've had to scale back my expectations.As with my pen reviews, I'll look at some various angles: comfort, ink quality, and the nib.COMFORTMost striking with these markers is the deviation from the traditional and familiar Sharpie design. This marker features a thicker barrel with shorter grip, which for me is quite comfy, and it feels as though I have great control over the line. The downside, however, of this shorter grip is that significantly more ink ended up on my fingers and on the interior of the cap (which then transferred to the end of the marker when posting the cap) when removing the cap even when being mindful. Not a big issue, but annoying.INKThe ink is par for course and if you've ever used a Sharpie marker before you'll know what to expect. The colours are vibrant and saturated, though are a touch darker than their cap indicates. (And I still find it irksome that they don't put the ink colour names on the barrel, or even on the packaging, though this didn't factor into my overall rating.)On plastic--think totes and such--don't expect true permanence. The ink will chip and flake after several hours, or in some cases can be wiped off easily using one's finger or a touch of rubbing alcohol. Spot test on any plastic on which you intend to use these markers. The ink stayed permanent on various metals, but others had a similar experience to the plastic. Another spot test situation.When it comes to labeling CDs or DVDs, the markers went on smoothly and stayed on, as expected.  Great on other solid, yet slightly porous surfaces, such as ceramics. (If using these markers on coated ceramics, however, you'll need to finish up with another clear coat to ensure the ink doesn't wash away.)As far as paper, especially the thinner or basic quality varieties, expect feathering and bleeding. The feathering is more pronounced when pressing hard for a wider line, but that would be venturing into nib territory. These markers play best with thick or quality art papers (think watercolour, mixed media, or acrylic paper).NIBOK. The brush tip. That's this marker's claim to fame, and I was definitely eager to test that claim.  Let me say first off that if you are expecting a Pentel, PITT, or Sakura level brush tip (or even a brush tip with actual bristles), you will make all sorts of sad faces. And after you've lowered your expectations, you should lower it a smidge more to ensure satisfaction.Straight out of the pack I expected each marker to have a nice tight brush that would produce rich thin lines, on par with the ULTRA FINE POINT Sharpie, but could only say that of three colours. In fact, the finest line on some of the colours was barely comparable to the line of a FINE POINT Sharpie.If you aren't looking for such fine lines (which actually aren't all that fine in the grand scheme of things), then the above shouldn't be a problem, plus these pens can produce some fantastic fat lines. But there's a trade-off.Fat lines mean hyper-saturation of ink in the paper, and depending on the paper, it could mean hyper-feathering. Depending on the work, this feathering might be considered unpleasant. And if you do a lot of shading or blocking in of colours, forget about getting a semi-thin line again.The brush snapped back well after the first few uses, and then started showing its age (too soon if you ask me). Can't say I didn't expect it to some level, but I did wish the brush tips could have held up better than they did, especially considering I'm not very abusive of my art pens or markers.Overall these are good markers, but I wouldn't retire the ULTRA FINE or FINE POINT Sharpies just yet. These are probably best if you plan to decorate more than pages in a sketchbook, or if you draw big and want some basic line variation. Otherwise it might be better to invest in some quality brush tip art markers.

If your printer requires #96 cartridges, this twin pack is the pack to purchase. They offer maximum printing capacity and good reliable printing. These HP cartridges rarely clog, they avoid the dreaded ink wasting clean cycles.I've had two HP printers over the past four years that both used this cartridge, and have had no problems with printing using HP cartridges. I get a decent page count out of this printer, about six months worth of printing. I print something at least once per day, so the cartridges don't sit idle for days on end.If I'm not in a hurry and printing on inexpensive paper, I usually ignore the flashing front panel low ink lights and wait until the one of the colors doesn't print anymore. This maximizes ink usage from these cartridges. If the printer stops printing because the lights are on solid or the software refuses to print, simply remove both cartridges and return them to the printer - you've now reset the ink level sensor and can wait until they stop printing.I always like to have a spare cartridge on hand, not because they have little printing capacity, but because I never like to be caught with my pants down and no ink to print.Compared to Lexmark, HP ink is less expensive. I think HP and Epson are pretty well matched on ink cost.

I ordered the HP LaserJet Pro P1102w Printer (CE657A#BGJ) for our office. The primary users of this are our company owner and the employee who assists him with billing. The purpose of this printer was to be able to have one closer to her desk so she doesn't have to walk across the building every time she prints an invoice, and also to prevent both of their print jobs from being held up by print jobs by the rest of the team upstairs.This little printer does just the trick. It is nice an small, so it fits well in the limited space we have in the reception area, but it is powerful enough it prints all of their documents quickly and well.Set up was easy. The software walks you through configuring it for your wireless network, and I had no issues installing it on the Windows PCs we needed it on. After the printer is configured, users can easily install the printer on their desktops by pointing their web browser to the IP address for the printer, and using the install wizard there.The boss also has a MAC computer and an iPad and has been able to configure both to print to this printer using Airprint.
