Bottom line: Very pricy, but if you need to deal with lots of paper, this scanner is a joy to use. Wonderful paper handling, speedy, compact and easy to use.Full review: I have to deal with mountains of paper for work, and much of it needs to be scanned for usage and archiving. My workhorse so far has been an Epson Workforce Pro GTS-50 and have been generally pleased with it. But, I'm always looking for something that will help streamline the workflow for scanning. I tried the Brother ADS2500W, which was a big disappointment in terms of paper handling capabilities.The Kodak i2800, however, is impressive. Really impressive. As you would expect at this price point, it hits all the usual check boxes of a higher-end scanner (such as TWAIN compatible, one-touch keys that can be mapped to specific scan parameters, duplex scanning, compact footprint, etc.) and accomplishes it in a straightforward, easy-to-use manner.But what I was most impressed with was the paper handling. That's where scanners often fall short, and, for me, is what makes me frustrated using them.It has a 100-sheet capacity feeder that does take 100 sheets (sometimes manufacturers inflate the capacity a bit). I started with my usual big stack of 20# paper, single sided, B/W scanned at 300dpi to a PDF. Took the stack without a problem, and did so VERY quickly. I then put in some crinkled pages. No problem. Put in some pages that were de-stapled. No problem. Dog-eared pages. No problem. It then became an office game of "who can jam the scanner?" The scanner won. This puppy can pull paper!Image quality is great, and the included software has all the usual image tweaks. I had no problems generating sharp B/W scans even with color input images and colored paper. To be clear, however, I don't put much demand on scanners with regard to image detail since I rarely scan above 300dpi. Still, the Kodak seems to have no problems producing scans at far higher resolutions than I use in the office.It has the typical fold-up configuration which is nice for minimizing the footprint and keeping the trays safe when not in use. It is more bulky than the Epson Workforce, but I'd still characterize it as compact. Straightforward install via a USB cable.The build quality appears to be solid, although I would have liked to see beefier input and output trays. It would also be nice to have a better display screen (the one feature that impressed me with the Brother). The screen it has is clear and usable, but a better one seems warranted at this price.The only notable downside is the price. It's expensive. This scanner is overkill for a small office with limited scanning needs (and certainly not at all appropriate for home use). If you're scanning less than 1,000 pages a month, or mainly deal with small batches, I'd suggest the Epson or the Fujitsu line of scanners. Their mid-range models are excellent values. But, if you have more demanding needs in terms of volume, take a hard look at the Kodak. While the price will sting, it streamlines the scanning workflow so much that I consider it to be cost effective.Highly recommend!

I bought this sharpener after much research and debate, I was a little nervous and didn't want to spend $25 on something that wouldn't work. HOWEVER; we were blown away.There is a trick to using it, I'm not sure everyone figured out due to the lack of directions, you squeeze the two black buttons together and pull the silver part all the way out, you then squeeze the black button that moves and put your pencil all the way into the sharpener, It is now latched in, Holding the sharpener firmly with one hand and the handle in the other (the latch holds your pencil) Start sharpening when you feel the resistance stop, then stop sharpening it means you're done, Squeeze the black buttons together again and take our your perfectly sharpened pencil. I was mainly using Dixon Ticonderoga 13872 Woodcase Pencil, HB #2, Yellow Barrel, 96 per Pack, the kids sharpened all 96 pencils without an issue, we then went in a search for more pencils, it even sharpened the junk pencils I normally throw away, then my daughters went crazy and searched down even the colored pencils. Everything sharpened perfectly!I think the bad reviews on this product are due to people not understanding about the "pull out, stabilizer" feature of the sharpener, if you just start sharpening without pulling out the stabilizer it is not going to work well.I have not found a reason to use the clamp yet, mainly because I don't know where I would put it.I think I may have found the perfect teachers gift for this Christmas!

Trained as a "close reader" I can hardly read an ordinary magazine without pen in hand (I hate graphite pencils).  I underline and annotate liberally, making it practically essential that I acquire my own texts rather than use library books or borrowed copies.  Unfortunately, by the time I'm through with a book, its value is considerably diminished by all the markings and other traces of the reader's activity (sometimes I can't read the text myself because of all the notes I've written between lines and in the margins).  I wasn't even interested in a Kindle until learning about the possibilities it offers the reader for providing annotations to the electronic text.Still, most of my reading is of new, hard-copy, old-fashioned texts, books moreover that it's advisable for more than cosmetic reasons not to write all over.  The Avery NoteTabs represent the best solution, or compromise, that I've discovered to date.  Unlike opaque stickers they permit you to write your own notes on the tab or to underline the underlying text that shows through each of the tabs without physically defacing or altering the text itself.  And they don't curl up and slip off the page--thanks to the plastic-like, fairly stiff make-up of the tabs.Consider the Avery NoteTabs an ideal compromise between writing directly on the text and covering it with loosely adhering pieces of paper.  It's particularly valuable to close readers of hard copy, especially those who are as inclined as I to reach for their pens at the first sign of an idea or detail that begs for commitment to memory and later reflection.  Of all the Avery products I've seen thus far, this is the most innovative--and my favorite.

Think of the Post-it Super Sticky Removeable Label roll as one of those odd, middle-of-the-road kind of products that at first you're not sure how it's supposed to be used. That's actually a good thing, because once you start using it, you realize that there are a ton of uses. I've used them to label food in plastic containers in the fridge, on computers, to mark something in a book, to leave myself a note on the computer monitor, to leave someone else a note on a package, to put a quick note on a stack of papers, etc. Basically, if something needs to be labelled with a quick note or other blurb of information, you can use this to do it.The labels themself come on a roll and you basically use it like a roll of tape. Pull the length of product you want to use, then rip it off on the serrated cutting edge. That's really about it. There are no set label lengths and using it is no harder than using a roll of tape. The labels are very sticky and stay on, but when it's time to remove them, doing so is very easy, without any kind of residue. They'll also stick to just about any clean surface. It's great for any quick, impromptu labelling instance that could come up.If there is any con to this product, it's that the way the serrated egde cuts them leaves them looking jagged. While this isn't a big deal when it comes to the way this product is likely to be used, it does kind of limit it if you're wanting something clean or professional-looking (which isn't really happening here anyways since there's no way to print on it). That's a minor quibble (almost have to be looking for something to dislike to cite that). This is a product with a wide application of uses, and good to have around when a situation calls for it. You might initially think that it's a limited product, but once you start using it you realize just how flexible a product it is by how many different ways you'll actually make use of it. The Removeable Label Roll really is a nice product, once you give it a chance.

Once placed on the side of my fridge, it couldn't be repositioned by sliding; I had to lift it off and place it again. This assures me that no matter how many items I load it down with, it's not going to slip or fall off. I'm using it for pens and a calculator, but it holds strongly enough that I wouldn't be afraid to use it for things like small scissors or screwdrivers.

I have found this little holder to be helpful. It is handy and attractive, but a bit difficult to install.Pro:- Looks nice, holds a standard sticky note (3" x 3").- Mounts easily to a wall or filing cabinet.- Easy to remove notes. Stays securely put in place.- Handy pen holder works well.- Can be removed.Con:- Cannot be used with standard cubical material - it has to be a hard surface to mount. This may be an issue for many corporate environments, although generally there may be mounting possibilities on the cabinets. I think (but did not check - I don't have a cubical) that the glue is strong enough to hold when mounted on the underside of an upper cabinet, although of course one could not use the pen holder.- The instructions are a bit difficult to read; they are small, and printed on the inside of the packaging. I managed to tear it apart and had to read across the tear. Not a big deal. The holder mounts with four glue backed velcro type strips (although they aren't technically velcro - the strips are all the same - they work the same way. I was a bit taken aback when the instructions said to apply the strips first, then press it to the wall, then remove the device to press the mounting strips to the wall. I expected the wall side to pull away, but it worked. Anyway, be prepared for a couple of minutes of very fine print reading!Overall, if you need more desk space and there is a free vertical wall or filing cabinet nearby, this works well. Recommended.

Easy to use and well built.  This thing is built like a tank.  Weighs about 40 pounds.  The lock is well designed and the box closes and opens easily.  Will it keep your papers safe in a fire?  I'd have to burn my house down to find out for sure and I'm not going to do that.  But it looks likely that it will do the job as long as you put the documents in a watertight container inside the box.  In a fire, the gypsum that lines the box will likely wet whatever is inside (gypsum is a calcium sulfate that contains water).  It's not for use for jewelery and photos, just documents.

My husband has a ton of meetings at work and he has found this notebook useful to jot down notes. It's nice to have the date the meeting occurred, main topic of discussion at the top and bullet points below (with enough room for elaboration) of things discussed. And since his notes are all in one place, they're easy to locate later when he wants to refer back to them.True, a regular notebook can just as easily fill this role however this looks a touch more professional, which is why my husband decided to use it at work.

The only thing wrong is that the pen is nearly dry. I will have to get another.I like the size, which is perfect for the fridge and shopping lists, the silver is interesting, gives it a different look, maybe to go with your brushed aluminum fridge, it looks great with my white one. Personally for me, the silver is the selling point as the pen is cheap and near dry and the size is big enough that I can put large notes to catch our (old) eyes across the room.

As a 20 year teaching vet,I would say this book is definitely targeted for the correct age group.It gives starter ideas to get the kids thinking on their own, a very important aspect in drawing out creativity.The book begins somewhat easy and progresses from their to more thought provoking "idea starters", as I call them.All in all this is a fine book and will begin the majority of children on  a quest to see things differently or more observantly with more attention to detail.My only concern would be it would not be  challenging to a naturally creative thinker, but on the other hand the "natural' can usually make a 'LOST"  outof playing with a leaf by any body of water (puddles included).So I would say worth the cost to try. Who would not benefit from being challenged to be observant and to think beyond the obvious???Homeschoolers will find it very useful since you have children with differing talents and thought processing. It can be re- used over and over by not writing IN it buton a seperate sheet of paper. If only one child, think re-sale at HS book fair !

These 2 5/8 x 3 1/4 labels are rather small to use for a shipping label.  I don't think a UPS or FedEx driver would appreciate having  this type of label to read.  I could be wrong but I don't think UPS or FedEx would accept this type of label.  USPS may not accept this label either. The From and To should be separated.  The label is too small in size to put on a package.  I wouldn't use these labels on a package.  I do not reccommend these labels.  I gave it a 3 because Avery is a good company.

I grow many varieties of vining plants and morning glories. These sticks are made of a durable plastic. I would say about 2-3 times thicker than the cheap ones that come with store bought plants. They are easy to write on withe a permanent marker of any color choice. I highly recommend these to anyone who is an any gardner to help keep track of your seedlings.

I like these labels since they are a bit larger than many of the address labels I usually use. When I mail a package, I like to use a return address label that is larger than the smaller ones I use on small envelopes. I know it doesn't make any difference to the post office, but I think the package has a nicer appearance with a slightly larger label and a seasonal image next to the return address. After all, I did spend several minutes wrapping the item for mailing so I like the finished product to look nice.

We love our Canon all-in-one but it uses a lot of ink. The one thing I really hate about the printer is it uses color ink even when we are only printing black and white or greyscale output. I would say we print 100 pages of black and white for every page of color but we go through color ink at about 1/4 the rate of the black ink.I first purchased just the large black cheapo cartridges to try them out. Except for having to be careful about dripping ink during installation the black worked fine. So this time I've switched to using the color inks as well.My wife recently asked me to print four 4 x 6 color photos for her, something we don't do often, and they came out great so the color cartridges work fine too.My only concern is potential long term damage that could be done to the print heads due to possible inferior ink but time will tell. Using these Sophia cartridges is WAY less expensive than the Canon OEM cartridges.July 9, 2013I now have used both the black and color ink cartridges and they are working fine. The only problem is I have to be careful as there is a drop of liquid ink as I open the cartridge that can make a mess. As long as I am aware of that I can manage it.

It was time for a new pencil sharpener in my classroom.  This thing works great.  It has an auto shut-off.  It doesn't always work, but you can tell it's done.  It can sharpen a brand new pencil perfectly in about 3 seconds.  It's not that loud either.

I used to sit and manually shred stacks of papers at work. I needed to remove the staples before putting the papers in the shredder. This Swingline Stack and Shred is a great addition to the office that needs to frequently shred confidential information. As long as the papers are not wrinkled the tray with the stack will take about 60 pages. You no longer need to be present to shred a stack of papers. It's efficiency is also not hindered by staples-they shred, too. In comparison with other traditional manual, or upright shredders, this machine is extremely quiet. It fits on top of a filing cabinet very nicely, and we've also used it at home, for the piles of junk mail and other unnecessary mail in the house. The pull out tray of the tray also creates less mess than other upright shredders. The smoothness of the shredding combined with quietness makes the job of the necessary shredding in any home or office environment seem easy, quick and less intrusive. We love this machine. We had no idea Swingline made products besides staplers,so this experience makes us want to try their other products as well-highly recommended!

These are the nice binders. They are heavy duty, so the rings don't break, or partially separate.  It has the four pockets, although I usually just use two.  I like the size on this one as well.  Not too large, but not so small that it makes it so you can't even use it.  The only bad part is the plastic they put over the top is not shiny.  I like the clear shiny.  This is frosted.  It also has a small tear in it.  I generally buy binders from the store for this reason.  I do like however that it has the clear plastic.  This allows you to slip in a cover sheet.  Some binders do not have the clear cover. Overall, I would still recommend, due to the actual binder system.

This is a well put together mouse pad that that is much better than  you run of the mill freebie mouse pads that you may get for promoting something.  If there is one drawback it is that is has that mouse pad smell that most new mouse pads have which then sticks to your hand for hours after using the mouse pad.

With tax preparation season upon us, my documents are all gathered in one folder. Separating those documents can be a time consuming process.The Wilson Jones Insertable Tab Dividers will help me to separate my documents into more distinct categories and make the work of compiling documents for taxes much easier.There are 8 folders with multi-colored tab identifiers. They are also three hole punched  so that they can be used in a binder. We receive many tax forms for investments. These pre punched folders can help separate items such as annuities, mutual funds, periodic statements, prospectus information and life insurance. I also appreciate that the sides are reinforced so if they are taken out of a drawer many times, this will help prevent tearing.Overall, this is a product that will be very useful and timely.

Absolutely loved the Epson Stylus NX625, super fast basic printer, no lag between sending to print and printing and the ink lasted longer than any other printer I have ever encountered. However time's change and our home needed more than a printer/scanner.Wanted an all in one that had AirPrint, HD Photo printing, Fax, double sided document printing option, cd printing and memory card compatible.This Epson XP-850 covered all my wants and then some. Brilliant photos, print from anywhere-computer, phone, tablet-, color fax, smaller than my old basic printer and after almost a month of use I am still using the original ink.ConsTray 1 is for 4x6 or 5x7 photo paper only, Tray 2 is for letter-legal size and the tray capacity is only around 50 sheets!!! Very small tray capacity. Also, basic black and white printing is not as fast as on my old Epson Stylus NX625.The Epson XP-850 more than meets my needs and I am very happy with the quality and ease of use. A++

I bought these for our Swingline Stapler as recommended by the manufacturer and could not be more satisfied.  The stapler maximizes the staples by going in fast, smooth and quiet.  My second boss said to me one day, "If we need staplers and staples buy only Swingline."  I may be wrong on the quote, but it is close.  The two go together perfectly and I am fully satisfied.

What you get is a decorated cardboard envelope that you slip inside a plain white mailer cardboard envelope. I wasn't totally clear on that until it arrived, so I was a bit confused as to what all the sizes were about!It's pretty slick that you can put in the 'wrapped' package inside of a mailer. I'm not convinced the double duty is necessary, but it is pretty fun.On the plus side, it took me about 30 seconds to "wrap" and mail a book in one of these dual envelope systems - so you can't beat that!

This is an excellent product that makes an ordinarily tedious job much easier.  The trick is the "Easy Apply label strips," which allow you to print all five index tab labels at one time using a Word template that Avery makes available online.  Once they're printed, you just peel the group of labels off of the sheet and press the labels onto the folder tabs.  There's also a set of individual labels if you don't need sets of five.  It takes less time to do it than it takes to read this explanation.  The dividers themselves seem very sturdy, and they should survive pretty rough handling in a notebook.A new way of doing divider tab labels isn't going to change the world, but this Avery product makes life just a little easier.  Bottom line:  Well worth the money.

Mine aren't quite as dry as many of the reviewers here seem to have received, but they definitely aren't "juicy" by any means... I just saw that another reviewer suggested storing them facing downward which I will try and update if that helps... I normally keep my dry erase markers sitting in a cup facing up and they work fine so I question the quality of these but for under four dollars I can't really complain. I was looking for low odor smaller markers for my 4yr old who likes to "write" on a white board and the built in erasers are excellent for her little hands as are the smaller markers. I think they are fine for occasional use or for a child but I'd look elsewhere for everyday or adult use.

These inks are great and long lasting. I have been using these on HP3915 printer. I don't use the printer much, and replace them once every year. No smudges/marks and well designed. I have been using HP printers and inks since 1999. Definitely recommend! The reason for 4 stars is it is expensive. The quality is good.

First off, for a really decent review of this item see the one by the Amazon User Neil E. Isenberg. He really details everything.For my part I just wanted to throw in a thumbs up for everything that has been said so far. I am very pleased with what I have seen come out so far including photos, standard prints and high quality images. In all cases, the printer did what it said on the tin.As far as some of the noise issues this printer makes, yes, that exists, but it is nothing compared to other printers of this type. I have been using ink jet printers for over 20 years and have yet to find a quiet one. On a very unscientific scale of printer noisiness, I would put the Pixma in the 2.5 out of 10 range (with 10 being obnoxious rock concert level). In other words, yes, you hear it but it is not like it wakes the neighborhood up.So far, the ink usage has been a bit better than expected.  I printed some normal pages and also a half dozen hi-res, full color images and while the ink cartridges took a hit, they did not drain to zero with one pass. I have not had to buy new cartridges, but they seem a bit more expensive considering you have more ink cartridge colors, but that is not such a big issue for me. If you are a hard core print person with either a lot of hi-res or large number of regular prints, it may make a difference.The setup was easy enough and it does help to be a bit savvy with your wireless networking. However, the network discovery worked really well and got me through most of the issues. The scanner works well and will suffice for most people’s needs.Again, Neil Isenberg’s review is far more detailed, but I wanted to chime in with my approval of the printer. After years of dealing with clunker, el-cheapo inkjets, it is refreshing to have a fairly sophisticated unit at my disposal.

I didn't know what to think when I ordered these labels, but I took the risk and it paid off.  Sheets had a weird smell when they arrived, the smell most likely seeped onto them when they were sitting around in the factory where they were made.  The weird scent could be smelled in my office for a couple weeks until it finally disappeared, but it wasn't that bad.  This was a superb deal for the amount of labels I use.  I just grab one off the huge stack of labels, put it onto the printers tray, print, and slap it onto my packages.  The ink prints perfectly, there are no smudges, and the labels peel off easily.  These labels are so inexpensive that the ink I will end up using across all 400 of them will end up costing more than the labels themselves.  Great deal!

I have a habit of leaving a white board on the back of the toilet, with notes and reminders for my husband. How can he say he didn't see it??? Anyway, I have been using a white board for years. Recently we remodeled the bathroom and have beautiful wood cabinets there, and I love having his instead!!! It looks nicer and works as well, if not better. Putting a little cup with colored chalk in it makes it fun, too.

Ever since working with manila folders in childhood to doing serious work as an adult, manila folders have been that often appreciated associate that for some reason likes to nick us once in a while...and sometimes too often.I've used these Cutless Manilas for quite a while now and so much appreciate them not giving me a deep gaping finger wound.  It's such a minor modification I imagine, but such a world of difference.  I no longer have this fear or ever present need to be vigilant when working with manila folders again.Great product.

I bought this printer in mid 2008.I don't do tons of printing, but enough that I know I wasted a lot of money printing documents with an inkjet printer for years before I bought this Brother Laser printer. The toner cartridges last and last. And if you don't do a lot of printing, another plus is the ink don't dry up.woooo hooooo

Smooth, good flowing ink! Feels great on Moleskine paper and Bristol Board. Reliable, doesn't clot, doesn't skip. Nice line variation, but never too wet. No feathering on any of the papers I've tried this on. Pretty remarkable dry time, and is a good every day ink. It's a little bit lighter than the blue-black I was expecting, but is still a very nice shade and darkens a little upon drying. The blotting paper comes in handy and has a very nifty dispenser at the bottom of the ink well. It's a very interesting well design, and although not as interesting as something such as a Mont Blanc well, still has the form and functionality to match the design. Unlike some believe, it is still a 50ml bottle of ink. The bottom part of the bottle contains a punt into the dispenser for the blotting paper, serving as a way to keep the dispenser attached, but also as a place for you to put the point of the nib in the bottle to ensure that you're deep enough to draw ink in, as well as allow you to get the very last drop of in out of the bottle. This is my first blue-black, and although it's not as black as I'd think it'd be, this is definitely one of my go to inks.

This is a good set for my home office, a light weight stapler, 5000 staples, and staple remover.  The stapler holds one full strip of staples (210 of them).  And the staple remover works well, one pull removal.

The scanner itself is very simple and easy to hook up. The directions for unpacking are very easy to follow and very simple.The scanner quality is ok, the "lid" is a little fragile and I might be a little concerned with it being easy to damage if a someone who was a little harder on things were to use it. Must be the reason for the 8 strips of blue tape you have to peel off the scanner when opening. I think the hardest part of the installation was getting through the tape on the outside of the box.The software installation was easy to follow.  Hinged lid expands to fit books.  Resolution of 4800 is more than adequate to meet my needs.  OCR works as well as any which is not saying much.I have used the scanner to scan photos and documents and have been impressed with the quality of the items that I have scanned. Costs 1/4 of what I paid for my last Epson scanner with similar output (which is 10 years old and still working great).

Make sure you're looking for something that maxes out at 35 pounds. I got this in order to facilitate sending packages. I'm always running to the post office just to weigh a package, then I come home and print out postage (often cheaper to purchase online and print at home), THEN back to the post office. I've already saved myself 6 round trips to the post office (about 30 total miles which saved me 1 gallon of gas - the savings will only accumulate). This item is a no-brainer, easy to use, clear and simple controls. It supports both English (pounds, ounces) and metric (kilograms) weight systems. The seller includes the 9 volt battery for running this in a portable mode.An easy 5 out of 5 stars for doing what it says it does.

If you've tried these (and who hasn't) they were a practical invention. The company keeps expanding its product line as new ideas arise. Some can seem a little unnecessary but one has an interesting addition: you can tear off the perforated sheet take it with one once you don't need to have it stick somewhere to remindyou of something.

This Scotch Super Glue is what I've come to expect from 3M. Unlike the typical super glues that are in a tiny tube and often can be used only one time, this glue has an easy to hold dispenser/container that dispenses the glue very accurately. It bonds most everything. I like it and believe that you will also. Highly recommended!

Scotch Magic Tape is another good product from 3M. It is the original "matte-finish, invisible" tape.  I use the tape to construct signs for students when I administer the ACT, SAT, and PRAXIS standardized tests.  I use a flip chart to direct examinees to the testing rooms and tape additions and changes to the basic flip page sign.  The tape disappears as advertised reducing distractions for the often nervous students. I can write from the paper to taped areas of the sign in pen, pencil, or magic marker with no reductions in the readability of the information.I also use the tape for posting direction signs on test site entry areas.  The tape holds well in cold weather when glass doors and windows become misty.  For testing documents and reports, I can cut and paste and then photocopy without the copies showing shadows of the tape.I highly recommend this product for office and presentation work. In this review, the 3/4 inch x 300 inches tape in a plastic dispenser is described.  It comes in a three pack cardboard container that can be used for storage.

We homeschool and are constantly dog-earing pages in books or writing notes for small projects. These post-it notes have come in handy for the two kids of this house. Flags for pages instead of bookmarks. Note flags for special messages, even a highlighting pen with post its. They absolutely love this post-it pack. It is a nice little smorgasbord if different post-its geared toward the student. A little pricey considering the ratios maybe bring the price down to around $10 other than that we really like it.
Hate moving and packing..I do however want my breakables to get there in one piece.  The perforated divisions every 12" was great.  no scissors required

These worked fantastic for laminating some cards that needed protection.  Very easy to slip the card inside and put it through my laminator.  No wrinkles.  Sealed smoothly.  I'll use these for photos next time!  Good product!

I like the larger bins that this consists of as opposed to the versions with the narrow bins. I use it to store embroidery floss and paired it with the drawer dividers. Worked like a charm. Great for small parts, crafts, etc. Had an older version with a mix of both sized drawers but these are much better, IMO.

You learn that when there is a power outage, the cordless will not work because the base is plugged into the electrical socket so its a good little phone to have plugged into a landline that's there when you need it, even if you have a cell phone ....because you could have a low battery and this landline though to some out dated, it sure helps in a pinch.!

My daughter is a professional photographer, so I thought who better to review this new Artisan 837:-I really enjoy the sleek design of this Printer; I have been using Epson Printers for sometime and upgraded from the Epson Photo Stylus R260, to this new model.It's an Elegant Printer, Fast, Stylish, and the Touch-pad is very neat, here's what else I'd have to say about it.It comes with a test Photo Paper sheet of a 4x6 so you can get an idea of just how fantastic the printing ability is you can test it out. -tested it, mind-blowing good, I'm a Photographer and the Print quality and color are phenomenal. But being used to Epson's old system on my previous printer this is set-up quite different. You have to face all paper downwards for printing, (gloss side down) maybe I'm just not looking but I couldn't see it stated anywhere. This in turn has caused me to damage a page of Printing. I use Epson Premium Photo Paper it's older paper not the brand new high gloss paper that you can currently purchase. Well the test sample they give you looks amazing but the paper I own even though it is still Epson it does not look as clear or bright I don't feel as though I should have to spend $35 on Paper extra when I just got it and want to use what's left of my own supply.Now the color preferences are something I'm still not sure about. Letting Photoshop or the Printer decide on color set-up I'd normally opt for the Printer. This Printer has more options however and I feel somewhat lost as to getting the correct result. The ink as anyone knows-crazy expensive by the time you've bought yourself three sets of ink you've paid for the Printer itself. The Cartridges that accompanied the box were halffull-I think that's a little cheap on Epson's part considering they cost around $75 to replace.It is a great Printer don't get me wrong, it was very easy to install and it look very glamorous compared to what I'm used to, it prints great when using the new Epson Paper and its fast with several options for print sizing within the Paper Tray. Biggest thing is EPSON need to lower the price of their refill packs and the Color Preferences need to work for more than just newer high quality paper.4 STARS

These magnetic push pins are great!  They are strong, and stick well to the magnetic dry-erase whiteboard I bought them to use with; the colors are nice, and these hold paper corners or post it notes onto the whiteboard very well, but shift and move about when I move them: these are push pin size, so they are nice and small, but are definitely high powered magnets, so they work great: would definitely recommend!

Tickets a heavy paper, only about half as thick as paperboard (65#)Kind of a disappointment coming from Avery. I've used & love a LOT of their products. This one missed the mark.Tickets tear easier from stubs than they do each otherGreat idea, but needs to be thickerNice size for events, etc. Might be OK for same day use.Takes inkjet OK, better with laser printer.Avery has online software, but you're better off if you have either the old software of just using MS Word OK, or better, Open Office Writer.Online software had some pictures, the program is extremely clunky, although can be used on pads & cell phones.It took me roughly 15 minutes to find out that you need to make an account, THEN you can find the software for the tickets, otherwise the web site will take you in circlesThe old Avery software wasn't great, but the new software leaves a LOT to be desired.I's suggest http://www.amazon.com/Blanks-USA-Pre-Cut-Numbered-TKS02X9WH/dp/B001T0HG7U/ref=pd_sbs_op_5 instead, as it is already pre-numbered and they are made with heavier paperYou can then use "Writer" or "Word" software."Open Office" is a free office suite Avery had yet to recognize, yet is a FAR superior program or MS Word, AND is open source! You can keep the basic features if you like, or add as many as you want & you can save to multiple formatsNot a lot of artwork to choose from, tabs are not in the order they need to be used. This wasn't a problem for me, as I'd used their old software before.Someone needs to start from scratch & make some software that is easier to use with Avery products!This is the first product of Avery's that I've truly been disappointed with.If you're going to have an event worth creating custom tickets, you'll want to do it on thicker paperboard (a 110# or above) , otherwise, you might as well , save the money, time & ink and buy a roll of 2000 standard tickets & be done with it!Here's a roll of 2000 standard tear ticketshttp://www.amazon.com/PM-Company-Deposit-Tickets-59005/dp/B003B1ZHFS/ref=pd_sbs_op_3ad, as I'm generally a fan of Avery products. It seems like on-line software was thrown together. The older software you downloaded was better, but srill needed some work to refine it.

I recently purchased this printer after reading favorable reviews in PC publications.  I was mainly interested in photo printing but wanted more versatility in order to reduce the clutter on an already overloaded desktop.  I've been nothing but impressed with the printer since taking it out of the box.Setup was easy, although the steps are in an unusual order compared to other printers/peripherals that I've installed in the past - pay attention to the setup poster.It prints beautiful photos with vivid color and crisp detail.  However, the speed has been the pleasant surprise:  I typically print a 4x6 at the highest resolution in about a minute and an 8x10 in under four.  Plain paper printing is also very good for everyday documents.The copier, scanner and fax functionalities all work as they should.  An intuitive control panel and LCD display make every function very easy to use.  The bundled software also allows control from your PC console and it's one of the nicer ones that I've seen (i.e. you can program your fax numbers from the PC rather than the printer's keypad and can even instantly import information from Outlook).The gripes that I have are minor compared to the output that this machine produces.  First, it is a very big printer - the pictures don't do it justice.  Second, it jerks back and forth while printing enough to cause minor vibrations in my desk.  I recommend figuring a way to put it on its own dedicated printer cart.  Third, for the price, it would have been nice to have the second paper tray thrown into the deal - every now and then I waste a piece or two of photo paper on the grocery list because I forgot to swap out the paper.To recap,PROS*  Excellent print quality for both photos and documents*  Print speed*  Ease of useCONS*  Bulky unit doesn't belong on most desktops*  High price doesn't include some extras that it should

If you use a lot of rubber bands in your daily work, this might be a *very* functional item for you. I don't use them that often, and I'm a little concerned that the bands will dry out, crack and break by the time I do. However, I like it mostly because it is a neat and attractive way to keep a few rubber bands on my desk, within easy reach. So, I won't worry too much about them drying out...by that time, I'll probably just get another. Lots of folks have noticed it on my desk and asked about it. So...functional and interesting as a desk accessory.

This is fantastic. I have been looking for something like this for my fridge for a few years now, and it never occurred to me to look for locker pockets!  I like to have pens and other items EVERYWHERE, on the fridge, front door, side of the bathroom cupboards, etc., but could only find low-quality magnet-pockets from the dollar store. They fall off all the time.  This thing is actually sort of hard to pull off! The magnet on the back is strong and covers the entire back. There is no way it's falling off. I put mine on the front door. Our front doorknob was broken, and every so often I'd have to slam it violently (I mean VIOLENTLY) to get it to shut. The pocket did not fall off, and nothing fell out. Sweet.Also, if you aren't using this in a locker but on something nice, you'll be happy to know that the magnet is covered in a slick plastic coating that keeps it from scratching anything. Not that you can slide it around, because it's attached too well.The dry-erase feature is a silly but as-promised bonus :)Also the red plastic in back is really more of a very-deep pink, in case that bothers you.I'm getting at least one more for my fridge. I wish more stuff in my house were metal so I could put these all over.PS: If you need to hold more things in one spot (on the fridge, say), you can getFive Star Locker Organizer, Tri-Pocket with Dry Erase Surface, 7 x 7.5 Inches, White with Teal Pockets (72628)for only a couple of dollars more. I'll take two of each, in each color!

I can imagine a committee of marketing guys struggling all night to come up with something new. Finally they invent the Pop-Up tape dispenser and go home but they have wasted their time.Its only advantage is that the strips of tape are pre-cut, the idea is that you pull out the next one from the cartridge and whack it on. But the dispenser did not work for me. When I pulled the first tape out, nothing came out of the slot to replace it. And trying to fix this was a pain. I gave up in disgust.My advice: stay with the old style spools of tape.

I'd love to review this printer, but I can't get it connected via wireless or by USB. We've had problems with our wireless connecting to our wireless at home, so we tried it at our office too, but it was a no-go. So then we tried it via a USB connection and that was a disaster. We've reviewed several printers for Amazon Vine so I don't think we did anything wrong in the set-up. After trying out the Dymo 260P label maker for Amazon Vine last spring, I decided to give this fancier Epson model a shot for compare and contrast. While they each use their own proprietary cartridge, both ran 12mm labels for my review, both are hand-held models for labeling on the go, and both use a typical dot matrix LCD screen. Turns out that is about as far as the comparison went.Out of the box, the LabelWorks LW-400 is a wider and heavier model.  It still fits in my palm, but not as naturally as the Dymo 260P. This model trades the ergonomic shape for a uniform rounded rectangle. So I have the opposite experience of the label cutting button being more accessible from the left hand grip than the right hand--a problem since I prefer to hold these things in my right hand to operate the keypad with my left. I suspect a man with average hand size will have no problem, but those with smaller hands simply won't find it as comfortable to hold.On a desktop or table top, the LW-400 is more suitable. Especially because it offers a noticeably wider keypad with increased functionality. Unlike the Dymo model's alphabetic board, this one uses a Qwerty layout for US familiarity. The keys aren't as stiff or cheap feeling, and all of them register easily.This unit also offers additional and much needed keys, such as dedicated "Shift"  and Caps toggle, dedicated font size, frames, punctuations, symbols, and so forth. This does stretch out more functions across multiple key bindings instead of a single "Format" button", so in compensation there is a Quick Tips label on the back of the unit to remind you where to find things.That, and the fact the Epson offers many more glyphs, symbols, frames, and text positioning options may also trade for the increased complexity. I like the Tab option which allows you to automatically format a label as a folder tab, a wire flag, or a cable wrap--making this at least more appropriate for home theater and PC users than the Dymo.Unlike the Dymo, this unit takes six standard AA batteries. I received a complimentary review supplement of batteries and cartridges to help test the Epson, and no batteries were contained inside the retail package, so expect to supply your own. That said, I use rechargeable Ni-MH batteries all over the house. So I appreciate another electronic device that can conform to my power scheme.Getting down to the real nitty gritty, the label quality is only a notch or two higher. The ink tends to print more completely--I haven't had any labels with faded or missing lines. Yet it is still pretty pixilated on curves of the characters. The labels are just as readable from across the room as the Dymo at the 24 point size, without reflecting too much glare from the laminate surface. The oldest labels I applied a month ago have not peeled. Mostly, I've been affixing them to plastic. The unit prints more quietly than the Dymo; it is nevertheless audible. By default, labels tend to have about a 1/3 inch margin from the text on the left and right hand sides. Users can specify exact label lengths in order to reduce or increase these margins.All in all, the Epson LW-400 is a higher quality model than the Dymo 260P I reviewed last spring. On the other hand, it takes longer to learn and doesn't hold in the hand quite as well. You may also have to supply your own batteries. It seems to me that the Dymo is suited to a user who must stand and walk about, labeling on the fly like the ninja, while the Epson is more useful for someone who is sitting at their desk. I recommended the LabelWorks LW-400 overall.

Bought this several weeks ago for the main task of replacing my old Brother fax machine, which was one of those old fashioned ink ribbon units.  Faxing was important for me so all in one without fax capabilities would be useless.  I didn't have to have wireless capabilities but it sure would be nice because I could place the unit in my living room.Unboxing and setupUnboxing the unit took a while as Brother packs down the unit very well to negate damage during shipping. Unit comes with starter ink cartridges which means they aren't nearly as filled with ink as the regular units.  This of course is standard practice by all companies so you are enticed to purchase the ink cartridges.  Fortunately, the Brother ink carts are relatively some of the cheapest out in the market!  Compared to HP or Epson, it's a steal to how cheap the cartridges are. To me this was a major factor in my decision to purchase the unit.Since it's a wireless ethernet printer, all one has to do is plug it into the electric socket and plug the phone line in.  Note that this unit does NOT have a handset.  But there is an auxillary phone jack so you can plug in a traditional phone directly.  I liked this feature because I'm not paying extra money on the handset portion, something that I would never really use.Setting up the printer for wireless was a piece of cake.  I use a very long string for me wireless security key, utilizing AES encryption.  No problem getting the unit configured; didn't have to look at any manuals since the large on screen LCD guides you through like a mini-computer. The password can be entered with the unit's alphanumeric keypad in the same way a phone's keypad allows you enter in characters.  By the way, the keys felt solid and expensive.  Overall construction of the Brother is high quality; quite a difference with some HP units I've come across which are flimsy to feel.Setting up the computer side I simply popped in the CD and let it go.  It did take a while to install everything and I was afraid of bloat.  But over the weeks I can say that I haven't had any issue with the Brother software crashing or hogging up resources.  Again, quite a difference with HP units (HP printer owners know what I'm talking about!)  The software is sophisticated such that it allows you to make all printer configurations right on the computer itself.  One final setup comment is that the computer NEVER had a problem "finding" where the wireless printer was.  I have to bring this issue up because my old HP wireless all in one frequently told me it couldn't find where the printer was, even though it was turned on!ScanningThe unit has a sheet feeder as well as a flatbed for letter sized documents.  The scanning is FAST even with high resolution.  I am used to scanning that takes a long time when doing something like a 600dpi scan but this Brother whips through them like it's a 100dpi document.  I couldn't believe it.  The printer allows you to scan directly to a computer in your network. The filetype is preconfigured as jpeg but you can easily change this to PDF and you don't need Acrobat for that.  I'm sure a lot of people will love the ability to scan directly to PDF here.  No need for conversions, or any of that fuss.  There's also the ability to scan to email but I haven't tried that; the included OCR was a big step up from anything I've used before.  I am sure this is in combination with the crisp scanning the unit is able to do -- characters are recognized readily without many errors at all.  In the past, I found OCR to be nearly useless with a lot of scanners.  Clearly not he case here.PrintingSince this is an inkjet, the quality of text black prints will always only be marginal when compared to a laser.  Clearly this is the case here.  A little fuzzy on the fonts but perfectly legible. Speed is nothing to write home about but not painfully slow either.  The paper tray is rather unusual in that it sits completely flush; no paper sticks out from the top or has a big exposed tray area.  This means getting dust or crinkled paper that sits in the tray is never going to be an issue.  I really like this since I have a dusty room and sometimes wont print anything for days at a time.The paper tray has a built-in dedicated photo card (4x6) loader as well.  This should NOT be mistaken as a dual paper tray -- the photo cards can only be used when "loaded" forward; unloading the unit then has the printer feeding from the usual paper stock.  Therefore, since there is manual effort required to select either tray, this is not a true dual paper feeder.Photo print quality was not anywhere as good as I've come across on Epson and HP units. This made it a little disappointing but not overly so.  The pics did not have any banding or anything, just that the colors were not vibrant.  They were still passable though and would be fine for a quick print that you need to do.  Even so, I've found that inkjets are poor mass photo printers anyhow; you're much better off with a dedicated dye-sub type printer for photos (which are horrible at text).The unit has built in slots for memory cards including the most popular formats of compact flash and SD.  With this, you can print directly from the cards.  There is also a USB port which supports any modern camera with direct printing; so you can hook up the camera and print.  I tried this with my Canon S5 camera and it did work just fine.FaxingFaxing can be done traditionally, through the unit or it can also be done with the virtual fax printer driver.  By this I mean that you can use "print" on your computer and in fact it loads the fax dialer.  Faxes can be sent out this way so you never need to physically be pushing buttons at the unit itself.  I tried both methods and they worked without a hitch.  I should add that I have Time Warner's VOIP system, not a traditional POTS phone system.  No problem at all faxing.SummaryOverall I find the Brother unit to be an incredible value.  Its price I notice keeps fluctuating all the time so you may want to observe its price before purchasing. In my case I was able to secure one for 89 buckaroos. I heard it can sometimes go lower than that but like I started this review out, I needed something to fax with.  The units build quality, cheap cartridges, seamless FAST scanning, as well as faxing capability make this unit a must-have for any homeowner.Update: I've since installed the printing drivers on my Dell Mini netbook. Anyone with a netbook knows that space and processing power is at a premium so bloated software is out of the question to install.  Not a single problem with this Brother unit as the software takes up very little resources.  For this, I used the driver pack from the Brother's web site rather than installing from CD.  I didn't choose to install the Paperwork software, but just the control center driver software.

I am very happy with this printer.  This is my second color laser printer; my first was a Lexmark that only survived about 60 pages of printing.  This printer produces better quality prints than the Lexmark, takes up about the same amount of space, but also is a fair bit louder.  I think I would find it uncomfortably loud in a typically-sized spare bedroom office (say, 12x12).  Of course, it's only loud when you're printing.I also have a Canon multi-function laser in my office.  This printer is quite a bit slower than the Canon to print a page of black and white text; most of that is due to the length of time it takes the printer to wake from sleep.  However, the print quality, even for black and white text, is MUCH better (I compared the two under a microscope).  The moment came for me to order a new printer when I was reading a PDF printout of an academic paper one night and I realized I might as well be looking at a fax machine output.  Comparing that document with the new printer is night and day.Business graphics are excellent with this printer; as others have mentioned photos can be a little dark.  Mac integration is easy; my Macs saw the printer without installing anything and then downloaded the driver and installed it when I went to use it.  No CDs or anything required.  This auto-detect worked on both Snow Leopard and Lion.The printer comes with 128 MB of RAM and is upgradable to 384.  The cost for the DIMM to upgrade it is $10 on Amazon, so I've ordered an upgrade.  I don't know that I need it, but I figured for $10, why not?  If I ever do need it, I would likely find out at a very bad time.The other big concern with buying a printer is the cost of supplies.  There are two capacities of toner cartridges available for this printer.  1500-page yields for color (C,M,Y) run around $50 on Amazon and a 2,500-page yield black (K) is also about $50.  On paper, that's about 13 cents per color page.  The higher yield cartridges run about $80 for 3500-page color and 6500-page black, which breaks down to 9 cents per color page (but 1.2 cents per black page!).My expectation is that I will get higher yields (based on previous toner experience).  I also think these prices are fair for the toner; some printers have much higher street prices for the toner.  Buying four high-yield cartridges for the printer is the same price as buying the printer on Amazon, but still cheaper than buying the printer at Staples.  As other reviews have mentioned, there are some "secret codes" to get more life out of the toner if the printer decides they are low but you feel otherwise.I got this printer for 60% of the price at Staples by buying here at Amazon.  I'm really happy with the purchase.  I have no idea how long the printer will last, but I will update this review in the coming months (and hopefully years).UPDATE Jan 2014:  A year or so ago, I added the second paper tray so I could print legal & letter without moving paper around.  And earlier this month, I upgraded to a much faster HP printer (that also costs a lot more).  This printer does a great job on text, and is fine for casual use--but I found it just too aggravating in terms of speed--if I wanted to print a document quickly so I could jot down some notes while I was on the phone, I could easily have to wait 2-3 minutes to get a printed copy of the document (maybe 5 pages of text).  It was hurting my business, so I made the switch--and comparing the more expensive HP to this, I can say the Brother has much lesser quality color printouts.  Still a good printer if you don't care about speed and don't need copier/scanner capabilities.  I've also been very pleased w/ the toner life span--I got far more pages out of the toner than they advertise.

PIXMA MX432 is a shiny All-in-one solution for printing, Scanning and fax multifunction device from a reputed manufacturer which does all the advertised features with flying colors but it could have been even better here is why...The wireless setup for the first time use is painful if you have older routers which do not have wireless distribution system (WDS) function as the wireless AP search requires you to have WDS feature to begin the initial pairing which for me was not possible. I kept on searching the menu's to see if I have the option to manually enter my SSID and passkey but there was none I could find. Finally, I was able to setup my wireless access point by plugging in the USB cable and installing the Canon software (Bloat ware)If you are like me, I personally hate installing plethora of manufacturer's software (Which is designed for newbie's) to setup a printer and use it's functionalities by big menus buttons, shortcuts on desktop and tons of software startups during system boot making the machine just crawl to knees as it hogs up the system with tons of applications starting at boot time. While these software does what it is supposed to do but it also adds tremendous unwanted apps in startup not to mention bugging you every so often to buy ink buy this buy that or register this and send anonymous data etc; etc;Okay after having the Wireless setup process done and assigning a Fixed IP address for my newly acquired shiny Canon printer I thought it would be time to get rid of the bloat ware and just use the drivers to use the printer for use but there also It failed as I could not get the Scanner functions to work correctly. Apparently the TWAIN driver does not get loaded under Windows XP when you install the drivers alone for the printer - this was bad.I could not get the TWAIN driver for the scanner separately under Windows XP machine with wireless mode. The Scanner and Printer worked only when I used the USB connection with minimal drivers - the end of story.I switched to a Windows 7 Ultimate machine and attempted to do the same thing and ended up in a similar condition wherein Printer functions worked just fine but I could not get the Scanner to work wirelessly.Out of sheer frustration I removed all the drivers again on Windows 7 machine and let Windows figure out the drivers automatically from windows update. To my surprise, the Windows driver update did the installation of drivers perfectly and I could get ALL the functions of the printer (Scanner/Printer/FAX) work perfectly using the wireless function.This tells me that Canon's software CD included forces you to use their bloat-ware in order for the all the functions to work correctly and somehow if you use their driver alone (Even the latest ones from Canon website) the Twain driver (For the scanner) does not get registered properly.Having said, the printer otherwise functions just fine. Scanning speeds are good. Scanning quality is better than expected for the price and it has automatic document feeder for multiple scanning and photocopying etc; It has only two cartridges, one black and one color. Which I somehow feel will bite me once they are nearing empty as it will force you to buy a full new color cartridge even if one ink is low. This is pretty much what is expected of these sorts of ALL-in-One devices.Another annoying thing about this printer is how loud the beeper is. Forget about turning ON or OFF this printer at night especially if you family is sleeping. It will make a loud BEEEEEEP! And every so often you can hear the head moving up and down the carousel just to re-calibrate or just check the ink levels - frustrating. I even turned the noise level down in the application but it did not help much.The Paper tray is another annoying contraption wherein it forces you to load from the front of the device and that occupies a ton of table space. The rear of the printer is bland and empty where I personally feel the paper tray should have been located. I hate to load paper every time I need to print something and I do not want paper sticking out of my printer collecting dust!The shiny surface is a DUST magnet. While it looks super cool black round shiny device. It gets dirty very quickly. The LCD display is very hard to read and not backlit so it is worthless in my opinion.Overall I personally think this printer could have been much better as I love other canon products and I feel that I was let down by the annoying experiences I had with this printer so far.There definitely better alternatives out there for the same price range.EDIT: APRIL 03, 2012--------------------To be fair and honest, Added one extra star making it an 'OKAY' product for the price! because apart from the issues described above the printer, scanner and FAX works just fine.

This meal planner makes it all work and keeps one on a diet.Staying on track and being honest with yourself takes monitoring, the kind this dry erase board makes available.  It may only give you enough planning one day at a time, and it may only give you room to write your calories and food plans daily, but it is an essential tool.  Yet, goal building and planning ahead are also part and parcel of dieting, so you need supplemental goal books and a journal to keep looking ahead, and, if for nothing else, other tools help you monitoring your results, so you can SEE your progress. How active you are will mean the difference between gaining and losing weight, and that factor is not figured into this table.)Still, a daily food chart keeps one on course.  I keep Tom Venuto's quick calorie chart on the 'fridge as well, which makes filling in this daily planner even easier.  A similar chart nearby will make your dietary journey also more efficient for your time and progress.

Up front is a panel for the various functions; scanning, faxing, and copying. There's an alphanumeric pad for faxing, and a backlit LCD dot-matrix display. You can hook this printer up to a home network. There are slots for memory cards also. There's an Ethernet cable port in back, so it's network compatible. I have mine hooked up to my home wireless network through a router, and it works fine.HP says this will do 33 pages per minute black and white and 25 color. Obviously it's an exaggeration, because it depends on the print quality. A fast draft print will come close, but for anything else, forget it. I'd get good color prints in over a minute on the maximum DPI. It uses print cartridges quickly also. I burned through a color and a back and white in a couple months of light use, less than 200 pages. HP cartridges are expensive and rarely go on sale.This does print great photos, although not as good as a dedicated photo printer like the PhotoSmart series. The Canon Pixima 4-in-1 series machines do the best job, but were a lot more expensive. Black and white, text comes out clean and sharp, but not as sharp as a laser machine. The scans come out good, but expect to wait for them. Same with copies. Scanning and copying are both PAINFYULLY slow with the 6310. Other machines do much better, and the higher end HP 4-in-1's perform all these tasks quickly.Overall, this is a good machine for light use or occasional use. It would be best for someone who needs to send an occasional fax, scan, or copy something. It does everything I ask it to, and does it good enough.Pros:Low priceHP qualityreadily available ink cartridgesQuick printingGood print qualityNetwork readyMulti-card readerAuto document feederConsSlow print speedsPainfully slow scanning and copyingExpensive ink cartridgesPhoto printing could be betterCartridges don't last long

The Canon Pixma MX340 is your pretty average featured multifunction inkjet machine.  The kind of machine that is at home in the home office, or now with wireless technology, you can pretty much put it anywhere with a plug where it is within range of your wireless router.  Perhaps the home office can now become a crafting room or a man den. Totally up to you.I have experience with an almost-equivalent featured machine from HP:HP Photosmart C7280 Color Inkjet Printerthat I have been using in my home (for personal and business use) for the past 2 years or so, so hopefully I can offer some insight.Size and appearance wise, I think the HP C7280 is more modern and pretty looking (think clean white ipod-ish) and Canon is pretty much a no-thrills office machine, aesthetically.They both offer inkjet printing, scanning, and faxing.  Both have ADF (document feeder).  The HP has automated duplexing (double sided printing) but that feature usually leads to me having to pull the printer off the shelf and extract little bits of paper from the inside.  Apparently, duplexing makes the HP very hungry.Even though the HP was released a couple of years ago, I find that the quality- at least in printing-is comparable between the two machines- if not a bit more accurate on the Canon.To test the Canon I took a lab printed photo of my son and made a color copy on regular paper, and then high quality print using the little packet of Canon photo paper included with the printer.  The copies were spot on- there was a little bit of darkening in the more shadowy areas of the copies, but the colors were so close to identical that I would not have guessed that the copies were indeed copies.Text printing quality is very nice as well.You can also print from pretty much anything that can be connected via USB. That's one built in feature I sort of like on the HP- the memory card slots are built in.  With the Canon I have a card reader dangling off the front so I can print shots from SD, Compact Flash, and Sony MemorySticks. Not the end of the world, but I will be adding a dedicated card reader just for the Canon, otherwise I can see epic hunts for the misplaced card reader in my future.The one major thing that I did not like about the Canon was the wireless hook up.  I followed the directions closely and it still took me 4 installs and over an hour of monkeying around to install the printer and have it actually communicate with my MacBook (running snow leopard).  I installed the drivers on our other computer (a networked MacMini running both OSX and Windows XP)  this morning and with a couple of clicks it was up and running... I think the use of the word "Register" in the easy install threw me- I thought it wanted me to REGISTER my new machine with Canon but really it was the needed step to bring the printer -computer connection to full functionality. I am pretty used to working with my mac, though I haven't installed a printer in 2 years until yesterday, but I would not want to troubleshoot the Canon over the phone for my parents, who are not so computer savvy.  That isn't to say that my HP was easy to set up, it was a nuisance as well, but I found it a bit more intuitive...The Canon software and the scanning to a networked computer are leaps and bounds above the HP which is a moody beast and sometimes works and sometimes doesn't.  The Canon software is easy to use and very efficient.Anyway...Pros:Nice print qualityDocument feeder is nice and smoothSoftware is nice for automating scanning and setting defaults to boost productivityIt's easy to open the whole thing up in case of a jam.  Haven't had a jam yet, but I'm well versed in clearing them, so I figured I'd take a peek.Cons (when compared to the HP printer):-Tiny little dot matrix screen is dark and hard to read for this tired eyed gal.  I much prefer the vivid color displays that allow more information to be seen at once.  This may be a problem for people with low(er) vision-Lots of scrolling through menus is frustrating.-only one paper tray, traditional "stand up" paper feeder in the back of the printer means that the height + width footprint of this machine when in use is another 6" or so over the listed dimensions, with a bit more clearance needed to fill the paper feeder.  The HP has a flat and mostly covered paper tray, with an additional tray for photo paper, which is nice because you don't have to keep swapping papers out of the machine when doing multiple job types... Because of this stand up paper feeder, this Canon wireless printer won't fit as easily onto most shelving units unless the shelves are a good distance apart. Whereas, the HP with the flat feeder can fit in a closet with plug access- out of site...Other than those things, I find the machines to be fairly comparable, and price-wise I would probably go for the Canon over the much more expensive HP as the features that make the HP a more advanced machine are what make it a frustrating machine, in my opinion.

The Swingline Stack-and-Shred line of shredders take a unique approach to shredding. Instead of manually feeding multiple sheets of paper into a cutter, the Stack-and-Shred uses a storage tray that you stack sheets of paper onto. The design allows you to walk away or do other things while the shredder does its thing.PROS:- Quiet operation- Innovative design- Large, 5-gallon capacity- Shreds paper clips, credit cards, and staplesCONS:- Struggles with non-letter-sized paper- Jams when wastebasket is half fullI've been securely shredding documents for years and have used several different shredders over that time. When I found out about the new way that Swingline's Stack-and-Shred shredders worked, I got excited. Well, as excited as one can get about shredders, I suppose.PERFORMANCEWith the Swingline Stack-and-Shred 80X shredder, you stack up to 80 sheets of paper in the storage tray and when you're ready to shred, just flip the power on and the Stack-and-Shred starts cutting the paper into confetti. For a guy who's been shredding documents for over 20 years, the process definitely threw me for a loop.Basically, the Stack-and-Shred has rollers, like on a printer, to drag sheets of paper down into the cutter. When the paper gets dragged down, it folds the paper in half before shredding it. This is why you can't place sheets of paper in the tray that are folded more than once. One sheet of paper folded once would equate to shredding four sheets of paper and the cutter is only rated for up to six sheets. Apparently, the cutter is built for endurance over maximum capacity. Many shredders, especially at this price range, can handle 10 or more sheets at a time, but shredding 80 sheets in a row would probably cause them to overheat. The Stack-and-Shred handled a full storage tray without any signs of overheating.After testing all different types of documents, I came to the conclusion that the Stack-and-Shred works best with standard, unwrinkled, letter-sized paper. The way that the rollers are positioned would cause problems with odd-sized paper and because it uses rollers, any wrinkled or previously folded sheets of paper would prevent the rollers from effectively grabbing them on a consistent basis.The manual 6-sheet shredding slot is suited for credit cards, thicker paper stock, legal-sized documents and other non-standard paper. One down side I found to using the manual slot was that if you keep stacked paper inside for shredding at a later time, you'd have to remove them in order to use the manual slot. Also, because the slot is located rather high above the cutters, short receipts sometimes wouldn't feed through easily.NOISE LEVELThe Stack-and-Shred is pretty quiet, for a shredder. I measured the sound output of a standard shredder and compared it with the Stack-and-Shred, confirming what my ears already told me. The ambient noise was about 18dB and went up to 60dB with a standard shredder running. The Stack-and-Shred's noise level was a muted, 48dB.MAINTENANCEThe Stack-and-Shred is maintenance-free, meaning, there's no need to oil the cutters. Swingline even recommends against using standard shredder oil.The 5-gallon, pull-out wastebasket is easy to remove, but emptying it was a bit awkward, because of its long and shallow shape. A sample shredder bag was included in the box of the Stack-and-Shred, but I'm not a big fan of using proprietary bags for disposal. The waste basket also caused the shredder to jam when it was only half full.Once I figured out what types of paper to use in the paper tray, the Stack-and-Shred rarely jammed, except when the wastebasket got partially full. The problem, I noticed, was that the shredded confetti didn't fill up evenly in the wastebasket. Therefore, when the confetti built up in the rear of the wastebasket, freshly shredded paper had no place to go and caused the cutter to jam. Though this was easily remedied by pulling the wastebasket out and giving it a good shake to spread the confetti around, it caused a big mess. My suggestion to Swingline would be to integrate a manual rake-like mechanism that spreads the confetti around evenly. That way, a user could even out the wastebasket periodically, preventing this type of jam and avoiding a mess.CONCLUSIONI love that Swingline created a new and innovative way to shred documents. It's quiet and can be a real time-saver. However, Swingline needs to find a way to better handle non-letter-sized paper. If you tend to shred a lot of odd-sized paper, the Stack-and-Shred may not be your best bet. If you stick to letter-sized paper though, the Swingline Stack-and-Shred 80X can provide a nice, care-free way to shred documents.* Review unit provided by Swingline

... but it sure works pretty well.I was very surprised at how nicely it worked dry. I thought, hey, just a piece of sponge - how special can it be?My board has had a lot of use - especially with markers that weren't meant to be used on a white board. The Powershred MS-460Cs is a powerful shredder that operates in near silence.  Coming from a 10-year old shredder that was about as quiet as a wood chipper, I am amazed at how quiet this shredder is.This shredder groans mightily when processing 12 sheets of paper (2 more than the maximum advertised), but it does get the job done.  If you put in too much paper, it has an automatic "reverse" function to eject the remaining sheets so you can try again.  The resulting confetti shred is so small that it is inconceivable that someone could reconstruct it without the aid of a supercomputer.  Each shred is about the size of a grain of  rice-- and not the "long grain" variety!The Safe Sense works as advertised, when your skin touches the shredder near the blades, the unit immediately turns off.  If you have young kids around, this is a great safety feature.Some nit picking: the unit comes covered in stickers advertising its capabilities.  These stickers probably help sell product when on display at Office Depot, but when you get it home and try to take them off, they are a nightmare.  The stickers fall apart as you peel them, leaving ugly gunk and paper all over your shredder.  I ended up having to use goo-gone and risking damage to the fine finish of the shredder to remove these marketing stickers.  Fortunately, goo-gone did not damage the finish.Also, my shredder arrived with a broken guide pin for the bin to go into the enclosure.  There are two guide pins and this thing weighs a lot so I decided not to return it.  But it is an apparent quality issue.This shredder is not powerful enough to handle some thick credit card applications that I receive without first opening the envelope and diving them up.  That's why I give it 4 stars instead of 5.

This paper is nice, works great and the price is fair.  I use it for mainly general purpose, B&W printing and so have not tried it with my color laser yet, but it seems like great quality paper with a nice surface and feel.  No complaints and can easily recommend this paper for general use.

The pencil looks ok. It was lighter than I expected. It's all plastic. It has a little bit of give when the lead touches the paper (this is how you power the turning mechanism). This give is not distracting at all.I hate writing with hard lead that sounds like it's scratching the paper only to get a faint line.So as soon as I replaced the included HB lead with the 4B that I normally use, the experience was much better.Of course I had to play with it, so if you start scribbling without lifting the lead off the paper it will start to write thick. Writing a few words "normally" it recovered and I got a sharp point again. it doesn't matter if you write cursive or not, it performs well.The only bad thing is that it feels cheap. I normally use a Pentel KerryPentel Sharp Kerry Mechanical Pencil, 0.50 mm, Metallic Black Barrel, 1 Unit (P1035A)which really feels like a substantial writing instrument. While I really like the kuru, it feels cheap in the hand in comparison.

The Quartet Magnetic Combination Calendar Board has a quality white board surface and cork board bottom.  It falls a little short with the white frame that seems a little inexpensive and the included pen that does not write very well.  The magnet on the included pen is only barely sufficient to hold it on the magnetic board.  The included magnets are colorful and work well. I'm using the Epson Workforce Pro WP-4530 in a small office with three other people.  Setting it up took a while, but it was a pretty easy installation and the printer has been working great since.The initial setup took a while because Epson secured every moving part with a piece of tape or a block of foam.  I spent a few minutes poking around to make sure that I pulled off every bit of tape and foam before plugging it in and hooking it up.  When it first booted up, the printer itself had to go through a long initialization process.  The LCD screen said that it would take about 12 minutes, which was pretty accurate.  I'm not sure what it was doing, but after 12 minutes, the printer was ready to use.  If you're a tech savvy person who has set up computers and wireless routers before, then you'll be totally at home setting up this printer.  The printer's LCD screen interface is very easy to use, and Epson also provides a set of software that lets you set up the printer from your desktop for USB and even network connections.Pros:- Fast printing.- Auto-duplex printing support.- Scanner has a auto-feed tray for scanning multiple pages.- The black and white print quality is great.  Color print quality is good.- Tons of connectivity options: ethernet, USB 2.0, WiFi B/G/N.- Supports USB thumbdrives.  You can print from and scan to a USB drive.- Supports scanning directly to computers, email and PDF with the Epson's software installed on your computer.- Supports WSD scanning for Windows 7 and Vista.Cons:- The printer doesn't seem to auto-detect when something is in the manual feed tray, but it detects things in the scanner feed tray.- All the moving parts feel a bit flimsy, especially the paper catch tray.- We're having problems scanning to a Windows 7 PC.  An error pops up on the desktop saying that the scanner is already in use.  WSD scanning works fine, but it's not as elegant as scanning with the Epson software.Notes:- The printer is about as loud as any other ink jet printer.  Since this isn't a laser printer, it doesn't hum when it turns on.- Epson claims that it's cheaper to maintain than a laser printer.  We haven't used up the start ink cartridges so I can't verify their claims yet.

I like these tabs because they are larger than the tabs that come with most hanging file, allowing you to write more or larger on the label.
