The only downside for me is that the label slides into two slits in the back of the tab; thus, the back of the label is not protected by plastic, and you have to fold the labels just right for them to fit in the slides well. The Wilson Jones Ultra Duty Ring Binder is well made and work well for storing important notes / document.What I like about the product- Nice Ploypro materials with a 5 year warranty- Holds about 400 sheets with its 1.5" size- Solid single touch operation for opening and closing the binder rings- 4 pockets ( 2 on the front cover and 2 on the back) for holding extra document

The price is cheap and so is this product. It's a small whiteboard in a plastic frame. The description said it's a calender board with a grid printed on it, so you can fill in each day of the month---however this is not the case. It's a plain whiteboard, nothing fancy.Pros:* It comes in a variety of colors. I chose green to coordinate with my sewing room and the color was exactly like I expected.* It's a magnetic whiteboard, so you can attach photos, sketches, or even business cards, and then make notes beside them.* It comes with a small dry-erase marker, so you can use the board immediately, without making an additional purchase of markers.* It comes with two large, round, clear plastic magnets, so you don't have to buy separate magnets to use the magnetic feature.Cons:* It's pretty small. Check the measurements and be sure the size is what you want, so you aren't disappointed.* The plastic frame is very cheap. There's actually a gap between the frame and the board, which increases when you apply pressure to the board---like when writing on it. I worry that the frame will eventually come loose.* The magnets it comes with are stuck to the board with a blob of sticky goo, which refused to wipe off once I removed the magnets. I had to pull out the Goo-Gone in order to clean the sticky spot off the board. (It worked nicely, but I shouldn't have to use a cleaning product to make my purchase usable.)* It doesn't have a hanger on the back, so you can't just hang it on your wall. It comes with both adhesive pads and magnets, so you can either stick it on your refrigerator (or a metal door, etc.), or you can use the adhesive squares to stick it to your wall. I don't care for either idea, personally. There is no metal surface to attach it to in my sewing room, and besides, several reviewers have stated that the magnets aren't strong enough to anchor the whiteboard in place, so it slides down. As for the adhesive squares, I'm guessing that if you use them, you can't easily move the board, and if you tried, I'm sure the adhesive would ruin the paint on the wall. This may not be the case, but I'm loathe to try it, just in case I'm right.In conclusion, this is a classic example of getting what you pay for. If you want a small, cheap whiteboard, this will serve you well. Personally, I would save my money and buy something a little higher in quality. I'll give it three stars and hesitantly recommend it, with the above-mentioned caveats.

Nice and easy to use, just touch one of 5 light options to get the brightness you want.  Makes reading print outs etc. a lot easier and glare free. Unlike a standard banker's box that comes with a lid on top, a storage drawer comes with a shell that it is inserted into.This makes it easier to stack these boxes while still retaining the ability to open a drawer at the bottom of the stack to inspect its contents, making things a lot easier for your back and biceps.1. This box is part of Smead's MO ("My Organizer") trio of products that also includesfile foldersand aslipcase-- papers go into the file folders, the folders go into this box (which functions as a sort of portable, mini file-cabinet "for the desktop, drawer or shelf"), and this box goes into the slipcase (which to me seems unnecessary).This box is extremely basic in material (medium-weight cardboard) and color (solid dark blue outside, unfinished white inside). You can of course turn that off if you don't want it to link from your cellphone to home phone set. Switching between using your cellphones and home phone line is easy and painless, and the price is reasonable.  There really isn't anything I don't like on this phone other than small quirks here and there over where the buttons are and such, those though are easy to get used to.  The set is expandable too since two phone sets is not always enough!

I previously had a PT-65 labeler; I'm replacing it with this new unit. It's lighter and still has all of the same functions as far as I can tell. This is the second Kodak Printer that I have reviewed during the last two months.  The first was the Kodak ESP Office 2170.  I was very pleased with that printer and equally pleased with this one.  In addition, I have an HP and Canon MP 640.  Compared to the HP and Canon, the Kodak printers have the slight edge.  For instance the Canon and HP use 5 ink cartridges and the Kodak printers use 2.  I find myself always looking for a single cartridge of one of the colors and then having to order it.  Particularly the Canon which for some reason requires two black cartridges - this is absurd.  Both of my Kodak printers utilize the same ink cartridges and now I don't have to deal with multiple vendors for two printers.  Also the paper loading on the Kodak printers is as easy as it gets.  The Canon design is poor in this area.I haven't done any studies on the use of ink, but it seems to me that due to the dual cartridge methodology, the Kodak requires less ink worries as it requires less cartridges to purchase and keep in inventory.The installation of the Kodak C315 was a piece of cake - that is - as long as you read the directions (which I never initially do).  So after getting ticked off because the Microsoft Windows 7 installer failed, I read the manual and found that you have to initiate the installation from the printer, not the PC.  This is different than most printers I've used as you generally use the Microsoft "install printer" wizard.  THIS WILL NOT WORK ON WINDOWS 7.  So once you begin the installation at the printer, your printer will be installed and selected as the default printer.Installing the WIFI was also easy and immediately picked up by the printer.  However, this is something that was a little different.  The printer gives you the `%' of signal strength being picked up from the WIFI router.  In my case, I moved the printer into another room so that it would be closer to the computer, but at least twenty feet from the WIFI router - this is also through two doorways and around the bend.  So I was very pleased that the printing and scanning was so effective at only 60% of signal strength.I printed pictures and they are stunningly clear and focused.  You can load individual 6x4 glossies or up to 20 at a time.  The ink was dry as the picture was coming out of the printer.I then used the scanner.  Again, you have to initiate from the printer, NOT the Windows 7 computer.  But this does make sense in that you can stand anywhere in the house and scan your document at the printer.  When you are finished, then you can go to the computer and the document is waiting for you in a pdf format and the pages combined into a single document.  This is a really nice feature.Again, I feel that Kodak is making huge strides in the printer market and providing user friendly features that other printers are not.

This handband dispenser is very comfortable.  It's doesn't hinder you as you do your projects or feel tight.  The stretchy band has an adjustable strap to fit all size hands. UPDATE - 10/4/2012:  I've had this printer 19 months and I still have the original ink cartridges installed. With other inkjet printers in the past, my ink would dry up from lack of use - I used this printer a couple days ago and I was astonished to see the ink is still good!******************I have been using the cheapest black-only HP LaserJet printer made - and there comes a time when you want to print in color.  After using this all-in-one for a little while, I am very impressed with its functionality - so much so that I have recommended this printer to a couple of people that I work with.I didn't bother installing the CD that was included with this after reading some of the other reviews here first.  I went straight to Epson's web site and downloaded the Drivers and Utilities Combo for Vista 32 bit and this was all I needed to get started.  I also recently went wireless at home and this was my first attempt to connect a wireless device to my network.  It worked flawlessly - the screen on the front of the printer recognized my network immediately and all I had to do then was enter my password.  To be honest, entering my password was probably the most time-consuming part of this entire set-up.  It's THAT easy!  I didn't bother hooking it up by a printer cable (not included) the first time as the quick-start guide recommended, there's no need to do it that way if you plan on going wireless with this.My first attempt at printing the Epson Test Page had a slight snag as I had not installed the "letter size" paper correctly; once I pushed the side tabs inward, the page printed.  I'm amazed at the fast printing speed of the printer, just as fast as my 3 year old LaserJet.  The paper drawer will hold half a ream of paper at one time.  Making a copy is just as fast as printing a document, all the feature buttons of the printer are located on the flip-up command center alongside the LCD screen.I haven't tried sending a fax yet as I don't have a phone line nearby, but I have tried the scanner.  You have a drop-down menu option of Home, Office or Professional Mode, and I noticed this scanner has a lot of the same features that I have at my job on my dedicated Microtek scanner that cost 5 times the price of this Epson.  One thing I like that this scanner does is you can auto-feed up to 30 pages to be scanned; I can't do that with my scanner at work.For the price of this all-in-one, you can't go wrong.  I highly recommend this for home use, and small businesses that don't generate a super large amount of paperwork, too.

Golly, I'm so grateful I found this on Amazon.  It just arrived yesterday, ordered two days prior, God love Prime!  I had another one for years, which I somehow misplaced.  Its flexibility makes it more than just a medium-sized book holder.  On the surface, it seems to be good only for your average NASB-sized hardback Bible (about an inch thick).  So the rest of this review is about how ELSE you use this thing.Right now, as I type, I've got the left 'hook' hanging over my flat-panel monitor.  So the thing is hanging by that left hook, diagonally (askew), and upside down.  The back long 'legs' are folded out, so think of the thing as in standing position.. but upside down.  A plastic clamp (could use even a big paper clip) holds a bunch of papers together, for input (about 10).  So this 'sturdy stand' also acts like a monitor clamp at eye-level, without the adhesive and flimsy plastic holders which so easily break.  The stand's rubber feet protect the metal ends from harming the monitor; frankly, the one hanging off the monitor isn't even touching the screen.  So two vital uses, not just one.You can also use the thing to prop up large/heavy books.  Or, to hold any size book yet allow you to turn the pages.  So, now it props up my huge Shakespeare book (about 2" thick?),  also here in Amazon, by Royal Shakespeare Company.  Or, ponderous short 3-inch (maybe 2+?) notebooks.  You just use the stand differently.  [A European style X-shaped dish rack, especially wood, is also useful.]  How?  Again, upside down.  I put the Shakespeare book on a mat, turned the 'sturdy stand' upside down and turned the back legs TOWARD each other.  Could use a rubber-like place mat, if reading from a table.  Something to give more traction for a heavy book.  Much better than your typical book holder, because it tilts backwards, and the upside down 'hooks' add support.Okay, so now suppose you don't need to read a book. You can fold the thing sideways and store it just about anywhere.. or, you can HANG it, using the forward 'hooks' for clothing, accessories, you-name-it.That's a lot of sturdy value, for five bucks. I love banker's boxes.  They hold just as much as I'm able to carry comfortably, stack neatly and have ample room for labeling, even if you swap out the contents on a regular basis.  When I moved a few years ago, most of my belongings went into banker's boxes, which made the whole process much simpler.However, not all banker's boxes are created equal and there are some significant differences you should be aware of:  First, some of them are miserably hard to put together.  You wouldn't think that something as simple as a rectangular box (Are you ready for the technical term?  Parallelapiped. I kid you not.) would be easy to put together, but many of them are constructed so that you have to separate parts on badly perforated lines, and refer to diagrams to figure out which flap goes where.  Another common issue is strength.  Not all banker's boxes are as sturdy as you might hope.  I have had a few give up the ghost under the pressure of a load of art books.In general, I tend to prefer Fellowes boxes both for ease of construction and sturdiness, and I have to say that the Presto scores high in both respects.  It's wicked strong, and will probably last through years of hauling and schlepping and stacking.  And clearly the name "Presto" wasn't given lightly because it comes together with almost no effort at all.  This is the Grand Pooh-Bah of banker's boxes, IMO.It may seem as if it also has a Grand Pooh-Bah price but that's only compared to flimsier boxes.  This kind of storage solution doesn't come cheaply.  You want cheap, go to that big Scandinavian store -- you know the one I mean -- and pick up some of their storage boxes.  They won't hold much and they take forever to put together, but they are prettier and yeah, they're a lot cheaper.  I keep yarn in those boxes, and that's fine.  Yarn doesn't weigh much. But when I need to haul books, cooking pans, garden supplies, and my antique cut glass dishes, I'll always opt for a box like the Presto.  I know I can trust it.

It is simple, though, to remove the board from the fridge, write on it, then put the board back.It also comes with a small, black dry erase marker that can be snapped into a holder at the top of the board.  This is very handy and means you won't be searching for the marker.The entire board is the size of an 8.5 x 11 piece of paper, with the writing surface about 1/2" smaller on the sides and 3/4" smaller on the top and bottom.

Or worse, having to repeatedly pull out staples because the stapler was not heavy duty enough and lacking in staples of adequate sharpness(You know us guys...We are determined because were men that we'll staple all 45 pages and we'll waste lots of time until we conquer it). It's pretty strong, but it could be more agressive as far as it's stickiness.  This 20X strength tape solves the stickiness problem (it is real agressive sticking) and is really so strong it's approaching the perfect tape for my business shipping needs.  I am a shoe retailer and many times I ship out individual pairs where my mid-weight tape is actually overkill...But, many times I ship out cases of heavy boots (6 pr. per case) and I have to layer the Scotch tape I'm currently using for insurance.  This is tiresome to take the time to double, even triple, up on al taped seams, etc. Plus, since my current tape isn't as aggressive as I'd like so I have to massage the box where the tape is laid down to be certain it adheres. You can see this makes shipping easily take twice as long as it should.  Scotch 20X Strength Packaging Tape solves all my problems and I can live with the overkill on smaller packages since I save time and money overall.  This is my new tape and I recommend it without reservation.

UPDATE: Keep in mind when reading this that it is based on a late 2006 model 17" MacBook Pro. More recent models can open wider and will probably work just fine with this stand. This original review was written in 2008 when that was not the case.I bought this for my 17" MacBook Pro. I currently use a Griffin Elevator at home and I wanted something to use in the office. This looked like a nice stand for a great price. It is a nice stand but does not work for my MacBook Pro at all.1) The stand is sturdy and should hold just about any laptop with ease.2) The mesh is nice if your laptop needs ventilation.3) The design of this stand is that the front of your laptop sits low while the rear end tilts up at an angle. This puts the display at a much higher location than normal, thus keeping you from bending your neck to view your screen. The problem is that when the base of your laptop is placed at this angle your display needs to tilt back VERY FAR in order for it to be vertical. I've been a fan of Canon printers for years, and it seems with every generation, they manage to make their printers faster, cheaper, or better.Sadly, the Pixma MX860 doesn't keep the tradition alive.Right off the bat, I've had the similarly pricedCanon Pixma MX850 Office All-In-One Inkjet Printer (2436B002)for just under a year now. So, I've got a decent foundation for comparison.Canon gets it right in a few areas with the MX860. The inclusion of wireless networking (especially at this price point) is excellent. Connecting to my WPA2 network was reasonably simple, though getting to it in OS X was a bit of a chore (System Preferences -> Printer -> MX860 -> Utilities -> Network). Once I got there though, it saw the networks I had running, and connected on the first try.The MX860 is also noticeably smaller than the MX850. Somewhat less narrow, and substantially less deep. The MX860 is still a desk monster, but it's more reasonably sized than its predecessor was.Print quality is excellent, as expected. The special calibration paper included with the MX850 was suspiciously absent from the MX860, until the manual confirmed that they're just not using it anymore. Aligning the print heads is basically the same 5 - 10 minute "which box looks better?" routine that's been around since at least the i800 series.Now, where the MX860 gets it wrong (and why I'd suggest picking up an MX850 instead, if you can still find one)...The LCD display no longer tilts. Either you don't use the LCD ever, and this makes no difference whatsoever to you, or you use the LCD, and will find this infuriating.Canon has once again imagineered new ink cartridges that are incompatible with everything else. I'm not a fan of refills or third-party cartridges, but in an office environment that already has Canon printers around, this can be a headache.Perhaps more irritating than Canon making new ink cartridges for the sake of making them, is that the new 221 series is smaller than the 8 series used in the MX850, but costs the same per cartridge.Finally, the MX860 looks and feels cheap, compared to its older brother. Canon seems to be taking some cues from HP's design on multiple fronts, which is unfortunate.All that aside, there's not much different between the MX850 and MX860. Scan and print times are basically the same, and differences in quality is negligible even at high resolutions.There's nothing inherently wrong with the MX860, and months from now, it'll be a solid buy. But while the MX850 is still around, I'd suggest grabbing it instead -- unless you absolutely need wireless and / or don't want to deal with setting up a WAP. Cheaper ink overall, better build quality, and no discernible lack in print or scanning quality make the 850 a better choice.

PROS - various web savvy features, alternate feed for different paper, wireless printing from a tablet or smartphone.CONS - nozzles subject to clogging, poor manualsI had no idea the additional capabilities of printers these days until my old all-in-one broke.  Besides the usual all-in-one features, this one has additional tricks:- You can scan to a cloud address, as well as to a computer or memory card, great for paperless record keeping.- This printer has an email address, so when you are away, you can email things to it which you want printed.- You can print lined and graph paper (though it is probably not cost effective, it could be handy in a pinch).- You can define an image to use as a watermark for personalized stationary.- It prints two-sided.- It will "autofit" if you are copying something small, automatically figuring out the enlargement percentage to fill the entire page.- It has an ID card mode so you can copy both front and back of an id card onto a single page (though it is a bit cranky about proper placement).I have used this printer with a Mac and with an iPad, and the software seems to work just fine.A potentially serious issue with this printer is that since the nozzles are part of the printer (rather than replaceable with each ink cartridge).  While this makes the ink cartridges cheaper (since they don't need to include nozzles and the nozzle control electronics), the nozzles can get clogged over time, and you need to blast out more ink in the cleaning operation.  After printing out maybe 50+ pages, some of which included color graphics, I printed some photos, and already there were spots skipped where a nozzle was clogged.  I am hoping this is just a fluke (another older epson printer I have hasn't had any clogged yet) but if it occurs regularly I'm will downgrade my rating. [ETA: one month later, after using up the ink it came with and installing new ink cartridges, I printed some more photos, and by then whatever was clogging the nozzle had cleared itself.]Another problem is that the documentation is lacking and/or wrong, and scattered.  The printed guide that comes with it only scratches the surface of what it does. There is an online version of the manual that includes some of the interesting features which I mentioned above, but they are a series of hyperlinked paragraphs, so it isn't easy to print out a full complete manual (or save a pdf of it to read paperlessly), and people who are not inclined to poke around might not discover some of these handy features at all.  Additionally, to use the web and cloud features, you need to set that up, but the url given in the manual only took me to an ad for this "Epson Connect" feature.  I finally used their online help system to find the correct dotcom page, EpsonConnect, where there is yet another 40 page manual about how to use these features.[UPDATE 6 Feb 2014] -  I have kept track of black ink usage.  For us, theEpson DURABrite T127120 Ultra 127 Extra High-capacity Inkjet Cartridge-Black(also available in a two-pack) prints a little more than 500 pages.  We print a mixture of pages with a variety of spacings.  I haven't been monitoring the color ink usage because it is too intermittent, but I haven't had any obvious episodes of ink clogging.[2/21/13 - updated with little details which I have discovered with continued use.]

After waiting for the delivery of this talking travel translator, I now have to wait for it to actually translate. It arrived intact in a little package without much non-recyclable materials, just the disposable plastic case which is easy to open and not much larger than the actual 3/4 of a deck of cards size of the translator. Included was a sheet of paper with 705 English travel related phrases, and a second sheet of paper which is the schematics and operating manual. Both are in English, folded and double-sided. Now for a review of the product.PROS:A voice announces what is on a little screen and you can change the language through any or all 7 options.With one button, you can hear it in your "Home" language.Favorites can be saved.It is small and lightweight.If you study this, you can learn phrases and speak them yourself, maybe after showing the display to a person who speaks the language you want to learn.You can enter addresses.CONS:If it needs to be reset or batteries fail, you lose all your addresses and saved favorites and there is no way to backup.It is not very sturdy in the hand and the buttons often have to be depressed more than once.Buttons are small, but the letters on the word imprints are as tiny as a tick before dinner.Arrow buttons don't always work and sometimes simply turn off the device.Digital display scrolls slowly with push of button alone to display the phrase.Backlight button is exactly the reverse of the manual's description and it turns off and on with no apparent logic.Audio quality is lousy with some phrases being unintelligible, even in my native English.Spanish has an extra audio blip on almost all phrase endings.Volume button on the rear feels like it doesn't click into the three levels but slides too freely.Volume often becomes weird with a sound that lasts for minutes of translations.You cannot see a phrase number, then enter the number. You need to scroll through each level and then you can save that phrase as favorite, then scroll through your favorites to access it again.Observations:There are so many phrases with negative connotations that it makes me want to stay at home with the doors locked. Examples include: 661 There is no electricity. 671 There are cockroaches in my room. 672 There is a smell of gas. 139 I have been bitten by a dog. 150 I have been attacked. 151 I have been raped. 162 I would like to speak to a woman. (There is no "I would like to speak to a man.") 171 Someone has stolen my..... (You can add another word like -- 474 Eggs, 463 Rib, 484 Pancake, 378 Whisky, 282 Two kilos of....)This translator was a disappointment to me because I expected the "Over 4900 Travel Related Phrases" to be phrases and not single words like days of the week, months, numbers, seasons and foods. On the other hand, sports include soccer, tennis, table tennis, golf, baseball, badmitton, and nothing more. I will continue to explore the gadget in the hopes of finding it more useful, but the main impression it made on me is that in order to use this effectively, one must follow the suggestion of phrase number 705, "Slowly, please."

[Update: 5-21-2012 - I am dropping 1-star from my original 5-star review on 12-13-2011.  WHY?  Because I have only now run out of one ink cartridge (light magenta). I thought I'd try the Panasonic multi-function printer since I figured it might help me in my home office. I've only really got a printer so the idea of having a scanner, copier and fax machine I could use for basic tasks sounded good to me. I'll break this down by task/feature.SetupThe printer was real easy to set up. Plug in a phone line, plug in a network cable (I'm using it on my home network) and plug in power. Install software. Done. The software isn't even really required. Now, the downside is, if you're looking to plug this into your computer because you honestly are just using it on one machine and don't really have a network setup then you're out of luck. It's got a USB port so you can do just that (plug it into your computer directly) but it doesn't come in the box. You have to go get one yourself. Not nice in my opinion. It's one thing to say "Network Ready" and another thing entirely to be "Network Required". That being said, you still can use it as a printer, copier and fax machine if you don't plug it into anything except the phone line.One other thing to note, the printer cartridge included in the package comes in two parts. One smaller part fits into a slot in the bigger cartridge (with the ink) and needs to be opened (you rotate a drum that presumably exposes the print head to the incoming paper). I'm a big and strong guy and I had a whole lot of fun trying to get that drum rotated during the setup. Granted I was afraid I'd break it but the piece you're pushing against is pretty solid plastic. It was more about how much resistance there was there. It's possible it was just a freak thing with my cartridge but you'd think it would either be easier or not require you to assemble the cartridge in the first place (my other laser printer has one cartridge).PrinterAs a printer, the Panasonic is pretty straightforward. I think the best part of it is that it's a laser printer. I'd always been used to seeing inkjet versions of these multi-function printers which has turned me off. It supports up to 600 dpi print outs with decent results. I did have some trouble getting the printer set up in Windows (using Win 7 64-bit) as the installer installed a printer in Windows that didn't seem to go anywhere. You could print to it but the documents just disappeared in to the ether. I deleted that and reinstalled the printer (just using the built-in/available driver that Windows offered which could still be the same drivers) and it worked great. It can push out 24 ppm and though I didn't run a speed test to check this out (not gonna waste paper on that...I don't print that much in a week) what I did print out came out in a snap.ScannerI was really looking forward to the scanner part since I have a more "pro" scanner but it's largely mothballed so it's a hassle to break it out to do any scanning. It was real easy to run a scan though the results are a bit iffy. For most documents, it was just fine. Scans were clean enough on regular paper. But, when I used paper that had even a slight gloss to it (I'm not talking magazine gloss, I'm talking matte coated paper), I'd get glare artifacts all over the place. Basically, the light from the scanner was (and I'm just theorizing here, not an expert) reflecting back enough to create something like a feedback loop. And, this didn't cover the entire page, just certain chunks of it. Even more odd was that the patterns, while consistent from scan to scan for the same document, were different from those when using the copy function. So, I can't say if this is a fault of the machine or the technology itself.The OCR software included with the printer is functional but nothing fancy. And when I say "nothing fancy", I mean it. The UI is incredibly retro (the software has a copyright of 2002). Whereas you'd expect to be able to use your mouse's scrollwheel to either scroll or zoom in/out, the app constrains you to set zoom levels (50% of actual, fit to window, etc.) and you have to click around between the horizontal and vertical scrollbars to get where you want to go. You can then use boxes (no magic wand or anything for you PhotoShop types) to define areas that have text, images, etc. It includes a feature that lets you edit the OCR's attempt at recognizing the word, number, punctuation though it can get tedious and the font they use to display the replacement character is terrible (sort of like a blobby Courier) to where you can't always be sure if you're looking at a zero versus an eight or a comma versus a period. The recognition itself is as good as the quality of the scan so your mileage will vary. Clean scans (non-glossy paper, straightforward fonts/text) work nearly perfect (line spacing might take a hit with a slightly misaligned original...especially since you can only rotate 90 degrees within the software). Anything else is a grab bag that usually results in missing sections or something that looks like a ransom note. If you really need OCR, you'll want to find something better.FaxAnother feature I was looking forward to. As much as faxing is on the decline (unless you're dealing with companies that really just don't trust online signatures for legal or other reasons), I still find myself wishing I had a fax handy at times. I usually end up heading to the Fedex store or letting my wife do it from work. By default, the fax feature is on and working. In my case, I don't have a dedicated fax line and I was only really planning on using this on an as needed basis. It took a sec to find the right place in the instructions to figure out the correct setting (in fact, the machine's own menu system had a print option to print a sheet of instructions related to that feature which helped the most). Once I did it though, I was golden. I faxed a doc off to someone (the one time I needed it in six months) and it went off without a hitch. They e-mailed me what they got as a PDF and it looked as good as you'd expect (it was an IRS form so text-dense, no graphics). Even better is the PC Fax feature which lets me "print" to the fax feature and fax something directly without having to print it out. The feature shows up as a printer and, when you print to it, prompts for a number to fax to--even offering a delayed send option so you can have it send out an hour later or something (say to avoid interfering with the phone during business hours). Very cool. The only down side is the software log that shows you sent and received faxes doesn't seem to retain those faxes despite setting it up NOT to delete sent faxes and the like.CopyThe copy feature is yet another function I've been wanting for a while. Of course, with a scanner, it's effectively a scan and a print but as I mentioned before, my scanner isn't exactly a convenient option. The copies worked well and, as you'd expect, are as fast as they can be with a fast scan and a 24 ppm printer. I didn't try a large copy job but I don't expect this thing to be some refrigerator-sized Xerox beast that churns out books in a few minutes. For the one-off copy, it works great.As mentioned above with the scanner, with certain paper types, you do see some artifacting but strangely the pattern is different from the scan. This could be because the copies are lower resolution than the scans (sort of a fast scan) so there's less opportunity for "feedback" from the light source but it's strange nonetheless. For the record, the copy scan looks better than the scan.ConclusionAll in all the product is good enough. I don't have a previous product that this is replacing (at least not one I've used in the past decade) so I can't really compare it to other products. But, if you're in the market for a multifunction printer that does it all and you aren't worried about the aforementioned scanning artifacting (i.e. it's not about the quality of the scans, just that you have a digital copy you can use), then go for it. The Panasonic includes all the features you'd expect but upgraded with tech that used to be only in dream machines that did just one thing. Just something about having one of these printers as a laser printer rather than an inkjet that seems to make it feel so much better than it used to be when buying one of these devices.

When purchasing binders, one needs to consider the use you have intended for them.  There are two things I look at,  the cover and the rings.  As a teacher and a mom, I have a lot of experience with binders.The cover:If I am simply going to put papers in them and store them on the shelf, I like the hard binders.  I use this type for filing recipes and documents I need to access.  Since they are stiff they are easy to shove back onto the shelf.  In the classroom these also work better, as they are less likely to slip off the shelf than the flexible cover binders.However, I find that buying hard binders for my kids leads to problems.  The kids like to stuff these into their backpacks, and the edges where the plastic is sealed quickly start to peel off, and the covers get folded over.  For them, I have found that a flexible binder in general will make it farther though the school year.  They will sometimes crack along the spine, but usually not enough to make the binder unusable, and a little duct tape will fix it.The rings:The second thing to look at is the rings.  The best ones (in my opinion) are the D shaped, as they hold more, with the little dimple on one side that fits into a depression on the other side.  This prevents papers from getting caught as you flip through.  They also hurt less if you snap them onto your fingers!  The other closure (a zig zag) tends to get misaligned over time with hard use, and the sharp edges hurt more if you close them on your fingers.This binder has a clear front in which to slip a cover, and more importantly if you are filing on a shelf, an insert area along the spine.  I am a fan of this extra, and have found that printing on cardstock, then laying the binder on a flat surface makes it easy to insert the label .  It also has  circular rings but they  do have the more desirable dimple to hollow closure.  It will lay flat when open.  There are two clear plastic pockets on EACH inside, one taller and one shallower for shoving in some papers at the front and back  (since this is such a huge binder, the front pocket is actually extra wide) for a total of 4 pockets.  That is a nice addition.  The cover does have that wrinkled look.

I acquired this for my daughter, who is a senior in high school. She has two main requirements for a binder:1. Sturdy - the covers don't tear off and the rings stay closed when they are supposed to.2. Pink color.This binder met both of those. It does not meet my requirements fully, though.1. Reasonably priced (almost $12 for one binder?). I would have purchased generic white binders, three for the same price as this one, at the warehouse store.2. D - ring instead of round shaped.That said, it wasn't my choice and there are zero complaints from the daughter. It has withstood her very casual abuse very well and looks on track to make it to college when she does.Since I pay the bills here, I took off one star for pricing, which I think should be about half of what it is.

These envelopes have a flap that needs to be lifted up to expose the sticky stuff that seals the envelope.  While it's a little slower to use than simply ripping off a strip, it's preferable to licking, and also nice not to have that leftover strip to throw away.  If you have a thousand letters to send at once, I don't see that this is any harder to use than the other two options.  But - though it hasn't happened to me - I can imagine you could get irritated and try to lift the flap faster and maybe end up wrecking an envelope or two.  But I'd use these, if I can find them in stores, over the other two.  Once sealed it appears that the seal is secure, too.  And hey, we could all use a little 'slow down and relax' in life, couldn't we?

I did a lot of research before I finally bought this hand truck, it didn't disappoint me. It's well-built, light but looks durable, foldable design makes it easy to store. It so happened that I had to pick up some furniture from a store shortly after I bought this, it worked great. Now I have to ask myself why I had not bought it sooner.
good, well-made and solid pencil. Sharpens reliably and writes like a good pencil should. Ticonderoga is a tried and trusted brand since my childhood and beyond. They have yet to fail me.

This board has a strip of cork which allows you to use a pushpin to stick photos, clippings etc onto it. I use this board to write down what I need at the store and I put up the coupons (if I have any) on the cork section. It really works for my family since I seem to be perpetually running out of pantry items, and misplacing the coupons that I print online.Since I have two other Quartet boards, it does help me use this one solely for grocery items.It comes with a dry erase marker, and 2 magnets. It is easy to install as it comes with self adhesive.Highly recommended!

This is a nice, compact laser printer.  If you need something for routine B&W printing, this printer will do the job.  I acquired it second hand from a friend, and it has worked really well.  I bought an after-market toner from Amazon for $20.00 and it has already gone at least 500 pages.  The quality is good for documents and emails, which is primarily what I use it for.  It is not super quiet and it is not super fast, but I use it at home to print between 25 and 100 pages per week and it works very well!

I use 1 inch binders to hold hard copies of my digital photographs and each notebook requires a spine label.  I have always had a hard time getting those paper labels stuffed completely into (under)the plastic spine overlay.  These Samsill binders somehow make that chore a snap.  I don't know what they did in the design to make that happen, but it works.I was often required to use card stock for my spine labels in order to get them into an ordinary binder.  These Samsill books allow me to use ordinary 20 pound copier paper.  And the labels slip right in.Having the D rings on the back cover is a nice feature and that configuration keeps my photographs flat and easily turned in the binder.

I really like these strips in principle but in actuality they have a lot of limitations.  I tried hanging a variety of lightweight items and found for the most part that while the strips cling tenaciously to the walls, they have quite a bit of trouble sticking to the objects to be hung.The first item I attempted to put up, a small picture 7" x 5", weighed 3.7 oz.  I used a full strip on the top and one on the bottom and within an hour, the strips were on the wall and the picture, on the floor.  I next turned my attention to a hooked rug whose side edges constantly curl under.  The rug hangs on a wall and its weight is fully supported; all I wanted from the Scotch strips was to prevent the edges from curling.  Nope.  Again, the strips remained on the wall while the edges of the rug went their own way.  The only items with which I had any success were single sheets of paper and small cards.So while I think the concept is great and I like the fact that the strips are reusable, I can't help but wish that the adhesive were a little stronger.

This is a good desk pen, feels good, writes good and the design reduces the fatigue from long use. It is also refillable, which makes it a little more value for the money. The ink flows good and is there when you want it (no drawing little circles to get the ink going).But my biggest problem with this pen was when I stuck it in my pocket for a day. The pen dissembled itself twice in my pocket and the button on the end kept falling off. This pen is fine if you are keeping it on your desk, but if you are looking for something to take with you in your daily travels, get something different.

We are sticky note junkies in our house and we are the type who love to go to the office supply store just for fun. We are also sort of picky about the products we use though so I was pleased to find such a high quality product as these note tabs. I was surprised at how sturdy they are. The main portion of the sticky note is a see through type of plastic that is lightly tinted. This portion is the size of about half of a standard sticky note and you can write on it or even use a highlighter but you are still able to view the original text underneath. The little tab on top of each note is nice because it acts as an indexing tool or a bookmark. I think these notes would be especially useful for cookbooks. We have also used several of them to mark up our homeschool textbooks. I like the way they are thick and sturdy, but still don't gum up the page. This combination pack is especially nice because yu can color code your tabs with the 3 colors included; blue, yellow, and green. They also remove easily and cleanly from pages of books and magazines.

The pen writes nicely--much better ink coverage and smoother writing than the new Paper Mate InkJoy pens.  The clip/clicker gets in my way when I reverse ends and use it as a stylus, though.  The clip/clicker is rather large.  So, I think the best use is as a decent pen and as a stylus in a pinch--and not the other way around.  It serves a purpose, although for my situations and purposes, a limited one.UPDATE Nov. 25, 2013:  I'm not changing my rating of this pen, because the pen/stylus feature that represents the "value" of this product still does not impress me.  But, I had to come back to this review to say:  The ink really does impress me; so much so, I came looking for the ink refills to use with other pens I own.  Somehow, the Zebra-brand ink writes over whatever hand/finger oils that hide unseen at the bottom of sticky notes and notebook pages.  Other inks skip when they come in contact with the oils from my hand--especially those highly-touted InkJoy pens.  If anyone else is interested in this ink, here are the refills that this pen uses:Zebra : JK Refills for G301Gel Rollerball Pens, Medium Point, 2 per pack, Black Ink -:- Sold as 2 Packs of - 2 - / - Total of 4 Each.

When I first opened these I thought they felt kind of cheap. They are mode of stamped metal with some sort of titanium coating on the blades. They do have a hefty and rigid feel though. They are also comfortable to hold. When I actually used them to cut a bandage my impression changed. One of the blades is serrated so it does not slip when cutting the bandage. The blades are sharp enough that it had no problem cutting and shaping the bandage while cutting the bandage and its backing.

I think that most homes now use a shredder. Perhaps it is a sad commentary on our society that we all feel the need to use one - if not every day - at least now and then.This is a very well made, compact, shredder that shreds completely, relatively quietly and is available at a modest cost.The best feature of the unit is that it is "hands free". You can stack up to 60 pages for shredding and the unit feeds the paper into the shredder. Alternatively, you have the option to manually feed the shredder from  top feed. The machine is not too fond of staples. The manufacturer claims that staples can go through the shredder and that it can if you separate the sheets first. YMMV on staples but that was my experience. I should add though that many larger, more expensive, feeders also are staple shy - so I do not think that this is an issue with this shredder alone - but ore likely a comment on all shredders! I also really like the compact size of the unit itself. Easily fits under a desk - or on top of it. I am also pleased the noise level is about as minimal as these things can go.All in all I am very pleased with this shredder - it would be a perfect home, small business, studio or other place that does not require doing large amounts of shredding - although this little gem can handle mor than I thought it could !

While Epson loves to tout their supposedly lower cost of ink, I've never experienced when comparing it to my HP color inkjet.  Epson uses a much smaller carrier and so replacement is much more frequent if you use the printer regularly.  I don't, it's a back to my laser when I need color and also doubles as my fax and scanner.  Amazon was fast with the delivery as always, well packaged and exactly as described.

This Amazon Basics Shredder is certainly recommended for the price range if you're looking for a fairly small (approximately the size of a small rectangular office trash bin) strip shredder.  It's quiet, equipped with an easy to carry handle, and easily shreds up to 8 sheets of paper, a single credit card, or a single cd/dvd.  This shredder has no issue with those annoying credit card offers (unopened) and although it slows with each increase of paper, there is no hint of struggle until you get past the recommended 8 sheets.  Shredding is strip-cut (approx 1/4-inch) for paper and credit cards so maybe not enough for super secret documents, but will do the job for routine shredding.  CDs/DVDs tend to shred in four bits--two thin strips at the edges and two more at the remaining middle.  Overall, a good and quiet shredder for 1/4" strip-shredding.

I bought the 6180DW because Brother's entry level printer was very expensive to operate. This printer's per page costs are much lower, so the total cost of ownership is also lower than most other Brother printers.I've run into two issues however, each costing one star. Both apply to Macs.The printer is often unresponsive. It has an aggressive power-save sleep cycle and a defect in its Mac drivers. That means it doesn't wake from sleep when it should. One has to press the 'Go' button to awaken it. (We use a wired ethernet connection to the network.)I thought a firmware update might help, but on a Mac this requires Java. Java is no longer a part of OS X, and it's an awkward installation with attendant security issues. Brother should support firmware updates through the printer's admin web GUI.Update: These days we have to press the Go button every time we want it to print. It doesn't 'sleep', it goes into a coma! There's something deeply wrong with the OS X drivers and the problem is not improving. Sadly, I now recommend Mac users avoid all Brother printers.

Pull off the tape, fold down the flap over the security envelopes, and press - there ya go, no more "gotta get a Coke NOW!" to wash that adhesive aftertaste out of your mouth!  The only improvement to me would be if they made a dispenser-type box so you didn't have to fold in/tuck the top every time you wanted an envelope - a tear out would be better, like they make on 12 packs of soda, so you could just grab one out of the box without opening it.  But otherwise, these are great.

There really isn't anything bad I can say about this product. It worked very well at stablizing, holding and protecting my worn books. On more than one occasion, I was relieved to have this tape at my disposal and because of that, I will now have many more years of enjoyment out of my older books.

We have a dry erase board that our kids use and when these became available I picked up the set for them to use. The colors are nice but really not too bold. I have not paid attention to what brand of dry erase markers I've used in the past but I have used some which made a much darker / bolder mark. On the other hand, those others tend to smell quite bad and this brand has almost no odor - and that is a very big plus.

These labels stick on securely but are still easily removable. They come off clean. They work great for project folders. If you want something more permanent, 3M also sells a great permanent adhesive version.

These have been a useful addition to my sticky note collection. I use them mostly for to-do and grocery lists - I stick a sheet to my fridge or desk and add to my list during the day. On my way out the door, I tear it at the perforation and put it in my purse. I also use them when I'm mailing something and want to add a short note that won't fit on one of the smaller notes. Their stickiness doesn't seem to last as long as the Post-It Note brand. Since I don't have to reposition these as much as the smaller type notes (because of the way I use them), it's not as much of a drawback for me as it may be for others. The colors are bright enough not to get lost in the clutter of my desk or drawings on my fridge, but not so dark that they won't show pen and pencil markings clearly. Overall, a good product for the way I use them.

I dream of first drafts that are good to go.  But mine aren't, and I put a lot of time and energy into revising.  My favorite pre revision field trip is to the office supply store.  Procrastination?  Organization?  I find good tools make it go faster.These perforated sticky notes in neon citrus colors are really good tools.  Long enough for some signficant notes, and bright enough to be noticed.  Like the perf. too.  Can carry around the note for inspriation.One warning - don't get caught in the rain or put down on a wet sink -- the colors run

These are good envelopes for mailing CD's. tiny books, and photos.  They're an essential office staple for those who mail often. Bubble envelopes are a time saver.  Also they are good environmentally because they are sturdy enough to be reused a few times.

After unpacking this printer, I set it up and input my Wifi name and password before installing the driver disk. My Windows 8 PC immediately recognized this printer and they have been getting along swimmingly since then. I have not been able to make this work on my Windows 7 desktop or laptop with the software CD or by downloading drivers. It gets to the point where the installer wants to "talk" to the printer wirelessly and neither of these computers will find it.The quick launch sheet sent with printer does warn you not to input the wifi name and password until the installer prompts you to, so I will remove my name and password eventually and try the install from scratch. I have the sneaking suspicion this will not make a difference though since the install doesn't ask for a particular passcode or anything and because the Wifi is connected. My HP wireless printer that I have been using for the last 1.5 years never had this issue. However, I don't consider this a critical situation, as I will use it almost primarily with my newer computer anyway, it is just puzzling to me that it is fickle. Since it could be my fault, I am not really docking it for this issue.My star docking is more because I don't really feel like this printer is a definite match for a laser printer in terms of print quality or the ink saturation on a piece of paper. When I print something with a block of darker black, I still have that inkjet damp feeling that a good laser printer avoids (at least to my recollection). I also did a test Word document with cluster diagrams and gradient shading in some of the blocks. I couldn't get the subtlety of the shading in the results at normal quality.I really like the copy features of this printer. Unlike most lower cost printers on the wireless market, this copier will actually let you add borders, enlarge a page, etc. from the console. After years of blowing things up in Photoshop or Windows Picture Viewer and then sending them to the printer, it is nice to hit a few buttons and get things rolling. The printer also auto-enlarges some documents for you. I put a standard stationery size letter on the bed and it blew up it to fit the 8.5 by 11 inch piece of paper without my telling it to. I timed it a few different times and 16.5 seconds seems to be the full time for a copy from hitting the "Start" button - this includes the scan for the initial copy. If you ask for multiple copies of the same document, it goes a little faster.

TheLogitech Speaker Lapdesk N700is definitely a luxury and an imperfect product. The sound improvement is not nearly as good as desktop computer speakers.  Still, it is an improvement over most internal speakers.  Similarly, the cooling is not the best out of the available coolers out there.  And the comfort of this unit as a lapdesk is also not the greatest.  But the combination of all these features in one unit make this a serviceable product.PROS:++ Sound is a step-up from internal laptop speakers++ Fabric bottom is thick enough and provides some friction for stability++ Integrated fan provides minimal cooling for your laptop++ Fan is extremely quiet++ Thick plastic body deflects remaining heat away from your lap++ USB connector powers the speakers and cooler++ Includes on-board controls: on / off switch, volume controls and a mute button++ Included rubber inserts can be placed in the fan grill to lift your laptop++ Flip-up *tabs* in the front provide a little stability so your laptop won't slide forwardCONS:-- Unit may be too heavy for some people-- Sound is still not great given the MSRP-- Padding is so firm it may be uncomfortable for some-- No curve in the surface to allow heat to escape from under your computer-- Curved bottom prevents the unit from laying flat in your lap-- The unit isn't deep enough, so it's unstable if you put it forward so the curve hugs your knees-- No mouse tray like the one in theLogitech N315 Portable Lapdesk-- Fan doesn't have any speed controls; it's either on or off-- The list price is excessive for what you get-- Only available with the cream colored surfaceThe weight of this unit may bother some people, as it is a little heavy.  This wasn't a huge issue for me but your mileage may vary.  The weight and design will prevent some smaller people from using it comfortably in their laps.  Those with a smaller laptop or a netbook should definitely consider theLogitech N550 Speaker Lapdesk.  It will accommodate up to a 13 inch laptop, like theApple MacBook Pro MC700LL/A 13.3-Inch Laptop, or anything smaller.  Just keep in mind that the N550 has no fan for active cooling, while the N700 does.Comfort is an issue with all of these lapdesks.  This unit has the thick padding and curved back that is shared by theLogitech N500 Comfort Lapdesk.  That unit includes no cooling or speakers.CONCLUSIONThis is a good product that is a jack of all trades, but it's worth the compromises.  It has some flaws, and it's not great in any one area.  But the combination of features is unique.  There's nothing else quite like it and I recommend it.  Just try to get it on sale if possible.Enjoy.

This is a great idea.  This looks and feels exactly like a plain white ruled tablet, which is the type I prefer to take my household notes on anyway.  The sorting/resorting ability is a great way to save those notes that I want to keep around for a while without having to fold them to the back while trying to keep them from tearing off the rest of the pad.  The perforations allow you to turn it into a standard size piece of paper when necessary.

The reviews of this device were so positive that I had to take the plunge and give it a try. Really, this is what I've wanted from the beginning-- Google Voice on a regular phone so I can receive calls when the PC is off. I don't like to talk on the phone much, and overall my phone usage is very minimal and I carry an iPhone at all times. I had a hard time justifying any monthly cost for phone service though I do have Vonage because I work from home and spend a lot of time on conference calls.Setup was 5 minutes or less. Simple. The web interface & device aren't that pretty, but really-- it doesn't matter once the phone is working, assuming there is little maintenance to do.Google Voice web portal really becomes your interface to your phone service, once set up the OBi becomes invisible. You don't *have* to have a PC as they say, but it adds to your ability to manage things.So far, so good. I've placed & received calls. The call quality is what I'd consider "Normal" if you've had Vonage before and had low/normal/high as far as bandwidth consumption goes.Note that it does NOT have Ethernet pass-through like Vonage, so you may find yourself a port short on the router.I'll update the review as I use the service more and see if I have any digital dropout or other issues.

I have no idea how I got through school without one of these for my backpack, but I'm just happy I discovered them in time to use with my kids. I have a sixth grade son who is not naturally organized at all (what 12-year-old boy is?) and his backpack is always in danger of bursting at the seams with piles of papers he has collected at school. Using this vertical orientation filer, we were able to tame the beast and so far (it's been three weeks) it seems to really be helping. We used an ultra-fine sharpie to write on the tabs for each folder, and labeled them as follows:"To Do"- for homework"To Return"- for completed stuff he has to turn in at school"Reference"-for things like basketball schedules and music class reference sheets"Take Home"- For stuff he can get rid of after he shows me"Needs Action"- For stuff I need to see/signHe loves that it doesn't take up too much room in his backpack and protects everything from getting smashed by his books, and that putting his stuff away is as easy as lifting the top flap and slipping the papers down in the appropriate slot. He doesn't even have to remove it from his backpack, which was really important because the whole reason his stuff was always a mess is because he is always in a rush and just shoving it in there. Now at least it's being shoved in a designated spot. This has been an ideal organizing tool to help him keep his papers under control and I would definitely recommend it.

Permanent adhesive labels have been in my home office for more years than I care to remember.  I have used other brands most of the time but thought I would give 3M brand a try.30 labels on a 8.5" x 11" piece of paper provide a quick way to make repetitive labels fast.  Of course, you can create a sheet of 30 different labels if you like as well.  There is plenty of "stick" so you label will stay in place but not so much that you can't get if off your fingers when applying it to the letter/file/etc. and they are inkjet friendly.This is just one more great product that 3M makes.

The cartridge I got was indeed a genuine Brother cartridge. Some previous reviewers had complained about getting non-Brother cartridges, but this problem seems to have been fixed.It comes mailed right in its own box, thanks to Amazon's hassle free packaging. You then use that box (and its cardboard inserts) with the included pre-paid mailing label to mail them your old ink cartridge for recycling (completely free for you). I really appreciate the efforts they've taken to make this product and its packaging more environmentally friendly than others.The cartridge itself came with very clear instructions on how to do the replacement, so you don't have to sit there and guess how to get the old one out and the new one in. I was able to change this cartridge with no confusion and no problems. The machine accepted it perfectly and immediately started printing from it.I have not used this cartridge long enough to judge on yield yet, so I will leave that part out of the review for now.*Note: always prep your new cartridge according to the instructions provided. For these, you shake them horizontally and "clean" them using the green slider at the back, making sure the slider is returned to its original position before installation.

The BIC Triumph pen writes really nice. The tip flows well and isn't scratchy feeling like some rollerball/gel pens can be. It makes a nice bold mark without being blobby. But, it doesn't have enough heft to it to be my favorite pen. When you hold it, it feels fairly flimsy and the click top retractor is plastic. But for the price I can't complain!

My first impression of this pencil cup was that it was small. I wanted something nice to replace the coffee mug full of pens on my desk and I wasn't sure this would hold enough stuff. However, I was able to put a dozen regular pens into it and still have room for more. This takes less desk space than the coffee mug and looks much more professional. The pencil cup has a smooth cloth bottom that won't scratch my desk, and the inside is lined with the same brown cloth. The stitching looks pretty nice. It's not real leather, but it will be easy to take care of.

I needed a smaller portable dry erase board for my math classes that I teach.  This is large enough for my small group to see, but not so big that isn't cumbersome to carry.  I ordered extra markers in difference colors.  The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is that the trim has as unsightly seam that is destined to break apart like all of the other 11 x 14 boards I've had with this same design.
Terrific ink. Works well in my printer. Easy to install. Came quickly. Was packaged in a box way too big for what was being shipped, is my only complaint.

I do a lot of packing and shipping from my home.  A few years ago, I didn't have a clue how very different packing tape could be.  Once you start trying different brands, however, it soon becomes apparent that all tape is not created equal.  I was happy to try this Scotch brand product.  Of note, it is called Security Tape as opposed to Packaging Tape and I'm not entirely sure what this designation entails.Compared against packing tape, this is on the less impressive side.  It is very thin, easy to tangle, and difficult to manage if the roll gets caught up.  As for stickiness and effectiveness, I don't have a particular problem.  I just imagined that Scotch would represent a higher end product and this compares to some bargain tape I've had in the past.I suppose this is called Security Tape due to the "Fragile: Handle With Care" logo emblazoned in red along the roll.  Because this is integrated along box seams during usage where you oftentimes overlap tape to make a solid connection, I was getting the message lost with frequency.  Generally speaking, if you want to securely package something than you might use more than one strip.  But look, at the end of the day, it's tape.  Is the roll useful enough? Sure.  Would I seek it out to buy it in the future? Nope.  KGHarris, 7/13.

These Neon Sharpies are all about fun. They brighten a lightly colored page up with text, circles, etc but I kept thinking of them as highlighters (which they aren't as they have a "normal" fine point Sharpie tip). I think they would be best for school posters, projects and to add a bit of fun to drafts at work.

I'm not sure who would carry this, but it does make a reasonable first impression.  The color, stitching, and hinges look good, but I noticed the following short-comings:1.  The cover material is easily scratched just by using your finger nails,2.  The inside cover sheet holder is opaque, won't hold pages without hanging out of the top of the folder, and the hinge takestwo hands to operate.3.  Additionally the opaque inside paper holder tears easily with repetitive use.So if you want a cheap binder that casts a good first impression and that can be tossed when it falls apart, buy this binder.  If you want to convey a deeper first impression, invest in something nice that will last.  Remember, you only get one shot at a first impression.

This binder has some great features, the most notable being the expandable accordion style folder that is built in and which can be accessed from either the inside or the outside of the binder.  The interior of the binder also has a small Velcro pouch that could hold a handful of pens, and a zippered mesh pocket that allows you to see what is inside.  There is a carrying handle,but the addition of a strap would be an improvement, especially at this price point.  The zippers on this binder operate smoothly and seem sturdy.

Great attention grabbing size for last minute hand-written signs like "This Way (arrow) to Meeting," "Clean Up Your Room," or "Lost Dog." No need to worry about taking off paint. After all, its a Post-it note.

I am on a committee for an Amateur Radio Field Day event (see ARRL for more details) this coming June; I am seeking a viable option for printing custom tickets for a radio club raffle drawing.  Avery has come to the rescue again!On Avery's website I was able to locate online templates, downloadable and customizable templates for MS Word including several pre-existing templates for School Raffles, Sports Raffles, Valentine's Party, etc.  The Avery online software was not only easy to use, but it also allowed for customized sequential numbering, inclusion of custom graphics, bar codes, QR codes, etc.  The templates allow for using the tear off portion on the right, the left or on the top.  Versatile!I ran a test batch of tickets, the tickets printed nicely on both our color laser as well as our multi-purpose inkjet. They were easy to separate without tearing off the ticket stub.  Highly recommend this 5-star product.

I cannot attest to how well this will hold up over time, but it is made of a brilliant, clear, heavy-gauge acrylic and looks great when new. It is a welcome design and my wife has found it attractive and functional in her work office. Injection molding sites are drilled out to look polished and professional. Very nice.
Absolutely would buy no substitutes for my Epson printer. These archival quality colors make photos that last. The colors are clear and not muddy, and perform perfectly on the chosen papers.

This is one of my favorite copy & printing papers. Georgia-Pacific was recommended to me years ago by a copier franchise owner. He told me it would not produce a lot of messy dust in the copier/printer as other papers do. I have been using it ever since. I have always liked the 5-ream pack-seeGP Copy & Print Paper, 8.5 x 11 Inches Letter Size, 92 Bright White, 20 Lb, 5 Reams/Carton (2500 Sheets) (998068C). It's convenient, but was not available this time with "Amazon Prime" shipping. In fact, the price was much higher (not being sold by Amazon). So, I saw these 3-ream cartons with "Prime." Like the 5-ream, these are easy to carry, compared to the bigger boxes of ten reams. I have always found the price to be one of the best bargains. It looks like Amazon is going to keep it like that. One of my main complaints about having paper like this delivered is that they so often come "beat-up!" Then, you have to go through the whole process of returning it. What a pain! I think we all hate that! Right? What's the use? Not this time! These came from the manufacturer in a thicker than normal cardboard box which seemed to resist shipping damage. Hopefully, this is where I will buy all my paper in the future.Update: 4/5/2014 -- Almost a year later, this is where I have bought most of my paper since. I am extremely satisfied with this paper, the size of the box, the convenience, the packing (if you buy more than one box), basically everything! And, in all this time I have not had a "beat-up" box of paper delivered.

I've been using the other EnduraGlide dry erase markers in the classroom for the last month, and have been loving them! I admit that I was a little hesitant at trying these, because my experiences with fine-tip dry erase markers before has been pretty crappy -- they usually just weren't dark enough to see well, even a few feet away. This printer has many great qualities, which I will discuss first. The cons, although insignificant, will be discussed after.My top two pros are basically in the title of my review. In fact, when the 840 came out a few years ago, it was touted as being the 'world's fastest all-in-one' which is the main reason I chose it. Needless to say, that particular printer did not live up to the claims (I wrote a review on it as well). So even though the 4640 was offered to me in exchange for my honest review, I hesitated. But since my older 840 is still going strong despite the less than stellar speed, I decided to give it this one a try... I glad I did!This printer is lightening fast, even with full color. I take a lot of photos and do a lot of color printing, both personally and for our business. I was blown away right from the start. I had run out of my premium photo paper, but still had some Epson Presentation Paper. So I loaded it up and printed an 8 x 10 1/2 full color photo of some flowers from my garden, and it turned out absolutely stunning...and it only took 20 seconds! Colors are vibrant & true, and the photo is as crisp as any I've printed. All subsequent printing I have done, whether black & white or color, has been perfect. And FAST! So to beat a dead horse here, I can't say enough about the quality and speed of this machine!As for the other functions (scanning, copying, faxing), I tried them all to be certain I could give them a thumbs up as well. And of course they all work beautifully. So bottom line I am very satisfied with this all-in-one printer.Before I get to the cons, I will say that yes, this is a big printer. With it set up and the paper trays extended (output tray and rear feed), the printer measures 18" wide x 18 1/2 " tall, x 25 1/2" deep. You will also need to allow room behind it in case you need to access the rear for paper jams, etc. Even though I have not had any paper jams, any good printer should have a rear access just in case.Ok, as I mentioned in the beginning, the cons are really insignificant, but my mention of them may be helpful to some.First of all, setup took longer than I am accustomed to; about 20 minutes to download and install everything. Even though there is a disc, you will be prompted to download the latest software. But once it's done, it's done. So not really anything to affect the rating, just a heads-up really.The second item has to do with which cassette to put premium paper in. The 'quick guide' that comes with the printer says to load photo or premium paper in the upper cassette only, 'in products that have two cassettes'. This printer does have two cassettes (the drawer type), as well as one rear paper feed (as shown in the 3rd thumbnail of the product photos). So, due to the instructions on the 'quick guide', I tried loading the premium paper in the upper cassette. But when I went to the properties box to choose paper type, etc, I couldn't find a choice for any type of premium paper in the 'cassette one' drop down box. Finally after some monkeying around, I was prompted to load premium/photo paper in the rear feed only. So I did, then chose rear paper feed as the source. And what'dya know, from that 'source' I was able to choose which premium paper I was using. So long story short here folks, is that premium papers can be specified only when the rear paper feed is chosen as the paper source.So, those are the cons. Once I got past them, they no longer affect me at all, so no stars were taken away. Hopefully some of you will be saved from the confusion of where to load premium paper.Ok, I think that's about it. If I run into anything else that I think should be mentioned, I will be sure to update my review. Have fun with this printer everyone, it truly is an awesome one!

So I'll start with my biggest complaint with this printer.  By biggest, I literally mean my complaint is this printer's size.  It's huge!  When it arrived at my house, the box was so big and heavy, I thought I was being sent TWO printers.  My office has an old Epson, which also prints 13 x 19", and the Canon Pixma Pro-1 easily dwarfs it in both size and weight.  In fact, it felt twice as heavy as the printer at work, which is why I had to look it up: the Pro-1 weighs in at 61 pounds!  If you're tight on space, but need the ability to print A3, you may want to look into a smaller model, such as one of the Epsons.Another possible negative for this printer is that, while it supports ethernet, meaning several users can access the printer for various jobs, it lacks wireless.  Of course, thismight not be a big deal for most users (and I can't imagine sending a huge TIFF over wifi for a print job), but other printers in this class offer this feature.  Even Canon's own Pro-10 has wireless capabilities, so it's unusual to me that their top-of-the-line model lacks that feature.And my final issue with this printer is with the ink.  As others may have noted, this printer drinks ink.  The initial priming dropped the ink levels by 25% and, heaven forbid you leave the printer inactive for too long (like I did), when it runs that priming cycle again, it delivers yet another big hit to your ink levels.  This might not seem like such a big deal, but when you consider that this printer takes 12 cartridges (11 ink and 1 chroma optimizer!) and costs $400 to replace as a set, you can see that this printer is not meant for the casual photographer who prints sporadically (read: ME).  I've only had it for a few weeks and after a handful of prints of various sizes and two priming cycles, I'm at 50%!  Of course, if I printed more regularly, I'm sure I'd see much better ink usage.  I would like to note, though, that this can be seen as a wash, because while it does drink ink, the tanks hold more ink than most other large printers, so you theoretically can make more prints (as long as you avoid that pesky priming/maintenance cycle).Now while most of my review seems focused on the negatives, it's because they are relatively minor if what you're in the market for is image quality.  If print quality is your main concern, then the Pixma Pro-1 is pretty much the only printer you should be looking at.  Some may argue that if you're printing large, from a distance, most people won't notice a difference between prints from this printer or one from a cheaper, smaller model.  While that may be true for some people, we photographers are a picky bunch and if you're showing off a photo, nothing but the best will do.  And with the Pro-1, you'll want to make sure your lens is tack sharp and your camera packs enough megapixels, because any graininess or softness will show.And while color prints are eye-popping, it's the monochrome prints that will make any black and white photographer's jaw drop.  Canon uses five (FIVE!) tanks of black and grays, which leads to the best gradation in black and white photos that I have seen from a sub-$1K printer.  I'm talking gallery-quality 13x19" prints with fantastic contrast and zero tint.  Simply amazing!Before I wrap up my review, I'd like to throw in some last-minute info that might be important to some readers.  The Pro-1 also includes a tray to allow for direct label printing to CD/DVDs, which I can't comment on, because I never used, though I'm assuming it works in much the same way as any other printer I've used.Print speed seemed about average, if a little slow, with a 4x6" color print finishing in about 2 minutes.  And yes, the Pro-1 can print word/text documents, though with the cost of ink, I can't imagine anyone really using it for that other than to avoid the dreaded priming cycle or because their regular printer is down.  Finally, and this might be important to some, while the paper feed can accept media of varying thickness/quality, the Pro-1 can NOT print from paper rolls--cut sheets only.For me, the Pixma Pro-1 boils down to one thing:  How important is image quality?  Sure you can find another 13x19" photo printer that can output 90% of the quality at half the weight/size, much less money, and with more interface options.  But there's always that 10%...  If you print a lot of black and white photos or if seeing your work in pristine quality is a top priority, then the Pro-1 should be at the very top of your list.

As a homeschooler, my printer gets a real workout day in and day out. I tend to be fairly hard on our printers because of this fact. Getting the printer connected to the wireless network was extremely simple. It can be done directly on the printer or on the computer once software is installed. While some people do not like the multiple ink cartridges, I appreciate them as there are definitely some colors that get used more frequently than others, so I appreciate being able to save money by just replacing that particular ink color.Concerns:On multiple occasions, I had issues with the printer cancelling a print job for large documents. I do not have this issue on my hp printer, so I was a little disappointed to see this happening.Another problem is the inability to feed documents for scanning/copying. The photos comes out looking beautiful.  It also works great as a document printer.  The duplex printing as well as multiple ink color cartridges are nice economical features. While I did run into a few issues as mentioned above, the printer did a nice job with the various print jobs as long as I kept the limitations in mind (create small print jobs). The printer works well with our Windows 7 computers and wireless network.If you're looking for a space saving printer, this may not be the printer for you as it does have a fairly big footprint. This lead is great for drawing or writing, HB is a firmer lead so it won't break as much but it's still dark enough to resist smudging (all lead is going to potentially smudge a little bit, but a softer lead will be darker and smudge more).Here's a list of lead grades from firm (lighter writing) to soft (darker writing):4H - 3H - 2H - H - F - HB - B - 2B - 3B - 4BThere are others but these are more commonly seen ones.
