The outside little pen-pockets are handy if you're leaving class fast and want to stuff your pen or pencil somewhere, and the zippered compartment on the front cover is handy for another couple of backup writing utensils, plus it'll fit a phone.The inside has a very small pocket for business cards or something similar, and folder-style pockets to hold syllabi, etc. in addition to the 3-ring binder section.This is a 2-inch binder, but it's a bit bigger than a regular binder with the rounded cover and zippers.  The main binder zipper doesn't close completely, which would be a problem if you're used to throwing your pens in the binder after the lecture, but since you've got a couple handy spots to quickly stash a pen on the outside cover, no problem.This is a nice binder, which seems likely to last a school year, and it's a pretty color, which is easy to see and grab amongst the mess of books, etc. where I keep it.

This is a great printer/fax/scanner/copier, especially for the price.It was easy to set up.  I had it set within a half hour after un-boxing it.I set it up to use my wireless router.  I installed the drivers on 3 computers-  1 running XP, one running Vista 64 bit, and one running Vista 32 bit.  It worked fine on all the operating systems.The printing quality is great.  For larger files it is a little slow, but they were 25 mb pictures.  Regular printing is very fast.The fax worked great.  Just plugged it in and made a few configuration changes.It copies in both black and white, and in color.  We like the top loading tray.  You don't have to lift the lid, your document just feeds through.The manual and the user interface made setting it up very easy.We needed a wireless printer because of the location we wanted to place it in.  It is nice because you can put it anywhere you have a plug.All in all I highly recommend this printer.

Wonderful for white boards.  This new product will even remove permanent marker, if you accidentally get it on your white board. (Which often happens in classrooms--oopsie--yes, I am guilty!) This eraser should hold up well to white board use.  I must admit when I saw how well the eraser did on the whiteboards, I attacked the tables,  permanent markings, glue, dirt and all.  This was a mistake, as a small portion of the eraser fell off.  These are not made for heavy cleaning of tables covered with gunk.They really cleaned the whiteboard, for which they were designed just fine, amazingly well in fact. However, they will start to fall apart with vigorous scrubbing of other surfaces.  For the white boards, they are a dream--so erase on.  You will find this product, money well-spent!

I use a lot of sheet protectors, specifically for recipes in a kitchen cookbook.  The sheet protectors allow me to keep the printed recipes relatively protected from spills and splatters so that I can have a conveniently organized recipe book without having to constantly replace papers.  I always need a few more sheet protectors, though, as my recipe collection expands, plus over time some sheet protectors get so grimy (despite wiping) as to need replacement.  That's where this product comes in!These claim to be “heavy weight” and as far as I can tell after comparing them to my standard weight protectors, they are a bit thicker.  I'm not sure, however, that they are so much heavier as to justify their increased price from the standard ones (they are, however, competitive with other brands for their weight as far as I can tell).  Either way, they are decent page protectors, and work well.  I was even able to fit five pages in one comfortably (not sure why you'd want to, though).  Size-wise, they are the same size dimensions as every page protector I've ever bought before, so nothing new there.  The holes for the binder are made of a slightly heavier plastic than the main body, which can help prevent tearing, so that is much appreciated.Well, there's not much more to say.  These are decent page protectors if you really want heavy weight ones, but I'm not sure they are so much more protective than standard weight as to justify their cost.  They perform well though, so I can't really complain!

I'm an Epson fan, anyway, and I must say, they packed a huge amount of features into this scanner! What quality! My wife had an old color slide ( 50+ yrs.)...as she was preparing to scan it, the "color positive" film came out of the cardboard frame...we placed it the space anyway, without the frame, and this scanner brought out 2 other people in the picture, that had not been visible when it was in the slide frame format. The resolution is brilliant, and this scanner can handle any task. I was going to buy a little scanner, that you put one slide at a time in, then I saw the Epson V330 for not too much more, and made my choice. It handles all types of film and slides, and photos, and text, and book pages...is light and doesn't take up a lot of space. Works great set up to the right of your work area, as the cover opens from left to right. Great product, and I recommend!

I love this X-ACTO Commercial Guillotine Trimmer! Wow this baby is sharp, and cuts like a dream! I had 10 sheets of printer paper and wanted to make a note book the size I was looking for and put it in the cutter and it cut so smooth and clean cut! I have always wanted one of these for my projects and was happy to try this one. It is LARGE so if you are looking for craft items and do not have room I would recomend a smaller size. I have a craft room and a table that it fits on nicely so it works well for me. Highly recomend!

I really like the Fellowes Saturn SL Laminator. It works well and is easy to use. My documents come out clean and professional every time. I also like that this machine runs cool so it's pretty safe. The laminator came with ten 3-mil letter-size pouches which was nice so I didn't have to go hunting for laminating sheets right away.I don't particularly like the design however. You have to feed paper directly from the back, instead of from the top. It makes things awkward because the only place I'm able to store the laminator is flush against the wall. I have to move it to another location in order to use it. It seems you need a pretty large work space to use this device. Luckily, it has a carry handle and it's extremely light weight. That brings me to the quality. For the price, it's pretty cheap looking. It's made almost entirely of plastic and the silver color looks spray painted on. I'm just saying, if you're looking for a high quality looking machine for the amount paid, this isn't it.Fortunately, I value function over style and as far that, this machine delivers. Therefore only one star was lost for the latter. I would still recommend this laminator.

Overall, this is a very nice printer and scanner.  Below are my specific comments on what I like, don't like, and wish it had.What I like:1. How fast it scans and prints.2. The quality of the scan and prints.3. How easy it is to use the LED control panel.4. The USB connection was easy to set up (but you do need your own cable).5. That it will print from the Cloud or mobile devices (I haven't used this feature yet).6. The variety of settings that can be used and tweaked for scanning or copying.What I don't like:1. The non-transparent ink cartridges.  My other Canon printers have transparent ink cartridges which makes it easy to see when the cartridge really is out of ink and needs to be replace.  Being able to change the cartridges only when they actually need it is a great way to cut down on the cost of inks for any printer!2. Even though it is only 6 inches high--it takes up a lot of desk space at 18.5" by 15".What I wish it had:1. An auto-feed mechanism for scanning or copying multiple pages.2. Larger capacity paper trays.3. A larger size platen.  This one is only 8.5 x 12. With the printer being so long and wide it would seem like they could make the platen larger as well!I hope this helps you decide on if this is the printer for you!

Included in this pack are 4 retractable ballpoint pens in 3 colors: black, blue, and red.  Overall these are decent pens.  The ink dries fast and does not smudge.  I didn't find anything "special" about them, but they are good every day pens.

Admittedly, when you're buying a wide format printer, you know it's not going to be some petite little thing that can fit anywhere, that said, I was a bit surprised by the size and weight of this printer when it arrived. At over 40lbs and nearly 2 feet wide, proper lifting procedures are required to unpack and set it up.Speaking of setup, this was significantly more of a hassle than I've had recently with other MFC's by Canon and HP. Printing to devices setup was most tedious, requiring an Epson account and the creation of an email address for the printer. Overall I found the process was less user friendly than it could have been. The other downside is that when you're printing from the app there's no option for color or b&w; (it defaults to color).I love that this can scan double-sided documents. What a time saver! I don't like that draft mode results in very light prints, it needs some setting between "so light the UPS and USPS scanners won't read it" and "perfect print that uses too much ink".But honestly, the main reason to own a printer this big is for the wide format printing and scanning capabilities. And this printer really shines at wide format. I've owned other wide format MFC printers that were able to print up to 11 x 17, but would only scan 9 x 14. Being able to print up to a whopping 13 x 19 and scan documents up to 11 x 17 is a real game changer. I'm able to scan old books and photo albums without having to mess with pasting a few images together, and printing this large means I can create more professional looking booklets, posters, and other documents right from my desktop.I do some graphic poster design, and it was always frustrating to have to print out a shrunk-down 8.5 x 11 version of the design and tell the client to try and visualize it larger. Now I can output drafts nearly as large as the finished product and the customer doesn't have to imagine anything, it's right there in front of him.I'm also very impressed with the print quality. Even photos come out color correct and very crisp at 11 x 17. I haven't tried anything larger because bigger photo paper is quite expensive - although I plan on testing it out soon. How great to be able to print photos this large without having to pay a higher price and wait for an online service to deliver them.If you do any graphics or photography work and find yourself sending medium-sized projects to your local print shop, you'll find this printer pays for itself pretty quickly in cheaper output costs and time savings. If they'd update the setup process, this would definitely be a 5-star printer.

I am working on a photo book project and I needed a binder larger than my old 1" o-ring binder I've used for years. When this binder arrived, I liked it immediately. It is well made with firmly melted seams. The inside cover pockets were not quite deep enough, but they, too were well sealed in the seam. My favorite feature is the function of the d-ring closures. The cover lays flat, so I can easily insert new pages or replace pages with ones I've edited without losing my place. It appears to me that the 1.5" d-rings hold as much as the 2" o-ring binders. Anyway, I certainly recommend it for people like me who want print copies of projects as well as digital copies.

I was in the market for an office chair so was glad to be offered the opportunity to try this one out, especially after seeing it was a HON. The box arrived in horrific shape; it looked like several people had beaten and kicked it severely for awhile or had rolled it down the side of a mountain. One flap on top was completely open and the box was covered in black crud. I feared some parts would be missing but thankfully, that was not the case. I think the box was not sufficiently sized for the weight of the chair and combining that with rough treatment from the delivery company caused it to look this way.I was surprised at how light the seat was but how heavy the back section was, although most of this was probably from the metal part of the frame which connected to the seat. The plastic piece that went over the middle section of the star base was rather pathetic - it did not fit properly and I was afraid any attempts to push it on better would snap it in two. The casters were quite difficult to get in the base but once in, felt like they would stay in place. I was very disappointed to see how cheaply made they were, being made completely of plastic except for the part that plugged into the base.From there, the most difficult task was holding the heavy back in place while screwing it onto the seat. The arms were not difficult to install after determining which way was the proper installation (instructions were not very helpful in this regard).  Overall, this chair took less time for me to setup than any other office chair I have purchased. It looks very nice although I thought the seat seemed rather firm and would likely be uncomfortable sitting for extended periods of time. My son tried it out and fell immediately in love with it. We did have to loosen the tilt adjustment quite a lot to allow the chair to lean back at all; we probably had to turn it 15-20 times.  It looks very nice at my son's desk and he is enjoying it without any complaints of it being too hard. Looking at the price of the chair, I think it is over-priced for the quality of what you are receiving when considering the cheap casters and the hard seat. However, it has held up well for the past month and looks very sharp in the office.

I like the smaller roll since I do not do much mailing.  It stuck to my box and tore easily when I used it.  I'm sure if I were purchasing tape at Christmas, I would want a longer roll, but for general use, it is perfectly fine tape.

This is a terrific product and can be mounted with the enclosed magnets or double stick tape. I am currently using this one at my office. It comes with a marker and two magnetic markers that you can place on certain dates for events, etc. If I am out of the office or my co-worker is we will place one of the markers on a specific date. Not sure if you can order more of the dots but I will have to research this. It does not come with a dry eraser; however, any towel or sponge will work. Can be used over and over again. Very impressive product and great idea for a smaller office or fore home on the refrigerator or wall. Gave it 4 starts because there was no eraser included. Otherwise it is a good value.

This is a neat little device for opening those hard clear plastic sealed packages. It sometimes works well but doesn't completely solve the problem of opening those packages. It used to easily cut the packages on the straight sides but doesn't work as well on the corners. And some packages have a sealed opening at the top where the package can hang on a rack, it also doesn't do much to cut that area open.The Scotch Safe Cut has a little cutting blade that you extend out by pushing down on a button at the top of the Safe Cut. Then when you are done you can retract it so the blade is covered and no chance of cutting yourself. It is supposed to have a refillable blade but I cannot find them anywhere. Overall, the price is reasonable and I highly recommend the Scotch Safe Cut as the best method yet to open those pesky plastic packages and believe me, I have tried everything.However, I finally gave up on this Scotch package opener as it wouldn't cut most of the plastic sealed packages that I got recently and the cutter kept falling out of the holder. I ended up just throwing it away as it was more trouble to use than it was worth. A good idea failed for poor design and implementation.

I do a lot of small package shipments and have just been using the standard clear shipping tape.  I normally run multiple pieces to ensure that the package will not break open in shipment.  I thought I would try this product to see if I can use less shipping tape for a package.Here is what I liked:1.  Tape fits into standard dispenser.2.  One strip of tape is extremely strong and resists breakage, this equates to less tape used.Here is what I did not like:1.  The tape is difficult to cut.  Perhaps my tape gun is just not as sharp as a new one, but it takes more effort to cut the tape.  I am tempted to us a box cutter instead of the cutting edge on the tape gun.Overall, I am very happy with the tape and can live with the extra effort to cut it.  Just something to be aware of.

You don't need to buy a laminating machine with possible heat/burn problems. All you need is some of these self laminating sheets.The pros:1. Cost effective means for laminating items for home, school, etc.2. Kids can laminate cards, certificates, etc. with assistance from a teenager or adult.3. Easy to use. The back of the sheet has simple instructions. There is a grid in 1" squares so that you can easily fit your item, mark and cut with a paper cutter or scissors.4. Laminate forms a nice, clear seal and is easy to smooth out bubbles.5. Works well on photos processed from film.6. Works well on paper. I tried on a 8 1/2" x 11" sheet and even though I had to pull back and adjust a bit this did not affect the paper.7. You can mark with a dry erase marker and wipe clean.Cons:1. Does not work well on pharmacy kiosk prints from digital. I tried on a print and when I went to peel back to adjust the sheet it pulled off the photo image. Good thing it was a replaceable digital reprint.2. It does take some care and practice to line up the corners.3. The look and feel is not quite as professional or sturdy as laminate from a machine.4. If you want something more solid, like an "out of office" card that will be used over and over, you might want to go with a machine laminate.

While put off by the cutesy teenage daisy design, I decided this mouse pad might be just the ticket for use with my optical mouse.  After using it for a couple of weeks, I've found that the gel wrist pad is too thick and causes my hand to fall asleep.  Other than that, the mouse works well on the surface and it grips well to my desk top.  I've been using it with the gel wrist pad turned to the top.

There's no more economical printer to operate than a Kodak.  In trying to remake themselves in a world shifting away from celluloid, Kodak has tried to rebrand themselves as a printer company.  The shift makes sense, and they've churned out some good products too.  But the company still seems to be struggling.  I hope they stay in the printer business because they really are far more economical to buy and maintain than any other printer we've found.  This ink isn't the most vibrant or true to color, but it's perfect for everyday use.  You don't have to stress over every little thing you print with this one.  Save the expensive ink changes for those special once-in-awhile prints you need to make.  This Kodak stuff is for everything else.

It's cute and a very stylish way to decorate your desk at work. This is one purse you can leave at the office. Just large enough to see what it is but it doesn't take up more space than a regular post it dispenser.
These labels are made from quality paper and really adhere to many surfaces.  My printer and these labels resulted in a professional job.

My first reaction to this was probably the same as people when pre-sliced bread came out. "What?!" Then I got to know it, and it is great! The deskgrip dispensers stick to most surfaces, with no sticky residue or mess, and are easy to move, they cling by a small rubber mat and can slide around no problem, just move to the edge to break the seal and relocate as needed. These are not made to be refilled although I am sure people have tried! The wrist dispensers are. just. awesome. They have an adjustable elastic strap and *bang* precut tape at your fingertips, great for wrapping presents. You could wear one on each wrist for ambidextrous wrapping. Very easy to refill, just slide the door open (to prevent loss or breakage, it does not come off completely), load the pad of precut strips in and close the door. So easy, so quick, so great!

I need the ink for my printer but I hate paying so much. My printer takes the 225 and 226 blank ink, but this does not have the 226. I'm not sure what the difference is between the two black inks, but since they are already selling this large combo why not include it?

This is a high quality, sturdy product.  There are 6 color-coded poly folders that fit within a larger file that closes shut- it is like a more versatile version of an accordion file, since the folders can be removed.  It can be hung on a wall (try Command hooks to not damage the wall surface) for space saving, so that all folders are easily visible and accessible.  There is a pocket on the front that is handy for loose papers or to show a calendar sheet (as shown on the package).  When it is folded up and closed, it is readily portable.  The folder colors are nice and bright (but not neon bright).  The outer folder is grey and looks professional when closed and on-the-go.  One thing I did not like was that the size of the folders was somewhat larger compared to a standard file folder – this makes it difficult to use them separate from the main file.  This is a great product, depending on your needs; it did not work exactly for how I wanted to use but I still recommend it.

The 3M Gel Mousepad Wrist Rest is just what I've been needing. When I use my computer for long periods of time, I find that my wrist is very sore. I did not take the clear plastic backing off the back, and I'm not having any problems with  the mouse skidding around at all. It has a smooth movement over the top of the pad.  I love the fact that the padding that fits under your wrist has a cool soothing feeling to it!The box has the following written on the bottom " Precise Mousing Surface Extends Battery Life 75% for wireless mice."I'm more than pleased with this product.

Everyone in our family is loving these pens. The pastels were a bit rough to start, however, one the ink got flowing they were fine. No issues with the glitter or metallics. We like the large variety in colors, and the very handy carrying cases. It's great how you can flip the lids around on the cases to stand the pens upright. My oldest daughter is using them at the moment to take notes from her Biology book, she thinks they are great and has asked if she can keep them. We all like them so much that she will probably just have to share!
THIS is the correction tape to use.  The Bic that I bought I had to throw away because it kept tearing and there was no way to rewind it.The Paper Mate works every time with no fuss.

Ok, I spend a lot of time at my computer both at work and home.  Footrests help with lower back pain (most people).  What about a footrest with a fan?The fan is mostly a gimmick.  The unit I received pushed very little air so as to be of limited value in cooling off your feet.  This appears to be a design problem since the fan is in the center of the footrest (between the feet).  However, the heat function worked as indicated though it smelled for the first few hours (coated heating element?). The footrest itself sits high off the ground with very minimal adjustments.  The build quality seems very solid however and the nobby surface feels good if you take your shoes off.The major problem I have is that of other reviewers. I cannot get my knees under the desk when using this footrest.  Not sure if this is an issue with all footrests since this is my first try at using one.  Even after a number of tries, it is awkward at best. I am only 5'11" so I am not sure why this is an issue.This might be a buy in the $15 range.  At the current price, I would stay away.

So you need a dry-erase calendar to plot out your...let's say...plans to rule the world? This is the one for you. It's small, so it doesn't take up a lot of wall space, but it's still big enough to be useful. You get a pen of questionable usefulness, and a couple of little magnets. It is fairly simple, but it does get the job done.

These labels are GREAT!  We print labels on our InkJet printer to label bottles for my daughter's daycare.  We had been using regular mailing labels that left a sticky residue on the Dr. Brown's bottles.  These labels stick great but then peel off easily without leaving a sticky substance on the bottles.  What a fantastic find... we will continue to purchase for this purpose.  Nice bright colors - they stick to things well but remove easily with no gunk left behind, and no damage to the label when removed.  Lots of uses for these labels!

Yes. Meg, you really do. This review will directly compare the HP OfficeJet Pro 8610 Printer with the Epson WorkForce WF-3540 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer, as they are both in the same price range and feature many of the same functions. Here we go!SET UP/APPEARANCE: As noted in other reviews, the OfficeJet Pro is kinda ungainly. Inelegant. Looks like a big black rock sitting next to me. About 1 hr. total set-up soup to nuts, and nothing too difficult or weird. You can watch a video about the printer features on the touchscreen as you set up the machine, and videos pop up on how to install various parts. Nice. This was easier to install than the Epson, mostly because it did not require a physical connection for set up. I do not always have an extra cable lying around. The only problem came when I tried to set up the fax: The OfficeJet asked me questions about the type of internet service I have that I actually did not know the answers to, and it tried to make me chose between having voice mail or having a separate answering machine, when I have both and the answering machine is built into the phone itself. I'm not sure that I won't run into fax problems because of the ambiguity of the options. The Epson printer didn't bother with any of that. Also, you can only use the phone cord that comes with the OfficeJet. What a terrible idea; how am I suppose to hunt around for a specific phone cord when I need to send the occasional fax? The Epson has the OfficeJet beat here hands down.USE: I like the touchscreen on this HP printer better than the one on the Epson. It's more sensitive, the display screen is bigger, and it's easier and more intuitive to use. Also, I can plug a USB storage device directly into the front of the printer. YAY. The Epson doesn't have that function; you have to use a SD card, which I don't like doing (they're too small and get lost easily). While you still have to play around with the interface to figure out what every button does, there are a LOT more tutorials/instruction pages on the OfficeJet, which I really appreciate. The ID scan function is GREAT, taking only a fraction of the time and doing a much better job.PRINTING QUALITY: As other reviewers have noted, it's okay. This is not the printer you want to get for printing out your prize artwork or presentation to Warren Buffet. I use my printers for everyday business and personal documents, virtually nothing else, and this machine is fine for that. The Epson has superior photo printing.OVERALL: This is actually better for my current needs than the Epson All In One, because 1.) I can scan to and print off of a USB device and 2.) I can easily scan ID cards, which I have to do all the time. 2-sided printing is also easier. If you need high-quality photo printing get the Epson, or another specialty printer. I am deducting a star here for the annoying fax issues and comparatively poor print quality on photos. Otherwise I liked it. Keep in mind HP, like Epson, will try to get your location and feedback sent from your printer on your every move, and you have to repeatedly deny them that all during set-up and after (they even offered me a "reward" because I installed their branded ink, but oops! they won't tell me what it is or let me redeem it until I agree to let them track me. How about, no.).  Also, Meg Whitman loves to talk about keeping jobs from going overseas but this printer is made in China. Yup.GRADE: BUPDATE 7/7/14: I almost upgraded the star rating to five, after printing out a host of two-sided copies. Two-sided copying on this printer is easy, and, as noted, the speed is excellent. But then I noticed that out of approximately ten separate jobs, the printer jammed twice. Each time the copy was ruined and once I had to fish it out of the heart of the printer by taking apart the front of the machine. 20% is not a good jam rate, unless you're a sandwich. So at four stars it stays.

This is a unique little package but it has it's limitations:- doesn't stick to binders- plastic is rigid- closure is difficult to use- not very deep therefore capacity is smallI will use them on dividers to store note cards and such but I can't see myself using them for a whole lot else.
This is a great deal for only $13.  I bought a single ream for $12 last time and this is a way better deal. It also arrived quickly.

What do I look for in a pen?  Smooth writing, an easy ink flow, a comfortable grip, and no smears.  Uni-ball Jetstream 101 Bold Point Rollerball Pens offer all this and more.This is an easy pen to write with; the ink flows smooothly and consistently. As a lefty I'm all too familiar with ink smears, and since it's quick drying this is an easy pen for me to use.Ease of grip is important in a pen for lengthy meetings or classes, and this pen is easy to hold, though not as easy as the specially designed padded pens.  But for the general user, it should be just fine.I like that it can be used for checks without fear of alteration; now if it just covered overdrafts.This set contains three colors:  black, blue, and red.Five stars. These are as described, heavier than the average manilla folder.  They are nice, assorted colors and do have larger tabs.  I immediately transferred some of my altered art clippings to a couple of these, and maybe these will help keep me more organized!  Very nice product.

I love these boxes.  You have an easy lift off lid, fits securely, and the width of the box is not to wide, making it easier to push against a wall and not take up too much space.The boxes have grab-hold slots on the side, as always needed.  Plus, there is an extra sheet of cardboard to have the bottom more secure and durable. Ok, you must think I'm nuts to be so enthusiastic about post-its...well, my entire desk is covered in them, and my daughter uses them as a phone book!  I love alternating colors to brighten up the notes I send to my staff, and the original yellow ones were getting boring!When leaving notes around the house for hubby, or a reminder before I left the house, I would have to tape my regular post it's with scotch tape.  So when I saw these new full adhesive notes were available for me to try through the Amazon Vine program, I grabbed them right away!They are the same size and color combo that are offered on the older version, but boy, these stick just great!  I don't have to worry about them falling off and my note getting lost..and as I work a lot from home and have to send actual paperwork back and forth, it's just perfect for my needs.I may even try them as gift tags for our holiday presents...

This is way more shredder than I probably need on a regular basis, but I'm in decluttering mode and really appreciated the speed and capacity while getting rid of a large box of old paper files!This shredder is best suited to a small business.  It's about the size of a large kitchen trash can but a little shorter and has locking wheels.  I admit to have gotten spoiled at work where "shredding" confidential documents means dropping them through the nice wide slot of the locked box that a shredding company comes and picks up every couple weeks.  So when I first started tackling a copy paper box full of old files, this shredder seemed a little slow.  And then I remembered my previous home shredder that had a measly 3 page capacity and was even slow in grinding through that little amount.  In comparison, this one is super speedy! It will take 16 pages at a time and chops through them pretty quickly.For security purposes, it shreds the paper into very very tiny pieces and when you shred multiple pages together, the pieces curl into each other.  I suppose a dedicated spy master could reassemble the shredded material but it would be a massive undertaking -- unless the CIA is going through your recycling, you shouldn't have to worry about anyone being able to read your shredded data.The 7-gallon bin holds a lot.  I shredded enough papers to fill it (there is a light that tells you when it is full -- along with the nice clear bin front so you can see it is full) and emptied it into a large kitchen trash bag, which I put into my recycling bin. The Workforce 630 is a solid all-in-one that will suit buyers looking for an affordable all-purpose solution to moderate printing, scanning, and copying needs.The setup is easy and I didn't have any major trouble with it. I had some difficulty setting it up in a wireless network initially, and had to interface it with my Windows 7 machine via USB to get the drivers installed, which the setup literature recommends for first setup anyway. Not a deal-breaker at all, but be advised that you may need to do the same before you station it away from your machine(s) and use it wirelessly. Driver installation wasn't a problem, and I haven't had any issues with incompatibility or detection.I was happy to discover that the ink cartridges were actually full, instead of half-full, which the pack-in cartridges usually seem to be with new printers. I also appreciate the four-cartridge system (discrete carts for black, yellow, blue, and magenta inks), although in past experiences, the color inks have depleted at a more-or-less even rate, but it's still nice to be able to replace only the colors that need replacing. Although this means you'll need to spend more money on carts when it's time to replace them, they'll last longer, and if you primarily do black-and-white printing (as I do), you won't need to replace them too often. The black cartridge has a bigger capacity than the others.The build is solid and the on-board interface is excellent- very intuitive with helpful on-screen guides. The supplied literature is also good- straightforward and easy to consult.The printing performance is very serviceable. I mainly print text documents, and am satisfied with the performance- not laserjet quality, of course, but definitely adequate. Graphics and diagrams come out sharp, too, and as long as you're not expecting your prints to look like laserjet prints, you'll be happy. Photos look fine, but this isn't a photo printer, so if you're a pro photographer, don't expect to use the 630 for your work or anything. Two-sided printing is a little more involved than I would have liked, but it gets the job done.The scanner works great and is pretty quick, as is the copier. I was a little disappointed with the speed on full-color copies, but again, we're not looking at a multi-hundred-dollar machine. As long as you're not trying to crank out 60 pages a minute or anything, you should be happy with the performance. I've not used the fax function, so I can't comment on it.One potential issue (which I've noticed other reviewers mention) is that the paper tray has a manual-centering format, which means you have to center the paper, then set the position of  the tray guides manually. I've only printed 8.5"x11" documents to this point, and haven't had any issues, but I can see potentially having some off-center prints as the result of not properly setting the guides on other sizes of paper. I'm not sure what the solution to this will be, other than printing a few test sheets, but I can't see it being a major problem. For special-format printing, like labels or stickers, users may need to make note of custom configurations, so as not to waste blank sheets.All things considered, the machine performs fine, and I'm happy with it. The build is primarily plastic parts, so I'll have to wait and see if there are any durability-issues with it as time passes, but for now, there are no problems.In summary, this is a solid printer that will appeal to general-purpose home and small-business users. It's a $100-range machine, and it won't replace the large office printer or the photo printer, but it's recommended for buyers who are just looking for an all-purpose machine for their desktop or home-use needs.

The applicator on the Scotch brand is precise and easy to use, but the real appeal is the clog-resistant bottle.  In the past, I've only needed super glue maybe once or twice a year, so getting the glue flowing again was always a pain because the tip would dry out--not so with the Scotch.The first time I used it was when my daughter broke a figurine that she'd gotten just the day before.  I applied the Scotch easily and let it dry overnight.  It bonded so well that I let her take the figurine to school a few days later for sharing.  A few weeks later, my daughter (notice a theme here?) broke a couple of cups from her ceramic play tea set. That's pretty much all you can ask for in a super glue.  I recommend it.

The Epson WorkForce Pro WP-4530 really surpassed most of my expectations.  For a home office or a small office, it's a wonderfully viable option.I'll start by saying that I received this Epson as a review unit.  I installed it in my home office and temporarily placed it on the print stand that my wireless HP has occupied the past two years.  However, the Epson will now be staying for a long time.The footprint of the WorkForce Pro is rather large.  Much larger than any HP or Brother that I've used and it's on par with the laserjet printers I have at work.  But the device is solid through and through.  There is a lot of blue tape that you will have to initially remove, but after that set-up is a breeze.  The cartridge door opens up in front and you shake and then pop the large ink cartridges in one at a time.  They easily slide into their designated slots and have a satisfying click when you push them in.  Terrific design.  The buttons on the face of the printer are all laid out well, and the color screen efficiently relays all the pertinent information needed.  The paper drawer does take some getting used to, but the entire thing pops out and essentially acts as a "paper cartridge" for your printing needs.  I load up at least 200 sheets of regular duty office paper at one time and it has room to spare.  While entire printer is big and somewhat bland, this is a great example of perfect functionality over stylish form.  I'll take that functionality anytime.I've installed several HP and Brother wireless printers in the past, and the Epson's wireless install was by far the easiest.  The included CD walks you through each minimal step.  It suggests that the first time you set up the printer that you use a USB cable (not included).  If you know your wireless router's SSID and passcode, I actually recommend just going straight to advanced wireless set-up.  It's not difficult at all.  The CD directs you to the printer when it's time, and you can simply ID or input your SSID, and then enter in the corresponding WEP or WPA code using the buttons on the printer.  Piece of cake.  During the procedure, the CD asks if you want to look for updated drivers.  I selected yes, the install wizard automatically downloaded them and then installed them.  Then it asked if I want to check for updated firmware.  I selected Yes, the program found the firmware, downloaded it and installed it.  After a reboot of the printer the install was finished.  Painless and productive.  Subsequent installs on other computer are even quicker since the printer only needs to be connected to the network that first time.  So far I've installed it on two 32-bit Vista computers, one 64-bit Vista, one 32-bit Windows 7 netbook, and two 64-bit Windows 7 computers.  Painless success with minimal effort each time.As far as functionality goes, the printer is legitimately fast.  Noticeably faster than my recent HP and light years faster than my old HP and Brothers.  The double sided laser printers at my work are still faster, but for a home office where you might print 25-150 pages every day, this printer is ideal.  The quality of printed documents is excellent.  However, the quality of photos is very average, even on glossy photo paper.  I attribute this to the lack of photo inks.  If you're a photographer with a home office, you'll need something else to supplement this unit.  Since the install CD updated the firmware for me I was able to take advantage of Epson's mobile device email-based printing.  You set up an Epson printer account and it assigns you a long email  at connect.epson.com address and password. From there you use a web browser to log onto your account and your can change the name of your Epson email address.  I recommend that you proceed into the settings and designate the names of other email accounts that are allowed to print email-print to your WorkForce Pro.  I granted permission to a dozen email address and tested it out.  I was able to print from computers, an iPad and Windows Phones by sending a documents via email to my Epson email account.  This worked better than I thought it would and the print transfer was remarkably fast.  If you want to print something reasonable from your phone, this will absolutely work for you.I was pleased with both the color and B&W; copy features. The scanner is above average.  It also includes a USB slot on the front panel so you can scan your documents directly to a thumb drive.  Scanning is pretty basic, no frills, just get-the-job-done with this unit/software.I don't have any real gripes about this unit that would knock off a star.  The printing is fast and documents are high quality.  The install process is painless.  Printing from several computers and your smartphone at roughly the same time is no problem for the WorkForce Pro.  I had a couple paper misfeeds, but they usually only occurred every 100 pages at most and were quick to unjam (just had to take out the "paper cartridge").  Seriously, the only complaint I could come up with is the starter ink cartridges.  The ink cartridges are huge (feels like 70% the size of a VHS tape), but the starter cartridges are not completely filled with ink.  Epson implores you to buy the XL versions of these cartridges that are completely filled, but why couldn't they just give you the XL versions in the first place?  I know that every printer company does this, but for a printer called the WorkForce Pro, I feel like I should at least get the XL black ink cartridge included.  Oh well...Overall, the WorkForce Pro WP-4530 is a beast of an inkjet printer.  If you require a very high volume of speed printing, I'd still probably recommend a laser printer.  For one step below that, or if you prefer inkjets, I would recommend this Epson without hesitation.

These come in a pack of 3 zip tied into a bigger cardboard box. For many years I was a Canon printer fan. I found their printers to be fast, quiet, and a good value.  I had tried some inexpensive HP inkjets, and I did not like them.My trusty Canon MP830 gave up the ghost after many years of trouble free service, and I thought I would try something different.  My 2 biggest peeves with the Canon were the lack of dual paper trays (had to constantly switch out letter and legal size paper), and the lack of XL type ink cartridges.  I was spending quite a bit on ink.  The HP 8600 Pro Premium caught my eye specifically because it addressed these 2 issues I had with the Canon.I have been using the HP now for a few weeks, and here are my observations:-Set up was quick, easy, and straightforward. Did not have any issues.  Took about 15 minutes to take it out of the box, take off all the tape, install the ink cartridges, install the software, power it up.-Nice LCD display.  Large and mostly appropriately touch sensitive.  I say "mostly" because every now then I do have to press a function more than once for it to register, but this is very minor issue.  I have had the same issue on my other touch devices, so this is nothing unique, and nothing that should concern you.-Printing is fast, and suprisingly quiet for a large inkjet printer.  I though my Canon was fast and quiet, but this HP is considerably better in both areas.-Auto feeder seems to work fine.  Have not had any jams or misalignments.-Duplex printing works great.  Fast.  No jams.-No issues with the dual paper trays.  I have letter size paper in tray 1 and legal size paper in tray 2.  Pulls from each tray just fine.  The only issue I have with the trays is that when you have the 2nd tray set up for legal paper, it extends out past the 1st tray, and it has an odd look to it.  I'm guessing that over time it will also allow dust to accumulate since it is more exposed.  Not a huge deal, but HP could have certainly done better with the design of the 2nd tray.-Scanning works fine.  I've done B&W;, color, single page and multipage, and I haven't had any issue.  Only odd thing is that the scanning functions are controlled entirely on the printer LCD.  Every previous AIO I have had allowed you to contol scanning function in the software.  Really a non issue, but something to note.-I don't use the fax, so I can't comment on that.-It is a large printer, larger than most inkjets, but in my opinion, not excessively so.  It takes up about the same room as my Canon MP830.  Just check the measurements, and make sure it fits in your space.-There are alot of other features that I haven't used yet, so I can't comment on (i.e. card stock, photos, etc).  As I use these features, I will come back and revise my review if there is anything worth noting.Overall, quite satisfied, and I am comfortable recommending as a home office printer, which is how I use it.**Upate 10/27/12** I was wrong about one thing.  I discovered that you can control the scanning functions via the software on the computer.  Not a big deal, but just wanted to point that out.**Update 1/13/14** I just answered a question about this printer, which prompted to me to update my review.  After 15 months, it is running like the day I got it.  No problems whatsoever.  Also, a pleasant surprise.....this printer is one of the most efficient inkjets I have ever owned.  Granted, I am not a high volume office, but with my previous Canon, I was installing new ink cartridges about every 3 or 4 months.  With this printer, I am on my 2nd set of cartridges after 15 months.  They are the XL cartridges, but still.  At 15 months I can't vouch for the truly long term nature of how this will hold up, but so far so good.  One of the best printers I have ever owned, and I've owned MANY.

I thought when I received this I was going to get the same old DIY, perforated business cards that look so incredibly awful and don't pass the mustard in anyone's world. I got an e-mail from Amazon to rate this purchase, so here's my review:1. I received a confirmation e-mail, same day.3. I received an e-mail on May 28 (next day), saying the item was shipped. So far so good.4. On June 4, I received an e-mail telling me my order was returned (by USPS) as undeliverable (hmmm).5. An exchange of e-mail with Amazon customer service over the next few days uncovered the fact that the item was returned by the Post Office as undeliverable because it was damaged!6. On June 7, I placed an order directly with HP for the same item for $27.99 (plus $1.68 tax), with free NEXT DAY shipping.7. The package arrived, as promised, on June 8 (via FedEx).So why 5 stars?1. HP makes quality products. I'm very happy with my printer and very happy with HP brand ink, which is the only brand I will use in it.2. The problem with the order was NOT Amazon's fault. Besides, they shipped the item the very next day.3. Even though the Post Office damaged the order, I must give them credit for NOT delivering damaged goods, which would have left ME with the responsibility to return it to Amazon.4. Amazon credited my purchase promptly.Bottom line: Amazon did their job very well. Even the Post Office looks good here (I do, however, prefer FedEx and/or UPS to the USPS for reliability and promptness). For a few dollars more I got my ink directly from HP overnight. I'm happy with my ink, happy with Amazon, and even pleased with the USPS. Of course, HP did a great job as well, but this is an Amazon review.You asked for it.

I give the tape itself 5 stars -it is fantastic, and is really the best tape to use on wrapping paper, because it does a great job of disappearing.  It is MUCH better, in fact, than the typical Scotch tape which can be removed and reused if not put on correctly --and which is not fully see through.  Though that tape also does a great job when used for wrapping, the Satin Finish tape is better.The only problem I had is that I was really surprised at how little tape came on each of these three rolls; it was ridiculous.  I had a "regular" single roll of Scotch Satin Tape and the tape on THAT roll was at LEAST three times the diameter of the tape on each of these 3-pack rolls.  So, the bottom line is that these three rolls of tape seem to have less tape than a single roll of the regular sized Scotch Satin Tape.  Basically if you like to have more rolls of tape lying around (for example, useful if other people are helping you wrap) AND the three rolls are cheaper, together, than a single roll, then go for the three rolls.  If, however, you like having less clutter, less wasting of resources (more plastic going into the garbage), and NOT running out of tape in the middle of wrapping, go for the single roll.  (The single roll also has the advantage of having a stronger case -and is sealed on both the front and the back.You can't go wrong with the quality of this product, just with the amount of waste, and the amount of tape you get for your money.Recommended as a single roll.  Not recommended as a three pack unless multiple people are wrapping at the same time.
This marker pen is perfect for what I wanted; extra fine point.  They last a long time & don't dry up as quickly as most others.

As someone who does a lot of scrapbooking and hand-written journaling, I'm always looking for writing options that include colored inks.Having used various PaperMate products over the years and been satisfied, I was interested in seeing how these color ballpoint pens would work. (I've basically only used red, black or blue standard ballpoints in the past. Never used any of the gel pens.)Pros:>Color assortment: In addition to two black, there is a light blue, deep blue, green, red, orange and purple.>>Color vibrancy>>When they weren't skipping, some had nice, smooth writing. (If you are used to really fine pens/tips, these are closer to a thick, rather than medium, point.)Cons:>>Bulky feel in hand; would prefer slimmer profile for ease of use.>>Not very sturdy construction. They seem as if they would easily break if not carefully protected when stored or used.>>Ink Smudging, blotching, graininess. All the colors smudged with the slightest bit of pressure. To ensure that I didn't end up with text that started with a blob of ink, I had to wipe the tips every time I wanted to use the pen. This is a pain and even when you did it, if you stopped inbetween, you would often get a blob where you started to print or write. Ugh.>>Ink "smoothness"/line: Problem with some colors in that they intermittently "skipped" when used, even when stored vertically. Line consistency varied even with consistent pressure.>>Grainy substance on tips: When I first opened the packs and went to use, each pen had a sort of granular substance on the neb as if the pens had been leaking and it coagulated on the tip. Had to wipe them off before using.This happened again after they had been stored (vertically in a cup). This leads me to think the ink will bleed out over time and possibly stain anything the pens are stored in.I guess one should not expect much for under $.80 a piece, but I think when even cheaper pens have a smoother line, don't smudge and don't seem to leak, you might come with higher expectations for these that are not met.I'm not familiar with other colored ballpoint pens but I'm thinking there might be others that more consistently meet my needs for smooth lines, minimal or no smudging, and don't need to be cleaned off before use.

My daughter loves all types of puzzles and this book is perfect for her.  The activities are enough to keep her attention without being overly difficult or very easy. OK, the title of this review may sound like hyperbole.  But these little tabs are really useful. Desk Jockeys of the World, Rejoice!

I use this at my graduate office at school and it works tirelessly and flawlessly.  The various eco options are nice for saving toner and paper and the duplexing works well. These are your basic, paper file folders with an extra pocket on the right side. Could be more sturdy, as they are thin weight and a little on the flimsy side. If you thumb through these on a frequent basis, I don't see them lasting a long time.

If you have a furnace and whole house water filters, you know that you need to keep track of when they were changed to keep things running smoothly!  Not too hard to do if you only have one item, but when you have two different whole house filters that are changed at different times (one is charcoal and the other is a sediment filter) and your furnace system has an electronic filter, a filtrate filter, and also individual floor filters, then it becomes a bigger project to keep track of.This small write board looked like a good option to attach to my furnace so that I could keep track of all of the filter changes easily.  So, I went ahead and ordered it.  Here is what I liked:1. The fit and finish on this unit is very good for the price you are paying for it. Yes, it is not built like a brick, but it is functional and does the job quite well.2. Mounting magnets and self adhesive mounting tabs are included in the kit. The magnets are not strong enough to hold the unit on the furnace side when it is running.  I went down to my local ACE store and purchased 4 regular flat magnets and attached them to the back of the board,  It now holds without any issue.3. A writing pen is included as well as two clear plastic magnets to hold notes and such onto the surface of this board. I now have a place for my written notes!  I wrote down each filter and then put a column for install and change date.  Now, I just change the dates as I change the filters.4. The board wipes clean very easily. The included pen has a holder that keeps it handy. The eraser on the end of the pen is best ignored.Here is what I did not like as much:1. There is really no place to put a dry eraser. However, I find that a paper towel works quite well to clean off a line when I need to change a date.2.  As I mentioned above, the included mounting magnets do not have much holding power.  If you are not going to use the mounting tape, you will probably need stronger magnets to hold this onto a metal surface.Overall, this is a nice unit that does the job I needed it to do.  I just had to tweak it a bit by adding 4 stronger mounting magnets.  The surface works great for keeping track of my filters and the two included clear plastic magnets easily hold  any notes to the board without issue.This is a nice product at a great price for the functionality it provides.  If you are mounting to a solid surface, the mounting tape included should work just fine.  If you want to attach it to a metal surface, you will probably want to buy stronger mounting magnets.

My husband hung it on the hall wall leading into our home office and now it is filled with all the things that had been hanging on the refrigerator as well as notes - honey to do's - whatever - I just love it!The size is great because we have a lot of things to do/reminders to do, etc.It's sturdy and it's durable and it looks nice on the wall and the corkboard is a much better quality than the one we had been using that I bought at a office supply store some years ago.We are very happy with it!

Having run a small law for over 25 years, despite a lot of new technology, the problem of printing has remained fairly constant. Small offices need laser printers and they need color scanners. Bought this printer several years ago.  Performance was average for an ink jet printer.  Construction quality was mediocre-minus. After about 30 minutes of walking through the bronzed block diagram he eventually agreed it was a hardware problem.  And, to their credit, HP mailed me a replacement frame which did fix the problem.

Wilson Jones invented the three-ring binder, so the company’s product line dovetails with such binders.  Hence the tab dividers for binders.I cannot live without dividers in my binders and over the years I’ve probably tried almost every type of divider known to man.  And, to label the dividers, I’ve written on them, pasted stickers on them, inserted folded card stock (that promptly fell out). You name it.Now Wilson Jones has come up with something pretty creative.  When you buy the company’s standard (but high quality) colorful plastic tab dividers, you will discover that they do not come with labels to affix to the divider, nor are you expected to write directly on the tab. Instead, you print out an 8.5 x 11 sheet of paper with your labels for each tab running down the side. You insert the sheet of paper into the provided plastic document holder and voila, the appropriate printed label lines up perfectly (well, almost…see below) under each tab divider.That means you can easily reuse the dividers without have to scrape off a previously affixed label or without having to paint white-out over something you wrote. You just print out a new page with new labels.On the Wilson Jones website you will find a template you can use to type your labels and print out the sheet of paper for the document holder.  It was much easier than I expected.My only quibble is that I had to make some small adjustments to the format of the page containing the labels.  Wilson Jones provides the templates in Word or PDF format.  The PDF template required quite a bit more rearranging of text than did the Word template.  For example, the PDF template left half the label on my printer drum.  The Word template simply required a few extra spaces here and there.  Of course, once you make the adjustments, you can simply save the file and reuse it endlessly.

I have an obsession for office supplies especially pens and pencils.  This is an expensive mechanical pencil but it is worth it.  It's comfortable to use and looks great. I love some of those little things in life, like this comfortably padded mouse pad. It has such a stylish design. While this is a pretty pricey tape, it has some unique characteristics that make it ideally suited for certain tasks. I’m using it to securely seal chemical solutions I use for hobby work in glass bottles. After closing the bottle (I use the Boston Brown bottles in either 2 or 4 oz size) with the screw-on cap, I put a band of this tape around it and heat seal it shut. It provides for a very tight seal.Unlike regular heat seal material, this is tape, so it sticks pretty well even without being heat shrunk. I get the best seal, as expected, when the bottle is clean and dry, but it still sticks pretty well even when the bottle has some moisture on it.It’s also great for marking bottles that have caustic solutions to ensure I remember to take extra care when decanting the solutions.The only quibble is the smell – the tape has a strong odor, mainly from the adhesive. Sort of a plasticky scent that is not all that pleasant. But, it dissipates pretty quickly.Not cheap, but for applications such as bottle sealing, this gets the job done very well.

I love to use these post-it tabs for my cookbooks. They're perfect for marking recipes I want to remember and be able to reference quickly. I love being able to write notes on them, too. This is a great source for Epson inks..I just can't find a better price...and they're brand new..wrapped and shipped perfectly! Thanks!

When I got this I wondered how well it would work as compared to the "magic eraser" foam cleaning pads that I normally use when I am cleaning my white boards. I love my laminator and these pouches are wonderful. Not too thick, heat up nicely, work great. No negative issues at all.

This is really nice paper, much cheaper than others I have seen here or in stores.On the package they have a "vibrancy scale" it's a list of their colors from "Fizz" - (Dynamite White) to "Bang" (Firecracker Fuchsia) and this one is near the top between "Boomin' Buff" and "Golden Glitter" (I have to admit I *LOVE* the color names!)It is a nice Canary yellow; we use it for instruction inserts for our products and it's great.****Jim

First off, this is a fairly large shredder. Be warned - it comes in a very large box that is contained in an even larger box with paper padding. They had to use a dolly to get this up to my second floor apartment! Thankfully, once the shredder was free from the enormous boxes, it didn't seem *too* oversized.The first thing I noticed when shredding was how quiet this machine is (which is a far cry from most of the smaller shredders I've used), and I was really pleased by that. However, I try very hard to review the product as if I had paid the purchase price, for I think it is only fair for those who read and rely on reviews. I am an avid user of sticky notes of all kinds, including the sort you use to mark off pages.  Having a fair bit of experience with this sort of thing, I can easily say that these note tabs are a distinct improvement.  The most important feature of these notes is their stiffness- they don't bend, meaning that you don't end up with a bunch of crumpled tabs.  Second, these notes are adequately sticky- they don't shift or fall, and yet are still easy to remove without messing up the paper.  Third, they're writable, and provide a good bit of writing surface- thus, you can put notes in the margins of your books without actually damaging said books.  This is great for students who might want to sell back textbooks, or who loan a copy of a book for a semester.  The one downside I can see to these notes is that because they don't bend, if you use them in books or notebooks that are shelved, it will be difficult to either stack on top or push them flush against the wall (depending on how you stack or shelve), but the moveability of these notes means that you can adjust them when you're ready to put stuff away.  I'm very please with these, and definitely need to stock up!

I think this is the fifth All in One printer I've reviewed in the last two years, and although I used to hate All in Ones, I've slowly grown more fond of them, especially after using many of the Epson models. I tried this printer out in our office for a few months, replacing the standalone Brother 5250 and Fujitsu Scanner I've been using. I do a lot of high-output printing, and usually go through a couple reams a day, so I was mainly worried about print speed, and how fast it would use up ink.Installation - Very easy and quick.  Usually I find setup of these very annoying because the on screen display is difficult to navigate, and it is a real pain to try to end in wireless passwords on their tiny screens and customize the printers. I've had this problem with older Epson All in Ones. Epson has made some pretty significant changes to their GUI over the last couple years, and enlarged the size of their display panels. They used to be about half the size of a desk of cards. The new panels are larger and very easy to move through now.  I had the wireless set up within 2 minutes and working great. I ended up using the direct network.Printing - Printing is okay, though not nearly as fast as I need for this printer to be a viable office printer for my needs.  I get around 11 or 12 pages a minute. I ended up connecting my old printer back up and just using it for scanning and copying.  Color printing looks very respectable, and the Epson handles color photos very nicely. I've had to replace the entire set of cartridges (there are four) once since owning it.Copying - Very impressed with the copying from the 845. Other printers usually copy too light, but the copying quality is very sharp and doesn't look much different from our standalone copier.Scanning - Scanning speed through the document feeder was not nearly as nice as my Fujitsu, but still very respectable for an All in One.  It handled multiple-page documents as well as older documents that other feeders will sometimes get jammed with.  One really nice thing about an All in One is that you have the flatbed option for scanning so I could use it for odd-shaped items or older photos that I wouldn't trust in a feeder. Only downside to this is you can't use the scanner over a network connection, since the processing is done on your computer. So I had to have it hardwired for that. It would seem like this should be something they could figure out and implement.Overall, I think the 845 is a fairly respectable printer for a small business that doesn't handle too much printing.  If it was a little faster I would consider replacing my office printer permanently, but for now, I'm content to use it for scanning and copying, as well as the occasional color printing.

On the outside, this is a 10-in x 11.5-in, 3-ring loose-leaf binder -- somewhat unstructured in that the covers are a flexible plastic, the spine is a strip of nylon-y canvas, and the rings/binding are exposed rather than covered behind the spine. Inside are 12 sections, each composed of loose-leaf pages for recording expenses and notes (see more comments, below*), plus a large, heavyweight, double-sided pocket page for stowing bills, receipts and other papers. The 12 sections match perfectly to year-long use, but each is an unlabeled template so you can begin anywhere in the year. There are also two full-page, clear-poly envelopes for more storage.*The loose-leaf pages come with pre-printed categories to get users started, and that's helpful; it's even better that users can just replace those pre-printed pages by going online (to the "extras" section at the meadorganizher website) to download simpler versions of the pages and then customize (somewhat clumsily)/save/print them as desired). However, I was disappointed that Mead didn't take the opportunity, in the loose-leaf pages of this financial product, to highlight some good financial practices -- the worst missed opportunity is that "Savings" is included in the "Personal" section of the Budgeting worksheet, alongside "Magazine Subscriptions" (?!) Savings should be its own category, incorporating investments, college planning, retirement, etc.In the end, the storage, organization, and documentation aspects make this a handy product. I recommend it to anyone wanting to get started; after a year, you may find it easy to assemble your own packet for future years. As an aside: I'm actually using the sections of my packet not as a monthly expense planner/tracker, but for each of the home improvement and landscaping projects we're initiating.

This product is meant for one purpose, and one purpose only, allow you present your PowerPoint (or related presentation software) remotely. No drivers necessary which is wonderful, and besides from closing the New Keyboard Wizard on my Mac, works like a charm. Logitech consistently produces quality products, and this is no exception. I had no issues making it work on presentations. The weight of the device isn't too heavy or too light and feels comfortable in my hand.However, for the price, I'd like to see this unit control other things outside of PowerPoint presentations -- by adding mouse control. Other competitors offer this wonderful feature (and even scroll wheels and volume controls.) Edward Tufte'sThe Cognitive Style of PowerPoint: Pitching Out Corrupts Within, Second Editiontries to get users out of using bland PowerPoint presentations and all this remote does is keep people in PowerPoint. I'd love to be able to take users out to the web and demo live web applications. But alas, this device won't be any help. For such a pricey device (double most of the competition) this is something that Logitech should look into for future product iterations.

Every time I've bought a computer printer in years past, I've agonized about whether to go with Epson or HP (I never really considered Brother, Canon or Lexmark, for reasons shrouded in the mists of time). Both Epson and HP have pretty good reputations for performance and reliability. In my experience, both brands' printers make good-quality prints. Both companies have printers with comparable features for similar prices. Ink usage and replacement cartridge prices are pretty much a wash. Having said that, I've been looking to replace two old printers recently. One is an HP LaserJet 4 with a damaged drum. It would cost far more to fix than it's worth (plus the toner cartridges are obscenely expensive). The other is an HP DeskJet 1120C. It still works, but I don't need its 11"-x-17" paper size capability, and it is glacially, unbearably slow.Thanks to Amazon's Vine program, I have now not only replaced my old printers, but I've done so in a way that I hope potential buyers will find useful. I chose BOTH an Epson XP-610 and anHP Envy 5530to review. Thus I can compare their features and performance, which hopefully will be of interest to anyone looking at buying a new all-in-one. I think these units offer similar performance and features at a similar price point, and probably attract the same type of user. So here goes...SETUPThere's not really much difference between setting up the two. Both come packaged in sturdy, colorful, tight-fitting boxes with lots of blue tape holding things in place and pieces of cardboard, foam or plastic wedged here and there in their innards to prevent the moving parts from moving during transport. Both come with: a software CD, a pictorial setup poster (but no users manual--you have to download those from the respective websites), a power cord and a starter set of ink cartridges. The HP uses two cartridges (Black and Tri-Color), the Epson uses five (Black, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Photo Black). The HP comes with a sample pack of 4"-x-6" Advanced Photo Paper, which I haven't tried yet. Anyway, both sets of cartridges are very small. I wonder how many pages of printout they're good for. Not many, I'd wager.Both units set up the same way, and it's a breeze. Remove all the packing material, plug them in, turn them on, load the ink cartridges and run the software CD. What could be easier? The setup processes ran very smoothly. Hooking them up to my WiFi network was also straightforward. Once I did that, the printers showed up in the Printers & Faxes folder of my ancient Windows XP system, from which I could designate the default choice for my applications. Piece o' cake. The only setup problem I had is that, for some reason that I haven't troubleshot yet, the Epson scan function doesn't work because it doesn't seem to be compatible with my computer. I have no idea why, but, since I have very little use for the scan function, I'm willing to let this slide for the moment. Advantage: I'd call this a draw.WIRELESS PRINTINGPrinting from my Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 was also easy, after I installed the appropriate free e-print apps downloaded from the Google Play Store. Epson's app is superior because it provides much more visibility into the printer's status and lets you control many more functions than HP's app does. Advantage: Epson, clearly.SPEEDI haven't timed them with a stopwatch, but the Epson seems noticeably faster than the HP. On the other hand, it takes a little longer to spool the job to the printer. I'd call this a draw.PRINT QUALITYPlain text and mixed documents print out fine from both units, with vivid colors and sharp, crisp text. The Epson might be just a hair better, but it's not by much.I also tested the photo printing function with both printers. To make the test valid, I printed the same image to both printers (one at a time, of course) on the same kind of 4"-by-6" glossy photo-quality paper, using the same software package (Corel PhotoPaint X5). Both printers took a minute or so to start printing, but they eventually kicked out results. The difference was greater than I expected. The HP print was far less brilliant and contrasty. It almost seemed to have a dulling film over it, like shooting through a thin but noticeable layer of gray smog. The Epson print was much bolder and had better contrast, with darker darks and lighter lights. Neither print looked a lot like what was on the screen, of course, which is to be expected. Both were extremely sharp. I would consider either one acceptable. The differences became apparent only when I compared them side-by-side. The differences may also depend on the scene content, lighting and other things, so I hesitate to make a hard-and-fast pronunciamento. However, based on this test, I liked the Epson's image quality considerably better than the HP's.OTHER FEATURESBoth units print, scan and copy. The Epson also prints on CDs and DVDs, a capability missing from the HP (or at least I haven't found it yet). That's a key difference. On the other hand, the Epson uses multiple input and output trays, including one just for CDs and one just for photo paper, that seem a little fussy and fragile to me. I prefer the Epson's bright full-color display to the HP's, and it seems more appropriately touch-sensitive. Advantage: Epson.The Epson has a smaller footprint but is taller than the HP, but either should fit into a typical user's desktop workspace. As best I can tell, neither one will scan slides or negatives. Again, perhaps such features are buried in the user's manuals that I downloaded, but they're not obvious at first glance. Advantage: Another draw.THE BOTTOM LINESo, after all that, what's my bottom line? Well, all things considered, and after a relatively short time using these all-in-ones and exploring their capabilities, I prefer the Epson XP-610 to the HP Envy 5530. My ratings reflect that preference: I rate the XP-610 with four stars ("I like it"), and I'm posting this same review for the Envy 5530 with a three-star rating ("It's OK"). If you are in the market for a wireless all-in-one, I hope you found this comparative review useful. Happy printing.

I have always wanted one of these but never got around to getting one. I cant believe I went this long without. makes it very easy to use on boxes. love it!

This is a vast improvement over the 5 subject notebook.  Cloth surrounds the spiral to prevent any snags.  A pen-loop allows for stowing of a pen or pencil. I ended up with two of these. One is in my daughter's locker and the other is on the side of my filing cabinet. I love this - the neoprene is flexible but not saggy. Fabulous folders from a well known brand name - sturdy and eyecatching, these folders will last longer than the paper you put in them. I like the sustainability of using 100% recycled products even in the home office. These folders are perfect for complex subjects needing sub-filing.

Love these labels!  They are coming in handy for so many things.  They print up beautifully and look so nice on bottle, jars, and boxes. In theory, this new dispenser is a novel idea.  It tape and dispenser works as advertised, although I elected not to adhere the base permanently to any particular surface. If you like to save an image of your handwritten notes, this product makes it easy to do so, and cleans up the angle while you do it.I wrote my note, I opened the app, and I aligned the four symbols within the four guide marks that take up much of the screen within the app. The resulting image was flattened out nicely and then aligned and cleanly trimmed.My iPhone, which I keep with me almost all of the time, comes with a notepad app, and the things I type remain in an editable format. At NNSY, I review, edit and issue administrative directives.  For a couple of years, I've been storing published directives inside Wilson Jones 2" Binders that were ordered directly from the company.  These binders endure frequent handling better than other brands I've used because of their knitted, reinforced spines.  These spines have a tendency not to crack and split with time and frequent usage.  Many of the Wilson Jones Binder's features (e.g., two plastic pockets, never-gap rings and PVC-free covers that can be custom designed using templates from the manufacturer's website) are similar to those of other brands.  Wilson Jones is more expensive but they are worth it if you desire long-term protection for your valuable paperwork.I was excited to receive the Wilson Jones 1" Binder (Model W63-14-267) from the Amazon Vine Program. The folders have three perforated holes and fit perfectly inside the three-ring binder.  Each color of folder represents a different item.  For example, all my user manuals for home and kitchen appliances are kept in the red folder.  Using the website for Wilson Jones, I easily customized the binder without needing to register; I don't have to worry about the company harassing me with e-mails.Joseph B. Hoyos
