I'm going to try to keep this review an exclamation-point free zone, but I do think these tabs are destined to rank up there with paper clips and sticky notes as utterly ubiquitous staples of the home and business environment for years to come.Emphasis on PAPER, here.  The packaging makes it clear enough that these tabs really aren't for hanging your heavier wall calenders, much less something framed or --shudder! (oops, exclamation point.  FAIL)-- breakable.But you've got the lightweight stuff, and you know you want it up on your walls, which already have enough holes in them, thanks.  Or maybe it's your kids with their quirky collections of paper ephemera.  "No tape on the walls", I used to yell at my eldest.  But the poster putty stuff never really seemed to keep a grip on the wall, and the weirdly felted "sticky stuff" I found a few years back was a bear to work with, sticking - well, like glue - to the paper backing that had to be removed for application.These tabs have none of these problems and - as touted - are residue-free.  The only question in my mind at this point is how they hold up over the long haul.  I'd rate them a real value if they can last a year, but I'm betting they'll last considerably longer.I'm using my Scotch Reusable Tabs to easily put up school and activity schedules for the kids, as well as exercising my own creativity by allowing myself to "tape" things to the wall, at least in my little home office space.  And inside a few kitchen cabinets.  And in the laundry.And my refrigerator thanks me for the break from having EVERY SINGLE THING that I need or want to have handy, or just to show off, magnet-ed to it.

I got these erasable markers to go with a new wipe-off calendar that came with only one black marker. Being a color person, these markers help me code events on my wall calendar, so they stand out better. Although the tips are a bit wider than I prefer, the "bullet" end made it relatively easy to write legibly in the small spaces on the calendar. Markings can remain on the board for some time, without permanently staining. They did not come with any kind of eraser, but wipe off easily with an old sock. I got this because I am a fan of the Biggest Loser and I have been losing weight over the past few months. I keep a daily food diary and I figured this would help me keep a record of what I ate day so I could easily tranfer the information to my food diary.I found the Daily Meal Planner to be helpful in keeping track of the water I drank and food I ate each day.  While I would have designed it a bit differently it is impossible to create something perfect for everyone so overall I am pleased.Pros:The size is the perfect for my refrigerator door. It is 11 X 14 so it did not cover the whole door but gave me enough room to write down what I was eating.The two magnetic strips fit easily on the back of the board. The board holds up fine on my refrigerator door. There is the option of mounting the board on a wall or regular door by using mounting tape that is included.The idea of putting 8 glasses on the board so people could mark off the number of glasses of water they drink each day is great. My doctor keeps on telling me to drink 8 glasses of water a day and I often would forget how much I drank.  This makes it easy to keep a record.There is plenty of room to include what I eat at each meal and what I have as snacks.The dry erase marker works fine and it is easy to wipe off. The holder for the marker works well. The board is sturdy and looks good.Cons/SuggestionsThese cons are more because based on my needs. I would have created the board a bit differently. It is impossible to create a product perfect for everyone so these are more suggestions than cons.I count more than calories. I count carbohydrates as well as sugars and fats. The board only has a square for calories. It would have been nice to have the square broken up into quarters so people who count more than calories could easily list them. I list them in the space for calories but it is tough space wise at times.The board only has room for breakfast, lunch and dinner as well as two snacks. I have three snacks including desert after dinner so one more snack space would have been nice.This is great if you eat your meals in one place. If you are home all the time it is perfect. If you work five days a week you have to plan your meals and put them on the board or just use this on the weekends. It would be nice if the board came with a small notebook/diary so if you ate out you could keep a record of what you ate and then transfer it to the board when you got home.Conclusion:This is a fine product to help with weight loss.  While it can't be perfect for everyone it certainly should be useful for most people.

I own 2 laminators, a Scotch TL901 (cheap) and a Fellowes Callisto (expensive), and have used both brands of pouches as well, in 3mil & 5mil. Using the Fellowes laminator, I had waving on the finished product using both mils, regardless of whether it was standard copy paper or card stock.I recently made 2 signs, one using this Fellowes 5mil pouch and one using the Scotch brand, using the Scotch laminator and both look flawless with no excessive waves.  Both appear identical, I can see no difference between the pouches.  Both will be hung outside, one stapled to a pole for a week (Scotch) & one hung on a fence indefinitely (Fellowes). I will try to post back in regards to the long term durability if there is an issue.All in all, this product does exactly what it is supposed to do, with no problems, and I can recommend.

If you have a mailing list in the hundreds, anything that shaves a little bit of time on the boring and repetitive parts of the project is very welcome. This new "easy peel" design couldn't be easier to use. You just bend the column every so slightly and you get an easy to grab edge that allows you to peel off each label without having to grab a corner by nudging with your fingernail, over and over again--even after going through the heat of a laser printer. I have found them to feed through smoothly (only one sheet at a time), not get jammed, not have one of the label corners accidentally adhere to the roller or feed dogs of the printer (yes, this has happened to me and it's a nightmare I'm glad to be able to put behind me). They work like a charm.NOTE TO AVERY:As much as I have loved these labels, I STILL have a slight objection. It has nothing to do with either quality, functionality, or design. It has to do with size. These one-inch high labels easily accommodate a three-line address. A four-line address fits. However, if you want to take full advantage of your word processor's capabilities and add a zip bar code line (which really DOES work in getting your mail delivered faster), you can fit it in on the three-line address, but it gets cut off on the four-line address.If you have a longer address structure, you're absolutely doomed. For example: I have several unmarried couples on my list. They each require a line. (Mr. John Smith, Ms. Mary Jones). I also mail some company executives, and this becomes a nightmare:Mr. John Smith, PresidentThe ACME Company1234 Main Street, Suite 5City, State, Zip//////bar code////////.This address does not fit on a 1" label.This makes creating a large mailing a real problem. I print the whole list (800+) in this label, then discard the ones that didn't fit and re-do them manually on label #05163, which are the next size up but, at 2" x 4" they are really to BIG. (#5962 which is 1 1/3" high doesn't provide that much of an improvement and it's still 4" wide!)Please, Avery, make a 1.5" x 3" label to accommodate the longest names and titles and the longest addresses and not look horrible on the envelope--and make them Easy Peel, just like this one.

This "No Soliciting" sign is very noticeable from a good distance away, which is useful since we have a fairly long walkway and don't want to overly inconvenience the solicitors by having them walk all the way up to our porch just to be turned away. On the one hand, it's nothing to get excited about: it's a pad like I used when I started working full time in the 1960s. This is a cool binder that might be just the thing for my 9th Grader to carry to her classes during the day.What I like about it is that it comes with both lined paper and graph paper which can be restocked from our supply as she uses it up. The cover is sturdy but still has the front pocket so she can 'customize' the look with a coversheet.Inside there are pocketed dividers.  The first two dividers each have an 'open' half page pocket for holding papers. (They are only closed on two sides so you slip paper into them.) They also have a smaller closed pocket with a plastic latch. Pretty cool. If she has note cards that should prevent them from falling out when she drops her binder.The other dividers have full page pockets (closed on 3 sides) with a 'locking flap' at the top. And all have subject tabs, although I'll have to get some sticky tabs in bright colors to stick on them so that they can have easy-to-read text. (The dividers and tabs are a dark smokey translucent color that would make it hard to read if you wrote on them.)WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOWThis is a really interesting design. I reviewed theFive Star Advance Wirebound Notebook, 5-Subjectand really loved the cloth covering. But that was because it covered the rings, which should keep them from getting snarled up with other items and bent. This binder has the cloth, but the large plastic rings are outside of the cloth. Being plastic they probably won't snarl like metal spirals will, but I don't know what other purpose it will serve, except perhaps to keep the papers cleaner.The plastic rings, by the way, separate by pulling them apart. At this time there is no way to tell how they will hold up to rough kid use, but they seem sturdy.

I put all my junk mail through this, even when they are in the envelope, all the time. It works and it works fine. I also put in old discs and old cards - it still works. These are just as described in the advertisement. The glue holds well and they are sturdy and not cheap looking. Not sure what else to say.

I've been wanting a bulletin board for the wall behind my home office desk chair for quite awhile.  The pictures in the room all have slender, vertical black metal frames so, when offered this vertical cork bulletin board with a black frame, I went for it.This frame is plastic and instead of meeting unobtrusively in the corners, the pieces meet about an inch away from the corners, with seams that are very noticeable; also, the vertical and horizontal pieces are of different widths. Being a simple item, there's not too much to say about file folders.  These do the job well, just as you'd expect.These file folders DO have a larger tab area for bigger labels, but I'm not sure from a functionality standpoint that it's that much of an improvement. I tried these envelopes to see if they offered the security that was claimed. Firstly no matter how I held them up to the light I couldn't see through them which is excellent and I even tried putting in a card with just my name on it in bold black lettering to no avail. So we're off to a good start there.Secondly I tried opening one carefully. An unsuspecting person may try to open the envelope normally, but even if you did it very gently the micro perforations would tear before you got an inch open. So armed with the knowledge the security feature was there I tried my best to incredibly slowly open the envelope. After a few minutes lightly plucking at it I did get it open without too much visible tearing, but even my very slow efforts did indicate tampering so again top marks. This is a nice 5 x 8, wide ruled, one sided pad. This is a feature-packed all-in-one that exceeds my expectations from a combo unit at this price point. Having installed the wireless software for the desktops and laptops in the house, and I am completely happy with the accessibility of the wireless printing.Setup is simple, and it is easy to use. The only thing I dislike is the latch for lifting and lowering the LCD screen; it is easy enough to operate, but while lowered, my large fingers need to fumble around to get at the right angle to depress the latch. The LCD can be used either flush with the unit or raised for visibility while standing over the unit. The LCD display is brilliantly lit, and the controls are quickly accessible; navigation arrows, minus, plus, back, start and stop buttons require only a light touch to activate and are easily distinguished.I still have plenty of scanning left to do, and the XP-410 makes it almost effortless. Scans are done placing the originals at the forward most position, with their tops oriented toward the scanner bed's right side. The XP-410 allows me to select the destination device to which the results of my scans, which are brilliantly translated, will be sent, directly from the unit's display.The copy feature allows up to ninety-nine copies per job, with options for black and white or color displayed on LCD screen. Settings for density, border layout, scaling, paper type and print quality are available.The results of the prints are fantastic, though I make an effort to use draft and grayscale settings for everything other than photo printing. Photo prints look incredible, and the inks are used efficiently with the photo paper option selected. The added benefit of print from either my computer or directly from my camera's memory card through the printer's available media card slot is great.PC-Free printing offers multiple templates, including wide or thin rule line paper, music sheet and graph paper. Personalized note papers are great for those who want to burn through ink using their own images for writing papers with vertical, horizontal or no lines. Calendar options include month-long or week-long with an hourly breakdown for writing a daily itinerary.The XP-410 features energy conserving power off and sleep timers. The power off timer can be set to thirty minutes, one hour, two hours or four hours. The sleep timer can be set at three, five, ten or fifteen minutes.I am still using the ink which came with the unit, and there are two-sizes of replacements available when I need more. I love that I can check the ink levels through the printer software so that I will not be caught by surprise when the supply is running low.I have primarily utilized a much older Samsung laser printer until I installed the Epson XP-410 Wireless All-In-One inkjet. The fact that there is no warm-up period required, combined with the wireless convenience, makes this printer a household favorite. I highly recommend the Epson XP-410 for any household with multiple computers or compatible mobile devices distributed throughout different areas of the home. High quality prints, beautiful scans, full-featured copies, PC-free templates, convenient wireless connectivity and so much more at such a low price brings significant value to this compact and feature-rich home office solution.

Somehow, after years of different tax-time promotions, our house had four shredders. Over time, we accidentally gave them all away, because... well... who needs four shredders?We did need one, though. Since I've had really outstanding luck with AmazonBasics cables, so it was really a debate between the cheaperAmazonBasics cross-cut shredderor spending a little more on this one. This seemed to be the more "serious" of the two, so I checked out, and waited to make some confetti.Assembly was straightforward, and the instructions were only necessary to figure out where the two locking casters were supposed to go.I put in a sheet of paper, and it was dutifully reduced to confetti. Much nicer than the strip shredders I had before, and now, there's no way someone's going to be able to go through my garbage and reconstruct my shameful collection of Starbucks receipts. I was impressed.Then I started shredding things that had been piling up, and noticed very quickly that this shredder is kind of wimpy. At about four pages, it starts making some really sad noises. And when I tried some credit card junk mail, it totally choked -- leaving me to think "Gee, even those free shredders were able to tell Citibank 'no thanks'." Speaking of credit cards, I happened to have one that expired last month, and gave that a shot. On one hand, the card has been totally obliterated, thanks to this shredder. On the other, it seemed like such a chore for the poor machine, I almost felt bad.The real pain, though, is the slot. If your documents aren't pristine and flat, set a little time aside to get them to go in to the very awkward slot. If you're okay with sitting down and feeding this sheet-by-sheet, you should be fine. Otherwise, this is a pain to use.Ultimately, I decided to send it back, and give the17-page AmazonBasics cross-cut shreddera try. Yes, I know it's not micro-cut, but an owner says it cuts about 1 1/4 x 1/4", which realistically, I think is enough to thwart anyone inclined to go through my garbage. With a top-loading slot and twice the rated capacity, it seemed worth the extra money.

The good news about the Epson XP-810 is that it prints photos beautifully. The bad news is that the ink runs out very fast and is expensive. If you're mixing text with photos, this means stopping in your tracks to replace ink cartridges, which is a nuisance. But, before you consider buying the XP-810, if you're really into printing out photos (or pictures in general) you might want to spend up for the Epson XP-850. While the XP-810 has Black, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Photo Black (that's kind of cool - wonder if it's pigment-based?), the XP-850 boasts a different, more nuanced assortment: Black, Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Light Cyan and Light Magenta. According to the manufacturer, the photos will resist fading and deterioration for 200 years. Since I won't be around to verify this, I can't comment on it. One more note about the ink. It spills easily (they include caps for the cartridges, but I recommend wearing thin disposable gloves when installing them). This isn't my first Epson printer, and I got inky fingers from their cartridges in the past which prepared me for this go-round. Soap and water doesn't help much...their ink is extremely tenacious!Printing isn't particularly fast, so if you are running a business from home you might not find this as efficient as you want (about 14 ppm black, 11 ppm color). The XP-850 is almost 30% faster and the HP Office Pro 8600 Plus is MUCH faster (about 20 ppm black, 16 ppm color). I currently own five printers, and go through them rather faster than most people, thanks to a cat who jumps on them. Like almost all printers now, the Epson is mostly plastic and thus easy to damage. But it has fairly sleek lines. I don't consider it really small, more of a mid-sized machine. While printing, it is about 17" wide, 24" deep and 8" high. Without printing, it's about 15" wide, 13" deep and 8" high, weighing about 21 pounds. Also, you need space to pull out the paper tray. There are two paper trays, but one is solely for photos, so if you need to print letter, legal and envelopes, you have to keep opening the single tray and changing paper. It's a mild nuisance.Some of the special effects offered are a waste of ink, in my opinion. For example, you can print college-ruled, wide-ruled and graph paper. Really? It's exponentially cheaper to buy that paper! Other aspects are far better. You can use auto photo correction, crop, rotate and enlarge photos, and print multiple photos on a single page (I am a BIG fan of that!).My opinion is that the Epson is best for someone who wants to print photos, and if you have the space and the money, it's a good idea to use a different printer, like the HP OfficeJet Pro 8600, for text. If you want to use just one printer, I recommend the Epson XP-850 instead of the 810 because of the nuanced inks. But, for the price, this is a decent printer.

I tried out this binding machine on a small, 15 page document with regular white copy paper just to see how it would do.  The set up is extremely easy: basically plug it in, start it up, get it to the correct setting, let it warm up (only takes a minute or two), insert your binder and let the machine do it's thing (which seems to be basically warming up the glue along the spine of the binder which allows the glue to spread and bind in the sheets).  I think it took less than a minute to do the actual binding.After it cooled I checked out the results --pretty good overall.  The first sheet was solid, but the second sheet was solid except maybe an inch or two at the top.  Most of the other sheets were fully glued in or had a little part at the top that didn't solidly set.  However, even the sheets that had some part unglued were attached firmly enough that I felt confident that they weren't going anywhere.I am planning on using it for making the kids reports and other school-related projects.I will say that although the results were pretty good and it seemed solid, I would not use this as a professional presentation tool because of the fact that there were some areas where the sheets didn't attach and that wouldn't look neat enough for my tastes.  There is of course the possibility that I'm missing the proper "finesse" or technique to get the machine to work perfectly and perhaps a few more tries could result in perfection.Two things to note: the machine does not normally come with any binders; you have to buy those separately.  Second, you can get many different sized binders, I believe up to 300 pages, so you could potentially bind a pretty large document.  I am planning on getting some larger ones and I will do an update to my review whenever that occurs.

I've been a user of HP printers for many years now, most recently a Photosmart C7250 All-In-One. The new HP Officejet 4500 Wireless has many of the capabilities of the C7250 for a much lower price.  Both are inkjet printers, of course, both are color fax machines, both can copy in black-and-white or color, both have a high-resolution scanner with document feeder and both have wireless connectivity.Of course you do give up some things for the lower (by about half) price: the 4500 has only a black and a tricolor ink cartridge with integrated print heads (the C7250 has six independent ink tanks), the 4500 lacks automatic two-side printing, lacks "photo printing" (though it does a decent job at printing images), and doesn't have a built-in card reader.  The 4500 is also considerably smaller, which can be an advantage in a small or home office.Setting up the 4500 is easy.  Even if you are going to use it wirelessly, you must connect it by USB to a PC (or Mac) for the initial installation.  After it is set up, you can disconnect the USB and run wireless-only.  A 3-foot USB cable is provided, which I consider too short, but at least it's there, unlike with many other printers.  The software installed smoothly for me, which was a novelty - I've had a lot of trouble with the latest HP software for my C7250.  In addition to the standard printer software, HP includes a basic I.R.I.S. OCR capability.  I tried the OCR and it did a good job of capturing the text, but it lost all formatting.  OmniPage it ain't.I was pleased to find that the network setup was handled through the PC (or Mac) software during the initial install - I was not looking forward to having to enter network keys on the printer's keypad.  I use WPA2-AES wireless and the HP 4500 had no problem with it.When you install the ink cartridges the printer spits out an alignment sheet which you then scan in so it can see how the print heads line up.  Clear prompts appeared on the lighted LCD panel on the printer and this was easy.I tried a variety of printing tasks and the 4500 handled them all well.  Text was clear and colored backgrounds showed no banding.  Although this is not a photo printer, it did a passable job printing a photograph on plain paper. The scanner worked well too, both using the glass and the document feeder. Printing is quiet and fast.Faxing I thought a bit awkward - you use the left-right arrow buttons to select color or b+w fax, enter the number (or use the address book), then press the green start button.  It then asks you to press 1 if you're scanning from the glass or 2 from the feeder, which I found annoying.  However, the faxing worked well, and when the number was busy, it automatically retried after one minute and then five minutes.  HP includes a special phone cord which you are supposed to use for the fax connection. I don't know what is special about it, but if you use a regular cord you must use a small adapter that HP also provides.HP claims that the 4500 meets EnergyStar requirements, so I tested power consumption.  When the 4500 was turned off, my meter read zero (the meter does not register tenths.)  When on and idle, 2 watts; when actively printing, 10-15 watts and when in standby mode, 1 watt.  I thought this exemplary.The only real gripe I have is a minor one - the paper feed tray (which doubles as the output tray) sticks out from the front quite a bit.  It does have a retractable output catcher, so it's not as bad as it could be.  However, I understand this is a trade-off for the box being so small.The "901" ink cartridges are not insanely expensive, but I don't know how long they last.  HP claims that cost-per-page is lower with theHP Officejet 6500. If your usage is modest, the HP Officejet 4500 may be just what you need at a very reasonable price.  If you print a lot, you may want a model with a higher-capacity paper tray, and of course if you print photos, there are better choices.  All in all, a very competent and modestly priced all-in-one device.  Recommended.

I printed from my iPad and did not need to get up to turn the printer on. The printer turned itself on. Really convenient. It also does great double sided prints with ease.The setup for wireless was a little difficult the first go round, but I got it to work the second time. Typing in a password was annoying. Setting it up on my computer also look a little bit of time because the printer does not show up on the computers settings when I hit the add button. Just the Epson Fax function showed up. I had to go through the install again and do some extra steps to get it to finally show up, but once it did it was good. There is no set involved to be able to print wirelessly from a tablet or phone.There is an SD and CF card reader to print photos and it also does a great job with that.The only drawback is the size and the amount of ink you have to buy. It's a very large and bulky printer. It is a work horse and it's shaped like one to. There seems to be a cartridge for every color there is, which means the ink will be pricy. It's about $65 for the color inks and $16 for the black on Amazon. If you don't need a lot of the functions on this printer there are cheaper ones where the ink is not at that price range. I have an all-in-one HP printer and the ink is about $30.I don't use the fax machine so I cannot comment on that.Update: One thing I have found is that the paper gets jammed a lot and sometimes will print out multiple sheets per page. I've adjusted the tray many times and it has not helped the problem.

I bought this arm based on the reviews.  I was thinking I could get a monitor arm for around $40, and I can, but I wanted to buy one that worked right, and I could just install and forget about.  This Ergotron was what I was looking for.It's heavy and solid.  It comes with everything you need to install from a corner/edge, or if you need/want to drill a hole in your desktop to mount it.  You get all the tools needed, and very clear instructions.  Ergotron just does it right, period.I'm currently using this model to hold up a 27" 2560x1440 monitor, it works like a charm.  I chose to drill a hole though the desk for the mount, and I even "modified" the nut a bit so it could fit in a tight spot.It's easy to adjust, just loosen the hex nuts with the included tools, put in place, and tighten.  I have mine tightened to the point where the monitor stands still, but I can move and tilt it when needed.Overall I'm happy with my purchase.  Also seriously considering the big ergotron arm to hold up my 27" iMac, so I can have both monitors "float".

This tape is pleasingly thick and easier to use than the cheap stuff.  For uses where tape strength is important, this is my choice.  But there are still plenty of times when a double layer of store-brand packing tape is more cost-effective.

The Wilson Heavy Duty Binder is a decent binder whose price and name put it in a poor light.  Competitive products from Avery in this price range have more feature and smoother opening and closing.  The Wilson binder has the standard old fashioned type, and the cover is not attractive enough for professional presentations (portfolios, etc.).  The primary redeeming factor is the hinge, which stretches rather than rips under pressure.  I would only recommend this product if that is your priority or if it is on a good sale.

I received the chance to review this stapler from Swingline.1.  What's in the box?  You receive the stapler.  There are no starter staples included, so you will need staples.2.  Aesthetic:  This would be the main consideration in buying this stapler.  It is chrome-like all around the top and bottom assembly.  IN the middle, it is a transparent blue plastic, especially around the base.  Through the plastic you can see the stapler assembly.  All in all, it is very nice looking item.  This stapler is definitely a step up from the previous utilitarian black item I was using.3. Use:  As this is a standard use stapler, it is not built for stapling through a 1000 pages with industrial strength.  It is clear that the stapler is built for standard home and office applications where light stapling is required.  At this task, it works, and works well.  I have not had issues with jams and things like that.  The stapler works easily and well.  I have dropped it on a hardwood floor twice and no issues arose.  I would recommend that the user keep the included static plastic wrap included on the top piece to keep away scratches.Overall, this is a nice-looking stapler.  It is a break from cubicle conformity.  Nice item and I would buy this for the money as it is a welcome change of pace.

My non-tech husband often came into the house with his work-related iPhone saying, "I need to get prints of these photos..." and I'd say,"Right now?" And he'd say, "Well, I have to meet with zoning and they need photos for the client's file, so ..." And I'd say, "Aaaargh, I'm in the middle of ... oh, just eMail the photos to me, I'll download and print them ..."Which was the easiest way to get the photos printed without connecting this to that and by any approach, it was always a big lot of pain in the neck.Which brings me to, not anymore.Over 15+ years I've been a fan of Epson printers. They play well with systems and software and produce simple documents or beautiful glossy photos with ease. The wireless printers, including this model, now also print from most phones and tablets, both Apple and Android operating systems. For my husband's office space, that means he can print whatever he needs without running through a gauntlet. Yeah for me! And for him!The setup was straight forward, and the WorkForce picked up the wireless signal through two concrete walls (have your password ready when you set up your wireless connection). It also operates as a FAX machine (incoming and outgoing), copy machine, scanner -- all his office equipment needs are in one machine, one outlet, one footprint.I take off one star because the manual didn't mention that an app needs to be installed from either iTunes or your Android market (a free app) to your tablet or smartphone. You can print without the app, but won't have any control over the paper, quality, alignments or other customizations for your print. Look for Epson iPrint in your appropriate market. And then, enjoy!

I received this product as a Vine reviewer, not knowing what to expect. I am so pleased with it. It is an amazing product. As part of the Vine program, I received triple A batteries which normally do not come with it and several print cartridges-both plastic and iron-on labels which are also purchased separately. It comes with one label cartridge- the white plastic tape. I have not tried the iron-on yet. Each kind of tape tells you what the print color is on the cartridge itself.I have gone on a labeling frenzy because this product is easy to use! I have labeled file drawers, my photo bag(inside on the cloth), shelves and cabinets. I labeled some items with glow in the dark tape which really works. The label tape can easily be removed for repositioning and then reapplied. The printer only uses up the space it prints on, not wasting tape. I did a 2 line label which was also easy. The scissor cuts beautifully.The key is reading the instructions. The keyboard works somewhat like a computer but since the space is smaller, some functions are different. I had to look up how to delete label names and how to do all in upper case.The one tricky part came when I went to remove the backing. It is split horizontally to make it remove easier. I was trying to peel a corner.This is one of those products you do not know that you need until you buy it. I can easily see how a business would need one of these to label file cabinets, inventory shelves, and other drawers, but it is just as good for household uses too.I look forward to using the iron-on labels. I am sure I will be ironing them on for days!

It's a fairly simple device. Simply connect the USB to Micro USB connector cable to your computer, set up the software to your computer and fill in any software questions, such as color, resolution number, etc.The unit runs on 3 (AAA) batteries that supply plenty of charge for the scanning light. It also needs a micro USB card (which is not included). Get at least a 2 GB micro USB card. The buttons are also very simple. There are tiny indicators for battery charge level, color vs. B/W, resolution (up to 900 'dpi'), and the numbers of pictures scanned and whether the scanner is connected to the computer. The secret to scanning is to hold the item to be scanned flat and to slowly go over the document in a straight manner. If you swerve, you may get a blurred area. If you hit a bump in the surface, you may get a shadowed area.After scanning, simply stop the scanner, plug the USB cable into your computer and download your images. At maximum scanning 'dpi', it takes about 10 seconds of steady scanning. If you want a lower 'dpi' quality, it takes even less time. You can also go as low as a one-two second scan if you choose `monochrome'. Character recognition on type is very good (OCR).This scanner is lightweight, small and handy if you travel and need to scan documents, legal letters, news-ads or just photos or drawings when away from your home. It's not perfect, but for the average user, it's a bargain. Kit comes with scanner, slip-on black cloth case, 3 (AAA) batteries, "magicscan OCR software" and directions (the directions are very small print). After a few tries, you'll get the ease of it all. Device supplied by manufacturer for an honest review.

I have a Brother ADS2000 document scanner. It is about the same price (actually a few bucks more expensive) than the Epson. It gave me a good comparison with this Epson DS-560. When I made the Brother purchase, I looked at this series of scanner and carefully read the reviews. I was put off by the concerns about setup. While I am a computer professional, I really don't need more hassle. But i the interest of science, I decided to give this Epson a try.PRO'S* Very fast and accurate scans. Epson is well known for its great photo scanners (I have one). The technology in the workforce is as good as my Brother. Scans are fast and process well.I expect that this machine will go on without problems for years.* Exceptional paper handling The Epson wins hands down. It did a great job of tackling paper that had been folded, bent corners, wrinkled, all sorts of stuff. It gave me no grief at all. My Brother can be choosy and will, on occasion, skew the paper and get jammed. So far the Epson didn't do that. This is a great feature.* Image quality is very good. It is on a par with the Brother (which is generally thought to be the best office scanner for the money). Colors were rendered well and black and white didn't smear or get muddy. Good job!CON'S* Horrible to set up. There is nothing intuitive or easy about setting up this scanner. It is not plug and play by any means. It comes with a bewildering array of software, all of which I didn't want. Setup instructions are useless. Expect to put in some serious time getting this going. In fairness, while the Brother was easy to set up, when Windows went to Windows Update to update the driver, the driver software it installed would not work with the scanner. That is not a Microsoft problem it is a Brother error in driver setup. To get it going again I had to reinstall and prevent updating the driver on the disk. At least the Epson avoids this annoyance.* Once installed, configuration is really difficult. This scanner is very versatile (I think), hence the elaborate configuration it needs.* Figuring out the settings for particular documents will take time. The learning curve is steep and a lot of experimentation is needed until you understand how to get the results you want.Many people want OCR (Optical Character Recognition) software to make indexing documents automatic. Trail (read: few features) software is included if you want that. Virtually every office scanner comes with this stuff, so it shouldn't figure in a buying decision. I have to say that given the number of really good office scanners out there with virtually identical features, the Epson's difficult setup and configuration would tip the scales for me to go to a competitor. That's too bad, really. Epson is a fine company with a strong reputation for quality products.

These markers are very handy to have around for anyone who uses a dry-erase board regularly. I have a calendar and a grocery list, so I use dry erase markers a lot. The ink gauge is really handy, as is the marker shape so they don't roll when you drop them. They write clean and neat, they have a smell but it isn't bad like some other markers and the color is bright and vivid. The eraser and spray is handy too.

I live in a townhouse community, so I have a lot of restrictions as to what I can and can't do to the outside of my house. Well I have a dryer vent that attracts sparrows every spring. The cost to clean this vent is $150. To put on a different vent cover I would have to get permission from the Board, and also be responsible for removing and replacing it with the original if I ever leave. What a pain! Well I purchased a plastic vented cover for the vent, and cut the cover to size, and attached it to my vent with this product. This has been a very rainy, stormy, and windy week, and the Velcro has held the plastic cover to the metal vent securely. The cover is easily removed for cleaning, or permanently if wanted, and the sparrows can't get in.UpdateHas made it through the entire spring, summer, and now fall seasons. We had some storms, and wind, where I was sure I would have to put the vent cover back on, but this Velcro kept that little plastic cover attached to the metal vent cover. The plastic cover is open of course, so that there is air flow, kind of like a berry basket, so the Velcro, on one side,isn't on a flat solid smooth surface, and it is still holding.

The quality of this printer is very good. The feature that I wanted and like is the fact that this is a network printer. I have both, a Mac and a PC and it works with both without a problem. The Mac was able to discover the printer without any help. The PC had to be configured with the IP address. After that minimum setup, it just worked.One word of caution is that this printer sucks a lot of power when warming up. In fact, I had to install a separate circuit just for the printer. Otherwise, it would turn my computer off every time it woke up. The back of it says it needs 10A, so keep that in mind.The only problem I've had with the printer (the reason I'm taking one star) is that after about 5 months, it started showing a 'fuser error' message on its screen which also said I should restart the printer. After restarting it, it would clear for a few minutes but then I would get the same message. I called customer service and they were very helpful. They suggested removing the fuser (gave me step by step instructions on how to do that) and installing it again. After that the problem was fixed.

The directions could be a little better, we had trouble, somehow it got on mirror view and we couldn't figure out how to get it off, We did finally get it back to regular printing but couldn't find in the directions how to do this unless I missed it. The printing is very small and not the easiest to read. It does print very nicely and it has functions like a flag to use when labeling wires which is a great function, my other label printer couldn't do this. The print type is good and easy to read. The unit is small enough to hold in your hand and very portable so it would be great for any occasion or place. There are a wide variety of label colors to choose too. A very functional machine.

No more licking!Works great on regular envelopes and also on a box of 500 older self-seal envelopes I had that the gum had deteriorated. Breathed new life in to aged self seal envelopes, works on regular envelopes, and no more nasty tongue!

I became an Epson Printer user (for at least 20 years) after I had a bad experiences with the most popular brand printers.  I bought the Epson 4530 to replace an older Epson that finally died.  This ink is great --- dries quickly, does not smear and the cartridge is very large and a lot easier to change than the smaller cartridges on previous models.  I would give this 5 stars except I think it is overpriced.

I was looking for something to organize some of my teacher papers... so when I was offered this I jumped at the chance.  I love it, it's super cute and trendy with the green and it looks like it's sturdy and will hold up.  It's been a huge lifesaver to sort my answer keys by grade for homeschooling.But I'll be honest.  If I had bought it I would be disappointed.  I can't imagine spending eighteen dollars on an item that is really just thick pieces of cardboard covered by sticky, trendy paper. I honestly think you can do better in the value department.

It is so easy to use these laser printer labels. There's a pre-loaded template in Word (you just have to select the item #), and they print clean and clear, and peel and stick easily. Just what we need in our busy lives -- simplicity!

This is exactly what it purports to be -- an excellent packing tape (always had great results with Scotch brand tape and adhesives) which can tear by hand rather than needing scissors, teeth, or a dispenser.  However, it can be cumbersome if you are a frequently packaging.  Since there is no dispenser, then when you use a roll, you let the tape stick back on itself -- necessitating that you find the edge and peel it back every single time you go to use it a fresh time.  Not such a bad payoff if you're the occasional user and want to throw a roll in your desk drawer without a huge dispenser taking up room.  But if you frequently package boxes for delivery, you'd be better off with the right tool for the job and that would involve a packaging tape dispenser and regular ol' packing tape will do in that case.

As a student and a teacher simultaneously, I'm always on the lookout for items to keep things organized--especially color-coded ones. These tabs are great! When attached to an item in a binder, they allow easy access and organization, without adding bulk. The matte surface of the tab is easy to write on, and if you use pencil you can even erase. A winner!

As my office goes paperless, the famous Bankers Box is an imperative to rid me of outdated paper files. There are four (4) boxes in this selection; each white cardboard box is 10  by 12 by 24.5 inches with handhold slots and black grips at each end for carefree lifting. An inner flap flattens re-enforcing the sturdy bottom of the box and then two (2) long outer half flaps fold over to act as covers to the box which are secured by black ties which then wrap around black buttons on each end. Now for shipment …..

I have been looking for a long time for labels to just write out an address on - not labels that have to go through a printer.These labels are large enough for package addressing.  And the other benefit is that they are thick and instead of trying to get old labels off boxes to use them to re-ship something, these labels totally cover up the old label with no show-through!  They are awesome!If you are wanting labels to write on and don't want to use a printer, these are for you.

I ordered these labels intending to use them with my printer.  The product name on Amazon product page did not say that the labels were WRITE-ON.  Upon receipt, I saw words "Write-On" printed on the packaging and then I found that (!) Technical Details (!) on Amazon say "Just write, peel, and stick".  I didn't think that it was necessary to read technical details for shipping labels, but now I know... Although, I wish the product name on Amazon included this very important fact.That being said, the labels work well.  They come in a neat pad attached together at the top, and just the right size for most applications.The labels are easy to write on (pen does not skip like it may on some other type of paper), and they stick well with edges staying down and not curling up.This is a great product if you need to create one or two shipping labels and are in a hurry, but if you need to ship a bunch of stuff, printer labels would be a much better solution.
my son used these to help him with school organization and apparently, they helped (which is always a plus!). Can't complain about that!

These "White Easy Peel Address Labels" from Avery really speed up addressing envelopes or packages.  The new "Pop-up Edge" design is a time saver.  A simple bend of the sheet back at a column, and you're ready to place the label.  They seem to stick well, even through the postal service. I never had one fall off of an envelope yet.  When sticking a lot of envelopes they make the job easy. Try them !

I like the method of wrist support on this much better than gel or memory foam type pads. It keeps the wrist and hand at a good angle and feels nice with a little 'bounce' to it to help keep your wrist happy.The mousing surface itself is very slippery, however the wife's cheap mouse has little round feet on it to slide on, and she says she can feel it catching on the pattern on the pad, and it irritates her. So she uses it with her old mouse pad on top of it, because she does like the wrist rest. My Microsoft mouse has two long strips at top and bottom to slide on, and it feels fine to me.It's a little pricey for a mouse pad, but the wrist support is nice and comfortable.
These Scotch self-sealing laminating pouches, bag tags with loops, work well. They have been easy to use and stay sealed.
These are well made and have several uses. I keep these on hand and use them as binder clips as well as a handy clamp for craft projects.

These are decent sticky notes, but fail the critical test vs. Post Its - they don't stick as well (and upon repeated use).The appearance is also a bit different from regular PostIts if you really want to be anal about it (you can see the band of adhesive from the front of the sticky note).Big issue - less sticky.  I'll stick to 3M Post Its.

There are only so many things you can say about a bulletin board:  it's strong, seems to be very sturdy and holds my notes nice.  I'm using all colors of push pins, so it's rather decorative, too.I've seen on websites where you can purchase fabric and staple fabric to the cork and make it very pretty.  You can also add ribbon, so that you don't need to pin notes, just slide them in.  I'm not sure about the ribbon but I do believe I want to try the fabric application so that I can have a strong, sturdy and nice and pretty bulletin board.We're moving in March and I'll have to pick a pretty fabric to match my yellow kitchen, which is where this bulletin board is going to be hanging out.  In the meanwhile, it's hanging out in my kitchen right now and it'll be there, covered with little and medium-sized notes.  I would recommend this bulletin board to anyone who needs one.  It's a nice size, not too big and not too small; it's just right for me.

We love these Scotch Restickable shapes. The kids will stick them on letters to grandmom, stick them on the refrigerator, their dresser mirrors. I walk around the house and I find stickers everywhere! I haven't found one on the dog yet but that's only because they don't stick too good to hair but everything else go for it! This is a great printer. It's easy to use, doesn't jam much and you can use "knock-off" ink to save lots of money. The printer alerts me when a color is low, which gives me plenty of time to log onto Amazon, buy a cheap refill and get it shipped.It prints great using heavy stock and regular 20 lb paper. Makes good photocopies and is very user friendly.If I was to buy another printer, I'd get the very same one.

I really didn't see that much difference in these envelopes versus the peel and seal envelopes.Both have the blue inside, but instead of having to pull the strip off where you seal the envelope, this kind of envelope you just raise that part, and then put the flap over that, make sure it's closed and that's it.The weight of the envelope isn't any heavier than regular envelopes.I do like that you don't have to lick the envelopes closed, but you don't have to do that with the peel and seal envelopes either, much in the same way you don't need to lick stamps anymore to adhere them.I did notice that this kind of envelope it is alittle harder to open, so I guess maybe that is a good thing?I always put a piece of scotch tape over the flap of the envelope, to make it harder for would be thieves to get into the envelope, but I also add sealing labels, so I do that to protect them too, as well as my mailing label, in case the envelope gets wet.I have had mail theft more than once.  Money taken out of an envelope that was meant as a gift to me, which I never received.  Have documented that with my postmaster general.This isn't a bad envelope, just ok, at least to me.  I would like to see an envelope that is alittle heavier than this, in the same size.  I have always liked the blue lining, which this envelope also has, so that it's harder to identify the contents of the envelope.

The Mead 2-Inch Zipper Binder is the right size for high school students. The tri-color blues are more subdued (a little duller) in person than in the photograph and they don't wrap around to the back which is totally the middle color. My daughter would have preferred that the back was designed in the darkest blue so it wouldn't show the dirt as much when you set it down (as you will).The front has to places for pens/pencils and a zippered pencil case/outer pocket feature that includes an inner pocket and two elastic bands for holding pencil/pens.  On the inside there are two gray "slash" pockets that go about halfway up the binder. It would have been nicer if one was a three-quarter pocket but on the left there is also a 1/4 of the way up grap pocket with an outer pouch attached to it with a flap done in two of the blue tones (about cell phone sized but not padded like you would want if you were putting you phone there so more likely for post-its, paperclips, etc. The binder itself can be spread out flat for convenience, which is nice.The real problem comes with the 2 inch rings. They open fine when you hold both end tabs but trying to close them is harder because the rim around the tabs pushes into your thumbs and its uncomfortable. The easiest way is snapping the rings back together by hand which is what folks often do, so your studentswill likely be fine with the binder if they don't mind that.

these adhere better than regular post-its. for one, instead of just the top being sticky, the entire back surface area is sticky except a strip of area where you lift and peel, i.e. the adhesive and non-adhesive areas are opposite to the regular post-its. i've stuck and removed these at least 10 times on boxes, papers, plastics and appliances, and they're still sticky!! also, no flyaways. i can't imagine using "regular" post-its over these super-sticky ones, unless you need to peel them off quickly, perhaps during a whiteboard chart/presentation with notes that need to be shuffled around.don't expect them to stick on non-flat surfaces - they're not stickers or permanent avery labels. these are a nice compromise between regular post-its and one-time-use labels. they are a bit pricey, so use them if you'll be moving and shuffling the contents of boxes, noting the same section of a long document which is constantly being edited, etc...
I like these pens so well, I purchased some of them for my equine veterinarian -- he never has a pen when it's time to calculate the bill.  I'm hoping he finds them function in his environment.

This Verbatim cartridge works great, fit perfectly in the printer. I've noticed it seems to yield a good amount of ink. Its very cheap though, so I love it and so does my family (We're mostly students and consume a lot!). The price was competitive. The Quartet Magnetic Dry Erase Board is just fine for quick notes, etc.  It works fine with the only limitation being that the magnets are not super strong.  But you do have the option of sticking it to a surface as well.  Unfortunatally there's not a lot more to say about a dry erase board but this one is just fine.

This is a great wireless color all-in-one.  I've had other all-in-ones from Samsung, Cannon, and other HP models, and this HP is my favorite so far.The first thing you'll probably want to know about is >>PRINT QUALITY<<.  No complaints here!  Black and text-only documents print clean and crisp, even on inexpensive copy paper.  Color printouts, particularly photos printed onto photo paper, are accurate and have no banding.>>SETUP<< was a breeze.  The installation software walks you through the steps, and I haven't had any issues accessing the printer wirelessly.  Also, the on-screen menus on the printer itself are extremely well-laid out and easy to navigate, and it responds quickly to each press of the finger.>>PRINT SPEEDS<< are pretty fast, especially compared to other units I've had in the past.  I also love the auto-duplex function for printing to two sides of the paper.  I actually changed my default settings for the printer to auto-duplex when I print unless I tell it NOT to since a lot of my printing is text only and I prefer to save sheets.  This way, I don't have to manually turn auto-duplex on every time I print.The >>COPY<< speed is decent, even when copying in color.  So far, the quality of copies are as close to the originals as I could ask for.The >>FAX<< features work good, although I did find that I had to reduce the baud rate in the printer settings for the fax so it would work over my VoIP line.  Once I reduced the baud rate to "Slow (9600)", I haven't had any issues sending or receiving faxes.  And I love the ability to fax 2-sided documents and the built-in address book for commonly used numbers.>>SCANNING<< speeds are also decent, and again the quality is as good as I could ask for.  And the "Scan to Digital Filing Network Folder" and "Scan to E-mail" buttons on the printer itself save me from having to go through all the steps of manually opening the scanning program and selecting my preferred settings and scanning and saving.  You can even set up your digital filing locations so when you scan to one particular folder that it saves as PDF in high quality, but when you scan to a different folder it saves as a JPEG instead.  Very cool.>>ANNOYANCE<<Now to the one small complaint that I have: every time I turn the printer on after it has been completely powered off (not just in power save mode), the printer goes through a "checking device... this may take several minutes..." stage that takes 2 minutes, and sometimes is followed by a ridiculous automatic "cleaning printhead" function that takes 8+ minutes and can't be canceled!  It's obnoxious, especially if you just have to make a quick copy or print a single document, so I no longer turn the printer off completely and instead have it go into power save mode automatically (which is energy star compliant).  Resuming from power save mode does NOT require those two time-consuming functions to repeat.All-in-all: a great all-in-one, especially under $250 (as of the time of this review).  It actually makes me look at HP a little more like I usually do Samsung... with love in my eyes!  :)

For the cost of these gift card mailers, you'd probably be better off just headed to get a standard greeting card and leaving the gift card inside.  While the gift card envelope has a special slot for the gift card and space to write a personal note, they're just too bland and generically decorated to be something that I would want to use to send a gift to someone special. Although the canon printers do sell the individual catridges, I recommend buying this pack.Individually you can pick and choose your color, but in the end you are going to need all of these cartridges and it's cheaper to buy them this way.The canon printers have been work horse for me and I've had no problem with the printers or the ink, just recommend buying the package of cartridges rather than the just the individual ones.

This chair was easy to assemble and didn't take long out of the box.  I like the fact that you can adjust the arms.  My husband uses the chair to read in. I'll start out by saying that I've been the proud owner of a Fujitsu S1300 scanner for the past two years. I have gone almost completely paperless at home through a combination of scanning to Evernote and Dropbox and haven't looked back since. The quality and convenience of my previous scanner was unmatched over the last couple years, but there had always been some items on my wish list.Enter the iX500I really believe this to be the end-all-be-all as far as scanners is concerned. I'll try to go through this review in a logical fashion.Purchase/InstallI actually received this unit on the first day it was released due to a connection I had (always love to be one of the first to have something). Bringing it home and unpacking it was familiar as this is my 3rd Fujitsu scanner (s1300 and s1300i for my parents) and setup was straight-forward. The install file on my MacBook was large, as usual, but took little time and was up and running. One of the main features/draws for this product was the wireless ability which I'll go into more detail later, but was easy to get setup. Overall took less than 10 minutes to start scanning. Nothing exciting.Initial ImpressionsThis thing is FAST. I never had a complaint about the speed of my s1300 or especially the s1300i, but holy cow, this thing scans documents like it's going out of style. Even at full resolution color on both sides it is hard to keep up with it.Secondly, this is by far an improvement over the s1300 in the aesthetics category. It looks like a very high end piece of AV equipment or something. So far my wife has not even attempted to make me move it off the kitchen counter where it currently resides. When folded up it is very unobtrusive and is very unassuming.I have to reiterate that I truly enjoy the fact that, now that this is 100% wireless, I don't have to keep it in my home office or attached to another computer (with 2 USB ports like the s1300s).Build quality is similar to the previous generations of Fujitsu scanners - superb.TestingSpeed - I was easily able to get the 25 pages per minute claim and even hit 32 pages while doing my latest mortgage refinance documents.Reliability - I put several documents through that either had a business card taped to them or a post-it note to see how it would handle them. All fed through perfectly fine and showed up as desired.Wireless - This is honestly the main reason for my upgrade. Having the ability to detach this device from any and all computers and allow for the scanning of incoming mail directly to Evernote is a godsend. The iOS app worked flawlessly to get the scanner to do whichever type of scan I wanted and instantly made available my documents. This means not having to pile up my mail on a weekly basis and batch scan it when I take everything up to the office. It also means I'm far more likely to scan a document before trashing it, ensuring that nothing is overlooked. In the past I've shied away from wireless peripherals like printers as I've had bad luck with them, but with the rigorous testing I've done this far I have yet to break this.Quality - As good as the S1300/S1300i as far as quality and OCR accuracy. This is somewhat secondary to main my needs but works well.Overall ThoughtsThis isn't the cheapest scanner you can buy but I honestly believe it to be the most convenient and well equipped. Aside from the cost savings of having to purchase filing cabinets, the psychological benefits of nothing have paper-clutter around the house and being able to find any document you need in an instant are huge. The iX500 has lived up to all my expectations and more so far.Future UpdatesI do plan on updating this review in the future with a few items. First, I am trying to get a video of the insane speed of this device uploaded. Secondly, I'd like to give some more insight into the reliability/long-term build quality of it. Perhaps in 3-6 months the latter will come. Please comment with any questions and I'll respond ASAP.Thanks

I bought these two scales simultaneously on Amazon. American Weigh Scale - AC-650 Digital Scale 650g x 0.1g Black They are by the same company, and obviously differ in weight max at 1000g or 650g. I will tell you more about them here to help you.I checked them both with a 50 gram weight, seen here, and they are each precisely at 50 grams, ideally calibrated straight out of the box.50-Gram Chrome Scale Calibration Weight Accuracy is spot on for each. Each has a Tare feature to allow one to deduct the weight of a container (too hard to explain, google if you need more info). Both made in China.They are precisely the same in that they are made by the same company, American Weigh. They both have a full 10 year warranty, and the same card is in each box indicating a 10 year warranty. They both have an AMS logo on them. They both shut off after one minute without use to save batteries, and they both require two AA batteries (included, but cheap no name batteries in each). They are both with blue backlighted screens during use, and the numbers on the screens are about the same size.AC-650 has: weighs up to 650 grams. Supplies ounces and grams only. 4.5 in x 2.5 in x 3/4 in, almost precisely the size of an iPhone. PLastic, with plastic buttons and metal scale bed. Removable clear case top, not hinged, fits well but loosely (as others have said in reviews, might fall off in a purse). No slip case. Solid build, battery hatch and weight is 117.7 grams/4.15 ounces.BT2-1000 has: weighs up to 1000g. Supplies ounces and grams and carats and ozt, gn and dwt (and if you need those, you likely know what they are). 5 inches x 3.5 inches x 3/4 inches--so 1/2 to 1 inch larger in length and width, but same thickness as the ac-650. Solid build, battery hatch and weighs 166 g/5.85 ounces. It feels heavier than the 650 by a long shot. It has a rubberized case which feel good but may wear and look poor over time, and it comes with a vinyl, soft slip case like a calculator. It has a hinged, attached flip plastic lid (which oddly and inconveniently, does not flip open all the way flat on the table--it stays about 1/2 closed all the time which can get in the way of larger items than hang off the scale). The plastic door can be unattached but would then leave the device to be turned on easily. Why? It has no physical buttons--it is a touch screen. Even the on and off button is on a touch screen. If the screen looks bigger on the 1000 than the 650, it's because extra screen room was used for the virtual buttons (on/off, tare, shift oz/g/dwt, etc.)If I was to carry one in my purse, or backpack, and needed only grams and ounces and wanted real buttons (the jury is really out, in my opinion, on the long term use of the touch screen on the bt2-1000--but it does have a ten year warranty), I'd choose the ac-650 based on size and device weight (it weighs 1/3 less), knowing that the clear plastic lid may get scratched (but the scale metal plate is well protected) and need an elastic to keep it on securely.The larger device is too "fixie", with slip case over hinged plastic case. The hinged case, although it sounds good, really just seems to be in the way, but I have to keep it on b/c of the touch buttons being easy to activate and turn on inadvertently. If one wanted a table scale, not as portable, and needed 1k grams, and measures other than ounces and grams, the bt2-1000 is great. I will use it on my table for weighing items I review for Amazon, and I will use the ac-650 on the go. Good scales, both.

Avery's Easy Peel 5160 address labels are much easier to remove from the printed sheet than the standard Avery 5160 labels.  But, that ease comes with a few limitations illustrated the images that I've uploaded.  These may or may not affect you.For this review, I printed an entire sheet of return address labels on each product.  The Easy Peel labels are unquestionably easier to remove than the standard labels, as you simply flex the sheet and the edges of the labels in one column detach from the backing sheet as shown in the photos I've posted.If you typically print full sheets of labels, you'll be pleased with the ease of removing the labels.  While the standard labels can sometimes curl, or get a damaged corner as you peel, these labels come off cleanly.But, there are two situations where the standard Avery product is still better:  printing single labels and re-using the sheet, and tearing the sheet into thirds for storage or distribution of labels.Microsoft Word (and other software) has the ability to print a single label on a sheet in the row and column specified in the label dialog.  This works well with the standard Avery product.  With the Easy Peel product, if you've accidentally bumped adjacent labels while peeling off printed ones, the labels may jam your printer.  (The jam-free guarantee refers to fresh sheets of labels.)If you typically tear your 5160 sheet at the perforations to get three columns of labels, you will not want to do that with the Easy Peel product.  As shown in the photos, unlike the clean edge of the older product, the Easy Peel coumn has  about 1/8" of the sticky label extending beyond the backing after tearing.

You can not only load it with papers but you can also store index cards in the two pocketed dividers.The other three dividers open for a title page or whatever you need to have front-and-center--maybe your syllabus, maybe a list of abbreviations, whatever.Some potential limitations: the capacity is for a ream of paper one inch thick. I bought this door security bar as well as aMaster Lock 265DCCSEN Dual-Function Security Bar. The Master Lock bar is made of a light weight metal. The top "fork" that goes under the doorknob is plastic and the foot is plastic with rubber on the bottom. The top and bottom cylinders (body) of the bar are locked by a metal pin that sticks through various holes in the bar. You push in the pin, slide the two cylinders to the length you want then allow the pin to pop out the closest hole. The Buddybar is made of thick steel and much more heavy duty than the Master Lock. The top and bottom pieces are locked together by a locking lever that fits into steel teeth on the side. All parts of the bar are steel including the fork at the top and the foot plate which is covered with a hard rubber to grip the floor.For both bars I did the following test: I put them on my front doors, which are a double set of doors, where the second door has slide bar locks at the top and bottom and the main door has a standard door knob that fits into the second door. The floor by my door is wood (just so you know what the foot was on). After installing the security bar and unlocking the front door I went outside through another door. I had the doorknob turned so it was only the security bar holding the door shut. I kept giving it very solid pushes with my shoulder for about 20 sec. I kept trying to see if I could knock the bar loose by repeated quick pushes (putting most of my weight into it) and quickly releasing.For the Master Lock bar the door itself was giving some, I noticed the area right by the knob (where the bar is) was giving a little. By the end of the 20 seconds it was slightly more lose, but was still holding firm enough to keep the door shut. When I went back inside and inspected it, the bottom of the bar had slid just a fraction of an inch (which is why it seemed looser at the end), but it was still secure. I'm sure if someone was really going all out they could eventually get through the door, but at least if they do I am confident I will be awake and ready to respond (and already on the phone with 911).When I used the Buddybar, there was noticeably less give in the door and it never got any looser. After the 20 second test I went in and checked and it had not budged at all. This thing is solid. If someone gets through my front door with this thing on it would require breaking the door itself.With information on bump keys (google it if you don't know what they are) easily available on the Internet it is becoming a more likely scenario for a thief to use one, thus potentially entering in total silence. While a chain lock or slide bolt would also make sure they had to make some noise for entry, I think the security bar will make the door more solid than either of those and give you more time to react. A medium set burglar who already bumped your deadbolt and doorknob lock could get through many chain or slide bar locks with one strong shoulder push. From my testing I think even a heavy set burglar would have to give at least several full on hits to defeat the Master Lock bar and would have to break the door with the Buddybar. In either case you should have more time to react.I think the Master Lock bar is a good economical bar and will be suitable for many people, but the Buddybar definitely provides superior security, though at a premium price.

The board pictured is a bigger board and it looks like there is a lot more cork than there actually is.  Shrink the cork about 33% and that is more realistic.  I measured mine and the cork width (the short direction) is only 5 X the width of the border. In other words, there is 1.5 inches of border to 7.5 inches of cork.When I measured the picture on the screen, however, it was clear the ratio there showed the cork being 7 X the width of the border.  In other words, the version on the screen looked to have a lot more cork surface area.  Shame on you, Quartet.Not sure why they'd show a fake picture, but if it weren't then I wouldn't take off points for its size, even though it is a bit small.Recommended ONLY if you want a really small cork board, and the 8.5 inch X 13.75 inch size works for you.

This little box of goodies is perfect for any student or office worker. It comes in a little compact box, so it's great for a trip or gift/stocking stuffer. I am an office supply junkie, so I've used almost all of these items separately in the past and would have loved this puppy to take to conventions or on work trips. It is slim enough to stuff in your purse or laptop case and has almost everything you need for a transportable office. I say almost because for me I would also need a pen and permanent marker, then I would have everything I use on a daily basis.LABELS: My favorite POST-IT brand tabs are the 1" tabs. They come in three florescent colors and can be labeled with a Sharpie if needed. They are strong, reusable, but don't fall off the paper so you won't lose your place. The test, study, and to do flags are the same size, but are of a lighter material for marking things that aren't so permanent. The arrow flags are the same thin label that can be removed and reused for quick markings.PEN: The highlighter with flags installed in the top of the pen is a useful, quick grab item if you don't have much space to carry or if you are running out the door and can only grab one tool. I prefer the pen with the flags vs. the highlighter, but that's just my personal preference.POST-ITS: The full adhesive POST-ITs can come in handy when you are trying to label something like a drawer or a wall - where regular POST-ITs might have trouble staying on. In this pack you get one square standard size and two long thin ones that are great for making notes along the side of a book or paper. I've come to love the Note Tab Top Tabs since I tried them awhile back. They have a thick, note card like quality to them and if you place them on the edge of a page, you can mark your place and put notes on the same page. The only item in this pack that I had never tried before was the Grid Notes, which is basically a larger POST-IT with grid lines on it rather than just lines. I can see how this sort of note will come in handy for me because I'm often pulling out a full grid sheet or a grid card to make notes, but this one will stick where I put it. No more grid note card falling out of my book when I walk down the hall!Like I said, the only thing I would have liked to see in this little pack (and it seems like they might have room for it) is a writing pen and a permanent marker to write on the tabs with.

Maybe I just got a bad batch or something.  The inside of each pouch isn't tacky at all.  It's almost impossible to keep pieces of cardstock or paper from sliding around inside when inserting into the laminator.  Then when that happens, the pouch and the items being laminated get ruined.  The pouches I bought before were sticky enough inside to keep stuff from slipping around.

The BIC pencil was easy to write with, but a little delicate to the touch.  The lead was very stable and did not break as I scribbled a page of notes.  The eraser worked well.  While I am not a mechanical pencil connoisseur, I was neither excited nor disappointed by the pencil.

is almost too good to be true.  I use it almost everyday for printing mailing labels.  Automatic cut is great.  Very good quality print and very quiet.

I've used my Magicjack successfully now for a year, and am sufficiently satisfied that we finally turned off our landline for good two months ago. Just about everything in our home, from our computers to our T.V. is now wireless. I like that. As I am one that fears new technology this was a big step for me but per usual, it all has worked out quite well.Having had several printers in my home over the past few years I can tell you truthfully that I still don't know a whole lot about them. For me they either work or don't work. They are either easy to install or they are not. They are either fast or they are slow. They either make good copies or they do not.We use this printer in our home and home offices (both my wife and I have our own office which is a good thing for more reasons than I can list.) Our printing needs are very low volume and speed is not a factor with us. Also, due to the nature of our work (mostly play, but indeed we do some work some of the time), the quality of the printing need not be of the highest of high grade.Now all that being said:This printer was amazingly easy to install. We have four computers; two PCs and two lap tops. The whole job was done in about 30 minutes. This is rather outstanding when you consider that neither my wife nor I am what you would call whiz-bangs. Actually our computer and electronic device skills and knowledge boarders on pathetic and we need simple, simple and simple, which with this copier we got.As to the quality of print. I am delighted with the quality of printed material. It is sharp, crisp and has a professional look. I really do not feel that this is a photo quality printer. It is fine and dandy for making general copies but they are not of the quality that I would present as presents or place in the family photo album. It is good enough for what we use if for.The speed is not all that bad. This is most certainly not a copier I would use in a "real" office situation where time is a big factor but since I am retired I have plenty of time on my hands anyway so this is no big deal for me. I will say that the scanning feature is quite slow...slow to the point of being almost a pain. I am not the most patient person in the world though, so that fact should be considered. We had not problems with the scanning feature. It should be noted that there is no feed tray here and you must scan documents one at a time. For us this is no big deal though.All in all, for our limited needs this is a fine product and we have no complaints other than the slowness of the scanning feature.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks
