இ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Summary:ѾѾѾ Somewhat recommended, with reservations and only lukewarm fuzzies.This device is just too much of an all-in-one compromise.  While it does offer more phrases than are usually presented in most travel books, it lacks the completeness and flexibility of a dedicated travel dictionary.  At best, you have the ability to speak some commonly used canned and pre-rehearsed phrases to people in a foreign country.  At worst, you may look like a dork holding the device up to someone, only to become thoroughly puzzled when they, in trying to be helpful, reply back to you with several sentences that you do not understand.In all major cities of the countries represented by the 6 cross-translated languages in this device, you can usually find someone who can understand some English.  The problem arises, especially in China, when you travel to smaller towns where the likelihood of finding no one who understands any English increases.  In such a situation, your best bet is to learn some of the native language using language books and CDs before you travel and bring those language aids along when you travel.  A device like this would mainly be handy as a communication aid of last resort.  A great concept...  But because it only accommodates pronunciation of pre-packaged phrases, and does not allow typing in of words or phrases, it is of limited use in actual scenarios of trying to communicate with someone.ѾѾѾѾѾ Excellent 5-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾѾ The unit is small and lightweight.ѾѾѾѾѾ Its cost is not that expensive; it is cheaper than buying phrase books in 6 different languages.ѾѾѾѾѾ It includes hundreds of common phrases organized into eight conversational categories.  It lets you save frequently used phrases for quicker access.ѾѾѾѾѾ The backlit LCD screen lets you see the translator in dark environments.ѾѾѾѾѾ It includes a password-protected electronic address book, world time display, and built-in alarm clock to extend its usefulness.ѾѾѾѾ Good 4-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾѾ I am always pleased with electronic devices that include two lithium batteries in the package instead of a lame "batteries not included" statement.ѾѾѾ Average not-good not-bad 3-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾѾ As someone who speaks German, Spanish, and Mandarin Chinese, I found that the sound quality was fairly good when headphones are plugged into the headphone jack.  But the built-in speaker tended to muffle some of the pronunciations, which is particularly problematic with languages like Mandarin Chinese, where slight subtle differences in the intonation and inflection of the pronunciation can result in huge, sometimes embarrassing, differences in meaning. (For example, by saying "ma" with 4 different tonal inflections to mean "mother", "scold", "hemp", and "horse", you could conceivably be saying either "Mother scold hemp horse." or "Horse scold hemp mother." or "Horse mother scold hemp.", thus providing much entertainment for the locals in China.)  And this device does not translate for Cantonese, which is another common, and quite different, dialect of Chinese.ѾѾ Bad 2-fuzzies feature ratings:ѾѾ There were various errors in the translations of both Spanish and Japanese. Overall, the European languages were rendered far better than the two Asian languages.ѾѾ Probably in the interest of keeping the unit small and compact, the ergonomics of the unit are unwieldy and very cumbersome.  If you were standing in the presence of a foreigner who did not understand a speck of English, to actually hold the unit in your hand and start to use the device to communicate something requires way too much button-pressing and, hopefully, lots of patience between both you and the foreigner during the amusing periods of silence while you press lots of buttons. The small LCD screen requires you to press buttons to scroll through most sentences. Unless you already had a phrase previously saved to your "favorites" list, navigating around the categories in search of a suitable phrase requires lots of button presses. And then by the time that you do actually find the appropriate phrase to use and hold the device up to the foreigner for him to listen to, if he really cannot speak any English at all, what will you do next when he speaks a reply of several incomprehensible sentences in his native language back to you?ѾѾ The Product Description for this talking translator mentions:"Being able to hear and see the phrases will help you blend in with the locals so you don't look like a tourist."But, trust me, if you are standing in a hotel, store, restaurant, or street of a foreign country holding this in your hand, you WILL look like a tourist just as much as someone who holds a language dictionary and phrase book in their hand.The Product Description also mentions:"Don't waste valuable time or luggage space if you're going on the trip of a lifetime or traveling on important business."Again, if you are going on a "trip of a lifetime" or traveling on important business, you WILL need the ability to communicate far beyond the phrases that this device offers.௫ Fuzzy Wuzzy's Conclusion:With the current state of the technology, *ALL* of the talking 1-way or 2-way multilingual translators that are currently available on the market right now are only marginally useful at best, and gimmicky complete wastes of money at worst.  Some of the electronic translators that only specialize in just one language are a bit better.  But any electronic dictionary or talking translator that tries to cover multiple languages is severely limited and compromised in what it can achieve.  And when you try to use these electronic devices in actual in-person conversations with a foreign person standing in front of you, they really do not work at all.  You would be FAR better off with a foreign language phrase book or practicing and learning with language tapes/CDs/software before you attempt to talk to people in a foreign language.

This is a pretty handy little stapler.  It is perfect for home use or possibly office use if you do not need to staple a lot of documents together.  While the unit claims to manage up to 15 sheets, this is a pretty far stretch.  This starts to show signs of fatigue at half of that count.  The device operates very different from traditional staplers.  Instead of your hand squeezing deploying the staples right from the get go and your hand strength compressing the staples, this one functions quite differently.  As you squeeze the handle, the potential energy is stored in an internal spring, when it reaches a predetermined load it releases the mechanism and the papers are stapled together.  This happens regardless of how hard or fast you squeeze the device.  It is very similar to pulling a trigger on a gun.I think this would be a great stapler for an elderly person who may be losing some grip strength, a child or someone with some physical disabilities that needs to bind a few documents together every now and then.  It would not be good for a higher use situation or one that requires binding many pages; especially if it is a more dense paper.I do like the way it opens for loading staples and the way it stands, ready for use.Would I pay $9.00 for it?  Nope.  This is a decent enough unit but it should be priced around $3.00.

There are many adjustments that can be made: 1) Seat height 2) Seat angle 3) Seat position (forward to back) 4) Arm rest height 5) Tension of tilt 6) Height of seat back 7) Fixed or dynamic position (i.e. ability to lock positions in place).The cushion is soft and comfortable.  It is relatively easy to clean by just blotting the surface.  I cannot comment on long term durability.  The seat back is a plastic mesh, which is soft to firm and the open circulation prevents feeling overheated when sitting for prolonged durations.  The arm rests are firm rubber but my right arm rest did not lock into place.OverallThe versatility, comfort and ease of installation make this a solid choice.  I would like to give them 4.5 stars but I gave them the benefit of the doubt for the minor QC issue that I described with the arm rest.

This thing is amazing.  It heats up quickly, in about 4 minutes.  It is very quiet, and works spectacularly well.  It is not lightening fast, but it certain does move thing through readily.  The top flips up for cleaning or clearing out any misfed items.  I haven't had any issue with misfeeds, though.  It accomodates items up to 12.5 inches wide, and has a detachable tray for the back (not shown in the picture) to receive the items as they pass through.  Also, although the picture looks as though there are no handles, there are handles on the sides that push in to accomodate your hands, and spring back for out for a smooth look.The machine is very sturdy and well made.  I expect that it will last years as long as it is cleaned once in a while.  A cleaning sheet is included in the package.I cannot say enough good things about this machine.  The only caviat is the rubber feet might stick to the surface you have it on.  I had it on a wooden table and they stuck.  I was able to get them unstuck, but had to clean the rubber residue off the table.

This is pretty cool Post-it dispenser.It's apple design looks great on my kitchen table, I also have Post-It notes on hand when I need them.Post-it refills can be bought at an office supply store.I also like the apple design because I'm a Beatles fan!

I was excited to try out this printer. I remember that the Kodak printers were a big deal on The Apprentice and I would love to buy affordable OEM ink. This printer has some great points, and then some not so great points:The Good- Wifi works well so far- Ink is cheap compared to HP ink- Built in card reader- CheapThe Bad- Poorly designed paper tray, in fact one of the worst I've seen- Color quality on photographs is not as good as on my HPAlthough this printer has all of those good things going for it, in the end I just didn't care for the color quality in photographs. For schoolwork, reports, etc the color is just fine, and this would make a good all around family printer, but I would just stay away from printing photographs. The two biggest benefits of this printer is the built in wifi and the cheap ink. If that is important to you, I would recommend this printer.

This is really a very good cartridge.  I have tried no name brands, but I have been very disappointed.Get the canon brand, spend a few more bucks, and get excellent quality as well as a great sheet count.  This cartridge lasted longer then any other cartridge I have tried.

Great price...Prime shipping. The standard in permanent black (or any color for that matter) markers. Definitely a go to writing implement at both home and work. I use them to label anything and everything. Two of my most frequent uses are labeling CDs I burn and laundry items. The ink stays on these items forever and continues to look crisp after years of use and washes (for the clothes only of course).

Georgia Pacific makes good paper. I've put many 1000's of sheets through my laser printer. I buy this brand of paper frequently, and I alternate buying this in the 1-pack, 3-pack, or 5-pack here on Amazon depending what the current price is, so I'm getting the lowest cost per ream.

I really liked the assorted designs of these tab dividers. I think they're very pretty and quite fun looking. I think the quality of these dividers is pretty average.  The listing states "Heavyweight Stock" but they don't seem very heavyweight to me.  They actually got a bit bent up in shipping.  They may not be as durable as some of the options on the market but they are probably quite a bit thicker than most of the options out there.  I'm sure there are some poorer quality options out there on the market but I'm sure there are many better quality ones as well.  The thing that may pull me towards these ones is the fun, unique designs.Although I like the fact that it's easy to just write on the tabs, it makes it hard to reuse the dividers. I have always thought it was a bit of a hassle to have to worry about printing out your tabs out on a computer or writing them on little perforated tabs that would be included that always seem to fall out. This is a quick and easy option and probably one that I prefer.I like this assorted design set. I think they're nice and girly. I'm happy to see that there are other options out there that may be more suitable but still fun for the guys.I would recommend these tab dividers. It's something different from the plain options that we've probably all used for years.

I like the slightly wider-than-normal, slightly heavier paper that Mead often includes in its notebooks. But most of all, I like this "Quick Notes" format--ruled paper for the first 2/3s of the page and, at the bottom, is a light yellow "Quick Notes" section, unlined and perfect for notes of information that are important to the written text above.  It's a unique design and I found it very useful.

I love these pencils. Now that I have followed the advice of other reviewers and bought a better pencil sharpener, a battery operated eraser, and a dusting brush, I am happy as a clam with my colored pencils and can enjoy them more, so thank you to all of the other reviewers! :-)These pencils are just fantastic. I have been practicing on Dover Coloring Book pages, and I love the results. It took a bit to figure out the best ways to blend colors (and I did buy a few books on colored pencil drawing), and I love my blender pencil. I would recommend these pencils to anyone, and buy them again in a heartbeat!

To begin with this chair is very large and heavy. The base is comprised of very large metal tubes that seem to be in excess of 2 inches, although I didn't measure them. I was a bit unsure of the welds that hold the stem of the casters so I asked a friend who is a retired welder and I was told they could be a bit cleaner but would probably take a lot of abuse, something I don't intend to do since sending it back would be a nightmare. The shipping weight of this chair is about 74 lbs, it was bad enough I had to haul it up three flights of stairs. The arms are also very heavy metal with, what I would consider, very good padding and are at a height than my arms can rest comfortably. My keyboard has a memory foam rest and I prefer to rest my wrists on that rather than resting my arms on the chair while typing. The back is very stiff bordering on being hard but not really uncomfortable and it is very wide. I wouldn't consider this a true high back either. I'm 6' 1" but it's only about an inch or two above my shoulders. I suppose it's okay to call it a high back for someone that is 5' 7". I think it would be nice if these manufacturers would add an adjustable headrest much like in a car. This isn't really a bad thing either, my last chair was a true high back and on more than one occasion I would nod out during a webinar. Fortunately many of them are recorded. The seat much like the back is very stiff. I weigh about 270 lbs and at first this chair was not very comfortable but after a few weeks and the butt pounds have accumulated it has become very pliable bordering on comfortable. I can only guess that in the ensuing weeks it will relax more. The handle to allow the chair to recline  is easy to work and in an accessible spot. The tension is a bit of a pain to adjust but once it's set it doesn't have to bother with again. I have a carpeted floor and the dual casters are excellent and move the chair very smoothly. My only major complaint is the actual height of the chair, from the floor to the seat. I had to raise my desk about 2" by installing casters. My knees would often hit the pull out drawer. I did consider removing the drawer but I keep my Wacom tablet in there so that quickly became a non-option. Installing the casters wasn't such a bad thing because after moving the desk I found some things I have been looking for awhile as well as finding some dust bunnies that were on the verge of becoming a life form.  So in the future it will be easier to find those things and control the dust bunnies. Overall I like this chair a great deal. It's very solid, on the verge of becoming comfortable  ( all things have to be broken in after all) and it's a very good looking chair. Considering the price it's also and excellent buy.P.S. One thing I did forget to mention is the problem of the bolt covers popping out, I read this in other reviews prior to buying this chair, the way to resolve it isn't by using super glue or just leaving them out but use a little known product, unless your a photographer, called Blu-Tak. It's a reusable adhesive used instill life or product photography to hold a object in place and it doesn't leave a residue. Anyway, knowing this was a problem I made a little ball of some Blu-Tak and stuck in the socket of the button and it holds it firmly in place, end of a potential problem. Not a truly inexpensive product but works great.

This is a paper clip and small note pad holder and does exactly what it is intended to do - hold paper clips and post its.  When it arrived it came in a small box, but I was surprised by the weight of this small box.  This holder is definitely not your typical flimsy plastic paper clip holder.  This could easily double as a sturdy paper weight. This is a very nice looking holder that would probably work with any office design - It is clear and professional.  I use it for my home desk.I gave it 3 stars because I like my desk top office organizers to be a little more multifunctional.  In my opinion, this would be a better product if it could hold files on the 2 side slits, but the slits aren't really high enough to support a medium size file.It works for what it is intended for and it looks nice.

This is a creative idea.  I like it for making notes as I read; I can tailor the size to the amount of writing I put on it.  The bright color is attention-getting, so you can use it to label things in the kitchen or elsewhere.I suppose it's relatively cheap, but then again, so are regular Post-its. I don't know if they'll sell refills, but if they do, that would be good; it would be a little wasteful to toss a plastic dispenser every time.

Here are some of my points on why I liked it and not so far.Pros:1. Prints multiple kinds of paper2. Easy to install and set up3. Nice look/design4. Wireless5. Prints, Copies, and Scans (Faxes too, but I don't need that)Cons:1. Took a while to get AirPrint to work2. Bigger than I thought3. A bit loud and slow (but it is a home printer so who cares)4. Some instructions not clear (like "press and hold WSP" but it doesn't tell you that the WSP is on your internet router, not the pritner)Overall I really like this printer and I am sure I will grow to love it over time. This will work with your iPhone, iPad, iPod, Mac, HP, etc. Just check the systems. Some older models don't work.

I can only gives this 4 stars because I'm a bit of a stickler (no pun intended!) when it comes to accurate product descriptions or labels.My definition of "Sure Start" means that the tape never sticks to its guide and or never falls-out of the guide and sticks to itself again and you spend 5 minutes spinning the clear tape round and round and wishing you had finger nails to get the tape started again.  (We've all done this, haven't we?) (If you could visualize when that's happened to you in the past, then you would be misled if you bought this Sure Start tape dispenser thinking it solved all of those issues!)"Sure Start" should also mean, you slap it down the side of a box and pull and it instantly sticks (starts) and you're done sealing your box in record time.Well this tape does not live up to my definition of "Sure Start" - it doesn't surely start everytime and you'll likely need to hold the tape down the side of the box to get it started.One thing it does do is "Glides Easy" - you pull and it unravels with minimal effort and produces low-noise.  This might be helpful if it is really late at night, it's about to rain (ie. you have arthritis) you're a procrastinator, it's the week before Christmas, and your kids are light sleepers. ;-)

From box to first print, took all of 10 mins to install and I couldn't be more pleased. Set up was beyond easy with the printer telling me what to do, I didn't even need the instruction booklet except for installing the cartridges. First plug in wall, put ink cartridges in, close cover and pop in the cd to install the printer's software. The CD comes with a creative zone and picture software for editing and making greeting cards, calenders,ect. It also allows you to add the printer to your wifi network either on the printer or on your computer. Multiple computers can print to the printer which is great for families of savy kids. I haven't tried printing from my cell yet, due to issues with the phone company, but there is an option to do so. I like the idea that you only need to replace the cartridge that is out of ink (there are 4, black, pink, yellow, and blue) which will undoubtly save on costs.The image that is produced is above my standard of quality. The speed is unreal. Printing 2 sided from your computer is within seconds, the paper doesn't even need to go back in through the feed since it is done the first time. copying and scanning, too, are a breeze and produces clear, perfect and instant touchable images. No needing dry time. Again, I couldn't be more pleased and I highly recommend this printer to any and everyone.

I *love* pink. And I like hearts. And I *love* Post-it Notes, so I thought this would be a great item to have on hand.And it is... except I wasn't expecting it to be so large (the package is 5" x 5.25") and so heavy (1 lb., 5 oz).And the heart holder is "whimsical" as the description states, but it would be cuter if there were some designs on it (like the designs on its packaging) - it's just pink.Taking it apart and refilling is quite simple - just unhook the latch on the bottom and the top pops off. The package came with a 50-sheet pad, but it looks like a 100-sheet pad would work as well, though I don't have one on hand to test it. As other reviewers have stated, this dispenser won't work with regular post-it notes - you have to use the pop-up kind.Pulling sheets out is easy and you don't have to worry about accidentally grabbing two or three.This is definitely not something you would want sitting on your desk at the office - unless you work for a creative company. :)

These storage boxes have been designed with multiple needs in mind.  They are extra sturdy, the handles are reinforced with hard, black (classy looking) plastic, and the front window enables one to see what is contained within the box.  These storage boxes are especially appealing if you need to keep them in a place where they'll be seen as they are decorated with a damask pattern. They are a little pricier than a standard storage box, so if they are just going to end up in the corner of a garage, the extra features probably aren't necessary.  However, if you need to use them in a home office or bedroom where they aren't out of sight, the decorative pattern and high quality construction are worth the extra money.

This is the neatest product! You get four different color bordered tabs and each color comes in a stack of 6 much like sticky notes. They are made of a durable yet paper thin acetate so they don't add any thickness when a lot of paper is stacked or inside a book to mark pages. The writing surface is a mat finish which is great for markers but if you use pencil it was surprising to me you could erase it and reuse them. These are like regular tabs having sticky on the bottom 2/3 of the back but the side you write on is on the opposite side. So the entire 2''x1.5'' is exposed on the page or folder in other words they don't go to the back of a folder or page they go on top so you will see the whole 2x1.5 tab. Actually the entire area is the same texture so you can make notes on the whole thing not just the 1/3 at the top in white. This is very cool for using in cookbooks you can make notes on the tab rather then writing on the book! They are also easily removable without damaging the page. Great for flagging a book. I use them in my field study notebooks indicating dates and things of interest so I can easily flip to that page when I need to refer back. I will definitely be buying more of these they are just so great for so many things!
The tabs are handy -- come in a row on a board so the different colors are not all loose once you open the package.

Convenient is the right word to describe this printer. It shares much of the functionality of Workforce 645, while adding an extra tray and physical buttons are replaced by a large touchscreen. Functionality wise they are the same.The touchscreen makes finding the right button easier, since only some of the buttons are activated (only those that make sense in the current context). The extra tray allows you to place that entire 500 page ream inside the printer.I say convenient because it automates most things that cheaper all-in-ones require you to do manually.The following was taken from my review of Workforce 635, since scanning functionality is the same:Duplex scanning with automatic sheet feeder is a godsend. I really like the scanning capabilities of this thing. You have the option to use either the flatbed scanner or the sheet feeder.I recently opened a bank account with a local institution, and they gave me 32 sheets of documents with terms and conditions (with text on both sides). As soon as I came home I placed the entire stack of papers in the automatic sheet feeder of this device, opened Adobe Acrobat X Pro, and told it to scan whatever is in the sheet feeder and create a PDF document. Workforce 635 scanned the entire stack (both sides of each page), and Acrobat automatically created a single PDF document of every page in that stack while I was occupying my time with other things. Saved me 10-15 minutes of manual work. I really liked that. :)To be honest my excitement comes from the fact that this is my first duplex scanner, so I'm not sure how it compares with other duplex scanners. I also used the regular flatbed scanner to digitize pages of a book, and was impressed with its scanning speed (about 2-3 seconds for grayscale scans at 300dpi).Print quality is fine. I had to clean the print heads a couple of times at first (lots of ink wasted), but now it's fine.Buyer beware: there are no cheap 3rd party ink cartridges for this printer. Epson has apparently declared war 3rd party suppliers, and currently Epson is the ONLY supplier of Epson ink here in the US. It would be a good idea to avoid Epson printers if you want the option of paying for cheaper 3rd party ink. Otherwise, this is a great all-in-one printer for the money.

I've always been a fan of these four-ink BIC pens. I remember when I was a child, my dad would bring them home from the office and I loved clicking the different inks down and writing with the different colors. So it was a bit nostalgic to see a more modern version of the pen, which feels very familiar but has some nice improvements like the softer grip area and more muted colors of black and gray instead of blue and white. Other than that, it seems to be the same pen. It is still fun to click down the different colors, but I appreciate that I don't have to go rooting for a red pen if I need one to correct my son's homework. I'm still not sure why they have a green pen but that doesn't really bother me; I just don't use it. The pens write smoothly and I have no real complaints about it.

Ok, so the Avery Stamps.com Postal Center does do what it needs to do. I used it (under the Vine Program) for a few weeks, but had to cancel prior to them zinging my credit card. I guess if I had a small sizable business or something (beyond some of my E-Bay sales), it might have been worth it to me. But, I don't so it's not worth giving my credit card on a monthly basis for something which I would only use occasionally.

Musicians have a unique challenge because we must note changes we are directed to make but often are using rental music that must not be returned with writing. I've found that problem with both classical orchestral parts and show music. For years I've either cut stickies into slender strips or, when they were available, bought the skinny stickies. So that has brought me to wanting to try this new kind since I hoped I would be able to see the music right through them.Yes. I can use this variety that way, I am pleased to tell you. On the pad they look opaque but individually they are quite translucent. So I can stick them on, the yellow will get my attention, and I can write (with soft pencil; that's what we all use) on the part of the sticky that is not covering the music. It's that simple. They will work.

I am usually on the computer somewhere between 6-12 hours a day, mostly working and gaming. My wrist normally starts to hurt after about an hour without support. Because of this, I had been using a stack of napkins for support. No longer! I haven't had any problems with this wrist rest, which I have been using for about a year. I just got another one of the same model for work, and noticed that it is significantly softer. Expect this to harden quite after a few months of use.

They are nice plastic dividers for the "classic" size day planner (approx 8  x 5 ").  They are somewhat colorful (medium blue/light gray/medium green/gold/medium purple)--not vibrant colors, but nice, with the durability of plastic.The "write-on" part is iffy.  I tried a ball point pen, highlighter, and gel pen.  They did NOT work well, but did come off.  A Skilcraft Ultrafine point Permanent marker went on well and came off completely, within 5 minutes of use.  A Super Sharpie permanent marker did NOT come off. A number 2 pencil works really well and erases completely.So, only the durability part is really good, unless you want to use a permanent marker.

I like how these dividers work because it simplifies the printing of the tabs and the finished result is very clean. Instead of individual labels for each divider, there is a single sheet that fits in a pocket in the rear and you read the labels through the colored tabs. It was very easy to download the template from Wilson Jones for printing the tab labels in MS Word. There is also an online Javascript tab label generator. On the downside, the dividers don't move as freely as I would like. They tend to grab the binder posts. Finally, note that the extra wide dividers stick out considerably (beyond the edge of a typical binder) and are best used for wide media (like sheet protectors).
Like most Canon products, this photo paper is very good quality. I ran some photos on my i960 with excellent results. I highly recommend this item.

I'm not sure how much can be said about a tape dispenser but here goes.  I chose this item from Vine because my desk is dark mahogany/black.  This tape dispenser matches the other black accessories on my desk and it's nice that it's a more modern design.  It also holds the wide transparent tape and sits firmly on the desk.

I got this for my wife, who has started making a scrapbook of/for our son. This works AWESOME!!! The ink still adds up in a hurry, even with the separate cartridges, but I haven't found an inkjet that doesn't. But the photos look amazing, there is no doubt about that. It beats running to Costco on a regular basis.It was easy to set up and worked great right out of the box. I haven't had a single problem with it. Yeah, you are spending a lot for this printer... but I think you get what you pay for. In the end, I think this is worth every penny!

This "climate controlled" footrest is an example of a pretty good idea that doesn't quite work the way it's supposed to.  It's OK, but it would have to rank pretty low on any list of must-have home office accessories.The footrest seems pretty well built, and it looks like it should stand up fine in normal use.  The height and angle adjustments are in the form of little movable legs.  The adjustment range is pretty limited-- no more than an inch or so-- and I wonder about the legs.  If one of them snaps off when the footrest is being slid across the floor, goodbye adjustments.The biggest problem I have with it is that, like several other reviewers, I can't get my knees under my desk when my feet are on the footrest unless I push myself farther away from the desk than is comfortable.  I thought at first that this might be a problem unique to me, but after seeing it mentioned in other reviews, I think it's a general issue.The "climate control" fan is not very useful.  There are two heat settings and a fan-only setting.  However, you will have to get down on your hands and knees and reach under your desk to adjust the switch.  In addition, the fan is in the center of the unit, which means the only way you can make it blow on your feet is to keep them pressed together in the center.  This is most definitely not comfortable.Bottom line:  This is an OK product, but in my view, it's not worth the current price.

This is a nice, compact, practical pencil sharpener.  The only novelty of it is the USB functionality, but I find that to be a great feature.  You can use AA batteries or an AC adapter (neither are included), but for me, the USB is much better.  With USB, I can just pull this out of a desk drawer, sharpen a pencil using my computer's power, and then put it back up in the desk not to be seen for a month or so.  I don't have to worry about dead batteries, and I don't have to keep the thing plugged into my wall or occupying my desk.The canister for shavings is enough to sharpen about ten pencils from brand new to sharp.  The power is on the weak side, I guess, but I found it more than adequate, albeit it took a little longer than it would with a standard electric model.  I've sharpened a box of pencils with this and haven't had any problems.
It is as if you turned your home phone into a smartphone. I love this company! It is the best!

These are very good markers. Our oldest daughter is a very good artist, and we wanted her to have some better tools to use than she had been in the past. We were not sure these would fit the bill, but she says they work great, and have very good color. The color lasts a long time, but dries very quickly. She is happy with the variety of colors this pack has.

I've been thinking about getting an all-around printer for quite a while now. I have a separate printer and scanner both from HP which are a few years old and they are pretty reliable. The printer that I own is a Photosmart printer which I mainly use to print images off my camera or memory card. It has served me well over the years and just when I was about to come down to purchase a replacement, here comes an all-around printer from Vine.First impression was "this printer is awesome!" It possesses all the capabilities that you will ever need to make your printing needs, whether it be documents or photos, glide like a breeze.  On the plus side, it will also do scanning, faxing and copying so you are pretty much covered as far as document-related tasks are concerned. Another aspect of this printer that totally blew me away was its wireless capability. You can connect it to your network at home and print wireless from your pc or laptop anywhere in your house where you are connected to your wi-fi.Installation was a breeze. If you have installed a printer to your PC via wired configuration before, then you will not have any problems here. If you have an HP PC, it will auto-detect this printer right away and auto install the necessary drivers. However, if you want to be have the flexibility in printing, you might want to install the included software. Installing this via wireless network, wasn't a problem either. There is a setting on the printer for a Wireless Wizard Set-up where it will detect your network and you can just follow the instructions on the display screen to finalize the connection. Once it is connected to your network, you have to install the software to configure your pc to print wirelessly from this printer. And once set up is done, you might want to place this hunk of a big printer somewhere stationary and unobtrusively so it doesn't get in the way of anything. The sheer size of this office printer did not fit anywhere on my computer table.The printing aspect of the Officejet 7500A is where it totally blew me away. First, the speed at which a consumer-based printer can print 33ppm for black and 32ppm for color is just plain fast. You can without a doubt, print documents to meet any deadline. The photo printing aspect of this printer is another factor that is just plain amazing. I tried to print a simple photo from my pc and detail on the photo was great.  The quality is almost the same as you would get from a photo developing shop. The memory card slot is also a useful tool if you want to print documents or photos from it,  no need for a PC. The scanning function is also great if you want to scan documents directly to your pc as with the copy function to produce multiple copied of a document.This printer is definitely a workhorse but it is definitely intended for an industrial or office setting. Its sheer size and speed is not usually intended for the casual home use. Nevertheless, it is a highly recommended product!

The Epson V37 is a really nice scanner for the price, but then I would expect no less from Epson, which has always seemed like a reliable choice.  I love that it's compact and that the lid will lift to accommodate a book.  The images themselves are high quality, exactly what I needed to scan in some old paper money.  The details are crisp and clean; I couldn't ask for better scans.What I don't like is the software suite.  The Epson Scan utility is fine for a stripped down, quick scan.  However it closes after each scan so if you have a lot of items to work on, you have to reopen the program each time you put something on the scan bed.  The rest of the programs all have some limitation or peculiarity that make them awkward at best.If you have a good image program that will recognize the scanner, use it.  Don't depend on the stuff Epson has included.  But do consider this scanner if you want a tidy little workhorse.

For whatever reason my cute little 8-year old daughter has been dreaming of a whiteboard for years.  While it is sad that her wish went unfulfilled for years, I am happy to say that she's had this Quartet whiteboard for about a month and she tells me the dream is everything she thought it would be.  She wrote a list of house rules on the whiteboard (rules such as "don't steal our food"), she pinned her soccer schedule to the bulletin board, she put a mustache magnet on the whiteboard, etc.So I have to say this whiteboard is a pretty cool package of versatility and size.  It's not huge so I could hang it on her door.  It's got the magnetic whiteboard and the corkboard.  My only knocks would be that the outer trim looks stainless steel but it's actually plastic and slightly flimsy and it comes with velcro to hang but doesn't have any hook options if you don't want to stick velcro glue to your nice doors (I actually jerry-rigged my own hanger in the back to hang it).Overall, this is a nice product in consideration of the $22 price tag.  4-stars from me (1-star deducted for plastic frame, lack of alternate hanging options).

The Canon Pixma MG3220 is a great printer. To have the capability to print from my phone and my iPad, is the best!!! It was very easy to set up. Actually there was virtually no installation at all. We just had to connect via Bluetooth and we were ready to go. The picture quality is the best I've seen so far. It's very compact, so you can have it anywhere. I highly recommend this printer as your go to for all of your home office needs.

this eraser never goes hard, creates almost no "crumbs", cleans up paper beautifully.  I just wish I could get it on the end of a pencil instead of in a separate utensil.  Until then,,,,,,,,,,,I love these.

I have used duct tape, masking tape and other type types to mark areas or hold things in place.  This tape is excellent and will be at the top of my list when I need something.I used it recently to mark a board on the deck for a repair crew coming out.  It was on the board for over a week and went through rain and cold nights.  It went on easily and stayed on.  It's red color made it easy to see (I had a number of pieces in different parts of the board).  And it came off easily enough without leaving much residual adhesive behind.You would need some scissors to cut it, though if you attempted to you could use your hands, but I would not suggest that since it would be hit or miss.A great tape that is easy to use and works great.

PRO:  Overall, the unit fit our small business needs perfectly, topping out at over 70 pounds capacity.  It's tiny footprint, ledgible LCD, and portability make it ideal for our eBay and Craigslist sales.  I put a 40 pound speaker on it, fearing I would crush the poor little guy, but no harm.  We run it on its 9V battery, but have not used its included ac adapter. OK, so sometimes the old fashioned way really isn't best. I got this because I was dissatisfied with the various electric pencil sharpeners we have, and longed for the silken-smooth action of the old-style Bostich sharpeners, complete with revolving openings for different sized pencils and handy vacuum seal that keeps it sturdily attached to your desk as you sharpen. Well after putting a dozen pencils of varying size and width through the blades of this Bostich, all I can say is Ugh. First of all, don't try to attach the vacuum base on wood. It will not stay put. Every time I fed a pencil into the sharpener opening and started to crank, the seal broke. It only worked on a formica-like surface, which did hold the seal pretty well. Second problem, noise: the thing is so loud my granddaughter came in from another room to ask what was making so much noise. I was sharpening a pencil, Honey. Wow, that's a noisy pencil sharpener! Third, clumsy cut: the sharpening blades are incredibly rough, chewing up everything from a simple basic #2 pencil to a thick charcoal drawing pencil and everything in between. The points on each pencil were anything but fine -- the charcoal fell apart, the drawing pencils never reached a point, and the paper on one type of pencil I've used for years was torn to bits. No other sharpener has ever done that. This is going in the round file.

The XP-410 offers a lot of features for the price. First, it doesn't take up much room on your desk. Second, it sets up quickly on a WiFi network - in my case, it took less than 20 minutes from opening the box to making a test print. Next, the text print quality on 20 lb paper is bold and bright and rather quickly for text. That's about all most folks need from a printer in a small home office but the XP-410 doesn't stop there. It also has a very high resolution scanning feature that rivals my 4 year-old desk-top scanner that cost about 3 times as much. Photo print quality is good too - amazing, really when you consider the low price. You can print pictures from your computer or directly from an SD card plugged into the SD slot. Sadly, there isn't a way to print directly using a compact flash card  (and no USP port for an adapter). Given the popularity of SD in the point and shoot world, that's not really a big negative. Offsetting that minor printing negative, at least for the Apple / iDevice world, there is a free Epson app that lets you print from your iTouch, iPhone or iPad. I installed the app and made a test from my iPad in about 7 minutes. NOTE - the app works for all Epson Wireless printers.Epson calls this a small-in-one rather than an all in one because there isn't a FAX capability built in (you can, of course, scan and email paperwork and photos) so be aware of that limitation if you need a FAX-enabeled home office device. Also, it comes with minimal ink cartridges, meaning you won't get much printing done after a few pages or color-rich photos. It uses a common Epson ink cartridge (200) but I recommend buying the 200XL if you do a lot of printing because the basic "tanks" run out quickly. On the plus side, unlike some printers that have large tricolor cartridges, you can change just the single tank that's run dry.I like this printer and give it a star for the size and price. A star for the excellent scanner quality. A star for the quality printing of text and photos and a star for the simplicity of setup and availability of iDevice printing. It only loses out on a 5 star rating due to the fact that the low price doesn't include even standard ink cartridges so you have to spend more right away to keep using the printer. That may be an attempt to come in at a particular price point but seems a little sneaky to me and annoying when you run out of ink very quickly. (If you buy this printer, order extra cartridges at the same time to avoid being caught short.)Recommended if you don't need FAXing and Compact Flash capability.

I've mostly gone paperless in my home office and hate receiving paper statements, receipts, and bills. For years, I've been using scanners on multifunction printers to scan any documents that I couldn't get in electronic form, but knew there were better solutions out there, like the NeatDesk. I finally got to spend some time with one and while my experience with it was mostly positive, there are some areas that could definitely use improvement.PROS:- Quick and quiet scanning- ADF supports up to a 50 page document- Scan docs, receipts, and business cards- OCR does a good job of creating searchable PDFs- Print documents and receipts directly to Neat software- Easily create reports based on receipt dataCONS:- Scans are occasionally crooked- Business cards scan poorly- Neat software is a little buggy- Free support by email onlyWith my multifunction printer, I primarily scanned documents to PDFs. The OCR software wasn't very good, so my PDFs weren't searchable. I came up with a naming scheme and folder organization that would allow me to easily find them later, but the process was laborious. I put the time into it because I hated the paper clutter in my life. I was excited about the NeatDesk because it had the potential to save me a lot of time.IN THE BOXThe NeatDesk for PCs comes with the desktop scanner, power adapter, USB cable, a driver CD and Nuance's PDF Converter Professional 6.0.HARDWAREThe NeatDesk's glossy white plastic body and the dark grey input and output trays make the scanner look like a premium piece of hardware. The input tray has a multipurpose guide for 8.5 x 11 paper, receipts, and business cards. The guide can be removed to allow up to 50 sheets to be inserted in the scanner at once(only 10 sheets can be used with the multipurpose guide).  The back of the NeatDesk has a power adapter plug, USB port and a power switch.During my time with the NeatDesk, it scanned quickly and quietly. I didn't experience any jams while scanning approximately 100 pages of documents, receipts and business cards. I was able to scan a few credit card receipts successfully, but I mainly stuck with full-page, 8.5 x 11 documents. More often than not, the documents scanned straight, but on occasion, they were slightly crooked. The problem is that there's no adjustable guide to help keep the paper straight as it goes through. You basically have to depend on the rollers to keep the page straight while it feeds through to the output tray. Like I said, it worked well most of the time, but I'd still like to see an adjustable guide to avoid crooked scans.The only real hardware issue I had was with business card scanning. They scanned inconsistently.  Many cards scanned crooked, while some only scanned partially. I tried scanning about 20 business cards and only four of them scanned acceptably. I don't particularly care about scanning business cards myself, but I think it's worth mentioning for those who are looking for a business card scanner.SOFTWAREWhen I received the NeatDesk, I had no idea how much the scanner relied on the software. In fact, you can't use the scanner at all without first launching the Neat software; the Scan and PDF buttons don't do anything without it. This obviously means that the NeatDesk application is vital to the whole experience. Unfortunately, I ran into problems with the software on two separate occasions, which required me to uninstall it and reinstall it. Since the last time however, I haven't experienced any further problems. I'm currently running version 5 SP5 (5.0.26_85).One of the really nice things about NeatDesk, is its ability to scan documents into searchable PDFs. This can make finding your files much easier, if your system can index the contents of a PDF file. If you save all your scans into the Neat database, files are even easier to find. Organizing your documents and receipts in the application is pretty painless, though you'll still have to correct some mistakes that the OCR system will inevitably make. The Neat database stores all your scans, which can be backed up manually. I prefer to have a copy of everything as a separate PDF file, so after I scan a document into the Neat software, I export it as a PDF as well. I also have the Neat software remind me every three days to back up the database. It'd be nice if there was a way to automatically back up the database, but I've gotten used to backing it up after every session.I like the layout of the Neat software and found it to be intuitive and clean. However, the UI relies heavily on a pointing device (mouse). I couldn't find a single keyboard shortcut I could use. In lieu of keyboard shortcuts, a customizable toolbar might have been useful, but that wasn't available either.CONCLUSIONThe NeatDesk is a nice desktop scanner that's quick and easy to use, as long as you don't rely on it for business cards. The hardware is just about perfect, but could benefit from an adjustable paper guide. I like the software's interface, layout and functions, but support for keyboard shortcuts or a customizable toolbar would make using the NeatDesk even better for power users. The software also has some stability issues that really shouldn't exist on a scanner that costs nearly $400. To their credit, however, Neat continues to update the software on a frequent basis. I still recommend trying out the NeatDesk desktop scanner, but your experience will most certainly depend on whether the NeatDesk software will run properly on your system.* Review unit provided by The Neat Company

Right out the box setup is easy. The printer is a nice size so you will need a bit of space to operate it comfortably. At first I thought I had to buy the ink to fill the cartridges, but no, you just give each cartridge a 5 second shake and insert them into the printer.  The printer then goes through a 12 minutes ink adjustment.After this you install the installation CD when it says to.  The problem is installation took an hour on my PC.  If you have a slow internet connection this could take longer.  This lengthy process was a bit of a drawback, and I tried to keep busy doing other things nearby while my computer cycled through this.  The instructions do state that using a USB cable (not included) would make the installation process quicker, but I couldn't find one at the time, and I'm not sure how quick things would have gone since there were a lot of necessary downloads.After an hour the printer was ready to go.Wow, printers have greatly improved over the years; this one is SO fast! The only drawback is the scanner, and I experienced the same with Epson's WorkForce 840; they are too slow!  It took just under a minute to scan one small page of writing on the flatbed scanner. It just seems to me, with all of the technology, scanning would have improved, but even my 8 year old HP Printer/Scanner seems to take just as long. Interestingly, if I use the multipage scanner, scanning is faster - 6 pages of full color text in 3 minutes!  I can live with that.Overall I love this printer!  I highly recommend it to anyone running a home office.  All though, I'd also like to recommendEpson WorkForce 840 Wireless Inkjet All-in-One Printer (C11CA97201), too, it's a smaller version of the WorkForce Pro WP-4540.Oh, and before I forget, another cool feature is that it's Airprint compatible!  Which means you can print pages from your iPhone, iPod, or iPad wirelessly ~> way cool!

Fantastic! That would be my single-word review.  I'm currently using this with an iMac (on OS X Lion), a Windows 7 machine, two iPhones (both on iOS 4 and now iOS 5,) and an iPad 1 (again with iOS 4 and 5.  Previously, we had an older HP printer that refused to be seen by one or the other computer, so the compromise was to use my iMac, since we could use the now-common "hacktivator" to allow printing from iPhones and the iPad, and the Windows box would just go without.  Now the Epson allows all devices to print, hassle-free.  I can't complain about that.Set up on the Mac was as easy as can be.  I found the printer on the network and the Mac found the drivers it needed by itself.  A couple days later, there was an update that the OS found, too.  Windows, on the other hand, was the usual, expected drawn-out "experience" that it always is.  Install... slowly, find updates, install those... slowly, find additional software, install... slowly, a few error messages, etc., etc. Finally it worked, a little over an hour later, and since then it's been fine.  And after that, I tested our i-devices - the worked perfectly, with the printer showing up as it should with its name under the Print option wherever that is available in iOS, no app needed.  The printer takes advantage of Apple's AirPrint feature, so don't bother downloading any apps unless you have an older iPhone that can't use this.Printing, scanning, everything has worked flawlessly, with excellent photo quality on Epson high-quality photo paper. There was some confusion on HOW to scan, however.  The printer has a screen that prompts you to scan directly, that doesn't work - it wants you to scan to a card, not to a computer.  To scan to a computer, you must initiate the scan from the computer first.  It makes sense, I guess, but it's a little clunky.  I don't know why I couldn't choose a destination from the screen and have the scan sent there, but whatever.  It's a minor problem - maybe a bigger one if the printer was physically located far away from the computer, but not for us.One of the killer features that few seem to talk about is Epson Connect.  This is a service that allows you to send pictures from anywhere to your printer.  More specifically, it lets you take a picture on your iPhone and have it printed at home immediately.  Basically, it works through email.  You sign up and are given a specific email address, and when you use that, the photo you send through the address is then passed on to your computer at home to the printer.  If you have it loaded with photo paper, you will have a beautiful 5x7 photo print waiting at home.  The neat thing about this is that you can give this address to others to send their own photos to your printer, and vice versa if they also have an Epson Connect capable printer.  I've used this a couple times just for fun, but I can see how it might be handy on vacation - you know how pictures pile up and we're all loathe to actually *pay* to print pictures now.  Now you can send them home while you're on vacation and have them waiting for you when you get back.

Lately my life has seemed so shallow and empty but at last I can sleep at night. Scotch Heavy Duty Shipping /Packaging Tape "far exceeds requirements," to borrow an old job-performance-review rating. This tape does the basic job of sealing and holding packages together, and goes beyond that by being exceptionally strong and very transparent (the 38 yards of tape are wound onto a spool that is 3/8" thick with tape, which I calculate to comprise roughly 115 layers, and one can read the label underneath all those layers almost as if the tape were not there). The transparency of the tape means that one does not have to worry about covering the mailing label, or anything else on the package on which it is being used--everything will remain as legible as if the tape were not there (except for its shiny surface). The tape is sticky enough and highly unlikely to slip.This tape unspools easily enough, and the dispenser includes an effective cutting edge; but this tape is engineered for strength and does not have the "quiet" feature of another Scotch packaging tape that 3M makes. You should buy whichever tape more nearly suits your needs--this tape for strength, the other for ease and quietness of unspooling.The only thing I can think of that might make the product better would be to provide a convenient surface on which to park the leading edge of the remaining tape so that it does not flop around and re-adhere to itself--sometimes getting tape "started" (i.e. unsticking the leading edge) again can be a little frustrating. There are a couple of protuberances on the plastic dispenser to which one can secure the tape and keep it from sticking to itself, but they do not seem to be particularly well designed for that purpose--they seem instead simply to be guides to help keep the tape straight as it comes off the spool.

Avery Clean- Edge Business Cards are designed to produce professional- looking business cards directly from your home office printer. I wear several different hats throughout the week and I have separate business cards for my many different occupations. Some of my business cards are ordered online, but others, I design and print myself. Avery Clean- Edge Business cards have proven to be a good business card for this purpose.So, what are the advantages with Avery Clean Edge Business Cards? The quality I noticed first was the easy separation of the cards after printing. You bend the cards and they snap apart with ease. It is amazing how they hold themselves together so well during handling and printing, yet they snap apart so easily. I also like that the ink dries quickly and doesn't smear. And, of course, it is nice to have a product like this handy when you need business cards quickly and don't have the time to wait for an order to arrive in the mail.On the negative side, these business cards are quite thin. Other consumers have noticed and stated the same thing, and it is very true. They are more like a piece of heavyweight paper than a card, and this is something to consider if you contemplate making a purchase. Also, I have found that the printing works best if I feed one sheet at a time through my printer. If I place two or more sheets in the feeder and print, there is a good chance the print one the second, third, etc., sheets will gradually slide down. This doesn't happen if the sheets are fed individually and, in fact, this is exactly what Avery recommends. Some printers may work fine with multiple sheets fed at once, but to play it safe, feed only one at a time.Business cards are a necessity and Avery Clean- Edge Business Cards are a good product to have on hand when you want to make business cards or some other item. The cost per card works out to about eleven or twelve cents each, which isn't necessarily cheap, but the cards offer the convenience of in- home printing and thus the price isn't too bad. Add to that the clean breaking action and the lack of any smearing and you have a good business card for general use.

The best way to review this printer is to compare it to peers in its class I have also owned and have conducted A/B comparison tests with to see where each excels. I have included the PRO-100 as the first in the comparison.CANON PRO-100 - MSRP $499DYE based printer+Excellent quality on Canon Platinum Pro Gloss, Semi-Gloss, and Luster paper+With above paper, photo will last 50 years framed or 300 years in photo album w/o fading+Very good quality on Matte and Fine Art paper, but...-No guarantee on fade resistance with fine art & matte paper since it is uncoated & porous+Excellent pop and dynamic range than pigment printers - great for posters!+Good Black & White, but it has a very slight brownish tint you would not notice unless you had a PRO-10/R2000 print to compare it to-Some papers are water resistant, but dye is much more prone to water damage than pigment+Fantastic build quality, fit and finish. Built like a tank.+Fantastic quality paper feed path, will take nearly any paper easily-Cannot print roll paper+Since it is dye, your prints will more closely take on the characteristics of the paper it is printed on as the ink is absorbed into the paper.+Can sit for over a year without printing or being turned on with no clogsCANON PRO-10 - MSRP $699PIGMENT based printer+Excellent quality on Fine Art & Matte paper+Very good color, but not as much pop/dynamic range as dye+Excellent black & white+Very good quality on Gloss, Semi-Gloss, and Luster paper-Non-matte paper requires an extra overcoat of gloss, which is one of the replaceable ink tanks. If you print on gloss/semi-gloss/luster primarily, you will be changing the gloss optimizer cartridge more than any other one.+Over 100 year lifespan on all papers, with the exception that pigment is more likely to chip, scratch, or flake if not protected by glass since it sits on top of the paper.+Water resistant+Fantastic build quality, fit and finish. Built like a tank.+Fantastic quality paper feed path, will take nearly any paper easily-Cannot print roll paper-Since it is pigment, less variation in finishes as ink sits on top of the paper.-Must be turned on every other week to prevent clogging. Turning printer on will be enough to prevent clogging with this printer.EPSON R2000 - MSRP $599PIGMENT based printer+Excellent quality on Fine Art & Matte paper+Very good color, but not as much pop/dynamic range as dye+Excellent black & white-Very good quality on Gloss, Semi-Gloss, and Luster paper-Non-matte paper requires an extra overcoat of gloss, which is one of the replaceable ink tanks. If you print on gloss/semi-gloss/luster primarily, you will be changing the gloss optimizer cartridge more than any other one.-100+ year lifespan on all papers, with the exception that pigment is more likely to chip, scratch, or flake if not protected by glass since it sits on top of the paper unlike dye.-Water resistant-Good build quality, fit and finish. Oddly you need a spare parts box for this printer as things like the DVD tray and large paper tray do not slide into the printer as they do in the Canon printers. The roll adapter also must be stored seperately.-Fair quality paper feed path, has problems with some types of paper (for instance HP trifold matte paper gave it problems at times). Expect more paper jams with this one.-Can print roll paper for panoramic-Since it is pigment, less variation in finishes as ink sits on top of the paper.-Must be turned on and nozzle check pattern printed 1x/wk to prevent clogging. Has a reputation for clogging more than CANON, which may be due to smaller nozzle size.OVERALL, I felt if you want the best printer for all situations, having both a PRO-10 for black & white and very important photos, and a PRO-100 for highly saturated prints like posters is the best combination. I was not impressed with the Epson R2000 as a package despite its quality prints (similar to PRO-10 in quality).If you can only pick one, look at the PROs and CONs and pick which is best! :)

By "high volume" the 5000L's specifications says it is capable of laminating 33 pouches in 10 minutes. I don't usually take the time to write a review, but this has probably been the worst product I have ever purchased on Amazon.First, you should know that I spent over 2 hours on the phone with Brother support.  They were very respectful.  Only problem is, this machine is a piece of crap.  It's supposed to be a multi-function device, but the only "function" that works on this thing is the printer--so why pay more for the other, dysfunctional, functions?FAXThe first problem is this machine HAS NEVER SUCCESSFULLY SENT A FAX.  I have tried at least 30 times, and some of the faxes are practically blank.  Now, like most people these days, I have digital phone service and one of the settings is for "basic" mode so it can be used with "inferior" digital phone service.  Yet even in basic mode, it has never once successfully sent a fax.  The support people blamed it all on the digital phone line.  I was treated to a 5-minute lecture about digital voice and bandwidth, which started with the statement "we do not support [digital phone service]".  While they blamed the problems on the phone service, they could not explain why I get 5 different error messages for the same "problem."  They also could not explain why I have never before had this problem in 7 years of digital phone service.The worst part is that this machine keeps resending the failed faxes over and over, without me asking it to do so, and it then prints several stupid 1-line reports repeating that the faxes failed.  Well duh!  There was already an error message on screen and a beeping noise telling me that each fax failed--again.  Customer support tells me that these settings (atomatic repeated attempts to fax without change of settings, and wasting paper and ink on numerous/redundant 1-line error messages) are permanent and cannot be changed.SCANNINGNot only does the fax not work, but some SCAN FUNCTIONS HAVE STOPPED WORKING.  I use this machine for online banking, among other things.  My bank's website controls the scanner remotely when I deposit a check online, but the scan/deposit function has recently stopped working and I get various error messages instead.OTHERThere are also a lot of quirks about this machine that I just don't like, but which are not primary functions.  For example: I have my home-office phone running through the fax machine.  Every time I use the phone, the machine and its display click on for the duration of my call; they then shut off as soon as I hang up.  It's creepy and it feels like the machine is monitoring my calls, so I leave it turned off most of the time.  The machine also routes the phone calls somehow.  After half an hour on the phone with my first support call, the representative instructed me to turn the machine off.  When I did so, the call was dropped.  The phone works just fine if the machine is already off, but DO NOT SHUT IT OFF DURING A CALL.  If you do, your call will be dropped.And finally, this thing is just poorly designed in my opinion.*The user interface is not at all intuitive.*The machine periodically turns on by itself and seems to warm up (and use ink?) for no apparent reason and without being sent any data.*It also prints A LOT of reports.  It prints a report every time a fax fails.  It prints a report every time the network settings are changed.  Some of these reports are 1 line and say something like "network setup OK."  I find myself asking, why did it waste paper and ink for this?  My hours on the phone with customer support revealed that all of these are permanent settings and cannot be changed.*Good luck using basic driver functions.  I hate how hardware manufacturers want you to use their memory intensive junkware bundles for something as simple as printing and scanning.  Give me drivers and software that allow me to send a print job and scan when I want to, without 8 perpetual processes that slow and monitor my every click.  I'm not even sure you can scan on this thing without a mega-suite of software.Brother makes some great products.  We've had the same Brother sewing machine for like 10 years, and I have a Brother laser printer that I am very pleased with (except the aforementioned and ubiquitous software issues).  But the MFC-J425W is not a good Brother product.  Save yourself a headache and get something else.

WHY A COLOR LASER PRINTER?Like others who have turned to a Laser color printer, I was sick of expensive Canon ink jet cartridges drying up before the ink was used and non-Canon cartridges caused streaking problems on my photos.  Since I've been very happy with my HP LaserJet 1018 for every day black and white printing, I decided to try a color LaserJet for my color printing needs, most of which consists of printing photographs.  As soon as I installed the Pro 200, I tried to print some color photographs on it and I was REALLY disappointed.  The color was way darker than what I was seeing on my monitor, and looked horrible.  Totally NOT acceptable, so I went to Staples and bought some paper designed for use in a color LASER printer.  All the photo paper I had on hand was of course for ink jet printers.  The woman at Staples recommended I NOT try to use ink jet paper on a laser printer for fear of it "fusing" the image on my laser printer's drum.  So I gave away my ink jet paper and bought a box of 100 sheets of Staples 8.5 x 11 laser color photo paper for under $25.  Not the highest quality in the world, but okay for test purposes.Since the paper I bought is 8.5 x 11, and most of what I want to print are standard 6 x 4 "snapshot" sizes I've had to use Publisher to "paste" and downsize photos onto a Publisher page, and then print and cut the photos from there.  I'm sure there are easier solutions, like buying some color laser paper in 6 x 4 size, which I'll do, but the box of 100 was all Staples had in stock so for test purposes I bought it.  The image quality from using this paper is 100% improved over the old ink jet paper... WAYYYYY better!!!  The images, of course, are not "HD photo image quality" but are acceptable enough for every day use, e.g., giving "snapshots" to friends, etc.  If I want to print a quality photograph I'll send the file to an outside lab like MPIX anyway, as I did when I had the Canon ink jet printer.WIRELESS PRINTINGTonight I asked my wife to try and test the wireless installation for use with her pc.  That's how I have mine installed.  After multiple, frustrating attempts to install the printer using the provided installation disk, I was unable to get it to work hard wired.  However it works perfectly in wireless mode with no connecting USB or other kind of cable attached to my PC from the printer.  Since my wife is on the same network as my computer via our router she gave it a try and in minutes was able to print on the HP Pro 200 from her computer on the other side of our home office.  COOL!  This is our first foray into wireless printing, and it's very nice to be able to share the color printer!A MINOR "CON"One irritant is that there is no "single sheet feed" capability on this printer.  By that I mean in order to print a color photo one needs to replace or add to the plain paper in the print tray with a page of the photo paper.  That requires removing the paper tray and adding the single sheet on top, then reinserting the paper tray.  If the photo paper is a different size than the plain paper in the tray then the tray paper must be removed before "sizing" the tray properly for the new paper.  That process does work okay, but it's not as easy as having a place to feed a single sheet without having to remove the paper tray.  C'est la vie.  It's not a BIG deal... just a pain in the butt.  Overall I'm happy with the quality, performance, noise level and size of the printer, and I LOVE the wireless capability.  I'd buy this printer again.  Not sure how long the toner will last, but I don't do all that much photo printing so it should be more economical than throwing away dried up and clogged ink jet cartridges.

This desk top plug and play label printer by Dymo is just that...a little printer that only works when connected to your (Windows or Mac) computer. It takes up very little desk space, just 4 " x 2" and it connects to your computer via USB cable. It has no screen or keyboard for data entry, everything must be entered through Dymo Label Light software which pops up on your monitor when the printer is attached. There is no power adapter. You need to insert an included rechargeable lithium ion battery which charges directly from the USB cord. The one thing that is necessary is that if you use a USB hub, it must be powered (connected to an electrical outlet).This software is very basic and easy to use.There is nothing to download. You can use any font that is available on your computer, you can bold, italic and underline. You can increase or decrease the size of the font. There is one border style, nothing fancy. You can print horizontally and vertically. You can insert images stored on your computer as well as "grab" a portion of data on your screen. It makes plain, straightforward labels.A big limitation, however, is that this printer only accepts the three narrowest sizes of standard use Dymo D1 label cassettes: ", 3/8", and ". If you want to make labels suitable for addresses you will need a printer that can accommodate 1" labels. I tried printing three and four lines on a " wide label and the results required a magnifying glass to be read. You can get a maximum of two lines on a " label.The full version of the Dymo label making software (v. 8.4) is available for free download on the Dymo web site. If you want more robust features, such as the ability to print bar codes, download information from data files such as Microsoft Excel, Access, and text files as well as Universal Data Links, insert auto-updated date and time stamping, or an automatic counter, or various shapes, downloading this software is recommended.This plug and play label printer is recommended if you know you will never need labels wider than ", if you only use labels for standard indoor tasks such as for files, and if you think you will never need to make labels without your computer being present. Considering the limitations, this label printer seems to be extremely expensive for what it offers.I own two other label printers:TheBrother Desktop Office Labeler with AC Adapter (PT2030AD)label maker which offers many nice, easy to use features and sells for about $30-$50 with an AC adapter. The down side is that this P-Touch has a poor quality, difficult to read screen, only accepts labels up to " wide and cannot connect to a computer. It does take regular batteries, works with an AC electric cord, and is relatively light weight and easy to carry around. It makes perfectly decent labels. It seems that Brother offers a wider variety of label types, sizes, colors and formats than Dymo.TheDYMO LabelManager LM 500TS Touch Screen Label Maker (1790417)is a top of the line,expensive, desktop label maker which has a large color touch screen, a full QWERTY keyboard, can either be used as a stand alone label maker or connect to a computer with Dymo Label software v.8, and it takes the full variety of D1 labels up to 1" wide. Although expensive, this printer does everything and is very easy to use.
