This portable label maker from Epson is the most flexible I've ever seen. It will print wirelessly via Bluetooth from an Apple phone or from an Android phone. It will print via a USB cable from a PC or a Mac. NOTE: It does not work with Windows phones as yet nor will it print wirelessly from computers even if they are Bluetooth equipped. It can be used with the included power cord or using 6 AA batteries. It uses a variety of Label Works cartridges that come in widths up to 1" and in materials like iron on fabric tape or ribbon as well as loads of different adhesive labels.So to get started, you will need to download the free Epson iLabel app to your phone or install the free Label Editor software available on the Epson website on your laptop or desktop. There is a fairly good printed manual included in the package and there are additional guides available on Epson's website along with an FAQ section. The full user's manual is available for download on the Epson website and I definitely recommend that you get it because it's very detailed and well written.The label printer recognizes what size and type of cartridge is currently installed in the printer so you can start designing your label immediately. There are a huge number of fonts in various sizes to choose from along with decorative frames and clip art to add to your label. You can select the text justification also. The iLabel app doesn't offer as many customization tools as the Label Editor software so I recommend installing both to get the most out of this device.One of the coolest features is the ability to create QR code labels which others can scan with their smartphones to see a huge amount of embedded information. The video by Epson which demonstrates this is a little misleading, though. You must understand what QR codes are and how they work. You must supply a link to the information or photo you wish to embed in the code to generate a QR code. This means that if you wish to take a picture of the contents of a box and generate a QR code label for that, as demonstrated in the video, you will need to first take the picture and upload it to an image hosting site. However, it does work very, very well and is extremely useful.The ribbon cartridges are delightful. It is regular ribbon that is used for wrapping packages or making bows that you can personalize by printing names or dates or phrases or artwork on. I printed some with Happy Birthday on the ribbon to tie around party favor bags and it looked fantastic!There are day-glo colored label tapes and glow-in-the-dark label tapes as well as a wide assortment of colors and widths. This allows for so many different business applications as well as lots of flexibility for home use.I have an iPhone so I was printing a label within 5 minutes of unboxing.Be aware that the Bluetooth connection with this printer can be quirky and when it gets unpaired, it can take some time to get your phone and the printer paired again. I've noticed this with a few of my other Bluetooth devices, but not all of them. I'm hoping that a future firmware upgrade will prevent this un-pairing from happening as frequently and will make it easier and quicker to re-pair.I also hope that a Windows phone app will be available in the future because it was frustrating to one of my household members that there is no app for his Nokia Windows phone.The cartridges are relatively expensive, IMO, but they are for most label printers now.Still, I LOVE this label printer and definitely recommend it if you need to make labels on a regular basis.

All offices and many homes can make good use of an easy-to-handle paper punch. As kids, we always had a single hole-puncher like those used (in the "Old" days) by ticket takers/punchers to show that a ticket had been used by punching a single hole in it. The first time I saw a Three-Hole-Punch, I was actually impressed with the technology!Today, of course, they are ubiquitous. This particular hole puncher has several things to recommend it. It's total length is only 10 1/2 inches, thereby reducing the space it takes up. It cuts holes cleanly in stacks I tried of up to 20 pages. The press-down bar locks when not in use, further reducing the not-in-use space it takes up. It feels solid and I expect it will do the job for quite a long time. I like what it does.It's shortcomings are twofold. Firstly, the three punches are not adjustable. It works nicely for punching a standard 3-hole configuration but is of no use for anything else. Secondly, the process of emptying the punched circles involves opening a hinged plastic door at the rear of the device that reminds me of the plastic door covers on cell-phone and camera ports. Itr is intended to be easy and convenient but is really neither. Turning the puncher upside down and shaking it to empty the punched holes is both awkward and a tad frustrating as all of the punches never seem to want to be shaken out!All-in-all, I liked it, plan to use it regularly and think it is a good value. The four star rating reflects the limitations in functional design described above.

Just like prior models, these newer ones are indeed black and embossed with the maker's name and trade name in gold as before, but the "USA" is conspicuously missing; they now come out of Mexico. Look out for the word "matte" in the product description, as they no longer have that shiny, hard varnish finish and feel -- it is indeed matte. Every few pencils comes one with a little paint missing up where the eraser begins; I have never known this to happen with prior generations of Black Warriors.Now I have lost my reference standard for the best made-in-USA mass-manufactured writing pencil, though my new south-of-the-border jobs sharpen well and are comfortingly black-leaded without excessive softness; they erase well because of that. PaperMate (owned by Sanford Brands and part of Newell Rubbermaid) is keeping the price low -- but at what cost? My old ones were practically impossible to use up with their hard leads and fine-milled wood. The new ones are probably okay (time will tell if they're outstanding) and hopefully better than the orangey hexagonal kind that can be had at chain office stores for a dime a dozen during school-supply season. If you know of a (somewhat) reasonably priced American-made writing pencil that excels (not a mechnical model or a French art pencil), please put a "Comment" below. Meanwhile, you get what you pay for. Thank you!

Before ordering this Fax machine I did a bit of research, well actually a lot because it wasn't so easy to look up the information I needed on the internet or in Amazon reviews.First question I asked myself was, could I use a Fax with my current AT&T; U-verse Voice? Secondly, could I continue to use my phone with an answer machine and two cordless phones without having to use the phone built into the Fax machine? I only wanted a Fax for personal use and; use occasionally, receive and send a maximum of ten pages, no color necessary, speed of sending and receiving not important, cost and efficiency were a must and I would want to use the same phone number for both fax and voice. There was way too many Fax machines to choose from and the prices went from low to very high.  No where could I find instructions on the internet as to whether or not I could use a Fax with my AT&T; U-Verse Voice.Through Amazon reviews, internet tech sites, brand names such as HP, Brother's and so on I searched and still couldn't get any answers. After a great deal of wasted time I finally gave up and called AT&T; U-Verse Voice tech support. The tech assured me I could use a fax with U-Verse Voice. It was very simple, I would plug my extension phone to the fax and use the plug from the extension phone to plug into the fax which was already plugged into my U-Verse Gateway allowing both my phone and fax to operate off VOIP but both phone and fax could not be used simultaneously, that is you can't talk on the phone while receiving or sending a fax.After reading Amazon reviews and internet reviews for the best fax for me, it turned out to be this one, Brother FAX-575. Just to be on the safe side before buying it, I read the manual on-line from page to page and it appeared this would have every thing I needed.Amazon shipped quickly and the installation began. Getting my external phone and fax connected was simple. Putting the fax together from the box was simple. As for programming the Fax, now that got a bit complicated but it appears I got it right. All phones have a dial tone. Brother allows you to send a test fax, registration, to them and they will send one back to you. Sending my two page fax was slow but easy. When Brother sent a Fax to me the fax caught the special fax tone just as my answer machine began. It cut the answer machine off about half way through and began printing the fax. The print was sharp, better than the ones I've seen at work.So far I can say this is the perfect Fax for me. There is still a few things I need to learn but so far so good. If you have AT&T; U-verse Voice, you can call their tech support if you want. Be sure to follow the instructions very carefully. You can use the manual they send you or use the one online which you can download and save.  Would I recommend this for AT&T; U-Verse Voice? ABSOLUTELY! If things change I will come back and update this comment but hopefully that won't have to be done.

Epson is a very greedy company. These are the exact words they say about their ink cartridges for the XP-600 printer, and presumably all of their printers:  "All ink colors are used for printing and all-in-one maintenance, and all colours have to be installed for printing. For print quality, part of the ink from the included cartridges is used for printer startup and a variable amount of ink remains in the cartridges after the "replace cartridge" signal".Really, we are all being fleeced by this company. You can fax, scan, print and more with this all in one device. As someone who works from home I have multiple printers and though they work well, each is lacking some feature or another. I own the XP-310 Epson printer, not this model. The Quartet 4-Month Dry-Erase Planner Board is a smart choice if your aim is to look at your home, work, or school schedule quarterly. I am currently using my board to set up our Spring and Summer homeschool activities, outings, books to be read, and more.  This board in my opinion  is one of the best ways to set up your schedule in advance. The white board surface allows for the ease of moving things around with simple erasing and re-writing. The fact that all plans can be seen in one place  is enough to keep me motivated and not over-scheduled!The board itself, has four blank calendar areas in which you can order in whatever way you please. There's a bullet type tip black ink dry erase marker included with and a place for it to clip into on the top of the board. The back of the board does have two plastic brackets to be used when mounting in place. The bottom back of the board has two small circles to keep the board level when it has been hung. The first laminator I received did not work at all.  I tried putting a laminating pouch or the cleaning sheet through it and it went about 2" and hit a wall and wouldn't go any further.  I even tried it on the different settings.  I tried looking inside to see if there was something that was stopping the pouch from going in, but couldn't see anything.  Also, when I first turned this one on to heat I saw steam and a little smoke coming out of each side; I wondered if that was because it was the first time trying it.  I then went to the Black & Decker web site and sent a message on their site.  The first message I did not receive a reply back from, so I wrote back and a very nice friendly helpful person replied and apologized.  This lady had me email her the receipt for the laminator and she emailed a form for me to fill out to receive a new one.  I have to admit after reading some of the reviews on the laminator I did not think I would actually receive another one, but alas UPS showed up to pick up the one that did not work and that same day I received a new one via FedEx.  The lady at Black & Decker even asked me to let her know if I had any issues with the new laminator, since this was a new product for them.I have put this new laminator through the ringer; lol.  After reading reviews that people had pouches stick and were not able to reverse them I wanted to really put this new one to the test.  It worked perfectly right out of the box and I have run 150+ pouches through it without one sticking or any problems at all.  And no, this new one did not steam and have smoke coming out of it the first time I used it.  It comes with a few test pouches; one 5ml and two 3ml, but no cold pouches.  Personally I think they should have supplied a few more hot pouches and some cold pouches (basically a sticky pouch that is run through the machine and is sealed). I have many crochet and knitting patterns that I use frequently that I have laminated using this machine, both the 5ml and 3ml.  The pouches have come out perfect every time and don't curl up on the ends like pouches do with another laminator I have.  If I had received this one to begin with I'd wonder why so many people have had problems with the machine.  It looks to me that quality control is not too good.If I have problems in the future I will edit this review. Right now I would give this new laminator 4 stars; the first one zero stars if possible. If anyone would like to know whom I contacted at Black & Decker, please leave a comment and I will get back to you with the info.  :-)

Photography is my hobby.  I own a Minolta X-700 MPS SLR film camera with multiple lenses, color filters, electronic flash, tripod, and a host of photography gadgets.  I also own a couple of point-and-shoot digital cameras.  I am seriously considering replacing my film camera with a Canon EOS 60D DSLR camera.  The greatest advantage of digital cameras is that the photographer can see the images immediately on the computer without waiting for the film to be developed.  But for a professional quality print, he still has to take the digital file to a commercial establishment - unless he owns a professional inkjet printer like this Canon PIXMA PRO-1.  It is a great complement to a DSLR camera for a digital photography professional or a hobbyist like me.  It gives the photographer total control on the finished product, no longer at the mercy of some disinterested technician at a photo print shop.With the right kind of print paper, the quality of the prints is excellent, comparable to that of prints made from film.  The color prints are brilliant but what is amazing is the quality of black and white prints.  They embody the subtle variations of shades I used to see in Ansel Adams' photography books.  I didn't know that an inkjet printer could do that until now.  This is possible because the PRO-1 has five black ink tanks of various gradations plus a chroma (gloss) optimizer.  There are twelve ink tanks in total.  They conveniently pop into their slots at the front of the printer behind two panels on the two sides of the receiver paper tray.  The printer accepts paper sizes ranging from 4X6 to 13X19 inches.  The paper loader is at the back of the printer which can hold up to 150 sheets.  A single-sheet manual feeder and a special CD/DVD print tray for printing directly on printable CDs and DVDs also come with the purchase.  My PRO-1 took slightly over 2 minutes to print a 4X6 image and under 4 minutes for an 8X10.  I connected my PRO-1 via a USB cable.  It can also be connected via Ethernet.  I don't have a home network so I leave it to other reviewers.Here is the bad news:Cost - At one thousand dollars a pop, the PRO-1 is major investment.  It is more expensive than a Canon EOS camera.  But that is only the beginning; there is the cost of ink to be considered.  It is a well-known secret that printer manufacturers sell their printers at cost or even at a loss, but they make a ton of money selling ink for them.  At the initial start-up, the PRO-1 consumed  of the ink reserve to "prime" the printer.  Within a few days, the levels of the twelve ink tanks were down to 50%.  During this time, I had been experimenting with printing pictures of various sizes, the largest of which was 13" X 19".  A full set of twelve PGI-29 ink tanks costs about $432 plus tax & shipping at the Canon website.  That is not chump change.  To keep the printer heads moist, I routinely print a test page at all my printers weekly.  I plan to do the same with the PRO-1.  I think it is a smart move considering the amount of ink used for  "priming" if the printer head dries up.  Then there is the cost of printing paper.  Good quality paper is essential for quality prints.  A 13X19 metallic paper can cost more than $2 each.  In short, it takes money to make quality prints.Physical set up - The picture on the Amazon webpage doesn't do the PRO-1 justice.  This thing is big, measuring approximately 18"X27-1/2"X9-1/2".  It takes up the entire 19-3/4"X29-3/4" top of my printer table.  It is the biggest piece of equipment in my computer room.  Since it is back loading, it requires a few inches of clearance from the wall for loading the paper.  It is also heavy, over 60 pounds.  It is best to have an extra pair of helping hands during physical setup, although I had been able to lift it to the printer table all by myself.  A petit lady may have problem doing that.In conclusion, this printer is far too expensive to buy and operate and takes up too much room for everyday use.  It is more appropriate as a picture printer for a professional digital photographer or a serious hobbyist.

Pros:Easy to useGreat results with film, 6x7, 645, and 135 (35mm)Cons:Software is a bit clunkyDigital ICE can do bizarre thingsLargest Improvements Over V500:Can now scan four 645 or three 6x7 negatives at a time (spec is 6x22cm).Bottom Line:Great deal for a flatbed scanner that is designed primarily for film and graphic arts use.  I don't think I would upgrade from the V500 unless you scan a lot of medium format film, and even then it might be worth checking to see if the new medium format insert would work in the V500 (I don't know if it would or not).  The software is the same as the V500.One of the large bottlenecks of the V500 is that it will only scan two 645 negatives at a time.  Since I usually cut in strips of 3, this is a problem.  It means I had to scan each strip twice, once to get two of the images, and a second time to get the third.  This means I had to 10 scans to get through a roll of 15 images.  The V600 allows me to do this in 5 scans instead of 10.  This is a nice time savings.Sometimes the Digital ICE produces some bizarre artifacts, like halos around sharp edges and in shadows.  It also at least doubles or triples the scan time.  The somewhat random nature of the results and slow scan times makes me avoid Digital ICE entirely.  The dust reduction does help, but do plan on spending 5 or 10 minutes in Lightroom removing dust spots from critical images.  Dusting your negatives and keeping them clean will help a lot.  Keep an antistatic brush and cotton gloves handy when scanning negatives.This is a great scanner for film shooters, and will quickly pay for itself over just 10 or 20 rolls of film.  Expect to get results comparable to a decent DSLR camera, if I had to wager a guess a 135 (35mm) negative might be comparable to a 6 MP SLR where the medium format might be more like a 12 MP equivalent, but these comparisons are dangerous and don't really mean a whole lot and I haven't done resolution testing.  This scanner is ideal for a hobbyist medium format film shooter that doesn't want to pay a fortune for scans, or someone looking to restore a few dozen rolls of film or slides.  Expect to spend 1 or 2 hours per roll processing though.

I recently purchased these Canon compatible cartridges for my new Canon ix6520 printer.  This was the second time I had purchased any kind of compatible ink cartridges.In my particular case, the print quality seems the same as with the original Canon cartridges.  I didn't have any problems with leakage or other defects in the cartridge.However, I do have a problem:  The chips on the the cartridges don't work.  The chips were reporting full ink levels after the ink levels had gone down substantially.  You can visually check the ink levels in these cartridges because the cartridges are transparent.After a certain amount of use, the chips started to report lower ink levels, but the levels were very inaccurate.  In fact, some cartridges were completely empty while the chips reported that the ink levels were at 1/2 - 1/3 full.I don't know yet what's going to be done about this.  The vendor contacted me right after my purchase, asking me to do a review for them.  I held off doing this review on Amazon until I had a chance to communicate with the vendor several times and thoroughly test the ink cartridges.  I told the vendor that if and when the cartridges worked perfectly (including the chips), I would be happy to give the cartridges a 5-star rating.Until then, it's 3 stars because of the chips.  Also, some of the negative reviews on this product were pretty scary.  Some people claimed that their printers were ruined by this brand of ink cartridges.Update: Thought I would add a little to my review.  I would like to add that these compatible cartridges might be basically pretty good but that they probably have a certain defect rate.  I figure that the defect rate should be measured by the total of 1 star and 2 star reviews.  I personally would not buy any product that has less than an average 4.5 stars and I almost consider a 3 star rating to be a negative.  To me, anything less than 4 stars indicates that customers are having some kind of trouble with the product.Whenever I've bought products from Amazon with ratings over 4.5 stars, the products have always been excellent.  For instance, I recently bought a Pentax K-5II camera and Metz flash for the camera through Amazon.  Both of these products were extremely highly rated and both are some of the best products that I've ever purchased anywhere.

We've been using the same little paper shredder for years - and have always just kind of 'lived with' the performance and jams.In the past couple of years, our business has grown; and, due to the number of federal documents with personal information that we handle, we do a lot of shredding. :)Anyway, when I went out to buy a new shredder, it didn't even dawn on me that I would be able to find an affordable unit with the performance of this Fellowes shredder!Here are the things we like about it:- There are definitely limits to what it can shred at one time - but it does such a great job monitoring itself that it doesn't seem possible to jam it.- The output bin is large enough to be truly useful, and is also easy to empty.  The shredded paper will kind of stack up in the middle - so we generally have to open it up and spread the paper bits around about once for every time we fill the bin up.  That's not a big deal at all considering we can fit 3 to 4 times the amount of shredded paper that our old unit held.- It is quiet.  This was definitely an unexpected & pleasant surprise.  It is definitely not silent; but, it just emits a deep hum instead of the high pitched sound our old unit had.- It looks good and is easily maneuverable thanks to the caster wheels.- I love the safety feature where it will turn off if you touch the shredder input.  I've tested it and it works great.- I know most paper shredders have a front window; but, that is also a nice feature.- The shredding is very effective and results in nice small pieces.The only downside I can even remotely think of is that the blades require occasional oiling; but, I deal with a lot of equipment and think that is pretty normal for a high-performance machine like this one.  I do wish, however, that the instructions had more info on how much oil is optimal - or how often we should oil the blades.Overall, if you're looking for a high-performance shredder that won't break the bank, then I highly recommend this unit!  It probably sounds dumb to get excited about a paper shredder - but the performance of this PowerShred has absolutely blown me away!

It always starts out well enough. A clean slate, unsullied and unspoiled.  But no matter how many times you vow "This time it will be different," it's only a matter of time before you scrawl that first phone number on the notebook divider. You think, okay, I can stop here.  One phone number and that's it. No more.  But then, one day, you open the notebook and there it is, a crooked flower pot, a scrawled column of numbers, a grocery list -- where did it come from?  You try to convince yourself it wasn't you...someone else found your notebook and wrote "Dentist, 3:45 Tues," and decorated it with smiling cartoon teeth.  Hey, let's stop living in denial.  You know who did it.  Everyone knows.  And you know it's gonna happen again and again and again.Denial got you here in the first place.  You're hooked on doodles and anybody who sees your notebook knows it.  You can see it in their eyes when you show up at a meeting.  Yeah, you have the act down pat. You take out the Cross pen thinking "This will impress them."  Maybe it does for a minute...but then you open up your notebook and there it is:  The Kool-Ade pitcher guy, or maybe Goofy pushing Mickey in a wheelbarrow.  Or are the free-range doodles your poison. Doesn't matter. It's all the same, and you know it.And you can't stop.One doodle is too many and a thousand aren't enough.  Squiggles, flowerpots, top hats, dollar signs.  You tried, sure you did, but the writing is on the wall...well, it's on the divider, but if we are gonna start quibbling over every little phrase, my coffee will get cold, so just keep it in check, huh.  Let's face it, you can't fight it.  Some people can draw that first squiggle and walk away.  Others can't.  Yeah, you know who I'm talking about. Until now, people like us had no choice but to live in the shadows...that part of the conference room where the light doesn't hit so well, shrinking away from the prying eyes of those around us, trying to hide the monkey on our back and the monkey doodle on our notebook divider.Well now things are different. Now we can stand up, crawl out of the darkness and take our place in the light once more.  Avery Plastic Durable Write-On Dividers are erasable. Yeah, you heard me.  Erasable.  So go ahead, do a sketch of your new client and add the horns and fangs.  Do a one-word critique of the boss, and do it in block letters with shading.  We're free at last. Because it's all un-do-able. That's right.  Use your pen, pencil or crayon. It's all good. Then take an eraser and VOILA! Clean slate.  You pretend to pay attention in class, at client meetings, conferences, whatever and no one will be the wiser because the evidence is all gone!Is this a great country or what?

They attach with a coiled cord.This comes with two AAA batteries, plus a cable to plug it into an electrical outlet. Most people will rely on the batteries, but the cord is there if you want to leave this plugged in for more frequent use.The small readout computer can be set to lb., lb and oz, kg or g. It weighs items up to 110 pounds. It also has Tare (to zero out the scale if a carton is placed on it first) and Hold modes.The thing I like about this scale is the fact that it separates the weighing platform from the weight readout. This means you can put a huge bulky package on it and not struggle to see the weight. Set the little computer where you want it for easy viewing and then weigh your package. Even if the package is five feet tall by four feet wide, you have your handy modes and weight readout at your fingertips.This is not a dainty, plastic lightweight. It is a very solid slightly hefty weighing platform. This can go on the desk or the floor and provide stable support. It also weighs lightweight items exactly, and after some slight calibration, which is easy to do after reading the little instruction pamphlet, extremely accurate. This is ideal for someone who not only weighs lots of smaller packages but has the occasional need to weigh a big heavy package. I think the idea to separate the weight and modes computer from the main weighing platform was brilliant. This makes it easy to see the weight at eye level while the platform can be holding a bulky package.This is high quality, and would be perfect for a small office. It comes nicely boxed and all parts are held in their individual compartments with molded foam. It takes up hardly any room for a scale that can weigh packages over 100 pounds. If you need a versatile scale I can recommend this.Pros:* Accurate, can be calibrated easily* Hold function to let you lock your weight readings* Separate weighing platform and readout makes it convenient to use* Weighs up to 110 pounds* Tare mode* Display can be wall mounted* Included AC adapter* Included AAA batteries* Solid construction, well made* Two year warrentyCons:* NoneWhile I was provided with a free sample it did not influence my recommendation.

Avery is one of the foremost names in office supplies and it is a business that can be counted on to produce items of quality. These labels are no exception. You don't need long fingernails to remove the labels. The tabs make the job easy.These labels are intended to stick on various items and they can be used on most any flat surface. With a simple pull of the tab, the labels can be removed. They retain enough of their stickiness that they can be used again, if desired. After several uses, the stickiness wears out and the labels cannot be used again. But they likely won't need to be reused more than a few times, so this shouldn't be a problem. Also, there is no need to worry about excess adhesive. With some labels, the stick is so strong that part of the label and/or adhesive is left behind when the label is removed. These labels eliminate that problem because there isn't any more adhesive than necessary. The labels stay in place, but once removed, they take all the adhesive and label with them.If there is any drawback to using these labels, it would be the limitations on certain surfaces. They stick to most anything, but because the glue is weak, they won't adhere to some surfaces for very long. One example is glass- the edges will start to become unglued in due time. They are best when attached to paper/cardboard products and they work fairly well on plastics, but they will lose their stick on other surfaces and thus should not be used if a permanent label is needed.Small labels like these are good for many common uses and Avery has, once again, come through with a simple yet quality product. I use them on children's items, desk folders, and other items that could use a descriptive label, but only in a temporary way. They are easy to apply and remove, and they make a useful addition to the general/office supplies of any home or business.

Quality Park Reveal and Seal Business Envelopes are a good envelope for general business use. These envelopes take away most of the hassle and waste when mailing letters, thanks to the self- adhesive closure and the fact that there is no pull- off strip.The main attraction of these envelopes is the way they seal. Rather than pull off a thin strip, you instead lift up a lower flap that remains attached to the envelope, revealing the adhesive underneath, and then fold the upper flap on top of it, to form a seal. This is more waste- friendly because there is no leftover strip. The common design of self- adhesive envelopes is to manufacture them with a pull- off strip that must be removed to reveal the adhesive section underneath. This works, but it means having a bunch of extra waste in the form of paper strips.I like that these envelopes don't create any additional waste and this is certainly their greatest advantage when compared to other self- adhesive envelopes. However, there are some disadvantages with this design and the main one is speed. Because you have to lift the adhesive flap completely from one end of the envelope to the other, these envelopes are not as fast to use as other self- adhesive envelopes with tear- off strips. This makes them a poor choice when you have to stuff and seal many envelopes and you have little time to spare.As for security, it is very good with this envelope. The marking on the inside of the envelope includes a checkered pattern with small lines and dots. It completely conceals anything inside the envelope. This provides some much needed peace of mind when mailing letters containing checks and other personal items. Also, I have noticed that the adhesive section cannot be lifted and resealed, which is good because it provides added security. There is no way a person can open the envelope cleanly, remove the contents, and then try to conceal their theft by resealing. The envelopes will tear if any effort is made to open them.Envelopes are not all the same, in spite of what some believe. Quality Park Reveal and Seal Business Envelopes are a very good envelope for general mailing use and rank a notch better than average.  Having to lift the adhesive flap makes this envelope impractical if you have dozens of items to mail at once and need to move quickly, but for other situations, Quality Park Reveal and Seal Business Envelopes are a good choice for your mailing needs.

I selected this printer over the Samsung ML-1430 and the Hewlett Packard LaserJet 1000. After reviewing all three online and then "live" at an office supply store, I ordered the Brother HL-1440. While the print quality may be similar for all three printers, the Brother HL-1440's build quality, easy memory upgrade path, and cheap consummables made it the clear front runner. Further distinguishing this machine is its superb handling of thicker media. It produces excellent results on cardstock, using a convenient manual feed slot on the front of the machine. Note also that the paper handling of the Brother is, in general, more robust than its Samsung and HP counterparts. The Samsung uses the top-loaded, ink-jet style paper feed system that tends to have less precise alignment. The HP uses a non-removable paper tray that is flimsy at best. The Brother, on the otherhand, uses a standard removable paper tray that is durable and handles envelopes and legal-sized paper just as easily as letter-sized. (And don't discount the handy manual feed for the single envelope.)Out of the box, USB setup of this unit on a Windows XP Home machine was a snap. The 1440 comes with a fully illustrated easy setup guide that will have you up and running in no time. All XP drivers are available on the disks that are shipping with these machines at the time of this review.One last note: Don't forget to order a USB (or parallel) cable with your printer!

I figured these might be a good addition for note taking, list keeping, keeping certain info front and center in the various notebooks I use to keep track of life, business, kiddo, etc...These are great- they stick well to notebook paper- these aren't like clings that will fall off-leaving you without your bookmark and the important info.  They stick so well I didn't think they could possibly come off without lifting paper bits and pen marks with them.But they did. They came off smoothly.I figured- it's textured plastic- I know most of my pens will crap out a few letters into the first word. But all of them wrote on it as though it was paper.  I figured- oh sure, now they will smudge.But the ink stayed true and crisp.The plastic is lightly textured (not bumpy, but not slickly smooth) and a sturdy thickness (a little stiffer than traditional overhead projector transparencies-like modern day plastic file folders)...The green of this particular model is light and fresh- noticeable but translucent enough that I can still see writing underneath it....I can see these as being extremely useful for a few purposes- obviously in notebooks and moleskines... Datebooks... For avid readers or students working on research or reports... I will be using these for my Moleskines but also in my child's workbooks from school- as these don't just pull off with the slightest movement he'll have to keep reminders front and center until he reads them (and not just push them off to the side as he has done with previous book marks)...I am thrilled with these... The size is adequate for most purposes. I think if you need that much more space you should probably just dedicate an entire page of your notebook to the topic, rather than just a tabbed marker...

We kept getting bothered by sales people this summer. And as my wife is injured it is hard on her going to the door 2 or 3 times a day.  So we decided to get one of these for the door.It has worked perfectly and it looks good. i highly recommend this sign for its simplicity of use and of message.

This mouse pad outgasses a bad chemical smell when first taken out of its packaging. I put it in an open window for about five days to air it out, and now the smell is gone.The wrist padding feels very comfortable on my wrist, and the mouse pad part works fine, too. I'm very pleased with this product and would freely recommend it to others. I only wish I hadn't just recently purchased two other mouse pads with wrist rests of an inferior brand. I would have preferred this one.

We've all used the self-sealing business sized envelopes that have that peel off strip which reveals the glue strip under the flap.  These envelopes accomplish the exact same level of convenience without leaving you with a peeled-off strip of waste paper in your hand.  In this case you simply stuff your letter into the envelope, then flip up a narrow flap which reveals the glue strip.  Simply close and seal the outer envelope flap and you are done.  Seems like a small innovation but it is very clever and I like these envelopes a lot! Highly recommended.

As I have said in other reviews of Private Reserve ink, I do love their products --the ink color is vivid and intense, and the bottle is convenient for me to use with my fountain pens.  But this particular, color, "Black Cherry" is almost exactly the same color as "Burgundy Mist" and both of them are simply two only ever-so-slightly different shades of chestnut brown.  A lovely shade of brown, to be sure, but just plain old brown.  The color chart provided at the Private Reserve website gives the impression that the colors of both of these inks are quite different, so do take care with that chart.  However, if you just want a nice brown ink, this one would do nicely.

The Bankers Box is very quick to assemble, and works just fine.  However, it is not that much quicker or higher quality than a traditional folding storage box, so I would just compare prices.  Overall, it's a quality product.Also, though not factored into the review, please note that 24" long means you have a lot more weight in the box to carry.  You may want two smaller boxes instead.
This unit has the power to do what it is rated for.  Like all shredders, it requires regular maintenance including periodic oiling of the blades.

I like these.  The numbered tabs adhere greatly to my textbook pages.  One of my instructors has assignments numbered, so these tabs complement his number system:  Tab #1 corresponds to Assignment #1, etc.  I simply stick the corresponding number of the tab to the same-numbered assignment in the textbook for quick reference.  These tabs look so much nicer and neater than the strips of post-it tape I've been using to mark book references.These are sturdy-made tabs, too.  They won't rip off or tear easily.  They are also easily removed and placed elsewhere (although, with time, the stickiness will surely wear off).  They also work well on thin paper, such as my Norton Anthology of American Literature.For pages with writing all over them, these tabs will not disguise any print, as one can read through the tab.My only complaint?  The small trial package I received didn't have enough tabs!

I purchased this printer rather than buy more cartridges for my Dell printer that jambed all the time.  Those expensive cartridges were half the cost of a new printer with cartridges and I was not stuck buying inflated cartridges from Dell

My wife is only 5 feet, so when sitting in a chair for any length of time, she needs a footrest. we searched online and found hundreds, most of which were either too high, too expensive or too ugly. She wanted something that was firm but light, looked good in the living room and was a fair price.After looking for a long time, we finally found these, which turned out to be better than we expected. They are very light but firm. The removable cover is very good looking, washable and fits in with all the furniture without being too noticeable. You can use them with the flat side down, or with it up so you can roll it around to a comfortable position. We are very pleased with these.

Ordered this for use not as a door stop, but as protection for the wall behind the trash can.  My kitchen trash can has a lid that is raised by a foot pedal.  After a few steps on the pedal, the can lid was hitting the wall.  I put 2 of these on the back of the trash can, and they have helped a lot to protect my wall.
Returned it.  The ink was not compatible with my computer. So I can't really rate this product.  I have no further comments to say.
I love these book rings.  They come in handy for so many different things.  This item would be so much better if the distributer sold a box of 100 rings in several different sizes.

Used a lot in my previous job whiteboards. Does the job, we used to replace once a month for some heavy writing. Easy to hold and wipes clean and nice. Have some water occasionally for wiping. White board was spick and span!

Although functionally it works the same, this is a nice alternative the the standard tape dispenser.  If seems a little more ergonomic and fits in the hand better. It comes in colors, which is a nice switch from the standard, clear ones we're so used to.  There is not a lot else you can say about at tape dispensor, but I'd recommend this one over the standard.

Post-it Notes Dispensers PBL-330 is a slick looking and viable pop-up note dispenser.  As indicated in the description, it (1) Increase productivity and style (2)  Keeps Post-its always within reach in a one handed heavy, great looking black dispenser, plus a non-skid pad to prevent it from sliding when pulling notes.. (3) Easy refill with Post-it Pop-up Notes.  A must for your desk - recommended.

I'm a huge fan of sticky notes and as long as they are easy to write on, stick well and come in a color other than yellow I am a fan.  These notes come in my favorite form, a brightly colored cube and they are of the same quality of a post-it note.  I find these invaluable at work where I make notes daily and like to have something in a color other than the generic yellow that my company purchases.  Overall, a good, quality product for a reasonable price.

After the ease of delivery and set-up and the much anticipated use of this "amazing" professional photo printer my husband and I were terribly disappointed. We have a $100 canon printer that prints no better than this printer. The quality was not at all what we had hoped with the price of this printer. Yes, it can print poster size and yes it can print on cds...all very cool, but the foundational point---quality of printing pictures---was absent. The prints, no matter the size, were flat and obviously printed from a home computer. I even purchased high quality printing paper.It wasn't fast, if that's important to you and it's just a giant printer in our house now we will probably rarely use. Again, the fact that it's versatile in size printing is neat, but I would be using it mainly for 4x6-8x10 printing and printing on cds.

If you just want to be able to scan stuff occasionally then look no further. This is a great little scanner that takes up little space and provides moderately paced scans (not too fast, but not too slow either). I use it with GIMP, Paint.Net and Photoshop Elements and the scanning software integrates with them perfectly. The scans are nice and crisp and it's powered via the USB cable so no extra cables or taking up socket space; and speaking of space, it's pretty slim so you can easily tuck it in behind your desk somewhere and just whip it out when needed. For the fifty something bucks this is priced at you cannot go wrong. Unless  you need any of the more advanced functions (like upright or film scanning) and just need a good, basic, color scanner--look no further.

My daughter goes through about 15-20 of these notebooks a year in High School. The last time we went to a B&M store to purchase them they were out of the College Ruled ones and only had Wide Ruled, which isn't accepted in her school. I was very happy and surprised to see that Amazon had them for less than $1, so I picked up the limit of three. They are now on the list of items I will order regularly, easy enough to add to any order I'm placing to avoid shipping them on their own and causing more wasted packaging.

The DYMO D1 labeling tape fit my Dymo Labelmanager Pnp Printer perfectly.  I like the looks of the labels and so far they stick very well in the applications I have found for them.  The tape seems a bit pricy, but not out of line with any other label maker tape.
Not too much you can say about these tabs--other than they work.  I use them to sort my cook book, and you can write things on them to make it easier to find what you're looking for.

These are great scissors and the color variety is fun.  They are blunt but still cut well after many, many uses.  The scissors open easy, but not too easy, and are not difficult at all to use.  The plastic holder, however, is extremely flimsy.  I thought at first that it was just part of the packaging, but then I realized that the flimsy plastic was actually the scissor holder.  It does, though, serve its purpose and I recommend this product.

This review is for the Expo biggest loser daily meal planner dry erase white board. I was pleased with the quality of this product overall. Make sure to use it with true erasable markers, NOT permanent markers, or you will quickly be sorry! While the product is intended for planning meals, I actually ended up using it to a greater extent for taking random notes (e.g. phone numbers, etc) while talking on the phone in my kitchen! Overall, I recommend this product from Expo.

The instructions could have been better.  Like, there could have been actual text explaining the parts rather than just a two sided piece of paper with somewhat unclear drawings.  That said, it was easy to plug the three height adjustment blocks into the stand.  I went for broke and did the maximum extension.  The extension feet are rubber so they shouldn't move around very much and they should hold the stand securely as they fit tightly into the holes designed to accept them.  I had some leftover screws but couldn't find where they were supposed to be used (nor could I see where they would be needed).The flat surface of the stand is thick enough to support the weight of my 24" widescreen monitor very easily with no sagging.  There's not much room left for other items on the stand once the monitor is housed on it but there's a good sized cubbyhole underneath for all your accessories.  It was easy to put together and I like the newer more contemporary design.  I'd previously been using a plastic drawer system (that was supposed to sit under my printer) to lift my monitor.  Now that component lives under my scanner.  It looks cleaner and the monitor height is perfect for my uses.  I'm happy!

I have a reference manual that has numerous chapters with unique headers. These tab dividers are just the ticket for finding the right chapter when I need to look up a function. The three holes in the sheets are a match for a three ring binder. The holes have a reinforcement strip which should suffice for normal usage. Having different colors for the insert holders is an added convenience. This is a useful product at a modest price.

Purchased this with some apprehension for my Brother 2240, as another generic failed the notorious "toner-empty-light-beam" test. Install was smooth and easy, up and running with success in seconds. Clean, non-powdery prints. Maybe the naysayers got bad individual products, but this cartridge is doing its job in my printer, at about half the price of the Brother OEM cartridge. That's 5-stars in my book!

These note tabs are extremely helpful and make for easy reference. They seem to be reusable, making them useful for me in my various research projects which might otherwise make me use too many.Each pack contains two sets of tabs, each with separate tabs numbered 1-10, this allows for more precise note taking and order of materials.  The only trouble I've had is getting used to using these instead of my more haphazard collection of torn slips of paper, dogeared pages, and otherwise significantly less useful tools. As I've kept them in my bag I've been surprised by how often they come in handy.

This is not at all what I thought it was going to be - in a word, something really useful. I suppose I imagined something with rings, like a binder. This "device" is useful to an extent - for example, sorting loose paperwork on your desktop, but isn’t useful if you need to carry that paperwork with you. There is nothing that will keep the paperwork from slipping out of the sorter other than the pressure of your palm. So for something you leave on your desk, it works great… for carrying around, not so much.I really do not see many applications for this so-called file sorter as there are other, better ways to sort papers. You can't even set this thing upright without the risk of things falling out and if you're going to run that risk why not just use an expanding file folder that will at least keep things where they're supposed to be, or stacks of plastic trays? I suppose it's a matter of preference, but really, I don't get it, and the three stars is me being generous.

The newer printers get, the more hungry they become for ink. What they actually do with it is beyond me- I am positive today's models have a giant jar in which they siphon ink into it in order to make the consumer purchase more and more ink.Thankfully, generic ink has become a popular commodity, if somewhat risky. Manufacturers always say ink will ruin your printer, but in this case these generic inks have not given me any issues with my printer. The 200BK inks are extremely expensive, and I print a LOT, so these two cartridges are coming in super handy. For the price of the ink, I'd rather get these two, rather than basically have to buy an entire printer again by itself.The cartridges fit in fine, the chips processes without any issues with the printer, and I have not noticed any lower print quality (I print primarily text, for those that print photos, you might have different results). For this price, it's worth the risk to try them out.

This is a great printer and it came well packaged. The touch screen is responsive and menus are well laid out. Wi-Fi setup is very easy although you do need to install the software from the CD or from Epson's site onto your computer.The automatic document feeder for the scanner works well and the quality of scanned documents is great. The printer it will automatically save the last PC you scan something to and then you can continue to scan from the printer to that PC without going to the PC which saves a lot of time. It's got multiple trays so you can load it with both photo and regular paper and are not always swapping out paper. Navigating through and choosing pictures to print from a memory card is also straightforward. Duplex printing works.There are very few negatives but the glossy surfaces of the printer do attract fingerprints. Also, there's no easy way to do duplex scanning (which is more of a nice-to-have, but would be nice to see in the future).

I recently purchased four bottles of Private Reserve Ink in the 50ML size and this is the only one that arrived in this style of bottle - oval shaped, larger and appearing to hold more than the other simple 50ML bottles.  I can't way which ink is my favorite color because they are each different and there are so many fountain pen inks available.  Although the Avacado color is not spelled as the avocado, the color is reminiscent of a ripe California avocado skin.  It is darker than a Florida avocado.  The green is bordering on a green-brown-black with a distinct kick to the tint.  The ink flows very well in each of the pens but realize that this is far from bulletproof.  Two days after using it on Rhodia paper, I licked a finger and touched the page, causing a smear that is a very pretty shade of green, more kelly like than the saturated ink on the page.  I like this ink.

I find this wrist pad to be comfortable to use, and to support mouse movement well.The design is similar to just about every other wrist pad; it has a flat area for the mouse, and a padded area to support the wrists. What sets this one apart is that the entire pad is constructed with Microban, which helps prevent bacteria from growing, and that it has a new cushion technology called "FoamFusion" that is supposed to be better.In use, I found that the cushioning is a bit firmer than other models (a good thing), and it does a good job of supporting my wrist. The mouse pad area works fine as well. I think it will be beneficial for my wrist when mousing.The pad emits a small level of chemical smell, but it is not too noticeable. I also own their keyboard wrist rest, and that one has a strong smell. The odor is coming from the non-slip bottom of the pad.Summary: Highly recommended.

These tabs are GREAT!  You can use them to stick lots of things to your walls. .  refrigerators. . . etc.  .and they don't stain and can easily be removed.Personally, I would order the 1-inch tabs, because if it's too large, and you don't want to "waste" them, then you can easily cut them to the size that you need.  But if you're hanging something larger, like a map or poster, when you need the 1-inch size, then you have it.I also think these are a very good value, especially because they are reusable.  I think you'll find that you'll be using them a lot!Scotch Reusable Tabs, 1 x 1 Inches, 18 Squares (R100)

This is a really nice scale for small business or personal use. While I don't think it should be used at a professional mailing office, it is accurate enough for general mailing. The base is heavy and mine arrived with a small crack in the plastic housing. It didn't affect the functionality of the product. The display screen plugs into the scale base but doesn't have a place to dock it to on the scale - a feature that would have been nice. The scale can be tarred (zeroed out) with something on it.My checks of weight were accurate to the ability of the scale.You can run the scale display off of AC using the power cord or batteries.I was provided a sample for evaluation and review.

No this printer doesn't have the sheer quality of the PRO-10 and the PRO-1, but it performs great for the price I paid. Colors are very vivid, especially when using the Pro Platinum paper but it's very good with the normal papers as well. I also handles card stock very well. The setup was super quick and easy and I like the WiFi capability.My only complaint with this printer at all is that is doesn't have any Linux drivers. Canon typically isn't very good about this but there are a lot of people in the world that could benefit from at least having the option. I would give this 5 stars if not for this issue.

The labels are of the high quality typical of Avery products. As the package says, they are opaque enough to cover existing labels, easy to print on with the typical format provided by UPS/USPS thorugh eBay, and adhear well. As others say, be careful to set the setting so as not to print the receipt, but otherwise a fine product. No compaints, so 5 stars.

I originally placed one in my shopping cart for my daughter.  I added another for me.  When I gave my daughter (young adult) her gift, she love it.  But then she has a fixation with office supplies : )  I love the organization and the style.  This item will fit in a book bag, or sideways in my messenger bag.  I used to carry several file folders with the "things to take care" paperwork within.  This is my new daily/weekly/monthly organizer.  I am looking for additional colors.  Place it in your cart - you will like it.

This is an average binder which a couple of nice qualities and a couple that aren't so great.The upside is that it is made of a durable plastic and PVC free. It has removable metal rings for recycling if you have recycling in your area. The stitching detail on the edges is cute.The downside is the inside. It has one flimsy inner pocket with a business card holder. Calling it a pocket is kind of stretching it. It's more of a holder. The thin plastic pocket is only attached on two sides so not really a pocket. Also an 8.5x11 sheet of paper does not fit into the pocket without sticking out the top. The paper not fitting inside the so called pocket is a big design flaw.I also think the price is high for this size binder.

Less bulky than other zipper binders.It has multiple compartments and a handle for carrying.I think this will hold up for the needs of my rising 5th grader. 2 inches should be plenty for her age/grade/assignments.It can fit in her back pack easily along with the other items she carriers to and from school daily.

I hadn't used a fountain pen since the 70's! Pilot makes awesome writing pens and this one is no exception! It writes so smoothly and just flows across the page. It was funny to see the look on my daughter's face when I showed it to her! Her generation doesn't know what a fountain pen is. I would recommend this, or any of Pilot's writing pens, if you're looking for a good, reliable writing instrument.

My wife is an Elementary School Teacher.  She absolutely loves these pens.  Great for grading papers, and for general use.  I use them at work, and also find them to preform very well and a very good price.
Where's like Iron, have two and highly recommend it for anyone that spends time at their desk. Home or Office

This is an extremely comfortable pen to hold and write with, The ink flows superbly and it just glides across the page as I write. It has a somewhat unusual look and the spongy material around the holding area may be a tad soft for some people but  I found it very easy to hold. According to the instructions, it is refillable (need to check into that) and mine has black ink. I would like another with blue ink.I would really consider this a mid to high end pen although the flimsy packaging it came in belies that rating. A very nice pen that felt very comfortable, just glides across the page as I write....Very nice!

This 7 Pocket Filer is extremely useful in many ways, including its excellent Durable quality. The 7 Pockets will hold several documents of Letter-size sheets, and they expand to hold more, which is an added bonus. I'm always searching for a good quality Pocket Filer that I can also carry to different locations, and this one fits my description.The color for me is an added feature, because I use different colored Fillers, for several projects. This Filler is useful for home, or office. The outside is Durable, and wipes clean. In addition, an accidental spill of a beverage will wipe right off, another good feature.All Pockets are Tabbed, and white, or colors of your choice can be inserted. This Filler also has a light handle, making it easy to carry, something I don't have to struggle with, when Arthritis flares up. This Pocket Filer will fit nicely in a backpack, or laptop bag, another bonus feature. In simple terms, I love it, and will indeed put it to good use! I will certainly be using additional Wilson Jones 7 Pocket Filers in the near future for Business, and Personal reasons. Extremely satisfied & highly recommended!
My new printer is working wonderfully!I've made copies on color and printed things from my computer.Didn't know wireless printers worked sooo, well.

This is one of those "nice to have" but I doubt I'd get it for myself. I can easily use the back of an envelope.What puts this above "envelope lists" is that it is right there on the fridge. I don't have to hunt the envelope down or worry that I accidentally threw it in the recycling bin.

Overall, this chair feels like the quality is above average for chairs of this type and especially in this price range.  The materials look good and have a nice feel (leather) and the plastic parts are well finished.  Everything felt solid and there were little touches that showed a better than average attention to detail.  Seams were all good and there were no blemishes of any kind (in itself fairly rare in this price range).  Once assembled, the chair looks nice and is comfortable, but this is not your lean back and relax type of "Executive" chair, this is more of a working, task chair.  Perfect for working at a desk.  You sit up straight and are well supported.  The adjustments work well and use a fairly typical mechanism.I will be using this for working at a computer desk and it seems fine for that.  I have a larger "executive chair that's more of the "relax and read a book" type that I will retire and use for other purposes.  It has hard plastic arms and the padded arms of this new chair are much more comfortable.  The seat is very firm, but that is fine with me.  The back will not support your head (my other chair does), but that's OK for working at a desk where I will sit upright and active.I was able to assemble this by myself with no help, but it would be a bit easier if you had someone to assist.  But I got it done in 1/2 hour and I work slowly.  The instructions were clear and I had no problems.  As others have noted, getting the back hooked up is the most difficult part, but even that is not too hard.  Would be easier with a second person, though.  But I was happy that I could get this done alone.  Some tips are follow the directions, move from bolt to bolt and back when tightening, don't just tighten one at a time.  Use the short L end of the hex wrench as the handle initially (insert the long piece into the bolt) and then switch to the long end (short piece into bolt) for final tightening.  Don't insert the bolt covers (the final step) put them and the wrench in a drawer and wait a week or too.  Then check and re-tighten the bolts one final time and put the covers in place.Pros:  Good qualityGood priceComfortableEasy to adjustNice materialsFairly easy to assembleWas well packaged and had clear instructionsCons:  None really at this priceMore of a task chair than an "executive" chairBack is not as high as most "executive" chairs (but high enough)Bottom line:  An excellent value at this priceI'm giving this chair 5 stars for quality and value.  I will see how it holds up under use and if any issues develop I will return and update my rating (as I always do).---------------------------------------------------Update 2012-07-27:  After about 2 months, no issues.

These tabs are unlike the others that require fitting into place one side at a time.  There's something definitely mundane about normal file folder tabs, like you can't imagine the 1% ever recycling them.  But you have to recycle tabs because over time the names of files change.This product is perfect for situations where the file folder name can change a few times over the life cycle of the actual file folder.  It's far easier to use this type of tab as it's easy to take on and off and looks the same each time.

As a rule I do like Wilson products and have several of their notebooks, but after a little shipping incident I might be loving them.  This one is purported to be ultra-heavy-duty and really is. Thinking about it, I must say that Wilson lived up to every claim it made for this notebook.  If UPS can totally demolish the box and the notebook survived with minimal damage the claims are valid.The ring binders pushed into the cover, which is now creased.  On the other hand, the ring binders did not break or bend at all.  This notebook does hold more sheets than most of mine and that binding held up through an obvious impact.  If I put a sheet in the front, no one would ever know the notebook had a little accident.I will be "personalizing" this notebook and it is large enough to hold sheets of photographs, the purpose I wanted it for.  With regular use the Wilson should hold up.  I'd stay away from trying to cram it in a backpack with lots of books because the uneven weight distribution might not help the spine.  If used as intended, this Wilson should last for a long, long time.FEATURES:►  Customizable cover and spine simplify binder labeling and personalization►  2 inch D-ring binder holds 550 sheets►  Features our strongest binder covers and extra durable hinge for years of reliable use►  Custom formulated, PVC Free polypro material lasts up to 10x longer than vinyl►  Never-gap rings close tightly to keep papers secureWILSON JONES:Wilson Jones WorkStyle Erasable-Tab Index DividersWilson Jones Cut and Sewn Binder, Round RingsWilson Jones WorkStyle Cut and Sewn Round Ring BinderWilson Jones Minute Book, Bound, Locking SpineWilson Jones Ring Ledger Sheets, 5 x 8.5 InchesWilson Jones 362 Basic Round Ring View BinderWilson Jones ColumnWrite Columnar PadWilson Jones 812 Telephone Address Book, Round RingWilson Jones Ring Ledger Binder, 1 Inch Capacity, 5.5 x 8.5 Inch Size, Blue

This is a pretty sturdy device. The assembly seemed pretty straight forward, but no matter what I tried, I couldn't get the end pieces on. I could assemble the "wheels" as instructed, but then the end pieces would not go on. I could put the end pieces onto the "wheels" first, but then they would slide onto the body piece. There was no support line listed, so I used the rocker without it, and found it rather enjoyable to have something to do with my feet. It also helped with my posture. I just wish it assembled properly. I am thinking maybe the ends or the feet are just defected in some way. My bad luck I guess, and I assure everyone, I followed the directions exactly.

I used this to mount a couple rear view mirrors to my computer monitors at work (so that people don't sneak up on me since my back is to the aisle) and FINALLY I found a product that keeps them attached. I've tried several different products that don't seem to last long, but this one appears that it is tough enough to last.
2 x 3 feet is the perfect siZe for my office wall.  Not too heavy and easy to put up.  Price is good, too!

This folder is great!  The colors are bright and vibrant.  The metal rings and the cardboard material seem of good quality.  My job requires me to be on call, so I am using this to hold the paperwork required for emergencies.  I feel like this folder will hold up well being transferred back and forth from car to on call locations.

I picked this up on a lightning deal for a steal.  Cheaper than the cheaper unit I had that this replaced.I could tell upon opening the box that this was definitely a different class than the normal home level units I've had in the past when I lifted the top out of the box and felt the weight.Another bonus for me - the wheels on the bottom are NOT permanently mounted - they come packaged separately so you can use them or not, your choice.Box is about the same size as most home units so there's no more capacity than I had previously, but there's a whole world of difference in the operation.  My last unit was supposedly good for 6 sheets, but if I actually did that, you could hear it chugging, and it would overheat and shut down a LOT quicker to protect itself from damage, so I generally did three at the most.  I don't have enough to shred to see if this one can do extended at 12 sheets any longer than the other could do extended with six sheets, but I would imagine it's not going to go that much better pushing it at its limit.  I may still get twice as much done, but I'd rather do six to eight sheets and be able to run through whatever pile is going away now.Noise isn't what I feared either.  I thought heavy duty would mean a lot more noise, but it's only a little more than what the other one did, certainly not overbearing.The black cover on the top tips back to allow you to feed the paper in, then snaps shut, closing that off.  Credit cards go in the middle where the paper woud normally be, CD goes in a separate slot on the front.  Both worked just fine.For the lightning deal I got it for, this was a no brainer.  But even at the normal price, it would've been worth the cost.

We do a lot of printing in my house – PowerPoint slides and papers for my classes; reports, checks, and various paperwork my mom prints for her church (where she is treasurer); and now my friend and I are trying to start a business.  My family and I have had great luck with previous Epson printers, so I was excited to try out another one.Set up was easy – plug in the power cord and go through the setup menu.  The printer comes with a disc for your Windows computer, though, for my netbook, I downloaded and installed the combo pack from Epson’s website as it was easier than connecting my USB DVD drive.  Having set up Epson printers for my friends and family (I am their free tech support), I was familiar with the basic installation procedure and Epson’s website.  If you have other Epson printers in your home or business you will still have to install the included (or downloaded) software in order to use the features of the printer.Printing is fast and quiet, even when compared to my Epson WorkForce 845, which seemed so fast before I received this one.  Colors are very vibrant and the print is very clear; however, I did notice some color differences between the same document printed on my 845 and the 4640.  In this particular document, a report created in MS Access Database, the blue title bar is a bit different in shade – the one from the 845 looks a bit purple when comparing and better matches the way the report looks on my screen.  The document also had light grey banded rows (every other row), and while the bands were very light when printed on my 845, the bands are barely visible at all when printed from the 4640.  The text is not as dark either – more of a dark grey than black.  Nevertheless, these are likely side effects of the fast and quiet printing, likely save ink, and are not really noticeable unless you are looking at documents side-by-side.  On the other hand, the 4640 prints pictures rather quickly and they look wonderful.Scanning, however, seems to take longer than my 845, though not by much.  The Epson Scan utility for the 4640 has the option to add another page when done scanning, which I thought was extremely convenient.  The scan program offers an “Office Mode” for basic scanning, and a “Professional Mode” with more advanced options.  Documents can be scanned using the ADF, which can scan two-sided documents, or using the scan bed.  Items scanned can be saved as bitmap, JPEG, TIFF, Multi-TIFF, or PDF files.The only complaint I have about the 4640 is that it does not give the option to scan wirelessly FROM the printer – you must initiate the scan from the computer.  This is something I love about my 845 and is quite useful.  However, for me, the ability to scan and add more pages to a PDF file makes up for the loss of that option.  (Plus, as a business printer, it would be very complicated if it was located in an area with more than a few computers.)  So far, I love this printer and recommend it if you need to print a lot.

This review is for the LAM95 model of Black & Decker Flash Thermal Laminator 9.5-InchThe product came with Black & Decker's Timeshield Thermal Laminating Pouch Starter Kit which contained one sample pouch each for the following document types: business card, luggage tag, 4" x 6" photo, 3 Mil Letter Size (there were actually two included), and 5 Mil Letter Size.  Additionally, there was also a looped band for use with the luggage tag, and a cleaning sheet that Black and Decker recommends feeding through the laminator before shutting the machine down to remove any adhesive residue that may bleed out onto the rollers during laminating.The included user manual provides operating instructions for three different models (LAM95, LAM95FH, LAM125FH) so be sure to refer to the appropriate sections for LAM95.  The manual also provides general tips on when to use the cold versus the hot laminating modes (e.g., use self-adhesive laminating pouches and the cold mode setting with heat senstive documents such as tickets, 3 mil pouches when laminating standard printer paper or similarly thin documents, and 5 mil pouches for thicker items like photos).  The instructions and tips were somewhat terse, but I found them to be sufficiently clear and helpful enough.Using the laminating pouches from the starter kit, I was able to laminate small and bigger-sized photos without a problem.  I've since been using the machine for laminating various letter-sized documents, and have yet to encounter a problem, not even jamming.  Unlike other machines, this laminator has a jam release mechanism to help clear jamming problems.The integrated corner punch allows you to ever so lightly soften the sharp-edged corners of your laminated items into slightly more rounded corners.  It doesn't work with the included pouches from the starter kits because those already have rounded corners. The punch does work with the product I got, however.  I simply inserted an index card with sharp-edged corners, and after pressing down the punch button, I can see each sharp-edged corner turn into a more rounded one.  When I opened the small drawer at the rear of the laminator for collecting the separated punch chips, I could see the tiny fragments cut off from the index card.Overall, I think this is an excellent laminator.  It heats up and laminates fast, has three laminating mode settings (cold, 3 mil, 5 mil), a jam release mechanism, an integrated corner punch, and the box it came in can be used as a carrying case.  It has been smooth sailing for me so far, so I don't really have any critical thing to say against it yet.

It is great for the kid's homework where regular document printing is all they need most of the time. It is great at printing email or any other reference where color is not much of a requirement. It is great at printing statements or documents from your financial institution and keeping it is as a back-up hard file. A great printer to supplement your regular color inkjet or laser printers where it meets your less demanding printing needs.

I've had a lot of shredders over the years and I have nothing but good things to say about this one by AmazonBasics.  It has a feature that my more expensive confetti-cut shredder does not, namely the temperature indicator. This unit has a 10-12 minute continuous run time before it gets too hot and shuts off, at which time you have to wait for it to cool down. I shredded an entire bin full by moving the slider switch to the "ready" position instead and taking my time. In this mode, the shredder stops between jobs and then continues when it senses paper at the slot.  At the end of shredding a whole bin full this way, the shredder was not even warm, even though I did this in one sitting.A few observations: The cutting unit on the top is not detachable from the base, which can make cleaning and un-jamming a little awkward.  The pull-out bin comes completely away for emptying, but there are a few rough edges on the inside of the bin where bits of paper can get caught when you tip it upside down.  The unit stands about 22-inches tall with the casters attached.  There is only one slot which takes paper, CDs, and credit cards... although the manual makes note of inserting the latter (CDs and credit cards) on the right side of the slot.Something I always shred is junk mail, but I loathe the time consuming and tedious task of first needing to remove forms from their envelopes and/or tearing off bits of the address labels.  I was impressed with the power of the motor to shred junk mail without removing it from its envelope.  This shredder just powered through envelopes and contents like it was nothing--that's the 17-sheet capacity I guess.  Very impressive, and now the shredder I will use for all junk mail.Overall, I found this to be a very powerful, capable, cross-cut shredder for mild everyday use. I thoroughly recommended it.
My pictures come out drugstore quality with no hassle. Having pre-cut 4x6 paper is fantastic for those rare occasions when we want to share prints.

I really wanted to like this product, as I have cut myself, sometimes fairly seriously, on a number of occasions using a utility knife to open both boxes and blister packs.  This product seemed to be the ideal solution to the problem, however, I was sorely disappointed with the end results.The concept is fairly simple and seems to be a good idea. Make a lightweight plastic handle with a blade that is sharp enough to open blister packs, while not so sharp as to cut yourself seriously if it slips. In addition, the blade is recessed so that only a small portion extends beyond the plastic so any cut is likely to be shallow.In reality, I discovered that it worked well on the first blister pack, was slightly less effective on the second, and by the third the blade was so dull that I needed all my strength to pull it through the plastic. It did continue to work well for opening the tape on boxes, but it needed a new blade after three blister packs to continue to use it for that purpose. That would get expensive in a big hurry!I will continue to stick to the tried and true methods I have developed for opening plastic blister packs, and will not bother to use this product in the future.

Just what I was looking for and not finding in the office products section of a store.  It's really an ingenious invention and somebody should be complimented.First of all, they're pretty.
