They are thin (not like the thickness of post-its) and of an unobtrusive, but very handy, size (1" x 3").It seems to me that if one keeps a pad near one's computer, and another in one's home or work office space, it's something one would be reaching for all the time.  I'm home-based, so I plan to keep them handily around for quick usage.How this product specifically quickly fulfilled a need of mine (and I found myself using it almost upon receiving it in the mail) is as follows:  I like to read a lot, and when doing so I like to put markers on the pages I want to reread at my leisure.  And with cookbooks, I like to mark the recipes I want to try making later on.  Up to now, I tried using a small-size post-it, but that didn't work because the stickiness left some of itself on the page when removed.  Or, turned the other way around, the sticky part didn't want to release itself from my objecting hand.  Then I experimented, folding the post-it in thirds (hiding the sticky side).  This worked, but it was somewhat bulky and would easily fall out of the book.  Bookmarks themselves are fine if only one is needed, but for many pages, one needs an endless supply and they are just too bulky and obtrusive for that particular use.  And if one just folds down the corner of the page in frustration, one pays the price there in days to come.  The book is permanently marred.  So happy days are here!There are an awful lot of labels on a tiny pad, they peel off extremely easily (be careful you don't inadvertently peel off two at one time), you can write on them if you so choose, and insert them on an object with the nonstick tab label facing any way you wish.  It stays in place very well, and when you want to take it off, it comes off effortlessly, leaving not a trace that it has been applied to something else.This product is going to be a permanent staple of my office product collection.  Thanks to Avery for coming up with it!

The Kodak i2400 scanner is at a strange price and performance point for a scanner of its capabilities, which are admittedly quite powerful.  It's a 40 ppm duplex scanner in 200 dpi mode with a 50 page feeder; this will serve well enough for most users, and is a noticeable upgrade from something like theFujitsu ScanSnap ix500).  However, if you're a small office user with multiple users, you're either better off with the cheaper and wifi enabled Scansnap or spending quite a bit more on the higher end and monster-fast (70 ppm!)Kodak i2800 Scanner.  4 stars.Comparatively, the i2400 is about as quick a scanner as you're going to find for a single user.  The 40 ppm rating does slow down a bit at higher resolutions, and it does also slow down a bit scanning to PDF files rather than images.  That said, the single touch scan (once you've preset your profile) is quite simple and I've not encountered a jam yet.The enclosed software is good but bit disappointing as it's slightly outdated; Paperport 12.1 and Omnipage 17.1 are decent programs - although Omnipage isn't anywhere close to Abbyy Finereader - but are two and one generations behind their current releases, respectively.  A TWAIN driver does make up for a lot of this, as the i2400 can be recognized by just about anything, unlike the ix500.The only real quibble with this is that it's not really designed for multiple users with a single USB connection.  As such, you're probably better off saving $200 and going with the slightly slower ix500 (although at higher resolutions, they're basically identical) with a Wifi enabled connection, or spending up and getting something that is truly workgroup ready.  4 stars.

Set-up/Install:This non-wireless scan-to-cloud-able EPSON scanner was easy to set up – just a power cord and a USB to connect to a laptop.  Just don’t miss the orange tape in the output tray.  There are quite a few pieces of tape that need to be removed from this well-secured machine.  But it was hideously time-consuming to install and update.  Using Windows 8, the installation CD (Apple users take note – you will need a DVD device for this) took 15 minutes.  Next, the EPSON site identified 6 updates; these took an additional hour, requiring both a restart and a change to my computer’s firewall settings.  Granted, my results might have been due to the state of my computer, provider, and the possibility that not all updates were vitally necessary.What You Do NOT Get:As factory-sent, the EPSON WorkForce DS-510  is not networkable.  But the user’s manual states an optional Network Interface Unit is available.  If you want to scan photos, you will need the recommended optional carrier sheet to protect important originals.  The last scanner I purchased provided this gratis.What You DO Get:3 different scan options:  Direct via scanner button (program behind it is re-assignable), icon/GUI via Epson Scan, icon/GUI via Document Capture Pro (allows more settings such as rotation, skew correction, resolution).2 non-EPSON programs:  ABBYY FineReader (OCR that creates editable and searchable formats) and NewSoft Presto! BizCard (a contact management program that makes business card images editable and searchable).3 Special Project Capabilities:  Image Stitching or Double-Sided Capability (creating one sheet from 2 originals),  Scanning to Cloud via Document Capture (supports these destinations:  Web Folder, Evernote, Google Docs, SugarSynch, and SharePoint), and for Windows users only there is the ability to manage jobs/files using blank pages or barcodes (up to 30 scan-jobs).Ability to scan wide size range of originals:  Business cards and small receipts can be scanned.  Basically, this unit supports originals from 2.1x2.9 inches up to 8.5x36 inches.Telephone Support:  For US and Canadian users, EPSON Connection offers a telephone number as a first-line of contact for diagnostic service.Limited Warranty:  Users who have purchased and use the unit in the US, Canada, or Puerto Rico may have a replacement unit shipped to them postage paid.  (Others pay freight.)  However, some folks may not like that their replacement could be a used refurbished unit.Last Words:Despite an auspiciously lengthy installation, the EPSON WorkForce DS-510 has been working reliably for just over a month for me.  It is sturdily built, fairly well-priced given its options, and I like the ability EPSON provides to make adjustments to the scans.  Particularly nice is the phone as a first-line of contact.  But I’m a bit concerned that I’ll need to be extra vigilant about what may be a high-maintenance high-update machine.

Summary: This is a fine and capable launch pad and rocket. You will still need to purchase rocket engines (which typically include igniters), wadding, and batteries. The Estes launch pad, however, has not been significantly improved over the last three decades. Further, the easy-to-assemble rocket is almost as difficult as a normal beginner's rocket. For people who want a simple build and require a launch pad, I recommend the Estes Alpha III Launch Set.RocketI'm not a big fan of this rocket. It flies fine, but the construction, which is meant to be simple, is nearly as complicated as many of the basic beginner rockets. If you want simple, get an Estes Alpha III or Quest Viper, in which the fins are part of a single plastic assembly. If you have the patience to glue fins to a tube, get something like an Estes Little Bertha, Estes Viking, Estes Hi-Flyer, Quest Astra, or Quest Novia.Launch PadYou would be hard pressed to get a launch system for less money and hassle. However, this pad has its drawbacks; if you stay in the hobby for any length of time, you will likely end up modifying it. The launch rod comes in two pieces for easy shipping. This leaves a seam in the middle that you need to sand down to smooth out. In the end, you will probably replace the rod with a single piece purchased easily from your hardware store. The blast plate is fine, but there is a plastic holder between the plate and the rod. I recommend adding a tiny overturned clay pot for heat protection (with the launch rod going through the pot's drain hole). The launch pad legs are fine. The launch controller appears to be unchanged from the old pad (dating back decades). That said, there is a lot of bang for the buck here. In this hobby, you can easily spend $70 just for a launch controller. Or, if you are handy, you can make your own pad and controller.If you are new to rocketry, before you go all-in and get yourself a launch pad, I recommend that you see if there is a local rocketry club. Not only will this save you the trouble of buying a pad, but also save you the trouble of figuring out if you need a launch waiver (some municipalities impose launch restrictions). With a club, you can show up with your rocket, fire it, watch a bunch of other crazy rockets, and be done with it. The club near me even provides free loaner rockets for interested parents and kids. Clubs also usually carry insurance, a useful thing to have when playing with high velocity pyrotechnic devices.I want to add that I'm really happy that Estes is still in business and is still competitive. How many of the brands you grew up with are still around and still producing the quality products they once made? Estes has done what they've had to do to survive, so who am I to criticize?

One reviewer said the binder was 3 inches thick and another said 2 1/2, so I measured it, and got... 2 3/4 inches. Anyway, it's big for what it is. Takes up a lot of shelf space. With only eight slots for folders (each with different functions), you have to have a strong idea of exactly what you're going to need for your project before you use it. You can't add to it beyond those eight folders.My "I-Organize Envelope" arrived with a permanent crease in its "spine" that causes it to remain distortedly open, and the clipboard is utterly useless. But that's all.I'm not sure why the "Secure File Folder" was designed the way it was-- you have to open two sides of an elastic, then open the folder itself and page through whatever's in there. I would think that the traditional type of folder (where you thumb through things on top) would have been a much more effective start, then the designer could have added an elastic or other security flap on top so things won't fall out.Beyond the first one, the folders won't lie flat well when the binder is open, either.But the main problem for me is that there's no easy way to take notes here-- there certainly should be a way to integrate a pad of paper or a three-ring mini-binder, which would turn this from a showpiece into something actually useful. As it stands, all I can see here is something you'd bring along to a meeting to impress somebody with how modern and organized you are. To me, it's not worth that kind of space.

OK, perhaps the staplers we have around our home office are a bit old and used compared to what you might have in your office, but I remember that if you have more than about 10-15 pages to staple, it's a struggle.  The more pages you have to staple, the more physical strength you must use.  And the more pages you have, the lower the chance the staple will actually succeed.  A fair amount of the time the staple will not fold over properly, or it will jam.My initial impression of this new stapler is that it solves these problems, completely.  For up to 28 pages of standard laser paper - which is what I tried it with - it works flawlessly, every time.  It takes the same mount of effort for 28 pages as for 2 pages, which isn't very much: to say that you can staple with one finger is NOT an exaggeration.  You can also do it with the end of your palm, but you will quickly realize that this is overkill: it simply does not take that much effort or strength.I admit I was dubious when I ordered the stapler, but I am now a believer.The worst thing I can say about this stapler is that it stands a little taller than most conventional staplers.  I don't consider that a problem.I was confused about loading staples, because with other staplers one loads them with points down, and on this one you have to put them in points up.  You can't close the unit if they are loaded wrong.  I figured it out eventually.  There is small embossed print on the bottom that says "read user manual before stapling".  There really is no user manual with the stapler, even online.  But, c'mon, it's a stapler.  Don't staple your body, or anything but paper.  The rest of what you need is probably in this review.The box comes with one full load of staples.  It says it "uses standard 1/4" staples" on the box.  On the stapler it is slightly more specific: "USE STANDARD 26/6 STAPLES".  That helps.  Turns out that PaperPro (the maker of this stapler) makes that kind of staples that are reasonably priced, and there are other brands, too.I think we have two or three staplers that use various sizes of staples.  We keep that many around to make sure that at least one of them work.  Now I think I'll take throw away the ones in worst condition or that use different staples to keep one spare until I get to know this one better, but it sure seems like a winner to me.

This workbook is a perfect "at home supplement" for my young daughter. The children in her kindergarten class have a very wide range of reading and writing skills (some can't recognize the word "the," while several kids in the class--including my child--can read 40 page books and are starting to spell medium-length words by sounding them out). The teachers do their best to keep everyone engaged, but as a parent I want to ensure my daughter is given sufficient opportunities to grow and stretch. This book is perfect for that, because it adds a "creative thought" element to writing, and it's something she enjoys doing in her spare time.The book starts out with a couple of pages for kids to practice their alphabet (the "ascender" and "descender" parts of the row are a different color, so they stand out more), then dives into the creativity portion... the next several pages ask kids to think of 6 things you'd find in an farm/classroom/party/etc. A subsequent set prompts them to think of various types of descriptive words for a particular item ("A duck sounds _____. A duck looks _______. A duck feels _______."). Another set of pages first ask for 3 words describing a single item ("My family is _____. My family is ______. My family is _____.") then prompts the writer to combine them into a single sentence ("My family is ______, _____, and ________.") So it not only encourages the creative thought, but coaches the child on how to assemble this type of sentence. Another batch of pages has "helper words" at the top (such as "flower pot, seeds, water") then prompts the user to write sentences using these words ("First _________. Second ___________. Third _________.")So the book provides enough structure to make it easy for the child to understand what is being asked, and the repetition makes it easy for them to remember the structure. The workbook itself is also high quality, with full color and thick pages. All in all, I found this an extremely useful tool for a child who's a moderately-fluent reader, has mastered writing all her letters, and is beginning to construct words independently... and think it would be good for any child at that stage of reading/writing, whether they be 4, 6, 8, or 10.

If you're someone who compulsively fills file folders (I have yet to meet any one who isn't), you've no doubt made the acquaintance of no small number of brands of file folder labels. But this is a business where the little things count: every tiny advantage deserves to be factored into the consumer's decision.  The reason I like these Avery labels:1.  They peel off more easily than any labels I've tried.2.  They're color-coded.3.  They indeed are adhesive, bringing considerable credibility to the maker's hyperbolic claims of permanence.4.  The length of the label allows room for including more critical details to distinguish one folder from another.Note to those who are distressed by the label's length, since it's likely to exceed the horizontal dimensions of many folder tabs: Some time ago I discovered that it makes more practical sense to simply cut away the tabs from file folders. Cut the tab so that the tops of both sides of a folder are identical, stick the label to the top of the folder--outside front cover or inside back, your preference--and you'll discover that rifling through a file alphabetically is not only easier but far less destructive.

First, I don't think a lot of the reviewers thoroughly tested this product, use them in an office, or use them in a variety of environments/printers. We tested these on a variety of surfaces & printers - here are our results:* Adhesion: They stick great to a variety of surfaces: thin file folders, thick file folders, cardboard boxes, regular copy paper, books, plastic (i.e., shrink wrapped items & blister packs). Same results each time - great adhesion.* Temperature: We tried these in warm (80F) and cold (20F). They do exceptionally well in the cold - even standard packing tape has problems in 20, but these adhere pretty well. They do not fall off easily.* Moisture: They even hold up well when slightly damp, or exposed to slight humidity. Unfortunately there is no way to report any "long term" testing at this time (i.e., if your records storage is not climate controlled - but I have no reason to suspect any problems).* Removability: Yes, great. They peel cleanly off any surface.* Re-usable: Yes! If using on cardboard, they can peel & re-use 3 or 4 times. If using on file folders, or a smoother surface (blister packs, glossy book covers, etc), even more. Adhesion is great.* Printer Jams: OOPS! ... near fatal flaw here for most people. Tested in 5 machines - jammed at least once in every machine. It jams in our laser printer & laser copier 25% of the time. It jammed in our ink jet printer once or twice.The problem is that these are slightly wider than 8.5" (actually about 8 and 7/16"). They don't feed in our plain paper copier/fax machine AT ALL - the paper width cannot be adjusted, and it simply wont grab the sheet. And, when combined with regular copy paper, it jams nearly 100% of the time.WHEN PRINTING: Make sure the paper width in your printer can adjust slightly, and make sure not to mix them with other types of paper. Also, it tends to feed better through printers (like our ink jet) that "straight" feed (as opposed to laser printers which feed paper through an S-shaped drum).* Re-feeding through printer: Here's another potential problem. They work best in only one direction. It's not designed to print 10 labels, turn it over, and print 10 different labels at some point in the future. That will waste labels for some people, who don't need to print 30 labels at a time. Also, if you try to feed it through a laser printer more than once, the edges will start peeling (due to the heat I suppose, which is not an issue with ink jet printers).* Laser vs Ink Jet: When they did feed properly, the resolution was great on both types of printer.* Cross-comparison: We compared these to 3M, HP, Avery, Office Depot Brand, and Office Max brand removable labels. They rank BEST for adhesion, temperature, removability, and re-usability...but *WORST* for printer jamming.* Conclusion: They are excellent in every way except for the occasional printer jam.

Other than my desire for a more suctiony suction, that is my only complaint.  I really love this dispenser and wouldn't want to go back to old Bessy.

I can shed multiple sheets, usually 4 or so at at a time, without jamming or overheating or slowing down.*It eats credit cards and staples.  I don't have to remove staples before feeding the machine and the credit cards go through easily.*It is enclosed on all sides so that little fingers can't slide in or under.*It has the safety sensor that shuts the shredder off when touched.  I haven't had any problems with it causing the machine function to stop unnecessarily.*It makes confetti rather than strips for more secure shredding.CONS:*I honestly don't have any complaints.

When you first hear about this Epson multi-function,it looks great  and promises a lot. The Print, scan, copy, fax, and wireless functions all sound really great. It has a superb scanner, that works well when scanning to a USB drive and the resolution is superb. The general printing capabilities work well for while, but then they go wacky and replacing the cartridges is a waste of time. When I kept on trying and trying to set up the wireless, I thought it was something I was doing wrong, but I followed the directions and the epson would not connect to the local wireless network , even though every other unit I have connects easily. The Air Print fails totally, and it is very disappointing. Most of the basic printing works well for a while, but then it fails. Overall, if you want a short term printer, that can scan very well after the printing fails ( and you get Fair to intermittent Faxing capabilities that work better with a fax modem). Some Epson's work very well, but this one just fails after a few months use.

My office has been buying these Pilot G-2 07 pens for the last couple years in blue and black ink and I'm not sure if I have ever used a simpler and better pen. The black ones for some reason don't seem to work consistently and run into the typical pen problem of going through times where nothing will come out, but the blue ones have always worked amazingly. The blue ones write SO easily that I refuse to grab any other pens from our supply cabinet and I even buy these at home now. In my opinion the grip feels great and the pen is easy to grab onto and keep in your hand. The ink in my experience comes out very thin and dries very quickly and only smears *immediately* after writing. After 2-3 seconds it is already dry and you're good to go. It is a click pen, and it doesn't appear to be any louder than other click pens; it may be slightly quieter.I cannot recommend the black pens because they are not as reliable, and I have not used the two other colors, but I can tell you that the regular blue pens are my go-to pens now. They are simply awesome.

This binder is about as solid as you can get. The dark brown looks great, even feels good. But you can tell right away this will last many years! Does everything you want in a paper binder, but is obviously built to last!

Looking to replace my tired Fujitsu ScanSnap S1500M (on my Mac) I thought I'd give the Epson a try. While the scanning is fast, easy and clear, the software falls way short. I've been typing for a living for a long time and never really looked into getting a wrist platform product before.  Man, I've been straining my hands for far too long...especially considering I type away on a keyboard for 8-10 hours daily.  This thing has been just what I've needed and I'm surprised it took me this long to figure out that they exist.  Better late than never!  Another great product from 3M!

If you're looking for appropriate return address labels for your holiday cards, these Gold Foil labels will do the trick nicely. Although the labels are quite shiny, they work perfectly with an ink-jet printer. After printing, I quickly rubbed my finger against the printed text and was unable to smudge the ink at all. The labels have sufficient room for a logo next to your name and address. While you could fit four lines of text here, a slightly larger print size and three lines of text works well.I loaded these labels into an HP PhotoSmart C309n-s for printing. I initially had a little difficulty getting the paper to engage properly. The pages have to be loaded face down in this particular printer and the mechanism pulling in the paper has to engage with the fairly slippery backing of the adhesive labels. The backing plus the labels are somewhat thicker than some label pages so the HP failed to load the page at first. Reloading with fewer sheets solved the problem. This probably says more about the HP than about the Avery labels, but it's worth noting.Avery has a template for the 8257 at their website; that's the appropriate template for these 8987 labels. I downloaded the template and used it in MS Word without difficulties on my Mac. The process of downloading the template and opening it in Word was straightforward and intuitive.None of the labels peeled off or made any threat of doing so in the printing process. I printed using black ink; contrast is very good (obviously not as good as with white labels, but certainly more than acceptable). You might find that a bold typeface works well with these labels.The package contains 10 sheets of 30 labels each. If you don't use the template, I'd recommend you print on a blank sheet of paper initially, then hold it up to the address label sheet to ensure that everything lines up well. That way you won't waste a sheet of labels on off-center printing.

This thing is fast!  It heats up very rapidly and feeds quickly too.  It's a solid unit and well made.  The design is simple.  This one is built for an environment where you're laminating often.  Plug it in, turn it on, and go!

I print all my own address labels, and have done so for my at-home business for years.  Lately I've been noticing that some labels I buy don't seem to work with the template given to use with them.  I use The Print Shop Deluxe software for making up my labels, and when I designed some using the template I was told to use, they printed totally off-center and not in the right place, wasting a bunch of printer ink on unusable labels.  This seemed to mostly happen with the new "easy peel" labels, which often had one product number but said on the package to use another product number template.  I got very frustrated by this.  I tried using an on-line Avery software, and had little better luck.  I'd pretty much almost decided no longer to print my own labels, but when given a chance to review this product, thought I'd give it another try.Well, so far so good.  I've just printed up about 15 sheets of labels, and all printed precisely correctly.  I have a fairly cheap HP inkjet printer, and it has printed them well.  These are smaller labels than I usually use, as I like to put a picture on one side of the address, and these are a little too small to do that and also have room for a legible address, but that's not the fault of the labels!  They are plenty big enough for an address that can be clearly read.  The smaller size also allows lots of labels to be made from the one pack.  So for now, my faith in Avery is restored!

This CD or DVD sized storage goes beyond the regular paper or plastic sleeves in which we traditionally store and transport or disc-sized media. It is a perfect fit for the media as the others are, but it has the added advantage of having an adhesive (that is secure and repositionable and which does not touch the media) so you can adhere your CD to a presentation binder, for example.It also has a laminated tab on the top or side (depending on how you position it) so you can use it to turn pages or to locate the CD or DVD. You can write on one side of the tab to label the contents. (The tab comes in a contrasting color. I would prefer for it to blend in a little less conspicuously, but that's just me). It also has a closing tab to ensure that the media doesn't drop out and that the end user can replace the disc after use.I suppose that business cards and photographs, folded invoices and receipts can also be presented using this holder, but it really looks like something designed to hold a CD or DVD, so if you put a business card in it, for example, it looks wrong. (I wonder if there is a coordinating business card sized one?)I love products that have multiple uses that, although intended for one thing, can be used in many other situations. This, I think, is limited to situations in which you want to add supporting material on CD or DVD media to your printed presentation, be it for business or for an educational presentation. For that purpose, it shines. It creates a practical, professional, secure, integrated, and elegant presentation. Sure beats handing out the CD's separately in a detached container.I used it for a proposal which I had printed out and bound at Kinko's. On a blank page at the very end facing out and visible from the back outside plastic cover, I placed the CD which contained additional information, photos and charts, and a pdf of the presentation in case they wanted to print additional copies. In this instance, it looked better to use the tab only for labeling and to center the container on the blank page, but there may be situations in which you want the tab to stick out.

I recently received an epson stylus nx430 color printer. It was super easy to install and get working, even with hooking it up to my wireless network. (Just as an FYI, it does NOT come with a USB cable, so if you need it to be wired you do need to supply your own cable.) I love having the availability to copy and scan in my school room (we homeschool) without the printer taking up a lot of space in the room. My one complaint is that I am having problems with the paper feeder taking photo paper. It prints beautifully on 8 1/2 x 11 paper, but it seems to have trouble grabbing my photo paper and running it through the machine. I'm not writing this printer off quite yet - I plan on trying some other brands of photo paper, but at this point, it is not catching 4x6 photo paper and running it through.Overall, I'm pleased with this printer for regular everyday copying and printing at home.

The Avery Flags are a great product for anyone. I used them on both plain paper printouts and in various texts. The Flags do stick but are removable without tearing the page. Writing on them can be tricky if you do not use a ball point pen. My favorite feature is that they are reusable. Overall the product is a worthwhile investment. I highly recommend for anyone and believe the product should be a "staple" in any home office.

This is a great binder for my middle schooler.  It is well made and appears sturdy.  I never totally trust these metal 3 rings to stay aligned... Time will tell if it will remain intact.  I like the zipper feature in case it fails.  I would never suggest using the handle....  If you forget to zip, you are in trouble.The folders are a nice addition.

Q. What is it?A. It's a weird tape-like substance that you can use over and over.Q. Why?A. Not really sure, but the Scotch R&D; guys have to keep inventing new stuff if they want to keep their jobs.Q. What do you get?A. Six strips of 1" x 3" double-back clear tape.Q. Huh?A. Right.So this stuff is pretty cool, but I can't think of that many uses for it. The one use that seems pretty practical is classrooms & conference rooms. I'm thinking of a corporate training center where the instructors make notes on big flip charts and then taped these to the walls. This tape would be perfect for that, because they could just use these same six strips of tape day after day after day. When the tape gets grubby after repeated use, you can just wash it off and then it's sticky again after it dries. I don't know if that's completely practical for classroom applications, but it works.Aside from that, it's not really practical for wrapping a present or repairing your spectacles. It's just a pre-cut piece of tape (6 of 'em) that you can use for adhering lightweight items to smooth/clean surfaces. That's it.
These are great! They stick very well, plenty of space for writing an address, and seem very durable. Will purchase in the future!

I've tried other brands that were supposed to be compatible, but they printed horribly. If you have a Brother Printer/Fax/Copier the only way to go is with Brother Ink by amazon and get prime for free two day shipping .

I picked this product to review because I recently purchased a 2010 planner that does not have dividers for each month.  I thought these might come in handy, so that I can use these to divide my planner by the months.I like the roundness of the label--easier to spot in my planner, but you would need to write really small for these to work, unless you didn't need to write on the colored part of the label, which I do.  I also think I would prefer a brighter color, to make them stand out.  These are pastel colors.  The colored part of the label is just alittle too small for me.These do seem very durable, where the more transparent part of the label is, and more room to write there too.It might be fun to think of all the useful ways a person can use these.  They are a definite improvement over regular dividers!
